property_title: Kaner Retreat: Serene Days Among India's Timeless Landscapes
property_intro: Set amid rolling countryside where birdsong marks the hours, Kaner Retreat offers a gentler rhythm of travel. Handcrafted interiors draw on local artisanry, with earthen textures, shaded verandahs and courtyards designed for lingering. Days unfold through village walks, slow-cooked regional feasts and conversations with the craftspeople whose skills shape every room. Working closely with neighbouring communities and championing native planting, the retreat gives back as generously as it welcomes. Arrive curious; leave quietly restored.

property_title: Flame of the Forest: Wild Luxury on the Edge of Bandhavgarh
property_intro: On the fringes of Bandhavgarh, where sal forest gives way to open meadow, Flame of the Forest offers just four suites shaped by handloom textiles, tribal artistry and vast windows framing the wilderness. Days unfold with tiger tracking at dawn, slow breakfasts beside the water and evenings spent listening to the calls of the forest. Guided walks with naturalists, village encounters and long-standing support for local conservation give every stay a deeper resonance.

property_title: Island Luxury Boutique Hotel Fulhadhoo: Barefoot Maldives Calm
property_intro: On Fulhadhoo, a slender island in Baa Atoll where fewer than three hundred people live, this intimate retreat sits between a shallow lagoon and a sandbank that seems to drift away at high tide. Rooms are simple and light-filled, cooled by sea breezes rather than excess. Days pass snorkelling coral gardens, sailing with local fishermen or sharing home-cooked Maldivian dishes. The hotel employs islanders, supports turtle protection and keeps plastic firmly off its shores.

property_title: Drenmo Lodge: Tracking Snow Leopards in Ladakh's Wild Highlands
property_intro: High in the Ulley valley, where Ladakh's ridgelines fold into snow leopard country, Drenmo Lodge offers eight quietly considered rooms warmed by sunlight and local craftsmanship. Days here begin with spotting scopes and Himalayan silence, guided by villagers who know every gully and pugmark. Built and run with the community that has long shared these mountains with wild predators, the lodge turns conservation into hospitality \u2013 and rewards guests with wildlife encounters few ever witness.

property_title: Kerala Tours: Barefoot Luxury on Aruba's Sunlit Shoreline
property_intro: Set along Aruba's breeze-cooled coast, Kerala Tours invites you into a gentler rhythm, where mornings begin with birdsong from the divi trees and afternoons drift toward turquoise water. Interiors pair island craftsmanship with cool, uncluttered spaces, while guided excursions reveal hidden coves, salt flats and the island's Arawak heritage. Local guides and growers shape every experience, ensuring your stay supports the communities who call this shoreline home. Come for the sunsets; linger for the stories.

property_title: Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge: Himalayan Views, Rooted in Place
property_intro: Set on a ridge high above Pokhara, Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge looks across terraced farmland to the Annapurnas and Machhapuchhre. Stone-and-slate cottages, hand-built by local craftsmen, open onto gardens alive with birdsong. Days unfold slowly here: village walks with naturalist guides, sunrise from the hilltop, unhurried suppers of produce grown on the estate. Long committed to reforestation, fair employment and neighbouring schools, the lodge offers a stay that gives back as generously as it gives.}

property_title: Suryagarh: Golden Sands, Living Traditions and Desert Calm
property_intro: On the edge of Jaisalmer, where the Thar Desert stretches into pale gold, Suryagarh rises in honey-hued sandstone, its courtyards and jharokhas echoing Rajasthan's fortress craft. Days here move gently: dawn rides past forgotten stepwells, folk musicians beneath the stars, chef-led forays into recipes from nearby villages. The hotel champions regional artisans, revives Marwari kitchen traditions and cares for local heritage sites, so every stay quietly strengthens the desert communities that give this place its soul.

property_title: Perfume Tourism - 24 MG Road: Scented Escapes in the City
property_intro: Set along the leafy stretch of MG Road, Perfume Tourism - 24 MG Road invites you into a world where fragrance shapes every moment. Interiors blend handcrafted Indian materials with quiet contemporary lines, while guided scent workshops reveal the artistry of local perfumers and the botanicals behind them. Ingredients are sourced from regional growers, supporting farming families nearby. Step out to markets and galleries, then return to a calm, softly perfumed retreat.

property_title: The Foresterie: Where Indian Woodlands Meet Quiet Luxury
property_intro: Tucked among towering sal and teak, The Foresterie invites you to slow down within one of India's most gently guarded forest belts. Timber-framed suites open onto birdsong and mist, their interiors shaped by local craftspeople and salvaged wood. Days unfold with tracker-led walks, riverside breakfasts and conversations with the naturalists who call this landscape home. A share of every stay supports village schooling and habitat restoration, making your retreat quietly consequential.

property_title: Casa Morada: Islamorada's Bayfront Haven of Barefoot Elegance
property_intro: Tucked along a quiet stretch of Florida Bay in Islamorada, Casa Morada gathers just sixteen suites around gardens of gumbo limbo and orchids. Days unfold slowly here: sunrise yoga on the coral terrace, kayaks slipping through mangrove channels, seagrass restoration with local marine biologists, and the bay turning copper at dusk. Interiors marry Latin American craft with Keys ease, while the kitchen leans on island growers and line-caught catch. Intimate, unhurried and quietly conservation-minded.

property_title: Brewery Gulch Inn: Redwood Warmth Above Mendocino's Wild Coast
property_intro: Perched above Smuggler's Cove on California's Mendocino coast, this ten-room inn was built from century-old redwood salvaged from the depths of the Big River – timber with a story in every beam. Days unfold slowly here: headland walks, birdsong in the gardens, then an evening light supper with local wine as fog drifts in over the water. Fireplaces, deep tubs and ocean-facing balconies invite lingering, while close ties to Mendocino's farmers and winemakers keep every plate honest.

property_title: Historic Tapoco Lodge: Riverside Calm in the Smoky Mountains
property_intro: Set where the Cheoah River tumbles through the Blue Ridge of western North Carolina, Historic Tapoco Lodge began life in 1930 as lodgings for the dam builders who shaped this valley. Today its restored rooms, riverside cabins and wood-warmed dining room welcome walkers, paddlers and drivers of the famed Tail of the Dragon. Whitewater release days, ancient poplars in Joyce Kilmer Forest and Appalachian producers on the menu keep the setting close at hand.

property_title: Hartstone Inn: Coastal Maine Charm in the Heart of Camden
property_intro: Tucked into a quiet street in Camden, Maine, Hartstone Inn occupies a graceful 1835 mansard-roofed home moments from the harbour and the trails of Camden Hills. Rooms blend antique character with considered comfort, while the kitchen has long been the draw: chef-led dinners built around Maine's fishermen, farmers and foragers. Days unfold with windjammer sailing, orchid-filled gardens and village bookshops, before returning for a fireside nightcap and genuinely unhurried hospitality.

property_title: A Stones Throw Away: Barefoot Bahamian Luxury by the Sea
property_intro: Perched above Gambier Village's limestone shoreline, just west of Nassau, A Stones Throw Away occupies a hand-built stone house shaded by sea grape and coconut palm. Rooms open to terraces where the Atlantic shifts through impossible blues, and breakfast arrives with fresh papaya and warm Bahamian bread. Antique furnishings and local artwork nod to the island's heritage, while long-standing ties to the historic village community keep the welcome genuinely rooted, unhurried and quietly generous.

property_title: Eremito Hotelito del Alma: Umbrian Stillness, Rediscovered
property_intro: Hidden within a thousand hectares of Umbrian wilderness, Eremito Hotelito del Alma is a hand-built hermitage where candlelight replaces Wi-Fi and silence is the house speciality. Guests sleep in stone celluzze, dine communally on vegetarian dishes drawn from the estate garden, and drift between yoga, forest walks and long soaks in the candlelit hammam. Powered by renewable energy and restored using local craftsmanship, it invites you to slow down, listen closely and leave lighter than you arrived.

property_title: Khem Villas: Where Ranthambore's Wilderness Meets Warm Welcome
property_intro: On the fringes of Ranthambore National Park, Khem Villas occupies land once farmed and now returned to forest, grassland and lake by a family devoted to tiger country. Days unfold with dawn safaris, birdsong from the watchtower and slow meals drawn from the kitchen garden. Cottages and tented rooms open onto wild greenery, while conservation work and village schooling projects continue quietly alongside. It is Rajasthan seen through the eyes of those who know it intimately.

property_title: Neeralaya: Riverside Serenity in India's Verdant Highlands
property_intro: Set beside flowing water and framed by forested slopes, Neeralaya invites you to slow your pace and settle into the rhythm of the surrounding countryside. Interiors blend local craftsmanship with quiet contemporary comfort, while days unfold through river walks, plantation trails and long, unhurried meals shaped by the season's harvest. The property works closely with neighbouring villages and champions thoughtful water stewardship, so every stay leaves something meaningful behind in the valley.

property_title: Atali Ganga: Himalayan Adventure Above the Sacred Ganges
property_intro: Perched on a forested ridge above the rushing Ganges near Rishikesh, Atali Ganga is where Himalayan adventure meets quiet comfort. Stone-and-timber cottages step down the hillside, framing views of the river far below. Days might begin with white-water rafting or a climb on the property's own rock face, and close with yoga as the valley darkens. Run with genuine care for the surrounding villages and forest, it's a retreat for those who like their luxury earned.

property_title: Surya Samudra, Kovalam: Cliffside Calm Above the Arabian Sea
property_intro:
On Kerala's southern coast, set on a palm-cloaked headland above the Arabian Sea, Surya Samudra gathers rescued Keralan timber houses 
ew puraround gardens of frangipani and spice. Days unfold slowly here: Ayurvedic treatments guided by resident physicians, sunrise yoga on the cliff, fishermen hauling in the morning catch below. Kovalam's lively shore lies close, yet the mood remains hushed, with local craftspeople and coastal produce woven through every meal and detail.

property_title: Backwaters & Beyond, Kumarakom: Where Kerala Slows to a Ripple
property_intro: On the fringes of Vembanad Lake, Backwaters & Beyond sits where paddy fields meet still water and the day is measured by passing canoes. Rooms open to palm shade and birdsong from the nearby sanctuary, while meals draw on the garden, the lake and recipes shared by neighbouring households. Drift out at dawn with a local boatman, learn to cook with coconut and toddy vinegar, and let Kerala reveal itself unhurried.

property_title: Samroha, Athirapilly: Rainforest Calm Beside Kerala's Falls
property_intro: Tucked into the forested folds of Athirapilly, where the Chalakudy river tumbles over Kerala's most storied waterfall, Samroha offers a gentler way to meet the Western Ghats. Rooms open to birdsong and mist, with interiors shaped by local craft, reclaimed timber and an unhurried sense of space. Days here might mean guided walks with naturalists, hornbill spotting at dawn, or plantation lunches drawn from neighbouring smallholdings. Conservation is quietly woven through it all, as is genuine kinship with the surrounding villages.

property_title: Vaidekam, Kannur: Coastal Calm on Kerala's Malabar Shore
property_intro: Set among coconut groves on Kannur's quiet Malabar coast, Vaidekam is a restored family home where terracotta floors, carved timber and shaded verandahs invite you to slow down. Days unfold with Ayurvedic treatments, home-cooked Malabar meals and unhurried walks to nearby beaches, backwaters and theyyam performances in village shrines. Local artisans and growers shape much of what you eat and admire here, making each stay quietly generous towards the community that surrounds it.

property_title: Narendra Bhawan: Royal Bikaner Reimagined with Wit and Warmth
property_intro: Once the residence of Bikaner's last Maharaja, Narendra Bhawan carries the eccentric spirit of a well-travelled prince through its layered interiors, where regimental portraits meet Deco curves and marigold-bright textiles. In Rajasthan's desert north, days unfold with camel-country drives, Jain temple visits and rooftop dinners scented with cumin and rose. Recipes drawn from royal kitchens, local artisans behind every detail and a genuine kinship with the surrounding city make each stay feel personal rather than performed.

property_title: Mary Budden Estate: A Himalayan Retreat in Binsar's Oak Woods
property_intro: Tucked deep inside Binsar Wildlife Sanctuary, high in Uttarakhand's Kumaon hills, Mary Budden Estate gathers a handful of restored colonial cottages within ancient oak and rhododendron forest. Days unfold gently here: birdsong at first light, guided walks along leopard trails, wood fires, and unhurried meals drawn from the kitchen garden. Interiors marry Himalayan craft with understated English character, while the estate's forest stewardship and local employment help this fragile woodland, and its snow-peak horizons, endure.

property_title: SwaSwara: Coastal Stillness and Soulful Living in Gokarna
property_intro: Tucked between the Arabian Sea and the forested hills of Gokarna, SwaSwara opens onto a crescent of quiet sand reached only on foot. Twenty-four laterite villas, hand-built with local stone and clay, hold open-air showers and rooftop meditation decks. Days unfold through yoga, Ayurvedic treatments, art therapy and Konkan-inspired vegetarian cooking drawn from the organic gardens. Rainwater harvesting, solar heating and long-standing village partnerships make this a retreat with genuine roots.

property_title: Spice Coast Cruises: Drifting Through Kerala's Living Backwaters
property_intro: Aboard a lovingly restored rice barge, Spice Coast Cruises glides through Kerala's palm-fringed backwaters, where village life unfolds along the water's edge. Handcrafted from coir, bamboo and reclaimed teak by local boatbuilders, each kettuvallam is powered thoughtfully and stocked with produce from nearby markets. Days pass with toddy-tappers at work, kingfishers overhead and Keralan meals cooked onboard. Overnight moorings in quiet canals invite conversation with the crew, many raised in the very hamlets you drift past.

property_title: Emboo River Camp: Silent Safaris on the Maasai Mara's Edge
property_intro: On the banks of the Mara River, Emboo River Camp watches elephants drift through the acacias and lions pad along the plains beyond. Kenya's first fully solar-powered camp, it explores the reserve in silent electric vehicles, so game drives unfold without engine noise. Suites are open to the light and air, water is recycled, and Maasai neighbours share in the camp's success. Days end with river breezes and firelit conversation beneath a vast African sky.

property_title: Coconut Lagoon: Heritage Living on Kerala's Tranquil Backwaters
property_intro: Reached only by boat, Coconut Lagoon sits where Lake Vembanad meets a maze of palm-fringed canals in Kerala. Its tharavadu \u2014 traditional Keralan homes rescued plank by plank and rebuilt within the grounds \u2014 house guests amid paddy fields, coir gardens and resident herons. Days unfold with canoe rides through village waterways, Ayurvedic treatments, cookery lessons rooted in Syrian Christian tradition, and evenings of Kathakali. Biogas, rainwater harvesting and local employment quietly underpin it all.

property_title: Arenas Del Mar: Rainforest Seclusion Above Manuel Antonio
property_intro: Set across eleven hectares of protected rainforest between Manuel Antonio's national park and two quiet Pacific beaches, Arenas Del Mar sits where jungle canopy meets tidal sand. Sloths and toucans pass through the treetops while suites open to ocean panoramas and private terraces. Days might involve guided wildlife walks, kayaking through mangroves or long afternoons by the sea. Family-owned and carbon-neutral, the property channels its efforts into local employment, reforestation and Costa Rica's conservation legacy.

property_title: Saruni Leopard Hill: Wild Serenity in the Masai Mara's Heart
property_intro: Perched above the Mara North Conservancy, Saruni Leopard Hill looks out across plains where wildebeest thunder and leopards move through the shadows at dusk. Just six glass-fronted suites are built into the rock, each with a private plunge pool and views that shift with the light. Guided walks with Maasai warriors, night drives and conservancy-led conservation work sit at the heart of the experience, supporting the landowners whose land you're privileged to explore.

property_title: The Datai Langkawi: Rainforest Luxury on Malaysia's Wild Edge
property_intro: Tucked between a ten-million-year-old rainforest and the quiet sands of Datai Bay, this Langkawi retreat invites you to slow down and listen. Hornbills call from the canopy, dusky langurs pass overhead, and resident naturalists reveal the forest's secrets on guided walks. Interiors of tropical hardwood and local craft echo the landscape beyond. Through its Datai Pledge, the resort funds marine conservation, wildlife research and village education ", making every stay quietly meaningful.

property_title: Batu Batu: A Private Island Sanctuary in Malaysia's Johor Sea
property_intro: Set on its own island in the Johor Marine Park, Batu Batu occupies twenty-two forested hectares fringed by white sand and coral gardens. Twenty-two timber villas sit quietly among the trees, cooled by sea breezes rather than excess. Days pass with snorkelling over reefs, kayaking to empty coves and dinners of freshly landed seafood. The resort funds Tengah Island Conservation, whose team protects nesting turtles and restores coral, employing villagers from the neighbouring mainland.

property_title: Pacuare Lodge: Rainforest Luxury on Costa Rica's Wild River
property_intro: Reached by raft along the churning Pacuare River, this remote retreat sits within a private rainforest reserve in Costa Rica's Talamanca foothills. Hand-built suites of local hardwood and thatch open to jungle canopy, some with plunge pools and candlelit outdoor bathrooms. Days unfold with canyoning, night walks and visits to neighbouring Cabécar communities. Profits protect thousands of acres of jaguar habitat, while local families form the heart of the team — luxury with genuine purpose.

property_title: Isla Palenque: Barefoot Island Living on Panama's Pacific Coast
property_intro: Set within Panama's Gulf of Chiriquí, Isla Palenque occupies 400 acres of private island rainforest fringed by seven beaches and the warm Pacific. Just eight casitas and a beachfront villa sit quietly among the trees, built from local hardwoods and open to the sound of howler monkeys at dawn. Days unfold with kayaking through mangroves, snorkelling, forest walks and long lunches. The island's conservation work and close ties with the mainland fishing village give every stay real meaning.

property_title: Zuri Zanzibar: Barefoot Elegance on Kendwa's Turquoise Shore
property_intro: On Zanzibar's north-western coast, where Kendwa's white sand meets water the colour of sea glass, Zuri unfolds across eight hectares of tropical garden planted with over 3,000 species. Thatched villas and bungalows draw on Swahili craft and Scandinavian restraint, while dhow sails pass at sunset. Days move between spice-scented cuisine, coral reef snorkelling and stargazing. Solar power, plastic-free practice and support for nearby village schools make the pleasure here quietly purposeful.

property_title: Kura Boutique Hotel: Rainforest Luxury Above Costa Rica's Pacific
property_intro: High in the hills above Uvita, Kura is an adults-only retreat where the rainforest meets sweeping views of the Whale's Tail coastline. Just eight suites, shaped in stone, timber and glass by Costa Rican designers, open onto an infinity pool that seems to spill into the Pacific. Days unfold with waterfall hikes, whale watching and cuisine drawn from nearby farms, while the surrounding land is protected in partnership with local families and conservation projects.

property_title: Brunton Boatyard: Harbourside Heritage in Historic Fort Kochi
property_intro: Where the Arabian Sea meets Kochi's storied harbour, Brunton Boatyard rises on the site of a former shipyard, its colonnaded verandahs and vast teak doors echoing Dutch, Portuguese and British craftsmanship. Watch Chinese fishing nets dip at dawn from your sea-facing balcony, dine on recipes revived from colonial-era kitchens, and wander Fort Kochi's spice lanes and synagogue on foot. Locally sourced produce, regional artisans and long-standing community ties give this handsome hotel genuine soul.

property_title: Amazon Planet Tambopata Lodge: Rainforest Living, Reimagined
property_intro: Reached by river from Puerto Maldonado, Amazon Planet Tambopata Lodge sits within a private reserve on the edge of one of Peru's richest wildlife corridors. Timber bungalows open to the forest canopy, where macaws, monkeys and a dawn chorus of unfamiliar voices set the rhythm of the day. Guided walks, canopy climbs and night paddles are led by naturalists from neighbouring communities, while ongoing reforestation and research projects ensure your stay directly supports the Tambopata it celebrates.

property_title: Chumbe Island: Barefoot Eco-Luxury on Zanzibar's Coral Reef
property_intro: Just off Zanzibar's west coast, Chumbe Island is a protected coral sanctuary where seven thatched eco-bungalows open entirely to the sea breeze. Solar power, rainwater harvesting and composting systems make each stay genuinely low-impact, while rangers guide you through a fully protected reef alive with more than 400 fish species. Wander the coral rag forest at dusk in search of giant coconut crabs, then dine on Swahili seafood as lanterns flicker and the tide draws breath.

property_title: Lapa Rios Lodge: Rainforest Luxury on Costa Rica's Osa Peninsula
property_intro: Perched above the meeting point of the Pacific and the Golfo Dulce, Lapa Rios Lodge sits within a thousand-acre private reserve on Costa Rica's wild Osa Peninsula. Sixteen thatched bungalows open to canopy views where scarlet macaws pass at eye level. Days unfold with naturalist-led walks, tidepooling and visits to the neighbouring village school the lodge helps support. Every stay protects primary rainforest, sustains local families and proves that comfort and conservation belong together.

property_title: Borana Lodge: Wild Laikipia Horizons and Rhino Conservation
property_intro: Set high on a ridge in Kenya's Laikipia highlands, Borana Lodge looks across 32,000 acres of conservancy towards Mount Kenya's snow-capped peaks. Eight cottages of local stone and olive wood open to sweeping views, while days unfold on horseback, on foot with Samburu guides, or tracking black rhino reintroduced to this landscape. A working cattle ranch and family home for generations, Borana channels every stay into wildlife protection, schools and clinics across neighbouring communities.

property_title: Nimali Serengeti: Where the Great Migration Comes to You
property_intro: Set on a quiet rise in the central Serengeti, Nimali Serengeti places you within reach of the migration's thundering passage, yet far from the crowds. Ten glass-fronted suites open to grasslands where lion and cheetah move at their own pace. Days unfold with unhurried game drives, bush breakfasts and starlit dinners, while the camp's solar power, water recycling and Tanzanian-led team keep its footprint light and its welcome genuinely local.

property_title: Jamtara Wilderness Camp: Starlit Nights in Pench's Wild Heart
property_intro: On the quiet northern edge of Pench Tiger Reserve, where teak forest gives way to farmland and the Satpura hills rise beyond, Jamtara offers ten canvas-and-stone suites shaped by local craft. Days unfold with tracking safaris, walks with Gond naturalists and long lunches under mahua trees; nights are best spent on the machan, sleeping beneath the stars. The camp runs on solar power, grows much of its produce and employs from surrounding villages.

property_title: Song Saa Private Island: Barefoot Luxury in Cambodia's Koh Rong
property_intro: Two tiny islands in Cambodia's Koh Rong Archipelago, joined by a hand-built footbridge, hold one of Southeast Asia's most quietly captivating retreats. Villas of reclaimed timber and driftwood hover over a protected marine reserve, where coral gardens and rainforest thrive under Song Saa's care. Days unfold with snorkelling, spa rituals in the jungle and Khmer dishes shaped by island produce, while the neighbouring fishing village benefits directly from the foundation's schools, clinics and conservation work.

property_title: Simbambili Game Lodge: Leopard Country in the Wild Sabi Sand
property_intro: Tucked into the Sabi Sand Game Reserve, where no fences separate the land from Kruger's vast wilderness, Simbambili sits above a dry riverbed frequented by leopard at dusk. Eight thatched suites blend Zanzibari carvings with private plunge pools and open-air showers, while dawn drives with expert trackers reveal the reserve's remarkable density of big cats. Guided walks, treehouse dinners and long-standing partnerships with neighbouring communities and anti-poaching teams give every stay quiet purpose.

property_title: The Malabar House — Where Fort Kochi's Heritage Meets Artistry
property_intro: Tucked beside the parade ground in Fort Kochi, The Malabar House occupies a 300-year-old mansion where Keralan craftsmanship meets contemporary Mediterranean colour. Fourteen rooms and suites open onto courtyards shaded by frangipani, while the pool garden invites long, unhurried afternoons. Dine on seafood drawn from local waters, wander to spice warehouses and Chinese fishing nets, or join an Ayurvedic ritual. Careful restoration and lasting support for regional artisans keep this quietly remarkable house rooted in its community.

property_title: Boulders Camp: Solitude Among the NamibRand's Granite Giants
property_intro: Tucked into a valley of wind-sculpted granite within the NamibRand Nature Reserve, Boulders Camp offers just a handful of canvas suites, each opening onto an ocean of red sand and profound quiet. Days unfold through guided walks, dune drives and stargazing beneath some of the darkest skies on earth. Part of the Wolwedans collection, the camp runs on solar power and channels its efforts into desert conservation and hospitality training for young Namibians.

property_title: Dera Amer: Wild Aravalli Beauty and Tented Luxury near Jaipur
property_intro: Tucked into acacia forest in the Aravalli foothills beyond Amer, Dera Amer feels a world away from Jaipur, yet lies barely half an hour from its palaces. Handsome canvas suites open onto scrubland roamed by nilgai, peacocks and the camp's rescued elephants, cared for alongside local mahout families. Days unfold with forest walks, village visits and long, lantern-lit dinners cooked over open flame \Rajasthani hospitality at its most unhurried, generous and quietly conservation-minded.

property_title: Zhiwaling Heritage: Bhutanese Craftsmanship in the Paro Valley
property_intro: Set among rice terraces and apple orchards in Bhutan's Paro Valley, Zhiwaling Heritage was built by Bhutanese hands using local stone, hand-carved timber and traditional painting techniques passed between generations. Days might begin with a walk to Taktsang, the Tiger's Nest, and close beside the fire in the Mad Monk bar. The family-owned hotel supports village artisans and monastic communities, offering a stay that feels rooted in place rather than borrowed from elsewhere.

property_title: Jicaro Island Lodge: Private Island Serenity on Lake Nicaragua
property_intro: Set on its own islet among the Granada archipelago, Jicaro Island Lodge floats between the waters of Lake Nicaragua and the smoking silhouette of Mombacho volcano. Nine timber casitas, built from fallen storm wood by local craftspeople, open to howler monkeys, herons and swimming from the shore. Days drift through kayaking, yoga, coffee-farm visits and market wanders in Granada, while the lodge's support for island schools and reforestation gives every stay quiet purpose.

property_title: Saruni Eagle View: Where the Mara Naboisho Wilderness Unfolds
property_intro: Perched on a ridge above the plains of Mara Naboisho Conservancy, Saruni Eagle View looks out over one of Kenya's richest lion territories. Nine tented cottages, dressed in natural linens and warm timber, open to uninterrupted views and a horizon shaped by acacia and sky. Days here move with the wildlife: walking safaris led by Maasai guides, quiet game drives, evenings by the fire. Conservancy fees support Maasai landowners and keep this corridor wild.

property_title: The Sarai at Toria: Riverside Calm on the Edge of Panna
property_intro: Set where the Ken River curves past farmland and forest, The Sarai at Toria offers eight thatched cottages between the temples of Khajuraho and the tiger country of Panna National Park. Founded by two conservationists, it runs on solar power, local craftsmanship and village partnerships. Days might involve boat trips past gharials and kingfishers, walks with naturalists, or unhurried afternoons watching the river drift by from your veranda.

property_title: Jehan Numa Retreat: Wild Bhopal, Horses and Heritage Living
property_intro: On the fringes of Bhopal, where Van Vihar's forest edges meet the shimmer of Upper Lake, Jehan Numa Retreat carries forward a family legacy shaped by generations of horsemen and conservationists. Airy suites open onto gardens and stables, where Marwari horses graze and mornings begin with riding lessons or birdsong-filled walks. Days unfold slowly: Bhopali cuisine drawn from regional recipes, spa treatments beneath the trees, and thoughtful excursions to Bhimbetka's ancient rock shelters and nearby tiger country.

property_title: Saseka Tented Camp: Barefoot Luxury in the Thornybush Wild
property_intro: Tucked into the Thornybush Nature Reserve, sharing unfenced boundaries with Kruger, Saseka Tented Camp brings a quiet sophistication to the South African bush. Ten canvas suites open onto the Monwana riverbed, where elephants pass at dawn and leopards move unseen through the scrub. Interiors blend natural linens, timber and handcrafted African pieces, while game drives, guided walks and treetop dining reveal the reserve's rhythms. Local guides and conservation partnerships ensure your stay supports the land and its people.

property_title: Qayaam Gah: A Kashmiri Hillside Retreat Above Dal Lake's Shores
property_intro: Tucked into a walnut and almond orchard on the slopes above Srinagar, Qayaam Gah looks out across Dal Lake to the Zabarwan range. Just a handful of rooms occupy this thoughtfully restored Kashmiri home, where hand-carved walnut wood, crewel embroidery and papier-mâché detailing tell of generations of local craft. Days unfold slowly here: orchard breakfasts, conversations with artisans, shikara mornings on the lake, and evenings warmed by wazwan cooked from the valley's own harvest.

property_title: Chanoud Garh: A Rajasthani Fort Reborn by Its Own Family
property_intro: Deep in rural Rajasthan, between Jodhpur and Udaipur, a 250-year-old fort has been coaxed back to life by the family who have called it home for generations. Chanoud Garh holds just ten suites, each restored with lime plaster, frescoes and heirlooms rather than replicas. Days unfold slowly here: village walks past potters and weavers, courtyard dinners of recipes passed down through the household, and conversations with hosts whose lineage is woven into every wall.

property_title: Plains Camp: Where Namibia's Vast Horizons Invite True Stillness
property_intro: Set on open grasslands where oryx drift past at dawn, Plains Camp offers a gentle kind of seclusion. Canvas and timber suites are shaped by the light and wind, framing views that stretch far beyond the horizon. Days unfold through guided walks, tracking on foot and evenings spent beneath extraordinarily clear skies. The camp works closely with neighbouring conservancies, supporting local guides and wildlife monitoring, so your stay quietly strengthens the landscape that surrounds it.

property_title: Aquila Eco Lodges: Off-Grid Elegance in the Grampians Ranges
property_intro: Tucked into bushland on the edge of Halls Gap, Aquila Eco Lodges sits where the Grampians' sandstone ridges meet quiet stands of gum. Each solar-powered lodge is designed to sit lightly on the land, with private decks where kangaroos graze at dusk and cockatoos announce the morning. Days unfold along walking trails, waterfalls and Gariwerd rock art sites, before evenings spent under some of Victoria's clearest skies, cocooned in warmth and considered comfort.

property_title: Marari Beach Resort: Barefoot Living on Kerala's Palm Coast
property_intro: Set among swaying coconut groves on Kerala's Malabar coast, Marari Beach Resort borrows the shape of the fishing village beside it, with thatched cottages, open courtyards and garden showers. Days drift between the Arabian Sea, Ayurvedic treatments and lazy backwater cruises through the nearby lagoons. Much of the produce arrives from local farms and the kitchen garden, while village fishermen, weavers and craftspeople remain part of daily life here, keeping the resort genuinely rooted in its surroundings.

property_title: The LUNGMĀR Remote Camp: Ladakh's High-Altitude Wilderness
property_intro: Set high on the Changthang plateau, where Ladakh's horizons stretch beyond measure, The LUNGMĀR Remote Camp offers a rare kind of seclusion. Handcrafted tented suites echo the palette of the surrounding hills, warmed by wool, woodsmoke and lantern light. Days unfold with nomadic shepherds, wildlife tracking across snow leopard country and star-filled silences. Built with Ladakhi artisans and run alongside local families, the camp channels its earnings into the valleys and communities that make it possible.

property_title: Bagh Villas: Wild Luxury on the Edge of India's Tiger Country
property_intro: Set among sal forests and farmland on the fringes of Bandhavgarh, Bagh Villas offers a quietly considered retreat where days begin with birdsong and end beneath vast Madhya Pradesh skies. Private villas open onto plunge pools and mahua trees, while interiors draw on local craft and earthy materials. Join naturalist-led safaris, village walks and seasonal kitchen gardens, supported by conservation partnerships and employment that keeps neighbouring communities at the heart of every stay.

property_title: Cloud Forest Lodge: Where Misted Canopies Meet Quiet Luxury
property_intro: Perched high above Costa Rica's northern valleys, Cloud Forest Lodge sits within a private reserve where mist drifts between ancient trees and quetzals call at first light. Timber-framed suites open onto the canopy, furnished by local artisans and warmed by wood-burning stoves. Days unfold with guided birdwatching, waterfall trails and cacao tastings alongside neighbouring farmers, while the lodge's reforestation work and community schooling programme quietly shape the valley's future. An invitation to slow down entirely.

property_title: Basata Eco-Lodge: Barefoot Simplicity on Sinai's Red Sea Shore
property_intro: On a quiet stretch of coast between Nuweiba and Taba, Basata sits where the Sinai mountains meet the Gulf of Aqaba. Handbuilt huts of stone, bamboo and palm open onto a fringing reef alive with coral and colour. Days pass slowly here: baking bread in the communal kitchen, snorkelling before breakfast, watching Saudi Arabia's peaks turn rose at dusk. Founded on principles of recycling, low-impact living and Bedouin partnership, it remains gently, deliberately unhurried.

property_title: The Alpina Gstaad: Alpine Craftsmanship in the Bernese Oberland
property_intro: Perched above the village of Gstaad, this chalet-style retreat looks across the Bernese Oberland's meadows and snow-dusted peaks. Reclaimed local timber, hand-carved detail and Alpine antiques give each room a sense of place, while the Six Senses Spa, a Japanese restaurant and a private cinema invite unhurried days. Built to Minergie environmental standards and closely tied to regional farmers and artisans, it offers mountain hospitality with quiet conscience and considerable warmth.

property_title: Kipling Camp: Wild Mornings on the Edge of Kanha's Sal Forests
property_intro: Tucked into forty acres of sal woodland beside Kanha Tiger Reserve in Madhya Pradesh, Kipling Camp has welcomed naturalists and curious travellers since 1982. Days unfold slowly here: dawn safaris in search of tiger and barasingha, birding walks with resident guides, and long lunches beneath the trees. Cottages are unfussy and characterful, run in close partnership with neighbouring villages, while decades of conservation work quietly underpin everything. Wild India, warmly and thoughtfully shared.

property_title: Shahpura Bagh: Heritage Living Among Rajasthan's Quiet Lakes
property_intro: Set within 45 acres of orchards, lakes and birdlife in rural Rajasthan, Shahpura Bagh remains the home of the family who built it, welcoming guests into elegantly restored royal residences. Days unfold with picnics beside ruined cenotaphs, walks to village wells and dawn boat rides among migratory birds. The estate supports local farming, schooling and craft, while candlelit dinners under the stars reveal a slower, more personal side of Rajasthan rarely found on the usual routes.

property_title: The Belgadia Palace: Heritage and Wilderness in the Mayurbhanj
property_intro: Set within twenty acres of gardens in Baripada, northern Odisha, this 200-year-old Victorian palace remains the home of the Bhanj Deo family. Nine restored suites open onto verandahs where mornings begin with birdsong and locally grown produce. Simlipal's tiger reserve and Sabai grass weaving villages lie close by, and the family's Mayurbhanj Foundation channels guests' curiosity into artisan livelihoods and tribal education. Expect candlelit dinners, storytelling and afternoons spent tracing Odisha's overlooked artistic legacy.

property_title: Kamara House: Refined Bush Living in South Africa's Wild Heart
property_intro: Set within South Africa's sunlit bushveld, Kamara House gathers guests into a home rather than a hotel, where light-filled interiors, handcrafted local pieces and long verandahs invite unhurried days. Mornings might begin with game drives alongside trackers who know each ridge and waterhole; afternoons drift towards the pool, or the kitchen table. Conservation partnerships and local employment shape every detail here, so your stay quietly supports the land and communities that make this corner of Africa so compelling.

property_title: Maison Perumal: Heritage Living in Puducherry's Tamil Quarter
property_intro: Tucked into Puducherry's Tamil Quarter, Maison Perumal occupies a lovingly restored 130-year-old Chettiar merchant house, where shaded courtyards, lime-plastered walls and antique teak columns hold the cool of the day. Ten rooms open onto verandahs scented with jasmine, while the kitchen serves Franco-Tamil dishes drawn from local recipes. Wander to the seafront at dusk, join a cycle ride past colonial facades, or simply linger over filter coffee as temple bells drift through the lanes.

property_title: Fivelements Retreat: Riverside Healing in the Heart of Bali
property_intro: Set along the sacred Ayung River near Ubud, Fivelements Retreat is woven from bamboo, thatch and local craftsmanship, its suites opening to jungle canopy and the sound of running water. Here, Balinese healers guide ancient rituals, plant-based cuisine is treated as an art form, and wellness programmes are shaped around your own rhythm. Village artisans and traditional knowledge sit at the centre of everything, making each stay a quiet exchange rather than an escape.

property_title: The Lodge at Wah, Palampur: Tea Gardens Beneath the Dhauladhar
property_intro: Set among the working tea gardens of Palampur, with the Dhauladhar range rising sharply beyond, The Lodge at Wah belongs to an estate that has been tended by the same family for generations. Colonial-era architecture, deep verandahs and locally sourced Kangra cuisine set the rhythm here. Walk the plucking trails with estate workers, learn how leaf becomes cup, or simply follow birdsong through the pines while the mountains change colour at dusk.

property_title: Spice Village: A Thekkady Eco Retreat Beside Periyar's Forests
property_intro: High in the Cardamom Hills, on the fringes of Periyar Tiger Reserve, Spice Village gathers thatched cottages among pepper vines, coffee bushes and fruit trees. Tribal building traditions shape every roof; solar power, rainwater harvesting and a zero-waste ethos shape everything else. Days unfold with guided forest walks, cookery classes led by the resident chef, and organic produce picked steps from your plate \u2014 all sustaining local livelihoods and the wildlife next door.

property_title: Hotel Aguas Claras: Caribbean Colour on Costa Rica's Wild Coast
property_intro: Tucked between rainforest and the surf of Playa Chiquita, near Puerto Viejo on Costa Rica's Caribbean coast, Hotel Aguas Claras is a cluster of pastel timber casitas dreamed up in homage to Afro-Caribbean Talamanca. Botanical gardens draw sloths and toucans; mornings begin with cacao from neighbouring farms and end with Creole cooking at Fresh. Local artisans shaped much of what you see, from hand-painted tiles to woven details, and reforested grounds keep the wilderness pleasantly close.

property_title: Diphlu River Lodge: Wild Rhythms on Kaziranga's Doorstep
property_intro: On the fringes of Kaziranga National Park, where the Diphlu River slips past tall elephant grass, this Assamese lodge offers a rare closeness to India's greatest rhino country. Eight bamboo-and-thatch cottages, raised on stilts and crafted by local artisans, look out over paddy fields and forest. Days begin with mahout-led safaris and end with Assamese home cooking, tea-garden walks and village encounters that channel guest spending directly into conservation and neighbouring communities.

property_title: Mihir Garh: A Handcrafted Fortress in Rajasthan's Golden Wilds
property_intro: An hour beyond Jodhpur, where scrub desert gives way to shepherd trails and Bishnoi villages, Mihir Garh rises from the sand like something half-remembered. Built by hand from local mud, lime and dung by regional artisans, its nine suites hold sunken baths, fireplaces and terraces open to enormous skies. Days unfold on Marwari horseback, in candlelit dune dinners and unhurried conversation with village families whose crafts and livelihoods the family-run estate has long championed.

property_title: MANVĀR Kumat: Where the Thar Desert Unfolds in Timeless Luxury
property_intro: Set among the shifting dunes and scrub forest between Jodhpur and Jaisalmer, MANVĀR Kumat is a quiet retreat in the heart of Rajasthan's Thar. Sandstone and earth tones echo the landscape, while jeep safaris reveal chinkara, desert fox and the Bishnoi villages who have long protected them. Days drift from dune breakfasts to folk music beneath vast skies, with local artisans and guides sharing the desert as only its own people can.

property_title: BrijRama Palace: Where Varanasi's Sacred River Awakens
property_intro: Perched on Darbhanga Ghat, BrijRama Palace occupies a 1812 riverside residence where hand-carved balconies open directly onto the Ganges. Mornings begin with temple bells and the slow procession of boats; evenings bring rooftop dining above the glow of aarti flames. Restored over six years by artisans using traditional techniques, the palace preserves original stonework, frescoes and India's oldest working lift. Guided walks through Varanasi's lanes, classical music recitals and dawn river crossings reveal the city's living rituals with quiet reverence.

property_title: Tiger Trails and Quiet Luxury at Svasara Jungle Lodge, Tadoba
property_intro: On the edge of Maharashtra's Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve, Svasara Jungle Lodge sits among teak and bamboo forest near Kolara gate, where langurs call at first light and tigers move through the undergrowth. Twelve airy suites blend local stone, timber and handcrafted detail, while naturalist-led safaris, birdwatching walks and unhurried afternoons by the pool shape the rhythm of your stay. Village partnerships, local employment and conservation research quietly underpin everything here.

property_title: Dune Camp: Wild Desert Seclusion in Namibia's Ancient Sands
property_intro: Set among the wind-sculpted dunes of Namibia's vast desert, Dune Camp offers a rare kind of quiet. Canvas suites are raised on timber decks, framing horizons of ochre sand and distant mountains, while interiors favour natural linen, local craft and warm lamplight. Days unfold with guided walks tracking desert-adapted wildlife, dune drives and evenings beneath extraordinary night skies. The camp runs on solar power and works closely with neighbouring conservancies, so your stay supports those who safeguard this landscape.

property_title: Senda Monteverde Hotel: Where Costa Rica's Cloud Forest Sings
property_intro: Tucked into the misted hills above Monteverde, Senda sits within its own regenerating forest, where bellbirds call and hummingbirds hover at eye level. Timber-and-glass casitas frame the canopy, while guided night walks, birding at dawn and visits to nearby coffee-growing families reveal the region's quieter rhythms. Native planting, careful water use and local employment sit at the heart of the operation. Return each evening to a hot bath, a good book and the sound of rain on leaves.

property_title: Craveiral Farmhouse: Slow Alentejo Living Among Rolling Hills
property_intro: Set within 25 hectares of cork oaks, orchards and vegetable gardens in Portugal's Alentejo, Craveiral Farmhouse sits a short drive from the wild beaches of Costa Vicentina. Timber-clad villas with private pools frame views across the countryside, while the kitchen draws on the estate's own harvest. Guests gather bread from the wood-fired oven, tend the animals, forage with the gardener or simply drift between vineyard, spa and stars. Regenerative farming and local craftsmanship shape every detail here.

property_title: Ladakh Sarai: Where Himalayan Stillness Meets Warm Hospitality
property_intro: Set among poplar groves and barley fields near Stok, Ladakh Sarai looks out to the snow-brushed Stok Kangri range from 3,500 metres. Yurt-inspired cottages, built with local stone, timber and mud plaster, keep the mountain chill at bay while the wood stove crackles. Days unfold with monastery walks, high-pass treks and homestay lunches shared with village families. Solar power, spring water and Ladakhi cooking anchor a stay that quietly supports the valley's communities.

property_title: Basecamp Wilderness: Barefoot Luxury on the Maasai Mara
property_intro: On the banks of the Talek River, where the Maasai Mara's plains stretch towards the horizon, Basecamp Wilderness offers a rare kind of quiet. Canvas tents raised on timber decks open to riverine forest, while solar power, harvested rainwater and locally crafted furnishings reflect decades of Maasai partnership. Days unfold with guided walks, game drives led by community trackers and evenings beside the fire, listening as the bush settles into darkness around you.

property_title: Bari Kothi: A Sheherwali Legacy Reborn Beside the Bhagirathi
property_intro: On the banks of the Bhagirathi in Azimganj, Bari Kothi opens the door to Murshidabad's forgotten grandeur. Once home to Sheherwali merchant princes, this 18th-century mansion has been painstakingly revived by the family who inherited it, its frescoes, courtyards and Belgian glass restored by local artisans. Days unfold with rare Sheherwali vegetarian feasts, heritage walks through silk-weaving lanes, and slow river afternoons ", conversations with hosts who treat every guest as kin.

property_title: Kasbah Tamadot: Atlas Mountain Serenity Above Asni Valley
property_intro: Perched high in Morocco's High Atlas, an hour from Marrakech, Kasbah Tamadot looks out across the Asni Valley towards Mount Toubkal. Once the home of an Italian collector, it retains his eye for antiques and intricate Moroccan craftsmanship, softened by rose gardens and Berber tents. Days unfold with mule treks to mountain villages, hammam rituals and mint tea at altitude. Local employment, artisan partnerships and the on-site Eve Branson Foundation weave the surrounding communities into every stay.

property_title: Rohet Garh: Heritage, Horses and Desert Life in Rajasthan
property_intro: On the edge of a village lake in rural Rajasthan, Rohet Garh has been home to the same family for sixteen generations. Whitewashed courtyards, frescoed rooms and shaded verandahs open onto gardens alive with peacocks and kingfishers. Ride Marwari horses across scrubland to Bishnoi hamlets, where communities have protected wildlife for centuries, or share supper drawn from the estate's own fields. Writers have found their muse here; you may simply find stillness.

property_title: Sanctuary Resort: Where Nepal's Wilderness Meets Quiet Luxury
property_intro: Set on the fringes of Nepal's lowland forests, Sanctuary Resort looks out across grasslands where rhinos graze at dusk and birdsong carries on the breeze. Rooms are built from local timber and clay, shaped by craftspeople from nearby villages. Days unfold with guided walks, canoe drifts along the river and slow suppers of garden-grown produce. A share of every stay supports anti-poaching patrols and community schooling, so your rest quietly sustains the wild around you.

property_title: Basecamp Adventure: Wild Riverside Living in the Maasai Mara
property_intro: On the banks of the Talek River, at the edge of the Maasai Mara, Basecamp Adventure invites you to settle into the rhythm of the wilderness. Canvas tents rest beneath indigenous trees planted by hand, part of a forest grown from bare ground over two decades. Days unfold with game drives, walks led by Maasai guides and visits to the nearby women's beadwork cooperative, where craft sustains families and conservation is a shared, daily practice.

property_title: Singinawa Jungle Lodge: Kanha's Wild Heart, Thoughtfully Lived
property_intro: On the fringes of Kanha National Park in Madhya Pradesh, Singinawa spreads across 55 acres of restored sal forest and grassland, where leopards pass through and birdsong marks the hours. Twelve stone-and-timber cottages sit apart from one another, furnished with tribal Gond artistry. Days bring tiger safaris with resident naturalists, visits to the lodge's own museum of tribal art, and conversations with the Baiga communities whose livelihoods and knowledge shape everything here.

property_title: Brij Villa: A Portuguese-Era Hideaway on Diu's Golden Shores
property_intro: On the sun-warmed island of Diu, where the Arabian Sea meets whitewashed churches and Portuguese arches, Brij Villa unfolds as a century-old residence lovingly restored. Just moments from Ghoghla beach, its seven rooms pair colonial bones with contemporary calm, opening onto courtyards shaded by frangipani. Days drift between cycling through fishing lanes, seafood suppers rooted in local catch and conversations with craftspeople who keep the island's traditions, and its quiet character, beautifully alive.

property_title: The Lodge at Wah, Kandbari: Tea Gardens Below the Dhauladhar
property_intro: Set within a working tea estate in the Kangra Valley, The Lodge at Wah looks straight up to the snow-tipped Dhauladhar range. Four elegant suites occupy a restored colonial-era bungalow, where wood floors, deep verandahs and family heirlooms invite unhurried afternoons. Walk the plantation with the tea makers, taste first-flush Kangra brews at source, or follow forest trails to village temples. The estate has sustained local livelihoods for generations, and guests become part of that story.

property_title: Villa Nai 3.3: Where Dugi Otok's Olive Groves Meet the Adriatic
property_intro: Carved into a limestone hillside on Dugi Otok, Villa Nai 3.3 hides beneath 22 hectares of centuries-old olive groves, its eight rooms opening to the Adriatic and the scattered Kornati islands beyond. Days here follow the rhythm of the harvest: tastings of the estate's celebrated oil, dives into the sea-fed pool, sailing towards Telašćica. Family-run and deeply rooted in island tradition, it offers a quiet, considered kind of luxury that feels wholly of this place.

property_title: Brij Gaj Kesri: A Timeless Bundi Retreat Below Aravalli Hills
property_intro: In the little-visited town of Bundi, where painted havelis lean over stepwells and the Aravalli hills fold around Taragarh Fort, Brij Gaj Kesri offers a gracious pause. Once a nobleman's residence, its arched verandahs, frescoed corners and courtyard gardens invite slow mornings and lamplit dinners. Wander to lakeside temples with a local guide, watch kingfishers at dawn, or learn Bundi's miniature painting traditions from artists whose families have kept this delicate craft alive for generations.

property_title: ABN Charaidew I: Sailing the Brahmaputra's Wild Heart, Assam
property_intro: Drifting along the mighty Brahmaputra, ABN Charaidew I offers a rare vantage point on Assam's shifting sandbanks, tea gardens and river islands. Cabins are simply elegant, with timber detailing and windows framing the passing shore. Days unfold through village walks, Kaziranga safaris in search of one-horned rhino, and visits to Majuli's monasteries. Local crews, regional cooking and partnerships with riverside communities ensure your journey supports the culture and wildlife that make this waterway extraordinary.

property_title: ABN Sukhapa: Slow River Journeys Through Assam's Brahmaputra
property_intro: Drifting along the Brahmaputra, ABN Sukhapa turns Assam's great river into a moving address. Handcrafted from timber and local artistry, her cabins open onto sandbars, silk-weaving villages and the grasslands of Kaziranga, where one-horned rhinos graze at dawn. Days unfold with guided walks, tea-garden visits and unhurried conversations with river communities whose livelihoods the vessel supports. Evenings bring Assamese cooking, birdsong and a stillness rarely found on land.

property_title: Hotel Hacienda de Abajo: A Living Museum on La Palma's Coast
property_intro: Set among banana plantations in Tazacorte, on La Palma's sun-warmed west coast, this 16th-century sugar estate has been reimagined as an adults-only retreat where over a thousand antiques, paintings and artefacts fill the halls. Tropical gardens shelter rare species, the kitchen draws on island produce and Canarian tradition, and volcanic beaches lie minutes away. Guided walks reveal Biosphere Reserve landscapes, while the hotel's careful restoration keeps local craftsmanship and heritage quietly alive.

property_title: ShivAdya Manali: Himalayan Calm Above the Beas Valley
property_intro: Tucked into the pine-clad slopes above Manali, ShivAdya frames the Beas valley and the snow-tipped Dhauladhar range from every window. Interiors draw on Himachali craft — local stone, deodar wood and handwoven textiles — while orchard walks, apple-season harvests and quiet mornings with mountain tea shape the rhythm of a stay. The kitchen leans on produce from neighbouring farms, and village artisans supply much of what you'll touch, sit on and take home.

property_title: Treehotel: Suspended Among Swedish Pines in Lapland's Calm
property_intro: High in the pines above the Lule River, Treehotel places you within Harads, a village of some 600 souls in Swedish Lapland. Each room is a work of architecture in its own right, from the mirrored cube that dissolves into the forest to a bird's nest of woven branches. Meals draw on Nordic larders, saunas warm winter evenings, and the surrounding woodland remains largely untouched, with local families and craftspeople central to every stay.

property_title: Sadhrana Bagh: Aravalli Orchard Living Beyond Delhi's Edge
property_intro: Tucked into the Aravalli foothills near Delhi, Sadhrana Bagh unfolds across a working orchard where guava trees, birdsong and long shadows set the rhythm of the day. Rooms are quietly composed, with local stone, handwoven textiles and verandahs made for slow mornings. Wander farm paths with the gardeners, cook with produce picked at dawn, or ride out at dusk. Village artisans and regenerative planting keep the estate rooted in the land it belongs to.

property_title: Pegasus Suites & Spa: Whitewashed Calm Above Santorini's Caldera
property_intro: Carved into the cliffs of Imerovigli, Pegasus Suites & Spa looks out across Santorini's caldera, where the volcano rises from water the colour of ink. Cave-cut suites in lime-washed stone open onto private terraces, plunge pools and sunsets that need no introduction. Days unfold slowly here: Aegean spa rituals, Greek breakfasts made with island produce, and family hospitality shaped by generations. Local growers and artisans supply much of what you'll taste and touch.

property_title: Brij Anayra: Tea-Garden Serenity Beneath the Dhauladhar Peaks
property_intro: Tucked into the tea slopes of Dharamshala, Brij Anayra looks out to the snow-edged Dhauladhar range, where deodar forests and monastery bells set the rhythm of the day. Interiors draw on Kangra craft and gentle Himalayan light, while days unfold with estate walks, tea tastings, home-style Pahari cooking and quiet corners for reading. The team works closely with local growers, artisans and guides, so your stay leaves something meaningful behind in the valley.

property_title: Posada Amazonas: Rainforest Living with the Ese'eja Community
property_intro: Set above the Tambopata River in Peru's southern Amazon, Posada Amazonas is co-owned with the Ese'eja community of Infierno, whose knowledge shapes every encounter here. Open-walled rooms invite the forest's night chorus in, while days unfold along oxbow lakes, canopy towers and trails where macaws, giant otters and monkeys make their presence known. Thatched timber architecture, candlelit dinners and guides raised in these forests lend a quiet intimacy to your stay.

property_title: Papaya Playa Project: Tulum's Wild, Bohemian Beachfront Retreat
property_intro: Spread across a kilometre of Tulum's Caribbean shoreline, Papaya Playa Project trades polish for something rawer: palapa-roofed casitas built from local timber and thatch, tucked between dunes, jungle and sand. Days drift from cenote swims and sunrise yoga to full-moon gatherings where DJs play until dawn. Turtle nests are protected along the beach, produce comes from nearby growers, and Mayan traditions shape the spa rituals. Barefoot, unhurried and quietly conscious.

property_title: Abode Ahangama: Barefoot Luxury on Sri Lanka's Surf Coast
property_intro: Set among coconut groves and rice paddies on Sri Lanka's southern shore, Abode Ahangama is a quiet retreat moments from some of the island's finest surf breaks. Sunlit interiors blend handcrafted local timber, linen and terrazzo, while ocean breezes drift through open-sided living spaces. Days unfold with dawn surf sessions, yoga, and Sri Lankan cooking led by neighbouring families. Produce arrives from village growers, and the team's reef and beach initiatives keep this stretch of coast flourishing.

property_title: Nimali Mara: Tented Elegance on the Serengeti's Wild Frontier
property_intro: Set in the northern Serengeti, within reach of the Mara River, Nimali Mara places you at the heart of the great migration's most dramatic act. Ten canvas suites open onto golden grasslands, their interiors layered with Tanzanian craftsmanship, warm woods and quiet comfort. Days unfold with unhurried game drives, bush breakfasts and evenings beside the fire. The camp works closely with neighbouring communities and treads lightly, leaving the wilderness precisely as it found it.

property_title: Refugio Amazonas: Rainforest Living Deep in Peru's Tambopata
property_intro: Four hours upriver from Puerto Maldonado, Refugio Amazonas stands within a private conservation concession bordering Tambopata National Reserve. Open-walled rooms framed in local timber invite the forest's night chorus indoors, while candlelit dinners follow days spent climbing the canopy tower, tracking macaws or paddling oxbow lakes with resident naturalists. Guests support the neighbouring Brazil nut harvest and a children's rainforest education programme, making each stay part of a longer story of protection along the Madre de Dios.

property_title: Torres del Paine: Patagonia's Wild Granite Heart Awaits You
property_intro: In the far south of Chilean Patagonia, where granite towers rise above glacial lakes and guanaco graze the open steppe, Torres del Paine offers a rare kind of quiet. Days here unfold on foot or horseback, tracing trails towards Grey Glacier before returning to interiors shaped by local timber, wool and light. Guides born to this landscape share its stories, while rewilding and conservation partnerships help safeguard the puma, condor and grasslands beyond your window.

property_title: Machu Picchu Lodge: Andean Cloud Forest Calm and Quiet Wonder
property_intro: Tucked into the cloud forest where the Andes soften into the Amazon, Machu Picchu Lodge sits within earshot of the Urubamba River and a short walk from the citadel gates. Rooms are shaped from local stone, timber and handwoven textiles, framing orchids, hummingbirds and mist-laced peaks. Days unfold with sunrise hikes, guided walks alongside Quechua naturalists and dinners built on Sacred Valley produce, while reforestation projects and community partnerships keep this remarkable valley flourishing for generations.

property_title: Bera Safari Lodge: Leopard Country in Rajasthan's Granite Hills
property_intro: In southern Rajasthan, where granite outcrops rise above the Jawai countryside, Bera Safari Lodge sits within one of the few landscapes where leopards and Rabari herders share the same terrain. Stone-and-thatch cottages open onto scrub and sky, with dawn drives, hilltop sundowners and evenings around the fire. The family behind the lodge has spent decades documenting these cats and working alongside village communities, so every stay quietly supports the coexistence you have come to witness.

property_title: Wayanad Wild: Rainforest Luxury in the Cardamom Hills of Kerala
property_intro: Tucked into a working cardamom and coffee plantation on the fringes of Kerala's Western Ghats, Wayanad Wild sits within one of the world's great biodiversity hotspots. Timber-and-stone cottages rest lightly among the canopy, where hornbills call at first light and streams thread through the undergrowth. Days unfold with guided forest walks, plantation trails and slow Malabar cooking. Run by CGH Earth, the retreat supports local livelihoods and the rainforest that shelters it.

property_title: Brij Nest: Where India's Quiet Corners Become Your Own
property_intro: Tucked away from the well-trodden route, Brij Nest offers a gentler way to know India. Interiors marry local craftsmanship with unhurried comfort, while wide verandahs invite long mornings with chai and birdsong. Days unfold through village walks, heritage trails and kitchens where regional recipes are shared rather than performed. The team works closely with artisans and neighbouring communities, ensuring your stay leaves something meaningful behind. It feels less like a hotel, more like arriving somewhere familiar.

property_title: Lotus Houseboat: Drifting Through Kerala's Living Backwaters
property_intro: Moored among the palm-fringed canals of Kerala, Lotus Houseboat invites you aboard a hand-crafted kettuvallam shaped by local boat builders using coir rope and bamboo, in keeping with generations of tradition. Days unfold slowly here: village markets glimpsed from the deck, toddy tappers at work, and chefs preparing Syrian Christian and Keralan dishes from the morning's catch. Your crew hail from nearby hamlets, and a share of every stay supports backwater clean-up and wetland restoration.

property_title: Bori Safari Lodge: Where Satpura's Wilderness Feels Untouched
property_intro: On the quieter fringes of Satpura Tiger Reserve, Bori Safari Lodge sits beside the Bori Sanctuary's teak and bamboo forests in central India. Just a handful of cottages, shaped from local stone and timber, look towards the treeline where leopards, sloth bears and gaur move unhurried. Days unfold through walking safaris, canoe drifts and forest breakfasts led by naturalists from nearby villages, whose livelihoods and knowledge are woven into the lodge's quiet conservation work.

property_title: Hotel Cruz del Vado: Heritage Charm in Cuenca's Old Quarter
property_intro: Set on a cobbled corner above the Tomebamba River, Hotel Cruz del Vado occupies a lovingly restored 19th-century home in Cuenca's storied El Vado district. Colonial bones meet contemporary comfort here: high ceilings, timber floors and a light-filled courtyard where breakfast lingers. Step out to artisan workshops, flower markets and Andean bakeries, all within the UNESCO-listed centre. The owners champion local craftspeople and neighbourhood renewal, so your stay quietly supports the culture that makes this corner of Ecuador so beguiling.

property_title: Shreyas Yoga Retreat: Stillness in Bangalore's Green Heart
property_intro: Set among twenty-five acres of orchards and organic gardens on the edge of Bangalore, Shreyas Yoga Retreat invites a gentler rhythm. Days unfold with guided asana beneath old trees, Ayurvedic therapies and vegetarian meals drawn from the kitchen garden. Thatched cottages and tented villas open onto lawns where peacocks wander at dusk. Guests are welcomed to join the retreat's seva work at a nearby children's home, a quiet reminder that wellbeing deepens when shared.

property_title: Maslina Resort: Barefoot Luxury on Croatia's Island of Hvar
property_intro: Tucked between pinewoods and the pebbled shore of Maslinica Bay, moments from the Venetian streets of Stari Grad, Maslina Resort brings a gentler rhythm to Hvar. Interiors of stone, oak and linen echo the island's palette, while the kitchen draws on the resort's own garden and the surrounding UNESCO-listed plain. Days unfold with sea swims, herb foraging, lavender fields and treatments rooted in Dalmatian botanicals shaped by a genuine commitment to local producers and low-impact living.

property_title: El Chaltén: Patagonia's Trekking Heart Beneath Monte Fitz Roy
property_intro: Tucked into a valley where the Andes fracture into granite spires, El Chaltén sits beneath the sheer profile of Monte Fitz Roy, with trails to glaciers and turquoise lagoons beginning at the doorstep. Interiors favour local timber, wool and wide windows framing the peaks, while guides born in these mountains lead you through Los Glaciares National Park. Meals draw on Santa Cruz producers, and a portion of every stay supports regional rewilding and native forest restoration.

property_title: Parador Nature Resort & Spa: Rainforest Meets Pacific Shore
property_intro: Set on a private peninsula above Manuel Antonio, Parador Nature Resort & Spa is embraced by rainforest where capuchins and toucans move through the canopy at dawn. Antique-filled interiors and Spanish colonial detail lend the resort real character, while terraces open onto the Pacific. Days unfold with guided wildlife walks, hilltop yoga, tennis and treatments drawn from local botanicals. Much of the surrounding forest is protected, and reforestation work continues alongside the neighbouring Quepos community.

property_title: Aradura, Kohima — A Refined Retreat in the Nagaland Highlands
property_intro: Set on a pine-clad ridge above Kohima, Aradura looks out across the folded blue hills of Nagaland. Interiors pair Naga weaves, bamboo craft and locally quarried stone with quiet contemporary comfort, while mornings begin with smoked pork, black rice and hill-grown coffee. Wander to war memorials and Angami villages, walk forest trails with local guides, or simply listen to birdsong. Artisans, farmers and storytellers from surrounding communities shape every stay here.

property_title: Glenburn Tea Estate: Darjeeling Days Beside the Rungeet River
property_intro: High on a hillside above the Rungeet River, this 1860s planter's retreat looks across tea gardens to the snows of Kanchenjunga. Eight rooms in two colonial bungalows are dressed in family antiques, hand-blocked fabrics and deep verandah chairs made for slow mornings. Days unfold with tea tastings led by estate pluckers, riverside picnics, forest walks and visits to the school and clinic Glenburn supports. Dinners are Himalayan, Bengali and unhurried, served under lamplight.

property_title: Discovery Houseboat: Drift Through Kerala's Living Backwaters
property_intro: Moored amid the palm-fringed canals of Kerala, Discovery Houseboat invites you to travel at the pace of the water. Handcrafted by local artisans using traditional coir and bamboo, this gently elegant vessel drifts past paddy fields, village jetties and fishermen casting at dawn. Days unfold with Keralan cooking aboard, birdwatching in the shallows and unhurried conversation with your crew, who are drawn from the surrounding hamlets and share their backwater knowledge with quiet pride.

property_title: Thornybush Game Lodge: Bushveld Luxury Beside the Kruger Wilds
property_intro: Set within a private reserve sharing unfenced boundaries with Kruger National Park, Thornybush Game Lodge looks out across the Monwana River, where elephants drink at dusk. Suites blend earthy textures with deep verandas and private plunge pools, while twice-daily game drives with expert trackers bring you close to leopard, lion and rhino. Behind the scenes, anti-poaching teams and local employment initiatives ensure your stay supports the wildlife and communities that make this landscape thrive.

property_title: Kanha Jungle Lodge: Where Central India's Wild Heart Beats
property_intro: On the fringes of Kanha National Park, this unhurried retreat sits among sal forests and bamboo thickets where tigers, gaur and the rare barasingha roam. Rooms open onto gardens alive with birdsong, while evenings gather around lantern-lit dinners and conversation with resident naturalists. Days begin with dawn safaris and drift into village walks with Baiga and Gond neighbours. Locally staffed and quietly committed to forest conservation, the lodge offers wilderness with genuine warmth.

property_title: Chapslee: A Living Heirloom in the Hills of Shimla
property_intro: Perched above Shimla amid deodar cedars and Himalayan views, Chapslee is less a hotel than a family home that has quietly kept its 19th-century character intact. Persian rugs, Belgian glass and inherited portraits fill rooms still tended by generations of the same household. Days unfold over croquet on the lawn, tea beneath the pines and slow conversation at a shared table. Its careful custodianship preserves both a house and a vanishing hill-station way of life.

property_title: Killa Bhawan: Living Within Jaisalmer's Golden Fort Walls
property_intro: Tucked against the 12th-century ramparts of Jaisalmer Fort, Killa Bhawan is a restored haveli where sandstone walls glow amber at dusk and the Thar Desert stretches endlessly beyond. Each room is dressed in hand-blocked textiles, mirrorwork and heirloom pieces gathered across Rajasthan. Days unfold slowly here: rooftop chai above the lanes, conversations with local artisans, sunset over the desert. As one of the fort's few remaining lived-in homes, it quietly supports the community that keeps this ancient citadel alive.

property_title: Karan Mahal: Royal Rajasthani Living Reimagined with Purpose
property_intro: Set within Rajasthan's amber landscape, Karan Mahal welcomes you into a heritage residence where frescoed halls, jharokha windows and hand-carved sandstone tell generations of stories. Days unfold slowly here: dawn walks through village lanes, cooking beside local women who share family recipes, and evenings on rooftops beneath desert stars. Restoration has been guided by regional craftspeople, with artisan workshops and water conservation projects supported by every stay. An invitation to live within living history, rather than simply observe it.

property_title: Chile's Patagonia National Park: Where Wild Horizons Are Restored
property_intro: In the Chacabuco Valley, where windswept steppe meets glacier-carved peaks, Patagonia National Park is the result of one of South America's most ambitious rewilding efforts. Former sheep estancias now shelter guanaco, huemul deer and the elusive puma. Stone-and-timber lodges echo the region's estancia heritage, with hearty Patagonian cooking and long views over Lago Cochrane. Walk the Lagunas Altas trail, ride with local gauchos, or simply watch condors trace the ridgelines above.

property_title: Casa Baronesa Waterfront Villa: Ecuador's Coastal Sanctuary
property_intro: Set where the Pacific meets Ecuador's mangrove-fringed shoreline, Casa Baronesa invites you to slow down entirely. Sunlit interiors of pale wood and local stone open to terraces where pelicans glide past at eye level. Days unfold with paddleboarding through tidal channels, market visits with the villa's chef, or simply reading as the light shifts. The owners work closely with neighbouring fishing families and support mangrove restoration nearby, so your stay quietly gives something back.

property_title: Brij Pola, Jawai: Where Leopards Roam the Ancient Granite Hills
property_intro: Set among the weathered granite outcrops of Jawai in rural Rajasthan, Brij Pola looks out over a landscape shared by leopards, migratory birds and the Rabari shepherds who have herded here for generations. Stone-and-earth cottages echo local craft traditions, while days unfold with hillside safaris, village walks and dinners beneath a vast desert sky. The lodge works closely with surrounding communities, whose quiet coexistence with big cats remains one of India's most remarkable conservation stories.

property_title: Tambopata Research Center: Macaws, Rainforest and Wild Nights
property_intro: Set within Peru's Tambopata National Reserve, a boat journey beyond the last village, this lodge sits deeper in the rainforest than almost anywhere else in the Amazon. Days begin at the world's largest known macaw clay lick, where scarlet wings fill the air at dawn. Simple, screened rooms open to the canopy, resident biologists share their findings over dinner, and every stay supports long-running parrot research and local Ese'eja livelihoods.

property_title: Angermeyer Waterfront Inn: Galapagos Living on the Water's Edge
property_intro: Set on a quiet cove across the bay from Puerto Ayora, Angermeyer Waterfront Inn traces its story to a pioneering family who settled these volcanic shores in the 1930s. Lava-rock walls, driftwood details and wide windows frame Santa Cruz's turquoise inlets, where marine iguanas bask within metres of your terrace. Days unfold with snorkelling, guided island crossings and conversations with naturalists, while the kitchen champions Galapagos growers and the inn supports local conservation on your doorstep.

property_title: Explora Rapa Nui: Where Easter Island's Ancient Stories Live
property_intro: Set on a gentle rise above Rapa Nui's volcanic grasslands, Explora looks out towards the Pacific in every direction. Low-slung and built from local stone and native timber, the lodge feels quietly at home here. Days unfold on foot, by bicycle or on horseback, guided by islanders who share the meaning behind the moai and the land that holds them. Evenings bring Chilean wine, considered cooking and skies untroubled by light.

property_title: M.V. Rudra Singha: Slow Voyages Along Assam's Wild Brahmaputra
property_intro: Named for an Ahom king, M.V. Rudra Singha drifts along the Brahmaputra, where sandbanks shift with the seasons and river dolphins surface without ceremony. Cabins are panelled in warm timber, framed by windows that turn Assam's floodplains into moving artwork. Days unfold through village walks, tea garden visits and skiff excursions into Kaziranga's grasslands, guided by naturalists who know these waters intimately. Local crews, regional cooking and community partnerships keep the journey rooted in Assam itself.

property_title: Explora Atacama: Desert Horizons, Starlit Skies and Salt Flats
property_intro: Set among the adobe walls and pepper trees of San Pedro de Atacama, Explora Atacama opens onto the world's driest desert, where salt flats shimmer and volcanoes rise on the horizon. Days unfold through guided hikes, high-altitude lagoons and horseback rides with local Likan Antai guides, followed by starlit observatory sessions. Interiors are quiet and unfussy, shaped by regional craft, while the lodge's conservation work protects the fragile landscapes you'll come to know intimately.

property_title: Nepali Ghar: Heritage Warmth in the Heart of Kathmandu
property_intro: Tucked between the prayer flags and courtyards of Thamel, Nepali Ghar is a modern tribute to Newari craftsmanship, where carved timber windows, hand-thrown ceramics and locally woven textiles set a quietly refined tone. Mornings begin with Himalayan coffee before walks to Durbar Square or Boudhanath's great stupa. The kitchen champions Nepali producers, while the house supports local artisans and schooling initiatives, making each stay part of Kathmandu's living story rather than a passing glance.

property_title: Utsav Camp: Desert Evenings and Starlit Calm in Rajasthan
property_intro: Set among the dunes and thorn scrub of Rajasthan, Utsav Camp offers a considered take on desert living. Canvas suites are dressed in block-printed textiles and handwoven rugs, crafted by artisans from nearby villages. Days unfold with camel trails, folk musicians at dusk and dinners beneath a sky untouched by light pollution. Water is harvested, solar power drawn from the sun, and much of the team hails from the surrounding communities.

property_title: Neeleshwar Hermitage: Barefoot Luxury on Kerala's Malabar Coast
property_intro: On a quiet stretch of Kerala's northern Malabar coast, Neeleshwar Hermitage gathers sixteen thatched cottages between coconut groves and an untamed shoreline. Inspired by the region's fishing villages, each pavilion opens to sea breezes and Ayurvedic calm, with treatments guided by resident physicians.
