Days drift from backwater voyages aboard a traditional houseboat to Theyyam performances and cookery lessons with local families. The kitchen garden, village partnerships and solar initiatives quietly sustain the community that shapes this place.

property_title: The Mountbatten Lodge: Colonial Grace in India's Green Hills
property_intro: Set among tea gardens and old-growth forest, The Mountbatten Lodge carries the unhurried elegance of another era without a hint of nostalgia for nostalgia's sake. Rooms are furnished with restored planter's teak, handwoven textiles and books worth lingering over. Days unfold with guided walks to spice groves, birdsong at dawn and dinners drawn from the kitchen garden. The lodge works closely with neighbouring villages, supporting local artisans and native tree planting across the surrounding slopes.

property_title: Destino M\u00edo: Barefoot Luxury on Mexico's Untamed Pacific Coast
property_intro: Set between jungle-clad hills and a wide sweep of Pacific sand, Destino M\u00edo invites you to slow down. Palapa-roofed suites are shaped by local craftsmanship, with hand-carved timber, woven textiles and breezes doing the work of air conditioning. Days unfold with surf lessons, horseback rides along the shore and turtle hatchling releases alongside marine biologists. The kitchen draws on nearby farms and fishing families, while ongoing reforestation quietly restores the coastline you'll come to know as your own.

property_title: Iguana Crossing: Galapagos Shores, Refined Island Living
property_intro: On the seafront in Puerto Villamil, where marine iguanas bask along the boardwalk and flamingos wade in nearby lagoons, Iguana Crossing occupies one of Isabela Island's most beguiling stretches of coast. Interiors of pale wood and volcanic stone frame the Pacific, while the rooftop pool invites long, unhurried afternoons. Days unfold snorkelling with sea turtles, hiking Sierra Negra's crater or joining tortoise conservation work led by naturalists deeply rooted in this remarkable archipelago.

property_title: The Rohet House: Heritage, Horses and Rajasthani Warmth
property_intro: Set beside a lake in rural Rajasthan, The Rohet House is the ancestral home of a family who have welcomed guests for generations, from wandering writers to riders drawn by the estate's celebrated Marwari horses. Frescoed walls, cool courtyards and bougainvillea-shaded terraces frame days spent visiting Bishnoi villages, weavers and potters nearby. Meals draw on recipes passed down through the household, while local employment and craft partnerships keep village traditions purposefully alive.

property_title: Visalam: Art Deco Grandeur in the Heart of Chettinad Country
property_intro: In the quiet village of Kanadukathan, Visalam was built in the 1930s by a merchant father for his daughter, and its Art Deco lines, Athangudi tiled floors and pillared courtyards have been carefully revived rather than reinvented. Days unfold slowly here: cycling past crumbling mansions, learning to temper spices with the resident cooks, or watching tile-makers at work. Staffed largely by villagers, the house sustains the crafts and cuisine that give Chettinad its character.

property_title: Sukoon Houseboat: Serene Days Adrift on Kashmir's Dal Lake
property_intro: Moored on the quieter reaches of Dal Lake, Sukoon is a hand-carved cedar houseboat where Kashmiri craftsmanship meets thoughtful contemporary comfort. Wake to mist lifting from the water, breakfast on deck as shikaras glide past, then drift towards floating gardens or Mughal terraces with local guides. Interiors layer walnut fretwork, papier-mâché detail and crisp linen, while kitchens draw on lake-grown produce. Artisan partnerships and small-scale hosting keep the experience personal and rooted in the valley.

property_title: Jim's Jungle Retreat: Wild Luxury on Corbett's Forest Edge
property_intro: On the fringes of Jim Corbett National Park, where sal forests give way to the Kumaon hills, this Uttarakhand retreat pairs handcrafted cottages and mud-plastered walls with genuine warmth. Days unfold with dawn safaris in search of tigers, guided walks through Kaladhungi's villages, and unhurried afternoons beside the pool. Local families form the heart of the team, while rainwater harvesting and forest regeneration quietly shape everything here. Evenings end around the fire, with the jungle breathing nearby.

property_title: Cabo Serai: Clifftop Tents and Forest Calm Above Goa's Sea
property_intro: Perched on a wooded headland above Cabo de Rama beach in south Goa, Cabo Serai unfolds across twenty acres of cashew and palm. Canvas tents and stone cottages sit lightly among the trees, framing the Arabian Sea below. Days drift between swimming in secluded coves, yoga on the cliff edge and long, unhurried meals of Goan seafood. Solar power, rainwater harvesting and local employment underpin it all, quietly and without fuss.

property_title: Windermere Riverhouse: A Quiet Riverside Retreat in Rural Kerala
property_intro: Set on the banks of a slow-moving Kerala river, Windermere Riverhouse is an intimate family home where days unfold at the pace of the water. Verandahs open to coconut groves, antique wood and local craftsmanship shape the interiors, and meals arrive from the kitchen garden and neighbouring farms. Drift out by canoe, wander village lanes with the household cook, or simply listen to kingfishers. Small in scale, generous in spirit, and firmly rooted in its community.

property_title: Windermere Estate: Cardamom Hills Living Above Munnar's Mist
property_intro: Set on a working cardamom and coffee plantation above Munnar, Windermere Estate looks across the Western Ghats to ridgelines that shift with the light. Rooms are built from local stone and timber, unhurried and quietly comfortable, with verandahs made for long conversations. Days might involve walking the spice trails with a resident naturalist, breakfasting on estate produce, or simply watching hornbills. The family owners employ and train locally, keeping the plantation's rhythms and its birdlife intact.

property_title: Tara Mountain Sarai: Himalayan Calm, Thoughtfully Reimagined
property_intro: Set among terraced fields and deodar forest in the Indian Himalaya, Tara Mountain Sarai is a small mountain retreat where local stone, timber and craft traditions shape every room. Days unfold slowly here: walks to village temples, orchard breakfasts, conversations with the farmers and weavers who supply the kitchen and studio. Snow peaks rise beyond the terrace, while solar power, spring water and hyper-local sourcing keep the footprint light and the welcome genuinely warm.

property_title: Wild Mahseer: Assam's Tea Heritage Beside the Eastern Himalaya
property_intro: Set within a working tea estate at Balipara, where Assam's plains rise towards the Eastern Himalaya, Wild Mahseer gathers four restored planters' bungalows among 22 acres of gardens and native trees. Days unfold with birding walks, tea tastings and journeys into Nameri's forests. Verandas, teak floors and Assamese cuisine speak of unhurried living, while the estate's Botanic Ark safeguards Himalayan flora and supports the surrounding communities who tend it.

property_title: Hotel Mama Cuchara: Colonial Soul in Quito's Storied Old Town
property_intro: Tucked into a lantern-lit corner of Quito's UNESCO-listed old town, Hotel Mama Cuchara occupies a lovingly restored 19th-century house where thick adobe walls, carved timber balconies and Andean textiles set the mood. Mornings begin with Ecuadorian coffee on the rooftop, framed by tiled domes and the slopes of Pichincha. Family-run and deeply rooted in the neighbourhood, it champions local artisans, regional produce and guided walks that reveal the city's chapels, markets and courtyards through resident eyes.

property_title: Entre Cielos Luxury Wine Hotel: Vineyard Serenity in Mendoza
property_intro: Set among eight hectares of Malbec vines in Luj\n de Cuyo, Entre Cielos looks straight to the snow-tipped Andes. Glass-and-steel suites hover above the rows, while a Turkish-inspired hammam invites long, unhurried afternoons. Days here move with the vineyard: pruning alongside the team, tasting single-parcel wines, cycling irrigation lanes. The kitchen leans on Mendoza's growers, and the estate farms sustainably, protecting the water and soils that give this high-desert corner its character.

property_title: Brij Lakshman Sagar: Where Rajasthan's Wilderness Slows Time
property_intro: Tucked into the scrubland of Rajasthan's Churu district, Brij Lakshman Sagar gathers just twelve earthen cottages along a rocky ridge above a private lake. Designed by Aman Nath, the mud-and-thatch kohras honour Shekhawati building traditions, with stone walls, open verandahs and plunge pools framing sunsets over the water. Days unfold with birdwatching, village walks and lantern-lit dinners under acacias. Local artisans and farmers shape the kitchen and craft here, keeping rural livelihoods thriving alongside the landscape.

property_title: Purity at Lake Vembanad: Slow, Serene Days on Kerala's Backwaters
property_intro:
On the palm-fringed shore of Kerala's largest lake, Purity holds just fourteen rooms 
filled with light, antique teak and locally woven textiles. Mornings begin with birdsong from the neighbouring paddy fields; afternoons drift by on a converted rice barge or an Ayurvedic treatment table. Fishermen still cast Chinese nets beyond the garden, and the kitchen buys its catch and coconuts from village neighbours \u2014 a quiet, considered kind of luxury that leaves Vembanad exactly as it found it.

property_title: Farmhouse Rwanda: Unhurried Days Among Tea Hills and Volcanoes
property_intro: Set among the emerald folds of Rwanda's countryside, Farmhouse Rwanda is a working farm and retreat where volcano views meet mornings scented with coffee and woodsmoke. Interiors pair handwoven Rwandan craft with quiet comfort, while days unfold through garden-to-table feasts, cycling on red-earth lanes, beekeeping and visits with neighbouring cooperatives. Much of what you eat is grown metres from your plate, and local families share in the farm's success. Come for stillness; leave with genuine connection.

property_title: Svatma Thanjavur: Where Tamil Heritage, Music and Devotion Meet
property_intro: In the temple town of Thanjavur, within walking distance of the Brihadeeswarar Temple, Svatma unfolds across a restored century-old family home and a contemporary wing. Antique Chettinad woodwork, Tanjore paintings and handwoven cottons speak of a region's artistry, while mornings begin with Carnatic music and yoga on the terrace. Guests dine on heirloom Tamil vegetarian recipes, visit bronze-casting workshops and meet local artisans whose crafts the hotel actively supports and helps sustain.

property_title: The Grand Dragon: Ladakh Warmth Amid Himalayan Horizons
property_intro: Set in the heart of Leh, The Grand Dragon rises against the ochre folds of the Ladakhi range, a family-run retreat where Himalayan hospitality feels genuinely lived rather than performed. Rooms frame views of Stok Kangri, while interiors draw on local craft, thangka artistry and hand-carved wood. Guests wake to apricot orchards and monastery bells, journey to Nubra and Pangong with local guides, and dine on Ladakhi recipes sourced from nearby villages and mountain farms.

property_title: Reni Pani Jungle Lodge: Wild Encounters in Satpura's Heart
property_intro: On the fringes of Satpura National Park in Madhya Pradesh, Reni Pani sits among teak and mahua trees beside a seasonal stream, where leopards pass in the night and birdsong marks the hours. Twelve stone-and-canvas cottages open to the forest, while walking safaris, canoe trips along the Denwa and canopy-level hides reveal a landscape few travellers reach. The lodge trains local naturalists and supports neighbouring villages, ensuring the wilderness thrives long after you've gone.

property_title: Rann Riders: Wild Encounters on Gujarat's Salt-Flat Frontier
property_intro: On the fringes of the Little Rann of Kutch, Rann Riders sits amid marshland and salt desert where wild asses roam and flamingos gather in their thousands. Cottages draw on the region's mud-and-thatch vernacular, with Kathiawari horses stabled nearby for rides across open country. Days unfold with jeep safaris, birdwatching at Nal Sarovar and visits to Rabari and Bharwad artisan villages, where weaving and embroidery traditions remain part of everyday life rather than performance.

property_title: The Bentwood Inn: Handcrafted Warmth in Wyoming's Wild Heart
property_intro: Set among lodgepole pines on three quiet acres near Jackson Hole, The Bentwood Inn was built from century-old timber salvaged after the Yellowstone fires. Five individually designed suites gather around a soaring stone hearth, where mornings begin with a chef-prepared breakfast and evenings unwind over local wines. The Tetons rise minutes away, with the Snake River, elk refuge and world-class skiing close by. It is an intimate, owner-run retreat that treats craftsmanship and place with genuine care.

property_title: Bio Habitat Hotel: Cloud Forest Serenity in Colombia's Andes
property_intro: Tucked into the green folds of Quind textstyle deep in Colombia's coffee country, Bio Habitat Hotel rises among towering guadua bamboo and mist-fed forest near Armenia. Suites of glass and native timber open onto birdsong and canopy views, while the spa, thermal waters and slow, produce-led dining invite you to linger. Guided walks reveal reforested trails and orchid-rich reserves, and local artisans and growers shape much of what you taste, touch and take home.

property_title: Hotel Otavalo: Andean Heritage, Colour and Craft in Ecuador
property_intro: In the heart of Otavalo, a town known across the Andes for its weavers and Saturday market, this restored colonial house opens onto flower-filled courtyards and mountain light. Rooms layer handwoven textiles and local timber with quiet comfort, while the kitchen draws on highland produce and Kichwa recipes. Days might begin with a market stroll, continue among the crater lakes of Cuicocha, and end beside a fire, listening to stories from the artisan families who shape the hotel's character.

property_title: Tilar Siro: Quiet Luxury Amid Ziro Valley's Pine and Paddies
property_intro: Tucked into Arunachal Pradesh's Ziro Valley, Tilar Siro sits among bamboo groves, pine ridges and the terraced rice fields tended by the Apatani for generations. Rooms of local timber and stone open onto mist and birdsong, while days unfold with village walks, shaman storytelling, foraged meals and slow mornings over Ziro-grown coffee. Built with community hands and guided by Apatani custom, it offers a rare, unhurried welcome into one of India's least-travelled corners.

property_title: ABN Charaidew II: Sail the Brahmaputra Through Wild Assam
property_intro: Drifting along the vast Brahmaputra, ABN Charaidew II carries just a handful of guests through Assam's shifting sandbanks, river islands and tea country. Cabins open onto wide waters, while evenings bring stories on deck beneath an unpolluted sky. Days are spent tracking rhino in Kaziranga, visiting weavers and Vaishnavite monasteries on Majuli, and meeting communities whose lives follow the river's moods. Crewed largely by local hands, this is Assam encountered gently, at the water's own pace.

property_title: Casino Hotel: Kochi's Harbourside Retreat on Willingdon Island
property_intro: Set on Willingdon Island, where cargo ships drift past coconut palms, Casino Hotel has been quietly shaping Kochi's hospitality story for decades. Rooms open onto gardens and a palm-fringed pool, while Fort Cochin restaurant serves the day's catch, chosen from ice and cooked to Kerala recipes. As part of CGH Earth, the hotel champions local sourcing, thoughtful waste practices and community livelihoods, making it an easy base for exploring Fort Kochi's spice lanes and backwaters.

property_title: Aashraya on the Ganga: Riverside Serenity in the Himalayas
property_intro: Set on the banks of the Ganga as it leaves the Himalayan foothills, Aashraya offers a gentler rhythm of days: river swims, forest walks and evenings spent listening to the water. Interiors favour local stone, timber and handloom textiles, crafted with village artisans whose skills the house helps sustain. Meals draw on Garhwali kitchen gardens, while guides from nearby hamlets share trails, temples and birdlife known only to those who live here.

property_title: La Urumpta Hotel: Quiet Luxury Among Argentina's Red Ravines
property_intro: Tucked into the ochre folds of the Quebrada de Humahuaca in Argentina's far north, La Urumpta gathers adobe walls, cactus wood and handwoven textiles around courtyards framed by mountains that shift colour through the day. Days here unfold slowly: high-altitude vineyards, Andean village markets, star-filled skies and cooking rooted in quinoa, llama and local herbs. Built with regional artisans and materials, the hotel supports Quebrada communities while offering a considered, deeply grounded retreat.

property_title: Basecamp Dorobo Mobile: Follow the Wild Through the Mara
property_intro: Basecamp Dorobo Mobile moves with the seasons across the Maasai Mara's lesser-trodden reaches, pitching camp where wildlife gathers and few vehicles venture. Canvas tents are quietly considered, with bucket showers, hand-crafted furnishings and lantern-lit dinners beneath acacias. Days unfold on foot with Maasai guides who read tracks and tell stories passed down generations. Run in partnership with local landowners, the camp channels revenue into conservancy leases, leaving nothing behind but flattened grass.

property_title: Saruni Samburu: Wild Horizons Above Kenya's Northern Frontier
property_intro: Perched high on a rocky escarpment within Kalama Conservancy, Saruni Samburu surveys a vast sweep of northern Kenya, with Mount Kenya shimmering on the horizon. Six open-fronted villas of local stone and timber frame elephant trails and starlit skies. Days unfold alongside Samburu guides, tracking wild dog, walking the hills, then retreating to a spa suspended above the valley. Run in partnership with the community, your stay supports Kalama's families and its returning wildlife.

property_title: Algodón Mansión: Belle Époque Charm in Buenos Aires' Recoleta
property_intro: Set on a quiet, tree-lined street in Recoleta, Algodón Mansión occupies a restored Belle Époque residence where marble staircases and Art Nouveau detail meet contemporary comfort. Ten generous suites open onto a leafy courtyard, while the rooftop terrace and spa invite slow afternoons between gallery visits and tango. Wines poured here come from the family's own Mendoza estate, where vineyards are farmed with care for soil, water and the surrounding community.

property_title: Basecamp Mara Houses: Private Comfort on Kenya's Wild Edge
property_intro: On the fringes of the Maasai Mara, where acacia shade meets open grassland, Basecamp Mara Houses offers private villas designed for slow, unhurried days. Solar power, local craftsmanship and Maasai-led guiding shape the experience, from dawn game drives to walks with guides who read the land as easily as a map. Your stay supports the Naboisho Conservancy and a girls' school nearby, so time here quietly extends beyond your own horizon.

property_title: Saruni Rhino: Track Black Rhino on Foot in Wild Sera, Kenya
property_intro: Tucked into the boulder-strewn hills of Sera Conservancy in Kenya's northern frontier, Saruni Rhino comprises just three open-fronted bandas built from local stone beside a seasonal riverbed. This is the only place in East Africa where you can track black rhino on foot, guided by Samburu warriors whose community owns and protects the land. Days unfold with walking safaris, starlit dinners and the quiet knowledge that your stay directly sustains one of conservation's most remarkable comebacks.

property_title: Nadis Hotel: Refined Calm and Warm Welcomes in Rural India
property_intro: Set amid India's quiet countryside, Nadis Hotel invites you to slow your pace and settle into a rhythm shaped by the land around it. Interiors pair locally crafted textiles and timber with uncluttered comfort, while days unfold through village walks, regional cooking with local families and long, unhurried evenings under open skies. Water is carefully conserved, produce sourced from nearby farms, and much of the team hails from surrounding communities — hospitality with genuine roots.

property_title: Get Hotel Molvento: Refined Argentine Calm Beneath the Andes
property_intro: Set within Argentina's wide, wind-brushed landscapes, Get Hotel Molvento invites you to slow your pace and settle into something quietly considered. Interiors pair local stone, warm timber and handwoven textiles, made by craftspeople from nearby villages. Days unfold with vineyard tastings, high-country rides and long lunches shaped by regional producers. Native planting and careful water stewardship shape the grounds, while guest stays support neighbouring schools t, and dinner is always worth lingering over beneath a sky thick with stars.

property_title: Basecamp Hill Top: Elevated Calm Above the Maasai Mara
property_intro: Perched on a rise above the Talek River, Basecamp Hill Top looks out across the Maasai Mara's open plains, where wildebeest columns and lion prides move with the seasons. Just six hillside suites, built from local timber and natural stone, offer privacy and quiet indulgence. Days unfold with guided game drives, walks alongside Maasai naturalists and visits to community-run enterprises, while the lodge's long-standing reforestation and women's beadwork initiatives give every stay lasting meaning.

property_title: Chitoor Kottaram: Kerala's Riverside Palace Kept for One Guest
property_intro: Reached by boat along a quiet stretch of Kerala's backwaters, Chitoor Kottaram was once the retreat of the Cochin royal family, and today it welcomes a single party at a time. Two rooms, a temple next door, palm trees leaning over the water, and a cook who prepares whatever you fancy from the day's catch. Days pass with canoe trips, village walks and long hours on the veranda. Lovingly restored, staffed by neighbours, and gloriously unhurried.

property_title: Quiet by the River: Slow Living on India's Gentle Waters
property_intro: Set along a slow bend of the river, Quiet by the River invites you to trade schedules for birdsong. Handcrafted interiors draw on local stone, lime plaster and village weaving traditions, while wide verandahs open to water, farmland and the shifting light of the day. Drift out at dawn with a fisherman, forage with the kitchen team, or simply read. Guests support riverbank restoration and livelihoods for neighbouring artisan families.

property_title: Brij Bageecha: An Orchard Hideaway Beyond Jaipur's Ramparts
property_intro: A short drive from Jaipur's palaces, Brij Bageecha unfolds across fruit orchards and flowering gardens where peacocks outnumber passing cars. Fourteen thatched villas, built in local stone and lime plaster by Rajasthani artisans, open onto private verandahs and pockets of shade. Days drift between organic farm breakfasts, pottery with village craftspeople, cycle rides through mustard fields and long, unhurried evenings under the stars. Traditional building crafts and neighbouring livelihoods are quietly sustained here.

property_title: Sawantwadi Palace: Royal Heritage in Coastal Konkan, India
property_intro:
Set between the Sahyadri hills and the Konkan coast, Sawantwadi Palace remains the residence of the region's royal family, welcoming guests into rooms hung with hand-painted Ganjifa cards. The craft, once near-extinct, is revived here in workshops where artisans paint alongside visitors. Days unfold with lacquerware demonstrations, temple walks and mango orchards heavy with Alphonso fruit, while evenings bring Malvani cooking drawn from family recipes. A living palace, not a preserved relic 
invites you to linger.

property_title: Travesia Atacama-Uyuni: A Journey Across Bolivia's High Desert
property_intro: Crossing from the Atacama into Bolivia's Altiplano, Travesia Atacama-Uyuni unfolds as a slow expedition through lagoons stained red with algae, geyser fields and the mirrored expanse of the Salar de Uyuni. Nights are spent in considered, low-impact camps and characterful lodges, warmed by woven textiles and Andean hospitality. Local guides share the language of the land, while partnerships with Quechua and Aymara communities ensure your passage leaves something meaningful behind.

property_title: Wellcomm Spa & Hotel: Colombian Calm in the Coffee Highlands
property_intro: Tucked into Colombia's green Andean folds, Wellcomm Spa & Hotel invites you to slow down where mountain air meets the scent of roasting coffee. Days unfold gently here: thermal-inspired treatments, unhurried breakfasts of estate-grown beans, and walks through gardens alive with hummingbirds. Interiors pair local timber and stone with quiet contemporary lines, while partnerships with neighbouring growers and artisans keep the surrounding community at the heart of every stay. Restorative, grounded and genuinely Colombian.

property_title: Saruni Wild: Untamed Seclusion on the Edge of the Mara Plains
property_intro: Tucked into a quiet corner of the Mara North Conservancy, Saruni Wild is a intimate camp of just three tents, shared with no one but the plains game drifting past at dawn. Days unfold with Maasai guides tracking lion across open grassland, bush breakfasts and walks through country few travellers ever see. Canvas interiors feel unfussy and considered, while conservancy leases and local employment keep this wilderness in Maasai hands.

property_title: Kila Dalijoda: Royal Forest Living on Odisha's Wild Frontier
property_intro: Set within the sal forests of Athagarh in Odisha, Kila Dalijoda is the century-old hunting lodge of a princely family, still kept much as it was. Verandahs open onto elephant country, the Mahanadi runs nearby, and days unfold with guided forest walks, birdwatching and slow meals of Odia home cooking. Family portraits and hand-me-down furniture tell their own stories, while conservation work and village partnerships quietly sustain the woodland that surrounds you.

property_title: Soulitude by the Riverside: Slow Days Beside a Kumaoni River
property_intro: Tucked into a fold of the Kumaon hills, Soulitude by the Riverside sits where a clear mountain stream curves past terraced fields and oak forest. Days unfold gently here: river swims, guided walks to hidden waterfalls, birdsong at breakfast and long conversations under the stars. Rooms are quietly considered, built with local stone and craftsmanship, while village partnerships and thoughtful sourcing keep the valley's rhythms intact. Come for the silence; leave a little lighter.

property_title: Eighth Bastion: Colonial Charm in the Heart of Fort Kochi, Kerala
property_intro: Tucked into Fort Kochi's lattice of spice lanes and sun-bleached churches, Eighth Bastion takes its name from the Dutch fortification that once stood here. Interiors nod to the quarter's layered past, with rattan, dark timber and cool courtyards inviting slow afternoons. Wander to the fishing nets at dusk, join a Kathakali performance, or let the kitchen introduce you to Kerala's Anglo-Dutch flavours. Part of CGH Earth, it champions local artisans, producers and gentle tourism.

property_title: Beach Gate Bungalows: Barefoot Coastal Living in Rural India
property_intro: Set where palm groves give way to soft sand, Beach Gate Bungalows offers a gentler rhythm along India's shoreline. Handcrafted cottages, shaped by local artisans from timber, thatch and lime, open onto sea breezes and birdsong. Days unfold with dawn swims, fishermen hauling in their catch, and slow suppers of coconut curry and fresh-caught seafood. The owners work closely with neighbouring villages, supporting turtle nesting sites and coastal planting, so your stay leaves the shore a little richer.

property_title: Basecamp Masai Mara: Riverside Living at the Heart of the Wild
property_intro: On the banks of the Talek River, where the Maasai Mara's plains begin, Basecamp Masai Mara offers a gentler way to meet Kenya's most storied wilderness. Sixteen hand-built tents sit among indigenous trees planted by the lodge itself, shaded and softly lit. Days unfold with Maasai guides who read the grasslands like family history, walking safaris at dawn, and visits to the women's beadwork cooperative that channels earnings directly into local schools and land conservancies.

property_title: M.V. Rudra Singha II: Unhurried Journeys on the Mighty Brahmaputra
property_intro: Drifting through Assam aboard the M.V. Rudra Singha II, days unfold at the pace of the river itself. Handcrafted teak cabins open onto shifting views of sandbars, silk-weaving villages and the grasslands of Kaziranga, where rhinos graze at dawn. Guided walks, tea-garden visits and river dolphin sightings are led by local naturalists, while much of the crew and produce come from communities along the banks. Evenings bring Assamese cooking, birdsong and remarkably wide skies.

property_title: Villa Beluno: Andean Serenity Amid Argentina's Vineyards
property_intro: Set against the snow-touched Andes, Villa Beluno rests among Argentina's vineyards, where mornings begin with birdsong and end with Malbec poured at sunset. Interiors pair local stone, handwoven textiles and warm timber, crafted by artisans from nearby villages. Guests ride into the foothills, harvest alongside growers, or simply drift in the pool as poplars sway. Water is carefully conserved, produce grown on site, and a share of every stay supports the surrounding community's schools.

property_title: Desert Lodge: Where Namibia's Ancient Silence Becomes Luxury
property_intro: Set among weathered granite outcrops on the edge of the Namib, Desert Lodge invites you into one of the world's oldest landscapes. Stone-and-glass suites frame apricot dunes and star-drenched skies, while sundowners on the escarpment reveal oryx tracing the plains below. Days unfold with guided desert walks, dawn drives and conversations with local guides whose families have read these sands for generations. Solar power, careful water stewardship and community partnerships keep this remarkable wilderness intact.

property_title: Saruni Mara: Six Secluded Cottages in Mara North Conservancy
property_intro: Tucked into a wooded valley within the Mara North Conservancy, Saruni Mara holds just six cottages, each hidden among ancient trees where colobus monkeys move through the canopy. Days unfold with Maasai guides who read the grasslands like a familiar page, followed by long lunches and the quiet of the Maasai Wellbeing Space. Interiors blend vintage safari character with warmth, while conservancy leases and local employment keep this wilderness intact for the communities who call it home.

property_title: Ramathra Fort: Rajasthan's Wild Heart, Lived Slowly and Well
property_intro: Rising above the Chambal valley in eastern Rajasthan, this 17th-century fort remains the home of the family who have kept it for ten generations. Just ten rooms and tents sit within its ramparts, looking out over farmland, lakes and ravines rarely reached by visitors. Days unfold with boat safaris among gharials, walks to village temples and dinners beneath the stars. Restoration here has been patient and local, with hospitality that sustains the surrounding community.

property_title: Lchang Nang Retreat: The House of Trees in Nubra Valley, Ladakh
property_intro: Tucked into the apricot orchards of Sumur, deep in Ladakh's Nubra Valley, Lchang Nang Retreat takes its name from the whispering poplars that shade its grounds. Willow-framed cottages, warmed by earthen tones and local craftsmanship, look out to the Karakoram's snow-scored ridges. Days unfold gently here: garden-grown meals, village walks, monastery visits and encounters with Bactrian camels on the dunes. Run with Ladakhi hands and hearts, it offers quiet luxury rooted firmly in place.

property_title: Haveli Dharampura: A Restored Jewel in Old Delhi's Heart
property_intro: Tucked within the lanes of Shahjahanabad, a short walk from the Jama Masjid, Haveli Dharampura is a lovingly revived 19th-century mansion rescued from ruin over six painstaking years. Carved sandstone arches, jharokha balconies and hand-laid stone floors frame just thirteen rooms. Days unfold with kathak recitals in the courtyard, rooftop dinners overlooking minarets, and heritage walks led by local guides. The restoration has spurred neighbourhood pride, employment and renewed interest in Old Delhi's craft traditions.

property_title: Ging Tea House: Darjeeling Heritage Amid Himalayan Tea Slopes
property_intro: Set within a working tea estate on the slopes below Darjeeling, Ging Tea House occupies a lovingly restored planter's bungalow where colonial-era timber, open fireplaces and Kanchenjunga views set the tone. Days unfold with garden walks among the bushes, tastings guided by those who pluck and process the leaf, and unhurried conversations over Himalayan cuisine. The estate supports its plucking community and traditional methods, making each cup here feel genuinely rooted in place.

property_name: The Legacy Mandawa by The Machan
property_title: The Legacy Mandawa by The Machan: Shekhawati's Painted Soul
property_intro: In the heart of Rajasthan's Shekhawati region, where frescoed havelis line sun-warmed lanes, The Legacy Mandawa by The Machan offers a graceful pause. Restored courtyards, hand-painted arches and lantern-lit terraces echo the artistry of a merchant past, while local guides lead you through Mandawa's open-air gallery of murals. Meals draw on regional recipes and nearby farms, and artisan partnerships help sustain crafts that shaped these walls. Evenings unfold slowly, beneath a sky thick with desert stars.

property_title: Orchard Mornings and Mountain Light at The Apricot Tree Hotel
property_intro: Set among fruit orchards in the village of Nimmu, where the Indus and Zanskar rivers meet, The Apricot Tree Hotel offers a gentler way to know Ladakh. Rooms are built in local stone and timber, warmed by sunlight and Ladakhi textiles. Days unfold with river rafting, monastery walks and home-style meals made from village produce. Staffed and supplied largely by neighbours, the hotel keeps its earnings, and its stories, close to home.

property_title: ABN Rajmahal: Drifting Through Bengal's Timeless Ganges Bends
property_intro: Handcrafted in Kolkata and styled with colonial-era restraint, ABN Rajmahal carries just a handful of guests along the lower Ganges. Days unfold slowly: terracotta temples at Kalna, silk weavers at Matiari, mustard fields and mangoes glimpsed from the sundeck. Ashore, small-group walks bring you into village kitchens and workshops, with fees shared locally. Onboard, Bengali cooking, cool cotton interiors and river breezes replace the noise of the road, and evenings end beneath an unhurried sky.

property_title: The Rajbari Bawali: Bengal's Reawakened Grandeur Near Kolkata
property_intro: An hour south of Kolkata, beyond fish ponds and paddy fields, a 300-year-old zamindar mansion rises from the village of Bawali. Rescued from ruin over a decade of painstaking restoration, its colonnaded courtyards, frescoed halls and antique-filled suites now welcome guests with quiet ceremony. Drift along the Hooghly by country boat, learn Bengali kitchen secrets, or wander lanes where local artisans and craftspeople share in the estate's revival. Evenings belong to candlelight and courtyard silence.

property_title: Nimali Tarangire: Wild Elegance Beside Tanzania's Elephants
property_intro: Set on a private concession bordering Tarangire National Park, Nimali Tarangire looks out over the seasonal riverbed where elephant herds gather beneath ancient baobabs. Ten tented suites blend handcrafted Tanzanian materials with a light, contemporary touch, each opening to uninterrupted bush views. Days unfold through guided walks, night drives and unhurried game viewing with expert local guides, while the camp's solar power and partnerships with neighbouring Maasai communities ensure your stay leaves something meaningful behind.

property_title: The Nanee: A Refined Retreat in Nepal's Living Hillsides
property_intro: Tucked into the terraced hills beyond Kathmandu's clamour, The Nanee gathers Himalayan views, birdsong and slow mornings into something quietly extraordinary. Handcrafted interiors draw on Newari craftsmanship, with local stone, timber and textiles woven by neighbouring artisans. Days unfold with guided walks through farming villages, seasonal cooking rooted in the estate's own harvest, and evenings spent watching light shift across distant peaks. A share of every stay supports village schooling and reforestation, making your visit part of the landscape's future.

property_title: Nimmu House: A Restored Ladakhi Manor Amid the Apricot Orchards
property_intro: Set in a quiet village between the Indus and Zanskar rivers, Nimmu House is a nineteenth-century Ladakhi residence brought gently back to life by its custodians. Whitewashed walls, timber ceilings and apricot orchards frame days spent trekking to cliffside monasteries, cycling mountain passes or learning to cook thukpa with local families. Solar power, spring water and village employment underpin it all, while starlit dinners in the garden linger long after departure.

property_title: Laalee: A Quiet Indian Retreat Woven from Land and Craft
property_intro: Set within India's slow, unhurried countryside, Laalee gathers guests into a home shaped by local hands \u block-printed textiles, lime-washed walls and courtyards that catch the last of the afternoon light. Days unfold gently here: village walks, kitchen sessions with regional recipes, evenings under an unpolluted sky. Artisans and neighbouring families share in its story, and much of what you eat is grown nearby. It is a place that rewards curiosity and lingering, rather than rushing on.

property_title: Anvil Hotel & Cache House: A Refined Basecamp in Jackson Hole
property_intro: Just two blocks from Jackson's antler-arched town square, Anvil Hotel sits within easy reach of Grand Teton's peaks and the elk-dotted valley beyond. Interiors nod to the American West with Chimayo weavings, leather and locally made furnishings, while the subterranean Cache House offers bunk-style rooms for those travelling light. Days unfold on the trails or slopes; evenings belong to Glorietta's wood-fired Italian plates and conversations with guides, artists and locals who call this valley home.

property_title: Huffman Creek Retreat: Wild Waters, Woodland Calm and Warm Welcome
property_intro: Tucked along a spring-fed creek where hardwood forest meets open meadow, Huffman Creek Retreat invites you to slow to the rhythm of moving water. Interiors pair honest timber and local craftsmanship with deep baths and long views, while days unfold through guided walks, foraging, fireside suppers and swimming holes shaded by sycamores. Native planting and careful land stewardship keep the watershed thriving, and neighbouring growers and makers shape much of what reaches your table.

property_title: Dunya Camp: Refined Desert Living Beneath American Skies
property_intro: Set within a wide sweep of high desert, Dunya Camp gathers a handful of canvas pavilions among juniper, sage and weathered rock. Interiors marry handwoven textiles with locally milled timber, while evenings turn to firelight, long tables and star-charting with resident guides. Days may bring horseback trails, guided walks with Indigenous storytellers, or simply the quiet of a shaded terrace. Solar power, harvested rainwater and partnerships with nearby ranching families keep this landscape thriving.

property_title: Onera: Sleep Beneath Texas Hill Country Stars in Glass Houses
property_intro: Tucked into the oaks and limestone ridges just beyond Fredericksburg, Onera is a collection of glass-walled retreats where the Texas Hill Country becomes part of the architecture. Wake to birdsong, soak in a copper tub under open sky, and watch constellations drift above your bed. Each house is thoughtfully built to sit lightly on the land, with native planting and dark-sky principles honoured throughout. Nearby vineyards, wildflower meadows and trails invite unhurried days.

property_title: Terramor Outdoor Resort: Refined Wilderness Beside Acadia
property_intro: Tucked within Maine's coastal woodland near Bar Harbor, Terramor Outdoor Resort places you moments from Acadia National Park yet deep among spruce and birch. Sixty-four canvas tents, each individually styled with artisan touches, come with wood-burning stoves, en suite bathrooms and private decks for evenings beneath uncommonly dark skies. Days might involve foraging walks, guided paddles or oyster tastings led by local makers, while low-impact design and Leave No Trace principles keep the surrounding forest quietly thriving.

property_title: The Alpine House: Mountain Warmth in the Heart of Jackson Hole
property_intro: Tucked into Jackson's walkable core, with the Tetons rising just beyond, The Alpine House was founded by two former Olympic skiers who understood exactly what a day in the mountains asks of you. Scandinavian-inspired interiors, timber warmth and a wood-fired sauna set the tone, while breakfast leans on Wyoming producers. Guests wander to galleries and trailheads, then return to fireside evenings. Conservation runs deep here, with support for the wildlife corridors that make this valley extraordinary.

property_title: The Bygone: Jazz Age Elegance High Above Baltimore's Harbour
property_intro: Perched on the upper floors of a Harbor East tower, The Bygone looks out over Baltimore's shifting waterfront and the Chesapeake beyond. Interiors nod to the 1920s with velvet, brass and works by Maryland artists, while the rooftop restaurant serves regional seafood sourced from local watermen. Days might begin with a stroll through Fell's Point's cobbled lanes and end with cocktails as the harbour lights flicker on below.

property_title: Résidence de l'Evêché: Heritage Calm in French Pondicherry
property_intro: Tucked into the quiet lanes of Puducherry's French Quarter, a few steps from the seafront promenade, this restored 19th-century bishop's residence pairs high-ceilinged rooms with bougainvillea-draped courtyards. Lime-plastered walls, antique teak and hand-glazed Athangudi tiles reflect careful conservation work with local craftspeople. Wake to filter coffee under the colonnade, wander to temple markets and Tamil-Creole kitchens, cycle towards Auroville, then return for evenings scented with frangipani. Refined, unhurried and quietly rooted in its neighbourhood.

property_title: Sitla Estate: Himalayan Orchards, Firesides and Slow Days
property_intro: Tucked into a working fruit orchard in Kumaon's Mukteshwar hills, Sitla Estate looks out to a horizon of snow-clad Himalayan peaks. Four generations of family life shape this colonial-era home, where log fires, hand-me-down furniture and home-grown produce set an unhurried rhythm. Walk through oak and rhododendron forest with resident naturalists, visit village weavers and orchardists, or simply read on the lawn. Conservation of the surrounding woodland and support for local livelihoods remain central to daily life here.

property_title: Mantra Koodam: Timeless Heritage in Kumbakonam's Temple Land
property_intro: Set among paddy fields and coconut groves in the Cauvery delta, Mantra Koodam gathers restored Chettinad-style homes into a village of shaded courtyards and cool verandahs. Kumbakonam's ancient temples and bronze-casting workshops lie moments away, while within, Ayurvedic therapies, silk-weaving demonstrations and slow Tamil cooking fill unhurried days. Timber, terracotta and lime plaster salvaged from vanishing mansions give each room its character, and local artisans and farmers remain part of everyday life here.

property_title: Palais de Mahe: Colonial Grace in Puducherry's French Quarter
property_intro: Tucked into a quiet lane of Puducherry's French Quarter, Palais de Mahe blends Franco-Tamil craftsmanship with the ease of coastal living. Louvred shutters, antique furnishings and a courtyard pool set the rhythm of the day, while the rooftop restaurant looks across terracotta roofs to the Bay of Bengal. Wander to the promenade at dawn, join a Creole cooking session, or explore heritage streets with guides who know their stories. Local artisans and produce shape every detail here.

property_title: Isla's Ridge: Highland Calm Above India's Misted Valleys
property_intro: Perched along a forested ridge where morning mist gathers in the valleys below, Isla's Ridge invites you to slow down. Interiors pair locally quarried stone with handwoven textiles from nearby villages, while wide verandas open onto birdsong and tea-scented air. Walk ancient footpaths with resident naturalists, forage with the kitchen team, or simply read as the light shifts. A share of every stay supports the surrounding community's forest regeneration and schooling initiatives.

property_title: Bandhavgarh Jungle Lodge: Where Tiger Country Feels Like Home
property_intro: On the fringes of Bandhavgarh's sal forests in Madhya Pradesh, this unhurried lodge sits among mahua trees and birdsong, moments from one of India's richest tiger habitats. Earth-toned cottages, locally crafted furnishings and wide verandas invite slow mornings between safaris, while naturalist-led drives, village walks and forest breakfasts deepen the connection. The kitchen draws on nearby farms, and the team is largely from surrounding communities, sharing an inherited knowledge of these woods and their wildlife.

property_title: Pepper Trail: A Rainforest Retreat in Wayanad's Green Heart
property_intro: Tucked into a working spice plantation on the fringes of Wayanad's rainforest, Pepper Trail invites you to slow down among vine-laced pepper groves and century-old planters' bungalows. Restored with heritage timber, cool stone floors and wide verandahs, each home opens onto birdsong and mist-softened hills. Wander guided plantation walks, forage for cardamom, or dine on Malabar recipes shaped by local growers. Conservation of native forest and long-standing village partnerships remain quietly at the heart of every stay.

property_title: Outbound Mammoth: Alpine Escapes Beneath the Eastern Sierra
property_intro: Tucked among Jeffrey pines on the edge of Mammoth Lakes, Outbound Mammoth pairs the ease of a mountain lodge with the intimacy of a private cabin. Days begin with coffee by the fire pit and end beneath some of California's darkest skies, with ski slopes, hot springs and Yosemite's high country within reach. Interiors are warm and unfussy, crafted with local makers in mind, while thoughtful stewardship keeps this Eastern Sierra landscape thriving for years ahead.

property_title: The Virginian Lodge: Jackson Hole's Warm Western Welcome
property_intro:
Set along West Broadway in Jackson, Wyoming, The Virginian Lodge places you minutes from Town Square and within easy reach of Grand Teton and Yellowstone. Behind its classic Western frontage lies a genuinely convivial retreat: timber-warmed rooms, an outdoor pool and hot tub, and a saloon where wranglers, skiers and climbers swap tales. Days begin with mountain air and end beside the fire, with local guides, outfitters and family-run kitchens shaping every encounter.

property_title: Mountain Lodges of Peru: Andean Trails, Warmth at Altitude
property_intro: Strung along the routes to Machu Picchu and the Salkantay and Lares valleys, Mountain Lodges of Peru offers a rare kind of trek: days spent crossing high passes and cloud forest, evenings beside a fire with a hot shower, a jacuzzi and a chef's dinner waiting. The lodges are built with local stone and timber, staffed by Quechua neighbours, and support Andean schools, weaving cooperatives and reforestation across the communities they pass through.

property_title: Getaways, India: Quiet Luxury Rooted in Land and Community
property_intro: Set within India's shifting landscapes, Getaways invites you to slow down and settle into a rhythm shaped by the land itself. Interiors draw on regional craft traditions, with locally sourced timber, handwoven textiles and artisans' work at every turn. Days might unfold with guided walks through native forest, conversations with village weavers, or long evenings beneath uninterrupted skies. Conservation partnerships and local employment underpin it all, so your stay leaves something meaningful behind.

property_title: Cranganor History Café & Riverside Château: Kerala's Living Past
property_intro: On the banks of Kerala's Periyar, where Roman, Arab and Chinese traders once bartered for pepper, this riverside château revives the spirit of ancient Muziris. Antique maps, curated libraries and a history café invite slow afternoons, while heritage-inspired interiors nod to the coast's layered past. Drift past coconut groves by boat, taste dishes rooted in local produce, and meet artisans whose crafts are quietly sustained here. A stay for those who travel with curiosity.

property_title: Callicoon Hills: Catskills Charm Reimagined in the Hudson Valley
property_intro: Set across 65 wooded acres in New York's Sullivan County Catskills, Callicoon Hills revives a beloved mid-century retreat with quiet confidence. Timber cabins and lodge rooms are dressed in warm woods, local artistry and vintage finds, while trails, spring-fed swimming and firepit evenings shape unhurried days. The kitchen leans on Hudson Valley farms and the neighbouring Delaware River rewards anglers and paddlers alike. Restored rather than rebuilt, it's a place where craftsmanship and community feel genuinely intertwined.

property_title: Camp Comfort: Refined Wilderness Living in the American West
property_intro: Tucked among towering pines and open meadows, Camp Comfort reimagines the great American camp for those who value quiet luxury. Canvas-clad suites reveal handcrafted furnishings, wood-burning stoves and deep soaking tubs, while days unfold with guided hikes, fly-fishing and long dinners built around regional produce. The land is tended in partnership with local conservationists, and neighbouring artisans shape much of what you'll touch and taste. Come evening, the fire is lit and the stars do the rest.

property_title: Marli Hill Bungalow: Highland Calm Among India's Tea Slopes
property_intro: Set among mist-softened tea slopes, Marli Hill Bungalow is a restored planter's residence where wood floors creak companionably and log fires take the chill off highland evenings. Days unfold with estate walks, tastings led by growers who have tended these bushes for generations, and long lunches drawn from the kitchen garden. Native trees are being returned to the surrounding hillsides, and local families share both the work and the rewards. Come for the quiet; stay for the conversations.

property_title: Lockhart Bungalow: A Tea Planter's Retreat in the Blue Nilgiris
property_intro: High in the Nilgiris, where mist drifts through Coonoor's tea gardens, Lockhart Bungalow opens its verandah to sweeping views and unhurried days. Once a planter's home, it retains its polished teak, log fires and generous garden, now paired with quietly considered comfort. Walk the plucking paths with estate families, taste single-estate leaf at the factory, or simply linger over breakfast as shola birdsong carries across the valley. Warm, personal hospitality rooted in a working landscape.

property_title: Rawla Bisalpur: Rajput Heritage Amid Rajasthan's Quiet Fields
property_intro: Set among mustard fields and gentle hills between Jaipur and Ranthambore, Rawla Bisalpur is an ancestral Rajput home restored by the family who still calls it theirs. Frescoed alcoves, hand-blocked textiles and courtyards cooled by peepal shade set the mood for unhurried days. Walk to the village potter, cycle village lanes, or track birds along the Banas. Meals draw on the estate's own harvest, and your stay supports local artisans, farmers and rural schooling nearby.

property_title: Kudrat - A Boutique Homestay: Where Nature Sets the Pace
property_intro: Tucked into the folds of the Himalayan foothills, Kudrat is a boutique homestay where mornings begin with birdsong and the scent of cardamom tea. Handcrafted interiors draw on local stone, timber and textiles, made by artisans from surrounding villages. Days unfold gently here: forest walks with resident naturalists, orchard harvests, slow suppers of produce grown steps from the table. A small, thoughtful retreat that gives back to the valley that shapes it.

property_title: Kasbah du Toubkal: Berber Hospitality in the High Atlas Mountains
property_intro: Set above the village of Imlil, at the foot of North Africa's highest peak, Kasbah du Toubkal is a restored fortress where Berber hospitality shapes every detail. Walnut ceilings, hand-woven rugs and terraces framing snow-dusted summits invite slow mornings and long conversations. Guided mule treks, hammam rituals and mint tea with local families fill the days, while a levy on every stay supports the Imlil community's school, ambulance and education projects.

property_title: Dhyaana Farms: Slow Days and Deep Green Calm in Rural India
property_intro: Set among orchards, paddy fields and birdsong, Dhyaana Farms invites you to trade schedules for seasons. Days here unfold gently: harvesting with the resident farmers, learning regional recipes over a wood fire, or simply reading beneath a mango tree. Interiors favour local stone, reclaimed timber and handloom textiles, crafted by artisans from neighbouring villages. Organic farming, rainwater harvesting and fair local employment underpin everything, making your stay quietly meaningful as well as restorative.

property_title: Kings Lodge: Wild Mornings on the Edge of Bandhavgarh
property_intro: On the fringes of Bandhavgarh National Park, Kings Lodge sits amid sal forest and rocky outcrops where tigers roam and langurs call at first light. Eighteen stilted cottages, built from local stone and timber, open onto private verandas shaded by trees. Days unfold with expert-led safaris, village walks and slow evenings around the fire. Solar power, water harvesting and a largely local team reflect a quiet commitment to Madhya Pradesh's forests and the communities beside them.

property_title: Pench Tree Lodge: Treetop Nights in Kipling's Jungle Heartland
property_intro: Raised among mahua and teak on the northern edge of Pench Tiger Reserve, this lodge places you within the forests that inspired The Jungle Book. Nine timber treehouses stand high in the canopy, where langurs pass at eye level and dawn arrives with birdsong rather than alarm clocks. Days unfold through game drives, guided walks and visits to neighbouring Gond villages, while the lodge's local team and conservation partnerships keep this wilderness thriving.

property_title: Kanha Earth Lodge: Unhurried Luxury in India's Tiger Country
property_intro: Tucked into sixteen acres of regenerated forest on the edge of Kanha National Park, this Madhya Pradesh hideaway sits where sal woodland meets bamboo and birdsong. Sixteen earth-toned cottages, built with local stone and timber, open onto private verandas made for slow mornings. Days unfold with tiger safaris, guided walks with resident naturalists and visits to Baiga and Gond villages, while the lodge's reforestation and employment programmes ensure your stay quietly strengthens the landscape that surrounds it.

property_title: Tree House Hideaway: Canopy Living on Bandhavgarh's Edge
property_intro: On the fringes of Bandhavgarh National Park, five timber houses rest among mahua and tendu trees, reached by wooden walkways rather than corridors. Mornings begin with birdsong and coffee on your private deck; afternoons might mean a jeep safari in search of tigers, or a walk through the sal forest with a resident naturalist. Twenty-one acres of once-barren farmland have been coaxed back into woodland, tended largely by neighbouring villagers who share their knowledge generously.

property_title: Denwa Backwater Escape: Satpura's Riverside Wilderness Retreat
property_intro: Set above the still waters of the Denwa river, this quietly elegant retreat looks across to the forests of Satpura National Park in Madhya Pradesh. Cottages and tree houses are dressed in local craft and earthy tones, with canoe crossings, walking safaris and birding mornings replacing the usual jeep-only rush. Run alongside village neighbours and committed to protecting Satpura's habitat, it is a place where wilderness feels close, considered and remarkably unhurried.

property_title: Waghoba Eco Lodge: Wild Tranquillity on Tadoba's Quiet Edge
property_intro: On the fringes of Maharashtra's Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve, Waghoba Eco Lodge sits among teak forests and farmland where leopards move quietly between villages and wilderness. Named after the tiger deity revered by local communities, the lodge blends earthen architecture with locally crafted detail. Days unfold with jeep safaris, guided walks with naturalists and slow evenings beneath vast skies. Staffed largely by neighbouring villagers, it channels tourism into conservation research and rural livelihoods.

property_title: Cempedak Island: Barefoot Bamboo Luxury in Indonesia's Riau
property_intro: Scattered across a granite-boulder shoreline in Indonesia's Riau Archipelago, Cempedak Island welcomes adults only to twenty bamboo villas, each hand-crafted by local artisans and cooled by sea breezes rather than air-conditioning. Days drift between private plunge pools, sailing traditional wooden boats and foraging in the organic garden that supplies the kitchen. Solar power, rainwater harvesting and the island's own reforestation and turtle protection work quietly underpin everything, alongside long-standing employment for neighbouring island communities.

property_title: Nikoi Island: Barefoot Elegance on a Private Indonesian Isle
property_intro: Ringed by granite boulders and warm South China Sea shallows, Nikoi Island lies a short boat ride from Bintan, yet feels wonderfully far from everything. Open-sided beach houses built from driftwood, bamboo and alang-alang thatch invite the breeze in, while days drift between kite-surfing, snorkelling and long lunches. Solar power, a working farm and the island's own foundation supporting local schools mean your stay quietly gives back to neighbouring village communities.

property_title: Playa Viva: Solar-Powered Serenity on Mexico's Wild Pacific Coast
property_intro: Set on a secluded stretch of sand near Juluchuca, an hour south of Zihuatanejo, Playa Viva is an off-grid retreat where treehouse casitas rise among palms and an estuary teeming with birdlife. Days unfold with surf lessons, horseback rides at dusk and turtle hatchling releases led by the resort's conservation team. Solar power, permaculture gardens and a long-standing partnership with the local village mean your stay quietly strengthens the coast that surrounds it.

property_title: Six Senses Laamu: Barefoot Luxury on a Remote Maldivian Atoll
property_intro: Adrift in the seldom-visited Laamu Atoll, Six Senses Laamu is the only resort for miles, reached by seaplane over water in every shade of blue. Driftwood-hued villas rise on stilts above a house reef where manta rays glide and turtles graze on seagrass meadows protected by the resort's own marine biologists. Days unfold with slow ceremony: sunrise yoga, ice cream by the sea, dinners in the treetops and evenings spent stargazing through the observatory telescope.

property_title: The Untamed Bandhavgarh: Wild Luxury on the Tiger's Doorstep
property_intro: On the fringes of Bandhavgarh's sal forests in Madhya Pradesh, The Untamed sits quietly among mahua trees and open grassland, where langur calls carry across the morning mist. Twelve earth-toned suites echo the surrounding landscape, with private pools and terraces framing the wilderness beyond. Days unfold with expert-led safaris, forest walks and conversations with naturalists who know these tigers intimately. Local artisans, farmers and guides shape the experience, ensuring your stay supports the communities living alongside this remarkable forest.

property_title: Sawai Shivir Ranthambore: Wild Luxury on the Tiger's Trail
property_intro: On the fringes of Ranthambore National Park, where dhok forest gives way to open Rajasthani scrub, Sawai Shivir offers a considered retreat within tiger country. Tented suites and pared-back interiors draw on local craft and earthy tones, framing views of the surrounding wilderness. Days unfold with dawn safaris, guided walks with naturalists and slow evenings beneath a canopy of stars. The camp works closely with neighbouring villages, supporting artisans, conservation initiatives and habitat protection beyond the park boundary.

property_title: FHR Wilderness Lodge: Where India's Wild Heart Welcomes You
property_intro: Set on the fringes of dense sal forest, FHR Wilderness Lodge invites you to slow down where tiger territory begins. Handcrafted interiors draw on local stone, timber and textile traditions, while wide verandas frame the treeline and the sounds of dusk. Days unfold with naturalist-led safaris, guided forest walks and unhurried meals sourced from surrounding villages. The lodge works closely with neighbouring communities on habitat protection, ensuring your stay strengthens the wilderness that surrounds it.

property_title: Kohima Camp: Nagaland's Hills, Heritage and Hornbill Spirit
property_intro: Set among the pine-clad ridges of Nagaland, Kohima Camp gathers a handful of canvas suites above a valley where Angami villages have farmed terraces for generations. Days unfold with morning walks to war memorials and weaving households, evenings around the fire with Naga cooking and stories. Timed to the Hornbill Festival, the camp works closely with local guides, artisans and growers, offering an unhurried, respectful window into India's north-eastern frontier.

property_title: Chamba Camp Diskit: Tented Elegance in Ladakh's Nubra Valley
property_intro: Beyond the Khardung La pass, where cold desert dunes meet apricot orchards, Chamba Camp Diskit unfolds beneath Ladakh's vast Nubra skies. Handsome canvas suites, dressed in campaign-era furnishings and warmed by wood-burning stoves, look towards the towering Maitreya Buddha and the ridges of the Karakoram. Days might bring monastery mornings with resident monks, riverside picnics, double-humped camel encounters or archery lessons, while local guides and artisans share the valley's living traditions with quiet pride.

property_title: Chamba Camp Thiksey: Luxury Under Ladakh's Himalayan Skies
property_intro: Set among poplar groves beneath the whitewashed tiers of Thiksey Monastery, Chamba Camp Thiksey brings refined comfort to the high desert of Ladakh. Handsome canvas suites open onto views of the Indus valley and the Stok range, while butlers, teak writing desks and copper bathtubs recall an earlier age of travel. Days unfold with monastery prayers at dawn, village walks, archery and polo, and conversations with Ladakhi artisans whose crafts the camp helps sustain.

property_title: Lunuganga: Geoffrey Bawa's Living Garden Estate in Sri Lanka
property_intro: Once a rubber plantation, Lunuganga became architect Geoffrey Bawa's lifelong experiment in shaping landscape. Overlooking Dedduwa Lake near Bentota, the estate unfolds through terraces, water gardens and framed views composed over five decades. Just seven suites occupy the original buildings, each filled with Bawa's collected art and furniture. Wander the grounds with a resident guide, swim beneath frangipani, or take breakfast on the terrace as herons drift past. The trust maintains the gardens and supports local craft, keeping Bawa's vision alive.

property_title: Wallawwa: A Colonial Manor House Retreat Near Colombo, Sri Lanka
property_intro: Tucked among coconut groves and frangipani gardens just twenty minutes from Colombo's airport, Wallawwa is a nineteenth-century manor house reborn as an intimate retreat. Antique planter's furniture, cool verandahs and a spa set within the grounds invite an unhurried pace. Chefs draw on the kitchen garden and nearby markets, while walks through neighbouring villages reveal everyday Sri Lankan life. Staff are largely drawn from the surrounding community, giving arrivals and departures a genuine sense of welcome.

property_title: Fort Bazaar: A Storied Sanctuary Inside Galle's Old Ramparts
property_intro: Tucked within the coral-stone walls of Galle Fort, Fort Bazaar occupies a lovingly restored merchant's townhouse where Dutch colonnades frame a courtyard shaded by frangipani. Eighteen rooms balance antique teak with contemporary calm, while the Church Street Social serves Sri Lankan flavours drawn from island growers. Spend mornings with a heritage walk past lighthouse and lacemakers, afternoons in the spa, and evenings on the rooftop as swifts wheel over centuries-old rooftops and the Indian Ocean beyond.

property_title: Kumu Beach: Barefoot Sophistication on Sri Lanka's South Coast
property_intro: Set between the Bentota River and a wide stretch of Indian Ocean sand, Kumu Beach is a ten-room retreat where surf-worn timber, woven textiles and low-slung daybeds create an easy sense of calm. Days drift from yoga on the deck to river safaris, turtle hatchery visits and long lunches of Sri Lankan seafood. Local artisans shape the interiors, while community and marine conservation projects benefit directly from every stay you enjoy here.

property_title: Camellia Hills: Serene Tea Country Living Above Castlereagh
property_intro: Perched on a promontory above Castlereagh Reservoir, Camellia Hills looks out across water and working tea fields in Sri Lanka's Dickoya highlands. Once a planter's bungalow, its five suites blend colonial character with contemporary calm, while butlers, log fires and unhurried dinners set the rhythm. Days might bring tea-plucking with estate workers, kayaking at dawn or walks to Adam's Peak trails. The estate remains part of a living tea community, supporting the families who tend it.

property_title: Goatfell: A Highland-Inspired Retreat in Sri Lanka's Hill Country
property_intro: Set among the mist-brushed tea slopes of Sri Lanka's central highlands, Goatfell is a restored planter's bungalow where colonial elegance meets genuine warmth. Log fires crackle at dusk, gardens spill with roses, and the estate's pluckers still walk the surrounding fields at dawn. Wander to hidden waterfalls, taste single-estate leaves at the factory below, or simply linger over long lunches on the veranda. Local families remain at the heart of the estate, sustaining a way of life worth preserving.

property_title: Nine Skies: A Tea Planter's Bungalow in Ella's Misty Highlands
property_intro: High in Sri Lanka's hill country, Nine Skies sits within the working tea fields of the Kelburne estate, where mornings arrive with birdsong and the scent of freshly plucked leaf. This restored planter's bungalow holds just five suites, each layered with colonial antiques, local craft and views towards the Ella Gap. Days unfold with estate walks, tea tastings led by resident experts and visits to nearby villages, while long-standing partnerships support the plantation community who call these hills home.

property_title: Kalkudah Beach House: Barefoot Serenity on Sri Lanka's East
property_intro: On Sri Lanka's quietly unfolding east coast, Kalkudah Beach House sits where coconut groves give way to a broad sweep of pale sand and reef-sheltered water. Airy interiors pair local craftsmanship with sea breezes, while days drift between lagoon paddles, cycle rides through fishing villages and long lunches of freshly landed catch. The house works closely with its Tamil neighbours, employing and sourcing locally, so your stay quietly supports a coastline still finding its voice again.

property_title: Zhiwaling Ascent: Bhutanese Craft and Calm in Paro Valley
property_intro: Set among rice terraces on the edge of Paro, Zhiwaling Ascent pairs contemporary comfort with the artistry of Bhutanese craftsmanship — hand-carved timber, locally quarried stone and murals painted by monastery-trained artists. Days might begin with a valley walk towards Tiger's Nest and end with hot stone baths, herbal teas and mountain air. Family-owned and staffed largely by neighbours, the hotel champions Bhutanese makers, seasonal produce and the quiet hospitality that lingers long after departure.

property_title: Cottar's 1920s Camp: Vintage Safari Romance in the Maasai Mara
property_intro: Set within a private conservancy on the edge of Kenya's Maasai Mara, Cottar's 1920s Camp draws on five generations of safari heritage. Canvas tents are dressed with campaign furniture, Persian rugs and monogrammed linen, while beyond the veranda the plains stir with wildebeest, lion and elephant. Days unfold with Maasai guides, walking safaris and starlit dinners, and your stay directly supports the community leases and anti-poaching teams protecting this remarkable wilderness.

property_title: Cottar's Bush Villa: A Private Retreat on Maasai Mara's Edge
property_intro: Set within a private wildlife conservancy bordering the Maasai Mara, Cottar's Bush Villa is a five-bedroom sanctuary reserved for one party at a time. Vast plains unfold beyond the infinity pool, while interiors blend colonial heirlooms with contemporary comfort. Days might bring guided walks with Maasai trackers, night drives or picnics beside the Olderkesi River. Lease fees paid to the local community protect 6,000 acres of wilderness, making every stay quietly consequential.

property_title: The Home in the Valley: Slow Living Among Sun-Warmed Hillsides
property_intro: Tucked into a green fold of the Spanish countryside, The Home in the Valley invites you to settle into a slower rhythm. Terracotta, lime-washed walls and reclaimed timber frame views of terraced groves and distant ridgelines. Days unfold with foraged breakfasts, guided walks with local shepherds and long afternoons beside the water. The owners work closely with neighbouring farms and replant native woodland each season, so your stay quietly nurtures the valley that shelters it.

property_title: Songtsam Lodge Shangri-La: Tibetan Soul in the Yunnan Highlands
property_intro: Set beside the centuries-old Songzanlin Monastery on the Tibetan plateau's southern edge, Songtsam Lodge Shangri-La opens onto barley fields, prayer flags and the low chant of monks at dawn. Rooms are dressed in hand-carved Tibetan woodwork, local textiles and antiques gathered from surrounding villages. Days unfold with monastery walks, highland picnics and visits to family homes, while the lodge employs and trains Tibetans locally, keeping craft, cuisine and culture quietly thriving.

property_title: Vakkaru Maldives: Barefoot Elegance on a Living Coral Island
property_intro: Set within Baa Atoll's UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, Vakkaru unfolds across a natural coral island fringed by banyan trees and a house reef teeming with life. Thatched villas and overwater retreats open to soft sand and shifting blues, while marine biologists invite you to help plant coral or track manta rays. Days drift between the spa's overwater pavilions, wood-fired dining and lagoon swims, with island craftsmanship and local partnerships woven quietly through every stay.

property_title: Amilla: Barefoot Luxury Rooted in the Baa Atoll's Wild Beauty
property_intro: Set within a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in the Baa Atoll, Amilla unfolds across a rare island jungle fringed by powder-soft sand. Treetop villas and beachfront residences sit lightly among banyans and breadfruit, while the island's farm, hydroponics and wellness kitchen shape a genuinely nourishing way to eat. Snorkel with manta rays, join marine biologists on the reef, or simply let the days soften. Thoughtful, unhurried and quietly generous to the communities and waters that surround it.

property_title: The Dwarika's: Kathmandu's Living Tribute to Newari Artistry
property_intro: In the heart of Kathmandu, moments from the temples of Pashupatinath, The Dwarika's rises from a remarkable act of preservation. For decades, its founder rescued hand-carved Newari windows and pillars destined for firewood, weaving them into courtyards where brickwork, bronze and terracotta tell centuries of stories. Artisans still work on site, sustaining crafts that might otherwise vanish. Days unfold with Himalayan-grown teas, restorative therapies and dinners drawing on royal Nepali recipes, gathered from mountain villages.

property_title: Anantara Ubud Bali Resort: Where the Jungle Meets Serenity
property_intro: Set above the Ayung River valley in Bali's cultural heartland, Anantara Ubud Bali Resort settles into terraced hillsides where rice paddies give way to dense tropical forest. Villas with private pools open onto canopy views, while thoughtful design draws on Balinese craft traditions and local artisanship. Days unfold with river treks, temple visits and offerings prepared alongside village families, before evenings spent listening to the valley's chorus from your own quiet terrace.

property_title: The Seed: Where Slow Living Takes Root in Bali's Green Jungle
property_intro: Tucked into a valley of rice terraces and river-fed jungle, The Seed invites you to slow your pace and pay attention. Rooms are built from bamboo, reclaimed timber and local stone, opening to birdsong and mist. Days unfold with permaculture harvests, cacao ceremonies and long swims beneath the canopy. Working closely with neighbouring farming families, the retreat reinvests in seed-saving and village schooling, so your stay quietly nourishes the land that surrounds it.

property_title: Anantara Kalutara Resort: Where River Meets the Indian Ocean
property_intro: Where the Kalu Ganga slips into the Indian Ocean, Anantara Kalutara Resort occupies a slender peninsula of sun-warmed palms and quiet water. Its architecture completes a vision begun by Geoffrey Bawa, all cool corridors, shaded courtyards and carefully framed horizons. Days unfold with river safaris through mangroves, Ayurvedic rituals and visits to the Kalutara Bodhiya temple, while turtle hatchery support and local sourcing tie the resort closely to the communities beyond its gates.

property_title: Desa Potato Head: Seminyak's Creative, Zero-Waste Beach Village
property_intro:
On the sands of Seminyak, Desa Potato Head reimagines the Balinese village as a cultural playground where music, art and good design meet a genuine commitment to sending nothing to landfill. Rooms and suites, shaped by Indonesian craft and reclaimed materials, open towards the Indian Ocean. Spend mornings in wellness rituals, afternoons at the beach club, evenings tasting plant-forward menus 
informed by local farmers. Waste-to-value workshops reveal how discarded objects become furniture, art and lasting livelihoods.

property_title: Dolkhar Resort: Ladakhi Heritage Reimagined in the Himalaya
property_intro: Set among apricot orchards on the outskirts of Leh, Dolkhar is a quietly considered retreat where Ladakhi building traditions meet contemporary calm. Nine villas of mud brick and poplar frame views of the Stok range, while the kitchen revives heirloom recipes using grains and greens grown nearby. Days unfold with monastery walks, textile workshops and conversations with local artisans, and the family behind it all champions Himalayan craft, seed diversity and village livelihoods with genuine conviction.

property_title: Patina Maldives: Barefoot Design and Wellbeing in Fari Islands
property_intro: Set on North Male Atoll's Fari Islands, Patina Maldives pairs Brazilian architect Marcio Kogan's clean, light-filled villas with lagoons that shelter thriving coral nurseries. Days unfold between the Fari Marina Village, where island residents and visiting chefs gather, and Flow, a wellness space exploring sound, breath and movement. Reef restoration, low-waste kitchens and homegrown produce underpin it all, while artists in residence lend the island a quietly creative pulse rarely found in the Maldives.

property_title: COMO Shambhala Estate: Bali's Sacred Jungle Retreat Awaits
property_intro: Tucked into the rainforest above Bali's Ayung River, near Ubud, COMO Shambhala Estate is a residential health retreat built around natural spring water long held sacred by local communities. Five private residences rest among tropical gardens, where terraces, timber and stone frame the valley below. Days unfold with hydrotherapy, Ayurvedic consultations, jungle treks and nourishing COMO Shambhala Cuisine, while resident experts guide each guest's own path. Balinese craftsmanship and local employment remain central to estate life.

property_title: Capella Ubud, Bali: Tented Luxury in a Living Rainforest
property_intro: Tucked into the Keliki rainforest above the Wos River, Capella Ubud reimagines the spirit of early Balinese exploration through fourteen tents and two hillside villas, each shaped around the trees rather than through them. Days unfold with river treks, silversmithing beside village artisans and ceremonies led by a resident priest. Bill Bensley's design honours the land's contours and the community that farms it, so the surrounding rice terraces and canopy remain gloriously intact.

property_title: Lodge Lorien: Native Forest Seclusion in New Zealand's Wilds
property_intro: Tucked among regenerating native bush, Lodge Lorien offers a quietly considered retreat where birdsong replaces traffic and the horizon belongs to mountains and sky. Interiors pair natural timber and stone with generous light, inviting slow mornings and long conversations. Wander private trails, forage in the kitchen garden, or let a guide reveal the valley's hidden waterways. Ongoing planting and predator control mean each stay helps the surrounding forest, and its rare birdlife, flourish for generations.

property_title: The Six: Barefoot Luxury on Sri Lanka's Untamed South Coast
property_intro: Tucked between paddy fields and the Indian Ocean on Sri Lanka's southern shore, The Six is an intimate villa retreat where six suites open to sea breezes and birdsong. Days unfold slowly here: sunrise swims, spice-scented cooking with local chefs, wildlife walks through nearby wetlands. Handcrafted interiors celebrate island artistry, while the kitchen draws on neighbouring farms and fishing boats. Small in scale, generous in spirit, it invites you to settle in and stay a while.

property_title: Malliouhana: Anguilla's Clifftop Retreat Above Meads Bay
property_intro: Perched on a limestone bluff between Meads and Turtle Cove, Malliouhana looks out across water so clear you can trace the reef from your terrace. Interiors nod to Anguillian craft with woven textures, local artwork and shaded arcades that catch the trade winds. Days drift between three pools, tennis at dawn and Caribbean-Mediterranean cooking rooted in island produce. The resort supports local artisans, musicians and marine conservation, so your stay quietly gives back to Anguilla itself.

property_title: Hermitage Bay: Barefoot Luxury on Antigua's Quiet West Coast
