property_intro: Tucked into a secluded cove on Antigua's north-west shore, Hermitage Bay is reached by a winding road through tropical hillside, opening onto a private crescent of pale sand. Just twenty-five plantation-style suites, each with its own plunge pool, look out across the Caribbean. Days unfold with sailing, snorkelling reefs and treatments in the hillside spa, while the kitchen draws on island growers and fishermen. Staff, largely Antiguan, lend the place its genuine warmth.

property_title: Casa de Uco: Vineyard Living Beneath the Andes of Mendoza
property_intro: Set within a working vineyard in Mendoza's Uco Valley, Casa de Uco unfolds across 300 hectares of vines, lagoons and wild grassland, with the snow-dusted Andes filling every window. Architect Alberto Tonconogy's low-slung design of raw concrete, timber and glass draws the landscape indoors. Days here might mean harvesting alongside the winemakers, riding out with gauchos, or tasting Malbec drawn straight from the barrel, while regenerative farming and local employment quietly underpin it all.

property_title: Chalets at Blackheath: Blue Mountains Serenity Among Gum Trees
property_intro: Tucked into the upper Blue Mountains, Chalets at Blackheath sits within whispering eucalypts, moments from Grose Valley lookouts and the waterfall walks of Govetts Leap. Timber-lined chalets open onto private verandahs, with wood fires, deep baths and windows framing the bush. Days unfold slowly here: village bookshops and long lunches in Blackheath, sunrise at Pulpit Rock, cockatoos overhead at dusk. The owners tend the surrounding bushland carefully, keeping native habitat intact for guests and wildlife alike.

property_title: Smiths Beach Resort: Coastal Calm on Western Australia's Edge
property_intro: Tucked into peppermint bushland above a crescent of white sand at Yallingup, Smiths Beach Resort places you where the Margaret River region meets the Indian Ocean. Villas and beach houses open to sea breezes, with timber, stone and light shaping easy days. Surf the point, walk the Cape to Cape Track, or let vineyards and caves fill an afternoon. Native revegetation and long-standing local partnerships keep this stretch of coast much as it should be.

property_title: Kristiania Lech: Where Alpine Heritage Meets Modern Artistry
property_intro: Perched above the village of Lech in Austria's Arlberg, Kristiania began life as the family home of Olympic skier Othmar Schneider - and still feels like one. Its 30 rooms are hung with contemporary art and warmed by reclaimed timber, while windows frame the Karhorn and Rüfikopf. Ski from the door in winter, wander wildflower meadows in summer, then return for spa hours and dishes built around Vorarlberg's small producers and mountain farmers.

property_title: The Sandpiper: Barbadian Elegance on the Platinum Coast
property_intro: Tucked within a mature tropical garden on the leafy west coast of Barbados, The Sandpiper opens directly onto the calm, coral-fringed waters of Holetown. Suites and tree-top villas are dressed in warm woods, local artistry and shaded verandas, while the kitchen leans on island growers and day-boat catch. Spend mornings paddling above turtles, afternoons beneath the mahogany canopy, and evenings with rum in hand. Family-run for generations, it remains genuinely rooted in its community.

property_title: Angkor Village Hotel: Timeless Siem Reap Charm and Calm
property_intro: Tucked down a quiet lane in the heart of Siem Reap, Angkor Village Hotel gathers timber-framed pavilions around lotus ponds and shaded gardens, moments from the Old Market and the temples beyond. Rooms echo traditional Khmer craftsmanship, with hand-carved details and locally woven textiles. Days might begin with a sunrise cycle through rice fields and end with apsara dance at the hotel's own theatre, supported by artisans and staff drawn from surrounding villages.

property_title: Hotel Three Sixty: Panoramic Rainforest Living in Costa Rica
property_intro: Perched on a forested ridge above Costa Rica's southern Pacific coast, Hotel Three Sixty gazes across the Golfo Dulce towards the wild Osa Peninsula. Ten glass-fronted suites open to birdsong and treetops, their clean lines softened by local hardwood and tropical greenery. Days unfold with waterfall walks, whale-watching and slow breakfasts above the canopy. The owners protect surrounding rainforest and champion nearby communities, so your stay quietly supports the wilderness framing every view.

property_title: Los Altos Resort: Pacific Horizons Above Costa Rica's Coast
property_intro: Perched on a forested ridge above Costa Rica's Central Pacific shore, Los Altos Resort looks out across Manuel Antonio's canopy to the ocean beyond. Sunlit suites open to sea breezes, while terraces invite slow mornings with toucans and titi monkeys as company. Days unfold with rainforest walks, surf lessons and boat trips along the coast, before dinner drawn from local growers and fishers. Reforested grounds and community partnerships keep this hillside retreat rooted in its place.

property_title: Nanuku Resort: Where Rainforest Meets Reef on Fiji's Coral Coast
property_intro: Set along Pacific Harbour's shoreline, where rainforest slips down to a quiet black-sand beach, Nanuku is a place of unhurried rhythms. Thatched villas and residences open to private pools, each paired with a Nanny and Nanuku Ambassador who share stories, songs and the island's traditions. Days unfold with reef snorkelling, horse riding at dawn or visits to neighbouring Beqa. Local artisans, village schools and marine protection efforts remain woven into every stay.

property_title: Esprit de France: Heritage Hotels with an Artful Parisian Soul
property_intro: Tucked into the quiet corners of Paris and beyond, the hotels of Esprit de France occupy buildings with genuine stories to tell u2013 former private mansions, artists' haunts and addresses that have watched centuries pass. Antique furnishings, original engravings and family-collected art fill rooms restored with care rather than reinvented. Days unfold slowly here: breakfast beneath vaulted stone, an afternoon in a nearby gallery, evenings spent listening to the neighbourhood settle into itself.

property_title: Relais de Chambord: Riverside Calm Beside a Royal Château
property_intro: Facing the extraordinary silhouette of the Château de Chambord, this Loire Valley retreat sits within a vast forested estate where deer roam and the River Cosson drifts quietly past. Interiors by Jean-Michel Wilmotte balance contemporary restraint with the grandeur beyond the windows. Days unfold with electric boat trips, dawn wildlife walks with estate rangers, and cycling through protected woodland, before spa treatments and dinners built around Sologne producers. A rare chance to wake beside a Renaissance masterpiece.

property_title: A77 Suites: Refined Athenian Living in the Heart of the City
property_intro: Tucked into a quiet corner of central Athens, A77 Suites invites you to settle into the rhythm of the city. Marble, muted linens and locally crafted furnishings shape interiors that feel considered rather than showy, while rooftop views drift towards the Acropolis. Days begin with Greek breakfasts sourced from small island producers and unfold into neighbourhood walks, gallery visits and evenings in Kolonaki's tavernas. A thoughtful base for travellers who prefer discovery to spectacle.

property_title: Rimondi Boutique Hotels: Venetian Soul in Old Cretan Rethymno
property_intro: Tucked into the lanes of Rethymno's Venetian quarter, Rimondi Boutique Hotels occupies a cluster of restored 16th-century mansions, where arched doorways and hand-cut stone meet contemporary Cretan design. Days drift between courtyard pools, rooftop views across terracotta tiles to the Fortezza, and a kitchen built on island producers and heirloom recipes. Staff, largely local, share the walks, wineries and coves they grew up with — an invitation to know Crete slowly, and rather well.

property_title: Manili Boutique Suites & Villas: Quiet Luxury by the Aegean Sea
property_intro: Set among olive groves and whitewashed stone, Manili Boutique Suites & Villas invites you to slow down and settle into the rhythm of Greek island life. Interiors pair local craftsmanship with natural linen, timber and light, while private terraces frame long views towards the sea. Days unfold with sunrise swims, family-run tavernas and walks along coastal paths. Locally sourced produce, low-impact design and close ties with island artisans shape every considered detail.

property_title: St Nicolas Bay Resort — Where Crete's Blue Meets Slow Luxury
property_intro: On a private peninsula just beyond Agios Nikolaos, St Nicolas Bay Resort unfolds across terraced gardens and three sheltered coves on the Gulf of Mirabello. Rooms and villas honour Cretan craft: handwoven textiles, cool local stone, verandas angled towards the water. Days drift between hidden swimming platforms, Minoan sites inland and unhurried lunches built from Lasithi produce. Family-run across generations, the resort tends its shoreline carefully and keeps its kitchens, cellars and stories firmly rooted in Crete.

property_title: Casa Delfino Hotel & Spa: Venetian Soul in Old Chania
property_intro: Tucked into the lanes of Chania's Venetian quarter, Casa Delfino occupies a 17th-century merchant's mansion where pebble-mosaic courtyards, family heirlooms and Cretan craftsmanship set the mood. Suites open onto rooftop views of the Old Harbour and the White Mountains beyond, while the cave-like spa invites slow afternoons. Three generations of the same family still welcome guests, championing local producers, olive growers and artisans, and offering walks, tastings and sailing trips that reveal Crete at its most genuine.

property_title: Nomad Mykonos: Cycladic Calm Above the Aegean's Shifting Blue
property_intro: Set into the hillside above Kalo Livadi, Nomad Mykonos trades the island's louder rhythms for something quieter and more considered. Whitewashed volumes, hand-thrown ceramics and reclaimed timber frame long views across the Aegean, while the kitchen leans on Cycladic growers and day-boat catch. Days unfold with yoga on the terrace, guided walks through dry-stone farmland, or slow afternoons by the pool. Local artisans shape much of what you touch here, from linens to lighting.

property_title: Laguna Coast Resort: Where Greek Shores Meet Quiet Luxury
property_intro: Set between a protected lagoon and the open Aegean, Laguna Coast Resort draws its character from the wetlands that surround it, where flamingos gather at dusk and salt flats shimmer in the late light. Interiors favour lime-washed walls, local stone and hand-thrown ceramics from nearby workshops. Days unfold slowly: kayaking the shallows, foraging with island cooks, or simply reading beneath the tamarisks. A share of every stay supports the lagoon's ongoing habitat restoration.

property_title: El Silencio: Cloud Forest Serenity in Costa Rica's Highlands
property_intro: Tucked into the misty highlands near Bajos del Toro, El Silencio unfolds across a private reserve of cloud forest, waterfalls and volcanic ridgelines. Timber-clad casitas open onto valley views, while trails lead to hot springs, hidden cascades and canyons few travellers ever see. The lodge works hand in hand with the surrounding village, sourcing from local farms and protecting hundreds of hectares of regenerating forest. Mornings begin with birdsong; evenings end beside the fire.

property_title: Meneghetti: Istrian Vineyard Living Rooted in Slow Luxury
property_intro: Set among vineyards and olive groves in Istria's gentle interior, near Bale and a short drive from the Adriatic, Meneghetti unfolds as a working estate rather than a conventional hotel. Restored stone buildings, private pool villas and a wine cellar sit within land the family has quietly nurtured for decades. Days pass with cellar tastings, olive oil harvests and dishes drawn from the surrounding fields, prepared by chefs who champion Istrian growers and centuries-old rural craft.

property_title: Lesic Dimitri Palace: Silk Road Elegance in Korčula Old Town
property_intro: Tucked into the walled heart of Korčula, this restored 18th-century bishop's palace opens onto the Adriatic with just six residences, each shaped around the spice routes once sailed by Marco Polo. Expect vaulted stone, Damascene textiles and hand-selected antiques, alongside a spa, a private wooden boat and dinners built on island produce and Grk wine from nearby vineyards. Careful conservation of the original architecture keeps local craft, heritage and hospitality quietly alive.

property_title: Secret Bay: A Rainforest Hideaway Above Dominica's Wild Coast
property_intro: Perched on a clifftop above two secluded beaches on Dominica's north-west coast, Secret Bay offers just a handful of hand-built villas among the treetops. Local craftsmanship and Guyanese hardwoods shape interiors that open entirely to birdsong and sea breeze. Days unfold with private chefs, river kayaking and forest walks led by islanders who know every trail. A dedicated foundation supports reforestation and local livelihoods, so your stay quietly strengthens the wild place surrounding it.

property_title: Hotel Del Parque: Colonial Grace Amid Guayaquil's Lush Gardens
property_intro: Set within Guayaquil's Parque Hist\u00f3rico, Hotel Del Parque occupies painstakingly rescued nineteenth-century houses, rebuilt beam by beam beside mangroves where sloths and scarlet macaws move through the canopy. Fretwork balconies, cool courtyards and just forty-four rooms create an unhurried retreat minutes from the city. Days unfold with cacao tastings, riverside walks and dinner at Casa Juli\u00e1n, where Ecuadorian produce meets French technique. Heritage conservation and local craftsmanship shape every corner of the stay.

property_title: Villa Mirae: Sunlit Serenity in the Heart of Provence
property_intro: Set among silvered olive groves and drystone terraces, Villa Mirae invites you to slow down and settle into the rhythm of the French countryside. Interiors pair lime-washed walls with locally crafted furniture, while shuttered windows frame long views towards the hills. Days might begin with market baskets from the nearby village and end beside the pool as cicadas quieten. The gardens are tended without chemicals, and the kitchen champions growers within a few kilometres.

property_title: Abbaye de la Bussière: A Cistercian Retreat in Burgundy's Heart
property_intro: Set within 15 acres of walled gardens, lakes and ancient woodland near Dijon, this 12th-century Cistercian abbey has been gently reawakened as a country house hotel. Vaulted ceilings, stained glass and frescoed corridors meet deep armchairs and log fires, while the kitchen draws on the potager and neighbouring vineyards. Days unfold with cellar visits along the Côte de Nuits, cycling the old canal path, or simply lingering beneath the cedars.

property_title: Château de Valmer: Vineyard Serenity on the Côte d'Azur Shore
property_intro: Tucked between organic vines and a century-old palm grove above the bay of Gigaro, Château de Valmer feels like a private Provençal estate that happens to open onto the sea. Rooms blend heritage detail with easy coastal calm, while days drift from vineyard walks to the beach club below. The kitchen leans on the estate's own produce, and the surrounding Cap Lardier reserve keeps this stretch of shoreline gloriously undeveloped.

property_title: Les Bergeries de Palombaggia: Corsica's Coastal Hideaway
property_intro: Tucked into a pine-scented hillside above Palombaggia's celebrated shoreline, Les Bergeries de Palombaggia gathers a handful of stone-built suites and villas among cork oaks and wild maquis. Rooms open to terraces framing the Cerbicale Islands, while interiors pair Corsican craftsmanship with cool linen calm. Days drift between the saltwater pool, boat trips along the granite coast and long lunches of island produce. The owners protect the surrounding gardens carefully, keeping this corner of southern Corsica quietly, contentedly itself.

property_title: Assiette Champenoise: Three Michelin Stars Amid the Reims Vines
property_intro: Tucked into wooded parkland on the edge of Reims, this family-run retreat sits within easy reach of Champagne's grandest cellars. Chef Arnaud Lallement's three-starred kitchen is the heart of the house, where langoustine and local produce meet an extraordinary cellar of grower cuvées. Rooms are calm and contemporary, dressed in warm timber and glass that draws the garden inside. Spend afternoons cycling between vineyards, then return for an aperitif beneath the trees.

property_title: Domaine du Mas de Pierre: Provençal Serenity, Reimagined
property_intro: Tucked between the olive groves and hilltop villages of southern France, Domaine du Mas de Pierre unfolds across gardens where lavender, cypress and birdsong set the rhythm of the day. Honey-toned stone and softly layered interiors nod to Provençal craft without pastiche. Days might mean tasting local wines, wandering scented pathways or slipping into the spa. The kitchen draws from nearby growers, and the estate's grounds are tended with quiet respect for the land itself.

property_title: Susana Balbo: Andean Vineyard Elegance in the Heart of Mendoza
property_intro: Set among the vines of Agrelo, in Mendoza's Luján de Cuyo, this intimate guest house belongs to the winery of Argentina's first female oenologist. Days unfold slowly here: barrel tastings, blending sessions and long lunches shaped by seasonal produce, with the Andes rising beyond the rows. Interiors balance warm timber and considered restraint, while the family's work championing women in wine and supporting local growers gives every glass a deeper story.

property_title: House of Jasmines: Andean Serenity in Argentina's Salta Hills
property_intro: Set among the sun-warmed hills outside Salta, House of Jasmines is a nineteenth-century estancia surrounded by jasmine-scented gardens, pepper trees and views towards the Andes. Once the retreat of actor Robert Duvall, its ten rooms blend colonial character with quiet contemporary comfort. Days unfold slowly here: horseback rides across the finca, tastings of high-altitude Torrontés, long lunches drawn from the kitchen garden, and evenings by the fire as the valley turns violet.

property_title: El Colibri: An Estancia Reverie in Córdoba's Rolling Sierras
property_intro: Set among the grasslands and gentle hills north of Córdoba, El Colibri is a family-run estancia where colonial architecture meets an unhurried rhythm. Days unfold on horseback with the resident gauchos, in the saddle at polo practice, or beside the pool under century-old trees. Interiors pair antique finds with quiet comfort, while kitchen gardens, local artisans and neighbouring producers shape the table. A place to ride out, slow down and belong for a while.

property_title: Hotel Jagdhof: Alpine Warmth in Austria's Stubai Valley
property_intro: Tucked into the Stubai Valley beneath Tyrol's glacier-capped peaks, Hotel Jagdhof is a family-run retreat where hunting-lodge heritage meets quiet contemporary comfort. Weathered timber, hand-carved detail and open fires set the mood, while the spa draws on mountain spring water and local herbs. Days unfold on forest trails and ski slopes, evenings around regional dishes sourced from Stubai farmers. Generations of the same family remain at the helm, and their care for this valley shapes every welcome.

property_title: TXAI Resorts: Barefoot Luxury on Brazil's Untamed Bahia Coast
property_intro: Tucked between Atlantic rainforest and a quiet stretch of Bahian shoreline, TXAI Resorts invites you to slow down entirely. Thatched bungalows rest among coconut palms, shaped by natural timber, local craft and the rhythm of the tides. Days unfold with horse rides along empty sand, canoe trips through mangroves, and treatments drawn from Amazonian botanicals. Behind it all lies genuine commitment: native reforestation, protected turtle nesting grounds and lasting partnerships with the neighbouring fishing community.

property_title: Post Lech: Alpine Heritage and Quiet Luxury in the Arlberg
property_intro: Set at the heart of Lech am Arlberg, where timber chalets meet some of Europe's finest ski terrain, Post Lech has welcomed guests for generations. Family-run and quietly grand, it pairs Tyrolean craftsmanship with panelled rooms, antique-filled lounges and a spa fed by mountain air. Days here might mean powder fields, guided hikes through alpine meadows, or long lunches over Austrian wines. The kitchen champions regional producers, and the village's careful stewardship keeps this valley refreshingly unhurried.

property_title: Zornitza Estate: Bulgaria's Vineyard Sanctuary in the Hills
property_intro: Cradled in the Melnik hills of south-western Bulgaria, Zornitza Estate looks out across its own vineyards towards the Pirin peaks. This Relais & Châteaux retreat pairs contemporary stone-and-glass architecture with heirloom Bulgarian craft, while its kitchen draws on estate gardens and forgotten regional recipes. Days unfold with cellar tastings of rare Shiroka Melnishka wines, walks through sandstone pyramids, and spa hours scented with local herbs. Guests support Melnik's smallholders and the revival of indigenous grape varieties.

property_title: Wickaninnish Inn: Where Pacific Storms Meet Refined Calm
property_intro: Perched on a rocky promontory at the edge of Chesterman Beach, the Wickaninnish Inn sits between old-growth rainforest and the open Pacific on Vancouver Island's wild west coast. Driftwood-inspired interiors, locally crafted furniture and floor-to-ceiling windows draw the weather indoors, making winter storm watching an event worth travelling for. Days unfold with beachcombing, surf lessons and cedar-scented spa rituals, while the kitchen champions Tofino's fishermen, foragers and Nuu-chah-nulth neighbours.

property_title: Ponant: Barefoot Elegance on Cape Verde's Atlantic Shores
property_intro: On the windswept edge of Cape Verde, Ponant sits between volcanic hills and an ocean that seems to change colour by the hour. Interiors draw on island craft — woven textiles, pale timber, local stone — while terraces open to warm trade winds. Days unfold with turtle-nesting walks, sailing across the channel, or slow mornings over pastel de milho. Guides are islanders, produce is grown nearby, and a portion of each stay supports coastal conservation.

property_title: Clos Apalta Residence: Colchagua Valley's Vineyard Sanctuary
property_intro: Tucked into the granite hillsides of Chile's Colchagua Valley, Clos Apalta Residence holds just four casitas above terraced vines of Carmenère and Cabernet Franc. Days unfold with cellar tastings, horseback rides through native forest and long lunches shaped by the estate's kitchen garden. Interiors in stone, wood and glass frame the valley without competing with it, while organic and biodynamic farming, along with protected woodland, keeps this remarkable landscape thriving for generations to come.

property_title: Tswalu: Kalahari Solitude Where Wild Spaces Breathe Freely
property_intro: Set within South Africa's largest private protected area, Tswalu unfolds across the red dunes and golden grasses of the southern Kalahari. Here, days are shaped by your own curiosity rather than a timetable: tracking pangolin and meerkat with expert guides, riding out at dawn, or simply watching black-maned lions from a shaded terrace. Interiors blend earthy textures with quiet comfort, while the Tswalu Foundation channels research and community partnership into restoring this remarkable desert wilderness.

property_title: Gal Oya Lodge: Wild Frontiers and Quiet Luxury in Sri Lanka
property_intro: Tucked against the boulder-strewn hills of Sri Lanka's least-visited national park, Gal Oya Lodge offers nine stone-and-thatch bungalows scattered across twenty acres of private wilderness. Days unfold with boat safaris in search of swimming elephants, guided walks alongside members of the indigenous Vedda community, and long evenings beneath extraordinary starlight. The lodge works closely with neighbouring villages and supports local conservation efforts, so your stay leaves something meaningful behind in this remarkably untamed corner of the island.

property_title: Grootbos Private Nature Reserve: Where Fynbos Meets the Sea
property_intro: Set high above Walker Bay near Gansbaai, Grootbos looks out across the Atlantic from within 3,500 hectares of ancient milkwood forest and flowering fynbos. Suites and villas are handsomely understated, letting the view and the light do the talking. Days might involve tracking whales, riding horses along empty beaches or botanising with a guide who knows every bloom by name. Behind it all sits a foundation training young South Africans and safeguarding one of the planet's richest floral kingdoms.

property_name: Tsara Komba Luxury Beach & Forest Lodge
property_title: Tsara Komba Lodge: Rainforest Seclusion on Nosy Komba's Shore
property_intro: On the volcanic island of Nosy Komba, between dense forest and the Mozambique Channel, Tsara Komba occupies a hillside of mango trees and birdsong. Ten villas in wood, stone and thatch open to sea views, while lemurs pass through the gardens. Days drift between snorkelling, whale-watching in season and Malagasy-inspired cooking built around island produce. The lodge supports local schools, fishermen and reforestation, so your stay quietly strengthens the community that makes it so memorable.

property_title: Bisma Eight: Ubud's Quietly Refined Retreat Among Rice Fields
property_intro: Tucked along Jalan Bisma, moments from Ubud's markets and temples yet cradled by rice terraces, Bisma Eight is a boutique hideaway of reclaimed teak, hand-cut stone and Japanese soaking tubs. Mornings begin with single-origin coffee at Copper Kitchen, afternoons drift towards the treetop pool, and evenings invite rooftop cocktails as gamelan drifts through the valley. The team works closely with Balinese artisans, farmers and neighbouring villages, so every stay quietly supports the community that shapes it.

property_title: North Island: Seychelles' Rewilded Sanctuary of Granite and Sea
property_intro: Set among ancient granite boulders and takamaka forest in the Seychelles, North Island is an eleven-villa retreat where restoration shapes every detail. Once a coconut plantation, the island has been carefully returned to its natural state, welcoming back giant tortoises, white-tailed tropicbirds and hawksbill turtles that nest along its shores. Villas of driftwood and thatch open to the Indian Ocean, while days unfold through diving, forest walks and conversations with the conservation team.

property_title: Shinta Mani Mustang: Himalayan Heights, Thoughtfully Grounded
property_intro: High in Nepal's Jomsom valley, where the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri massifs frame an ancient salt-trade route, Shinta Mani Mustang offers 29 suites shaped by Bill Bensley's playful reverence for Thakali craft and colour. Days unfold with guided walks to cliffside monasteries, apple-orchard tastings and conversations with local families, before wood fires and long soaks in deep tubs. A portion of every stay supports the Shinta Mani Foundation, funding education and livelihoods across the surrounding mountain villages.

property_title: Sussurro: Barefoot Luxury on Mozambique's Whispering Shores
property_intro: Tucked between a tidal lagoon and the Indian Ocean near Morrungulo, Sussurro is a study in quiet craftsmanship. Seven earth-toned suites, built from local timber, lime and stone, open onto dunes where fishermen still cast by hand. Days drift between dhow sailing, snorkelling coral gardens and long, unhurried lunches shaped by the day's catch. Sussurro works closely with neighbouring villages, employing and training locally, so your stay quietly strengthens the community that surrounds it.

property_title: Tri Lanka: Lakeside Serenity Among Koggala's Cinnamon Groves
property_intro: Set above the still waters of Lake Koggala on Sri Lanka's southern coast, Tri Lanka unfolds across a hillside cinnamon plantation, its architecture shaped by the golden ratio and built with recycled teak, local stone and living green roofs. Days here drift between spice-garden walks, yoga in the treetop pavilion, Ayurvedic treatments and boat trips to island temples. Solar power, rainwater harvesting and close ties with village artisans make the pleasure feel genuinely earned.

property_title: Wa Ale Resort: Barefoot Luxury in Myanmar's Wild Mergui
property_intro: On a protected island in Myanmar's remote Mergui Archipelago, Wa Ale Resort sits between jungle-clad hills and a beach where turtles return each year to nest. Ten tented villas and treetop hideaways are crafted from reclaimed timber, opening to the Andaman Sea. Days drift between kayaking mangrove creeks, snorkelling untouched reefs and dining on Burmese flavours. Profits support the Lampi Foundation, funding marine research, ranger patrols and schools across neighbouring fishing villages.

property_title: Nikoi Private Island: Where Indonesia's Wild Sea Meets the Calm
property_intro: Scattered with granite boulders and fringed by reef, Nikoi lies a short boat ride from Bintan in Indonesia's Riau Archipelago. Open-sided beach houses, built from driftwood, alang-alang thatch and local stone, invite the breeze indoors. Days drift between sailing, snorkelling, forest walks and long lunches with island-grown produce. Much of the island remains untouched, and guest stays help fund the Island Foundation, supporting education and livelihoods in neighbouring fishing villages.

property_title: Cempedak Island: Barefoot Bamboo Luxury in Indonesia's Riau
property_intro: Scattered off the coast of Bintan, Cempedak Island is an adults-only retreat where handcrafted bamboo villas rise above granite boulders and the South China Sea. Days unfold with tidal-flat walks, sailing on traditional pinisi-style boats and long lunches shaped by the island's own gardens. Solar power, rainwater harvesting and a marine conservation programme underpin it all, while local craftspeople from nearby villages have shaped every curve of the architecture.

property_title: Nay Palad Hideaway: Barefoot Luxury on Siargao's Untamed Coast
property_intro: On the palm-fringed edge of Siargao, where the Pacific rolls in over reef and rock pools, Nay Palad Hideaway offers just nine handcrafted villas shaped by local artisans from bamboo, driftwood and thatch. Days unfold without a schedule: island-hopping to Sohoton's lagoons, surfing at dawn, or dining wherever the mood takes you. Staffed almost entirely by neighbouring villagers, with reef protection and school support at its heart, this is generous, unhurried, barefoot living.

property_title: NIHI Sumba: Wild Shores, Ancient Culture and Barefoot Luxury
property_intro:
On the untamed southwestern coast of Sumba, NIHI sits above a legendary surf break, where thatched villas of timber and alang-alang grass open to the Indian Ocean. Days unfold with bareback rides along the sand, treks to Nihi Oka's waterfalls and afternoons in the spa above the cliffs. A remarkable portion of proceeds supports the Sumba Foundation, funding clinics, clean water and schools across the island 
inome as guests, part of something larger.

property_title: Three Camel Lodge: Gobi Desert Wilderness, Rooted in Mongolia
property_intro: Set against the volcanic outcrops of Mongolia's Gobi, Three Camel Lodge is a gathering of handcrafted gers built without a single nail, in keeping with nomadic tradition. Days unfold among dinosaur fossil beds, singing sand dunes and the herding families who have shaped this land for centuries. Evenings bring local cuisine, throat singing and skies extravagant with stars. The lodge invests in conservation, education and craft, ensuring the desert's future belongs to those who call it home.

property_title: Misool: A Private Island Sanctuary in Raja Ampat's Coral Seas
property_intro: Set on a remote island in southern Raja Ampat, Misool is reached only by boat across water so clear the reef seems suspended beneath you. Timber cottages stand on stilts above the lagoon, built by local craftsmen using reclaimed ironwood. Days unfold between dive sites teeming with life, kayaking through limestone karsts and long afternoons in a hammock. The surrounding marine reserve, patrolled by rangers from neighbouring villages, is protected by the resort itself.

property_title: The Headwaters Eco Lodge: Glenorchy's Quiet Alpine Sanctuary
property_intro: At the head of Lake Wakatipu, where the Rees and Dart rivers spill from the mountains, The Headwaters Eco Lodge sits lightly on regenerating wetland in tiny Glenorchy. Timber-clad suites, off-grid systems and locally made furnishings frame views of the Humboldt Range, while days unfold into guided walks, horse trekking and long soaks under southern stars. Profits support native planting and community projects, so your stay quietly restores the valley that surrounds you.

property_title: One&Only Moonlight Basin: Where Montana's Big Sky Awakens You
property_intro: Tucked into the forested slopes of Montana's Madison Range, One&Only Moonlight Basin sits within a vast private wilderness beside Big Sky's celebrated ski terrain. Timber-and-stone lodges and generous villas frame views of Lone Peak, while days unfold with fly-fishing, horseback trails, powder mornings and evenings spent beneath extraordinarily dark skies. Menus lean on Rocky Mountain producers, and conservation partnerships protect the surrounding habitat and wildlife corridors, so your stay quietly supports the valley that makes it so remarkable.

property_title: Mahu Whenua: High-Country Serenity in New Zealand's Southern Alps
property_intro: Set across 53,000 hectares of restored high country between Wanaka and Queenstown, Mahu Whenua is a working merino station turned conservation sanctuary. Four intimate lodges, crafted from schist and native timber, look out over tussock ridgelines and braided valleys. Days unfold on horseback, by mountain bike or heli-picnic among alpine peaks, while evenings bring long-table dinners of Central Otago produce. Every stay supports the country's largest private covenant, protecting this landscape in perpetuity.

property_title: Saffire Freycinet: Tasmania's Coastal Sanctuary of Stillness
property_intro: Overlooking the pink granite peaks of the Hazards and the oyster-rich waters of Great Oyster Bay, Saffire Freycinet sits lightly on Tasmania's east coast. Twenty suites curve into the landscape, their timber and glass framing wilderness rather than competing with it. Wade into the bay to shuck oysters, meet rescued Tasmanian devils in the on-site conservation enclosure, or walk with a guide to Wineglass Bay. Regenerated coastal heathland surrounds you, and local producers shape every plate.

property_title: Longitude 131": Uluru's Red Heart, Seen from Your Own Dune
property_intro: Set among the desert oaks of Australia's Red Centre, Longitude 131" places just sixteen tented pavilions on a lone dune facing Uluru. Each opens to sunrise over the monolith, with interiors that nod to the pioneers and pastoralists who shaped this country. Days unfold through Anangu-guided walks, dinners beneath the Milky Way at Table 131", and quiet hours in the Spa Kinara. Guest contributions support the Australian Wildlife Conservancy's work across the arid interior.

property_title: El Remanso Lodge: Rainforest Living on Costa Rica's Osa Coast
property_intro: On the wild edge of the Osa Peninsula, where primary rainforest tumbles towards the Pacific, El Remanso occupies 63 hectares of protected land beside Corcovado National Park. Hardwood cabins and treetop villas open to birdsong, waterfalls and ocean horizons, while scarlet macaws pass overhead at breakfast. Days might mean canopy climbs, night walks with resident naturalists, or simply the plunge pool. Family-run and solar-powered, the lodge reinvests in local conservation and employs its neighbours.

property_title: Morgan's Rock: Pacific Wilderness and Barefoot Luxury, Nicaragua
property_intro: Set above a private crescent of sand on Nicaragua's Pacific coast, Morgan's Rock unfolds across thousands of acres of tropical dry forest, working farm and protected shoreline. Hardwood bungalows stand on stilts among the canopy, reached by a swaying suspension bridge. Days drift between horse rides, turtle hatchling releases and long lunches grown metres from your table. Reforestation, a hatchery and local employment underpin it all: conservation you can taste, hear and feel from your hammock.

property_title: Metohi Kindelis: A Centuries-Old Cretan Estate in Full Bloom
property_intro: Just beyond Chania, three restored farmhouses stand within a working estate that has been in the same family for four centuries. Here, organic groves of avocado, citrus and olive frame stone-walled suites where whitewashed simplicity meets antique Cretan craftsmanship. Wander the biodynamic gardens with the owners, swim in the spring-fed pool, then dine on produce picked that morning. It is agriculture as hospitality \u2013 unhurried, deeply rooted and quietly remarkable.

property_title: Breac.House: A Considered Coastal Retreat on Donegal's Wild Edge
property_intro: Set above Sheephaven Bay on the Horn Head peninsula, Breac.House looks out towards Muckish and Errigal across a landscape shaped by Atlantic weather. Four guest suites, built from Donegal stone, timber and slate, frame the view and the shifting light. Days here might involve walking empty strands, meeting local makers, or lingering over breakfast of neighbouring farms' produce. Craftspeople from the county furnished every room, and the hosts' knowledge of this coast is generously shared.

property_title: Aristi Mountain Resort: Where Zagori's Stone Villages Whisper
property_intro: Set among the slate roofs of Aristi, high in the Zagori region of Epirus, this family-run retreat looks out over the Astraka peaks and the Vikos Gorge. Rooms are built from local stone and timber, warmed by fires and hand-woven textiles. Days unfold with river swims, guided walks to hidden monasteries and dishes drawn from village growers, while the owners' work protects the surrounding forests and mountain trails for generations to come.

property_title: Vila Planinka: Alpine Stillness in Slovenia's Jezersko Valley
property_intro: Tucked into the Jezersko valley beneath the Kamnik	o Planinka is a quiet ode to Slovenian craftsmanship. Larch, linen and local stone shape interiors warmed by an open hearth, while glacial peaks frame every window. Days unfold with mountain hikes, foraging alongside the chef, or long hours in the herbal steam room. Menus draw on neighbouring farms, and the villa's careful stewardship of this fragile valley means your stay quietly sustains the community that shaped it.

property_title: Zlata Ladjica: Riverside Charm in Ljubljana's Golden Old Town
property_intro: Moored beside the Ljubljanica, a few steps from the Cobblers' Bridge, Zlata Ladjica occupies a lovingly revived merchant house in Ljubljana's old town. Rooms pair original beams and stonework with quietly contemporary Slovenian craft, while the ground-floor bar pours regional wines chosen from small family growers. Wake to café chatter drifting up from the embankment, wander to the Central Market for breakfast, then return to a hush that feels wonderfully private in the city's centre.

property_title: Villa Lena: Creative Living Among Tuscany's Rolling Hills
property_intro: Set within 500 hectares of Tuscan woodland and olive groves near Palaia, Villa Lena is part farmhouse retreat, part artists' residency. Restored 19th-century buildings hold vintage-furnished apartments, while the organic farm supplies the kitchen with vegetables, honey and wine. Days unfold with pasta-making lessons, forest walks and open studios where resident artists work. Children roam freely, dinners stretch late, and guests leave having glimpsed a slower, more considered way of living in the Italian countryside.

property_title: Reschio Estate: Umbrian Hills, Timeless Italian Living Restored
property_intro: Set across 3,000 acres of woodland, olive groves and pasture on the Umbria–Tuscany border, Reschio is a working estate where a tenth-century castle has been coaxed back to life by architect Count Benedikt Bolza and his family. Interiors are made in the on-site workshops, horses are schooled in the classical tradition, and dinner draws on the kitchen garden. Farmhouses have been restored stone by stone, keeping villages, crafts and centuries-old landscapes alive.

property_title: Feynan Ecolodge: Candlelit Nights in Jordan's Ancient Valley
property_intro: Deep within the Dana Biosphere Reserve, Feynan Ecolodge sits among copper-hued hills where Bedouin families have herded goats for generations. Candles light the corridors after dusk, solar power runs the rest, and the rooftop becomes an observatory beneath an unusually dark sky. Days unfold with mountain walks, shepherd's tea and visits to a local copper workshop. Owned by the Royal Society for the Conservation of Nature, the lodge employs its Bedouin neighbours and channels earnings straight back into the valley.

property_title: The Wickaninnish Inn: Storm-Watching on Tofino's Wild Pacific
property_intro: Perched on a rocky promontory where Chesterman Beach meets the open Pacific, this family-run inn on Vancouver Island's west coast has drawn kindred spirits since 1996. Rooms of driftwood-hued timber and local artistry frame ancient rainforest and rolling surf, while winter storms arrive as theatre. Expect cedar-scented spa rituals, foraged coastal cooking and guided walks shaped by Nuu-chah-nulth knowledge. Conservation runs deep here, from shoreline stewardship to lasting partnerships with Tofino's community and its makers.

property_title: Post Ranch Inn: Where Big Sur's Cliffs Meet the Pacific Skies
property_intro: Perched 1,200 feet above the Pacific on California's Big Sur coast, Post Ranch Inn folds into the ridgeline rather than rising above it. Timber and glass lodgings burrow into hillsides and cling to cliff edges, framing whales, condors and fog-laced redwoods. Days unfold with guided nature walks, stargazing, spa rituals and produce-led dining at Sierra Mar. Solar power, native replanting and careful stewardship of this fragile landscape make each stay feel quietly, genuinely earned.

property_title: Playa Viva: Barefoot Luxury on Mexico's Wild Pacific Shore
property_intro: Tucked between an estuary and a stretch of untamed Pacific coast south of Zihuatanejo, Playa Viva feels wonderfully removed from the ordinary. Treehouse casitas and open-air suites are built from local materials, powered by the sun and cooled by sea breezes. Days unfold with horseback rides along the sand, turtle releases at dusk and long, unhurried meals sourced from the property's own permaculture farm. Behind it all lies a working commitment to regeneration and the neighbouring village of Juluchuca.

property_title: Fogo Island Inn: Where Newfoundland's Wild Edge Feels Like Home
property_intro: Perched on stilts above the rocks of Newfoundland's northern shore, Fogo Island Inn looks out across the North Atlantic, where icebergs drift past in spring and whales surface in summer. Every room faces the sea; every chair, quilt and table was made by island hands. Wander with a local guide, forage on the barrens, or sit by the fire with a book. All operating surplus returns to the community, sustaining a way of life centuries in the making.

property_title: Briqueterie Champagne: Refined Calm Amid the Vineyard Slopes
property_intro: Set among the vine-striped slopes of Champagne, Briqueterie is a former brickworks reimagined as a quietly elegant retreat. Beneath its handsome red-brick façade you'll find a spa carved into the old cellars, a kitchen devoted to Marne-grown produce, and cellar visits with the growers who tend nearby parcels. Cycle between villages, taste chalk-fresh cuvées at dusk, then settle in beside the fire. Warm, unhurried and deeply rooted in its terroir.

property_title: Purs: Quiet Refinement on the Banks of the Rhine in Andernach
property_intro: In the old heart of Andernach, where the Rhine slips past one of Germany's most venerable town walls, Purs occupies a cluster of restored merchants' houses reimagined by Belgian designer Axel Vervoordt. Rough plaster, aged timber and considered emptiness set the mood; just eleven rooms keep things intimate. Downstairs, Michelin-starred cooking draws on Eifel farms and Mosel vineyards. Wander to the geyser, cycle the riverbank, then return to a courtyard hush that feels entirely your own.

property_title: Jagdhof Glashuette: Forest Serenity in Bavaria's Quiet Hills
property_intro: Tucked into the wooded hills near Passau, Jagdhof Glashuette is a former hunting lodge where Bavarian craftsmanship meets genuine calm. Hand-carved timber, antique glassware and open hearths set the mood, while forest bathing, spring-fed pools and a spa drawing on local herbs invite you to slow right down. Kitchens favour produce from neighbouring farms, and woodland walks begin at the door. Evenings end with regional wines and the particular hush that only deep forest brings.

property_title: Villino: Lakeside Calm and Quiet Character on Lake Constance
property_intro: Set within a leafy garden a short stroll from the shores of Lake Constance, Villino is a family-run retreat where every room tells its own story, layered with hand-picked antiques, textiles and colour. Days unfold between the vineyards and orchards of Lindau, the spa's herb-scented steam rooms and a kitchen that draws on neighbouring growers and producers. Cycle the lakeside paths, swim before breakfast, then linger over dinner beneath the pergola as evening settles.

property_title: Weissenhaus: Baltic Beaches, Manor Grandeur and Wild Woodland
property_intro: Set along a private stretch of Baltic coast in Schleswig-Holstein, Weissenhaus unfolds across a restored 18th-century estate of meadows, beech woodland and dunes. Guest rooms occupy the manor house, thatched cottages and old farm buildings, each thoughtfully renewed rather than rebuilt. Days pass with sea swims, forest walks, spa hours and dinners drawn from the estate's own gardens. Rewilding projects and local craftsmanship underpin it all, quietly and without fanfare.

property_title: Eliamos: Kefalonia's Olive-Grove Sanctuary by the Ionian Sea
property_intro: Tucked into the hillsides of southern Kefalonia, Eliamos sits amid centuries-old olive trees, with the Ionian shimmering below and Mount Ainos rising behind. Stone-built suites open onto private terraces, their interiors shaped by local craftsmanship and quiet restraint. Days unfold slowly here: spa rituals with island botanicals, dinners drawn from the kitchen garden and neighbouring farms, sunset swims at Lourdas beach. It is a place that gives back to its landscape, and to those who linger.

property_title: Villa Bokeh: Antigua's Refined Retreat Beneath the Volcanoes
property_intro: Set within walled gardens on the edge of Antigua, Villa Bokeh looks out to the Agua volcano and the cobbled streets of Guatemala's colonial heart. Just eleven suites, filled with Guatemalan textiles, antiques and locally made ceramics, surround a heated pool and orchard. Days might involve coffee tasting with nearby growers, cacao workshops or riding into the highlands. The kitchen champions regional producers, while the villa supports local artisans and the community that shapes it.

property_title: Ballyfin Demesne: Regency Splendour in Ireland's Green Heartland
property_intro: Set within 614 acres of woodland, lake and parkland at the foot of the Slieve Bloom Mountains, Ballyfin is a Regency house brought back from ruin through years of painstaking craftsmanship. Only twenty rooms mean the estate feels entirely your own: mornings spent rowing, riding or clay shooting, afternoons in the conservatory with a book. Gardens and glasshouses supply the kitchen, while local artisans and skills sustained the restoration and continue to shape life here.

property_title: Cashel Palace: Georgian Splendour Beneath the Rock of Cashel
property_intro: In the heart of County Tipperary, this 18th-century Palladian house rests in the shadow of the Rock of Cashel, once home to the kings of Munster. Twenty-eight acres of restored gardens supply the kitchen, while original panelling and plasterwork sit alongside quietly contemporary interiors. Walk the Bishop's Path to the medieval ruins, fish the Suir, or settle into the spa. Local craftspeople shaped much of what you'll touch here.

property_title: Liss Ard Estate: Lakeside Serenity on the Wild Edge of West Cork
property_intro: Just beyond Skibbereen, Liss Ard Estate unfolds across 160 acres of woodland, meadow and lake shore, where paths wind past oaks planted generations ago. Rooms in the Victorian country house and garden lodges are quietly composed, letting the landscape lead. Wander to James Turrell's Irish Sky Garden, a grass crater framing the changing West Cork light, then return for dinner drawn from nearby farms and waters. Wildflower meadows and native planting are tended with patient care.

property_title: Villa Della Pergola: Alassio's Historic Gardens by the Sea
property_intro: Set above the bay of Alassio on the Ligurian Riviera, Villa Della Pergola is an Anglo-Italian residence surrounded by gardens that shelter Europe's largest collection of agapanthus alongside centuries-old wisteria and citrus groves. Restored with care by a local foundation, the villa welcomes guests into frescoed rooms and shaded terraces where the Mediterranean glitters below. Wander the botanical paths at dusk, dine on Ligurian produce, and let the sea breeze set the pace of your days.

property_title: Grand Hotel Villa Serbelloni: A Lake Como Legend Reimagined
property_intro: Poised on Bellagio's headland where Lake Como divides, this nineteenth-century villa has welcomed guests since 1873 with frescoed salons, Murano chandeliers and terraces that open onto water and mountains. Wander gardens shaded by cedars and camellias, swim in the lakeside pool, or dine on Michelin-starred Lombard cooking sourced from nearby producers. Long-standing ties with Bellagio's artisans and boatmen shape the experience, offering a quieter, more considered way to know this shoreline.

property_title: Hotel Hermitage: Elban Shores, Pine Groves and Quiet Luxury
property_intro: Set along the sheltered bay of Biodola on the island of Elba, Hotel Hermitage sits between Tuscan pine woods and a long stretch of pale sand. Days unfold slowly here: sailing across the Tyrrhenian, tasting Elban wines grown on granite slopes, or wandering coastal paths once walked by Napoleon. Interiors nod to maritime Tuscany with linen, timber and terracotta, while the kitchen draws on island growers and day-boat fishermen who have supplied the family for generations.

property_title: Hotel Cappella: Quiet Italian Luxury Rooted in Its Landscape
property_intro: Set among olive groves and gentle hills, Hotel Cappella invites you to slow down in a corner of Italy still shaped by its seasons. Interiors pair restored stone with contemporary craft, much of it made by artisans a short drive away. Days unfold with vineyard walks, market mornings and long dinners built around produce from the estate gardens. Regenerative farming and local partnerships keep the surrounding countryside thriving, well beyond your stay.

property_title: L'Albereta: Sparkling Franciacorta Hills and Lake Iseo Views
property_intro: Set among the vine-striped slopes of Franciacorta, L'Albereta occupies a 19th-century country residence gazing towards Lake Iseo and Monte Orfano. Rooms and suites blend heirloom furniture with contemporary calm, while the kitchen draws on the estate's own gardens and neighbouring growers. Days unfold slowly: cellar tastings with the Moretti family's sparkling wines, cycling between vineyards, or restorative treatments at the celebrated wellness centre. It is a place where Lombard hospitality feels genuinely personal, unhurried and quietly generous.

property_title: Villa Abbazia: Timeless Italian Calm Among Ancient Olive Groves
property_intro: Set within a restored monastic estate, Villa Abbazia unfolds among ancient olive groves, vineyards and stone terraces that have shaped this corner of Italy for centuries. Interiors pair vaulted ceilings and frescoed alcoves with linen, lime plaster and locally made furniture. Days might begin with harvest walks or slow cookery lessons led by neighbouring farmers, and end beside the pool as swifts circle the bell tower. Regenerative farming and local craftsmanship quietly underpin everything here.

property_title: Il Bottaccio: Sculpture, Marble and Tuscan Coastal Stillness
property_intro: Tucked between the marble-veined Apuan Alps and the Versilia coast, Il Bottaccio occupies an eighteenth-century olive mill in Montignoso, where spring water still runs beneath vaulted stone. Contemporary sculpture sits alongside original millstones, and suites open onto gardens scented with citrus and jasmine. Days unfold slowly: kitchen gardens supplying the table, tastings of local olive oil, quiet excursions to Carrara's quarries and hilltop villages. Owner-led, deeply rooted in its valley, and quietly extraordinary.

property_title: Il San Corrado Di Noto: Baroque Serenity in Sicily's South
property_intro: Set among olive groves and dry-stone walls on the edge of Noto, Il San Corrado occupies a restored 18th-century villa where honeyed limestone meets contemporary Sicilian craft. Days unfold slowly here: swimming beneath carob trees, dining on produce from the estate's own gardens, tracing the Baroque streets and Vendicari's coastal wetlands nearby. Local artisans shaped much of the interiors, while the surrounding land is farmed with quiet care, deepening the sense of belonging to this remarkable corner of Sicily.

property_title: Il Borro: A Restored Tuscan Village Among Vines and Olive Groves
property_intro: Tucked into the hills of Valdarno, between Florence and Arezzo, Il Borro is a medieval hamlet brought gently back to life by the Ferragamo family. Stone cottages, artisan workshops and a organic wine estate sit within 1,700 acres of vineyards, woodland and olive groves. Days might mean riding through the valley, foraging with the chef, or tasting Super Tuscans in the cellars. Farming here is fully organic, and craft traditions are kept alive by resident makers.

property_title: Petra Segreta Resort: Sardinia's Hilltop Sanctuary of Stone
property_intro: Tucked into the granite hills above San Pantaleo, Petra Segreta Resort looks across juniper, myrtle and olive groves towards the distant glimmer of the Costa Smeralda. Stone-built suites, hand-crafted by Sardinian artisans, open onto terraces scented with wild herbs. Days unfold slowly here: walks through the maquis, treatments drawing on island botanicals, and dinners built around produce from the kitchen garden and nearby growers. It is Sardinia at its most quietly authentic.

property_title: The C\u014dmodo: Alpine Soul and Slow Living in Bad Gastein
property_intro: Set in the Salzburg valley of Bad Gastein, The C\u014dmodo occupies a lovingly revived 1960s hotel where mid-century lines meet mountain calm. Days unfold with thermal springs, forest trails and ski runs on the doorstep, before returning to a sauna, a record on the turntable, or a plate built around Austrian growers and foragers. Local craftspeople shaped much of the interior, and the mountains beyond invite you to slow down and simply be present.

property_title: Rote Wand: Alpine Craftsmanship in Austria's Lech Valley
property_intro: Tucked into the meadows of Zug, a hamlet above Lech, Rote Wand has been shaped by the same family for generations. Larchwood chalets and a centuries-old Schualhus set the scene for dining that draws on Vorarlberg's farmers, cheesemakers and foragers. Days unfold on the Arlberg's slopes and high pastures; evenings turn to the fondue table, the wine cellar and the sauna. A house where mountain tradition feels genuinely lived rather than staged.

property_title: Twelve Senses Retreat: Mindful Luxury on the Encinitas Coast
property_intro: Tucked into the flower-growing hills of Encinitas, moments from the Pacific, Twelve Senses Retreat invites you to slow down without giving up comfort. Rooms are calm and considered, with organic linens, artisan touches and light that shifts with the day. Mornings might begin with sound healing, breathwork or yoga; afternoons with farm-fresh plates and a barefoot wander to the surf. Solar power, thoughtful sourcing and close ties with local growers and healers shape everything here.

property_title: Hotel Healdsburg: Sonoma Wine Country Calm on the Town Plaza
property_intro: Set on Healdsburg's leafy plaza, where Sonoma's Dry Creek, Alexander and Russian River valleys meet, this understated retreat pairs clean-lined interiors with redwood, stone and locally made craft. Days drift from the saltwater pool to the spa's vineyard-inspired treatments, then to Chef Charlie Palmer's kitchen, where growers and winemakers are named on the menu. Cycle to family-run cellars, browse the farmers' market, and return to rooms filled with soft northern light.

property_title: Almyra: Sunlit Seaside Serenity on Cyprus's Paphos Coast
property_intro: Overlooking Paphos harbour and the Mediterranean beyond, Almyra pairs clean, contemporary design with the easy rhythm of the Cypriot coast. Sea-facing rooms open onto private terraces, while roof gardens, four pools and a cliffside spa invite unhurried days. Dine on Cypriot flavours drawn from island growers, join a diving lesson or explore the UNESCO-listed mosaics nearby. Committed to protecting nesting turtles and supporting local artisans, Almyra offers luxury that feels genuinely rooted in its place.

property_title: Five Seas Hotel: Cannes Elegance Just Steps From La Croisette
property_intro: Tucked into a quiet street moments from La Croisette, Five Seas Hotel brings a collector's spirit to the heart of Cannes. Interiors weave travel-inspired craftsmanship with Riviera light, while the rooftop pool frames views across terracotta rooftops to the Esterel hills. Days drift between the spa's Cinq Mondes rituals, Provençal markets and film-festival buzz. Locally sourced menus, family ownership and long-standing ties to Cannois artisans give this intimate address a genuinely rooted charm.

property_title: Louis Hotel: Munich's Refined Retreat Above the Viktualienmarkt
property_intro: Overlooking Munich's bustling Viktualienmarkt, Louis Hotel places you at the heart of the city's culinary life, where market traders have sold produce since 1807. Interiors pair natural oak, limestone and handwoven textiles with quiet Bavarian restraint, and balconies open onto the square below. Breakfast celebrates regional producers just steps away, while the rooftop Japanese restaurant offers a different perspective entirely. The Residenz, Hofbräuhaus and Englischer Garten sit within an easy stroll.

property_title: Manna: Modernist Serenity Amid Arcadia's Ancient Fir Forests
property_intro: High on Mount Mainalo, where fir forests hush the Arcadian air, a 1920s sanatorium has been reimagined as Manna. Rough stone and warm timber frame long views across the Peloponnese, while fires crackle, thermal waters steam and the kitchen draws on produce from neighbouring villages. Days unfold slowly here: forest walks, mountain trails, conversations that linger. Restored with care and staffed by locals, it gives quiet purpose to a corner of Greece few travellers reach.

property_title: Athenaeum InterContinental: Where Athens Art Meets Wide Sky Views
property_intro: On Syngrou Avenue, moments from the Acropolis and the coast road to Sounio, the Athenaeum InterContinental gathers over 750 works by Greek artists across its marble-cool interiors, making a stay here feel closer to a gallery visit. Days drift between the rooftop pool, contemporary Hellenic cooking and long views over the city to the Saronic Gulf. Thoughtful energy and water initiatives, plus partnerships with local producers and charities, keep its Athenian roots firmly in view.

property_title: Laluna: Barefoot Balinese Serenity on Grenada's Quiet Shore
property_intro: Tucked above a crescent of pale sand on Grenada's south-western coast, Laluna pairs Balinese craftsmanship with Caribbean ease. Hand-carved teak, batik textiles and open-air cottages tumble down the hillside towards Portici Beach, where the water is warm and the pace unhurried. Days might involve yoga in the treetop shala, chocolate-making with island growers, or dinners built around produce from the kitchen garden. Locally staffed and quietly protective of its shoreline, it feels less like a hotel than a well-kept secret.

property_title: Sextantio Le Grotte Della Civita: Matera's Candlelit Cave Stays
property_intro: Carved into the limestone flank of Matera's Sassi, these ancient cave dwellings gaze across the ravine towards the Murgia plateau. Rooms are lit by candles and warmed by wool blankets, furnished with salvaged pieces that honour Basilicata's rural past rather than dressing it up. Breakfast is served in a deconsecrated chapel, using produce from nearby growers. A pioneering restoration project, it returned life and livelihoods to a quarter once abandoned, and invites you to sleep inside its story.

property_title: Iki Retreat Kairi Murakami: Island Calm on Japan's Genkai Sea
property_intro: On Iki Island, a scattering of green in the Genkai Sea off Kyushu, Iki Retreat Kairi Murakami looks out across water that has carried traders and fishermen for centuries. Rooms are quietly composed in local timber and stone, each with its own hot-spring bath drawn from the island's onsen. Days unfold with shore walks, island-grown produce and Iki beef at the table, and evenings spent under famously dark, star-strewn skies alongside welcoming island hosts.

property_title: Es Racó d'Artà: Barefoot Slow Living on Mallorca's Wild Coast
property_intro: Set within a vast private estate on Mallorca's untamed north-east, Es Racó d'Artà unfolds between pine-clad hills, olive terraces and the Llevant mountains. Restored stone buildings hold sunlit rooms of lime plaster and linen, while days drift between spring-fed pools, mountain trails and yoga at dawn. The kitchen draws on the estate's own gardens and orchards, and rewilding work quietly returns native habitats. A place to slow down, breathe deeply and rediscover the island's older rhythms.

property_title: Elvicenc: Slow Living Among Catalonia's Vines and Stone Walls
property_intro: Tucked into the gentle folds of the Catalan countryside, Elvicenc is a restored farmhouse where centuries-old stone meets considered contemporary design. Days here unfold slowly: breakfast beneath the fig tree, walks through vineyards and cork oak woodland, evenings spent with wines from neighbouring growers. The owners work closely with local artisans and farmers, and much of what reaches the table is grown within sight of the terrace. A quietly generous retreat for those who travel with intention.

property_title: Anayela: Poetry, Patios and the Heart of Marrakech's Old Medina
property_intro: Tucked down a quiet derb in Marrakech's old medina, Anayela is a restored 19th-century riad where a young bride's love letters, discovered during renovation, inspired every room. Zellige-lined courtyards, citrus trees and candlelit rooftop dinners set the mood, while the family's schooling and training initiatives support neighbours just beyond the door. Wander the souks with someone who knows them intimately, then return to cool tadelakt walls and the scent of orange blossom.

property_title: Rabot Hotel: Cocoa-Scented Seclusion in Saint Lucia's Hills
property_intro: Set within a working cocoa estate above Soufrière, Rabot Hotel looks out to the Pitons through a canopy of rainforest and fruit trees. Timber lodges open to the breeze, hammocks sway above the valley, and days unfold with cocoa-pod picking, bean-to-bar workshops and swims beneath waterfalls. The kitchen draws on the estate's harvest and neighbouring farms, while replanting and local employment keep the plantation's heritage alive. A rare place where indulgence and cultivation grow side by side.

property_title: The Cambrian: Alpine Calm Above the Rooftops of Adelboden
property_intro: Perched on a sunlit ledge above Adelboden, The Cambrian looks out across the Engstligen valley to a horizon of snow-dusted peaks. Interiors pair Swiss timber with mid-century restraint, while the outdoor pool steams gently against the mountain air. Days unfold with guided hikes, cheese-makers' visits and long soaks in the spa. Family-run in spirit, the hotel champions regional producers and Bernese Oberland craftsmanship, making every stay quietly rooted in its valley.

property_title: CERVO Mountain Resort: Zermatt's Warm Alpine Hideaway
property_intro: Perched above Zermatt with the Matterhorn filling the windows, CERVO gathers a cluster of timber chalets into something closer to a village than a hotel. Days begin with skis clicked on at the door and end in Onsen-inspired baths, Peruvian-Nikkei plates or a glass poured beside the fire. Reclaimed wood, locally sourced ingredients and a car-free valley shape the experience, as does a team who treat guests as neighbours rather than visitors.

property_title: Setouchi Retreat: Island Calm on Japan's Inland Sea Shores
property_intro:
Cradled by the gentle islands of Japan's Seto Inland Sea, Setouchi Retreat looks out across mirror-still water dotted with pine-topped isles. Interiors draw on local craft 
and quiet cedar and washi, while wide terraces invite long, unhurried mornings. Days might bring cycling coastal lanes, a boat to nearby art islands, or a kitchen table laid with citrus, sea bream and olive oil from neighbouring groves. Fishing families and artisans here shape every stay, keeping island traditions alive.

property_title: Duchi D'Aosta: Habsburg Grandeur on Trieste's Seafront Square
property_intro: Facing the vast Piazza Unità d'Italia, where Trieste opens directly onto the Adriatic, Duchi D'Aosta occupies a handsome nineteenth-century palazzo layered with Habsburg detail and contemporary comfort. Frescoed ceilings, Murano glass and warm timber set the mood; below, a vaulted Roman-era cellar houses the spa. Days drift between literary cafés, Carso vineyards and family-run osterie, guided by staff who know the city intimately. Regional producers shape the kitchen, honouring Trieste's crossroads of Italian, Slovenian and Austrian flavours.

property_title: Londra Palace: Venetian Grandeur on the Riva degli Schiavoni
property_intro: Overlooking the lagoon along the Riva degli Schiavoni, Londra Palace has welcomed writers, composers and curious wanderers since the 1850s \composed here. Its hundred windows frame St Mark's Basin, while interiors blend Biedermeier antiques with contemporary Venetian craftsmanship. Days unfold with rowing lessons in a traditional batela, visits to island workshops, or lingering over Michelin-recognised cooking at Do Leoni. Committed to sustaining local artisans and the fragile lagoon, it offers a Venice experienced slowly, thoughtfully and rather personally.

property_title: Monaci Delle Terre Nere: Life on Etna's Black-Earth Vineyards
property_intro: On Mount Etna's northern slopes, this 19th-century manor sits amid organic vineyards, orchards and lava-strewn terraces, where Sicily's volcanic soils give wine its smoky depth. Rooms blend antique Sicilian craft with contemporary art and salvaged materials, while dinners draw from the estate's own gardens. Days unfold with barefoot walks through olive groves, cellar tastings and guided ascents towards the crater. Biodynamic farming and long-standing local partnerships keep this quietly generous corner of the island thriving.

property_title: Beniya Mukayu: Stillness, Hot Springs and Kaga Craft Artistry
property_intro: Tucked into the wooded hills of Yamashiro Onsen in Ishikawa, Beniya Mukayu takes its name from a Noh phrase suggesting graceful emptiness 	he room mine"

property_title: Tenku: Where Japan's Mountain Skies Meet Quiet Refinement
property_intro: High among Japan's forested slopes, Tenku offers a rare kind of stillness. Timber-framed rooms open onto valleys that shift with each season, while cedar-scented onsen waters invite long, unhurried soaks. Days here might mean walking ancient pilgrim paths, learning the craft of local artisans, or lingering over kaiseki shaped by nearby farms. Built with regional materials and tended by families who have long called these mountains home, Tenku feels less like a retreat and more like an invitation.

property_title: Enowa-Yufuin: Thermal Waters, Mountain Air and Quiet Artistry
property_intro: Tucked beneath the twin peaks of Mount Yufu in Kyushu's hot-spring valley, Enowa-Yufuin gathers art, agriculture and geothermal water into one considered whole. Rooms open onto rice terraces and private onsen baths; meals draw on the estate's own farm and Oita's fishermen and growers. Wander the sculpture-dotted grounds, join a seasonal harvest, then linger in the sauna as mist settles over the fields. A stay that feels rooted, unhurried and genuinely of its place.

property_title: Park Hotel Sonnenhof: Alpine Serenity Above Vaduz's Vineyards
property_intro: Perched above Vaduz amid terraced vineyards and its own wooded park, Park Hotel Sonnenhof looks across the Rhine Valley to the Swiss peaks beyond. Family-run for generations, this Liechtenstein retreat pairs quietly elegant rooms with a kitchen devoted to regional producers, from Alpine cheeses to wines pressed a short stroll away. Days unfold with mountain walks from the doorstep, afternoons in the spa, and evenings watching the valley light soften over the princely castle.

property_title: Otahuna Lodge: A Victorian Estate Amid Canterbury's Gardens
property_intro: Set within 30 hectares of gardens and native woodland just beyond Christchurch, Otahuna Lodge occupies one of New Zealand's finest Victorian homesteads, lovingly restored to its 1895 grandeur. Seven suites open onto lawns where daffodils carpet the hillside each spring. Days unfold with truffle hunting, kitchen-garden harvests and long lunches shaped by the estate's own produce, while replanting programmes gradually return indigenous bush to the Halswell Valley. Dinner is served at a single table, by candlelight.

property_title: Blanket Bay: Alpine Grandeur on the Shores of Lake Wakatipu
property_intro: Tucked beneath the Humboldt Mountains on the quiet northern reaches of Lake Wakatipu, Blanket Bay feels wonderfully far from anywhere, yet sits within easy reach of Queenstown. Schist stone and native timber frame vast windows and open fires, while days unfold with heli-picnics on glaciers, fly fishing on braided rivers and walks through beech forest. The surrounding high-country station is carefully stewarded, with native planting and predator control protecting the valley's birdlife for generations to come.

property_title: Hotel Sol y Luna: Andean Grace in Peru's Sacred Valley
property_intro: Set amid eucalyptus groves and terraced fields near Urubamba, Hotel Sol y Luna scatters its casitas across gardens framed by the Andes. Each is individually imagined, filled with the work of Peruvian artists and craftspeople. Days unfold on horseback with Peruvian Paso horses, in the kitchen with valley producers, or simply beneath the mountains. Profits support the neighbouring Sol y Luna school, educating children of the Sacred Valley for generations to come.

property_title: Casa da Calçada: Renaissance Grandeur on the Tâmega Riverbank
property_intro: Overlooking the Tâmega in the granite town of Amarante, this 16th-century manor has been coaxed into gentle modernity, its frescoed salons and antique tiles softened by garden light. Vineyards of the Douro and Vinho Verde begin at the doorstep, ready for tastings, hikes and market mornings alongside local producers. Dinner at the Michelin-starred Largo do Paço draws on the estate's own orchards, while family stewardship keeps regional crafts, recipes and traditions quietly thriving.

property_title: Vermelho Hotel: Artistry and Alentejo Calm in Melides, Portugal
property_intro: In the whitewashed village of Melides, a short cycle from Alentejo's wild Atlantic beaches, Vermelho is Christian Louboutin's love letter to Portuguese craft. Hand-painted azulejos, filigree ironwork and playful antiques fill thirteen individual rooms, each shaped by artisans the hotel continues to champion. Days unfold slowly here: cork oak groves, rice paddies, long lunches at Xtian, and evenings in the courtyard bar among locals. Village life, richly imagined rather than reinvented.

property_title: L'AND: Where the Alentejo's Vineyards Meet a Ceiling of Stars
property_intro: An hour from Lisbon, near the walled town of Montemor-o-Novo, L'AND rests among cork oaks, olive groves and its own working vineyard. Suites open to private courtyards, and retractable roofs invite you to fall asleep beneath the Alentejo's famously dark skies. Days unfold slowly here: tasting estate wines, foraging with the chef, or wandering to Évora. Local stone, clay and craft shape every room, while the kitchen draws on neighbouring farms and long-held regional traditions.

property_title: Valverde Santar: Manor House Living in Dão's Vineyard Country
property_intro: In the village of Santar, at the heart of Portugal's Dão wine region, an eighteenth-century manor has been coaxed gently into its next chapter. Formal gardens laid out by Jacques Gréber unfold towards vines and granite hills, while interiors pair heirloom detail with quiet contemporary calm. Days here might mean tasting cellar-aged Dão reds, walking with the village winemakers, or simply lingering beneath the camellias. A place shaped by local hands, and all the better for it.While()</br>

property_title: Hotel Epoque: Refined Bucharest Living Beside Cișmigiu Gardens
property_intro: Tucked on a quiet street beside Bucharest's Cișmigiu Gardens, Hotel Epoque pairs Belle Époque grace with the ease of a private residence. Just forty-five rooms, each individually dressed in antiques, artwork and locally made textiles, look out over lime trees and lantern-lit lanes. Days begin with Romanian pastries and end with candlelit dinners in the glasshouse restaurant. The team champions small producers and craftspeople, ensuring your stay quietly supports the city that shaped it.

property_title: Matca Hotel: Quiet Romanian Luxury Rooted in Nature and Place
property_intro: Set within Romania's gently rolling countryside, Matca Hotel offers a considered retreat where local craftsmanship shapes every room. Handwoven textiles, reclaimed timber and soft natural light create interiors that feel calm rather than curated. Days unfold slowly here: foraging walks with village guides, seasonal menus drawn from nearby smallholdings, and long evenings beneath uncommonly dark skies. The team works closely with surrounding communities, supporting regional artisans and regenerative farming, so your stay quietly sustains the landscape that surrounds it.

property_title: Grad Otocec: Slovenia's Island Castle on the Krka River
property_intro: Set on its own wooded island in the emerald Krka River, Grad Otocec is Slovenia's only castle hotel — a medieval stronghold reached by stone bridge, where vaulted chambers and antique furnishings meet quietly contemporary comfort. Days unfold with riverside breakfasts, fly-fishing, horse riding across the surrounding estate and tastings of Dolenjska wines from neighbouring vineyards. The kitchen leans on local growers and foragers, while careful restoration keeps the castle's centuries-old character intact for those who notice such things.

property_title: Kendov Dvorec: A Slovenian Manor Where Time Slows Gently
property_intro: Tucked into the village of Spodnja Idrija, beneath wooded hills and mercury-mining heritage, Kendov Dvorec has welcomed guests since the 14th century. Family-run and lovingly restored, its rooms hold hand-embroidered Idrija lace, antique furnishings and quiet views over the Idrijca valley. Dinner draws on garden herbs and neighbouring farms, served in candlelit rooms. Walk to the Wild Lake, learn lacemaking from local artisans, or simply linger over breakfast beneath the chestnut trees.

property_title: Ellerman House: Atlantic Views and Art Above Bantry Bay
property_intro: Perched on the cliffs of Bantry Bay, Ellerman House looks out across the Atlantic towards Robben Island, with Cape Town's city bowl and the winelands within easy reach. This former shipping magnate's residence holds one of the country's finest private collections of South African art, alongside a wine gallery of some 7,500 bottles. Terraced gardens, spa treatments and whale-watching from the pool terrace fill the days, while long-standing conservation partnerships support penguin colonies and local communities.

property_title: Jabulani: Where Elephant Stories Shape Every Kapama Sunrise
property_intro: Set within Kapama Private Game Reserve on the fringes of the Greater Kruger, Jabulani is home to a rescued elephant herd whose presence shapes life here. Six suites and a private villa open onto bushveld, styled with collected antiques, deep verandas and quiet luxury. Days unfold with unhurried game drives, conversations with elephant carers and long dinners beneath acacias, while the neighbouring orphanage and community programmes ensure your stay leaves something lasting behind.

property_title: Londolozi: Where Leopards Roam and Legacy Lives in the Sabi Sand
property_intro: Set along the Sand River in the Sabi Sand Reserve, bordering the Kruger, Londolozi has been shaped by five generations of one family's devotion to restoring this land. Leopards move openly here, habituated over decades of patient tracking with Shangaan guides. Camps blend contemporary calm with deep local craft, while yoga, healing therapies and photographic studios invite slower days. Community schools, conservation training and rewilded riverbanks make every stay quietly consequential.

property_title: Esiweni Lodge: Clifftop Living Above KwaZulu-Natal's Wild Plains
property_intro: Set high on a rocky escarpment in the Nambiti Private Game Reserve, Esiweni Lodge looks out over the Sundays River valley, where elephant and lion move through acacia country far below. Just five glass-fronted suites mean mornings begin quietly, with coffee, binoculars and space to think. Guided drives, walks and battlefield excursions reveal KwaZulu-Natal's layered history, while the reserve's conservation work and local employment ensure your stay leaves something meaningful behind.

property_title: Silvan Safari: Riverine Seclusion in the Heart of the Sabi Sand
property_intro: Hidden within a grove of ancient trees on the banks of the Manyeleti River, Silvan Safari sits in the Sabi Sand Reserve, where leopards move through dappled shade and elephants pass within view of your suite. Six glass-fronted villas balance handcrafted African artistry with quiet contemporary calm.
