Days unfold with expert-led game drives, guided walks and treatments overlooking the riverbed, while the lodge's conservation work and local partnerships give every stay lasting purpose.

property_title: Cap Menorca: Where Mediterranean Calm Meets Island Craft
property_intro: On Menorca's quieter reaches, where dry-stone walls trace the land towards the sea, Cap Menorca offers a gentler rhythm. Interiors pair lime-washed walls with local timber and island ceramics, framing views of pine, scrub and turquoise water. Days unfold with coastal walks along the Camí de Cavalls, boat trips to hidden coves and long lunches built on produce from nearby farms. A UNESCO Biosphere Reserve shapes everything here, from water stewardship to partnerships with Menorcan artisans and growers.

property_title: Helguera Palacio: A Cantabrian Manor Where Time Slows Down
property_intro: Set among the green valleys of Cantabria, Helguera Palacio occupies a restored 18th-century manor where stone walls, beamed ceilings and antique furnishings meet quiet contemporary comfort. Mornings begin with local breads and cheeses from nearby farms; afternoons invite walks through meadows towards the Picos de Europa or the wild beaches of the northern coast. The owners' careful restoration honours traditional craftsmanship and regional producers, offering a genuinely rooted stay rather than a polished imitation of one.

property_title: Mas De Torrent: Timeless Empordà Elegance Among Olive Groves
property_intro: Set among the cypress-lined lanes of Baix Empordà, this restored 18th-century Catalan farmhouse looks out over vineyards, olive groves and the medieval village of Torrent. Interiors pair vaulted stone with contemporary Catalan art, while gardens open onto quiet pools and long lunches beneath the pines. Days might mean cycling to Costa Brava coves, foraging with local chefs, or tasting Empordà wines from neighbouring growers. Produce comes from nearby smallholdings, and craftsmanship here remains proudly, persuasively regional.

property_title: Resplendent Ceylon: Tea Country, Wild Coast and Ancient Trails
property_intro: Spanning Sri Lanka's tea-clad highlands, southern cliffs and the wilds bordering Yala, Resplendent Ceylon's small collection of Relais & Châteaux retreats forms a journey rather than a single stay. Colonial-era planters' bungalows, cocoon-shaped lodges and clifftop villas each answer to their landscape. Days might mean plucking tea at dawn, tracking leopards, or whale-watching off Weligama. Founded by the Dilmah family, profits support the MJF Foundation's community and conservation work across the island, from schools to reforestation.

property_title: Aïda Hôtel & Spa: Alpine Calm, Thoughtfully Reimagined
property_intro: Tucked into the Swiss mountainside, Aïda Hôtel & Spa pairs the quiet confidence of alpine tradition with interiors shaped by local timber, stone and craft. Days unfold slowly here: forest trails at first light, a long soak in the spa, then regional produce served by chefs who know their growers by name. Family-run and firmly rooted in its valley, the hotel supports neighbouring farms and artisans, making every stay feel genuinely connected to the landscape beyond the window.

property_title: Hostellerie Du Pas De L'Ours: Alpine Elegance in Crans-Montana
property_intro: Tucked into the sunlit slopes above the Rhône Valley, this intimate Relais & Châteaux retreat in Crans-Montana pairs weathered alpine timber with quietly considered comfort. Just eleven rooms and suites open to views of the Valais peaks, while the kitchen draws on mountain producers and foraged detail to remarkable effect. Days might begin on the ski lifts or high-altitude trails and end beside a crackling fire, with cheeses, wines and warm Swiss hospitality close at hand.

property_title: Alex Lake Zurich: Lakeside Calm on Switzerland's Gold Coast
property_intro: On the shores of Lake Zurich in Thalwil, Alex Lake Zurich turns its full attention to the water. Every suite and residence opens onto a terrace or balcony above the lake, with kitchenettes, natural materials and warm timber creating the ease of a private apartment. Swim from the hotel's own jetty, borrow an electric boat, or linger over regional produce at the waterfront restaurant. Zurich's centre lies minutes away by train, yet feels agreeably distant.

property_title: Ahama: Barefoot Luxury Among Turkey's Sunlit Aegean Shores
property_intro: Tucked between olive groves and the glittering Aegean, Ahama invites you to slow down. Stone-and-timber interiors echo the surrounding landscape, while shaded terraces open onto sea breezes and birdsong. Days unfold with swims from quiet coves, walks along ancient footpaths and long lunches built around produce from neighbouring farms and family-run kitchens. Local artisans shaped much of what you'll touch here, and the owners' quiet commitment to the coastline ensures this corner remains as unhurried as you found it.

property_title: Pine Cay: A Private Island Retreat in Turks and Caicos
property_intro: Reached only by boat or small plane, Pine Cay is an 800-acre private island edged by two miles of powder-soft shoreline in the Turks and Caicos. There are no cars here, only sandy paths, bicycles and birdsong. Twelve breezy rooms open straight onto the beach, while freshwater ponds shelter nesting waterbirds protected under a long-standing conservation trust. Days drift between reef snorkelling, kitesurfing and long lunches shared with fellow islanders who quickly feel like old friends.

property_title: Pale Hall: Storied Victorian Elegance on the River Dee, Eryri
property_intro: Tucked into the Dee Valley on the fringes of Eryri, Pale Hall is a Victorian mansion powered, since 1920, by its own hydroelectric turbine on the river below. Fifty acres of gardens and woodland surround hand-painted ceilings, panelled corners and eighteen individually dressed rooms. Dinner leans on Welsh growers, foragers and farmers, while walks, wild swims and slate-country drives begin at the door. Queen Victoria slept here; you may find it hard to leave.

property_title: White Sand Villas: Barefoot Luxury on Zanzibar's Shores
property_intro: On Zanzibar's south-eastern coast, where the Indian Ocean shifts between turquoise and glass, White Sand Villas offers a handful of private villas set within palm groves and coral-rag gardens. Each has its own pool, sun-warmed terrace and interiors shaped by Swahili craftsmanship. Days unfold with dhow sails, spice-scented dinners and reef swims guided by local fishermen, while the villas' partnerships with nearby Paje community projects mean your stay contributes to the island beyond its shoreline.

property_title: The Little Nell: Alpine Elegance at the Foot of Aspen Mountain
property_intro: Set at the base of Aspen Mountain, where the gondola waits a few steps from the door, The Little Nell blends mountain-town warmth with quiet sophistication. Interiors layer soft leather, timber and firelight, while ski concierges, wine cellar dinners and summer hikes through the Elk Mountains shape each stay. The hotel's ties to local land trusts and Aspen's arts community run deep, offering guests a genuine sense of place rather than polished detachment.

property_title: The Ivy: Refined American Escapes Rooted in Place and People
property_intro: Tucked between leafy streets and open countryside, The Ivy offers a considered kind of comfort — the sort where mornings begin slowly and evenings linger. Interiors pair heritage architecture with locally made furnishings, while gardens supply the kitchen through the seasons. Guests can walk nearby trails, meet the growers behind their supper, or simply retreat with a book. Partnerships with regional artisans and conservation groups ensure your stay leaves something meaningful behind.

property_title: Bedford Post Inn: Quiet Luxury in Westchester's Horse Country
property_intro: An hour north of Manhattan, in the leafy hamlet of Bedford, this restored 1860s coaching inn sits among stone walls, riding trails and orchards. Eight individually dressed rooms pair beamed ceilings with deep baths and slow mornings. Days unfold across the yoga loft, the farm-led kitchen and long walks through neighbouring reserves, while much of the menu comes from growers within the county. It is the countryside, close enough to reach on a whim.

property_title: Dunton: A Restored Colorado Ghost Town Wrapped in Wilderness
property_intro: Tucked into a remote valley beneath Colorado's San Juan Mountains, Dunton is a 19th-century mining town brought gently back to life. Hand-hewn log cabins hide woodburning stoves, deep baths and thoughtful design, while geothermal hot springs steam beside the Dolores River. Days unfold with fly fishing, horseback rides and backcountry skiing, followed by long dinners in the old saloon. Surrounding land is held in conservation, keeping this valley wild for generations to come.

property_title: The Charlotte Inn: Timeless Martha's Vineyard Elegance Awaits
property_intro: Tucked along a leafy lane in Edgartown, The Charlotte Inn brings the grace of a 19th-century sea captain's home to Martha's Vineyard. English antiques, botanical prints and walled gardens set the tone, while candlelit dinners and unhurried mornings invite you to slow down. Harbour walks, island beaches and local growers are moments away, and the innkeepers' care for the Vineyard's heritage shows in every restored beam, hand-tended border and warm island welcome.

property_title: Old Edwards Inn: Blue Ridge Mountain Charm in Highlands, NC
property_intro: Tucked into the Blue Ridge Mountains in the village of Highlands, North Carolina, Old Edwards Inn brings together stonework, antiques and gardens that have matured over generations. Days here might mean a spa ritual beneath vaulted timber, a round on the Tom Jackson-designed course, or foraging waterfall trails just beyond the gate. The kitchens lean on Appalachian growers, while the inn's stewardship of local land and craft keeps this corner of Carolina quietly, genuinely itself.

property_title: Inn At Hastings Park: Historic Charm on Lexington's Green
property_intro: Set along Lexington's storied Battle Road, moments from where the American Revolution began, Inn At Hastings Park gathers three restored 19th-century buildings around leafy gardens just outside Boston. Interiors layer New England heritage with playful contemporary design, while Artistry on the Green serves seasonal menus sourced from Massachusetts farms. Borrow a bicycle for the Minuteman trail, settle by the fire in the Parlour, and enjoy a village stay shaped by genuine local craftsmanship and warmth.

property_title: Tributary Hotel: Refined Wine Country Living in McMinnville
property_intro: Set on a leafy corner of McMinnville's historic Third Street, Tributary Hotel brings quiet sophistication to Oregon's Willamette Valley. Just twenty guest rooms occupy a thoughtfully restored 1920s building, where warm timber, locally made ceramics and softly layered textures invite you to slow down. Downstairs, an acclaimed kitchen champions Pacific Northwest growers and foragers, while vineyard visits and coastal drives sit temptingly close. Independent boutiques, tasting rooms and Pinot Noir country begin at the doorstep.

property_title: Blackberry Farm: Where Appalachian Farmland Meets Fine Dining
property_intro: Tucked into 4,200 acres at the foot of Tennessee's Great Smoky Mountains, Blackberry Farm is a working farmstead where heritage livestock, kitchen gardens and dry-aging cellars shape every plate. Days unfold with fly fishing, truffle hunts, cookery classes and long walks through wildflower meadows. Interiors nod to English country living, softened by Southern warmth, while the estate's seed-saving, cheesemaking and Foothills Land Conservancy partnership keep this remarkable valley thriving for generations to come.

property_title: Ocean House: Elegant Seaside Living on Rhode Island's Bluffs
property_intro: Perched on the bluffs of Watch Hill, Ocean House looks out across Block Island Sound from a stretch of private Rhode Island shoreline. Behind its clapboard facade lies a faithfully rebuilt landmark, furnished with restored heirlooms and works by regional artists. Days unfold with sailing lessons, coastal foraging walks and croquet on the lawn, while the kitchen gardens and local fishing partnerships shape each menu. Salt air, quiet ceremony and genuine New England warmth throughout.

property_title: The Swag: Mountaintop Seclusion on the Edge of the Smokies
property_intro: Perched at 1,500 metres along a private ridge in North Carolina, The Swag opens directly onto the Great Smoky Mountains National Park through its own gate. Hand-hewn timber cabins, salvaged from centuries-old Appalachian structures, frame views that shift with the mist. Days unfold with guided hikes, wild-foraged tasting menus and evenings beside a woodburning stove. Conservation runs deep here, from protected old-growth forest to partnerships supporting the region's craftspeople and mountain heritage.

property_title: H\u00f4tel Ile De La Lagune: Serene Island Living in Saint-Cyprien
property_intro: Set on its own small island between the Mediterranean and the lagoons of Saint-Cyprien, H\u00f4tel Ile De La Lagune feels pleasingly removed from the everyday. Catalan light fills airy, contemporary rooms, while the Pyrenees rise beyond the water. Days drift between the spa, the pool and the Michelin-starred kitchen, where Roussillon producers shape each menu. Wander the sandy shoreline, sail the coast, or simply watch flamingos gather at dusk across the still, protected wetlands.

property_title: Torfhús Retreat: Turf-Roofed Luxury in Iceland's Golden Circle
property_intro: In the farmlands of southern Iceland, near Skálholt and the Golden Circle, Torfhús Retreat draws on centuries-old building traditions: turf-clad walls, hand-hewn driftwood beams and stone hearths, warmed by geothermal water. Each cottage has its own basalt bathing pool beneath open skies, where winter nights bring the aurora. Days unfold slowly — Icelandic horses, waterfalls, wild herbs gathered for the kitchen. Built by local craftspeople using regional materials, it's a quiet act of cultural preservation you can sleep inside.

property_title: Hotel Villa Sostaga: Hillside Serenity Above Lake Garda's Shores
property_intro: Perched among olive groves and chestnut woods high above Lake Garda, this early twentieth-century villa in Gargnano feels like a private family home rather than a hotel. Frescoed ceilings, antique furnishings and a panoramic terrace set the scene for slow mornings and long, wine-led dinners. Days unfold with guided walks in the Alto Garda park, boat trips to lakeside villages, and cooking sessions built around produce from neighbouring growers and the villa's own garden.

property_title: The Pinnacle Kigali: Elevated Calm Above Rwanda's Capital City
property_intro: Set among the green ridges of Kigali, The Pinnacle rises above a city known for its order, warmth and quiet confidence. Interiors pair Rwandan craftsmanship with generous light and considered comfort, while terraces frame views across the valleys at dusk. Days might begin with locally roasted coffee and end with a chef's tasting menu built around highland produce. Staff, largely drawn from surrounding neighbourhoods, share the stories and makers behind every detail.

property_title: The Lombok Lodge: Barefoot Refinement on Indonesia's Coast
property_intro: Set above the tranquil waters of Medana Bay in northern Lombok, The Lombok Lodge pairs uncluttered contemporary design with genuine Sasak hospitality. Each all-inclusive suite opens to a private pool and views across the strait to the Gili Islands, where snorkelling, sunset sailing and visits to nearby villages fill unhurried days. The kitchen draws on local growers and fishermen, while the lodge invests in island schools and reef care, so your stay quietly supports the community around it.

property_title: Loggers Lodge: Riverside Seclusion in Sweden's Wild North
property_intro: Set beside a slow-moving river in the forests of northern Sweden, Loggers Lodge draws on the region's timber heritage, with hand-built cabins of local pine warmed by wood-fired stoves and lit by long summer evenings. Days pass foraging with local guides, paddling quiet waterways or tracing elk through the pines. Meals celebrate what the surrounding land offers, prepared with neighbouring smallholders, while the forest itself is managed with patience rather than profit in mind.

property_title: Casa Gangotena: Belle Époque Splendour in Quito's Historic Heart
property_intro: Overlooking the flower-filled Plaza San Francisco, this restored 1920s mansion places you at the centre of Quito's UNESCO-listed old town, where church bells and market chatter drift up to your window. Behind its façade lie Art Deco details, a hidden orchid garden and cuisine drawn from Andean growers. The family-run house employs and trains local residents, supports heritage restoration, and guides curious guests through the neighbourhood's chocolate workshops, colonial cloisters and cloud-forest surrounds beyond the city.

property_title: The Fleming: A Maritime-Inspired Retreat in Wan Chai, Hong Kong
property_intro: Tucked into the animated streets of Wan Chai, The Fleming draws its character from Hong Kong's harbour heritage, echoing the ferries that once carried workers across Victoria Harbour. Brass fittings, ribbed green tiles and custom joinery lend each room a quiet, ship-like intimacy. Below, Osteria Marzia serves coastal Italian plates worth lingering over. Refillable amenities, filtered water stations and locally made toiletries reflect a considered approach, while dai pai dongs and tram lines wait just outside.

property_title: W15 Hanthana: Misty Mountain Serenity Above Kandy's Valleys
property_intro: Perched on the Hanthana range above Kandy, W15 Hanthana gazes across tea slopes and forested ridges where morning mist lingers long after sunrise. Glass-fronted suites and clean architectural lines frame the valley, while an infinity pool seems to spill towards the hills. Days unfold with walks to the Peradeniya botanical gardens, temple visits in the old royal city, or unhurried Ceylon tea on your terrace. Local artisans and growers shape much of what you'll taste and admire here.

property_title: W15 Ambuluwawa: Misty Hill Country Serenity Above Gampola Valley
property_intro: Perched on a ridge near the sacred Ambuluwawa peak, just beyond Gampola, W15 Ambuluwawa gazes across tea slopes, paddy terraces and the winding Mahaweli river. Glass-walled suites and cantilevered pools draw the mountain air indoors, while interiors pair local craftsmanship with quiet contemporary lines. Days unfold with sunrise hikes to the tower, visits to village tea smallholdings and slow dinners built around produce grown nearby, supporting the communities who have farmed these hills for generations.

property_title: Crossbasket Castle: Scottish Grandeur Beside the Rushing Calder
property_intro: Set within wooded grounds where the River Calder tumbles over its own waterfall, Crossbasket Castle stands just beyond Glasgow, yet feels worlds away. Centuries of Scottish history have been carefully restored here, from the tower house's spiral stair to hand-painted ceilings and a marble staircase. Expect fine dining, whisky tastings and walks through native woodland, plus close ties with local growers and craftspeople. Come for a celebration, or simply to slow down beautifully.

property_title: Greywalls Hotel: Edwardian Elegance on the East Lothian Coast
property_intro: Set on the edge of Muirfield's famous links, with the Firth of Forth glinting beyond, Greywalls is a Lutyens-designed country house wrapped in walled gardens laid out by Gertrude Jekyll. Log fires, a book-lined library and Chez Roux's seasonal Scottish cooking make lingering easy. Wander to Gullane's beaches, walk the coastal paths, or simply watch the light shift across the herbaceous borders, tended with quiet care by the resident gardeners.

property_title: Inverlochy Castle: Highland Grandeur Beneath Ben Nevis's Gaze
property_intro: Set in the shadow of Ben Nevis, Inverlochy Castle has welcomed guests since Queen Victoria sketched its glens in 1873. Loch and mountain frame every window, while inside, frescoed ceilings and Venetian crystal meet Highland warmth. Days unfold with fly fishing on the River Lochy, foraging walks through native woodland, and dinners built around Scottish estates and coastal boats. It is a house that rewards slowness, and the surrounding wilderness asks little more than your attention.

property_title: Foxhill Manor: Your Private Arts and Crafts Cotswolds Retreat
property_intro: Perched above Broadway with the Vale of Evesham unfolding below, Foxhill Manor is an Arts and Crafts house reimagined as a home you take over entirely. There are no menus or timetables here: your chef cooks what you fancy, the cinema room waits, and eight individual bedrooms invite lingering. Beyond the honey-stone terraces lie 500 acres of Farncombe Estate, where woodland walks, falconry and Cotswold villages reward the curious. Come as guests, leave as family.

property_title: Sailrock South Caicos: Untamed Shores and Quiet Island Luxury
property_intro: On the wind-brushed ridges of South Caicos, an island still shaped by salt ponds and fishing sloops, Sailrock sits between the Atlantic and the Caribbean Sea. Villas and hillside suites open to reef-fringed water, with plunge pools, timber accents and space to breathe. Days drift between bonefishing flats, diving the wall and long, empty beaches. The resort works closely with local fishermen and conservation partners, so your stay quietly sustains the island's future.

property_title: The Retreat Koh Chang: Rainforest Calm Above the Gulf of Thailand
property_intro: Tucked into the jungled hills of Thailand's second-largest island, The Retreat Koh Chang looks out across the Gulf towards a horizon broken only by fishing boats. Days unfold slowly here: barefoot yoga beneath the canopy, waterfall walks with local guides, mangrove paddles at dusk. Timber pavilions and open-air bathrooms invite the forest indoors, while kitchens draw on nearby smallholdings and village fishermen. It is a place that rewards those who arrive ready to listen.

property_title: Crans Ambassador: Refined Alpine Living Above the Rhône Valley
property_intro: Perched above Crans-Montana, with the Rhône Valley unfurling below and the Matterhorn on the horizon, Crans Ambassador feels quietly removed from the world. Interiors of pale timber, stone and Alpine wool frame those views, while the spa and heated outdoor pool invite long, unhurried afternoons. Ski straight to the slopes in winter; in summer, follow the historic bisses irrigation channels with a guide. Local producers, seasonal menus and Valais wines keep the mountain's character firmly at the centre.

property_title: Villa Soro: Belle Époque Serenity in San Sebastián's Gardens
property_intro: Set behind wrought-iron gates in a leafy corner of San Sebastián, Villa Soro is a restored 19th-century residence where Belle Époque details meet a calm, contemporary hand. Magnolias shade the garden, bicycles wait by the door, and the beaches of La Concha and Zurriola are minutes away. Breakfast draws on Basque producers, staff share their favourite pintxos counters and coastal walks, and the house feels less like a hotel than a well-loved family home.

property_title: The Lodge Mallorca: Serene Escapes in the Tramuntana Hills
property_intro: Tucked into the folds of Mallorca's Serra de Tramuntana, The Lodge Mallorca is a quietly confident retreat where dry-stone terraces, olive groves and sea-scented air set the pace. Interiors pair local craftsmanship with soft, sun-warmed textures, while days unfold with mountain walks, estate-grown produce and long, unhurried dinners. Conservation of the surrounding landscape and close ties with island artisans and growers give every stay real substance beyond its beauty. Arrive curious; leave restored.

property_title: Racha Yai: Barefoot Island Serenity in Thailand's Andaman Sea
property_intro: Just south of Phuket, Racha Yai rises from the Andaman Sea with powder-white bays and water so clear you can count the fish from your terrace. Villas and pool suites open to sea breezes, styled with natural timber, stone and quiet restraint. Days drift between reef snorkelling, coral restoration dives and long lunches of southern Thai cooking. Local crews lead the boats and kitchens, keeping the island's livelihoods and marine life thriving together.

property_title: Finca Serena Mallorca: Slow Living Amid Vineyards and Hills
property_intro: Set within 30 hectares of vineyards, olive groves and lavender in Mallorca's rural heart, Finca Serena is a restored country estate where days unfold at their own pace. Interiors pair local stone and timber with quiet contemporary design, while the kitchen draws on the property's own gardens. Guests can wander the vines, ride out into the Tramuntana foothills, or simply linger by the pool as the light shifts across the valley.

property_title: Cap Rocat: A Historic Cliffside Fortress Above the Bay of Palma
property_intro: Carved into the cliffs at the mouth of Palma Bay, this 19th-century military fortress has been reimagined as an intimate Mallorcan retreat. Former gun emplacements are now private terraces with plunge pools, stone corridors open onto wild coastal garrigue, and the sea shifts colour all day. Swim from the fort's own cove, dine on produce from the kitchen garden, and appreciate a restoration that safeguarded both the architecture and the surrounding protected shoreline.

property_title: Bank Hotel: Stockholm's Waterfront Grandeur, Reimagined
property_intro: Set within a stately 1910 banking house on Stockholm's Blasieholmen quayside, Bank Hotel opens onto views of the Royal Palace and the harbour beyond. Marble halls and vaulted ceilings now frame velvet lounges, contemporary Nordic art and a glass-roofed brasserie where locals gather over long lunches. The Sophie's Bar rooftop catches the late northern light, while the Old Town, Djurgeshingly close by. A stay here places you at the city's cultural heart, moments from museums, galleries and island ferries.

property_title: Bergwelt Grindelwald: Alpine Calm Beneath the Eiger's Gaze
property_intro: Tucked into the meadows of Grindelwald, Bergwelt sits beneath the north face of the Eiger, where cowbells and glacier air set the rhythm of the day. Interiors pair Swiss timber with quiet contemporary lines, framing views that shift with every hour. Walk to the Jungfrau railway, ski from the village, or linger in the spa after a long ridge hike. Regional producers, local craftspeople and family stewardship keep this mountain welcome genuinely rooted.

property_title: VALA Hua Hin: Barefoot Elegance on Thailand's Gulf Coastline
property_intro: Set along the quieter reaches of Hua Hin's shoreline, VALA is a low-slung retreat of pale timber, tidal pools and sea breezes drifting through open pavilions. Days unfold slowly here: long swims, Thai cookery sessions with local producers, cycling past fishing villages and salt flats. The design nods to Gulf of Thailand vernacular, while the team works closely with nearby communities and coastal clean-up initiatives. Evenings bring grilled seafood, soft lamplight and the steady rhythm of waves.

property_title: Nira Caledonia: Georgian Charm in Edinburgh's Leafy New Town
property_intro: Tucked into a quiet cobbled crescent in Edinburgh's New Town, Nira Caledonia occupies two restored Georgian townhouses within a UNESCO World Heritage setting. Original cornicing and sash windows meet deep velvets, tartan accents and thoughtfully sourced Scottish craftsmanship. Days begin with local produce at Blackwoods Bar & Grill, then unfold along Stockbridge's independent shops and the Water of Leith. Staff share their city generously, from whisky tastings to hidden gardens few visitors ever discover.

property_title: Kestelinn Alaçatı: Where Aegean Stone Meets the Art of Slow Living
property_intro: Set among the windswept vineyards and fig groves of Alaçatı, Kestelinn is a quietly confident retreat where local stone, lime plaster and reclaimed timber shape rooms that feel unhurried. Mornings begin with village-grown produce and herbs gathered nearby; afternoons drift towards Aegean coves, windsurfing bays and the cobbled lanes of the old town. Artisans from the region furnished each space, and much of the garden is tended without irrigation, honouring the peninsula's fragile balance.

property_title: Maison Dedine: Whitewashed Calm on Tunisia's Sunlit Shores
property_intro: Set within a restored village house of thick lime-washed walls and shaded courtyards, Maison Dedine invites you to slow down among olive groves, jasmine and the salt-tinged air of the Tunisian coast. Interiors pair handwoven Berber textiles with local ceramics, each piece sourced from nearby artisans. Days unfold with market wanders, home-cooked feasts of sun-warmed produce and rooftop evenings beneath an enormous sky. Family-run and quietly generous, it offers a genuine welcome rather than a performance of one.

property_title: Nantipa: A Refined Beachfront Retreat on the Nicoya Peninsula
property_intro: Tucked between jungle and surf on Santa Teresa's shoreline, Nantipa unfolds across the sand in a scatter of thatched casitas shaped by Costa Rican craftsmanship. Days drift from sunrise yoga to Pacific swells, horseback rides through the hills and long lunches of just-landed fish at Manzú. The Nicoya Peninsula's Blue Zone spirit runs deep here, upheld through local hiring, plastic-free practices and quiet respect for the turtles that nest a few steps away.

property_title: San Canzian Hotel & Residences: Istria's Restored Village Retreat
property_intro:
Tucked into the hilltop hamlet of Mu
tvoran in inland Istria, San Canzian occupies a cluster of centuries-old stone houses brought gently back to life. Original walls meet contemporary interiors, olive groves stretch towards the Adriatic, and a Roman basilica stands quietly nearby. Days unfold with truffle hunts, cycling through oak forest, and dinners built around produce from neighbouring farms. It is a place where local craftsmanship, slow rhythms and thoughtful restoration shape every corner of the stay.

property_title: Park Lane Copenhagen: Refined Calm Beside the City's Lakes
property_intro: Overlooking Copenhagen's lakes, Park Lane occupies a graceful corner of the city where cycle lanes, canal-side cafes and design studios shape the rhythm of the day. Interiors pair Danish craftsmanship with warm, tactile materials, while the kitchen leans on Nordic growers and seasonal catches. Walk to Nyhavn, browse Vesterbro's galleries, or simply linger by the water as swimmers greet the morning. Thoughtful energy practices and local partnerships underpin every stay here.

property_title: Eagles Resort: Halkidiki's Pine-Fringed Shore Awaits You
property_intro: Set along a golden crescent of Aegean coast in Halkidiki, Eagles Resort rests where centuries-old pines meet clear Greek waters, with Mount Athos rising on the horizon. Interiors draw on natural stone, linen and light, while days unfold between the private beach, thoughtful spa rituals and menus built around Northern Greek producers. Sail to secluded coves, learn the region's olive and honey traditions, or simply let the sea air slow your pace entirely.

property_title: Münchner Kindl: Bavarian Warmth and Quiet City Character
property_intro: Named after Munich's emblematic child, Münchner Kindl gathers the city's spirit into a place of easy elegance. Pale timber, locally woven textiles and light-filled rooms set the tone, while the surrounding streets offer beer gardens, galleries and the leafy sprawl of the Englischer Garten within walking reach. Mornings begin with regional produce from nearby growers; evenings drift towards the Isar. Staff share their own Munich — the markets, the swimming spots, the corners guidebooks overlook.

property_title: ACRO: Where Cycladic Stone Meets the Slow Rhythm of the Aegean
property_intro: Set on a sun-warmed Greek hillside, ACRO looks out across olive terraces towards water that shifts colour through the day. Local stone, lime plaster and handmade textiles shape interiors that feel calm rather than showy, the work of craftspeople from nearby villages. Days unfold with sea swims, market mornings, long tables of island cooking and walks along old shepherds' paths. Water is harvested, produce grown close by, and hospitality stays refreshingly personal.

property_title: Casale Panayiotis: A Reawakened Village in the Troodos Hills
property_intro:
Tucked into the Marathasa valley, where mountain streams thread between terraced orchards, Casale Panayiotis occupies a cluster of restored stone houses in the Cypriot village of Kalopanayiotis. What began as one man's determination to bring his birthplace back to life now draws guests to sulphur springs, a mountain spa and cooking rooted in Troodos produce. Byzantine frescoes wait a short stroll away, while village bakers, beekeepers and winemakers remain part of daily life here 
certainly worth lingering over.

property_title: Olas Tulum: Barefoot Coastal Living on Mexico's Caribbean
property_intro: Set between jungle and shoreline on Tulum's beach road, Olas Tulum invites you to slow down within walls of local limestone, warm wood and soft, filtered light. Days unfold with cenote swims, Mayan ruins at dawn, and long lunches shaped by regional produce. Solar power, rainwater harvesting and partnerships with nearby artisans and conservation projects keep the footprint gentle. Fall asleep to breaking waves, wake to birdsong, and rediscover the rhythm of the Caribbean coast.

property_title: Blue Apple Beach: Island Living Beyond Cartagena's Old Walls
property_intro: A twenty-minute boat ride from Cartagena's ramparts, Blue Apple Beach occupies a stretch of Tierra Bomba where the Caribbean laps at dark volcanic sand. Rooms are dressed in local craftsmanship — woven palm, hand-thrown ceramics, sun-bleached timber — while days drift between the saltwater pool, long lunches and rum tastings. The team invests in island schooling, waste recycling and fair employment, so your stay quietly strengthens the community that shapes it. Cartagena's nightlife waits, should you want it.

property_title: Hacienda Zuleta: Andean Heritage, Horses and Soaring Condors
property_intro: High in Ecuador's northern Andes, this 17th-century working farm has been home to the Plaza Lasso family for generations. Cobbled courtyards, wood-beamed rooms and open fires sit within 4,000 acres of pasture, cloud forest and lakes. Ride Zuleteño horses across the páramo, meet the embroiderers whose needlework supports village families, and visit the condor rehabilitation project. Dairy, cheese and vegetables come from the land itself, served at long, convivial tables.

property_title: Mashpi Lodge: A Glass Sanctuary in Ecuador's Cloud Forest
property_intro: Suspended above the Choca0 cloud forest, three hours from Quito, Mashpi Lodge is a study in glass and steel that invites the wilderness indoors. Hummingbirds hover at your window; mist drifts through 1,300 hectares of protected reserve once destined for logging. Ride the aerial gondola above the canopy, walk with resident biologists, or linger in the observation tower at dusk. Staff hail from neighbouring villages, and every stay directly funds ongoing research and forest protection.

property_title: EcoCamp Patagonia: Geodesic Dome Living Beneath Torres del Paine
property_intro: Set within Chile's Torres del Paine National Park, EcoCamp Patagonia gathers a cluster of geodesic domes across a windswept hillside, framed by the granite towers themselves. Inspired by the shelters of the Kaweskar people, the domes run on renewable energy and composting systems, leaving the terrain undisturbed. Days unfold on guided treks, horseback rides and puma-tracking outings; evenings bring Patagonian cooking, local wines and the vast southern sky through your skylight.

property_title: The Scarlet Hotel: Clifftop Calm Above Cornwall's Wild Atlantic
property_intro: Perched above Mawgan Porth on Cornwall's north coast, The Scarlet is an adults-only retreat where floor-to-ceiling glass frames the restless Atlantic and gorse-covered cliffs. Interiors pair Cornish craftsmanship with a genuinely low-impact ethos, from biomass heating to a reed-bed water system. Days unfold between clifftop hot tubs, ayurvedic-inspired treatments and long, sea-air walks, before dinner built around growers and fishing boats just along the coast. Quietly radical, deeply restorative, and unmistakably Cornish.

property_title: Heckfield Place: A Georgian Retreat Rooted in Hampshire Soil
property_intro: Set within 400 acres of Hampshire woodland, lakes and biodynamic farmland, Heckfield Place is a Georgian house restored with quiet conviction. Interiors favour honest materials and antiques over ornament, while the kitchen gardens and Home Farm shape each day's menus. Wander walled gardens, swim in the lake, or settle into the cinema and Little Bothy spa. Conservation runs deep here, from regenerative farming to woodland stewardship, making every stay feel purposeful.

property_title: Holkham Estate: Wild Norfolk Coast, Palladian Grandeur & Care
property_intro: On Norfolk's north coast, Holkham Estate unfolds across salt marsh, pinewoods and one of England's finest beaches, with a Palladian hall at its heart. Stay in thoughtfully restored cottages and inns, cycle the parkland, forage the shoreline or join keepers tracking spoonbills and natterjack toads. Regenerative farming, rewetted wetlands and local craftsmanship shape everything here, from the produce on your plate to the estate villages that keep this coastline quietly alive.

property_title: Grove Narberth: Pembrokeshire's Garden Retreat Reimagined
property_intro: Set within 26 acres of Pembrokeshire meadow and woodland, Grove Narberth pairs a restored Georgian manor with Welsh longhouse cottages and kitchen gardens that shape each day's menu. The coast path and Preseli Hills lie within easy reach, yet many guests linger for foraging walks, wild swims and evenings by the fire. Interiors celebrate Welsh craft and slate, while rewilded grounds, local producers and village partnerships keep the estate rooted in its own corner of the county.

property_title: 42 Acres: Regenerative Retreats in Somerset's Green Heartland
property_intro: Tucked into the folds of the Somerset countryside, 42 Acres is a working farm and retreat where woodland walks, wild swimming and long, unhurried meals set the rhythm of the day. Interiors are quietly considered, all natural materials and soft light, while regenerative farming and rewilding shape everything grown and served here. Come for a yoga gathering, a creative residency or simply space to think, and leave feeling genuinely restored.

property_title: Andronis Minois: Barefoot Luxury on Santorini's Quiet Shore
property_intro: On Santorini's south-western edge, Andronis Minois looks out across the Aegean from Vlychada, where volcanic cliffs have been sculpted by wind into something close to lunar. Whitewashed suites open onto private terraces, interiors shaped by local stone, timber and the island's soft light. Days unfold with Cycladic cooking rooted in island growers, wine tastings among nearby vineyards, and swims from black-sand beaches. Refreshingly unhurried, it offers Santorini as islanders themselves know it.

property_title: Santorini Secret Suites & Spa: Sunset Calm Above the Caldera
property_intro: Carved into the cliffs of Oia, this intimate retreat looks out across the caldera towards the volcano and the slow drift of passing boats. Cave-style suites in whitewashed stone and pale linen open onto private plunge pools, while the spa draws on local herbs and volcanic minerals. Days unfold with Cycladic cooking, island wines and vineyard walks, guided by a team who champion Santorini's growers, artisans and long-held traditions.

property_title: Canaves Oia: Whitewashed Calm Above Santorini's Caldera Rim
property_intro: Carved into the cliffs of Oia, Canaves Oia occupies former wine caves where volcanic stone now shelters cool, sculptural suites and private plunge pools above the caldera. Days unfold slowly here: sunrise swims, Cycladic cooking with island growers, sailings past Thirassia. The family behind it has restored these vaulted spaces with local craftspeople and champions Santorini's Assyrtiko vineyards. Dine on Aegean catch and garden herbs, then watch the light shift across the water until dusk.

property_title: Kois Mansion: A Refined Retreat Rooted in Greek Tradition
property_intro: Set within a lovingly restored stone residence, Kois Mansion invites you to slow down amid olive groves, mountain air and the quiet rhythms of village life. Original architectural details meet considered contemporary comfort, with local craftsmanship shaping every room. Days here might mean tasting regional wines, walking old shepherds' paths, or sharing recipes with neighbours whose families have farmed this land for generations. It is Greece experienced gently, warmly and with genuine respect for place.

property_title: Porto Zante Villas & Spa: Zakynthos Seclusion by the Ionian Sea
property_intro: On a quiet stretch of Zakynthos coastline, framed by olive groves and the clear Ionian, Porto Zante offers just a handful of private villas, each with its own pool and stretch of shore. Days unfold gently here: spa rituals beneath the pines, sailing to hidden coves, dinners shaped by island growers and fishermen. Interiors favour marble, timber and light, while the family owners quietly support local producers and protect the surrounding shoreline.

property_title: Hotel Rangá: Aurora Nights Beneath Iceland's Southern Skies
property_intro: On the banks of the salmon-rich Rangá river, this timber lodge sits between Hekla's slopes and the black sands of Iceland's south coast. Rooms nod to the seven continents, while the observatory's telescopes and lagoon-side hot tubs invite long nights beneath the aurora. Days bring glacier walks, horse riding and river fishing; evenings, a kitchen shaped by Icelandic farmers and fishermen. Wake-up calls for the northern lights are, quite happily, part of the service.

property_title: Desa Hay: Where Bali's Quiet Countryside Welcomes You Home
property_intro:
Tucked among rice terraces and coconut groves in Bali's gentle interior, Desa Hay unfolds as a village reimagined 
atural materials, open pavilions and pools that mirror the sky. Days here move to the rhythm of the land: barefoot walks to neighbouring farms, cooking with produce picked that morning, evenings scented with frangipani. Local artisans shaped much of what you'll touch, and the surrounding community shares in what the retreat creates.

property_title: The LOST Lindenberg: Quiet Luxury Amid West Bali's Jungle Coast
property_intro: Tucked into a coconut grove near Pekutatan, on Bali's little-travelled west coast, The LOST Lindenberg feels like a discovery. Slender timber towers rise among the palms, each suite reached by ladder-like stairs, with the black-sand shoreline and a sunken pool moments away. Days drift between yoga, ocean swims and unhurried Japanese-Indonesian dining. The team works closely with neighbouring villages and local turtle conservation efforts, so your stay quietly supports the coast that surrounds it.

property_title: La Reserve 1785: Rainforest Seclusion in Bali's Wild Heart
property_intro: Tucked into the jungle-clad valleys above Ubud, La Reserve 1785 gathers a handful of villas beneath a canopy alive with birdsong and river mist. Interiors pair reclaimed Javanese timber with soft, earthen tones, while days unfold through guided walks, spring-water bathing and menus drawn from the estate's own gardens. Local artisans and neighbouring farmers shape much of what you'll see and taste here, and reforestation quietly continues beyond the terrace, just past the treeline.

property_title: The Ungasan Clifftop Resort: A Cliff-Edge Retreat in South Bali
property_intro: Perched high above the Indian Ocean on Bali's Bukit Peninsula, The Ungasan gathers five private villas along a limestone ridge, with the white sands of Melasti Beach reachable by inclinator below. Days unfold slowly here: sunrise yoga, Balinese cooking with the estate's chefs, or an afternoon at Sundays Beach Club. Thatched pavilions and local craftsmanship reflect island tradition, while reef care, coastal clean-ups and village employment keep the surrounding community and shoreline thriving.

property_title: The Wilder Townhouse: Victorian Elegance in Dublin's Green Heart
property_intro: Tucked between the leafy squares of Dublin's south side, The Wilder Townhouse occupies a handsomely restored Victorian red-brick once home to a charitable institution. Original mouldings, salvaged furnishings and softly lit corners set the mood, while the Gin & Tea Rooms pour botanical cocktails beside a walled garden. St Stephen's Green, Grafton Street galleries and canalside walks lie minutes away. Adults-only, quietly run and locally sourced, it rewards those who prefer character over convention.

property_title: Palazzo Gattini: Noble Living Above Matera's Ancient Sassi
property_intro: Perched on Piazza Duomo in Matera, Palazzo Gattini occupies the former residence of the city's counts, its windows framing the tufa rooftops of the Sassi below. Vaulted ceilings, frescoes and family antiques sit alongside a spa carved from the rock itself. Days unfold with guided walks through cave churches, Lucanian wine tastings and dinners built around Basilicata's small producers \u2014 a stay that gives back to the city that shaped it.

property_title: Donna Carmela Resort & Lodges: Botanical Serenity Below Etna
property_intro: Tucked between Etna's dark slopes and the Ionian shore near Riposto, Donna Carmela sits within a working nursery where rare species from across the world have been nurtured for generations. Timber lodges rest among jasmine, palms and citrus, their calm interiors framing green horizons. Days unfold with garden walks, Sicilian cooking with produce from the estate, volcano hikes and slow swims. A place shaped by plantsmen, botanists and a genuine devotion to the land.

property_title: Rosapetra Spa Resort: Dolomite Stillness Above Cortina Valley
property_intro: Set on a quiet meadow above Cortina d'Ampezzo, Rosapetra looks out to the Dolomites' pale spires, their colour shifting with the hours. Interiors pair local larch and wool with contemporary calm, while the spa draws on mountain herbs and Alpine water rituals. Days unfold with guided walks, forest foraging and dishes shaped by Ampezzo producers at the resort's celebrated restaurant. Family-run and rooted in the valley, it offers the sort of unhurried welcome that lingers long after departure.

property_title: Lungarno Collection: Florence Framed by River, Art and Craft
property_intro: Gathered along the banks of the Arno, the Lungarno Collection places you at the heart of Florence, where Ponte Vecchio views meet quiet courtyards and Renaissance workshops still hum nearby. Each address has its own character, from riverside suites hung with original Picasso sketches to a former convent shaded by olive trees. Expect kitchens led by Tuscan producers, cocktails poured with local botanicals, and a genuine commitment to the city's artisans, galleries and cultural life.

property_title: Vintry & Mercer: Where the City of London's Trade Routes Live On
property_intro: Tucked between Mansion House and the Thames, Vintry & Mercer takes its name from the wine merchants and silk traders who once shaped these lanes. Interiors nod to that heritage with deep tones, bespoke tailoring details and salvaged materials, while the rooftop bar and Do Not Disturb restaurant draw City locals as much as guests. Expect thoughtful service, spice-scented cocktails and morning walks past Wren churches orring for exploring London on foot.

property_title: Prince Hotel Nagoya: Sky-High Serenity Above Japan's Heartland
property_intro: Perched high above Nagoya's Minato Aqls district, Prince Hotel Nagoya occupies the upper floors of a landmark tower, where floor-to-ceiling glass frames the Ise Bay, the city's glittering sprawl and, on clear mornings, distant mountain ridges. Interiors balance restrained Japanese craftsmanship with contemporary calm. Below, waterfront parks, aquariums and local eateries invite unhurried exploration, while the hotel's ties to regional producers bring Aichi's seasonal ingredients and artisan traditions quietly to the table.

property_title: The Ampersand Hotel: South Kensington's Elegant Curiosity
property_intro: Tucked into a quiet corner of South Kensington, moments from the Victoria and Albert and Natural History museums, The Ampersand celebrates the curiosity of its surroundings. Interiors nod playfully to botany, astronomy and music, with bedrooms bathed in light and character. Downstairs, Apero serves Mediterranean small plates, while afternoon tea arrives with a scientific twist. Hyde Park lies within strolling distance, and the hotel's local partnerships keep it firmly rooted in the neighbourhood it calls home.

property_title: Isle of Eriska Hotel: A Private Island Retreat in the Highlands
property_intro: Reached by a slender iron bridge on Scotland's west coast, Isle of Eriska occupies its own 300-acre island of woodland, shoreline and salt marsh. Badgers visit the terrace at dusk, otters slip through the bay, and the Baronial house holds log fires, sea-facing rooms and a kitchen shaped by the island's garden and nearby waters. Days pass with sea kayaking, forest walks and links golf, while ongoing habitat and wildlife work keeps this fragile landscape thriving.

property_title: Dunluce Lodge: Refined Coastal Living on Ireland's Wild North
property_intro: Perched above the Atlantic on Northern Ireland's Causeway Coast, Dunluce Lodge looks out towards the ruined castle that gave it its name, with Royal Portrush and the basalt columns of the Giant's Causeway close by. Interiors draw on local craft and linen, timber and stone, while the kitchen leans on Antrim growers and fishermen. Days here might mean links golf, cliff-top walks, whiskey tastings in Bushmills, or simply the fire and a long view.

property_title: Seaton House: Coastal Grandeur on Scotland's Wild Shoreline
property_intro: Set amid windswept gardens where the land gives way to the sea, Seaton House offers a considered kind of Scottish escape. Grand rooms are dressed in muted tweeds and locally made furnishings, with peat fires crackling long into the evening. Days here might mean foraging along the tideline, walking with the estate's gamekeeper, or simply watching the weather roll in. Produce comes from the kitchen garden, and restoration work continues quietly across the surrounding woodland and dunes.

property_title: Riverview Ranch: Riverside Seclusion in the American West
property_intro: Set along a slow bend of water where cottonwoods lean towards the current, Riverview Ranch offers a quieter kind of luxury. Days here unfold at their own pace: fly-fishing at first light, riding out across native grassland, evenings spent beside the fire as the valley cools. Interiors pair reclaimed timber with handwoven textiles from local makers, while ongoing habitat restoration keeps the riverbanks thriving. A working landscape, generously shared, and remembered long after departure.

property_title: Under Canvas Bryce Canyon: Starlit Safari Tents in Red Rock
property_intro: Set among juniper and sage on Utah's high plateau, Under Canvas Bryce Canyon places you minutes from the amphitheatre of hoodoos that makes this corner of the American West so beguiling. Safari-inspired tents bring wood-burning stoves, en-suite bathrooms and canvas walls that open to a certified Dark Sky horizon. Days unfold with guided hikes and horseback trails; evenings gather around the fire. Low-impact by design, the camp treads gently on the land it celebrates.

property_title: Topping Rose House: Bridgehampton's Elegant Farmhouse Escape
property_intro: Set in a restored 1842 Greek Revival mansion at the heart of Bridgehampton, Topping Rose House pairs Hamptons ease with quiet sophistication. Interiors balance historic bones with contemporary calm, while the kitchen draws on the hotel's own working farm just down the lane, harvesting produce hours before service. Days unfold between the heated pool, spa treatments and shuttle rides to Sagaponack's shoreline, with village galleries, farm stands and vineyards waiting a short stroll from the door.

property_title: Camden Harbour Inn: Coastal Maine Elegance Above the Harbour
property_intro: Perched on a quiet rise above Camden's schooner-filled harbour, this 1874 mansion looks out across Penobscot Bay to the Camden Hills. Inside, antique bones meet bold colour, Dutch design flair and rooms warmed by fireplaces and claw-foot tubs. Dine at Natalie's on Maine lobster and day-boat catch, sourced from neighbouring farms and fishermen. Days unfold with windjammer sails, forest trails and village galleries, before evenings settle into the terrace with a sundowner in hand.

property_title: The Stavrand: Redwood Serenity on Sonoma's Russian River
property_intro: Tucked among towering redwoods on the banks of the Russian River, The Stavrand invites you to slow down in Guerneville, moments from Sonoma's celebrated vineyards and the Pacific coast. Once a 1920s lodge, it has been thoughtfully reimagined with natural textures, local craftsmanship and a genuine sense of ease. Wander the gardens, sip wines from neighbouring growers, dine on produce grown nearby, then linger by the fire pit beneath a canopy of ancient trees.

property_title: Rusty Parrot Lodge: Handcrafted Mountain Living in Jackson Hole
property_intro: Moments from Jackson's boardwalks and a short drive from Grand Teton's peaks, Rusty Parrot Lodge welcomes guests with hand-carved timber, fireside corners and rooms shaped by local artisans. Days here might begin with a guided wildlife drive, fly-fishing on the Snake River or a treatment in the intimate spa, and end over ranch-inspired cooking that champions Wyoming growers. Family-run and deeply rooted in its valley, the lodge supports conservation efforts protecting the wildlife beyond its windows.

property_title: L'Auberge de Sedona: Creekside Calm Beneath Red Rock Country
property_intro: Tucked along the banks of Oak Creek in Arizona's red rock country, L'Auberge de Sedona unfolds beneath towering sycamores, where cottages and creekside suites sit within earshot of running water. Days here might begin with a riverside breakfast, drift into forest bathing or a guided hike among the sandstone formations, and end at a table celebrating regional growers. Native planting, water stewardship and close ties to local artisans and Indigenous traditions shape the experience throughout.

property_title: Namia River Retreat: Riverside Calm on Hoi An's Green Edge
property_intro: Set along the Thu Bon River's quiet channels, moments from Hoi An's lantern-lit lanes, Namia River Retreat unfolds among coconut palms, rice paddies and water gardens. Timber, stone and handwoven textiles by local artisans shape rooms that open to birdsong and slow-moving water. Days might begin with a basket-boat paddle through the nipa palms, a market visit with the kitchen team, or simply a long swim before dusk settles over the fields.

property_title: Mandarin Oriental Qianmen: Courtyard Living in Historic Beijing
property_intro: Tucked into the grey-brick hutongs just south of Tiananmen Square, Mandarin Oriental Qianmen occupies a cluster of restored Qing-era courtyard homes, each with its own walled garden and quiet entrance. Craftsmen revived original timber frames and tiled roofs, keeping the neighbourhood's rhythms intact. Mornings begin with tai chi beneath the pomegranate trees; afternoons might mean calligraphy, a Peking duck masterclass, or wandering lanes where locals still gather. Beijing's oldest quarter, offered with genuine intimacy.

property_title: Southern Ocean Lodge: Wild Coastal Luxury on Kangaroo Island
property_intro: Perched above a curve of untouched coastline on Kangaroo Island, Southern Ocean Lodge draws the eye straight to the horizon. Rebuilt with even greater sensitivity after the 2020 bushfires, its limestone, glass and timber suites sit low among the coastal heath, warmed by open fires and South Australian wine. Days unfold with naturalist-led walks, sea lion encounters and cliff-top dining, while the lodge's revegetation and wildlife work quietly restores the landscape that surrounds you.

property_title: Chiva-Som Hua Hin: Thailand's Pioneering Coastal Wellness Haven
property_intro: Set along the Gulf of Thailand in Hua Hin, Chiva-Som unfolds across seven acres of tropical gardens, lotus ponds and beachfront where royal Siam once retreated. Here, wellness is deeply personal: consultations shape your days, from Thai massage pavilions to holistic therapies rooted in Eastern tradition. Meals draw on the resort's own organic gardens, while plastic-free practices and long-standing community programmes reflect a quieter kind of luxury, one measured in how restored you feel on leaving.

property_title: Patina Osaka: Where Japan's Boldest City Reveals Its Soul
property_intro: Rising above the Nakanoshima riverfront, Patina Osaka sits between the city's cultural quarter and the lively lanes of Kitashinchi, where izakaya lanterns glow after dark. Interiors draw on Osaka's merchant heritage and craft traditions, with locally made ceramics and textiles softening contemporary lines. Guests might join a knife-sharpening session with a Sakai artisan, wander to the Museum of Oriental Ceramics, or return to a spa overlooking the water. Thoughtful sourcing supports Kansai makers and growers throughout.

property_title: Rosewood Hong Kong: Harbourfront Elegance with an Artful Soul
property_intro: Rising above Victoria Dockside in Tsim Sha Tsui, Rosewood Hong Kong looks straight across the harbour to Hong Kong Island's shimmering skyline. Interiors by Tony Chi feel more like a collector's residence than a hotel, layered with over 4,000 artworks and quiet corners for lingering. Days unfold between Asaya's restorative rituals, Cantonese classics at The Legacy House and rooftop gardens above the city. Sustainability runs deep here, from local sourcing to spirited support for Hong Kong's creative community.

property_title: Aman Nai Lert Bangkok: Serenity Above a Storied Garden
property_intro: Rising above the century-old Nai Lert Park in the heart of Bangkok, Aman Nai Lert Bangkok offers a rare kind of calm within Thailand's most spirited city. Suites frame views across tamarind canopies and glittering skyline, while spa pavilions, gardens and quiet terraces invite unhurried days. The design draws on Thai craftsmanship and the Nai Lert family's legacy, and guests are welcomed into the neighbourhood's living heritage, from heirloom recipes to the garden's protected trees.

property_title: Pemako Punakha: Riverside Serenity in Bhutan's Sacred Valley
property_intro: Set along the Puna Tsang Chhu in Bhutan's fertile Punakha Valley, Pemako blends contemporary architecture with local craftsmanship, timber, stone and hand-painted detail framing views of terraced rice fields and forested ridges. Villas open to the river's steady murmur, while the spa draws on Bhutanese healing traditions. Days might bring a walk to Khamsum Yulley Chorten, a farmhouse lunch with valley families, or quiet hours beside the water, with local artisans and produce supported throughout.

property_title: Capella Sydney: Heritage Grandeur in the Heart of the City
property_intro: Housed within the sandstone splendour of the former Department of Education building, Capella Sydney brings new life to a landmark that has watched over Sancta Sophia Gardens for a century. Steps from Circular Quay and the Opera House, it pairs restored Edwardian detail with contemporary Australian artistry, a serene subterranean spa and dining that champions local growers. Expect warm, unhurried service, curated cultural encounters and a genuine sense of belonging to Sydney itself.

property_title: The Middle House: Where Milanese Calm Meets Shanghai's Spirit
property_intro: Tucked into Jing'an's leafy lanes, moments from the boutiques of HKRI Taikoo Hui, The Middle House brings a quiet Italian sensibility to central Shanghai. Piero Lissoni's interiors pair bamboo, silk and stone with courtyards that hush the city outside. Days might begin with tai chi, drift through Cantonese and Sichuanese kitchens, and end over cocktails above the rooftops. Thoughtful design choices, LEED Gold credentials and local artisan partnerships give the house its conscience.

property_title: Bishopstrow Hotel & Spa: Georgian Calm on Wiltshire's Wylye
property_intro: Set within 27 acres of walled gardens and riverside meadow near Warminster, Bishopstrow Hotel & Spa occupies a graceful Georgian house on the banks of the River Wylye. Log fires, antique portraits and deep armchairs invite unhurried afternoons, while the spa's indoor and outdoor pools and thermal rooms restore weary limbs. Kitchen gardens and Wiltshire growers shape the menus, and Stonehenge, Longleat and the chalk downs lie temptingly within easy reach.

property_name: Is Cheas Luxury Boutique Hotel & Wine Farm
property_title: Is Cheas Luxury Boutique Hotel & Wine Farm: Vineyard Serenity
property_intro: Set among terraced vines and Mediterranean scrub, Is Cheas is a small wine estate where Sardinian tradition meets quietly considered design. Stone, linen and light shape the handful of suites, while days unfold with cellar tastings, walks through native flora and slow lunches drawn from the surrounding land. The family behind it farms with restraint, reviving old grape varieties and working alongside village artisans. Come for the wine; stay for the unhurried rhythm and generous welcome.

property_title: Vista Verona: Refined Living Above Italy's Timeless Rooftops
property_intro: Set within a restored palazzo in the heart of Verona, Vista Verona looks out across terracotta rooftops towards the Adige and the hills beyond. Interiors pair frescoed ceilings with quietly contemporary furnishings by Veneto artisans, while the rooftop terrace invites slow evenings over Valpolicella. Days might begin with a market walk, followed by cellar visits among neighbouring vineyards. The owners support local restoration crafts, ensuring the building's stories continue for generations of curious guests.

property_title: Blue Waters Resort & Spa: Antigua's Quiet Coastal Sanctuary
property_intro: Tucked into a sheltered cove on Antigua's north-western shore, Blue Waters Resort & Spa unfolds across gardens of frangipani and sea grape, with two private beaches and views towards distant islands. Rooms and villas favour breezy, understated design, while the spa draws on Caribbean botanicals. Days might mean sailing, snorkelling over protected reefs or dining beneath the stars. The resort supports local marine conservation and works closely with Antiguan growers, artisans and schools.

property_title: La Roccia Wellness Hotel Dolomites: Where Alpine Calm Awaits
property_intro: Set in the Val di Fiemme, where the pale peaks of the Dolomites rise above larch forest and meadow, La Roccia is a family-run retreat shaped by local stone and spruce. Days unfold gently here: forest walks with resident guides, spa hours scented with mountain pine, and dinners built around Trentino cheeses, grains and wines. Timber comes from sustainably managed valley woodlands, and long-standing ties with nearby growers and artisans quietly enrich every stay.

property_title: Lujo Hotel Bodrum: Aegean Living, Reimagined with Intention
property_intro: On Bodrum's Torba shoreline, where pine-covered hills meet the calm of the Aegean, Lujo invites you to slow down without giving anything up. Days here drift between private beaches, a nourishing spa and kitchens led by chefs who champion regional producers and Turkish culinary heritage. The design nods to Anatolian craft, while wellbeing rituals, live music and thoughtfully curated art keep curiosity alive. It is generous, personal hospitality shaped around how you actually want to spend your time.

property_title: Ayada Maldives: Barefoot Luxury Beneath the Gaafu Dhaalu Skies
property_intro: Far south in the Huvadhoo Atoll, Ayada Maldives occupies its own island of powder sand, ringed by a reef where turtles glide and manta rays pass through. Villas blend Maldivian craft with Ottoman-inspired detail, opening onto lagoon or garden. Days unfold with reef snorkelling, Turkish hammam rituals and dinners over the water, while the resort's coral restoration work and island partnerships keep this remote corner thriving for generations.,

property_title: Palazzo Giovanelli Gran Canal: Venetian Grandeur Reimagined
property_intro: Overlooking the Grand Canal in the quiet Santa Croce district, Palazzo Giovanelli offers a rare chance to live within a restored 16th-century Venetian residence. Frescoed ceilings, Murano glass and Rubelli silks recall the palazzo's patrician past, while sensitive conservation keeps local artisan traditions alive. Step from the water entrance into gondolas, guided walks through neighbourhood workshops, or breakfast beneath the beamed piano nobile ceiling. The Rialto and Frari basilica sit within an easy stroll.

property_title: Ancora Cortina: Dolomite Elegance in the Heart of Cortina
property_intro: Set on Corso Italia in the heart of Cortina d'Ampezzo, Ancora looks out to the pale peaks of the Dolomites, a UNESCO landscape of extraordinary drama. Behind its historic facade, interiors layer Alpine craftsmanship with contemporary warmth, celebrating local artisans and Ampezzo tradition. Days unfold on the slopes or mountain trails, evenings around candlelit tables of Veneto cooking. It is a house with genuine character, where the town's rhythms feel close and welcoming.

property_title: Grand Hotel Portovenere: A Ligurian Harbour of Quiet Grandeur
property_intro: Set within a restored 17th-century Franciscan monastery, Grand Hotel Portovenere looks across a harbour of pastel houses to the wild island of Palmaria. Vaulted ceilings and cloistered calm meet contemporary Ligurian design, while the terrace restaurant celebrates day-boat fish and produce from nearby smallholdings. Days unfold slowly here: swimming from the rocks, sailing towards the Cinque Terre, or walking coastal paths through a protected marine park the hotel actively helps safeguard.

property_title: Eriksberg Hotel & Nature Reserve: Sweden's Wild Coast Retreat
property_intro:
On Blekinge's south-eastern coast, Eriksberg unfolds across 900 hectares of forest, meadow and shoreline where red deer, bison and wild boar roam freely beyond your window. Glass-fronted suites and hillside hides are designed for quiet observation, while the kitchen draws on game, herbs and produce from the estate itself. Days pass with safari drives, forest saunas and slow lakeside swims 
theres time, too, to understand how careful stewardship has allowed this landscape and its herds to flourish.

property_title: Château Louise de la Vallière: Loire Valley Living, Reimagined
property_intro: Set within ancient parkland near Tours, this seventeenth-century château carries the name of Louis XIV's first love — and something of her spirit too. Interiors pair original panelling and stone with contemporary comfort, while the surrounding woodland, walled garden and beehives supply the kitchen. Days unfold with truffle hunts, vineyard visits along the Loire, or simply a book beneath the cedars. Restored with care by owners committed to local craftsmanship, it feels less like a hotel, more a private invitation.

property_title: ENVI Sisini Serengeti: Wild Serenity on Tanzania's Golden Plains
property_intro: Set within the Serengeti's sweeping grasslands, ENVI Sisini invites you to slow down where wildebeest thunder past and lions rest beneath acacias. Tented suites, dressed in natural linens and locally crafted timber, open onto uninterrupted horizons. Days unfold with guided game drives, bush breakfasts and star-strewn evenings around the fire. Solar power, low-impact design and partnerships with neighbouring Maasai communities ensure your stay supports the land and the people who have long called it home.

property_title: Paradise Plains: Where Kenya's Wild Horizons Feel Like Home
property_intro: Set amid the golden grasslands of Kenya, Paradise Plains looks out across country where elephant trails cross ancient acacia shade. Canvas-and-timber suites are dressed in Maasai beadwork and locally woven textiles, opening to views that shift with the light. Days unfold with guided game drives, walks alongside Samburu trackers and long, unhurried dinners under starlight. Guest stays directly support community grazing programmes and anti-poaching patrols, making every night here quietly consequential.

property_title: Royal Malewane: Bushveld Grandeur in South Africa's Wild Heart
property_intro: Set within the private Thornybush Reserve, sharing unfenced boundaries with the Kruger, Royal Malewane pairs deep bush knowledge with a wonderfully unhurried sense of home. Its suites, dressed in antiques, linens and copper baths, open onto wilderness where elephant pass at dawn. Guiding here is among Africa's most decorated, while the Africa Foundation supports neighbouring schools and clinics. Expect long tracking walks, a spa among the trees, and evenings that linger beneath enormous skies.

property_title: Villa Roma Imperiale: Coastal Elegance on Tuscany's Riviera
property_intro: Set among umbrella pines a short stroll from Forte dei Marmi's shoreline, Villa Roma Imperiale carries the quiet confidence of a family home rather than a hotel. Interiors pair mid-century Italian pieces with contemporary artwork, while the garden pool invites long, unhurried afternoons. Days might begin with Apuan Alps cycling and close over Versilian seafood shaped by nearby growers. Family-run for generations, it supports local artisans and marble workshops throughout the surrounding valleys.

property_title: Grand Hotel Minerva: Rooftop Views over Renaissance Florence
property_intro: Overlooking the serene Piazza Santa Maria Novella, Grand Hotel Minerva occupies a former Dominican convent where scholars once gathered among cloisters and courtyards. Today, contemporary Florentine design meets centuries-old stonework, and the rooftop pool frames Brunelleschi's dome at eye level. Days unfold through artisan workshops in Oltrarno, market mornings and Tuscan cooking led by local producers. Careful restoration, regional sourcing and long-standing ties to neighbourhood craftspeople keep the hotel rooted in the city it celebrates.

property_title: Corpo Santo Lisbon Historical Hotel: Where the City Whispers
property_intro: Tucked into Cais do Sodr\u00e9 beside the Tagus, Corpo Santo rises above a preserved fragment of Lisbon's 14th-century city wall, discovered during construction and now displayed within the hotel itself. Warm woods, Portuguese craftsmanship and quiet corners set the mood, while breakfasts of regional produce and a genuinely green ethos reflect the owners' care for city and staff alike. Step out to Bairro Alto's fado houses, riverside markets and tiled facades, then return to unhurried calm.

property_title: The Isolano: Island Serenity on Croatia's Adriatic Shoreline
property_intro: Set among pines and limestone terraces on Croatia's Adriatic coast, The Isolano offers a quieter kind of luxury. Sun-warmed stone, linen and locally crafted timber shape interiors that feel unhurried, while sea-facing terraces invite long lunches of island-grown produce and Dalmatian wine. Days unfold with swims in hidden coves, sailing at dusk or foraging with neighbouring growers. The owners work closely with village artisans and fishermen, ensuring your stay sustains the traditions that make this shoreline remarkable.

property_title: Madifushi Private Island: Where Meemu Atoll's Reefs Come Alive
property_intro: Set within the seldom-visited Meemu Atoll, Madifushi Private Island is a slender stretch of white sand fringed by a lagoon so clear it seems lit from below. Villas of timber and thatch open onto reef or shoreline, while days unfold through diving with resident marine biologists, sandbank picnics and Maldivian cooking with local chefs. Coral restoration and close ties with neighbouring island communities give this quiet corner of the archipelago genuine depth beyond its beauty.

property_title: The Reverie Saigon: Italian Artistry Above Ho Chi Minh City
property_intro: Rising above District 1, The Reverie Saigon occupies the upper floors of the Times Square building, with the Saigon River curving below and Nguyen Hue's boulevards within strolling distance. Interiors are a showcase of Italian craftsmanship, where Giorgetti furnishings, hand-cut marble and commissioned mosaics reward slow appreciation. Guests dine on Cantonese classics, take afternoon tea overlooking the rooftops, then retreat to a spa suite. Staff share their own city, from hidden coffee houses to family-run tailors nearby.

property_title: Maison Senato: Milan's Quietly Refined Address for Slow Days
property_intro: Tucked along a leafy street between Milan's Brera district and the Giardini Pubblici, Maison Senato offers a considered alternative to the city's busier addresses. Interiors pair restored period detail with contemporary Italian craftsmanship, much of it sourced from workshops within walking distance. Mornings begin with pastries from the neighbourhood bakery; afternoons might drift towards private gallery visits or the canals. It's a house that rewards curiosity, and encourages guests to experience Milan as residents rather than visitors.

property_title: Suyian Lodge: Wild Laikipia Living on a Pioneering Reserve
property_intro: Set within a 44,000-acre reserve on the Laikipia plateau, Suyian Lodge looks out across acacia country where elephant, wild dog and Grevy's zebra move freely. The cottages are handbuilt from local stone and timber, open to the breeze and the sound of the Ewaso Narok. Days unfold on horseback, on foot with Samburu guides, or beside the river. Community-owned and conservation-led, Suyian invites you into a landscape shaped by generations of stewardship.

property_title: Quinta Filippa: Slow Living Among Portugal's Vineyard Hills
property_intro: Set among cork oaks and terraced vineyards in Portugal's gently rolling countryside, Quinta Filippa is a restored farmhouse estate where centuries-old stone meets considered, contemporary calm. Days unfold slowly here: harvesting figs and tomatoes from the kitchen garden, tasting wines with the growers who tend the surrounding valleys, swimming as the hills soften into dusk. Local artisans shaped much of the interiors, while regenerative farming and native planting quietly restore the land, making every stay feel genuinely rooted in place.
