property_title: Noka Camp: Cliffside Serenity in South Africa's Waterberg
property_intro: Perched along a cliff above the Palala River in the Waterberg's Lapalala Wilderness, Noka Camp holds five glass-fronted villas suspended between rock and sky. Days unfold with rhino tracking, guided walks and river swims, before dinner arrives on your private deck. Solar power, recycled water and thoughtfully sourced materials underpin the design, while the reserve's conservation school nurtures the next generation of custodians. It is a place where quiet luxury and genuine purpose share the same view.

property_name: Jack's Camp by Natural Selection Safaris
property_title: Jack's Camp: Botswana's Makgadikgadi Salt Pans Reimagined
property_intro: On the shimmering edge of Botswana's Makgadikgadi Pans, Jack's Camp stands as a legend reborn. Ten billowing canvas tents echo 1940s expedition style, filled with Persian rugs, brass fittings and a museum of desert curiosities gathered over decades. Days bring quad-biking across the salt crust, walks with Zu/'hoasi Bushmen trackers and encounters with habituated meerkats. Beneath skies untroubled by light, this pioneering camp continues its long partnership with local communities and Kalahari research.24 words remain unused.</intro>

property_title: Casa de São Lourenço: Wool, Wilderness and the Serra da Estrela
property_intro: High on the granite slopes above Manteigas, this restored 1940s modernist retreat looks out across Portugal's Serra da Estrela, where glacial valleys and shepherds' paths still shape daily life. Interiors are dressed in Burel, the local wool whose mill was rescued from closure, bringing weavers back to the mountains. Days unfold with hikes to icy lagoons, star-filled skies, spa hours and mountain cooking, before firelit evenings and windows brimming with panorama.

property_title: Europa Palace Hotel: Refined Italian Living, Gently Reimagined
property_intro: Set within easy reach of Italy's sun-warmed coastline and historic streets, Europa Palace Hotel welcomes guests into a world of quiet elegance. Interiors pair period detail with contemporary calm, while terraces invite long, unhurried breakfasts. Days might begin with a swim, drift into market visits with local producers, and end over regional wines poured by staff who know every vineyard by name. Thoughtful sourcing and lasting ties with nearby artisans give each stay genuine depth.

property_title: Vilalara Grand Hotel Algarve: Clifftop Calm Above the Atlantic
property_intro: Set between Armação de Pêra and Lagoa, Vilalara rests on low cliffs above three quiet coves, its subtropical gardens tumbling down to the Atlantic. Thalassotherapy has been practised here for decades, drawing on seawater drawn straight from the shore, while kitchens lean on Algarvian growers and day boats. Rooms open to terraces scented with jasmine and pine; mornings might mean sea-pool laps, coastal walks along the Rota Vicentina, or simply birdsong and breakfast.

property_title: Hotel Villa Franca: Rooftop Views Over Positano's Pastel Hills
property_intro:
Perched at the upper reaches of Positano, Hotel Villa Franca looks out across tumbling pastel houses to the Tyrrhenian below. Interiors pair hand-painted Vietri tiles with cool linen and family-collected art, while the rooftop pool and terrace restaurant reward the climb with long, unhurried afternoons. Days might begin with a lemon-grove walk on the Path of the Gods and end over Campanian wines poured by staff whose roots run deep along this coast.

Warmly run, quietly refined.

property_title: Mombo & Little Mombo by Wilderness: Where the Okavango Opens Up
property_intro: On the northern tip of Chief's Island, deep within Botswana's Okavango Delta, Mombo and its intimate sibling Little Mombo overlook floodplains where lion, leopard and rhino move in astonishing numbers. Raised suites are dressed in soft linens, brass and hand-crafted detail, with plunge pools facing the grasslands. Days unfold through game drives, guided walks and long, unhurried lunches. Solar-powered and rooted in the rewilding of Botswana's rhino, this is conservation you can witness from your veranda.

property_title: Nirjhara, Bali: Waterfall Serenity Amid Rice Fields and Bamboo
property_intro: Tucked into a valley near Tanah Lot, where the Nirjhara waterfall spills through jungle and terraced rice fields, this retreat feels wonderfully removed from Bali's busier shores. Bamboo and volcanic stone shape airy suites and treehouse-style villas, opening to birdsong and river sound. Days unfold with yoga above the water, farm-led dining, and walks to nearby villages, guided by a team who champion local craft, regenerative farming and quiet, considered luxury.

property_title: HOTEL de LEN: A Larch-Scented Retreat Below the Sella Towers
property_intro: In Corvara, at the heart of Alta Badia, HOTEL de LEN takes its name from the Ladin word for wood " and the building is a quiet tribute to it. Untreated local larch and spruce, joined without glue or nails, scent rooms that frame the Sella massif. Days unfold with mountain guides, Ladin cooking and alpine spa rituals, while the family behind it champions valley artisans, regional producers and low-impact building traditions.

property_title: Terra Rosa Country House & Vineyards: Wine, Land and Quiet
property_intro: Set among rolling vines and cork oaks in Portugal's sun-warmed countryside, Terra Rosa Country House & Vineyards invites you to slow down. Rust-red walls, whitewashed interiors and shaded terraces open onto working vineyards, where harvest days and cellar tastings reveal the estate's craft. Days unfold with olive groves to wander, regional dishes shaped by neighbouring producers, and evenings spent beneath extraordinarily dark skies. A place tended with care, for land and community alike.

property_title: Hotel Santavenere: A Cliffside Retreat on Maratea's Coastline
property_intro: Tucked among olive groves and Aleppo pines above the Tyrrhenian Sea, Hotel Santavenere looks out over Maratea, Basilicata's little-known stretch of coast. Frescoed ceilings, hand-painted majolica and family antiques give the villa its unhurried character, while private coves and a seawater pool wait below. Days might involve foraging with local fishermen, hiking to the Christ the Redeemer statue, or simply lingering over Lucanian recipes made with produce from neighbouring smallholdings.

property_title: Le Carrube Masseria: Organic Puglian Calm Among Ancient Olives
property_intro: Set amid centuries-old olive groves and carob trees near Ostuni, Le Carrube Masseria is a restored Puglian farmhouse where whitewashed vaults, hand-thrown ceramics and linen shade create an unhurried rhythm. Days unfold with organic breakfasts from the estate garden, cycling along dry-stone lanes to the Adriatic, and long lunches beneath the pergola. Solar power, natural materials and local artisans underpin the pared-back design, while nearby villages reward those curious enough to wander at their own pace.

property_title: H"tel Madame R\u00eave: Parisian Poetry Above the Rooftops
property_intro: Housed in Paris's former central post office, H\u00f4tel Madame R\u00eave occupies a landmark address beside Les Halles, moments from the Louvre and Rue Montorgueil. Behind its restored fa\u00e7ade, glasshouse dining rooms and terraces frame views across the city's zinc rooftops to Saint-Eustache. Interiors balance grand proportions with quiet warmth, while the kitchens champion French growers and seasonal produce. Slip into the rooftop bar at dusk, then wander the Right Bank as the streets soften into evening.

property_title: Amethyst Selene Suites: Refined Greek Island Living Awaits
property_intro: Set among whitewashed lanes and olive-shaded terraces, Amethyst Selene Suites offers a quietly considered retreat where Aegean light shifts across handcrafted stone, linen and locally thrown ceramics. Each suite opens to sea air and slow mornings, with breakfasts drawn from neighbouring farms and evenings spent watching the horizon soften. Sail with island fishermen, forage wild herbs, or simply linger. Rainwater harvesting, solar power and partnerships with village artisans keep this sanctuary rooted in its surroundings.

property_title: The Sense Experience Resort: Tuscan Coast, Naturally Refined
property_intro: Set among umbrella pines on Tuscany's Etruscan Coast, The Sense Experience Resort opens directly onto a soft sweep of sand near Follonica. Interiors favour natural timber, linen and light, while days unfold with sunrise yoga, sailing lessons, cookery sessions and slow cycles through the Maremma. Solar energy, plastic-free practices and menus built around Maremman growers and fishermen underpin it all. Evenings bring Vermentino, seafood and the low hum of waves beyond the dunes.

property_title: Rosselli AX Privilege: Valletta's Refined Palazzo Retreat
property_intro: Tucked along Merchants Street in the heart of Valletta, Rosselli AX Privilege occupies a lovingly restored 16th-century palazzo, where original stonework and vaulted ceilings meet contemporary Maltese craftsmanship. Just 25 rooms mean attentive, unhurried service, while the rooftop terrace frames the city's honey-coloured domes and belfries. Dine at Under Grain, explore baroque churches and harbour bastions on foot, and appreciate a restoration that safeguarded local heritage and skills for the community's future.

property_title: Tortuga Bay Puntacana: Barefoot Elegance on White Caribbean Sands
property_intro: Tucked within the gated greenery of Puntacana Resort & Club on the Dominican Republic's eastern shore, Tortuga Bay opens onto a pale crescent of sand shaded by coconut palms. Oscar de la Renta's hand shapes the villas, all cool linens and louvred light, while butlers arrange dawn paddleboarding, Ecological Reserve walks or Punta Espada golf. Guests support the Puntacana Ecological Foundation, whose coral nurseries and community schooling quietly shape this stretch of coastline's future.

property_title: Mykonos Lolita: Cycladic Calm Above the Aegean's Blue Horizon
property_intro: Perched on a quiet Mykonian hillside, Mykonos Lolita looks out across the Aegean where the island's famous energy softens into something gentler. Whitewashed curves, handwoven textiles and local stone reflect Cycladic craft traditions, with island artisans and producers shaping much of what you'll touch and taste. Days unfold slowly here: swimming before breakfast, exploring hidden coves by boat, dining on Mykonian cheeses and garden herbs, then watching the sun slip behind the water.

property_title: PihlasResort: Lakeside Calm in the Heart of Finnish Forest
property_intro: Set among rowan trees and pine forest beside a still Finnish lake, PihlasResort invites you to slow down without giving anything up. Timber-clad villas frame the water through generous windows, while wood-fired saunas, quiet canoe mornings and winter skies thick with stars shape the days. Interiors favour local craft and honest materials, and much of what reaches the table is grown or foraged nearby. It is a place that rewards attention, and returns it in kind.

property_title: Mykonos Blu: Cycladic Calm Above Psarou's Shimmering Bay
property_intro: Draped across a hillside above Psarou Bay, Mykonos Blu gathers whitewashed bungalows and private pools into a village of its own, where bougainvillaea spills over sculpted stone and the Aegean glitters below. Interiors nod to Cycladic craftsmanship, with local marble, woven textiles and light that shifts through the day. Days unfold with yoga on the terrace, Greek wines poured at sunset and menus built around island growers and small fishing boats.

property_title: Corfu Imperial: Ionian Serenity on a Private Greek Peninsula
property_intro: Set on its own peninsula in Kommeno Bay, Corfu Imperial unfolds across gardens of olive and cypress, with the Ionian glinting on three sides. Ivory-toned suites and secluded villas open to private pools and quiet coves reached by winding stone paths. Days drift between sailing, Greek cookery lessons and shoreline dining, while island growers and fishermen supply the kitchens. Blue Flag beaches and careful stewardship of the coastline keep this stretch of Corfu remarkably unhurried.

property_title: Caramel: Barefoot Elegance Along Crete's Sunlit Northern Shore
property_intro: Set between the Cretan Sea and the foothills near Rethymno, Caramel unfolds as a village of low-slung suites, olive groves and hand-finished stone. Days drift from sea-view terraces to Minoan trails, cookery lessons with village producers and long lunches built on island ingredients. Interiors favour natural linen, timber and light, while the family behind it champions local growers, artisans and marine care. It is Crete at its most gracious: unhurried, generous and quietly beautiful.

property_title: Cape Sounio: Pine-Scented Bungalows Beside Poseidon's Temple
property_intro: Where Attica meets the Aegean, Cape Sounio unfolds across a pine-clad hillside beneath the marble columns of Poseidon's temple, an hour's drive from Athens. Bungalows and villas descend in terraces towards a private cove, many with plunge pools framed by olive and myrtle. Days pass with Greek cookery lessons, sunset sails and stargazing above the ruins, while the resort tends its native woodland and works with nearby producers to bring the region's flavours to the table.

property_title: Amirandes: Cretan Shores, Timeless Grace and Quiet Luxury
property_intro: On the northern coast of Crete, just beyond Heraklion, Amirandes unfolds along a sheltered stretch of Aegean shoreline where Minoan motifs, mosaics and water gardens shape every view. Suites and villas open to private pools and sea breezes, while kitchens draw on Cretan growers and the island's celebrated diet. Days might mean sailing, ancient Knossos, or pottery with local artisans. Beach clean-ups and marine care reflect a genuine commitment to this coastline's future.

property_title: The Roc Club: Slow Aegean Days on Greece's Untamed Coastline
property_intro: Tucked between olive groves and a shoreline where the water turns impossibly clear, The Roc Club invites you to settle into the rhythm of the Greek coast. Interiors of lime-washed stone, linen and locally crafted timber feel calm rather than showy. Days unfold with sunrise swims, sailing trips to hidden coves and long tables of produce grown nearby. Family-run and quietly committed to protecting its landscape, it rewards those who prefer substance to spectacle.

property_title: THE DOLLI at Acropolis: Athens Framed by Ancient Splendour
property_intro: Set within a restored 1925 neoclassical building in Plaka, THE DOLLI at Acropolis places you a whisper from the Parthenon, its marble columns visible from bedroom windows and the rooftop pool. Interiors blend Italian craftsmanship with Greek antiquity, while the terrace restaurant turns Attic produce into something quietly memorable. Wander to Monastiraki's workshops, or let the concierge arrange private museum hours. A carefully conserved landmark, it keeps Athenian artisanship and neighbourhood life at its heart.

property_title: Viceroy at Ombria Algarve: Where the Hills Hold Their Calm
property_intro: Tucked into the rolling hills near Loulé, far from the Algarve's busier shores, Viceroy at Ombria Algarve rises from a valley of cork oaks, olive groves and old carob trees. Its architecture borrows from Portuguese villages, with courtyards, stone and shade drawing the eye outwards. Days might mean golf on a sustainably designed course, a spa ritual, foraging with local growers or stargazing in a certified dark-sky reserve. Regeneration of the land guides everything here.

property_title: Naama Beach Villas & Spa: Desert Calm on the Arabian Gulf
property_intro: Set along a quiet stretch of Arabian Gulf coastline, Naama Beach Villas & Spa pairs low-slung, light-filled architecture with the soft palette of the surrounding desert. Private pools open to sea breezes, while the spa draws on regional rituals and botanicals. Days drift between mangrove paddles, dune drives with Emirati guides and long lunches of locally landed seafood. Thoughtful water stewardship and partnerships with nearby communities give this retreat a genuine sense of place.

property_title: Hotel Kitzhof Mountain Design Resort: Alpine Living, Refined
property_intro: Perched on a sunny hillside above Kitzbühel's medieval centre, Hotel Kitzhof Mountain Design Resort looks out across the Kitzbühel Alps through walls of glass. Interiors pair Tyrolean timber and loden with contemporary lines, while the rooftop pool and 3,600-square-metre spa invite long, unhurried afternoons. Local producers shape the menus, ski slopes and summer trails begin moments away, and the family-run team shares an easy familiarity with the valley's traditions, seasons and quieter corners.

property_name: Evolve Back Gham Dhao Lodge, Kalahari
property_title: Evolve Back Gham Dhao Lodge: Where the Kalahari Speaks Softly
property_intro: Set amid the ochre grasses and ancient pans of Botswana's Kalahari, Evolve Back Gham Dhao Lodge draws its rhythm from the desert itself. Suites echo San heritage in earthen tones and handcrafted detail, each with a private plunge pool facing endless horizons. Days unfold with San trackers reading the sand, meerkats at sunrise and skies thick with stars. Community partnerships and low-impact design ensure your stay gives back to this remarkable wilderness.

property_title: Evolve Back Kamalapura Palace, Hampi: Where Empires Once Rose
property_intro: On the fringes of Hampi's boulder-strewn plains, Evolve Back Kamalapura Palace draws its inspiration from the palatial architecture of the Vijayanagara empire, whose ruins lie scattered nearby. Courtyards, colonnades and lotus ponds frame private-pool suites, while local artisans and villagers shape much of the experience. Days might begin with a coracle ride along the Tungabhadra, a guided walk among ancient temple complexes, or Ayurvedic treatments drawn from centuries-old traditions, ending with Kannadiga cuisine beneath a vast, star-scattered sky.

property_title: W Costa Navarino: Design, Sea and Soul on the Messinian Riviera
property_intro: Set above the Ionian Sea on the south-western tip of the Peloponnese, W Costa Navarino brings playful, colour-drenched design to a coastline of olive groves, sea caves and Navarino Bay's storied waters. Days drift between clifftop pools, Messinian wine tastings and dawn walks where loggerhead turtles nest. Local stone, ceramics and craftsmanship shape the interiors, while partnerships with nearby villages and habitat restoration keep the region's culture and shoreline flourishing for generations to come.

property_title: The Romanos: Messinian Shores, Olive Groves and Sea Breezes
property_intro: Set along the Ionian coast of Messinia, The Romanos unfolds across dunes, olive groves and gardens where Costa Navarino's landscape has been carefully restored, with thousands of ancient olive trees replanted rather than lost. Rooms open to sea or greenery, terraces catch the afternoon light, and days drift between spa rituals, sailing, and walks to Voidokilia Bay. Nearby, family-run tavernas, Byzantine chapels and Nestor's Palace reward those curious about the Peloponnese beyond the shoreline.

property_title: The Westin Resort Costa Navarino: Messinia's Unhurried Coast
property_intro: Set above a golden sweep of Ionian shoreline in southwest Messinia, The Westin Resort Costa Navarino unfolds among olive groves, dunes and centuries-old trees replanted rather than removed. Rooms open to sea breezes and terraces shaded by greenery, while days drift between championship golf, sea kayaking, Navarino Bay's Venetian castles and cookery lessons rooted in local farms. It's a place where Greek hospitality, careful conservation and genuine village connections shape every moment.

property_title: Munduk Moding Plantation: Bali's Cloud-Kissed Coffee Highlands
property_intro: High in northern Bali's volcanic ridges, Munduk Moding Plantation sits within a working coffee estate where mist drifts through arabica rows and the mountains fall away towards the Java Sea. Villas and suites, built by local craftspeople from timber and volcanic stone, open onto an infinity pool suspended above the valley. Days unfold with plantation walks, waterfall trails and Balinese cookery, while the resort's schools and reforestation projects sustain the surrounding villages.

property_title: Grace La Margna St Moritz: A New Chapter in Engadin Elegance
property_intro: Overlooking Lake St Moritz from the edge of the Engadin's larch forests, Grace La Margna reawakens a beloved 1907 landmark with clean lines, warm timber and glass framing the peaks. Days here move between glacier air and the spa's quiet heat, with mountain guides, curated art and Alpine-sourced menus shaped by local producers. Restoring rather than replacing, the hotel keeps its heritage facade intact while championing Graubünden makers, craftspeople and the valley's fragile landscapes.

property_title: Cauayan Island Resort: Palawan's Private Shoreline Sanctuary
property_intro: Set on a secluded stretch of coast near El Nido, Cauayan Island Resort looks out across limestone islets and the clear waters of Bacuit Bay. Villas built from local hardwood and thatch step down the hillside, each opening to sea breezes and long, unhurried views. Days drift between island-hopping by bangka, snorkelling over protected reefs and slow suppers of just-landed seafood, supported by a resort that employs and invests in nearby Palaweño communities.

property_title: Taskonaklar Hotel Cappadocia: Cave Living Above the Rose Valley
property_intro: Carved into the soft tuff of Uçhisar, Taskonaklar looks out across Pigeon Valley towards the distant peak of Mount Erciyes. Restored stone mansions and cave rooms retain their arched ceilings, hand-cut niches and Ottoman detailing, furnished with kilims woven by local artisans. Wake to balloons drifting past your terrace, breakfast on village preserves and warm pide, then walk the valley footpaths straight from the door. Craftsmanship here is preserved, not imitated.

property_title: Chalet Le 1550, Courchevel: Alpine Living, Quietly Refined
property_intro: Set in Courchevel's village of Le Praz, Chalet Le 1550 sits where Olympic ski jumps meet centuries-old Savoyard timber. Reclaimed wood, stone and generous light shape interiors that invite slow mornings and long, lingering suppers. Step out to tree-lined pistes, or take the gondola towards the higher slopes and return to a crackling fire. Locally sourced menus, family-run producers and a genuine village rhythm make this a stay rooted in its mountain community.

property_title: L'Étoile des Baux: Provençal Serenity Beneath the Alpilles
property_intro: Tucked into the limestone folds of the Alpilles, L'Étoile des Baux looks out across olive groves and vineyards towards the hilltop village of Les Baux-de-Provence. Interiors pair pale stone and reclaimed timber with locally made furnishings, while the gardens are planted for pollinators and shade. Days here might mean tasting estate olive oil, cycling between Saint-Rémy's markets, or simply drifting between cypress-lined terraces as the mistral softens and the evening light turns golden.

property_title: Les Hauts de Gordes: Hillside Calm in the Heart of Luberon
property_intro: Perched above the terraced slopes of Gordes, Les Hauts de Gordes looks out across the Luberon's ochre villages, lavender rows and dry-stone walls. Interiors pair pale local limestone with linen, antique olive wood and quiet contemporary lines. Days unfold slowly: swimming beneath the pines, cycling to Sunday markets, tasting wines from neighbouring family estates. Provençal artisans and growers shape much of what you eat, drink and admire here, keeping the valley's traditions gently alive.

property_title: Alpin Panorama Hotel Hubertus: Where the Dolomites Rise
property_intro: Perched above the meadows of Valdaora in South Tyrol, Alpin Panorama Hotel Hubertus frames the Dolomites through vast windows and a sky pool that seems to float towards the peaks. Family-run for generations, it pairs local larch, loden and stone with quietly inventive alpine cooking rooted in nearby farms. Days unfold with forest walks, wellness rituals in the mountain sauna, and evenings watching alpenglow settle across the Plan de Corones ridgeline.

property_title: Hacienda Los Milagros: Timeless Mexican Warmth and Wild Beauty
property_intro: Set among sun-warmed hills and centuries-old stone walls, Hacienda Los Milagros invites you to slow down in a corner of Mexico where tradition still shapes daily rhythms. Restored with reverence, its shaded courtyards, hand-painted tiles and candlelit corridors tell stories of generations past. Ride out at dawn, forage with the kitchen team, or learn from local artisans whose craft the hacienda helps sustain. Native gardens and spring-fed waters flourish here, quietly tended and generously shared.

property_title: Lazure Hotel & Marina: Bay of Kotor Living, Beautifully Restored
property_intro: Set along the shoreline of Herceg Novi, where the Bay of Kotor narrows between mountains and open Adriatic, Lazure Hotel & Marina occupies a lovingly restored 19th-century naval building. Vaulted stone interiors meet contemporary calm, while the private marina invites slow mornings and sailing afternoons. Dine on Montenegrin catch and garden produce, swim from the terraced rocks, then wander into the old town's lanes. Local craftsmanship and heritage conservation shape every detail here.

property_title:
Casa Nossa by Jos
e Avillez: A Chef's Table in the Alentejo
property_intro:
Set among cork oaks and vineyards, Casa Nossa by Jos
e Avillez is the celebrated chef's own retreat in Portugal, where the kitchen leads and everything else follows. Days unfold at a gentle pace: foraging walks, long lunches beneath the pergola, conversations with growers who supply the table. Interiors favour lime-washed walls, local stone and Portuguese craftsmanship, while regenerative farming and partnerships with nearby producers keep the surrounding countryside, and its community, thriving.

property_title: The Royal Crescent Hotel & Spa: Georgian Bath, Quietly Grand
property_intro: Set at the centre of Bath's most celebrated Georgian crescent, this listed townhouse hotel keeps its 18th-century bones intact while feeling wonderfully lived-in. Behind the honeyed stone facade, walled gardens open onto the Dower House restaurant, where West Country growers shape the menu, and the Bath House spa invites long, unhurried afternoons. Antiques, hand-painted papers and open fires set the mood; the city's baths, bookshops and abbey lie moments beyond the front door.

property_title: 11 Cadogan Gardens: Chelsea Elegance Behind a Red-Brick Door
property_intro: Tucked along a leafy Chelsea garden square, 11 Cadogan Gardens occupies four Victorian townhouses where panelled corridors, antique portraits and bold contemporary fabrics sit in easy conversation. Sloane Square and the boutiques of Duke of York Square wait moments away, yet the mood indoors remains hushed and wonderfully private. Sip a cocktail in the Hollywood-glamour bar, dine on seasonal British produce, then retreat to a room dressed with genuine character rather than uniform polish.

property_title: The Lygon Arms: Honeyed Cotswold Stone and Centuries of Welcome
property_intro: On Broadway's high street, where honey-coloured stone catches the late afternoon light, The Lygon Arms has offered shelter since the 14th century \among slept beneath its beams. Today, log fires and flagstone floors meet a spa, a barn conversion and gardens tended for pollinators. Walk the Cotswold Way from the door, explore village makers and growers, then return to a dining room where local farms shape each menu.

property_title: Cliveden House: A Storied Berkshire Estate Above the River Thames
property_intro: Set high above the Thames on 376 acres of National Trust parkland, Cliveden House has hosted three centuries of guests, gossip and grand gestures. Its Italianate façade gives way to panelled drawing rooms, log fires and bedrooms named for former residents. Wander the formal parterre and water garden, glide downriver in a vintage launch, then retreat to the spa. Kitchen gardens supply the restaurants, while conservation work keeps this landscape flourishing for generations to come.

property_title: Terre Blanche: Provençal Serenity Among Hills and Olive Groves
property_intro: Set across 750 acres of Provençal countryside near the hilltop village of Tourrettes, Terre Blanche unfolds in a landscape of olive groves, oak woodland and lavender. Suites open onto private terraces with views towards the Esterel hills, while two championship golf courses, a spa built around water and a kitchen garden shape unhurried days. Local producers supply the restaurants, and native planting and beekeeping sustain the estate's wildlife — Provence, quietly and generously interpreted.

property_title: EPIC SANA Algarve Hotel: Refined Coastal Living in Albufeira
property_intro: Set among pine groves above Falésia Beach, EPIC SANA Algarve Hotel brings a considered calm to the Albufeira coastline. Light-filled interiors open onto gardens and five pools, while the Sayanna Wellness spa invites slower mornings. Dine on Algarvian catch and produce from nearby growers, wander the red cliffs at dusk, or let the little ones loose in the kids' club. Sustainability runs quietly through it all, from energy efficiency to local sourcing.

property_title: Chewton Glen Hotel & Spa: Where the New Forest Meets the Sea
property_intro: Tucked between the ancient woodland of the New Forest and the Solent shoreline, Chewton Glen unfolds across 130 acres of Hampshire countryside, where deer graze and kitchen gardens supply the plate. Treehouse suites hover among the canopy, the spa's hydrotherapy pool invites slow mornings, and days might be spent foraging, riding or sharpening your knife skills in the cookery school. Local producers and woodland stewardship are quietly championed here — refined, unhurried and genuinely generous.

property_title: La Signoria: Corsican Serenity Between Pinewoods and Calvi Bay
property_intro: Set within a centuries-old estate of eucalyptus, olive and umbrella pines just beyond Calvi, La Signoria feels like a private Corsican domain rather than a hotel. Ochre walls, cool stone floors and antique-filled rooms speak of the island's Genoese past, while the kitchen draws on garden herbs, mountain cheeses and day-boat fish. Spend mornings hiking the Balagne hills, afternoons by the pool, and evenings beneath the plane trees.}

property_title: Go Quito Hotel: Andean Warmth in Ecuador's Highland Capital
property_intro: Tucked between the volcanic peaks that cradle Ecuador's capital, Go Quito Hotel offers a considered base for exploring one of South America's most beguiling cities. Colonial plazas, artisan workshops and the Equator itself lie within easy reach, while interiors pair contemporary calm with Andean craftsmanship. Local guides share the city through their own eyes, breakfasts favour Ecuadorian growers, and staff from surrounding neighbourhoods bring genuine warmth to every arrival. A thoughtful beginning to any highland journey.

property_title: La Maison d'Estournel: Vineyard Days in the Heart of the Médoc
property_intro: Set among the gravelly vineyards of Saint-Estèphe, this 19th-century chartreuse belongs to the celebrated Cos d'Estournel estate. Fourteen rooms unfold with unfussed elegance: linen, timber and light, arranged around a walled garden and a discreet pool. Days drift between cellar tastings, cycling the Gironde's quiet lanes and long lunches drawn from the kitchen garden and neighbouring producers. Wines are farmed with organic care, and the welcome feels less like a hotel than a friend's country house.

property_title: Illa Experience Hotel: Heritage, Art and Andean Warmth in Quito
property_intro: Set in San Marcos, one of the oldest and most characterful corners of Quito's UNESCO-listed centre, Illa occupies a lovingly restored 19th-century house where each floor tells a different chapter of Ecuadorian history through art, craft and design. Days begin with volcano views from the rooftop and unfold through chocolate tastings, market walks and conversations with local makers. Family-run and community-minded, it offers a genuinely personal way to know the capital.

property_title: King Jason Zante: Refined Adults-Only Calm on Zakynthos
property_intro: Set among the gentle green folds of Zakynthos, moments from the sands of Kalamaki, King Jason Zante is an adults-only retreat shaped for slow, unhurried days. Interiors favour natural textures and soft Ionian light, while swim-up suites open directly onto water. Dine on Zakynthian produce, unwind in the spa, then walk to the bay where loggerhead turtles nest under local protection. It is thoughtful island living, close to nature yet quietly indulgent.

property_name: Tanah Gajah, a Resort by Hadiprana
property_title: Tanah Gajah: Art, Rice Fields and Ubud's Quiet Elegance
property_intro: Set among five hectares of rice terraces on Ubud's eastern edge, Tanah Gajah was once the private residence of celebrated Indonesian designer Hendra Hadiprana. His collection of Balinese art still fills the pavilions, while just twenty villas share gardens, lotus ponds and views towards Mount Agung. Days unfold with barefoot walks past farmers tending the fields, spa rituals beneath thatched roofs, and dinners drawing on produce grown and harvested close by.

property_title: Matetsi Victoria Falls: Quiet Luxury on a Wilder Zambezi Bend
property_intro: Fifteen miles of private Zambezi riverfront lie upstream of Victoria Falls, and Matetsi has them almost entirely to itself. Suites of stone, timber and glass open onto the water, where elephants drink at dusk and the current carries the distant sound of the falls. Days unfold with river cruises, walking safaris and guided game drives across a 55,000-hectare reserve, protected through anti-poaching work and long-standing partnerships with neighbouring communities and their schools.

property_name: Seven Secrets Resort by Hanging Gardens
property_title: Seven Secrets Resort by Hanging Gardens: Lombok's Coastal Calm
property_intro: On Lombok's west coast, where Mangsit's black-sand shore meets gardens shaded by frangipani, Seven Secrets Resort unfolds as a village of villas and hidden courtyards. Days drift between the beachfront pool, Sasak-inspired spa rituals and boat trips to the Gili Islands, with Mount Agung silhouetted across the strait at dusk. Local artisans shaped much of the woodwork and textiles here, and the kitchen draws on nearby farms and fishermen, keeping island traditions quietly, genuinely alive.

property_title: Jashita Tulum Hotel: Barefoot Serenity on Soliman Bay Shores
property_intro: Tucked between the turquoise calm of Soliman Bay and the wild green of the Sian Ka'an biosphere, Jashita feels like a secret shared among friends. Suites open onto white sand and sea breeze, with Mediterranean lines softened by Mayan craftsmanship. Days unfold slowly: snorkelling the reef, kayaking to hidden cenotes, or lingering over Italian-Mexican plates. Sea turtles nest metres away, protected by the hotel's own conservation efforts alongside the local community.

property_title: Castle Hot Springs: Arizona's Secluded Desert Spring Retreat
property_intro: Tucked into a remote Sonoran Desert canyon an hour from Phoenix, Castle Hot Springs draws its warmth from mineral springs that have soothed travellers for centuries. Bungalows and sky-view cabins sit among palms and citrus, while the farm supplies much of what appears on your plate. Days unfold with via ferrata climbs, horseback rides and stargazing beneath famously dark skies. Arizona's oldest resort, thoughtfully revived, remains off-grid, solar-powered and delightfully free of mobile signal.

property_title: Voaara Madagascar: Barefoot Luxury on a Wild Island Shore
property_intro: On Madagascar's remote coastline, Voaara unfolds among baobabs and turquoise shallows, where handcrafted villas of local timber and thatch open to the sea breeze. Days pass snorkelling coral gardens, paddling mangrove channels or walking with village guides who know every bird call. Meals draw on island produce and the morning's catch. Reef protection and community partnerships underpin everything here, so time spent at Voaara leaves the surrounding waters and villages measurably stronger.

property_title: Time + Tide Tsara Komba: Barefoot Luxury on Nosy Komba
property_intro: On the forested slopes of Nosy Komba, between Nosy Be and Madagascar's mainland, Time + Tide Tsara Komba unfolds across a hillside of wild spices and ylang-ylang. Eight timber lodges look out to the Mozambique Channel, where humpback whales pass and lemurs wander close. Days drift between snorkelling coral gardens, sailing to remote islets and dining on Malagasy flavours grown nearby. The lodge supports village schools and marine protection, making every stay quietly meaningful.

property_title: Creta Maris Resort: Cretan Shores, Gardens and Slow Days
property_intro: Set along the sandy edge of Hersonissos on Crete's northern coast, Creta Maris unfolds like a village in miniature, its whitewashed low-rise buildings threaded with bougainvillaea and shaded courtyards. Days drift between the Aegean, olive groves and a cookery school celebrating the island's Mediterranean diet. The resort's commitment to renewable energy, zero single-use plastics and local producers runs quietly through every meal, while Minoan Knossos and the Lasithi mountains wait just beyond the gates.

property_title: The Olivar Suites: Corfu's Olive Grove Retreat by the Ionian Sea
property_intro: Tucked into a centuries-old olive grove on Corfu's gentle south-east coast, The Olivar Suites unfolds between silvery branches and the shallow, glassy waters of Messonghi. Suites in earth tones and local stone open onto private gardens, while barefoot dining draws on Corfiot producers and the estate's own oil. Days pass slowly here: sea kayaking, cookery lessons, cycling village lanes. The grove remains protected, its trees still harvested each autumn, its birdsong undisturbed.

property_title: Grand Resort Bad Ragaz: Alpine Thermal Waters & Quiet Luxury
property_intro: Set where the Rhine valley meets the peaks of eastern Switzerland, Grand Resort Bad Ragaz draws on thermal water flowing from the nearby Tamina Gorge, a healing tradition dating back centuries. Days unfold between medical spa treatments, golf across two courses, and dining that ranges from Michelin-starred tasting menus to garden-fresh simplicity. Contemporary art punctuates the grounds, local producers supply the kitchens, and the mountains beyond invite walking, cycling and unhurried thinking.

property_title: Hotel Number Nine: Refined Italian Living, Quietly Reimagined
property_intro: Tucked into a handsome corner of the city, Hotel Number Nine welcomes guests into a restored townhouse where original stonework meets considered contemporary design. Mornings begin with espresso on the terrace; afternoons unfold through neighbouring piazzas, artisan workshops and family-run trattorie known only to locals. Interiors favour Italian craftsmanship, natural materials and pieces sourced within the region, while partnerships with nearby producers keep the kitchen seasonal. Intimate, unhurried and genuinely rooted in its surroundings.

property_title: Le Farnatchi: A Hidden Riad Sanctuary in Marrakech's Medina
property_intro: Tucked down a quiet derb in Marrakech's old medina, Le Farnatchi gathers a handful of former riads around courtyards of citrus trees, carved cedar and hand-cut zellige. Suites open onto private terraces where the call to prayer drifts over the rooftops. Days might begin with a hammam ritual and end with Moroccan cooking learned from the kitchen team. Local artisans shaped every detail, and their craft continues to be championed here.

property_title: Hotel Tannenhof Superior: Alpine Calm in Austria's Mountains
property_intro: Tucked among Austria's pine-clad slopes, Hotel Tannenhof Superior offers a gentler rhythm of mountain living. Interiors pair locally milled timber with soft wool and stone, warmed by open fires after days on the trails or pistes. Family-run for generations, the house serves regional produce from neighbouring farms and dairies, while the spa draws on Alpine herbs. Wake to valley views, wander forest paths from the door, and let the mountains set the pace.

property_title: White Pearl Resorts: Barefoot Luxury on Mozambique's Wild Coast
property_intro: Set along a remote stretch of dune-backed shoreline in southern Mozambique, White Pearl Resorts looks out over the Indian Ocean where humpback whales pass each winter and turtles nest above the tideline. Twenty-two glass-fronted villas open to sea breezes, their pared-back design shaped by driftwood tones and natural light. Days drift between ocean safaris, dhow sailing and treatments overlooking the water, while the resort's turtle monitoring and local employment quietly sustain this fragile, extraordinary coast.

property_title: La Selva Eco-Lodge and Retreat: Where the Amazon Awakens Slowly
property_intro: Set on the shores of Garzacocha lagoon deep within Ecuador's Yasuní Biosphere Reserve, La Selva is reached only by river, an hour downstream from Coca. Palm-thatched suites open to mirrored water and morning mist, while canopy towers, kayaks and Kichwa-guided forest walks reveal one of the planet's richest ecosystems. Owned in partnership with the neighbouring community, the lodge channels its earnings into conservation, education and local livelihoods. Evenings belong to candlelight, cacao and cicadas.

property_title: The Donna Portals: Coastal Calm Above Mallorca's Marina Bay
property_intro: Perched above the yacht-lined bay of Portals Nous, The Donna Portals brings a quieter kind of Mallorcan luxury to the island's southwest coast. Interiors pair local stone, linen and handcrafted ceramics with light-filled terraces framing the Mediterranean. Days unfold with sunrise swims, cycling through Tramuntana foothills or long lunches drawn from nearby farms and day boats. The team works closely with island artisans and growers, so every stay quietly supports the community that shapes it.

property_title: La Fiermontina Ocean: Barefoot Artistry on Morocco's Atlantic
property_intro: Set between eucalyptus groves and the wild Atlantic shore near Taghazout, La Fiermontina Ocean is a family-founded retreat where Moroccan craftsmanship meets contemporary art. Whitewashed rooms open onto gardens and sea views, while days unfurl through surf lessons, hammam rituals, yoga and long lunches built around produce from local growers. The owners work closely with Berber artisans and neighbouring villages, so every woven textile and hand-thrown vessel carries a story worth taking home.

property_title: Palazzo delle Pietre: Stone, Light and Italian Slow Living
property_intro: Set within a lovingly restored stone residence, Palazzo delle Pietre invites you to settle into the rhythm of Italian village life. Vaulted ceilings, lime-washed walls and locally quarried stone frame rooms that feel lived-in rather than staged. Days unfold with market visits, vineyard walks and long lunches prepared from neighbouring farms. Artisans from the surrounding region shaped much of the interior, and their craft continues to support the community that makes this place quietly extraordinary.

property_title: Cheetah Plains: Solar-Powered Safari Living in the Sabi Sand
property_intro: Set within the Sabi Sand Game Reserve, sharing unfenced borders with Kruger, Cheetah Plains reimagines the safari lodge as three private plains houses, each taken exclusively with its own chef, host and guide. Architecture in raw concrete, timber and glass frames the bushveld, while electric game vehicles trail leopards in near silence. Entirely solar-powered and rooted in local employment and land restoration, it offers a rare thing: wilderness immersion that gives more than it takes.

property_title: Dukley Hotel & Resort: Adriatic Serenity on Budva's Shore
property_intro: Set on its own pine-scented peninsula between two sandy bays near Budva, Dukley Hotel & Resort offers a rare kind of privacy along Montenegro's Adriatic coast. Contemporary suites open onto terraces where the sea shifts from turquoise to indigo, while a private beach, marina and wellness spaces invite unhurried days. Dine on Mediterranean produce from nearby growers, wander the old town's stone lanes, then return as the Lustica hills fade into dusk.

property_title: MalaMala Game Reserve: Where the Wild Sabi Sand Comes Close
property_intro: Bordering the Kruger National Park along the Sand River, MalaMala occupies one of the most game-rich corners of the Sabi Sand, with no fences to interrupt the movement of elephant, lion and leopard. Once a hunting concession, it has been devoted to conservation since 1964, and its land has been returned to the N'wandlamhari community. Days unfold in open vehicles with seasoned rangers; evenings on your veranda, listening to the bush settle.

property_title: La Fiermontina Luxury Home: Art, Family and Puglia's Soul
property_intro: Tucked behind honey-coloured walls in the heart of baroque Lecce, La Fiermontina began as one family's tribute to their Puglian roots. Sculptures by Fiermonte and Matisse punctuate the olive-shaded gardens, while whitewashed rooms hold hand-woven textiles and locally quarried stone. Days unfold slowly here: breakfast beneath the ancient olive trees, cookery lessons with Salento producers, cycling to the Adriatic. Restored with local artisans, the house supports the craftspeople and growers who shape its character.

property_title: Fregate Island Private: Seychelles' Wild Sanctuary Retreat
property_intro: Set adrift in the Indian Ocean, Fregate Island Private is a granite outcrop where giant tortoises roam freely and seven beaches remain gloriously uncrowded. Sixteen timber residences sit high among the treetops, opening to views over Anse Victorin and the forest canopy below. Days unfold with marine biologists, birdwatching among rare magpie robins, or dining wherever the mood takes you. Decades of rewilding have restored native woodland here, making conservation the quiet heartbeat of every stay.

property_title: Kennedy's Group: Refined Greek Coastal Living, Thoughtfully Done
property_intro: Set along the Greek coast where pine-scented breezes meet the Aegean, Kennedy's Group offers a considered take on Mediterranean hospitality. Interiors pair local stone, handwoven textiles and soft natural light, creating spaces that feel calm rather than curated. Days unfold slowly: sea swims before breakfast, market visits with local growers, long dinners built around regional produce. The team works closely with nearby villages and artisans, ensuring your stay quietly supports the community that gives this stretch of coastline its character.

property_title: La Residence: Franschhoek's Vineyard Sanctuary of Colour
property_intro: Set among vines, plum orchards and olive groves in the Franschhoek Valley, La Residence is a theatrical retreat where mountain views meet interiors layered with silk, antiques and colour drawn from across the world. Days unfold slowly: tastings at neighbouring estates, horse rides through the valley, long lunches beneath the oaks. The surrounding 30-acre estate is tended with care, and the team's ties to the local village run deep, shaping a stay that feels genuinely rooted.

property_title: Palazzo di Varignana: Olive Groves Above the Bolognese Hills
property_intro: Set among the rolling hills east of Bologna, Palazzo di Varignana unfolds across terraced gardens, vineyards and some 500 hectares of olive groves that yield the estate's own oil. An eighteenth-century villa sits at its heart, restored with restraint and paired with contemporary suites, thermal-inspired pools and a spa built around slow, considered wellbeing. Days might mean harvest walks, cookery lessons with Emilia-Romagna's finest produce, or simply the long view over the Apennines at dusk.

property_title: The Boca Raton: Where Florida's Gold Coast Glamour Still Endures
property_intro: Set between the Intracoastal Waterway and a private stretch of Atlantic shoreline, The Boca Raton has welcomed guests since 1926, when Addison Mizner's Mediterranean vision first rose from the Florida sand. Today its five distinct hotels, half-mile beach club and cathedral-ceilinged Cloister invite slower days: tennis at dawn, paddling through mangrove channels, dinners drawn from Florida growers. Restoration work honours the original architecture, while sea turtle nesting programmes quietly protect the coastline just beyond your terrace.

property_title: Hotel Mediterraneo Sorrento: Citrus Gardens and Cliffside Views
property_intro: Perched on the cliffs above Sorrento's rocky shoreline, Hotel Mediterraneo looks across the Bay of Naples towards Vesuvius, with Capri shimmering on the horizon. Lemon and orange groves scent the terraces, while a private lift carries guests down to the sea. Interiors pair handmade Vietri tiles with quiet contemporary comfort, and the kitchen leans on produce from the hotel's own gardens and neighbouring Campanian farms. Days unfold slowly here: swimming, boat trips along the peninsula, and long dinners under the pergola.

property_title: Castello di Velona: Thermal Calm Above Tuscany's Val d'Orcia
property_intro: Perched on a hilltop above the Val d'Orcia, this eleventh-century castle looks out across Brunello vineyards, cypress ridges and the distant slopes of Monte Amiata. Thermal springs feed the spa, while stone-vaulted suites pair medieval bones with quietly contemporary comfort. Days unfold slowly: cellar tastings with local growers, truffle hunts, horseback rides through the UNESCO-listed valley. Careful restoration has kept original masonry and frescoes intact, and the kitchen leans on estate produce and neighbouring Sienese farms.

property_title: Chablé Maroma: Barefoot Luxury on the Riviera Maya's Shore
property_intro: Set between mangrove-fringed jungle and the pale sands of Maroma Beach, Chablé Maroma unfolds as a collection of casitas with private plunge pools, shaded by native palms. Mayan healing rituals shape the spa, while menus draw on Yucatecan gardens and the day's catch. Sea turtles nest on the shoreline under the resort's watch, and local artisans inform the interiors. Days drift between cenote swims, hammocks and long, unhurried dinners beneath the stars.

property_title: Cresta Palace Celerina: Alpine Warmth in the Engadin Valley
property_intro: Set in the sun-filled village of Celerina, moments from St Moritz, Cresta Palace opens onto the wide Engadin valley and its larch forests, frozen lakes and high mountain passes. Behind the historic 1906 facade, interiors blend Alpine craftsmanship with contemporary calm, while the spa, terrace and family-friendly spaces invite unhurried days. Ski, walk or cycle straight from the door, then return to regional cooking rooted in nearby farms and long-standing valley partnerships.

property_title: Masseria Montenapoleone: Puglia's Slow-Living Country Retreat
property_intro: Set among ancient olive groves in Puglia's Valle d'Itria, Masseria Montenapoleone is a restored seventeenth-century farmhouse where whitewashed stone, vaulted ceilings and hand-thrown ceramics tell of generations past. Days unfold slowly here: breakfasts of garden fruit and local cheeses, cookery lessons with the family, cycle rides to Ostuni's white streets. The gardens are tended organically, produce comes from neighbouring smallholders, and the welcome is genuinely familial eel yourself already lingering at the long table under the pergola.

property_title: Castilla Termal Brihuega: Where Lavender Meets Thermal Waters
property_intro: Set within a meticulously restored royal cloth factory commissioned by Carlos III, this Guadalajara retreat looks out over the rolling Alcarria and the lavender fields that turn Brihuega violet each July. Vaulted stone galleries and hushed courtyards lead to thermal waters drawn from beneath the hillside, while the kitchen leans on honey, saffron and produce from neighbouring villages. Heritage conservation and local craftsmanship shape every corner, making a stay here feel quietly purposeful as well as restorative.

property_title: Castelfalfi: A Restored Tuscan Village Among Rolling Vineyards
property_intro: Tucked into the wooded hills between Florence, Siena and Pisa, Castelfalfi is a medieval borgo brought gently back to life across 1,100 hectares of vineyards, olive groves and oak forest. Stone farmhouses and a hilltop castle have been restored with local craftsmanship, while the estate's cellar, kitchen gardens and beehives supply its tables. Spend days truffle hunting, riding through the valleys or simply watching the light shift over Tuscany.

property_title: Chablé Yucatán, México: Jungle Sanctuary of Maya Wellbeing
property_intro: Set within a restored 19th-century hacienda deep in the Yucatán jungle, Chablé Yucatán gathers its casitas around a sacred cenote once used by Maya healers. Days unfold with temazcal ceremonies, cenote swims and cooking rooted in the estate's own gardens. Contemporary architecture meets centuries-old limestone walls, while local artisans, beekeepers and conservation of native flora shape daily life here. It is a place to slow down, listen and reconnect with something older than luxury.

property_title: Rainforest Expeditions: Amazon Immersion in Peru's Wild Heart
property_intro: Deep in the Tambopata region of southern Peru, Rainforest Expeditions welcomes guests into three lodges shaped by the forest itself, with open-walled rooms that invite birdsong and river breeze indoors. Founded in partnership with the Ese'eja community of Infierno, it channels its earnings into local livelihoods and long-term research. Days unfold along oxbow lakes, macaw clay licks and canopy towers, guided by naturalists who read the Amazon like a familiar page. Something new reveals itself hourly.

property_title: Naturalis Bio Resort & SPA: Organic Serenity in Salento, Puglia
property_intro: Tucked among centuries-old olive groves in Andrano, deep in Puglia's Salento, Naturalis Bio Resort & SPA turns rural life into something quietly indulgent. Rooms in restored stone buildings open onto gardens where herbs, citrus and vegetables are grown for the kitchen, while the spa draws on plant-based rituals. Days drift between the pool, yoga beneath the pines and cycling to the Adriatic coves nearby. Organic farming, local artisans and seasonal Salentine cooking shape every stay.

property_title: Tenuta Centoporte: Salento Serenity Among Ancient Olive Groves
property_intro: Set in the sun-warmed countryside near Otranto, Tenuta Centoporte unfolds across olive groves and dry-stone walls where Salento's dolmens and menhirs still stand. Pale local stone, vaulted ceilings and shaded courtyards shape rooms that feel unhurried, while the pool and gardens invite long, slow afternoons. Days might bring cookery lessons with produce from nearby growers, cycling to Adriatic coves, or evenings of Puglian wine. Family-run, rooted in the land and generous with its stories.

property_title: Torre a Cona: An Historic Tuscan Villa Where Time Slows Down
property_intro: Set on a hilltop just beyond Florence, Torre a Cona presides over olive groves, vineyards and quiet oak woodland. This eighteenth-century villa remains in the hands of the family who have farmed the estate for generations, with frescoed salons, walled gardens and a working cellar producing Chianti and olive oil. Days unfold with vineyard walks, cookery lessons and long lunches beneath the loggia \u2014 Florence close by, yet delightfully easy to forget.

property_title: The Rebello Hotel: A Riverside Reawakening in Vila Nova de Gaia
property_intro: Set along the Douro's southern bank in Vila Nova de Gaia, The Rebello occupies a cluster of restored warehouses and workshops once bound to the river trade, now reimagined with tactile stone, timber and light. Porto's bridges glitter across the water; port lodges and studios line the streets behind. Days drift between the rooftop pool, spa rituals and slow dinners, while local makers and producers shape much of what you touch, taste and take home.

property_title: Hotel Metropole Venezia: Venetian Curiosities on the Lagoon
property_intro: Moments from St Mark's Square, on the Riva degli Schiavoni, Hotel Metropole gazes across the lagoon towards San Giorgio Maggiore. Behind its historic facade lies a labyrinth of antiques, fans, corkscrews and curios gathered across generations, alongside a scented garden that perfumes the halls. Once a music school where Vivaldi taught, it remains devoted to craft: Murano glass, Fortuny silks, Venetian recipes reimagined, and quiet support for the city's artisans and cultural life.

property_title: Erosantorini: Cliffside Seclusion Above the Santorini Caldera
property_intro: Carved into the volcanic cliffs of Akrotiri, Erosantorini is a private estate where terraces, plunge pools and cave-cut suites step down towards the caldera. Stone, timber and locally crafted furnishings echo the island's raw geology, while a dedicated team arranges vineyard tastings, sunset sails and dinners guided by Santorinian growers. Only a handful of guests stay at any time, keeping the estate quiet, the water and produce carefully sourced, and the island's traditions genuinely close at hand.

property_title: AlmaLusa Baixa/Chiado: Lisbon's Soul in a Historic Townhouse
property_intro: Set on Praça do Município, moments from Chiado's bookshops and the Tagus waterfront, AlmaLusa occupies an 18th-century townhouse restored with quiet confidence. Just 28 rooms pair original stonework with furniture, ceramics and textiles made by Portuguese artisans, many from small family workshops. Downstairs, Delfina serves regional cooking rooted in local producers, while the concierge points guests towards neighbourhood tascas and tram routes rather than crowds. It is Lisbon at close range, unhurried and genuinely lived-in.

property_title: SOWK Resort: Where Thailand's Quiet Landscapes Invite You In
property_intro: Tucked into Thailand's gentler countryside, SOWK Resort offers a rhythm shaped by birdsong, warm breezes and unhurried mornings. Timber, stone and open-sided pavilions frame views of rice fields and distant hills, while interiors favour local craftsmanship over ornament. Days unfold through market visits, cycling along village lanes and cooking with produce grown nearby. The resort works closely with neighbouring farmers and artisans, ensuring your stay leaves something meaningful behind long after you depart.

property_title: Hotel de Russie: Rome's Hidden Garden Between Two Grand Piazzas
property_intro: Tucked between Piazza del Popolo and the Spanish Steps, Hotel de Russie conceals one of Rome's great surprises: the terraced Secret Garden, where citrus trees, fountains and resident butterflies climb towards the Pincio. Interiors by Olga Polizzi balance Roman grandeur with quiet restraint, while the Wellness Zone and Stravinskij Bar draw a loyal local following. Beekeeping on the terraces, seasonal produce from nearby growers and guided walks through artisan quarters deepen the sense of place.

property_title: La Gemma Hotel: Refined Florentine Living in the Heart of the City
property_intro: Tucked into a quiet corner of Florence, moments from the Duomo, La Gemma occupies a handsome palazzo where Renaissance proportions meet contemporary Italian craft. Rooms are dressed in local marble, hand-woven textiles and pieces by Tuscan artisans, while the kitchen draws on producers from the surrounding hills. Days here might begin with a private gallery visit and end over dinner beneath vaulted ceilings, the city's rhythms unfolding just beyond the shutters.

property_title: AlmaLusa Alfama: Where Lisbon's Oldest Quarter Truly Comes Alive
property_intro: Tucked into the tiled lanes of Alfama, where fado drifts from doorways and washing lines criss-cross the sky, AlmaLusa offers a considered welcome to Lisbon's most storied quarter. Interiors pair restored period details with Portuguese craftsmanship, from cork to hand-thrown ceramics, while the kitchen champions small regional producers. Wander to the Sé cathedral, catch a tram rattling past, then return for a glass of Alentejo red. Family-run, quietly generous and deeply rooted in its neighbourhood.

property_title: Palazzo Margherita: Southern Italian Splendour in Basilicata
property_intro:
In the hilltop town of Bernalda, deep in Basilicata, a 19th-century palazzo opens its doors with unhurried southern warmth. Restored by the Coppola family with local artisans, its nine rooms wear hand-painted ceilings, Moorish tilework and Jacques Grange's careful eye. Days drift between the walled citrus garden, pasta-making with Bernaldese cooks and evening films in the courtyard. Beyond the gates lie Matera's cave dwellings, Ionian beaches and villages where nobody hurries.

A rare, rooted kind of luxury.}
