property_title: Miavana: Barefoot Luxury on Madagascar's Wildest Frontier
property_intro: Reached by helicopter over turquoise shallows, Miavana rests on Nosy Ankao, a private island off Madagascar's remote north-east coast. Fourteen villas open onto powder-soft sand, their design shaped by local craftsmanship and shifting sea light. Days might involve tracking lemurs in nearby forests, diving with turtles, or kitesurfing across empty lagoons. Behind it all sits serious conservation work and partnership with neighbouring villages, ensuring this extraordinary corner of the Indian Ocean thrives long after you've left.

property_title: Sandblu Resort Santorini: Whitewashed Calm by Volcanic Sands
property_intro: On Santorini's quieter south-eastern coast, Sandblu Resort looks out across dark volcanic sand and open Aegean horizon, far from the crush of the caldera towns. Sculpted whitewashed suites, private plunge pools and shaded terraces echo Cycladic building traditions, while menus lean on island growers, Assyrtiko vines and the day's catch. Spend mornings swimming before breakfast, afternoons exploring Kamari's vineyards and ruins, and evenings watching the sea turn silver.

property_title: GoldenEye: Ian Fleming's Legendary Slice of Jamaica's North Coast
property_intro: On the shore at Oracabessa, where Ian Fleming wrote the Bond novels, GoldenEye unfolds across lagoons, private beaches and gardens thick with breadfruit and sea grape. Villas and beach huts are dressed in Jamaican craftsmanship, louvred and open to the trade winds. Days drift between paddleboarding the brackish lagoon, reggae evenings at Bizot Bar and snorkelling the Oracabessa Fish Sanctuary, a community-led reef project quietly restoring life beneath the water.

property_title: Petit St. Vincent: A Private Grenadine Island of Quiet Luxury
property_intro: On its own 115-acre island in the southern Grenadines, Petit St. Vincent has no telephones or televisions — guests raise a yellow flag for service, or a red one for solitude. Twenty-two stone cottages, built by local craftsmen from island bluebitch rock, sit among hibiscus and sea grape above nine beaches. Days drift between the Jean-Michel Cousteau dive centre, hilltop yoga and the organic garden, while coral restoration and island schooling quietly shape the community.

property_title: Jade Mountain: Open-Air Sanctuaries Between Saint Lucia's Pitons
property_intro: Rising above Soufri\u00e8re on Saint Lucia's forested west coast, Jade Mountain frames the Pitons through sanctuaries that dispense with fourth walls entirely. Each has its own infinity pool, hand-laid tilework and uninterrupted view of the Caribbean Sea. Days unfold with reef snorkelling, cocoa harvesting on the estate's historic plantation and dinners built around produce grown metres from the kitchen. Local craftsmanship shapes every detail, while long-standing community partnerships keep the surrounding marine reserve and rainforest thriving.

property_title: Segera: Laikipia's Living Canvas of Wilderness and Wonder
property_intro: Set on the Laikipia plateau with Mount Kenya rising beyond the acacia, Segera is a 50,000-acre retreat where art, agriculture and conservation meet. Six timber villas stand amid gardens once grazed bare by cattle, now restored to teeming grassland. Days unfold on horseback, on foot with Maasai guides, or wandering a sculpture collection that rewards slow looking. Rhino and wild dog roam the reserve, while nearby communities share in its healthcare, schooling and enterprise.

property_title: Alladale Wilderness Reserve: Rewilding the Scottish Highlands
property_intro: Tucked into 23,000 acres of glen, loch and regenerating forest in Sutherland, Alladale Wilderness Reserve invites you to settle into a Victorian lodge or one of two remote cottages, where log fires, wood panelling and long views set the pace. Days unfold with stalking, wild swimming, mountain biking or tree planting alongside the rangers restoring native woodland. Every stay supports ambitious rewilding work and the Highland communities who make it possible.

property_title: Broughton Sanctuary: Wild Yorkshire Renewal on an Ancient Estate
property_intro: Set within 3,000 acres of the Yorkshire Dales, Broughton Sanctuary unfolds around a 900-year-old hall still cared for by the same family. Ancient woodland, restored moorland and wildflower meadows form part of an ambitious rewilding project, while interiors pair heirloom antiques with quiet contemporary comfort. Days here might mean breathwork at dawn, wild swimming, forest walks or long dinners drawn from the kitchen garden ully wild, thoughtfully held, and deeply rooted in place.

property_title: Treehouse London: Handcrafted Calm Above Bustling Marylebone
property_intro: Perched on Langham Place, moments from Regent Street and the green sweep of Regent's Park, Treehouse London gathers reclaimed timber, vintage finds and handmade textiles into rooms that feel more like a friend's eyrie than a hotel. Climb to The Nest for rooftop views across the city's rooftops, or settle into Madera's Mexican-inspired plates. Low-waste practices and local makers underpin every detail, quietly and without fuss.

property_title: Soneva: Barefoot Luxury and Slow Wonder in the Maldives Atolls
property_intro: Scattered across the Maldives' quieter atolls, Soneva invites you to slip off your shoes and settle into a rhythm shaped by tides, stars and sand underfoot. Timber villas open to lagoons and jungle canopy, while astronomy nights, glass-blowing studios and open-air dining sit alongside ambitious coral restoration, waste-to-wealth recycling and community schooling. It is a place where indulgence and responsibility sit comfortably together, and where days unfold with unhurried, imaginative ease.

property_title: Shakti Himalaya: Unhurried Village Journeys in Ladakh & Sikkim
property_intro: High in the folds of Ladakh, Sikkim and Kumaon, Shakti Himalaya invites you to walk between villages, staying in restored stone houses and heritage homes tended by local families. Days unfold gently: mountain trails, monastery mornings, riverside picnics and dinners of home-grown produce. Interiors are quietly elegant rather than showy, and each journey channels income directly into the communities that host you, keeping traditions, craft and Himalayan hospitality thriving well beyond the guest's stay.

property_title:
Whitepod: Geodesic Alpine Living High Above the Rh

e Valley
property_intro:
Perched on the slopes above Les Cerniers in Switzerland's Valais, Whitepod scatters domed pods across alpine meadows, each framing views towards the Rh

e Valley and Dents du Midi. Interiors pair timber, wool and wood-burning stoves with quiet restraint, while days unfold through private ski slopes, snowshoeing, dog-sledding and sunrise hikes. Solar power, spring water and low-impact construction keep the mountain intact, and local producers shape menus rooted firmly in the surrounding valleys.

property_title: Eleven Deplar Farm: Wild Luxury in Iceland's Troll Peninsula
property_intro: Set in the Fljót Valley on Iceland's remote Troll Peninsula, Eleven Deplar Farm is a former sheep farm reborn as a retreat of quiet sophistication. Turf-roofed and low-slung against the mountains, it opens onto heli-skiing descents, salmon rivers, sea kayaking and geothermal waters beneath the northern lights. Interiors marry Nordic restraint with deep comfort, while local guides, farmers and fishermen shape each day. Just thirteen rooms, so the valley feels wonderfully, generously your own.

property_title: La Peschiera Hotel: Whitewashed Serenity on Puglia's Adriatic
property_intro: Set on a rocky ledge between Monopoli and Savelletri, La Peschiera Hotel takes its name from the 17th-century fish ponds still lapping at its terraces. Thirteen whitewashed suites open directly onto the Adriatic, where saltwater pools blur into the sea and breakfast arrives with the scent of wild fennel. Days unfold slowly here: swimming from the rocks, wandering olive groves tended for generations, or dining on the day's catch from local Pugliese fishermen.

property_title: Hotel De La Ville: Timeless Roman Views Above the Spanish Steps
property_intro: Perched at the top of the Spanish Steps, Hotel De La Ville looks out across Rome's rooftops from a hushed corner of Via Sistina. Inside, Grand Tour references meet contemporary Italian craftsmanship, with frescoed ceilings, antique maps and locally sourced marble. Days unfold with guided walks through Trinit	a dei Fiori's artisan workshops, spritzes on the Cielo terrace and gardens tended in partnership with local growers \u2014 an address that rewards slow, curious travellers.

property_title: Albergo Pietrasanta: Tuscan Marble, Art and Quiet Elegance
property_intro: Set within a restored seventeenth-century palazzo in the heart of Pietrasanta, this intimate retreat sits moments from sculptors' studios, marble workshops and the piazza where Michelangelo once sourced his stone. Frescoed ceilings, antique furnishings and a glass-roofed winter garden speak of careful restoration rather than reinvention. Days unfold between contemporary galleries, Versilia's beaches and the Apuan Alps, before returning to a courtyard scented with citrus. A place where Tuscan craftsmanship remains gloriously, tangibly alive.

property_title: La Roqqa: Coastal Elegance Above Tuscany's Porto Ercole Bay
property_intro: Perched on the hillside above Porto Ercole, La Roqqa looks out across the Tyrrhenian Sea from the wild Monte Argentario peninsula. Rooms are dressed in soft earth tones and Italian craftsmanship, while rooftop restaurant Scirocco serves seafood drawn from local waters. Days unfold between the saltwater pool, hidden coves reached by boat and walks through Maremma's maquis. Plastic-free by design, the hotel champions regional producers and quietly supports the fishing community that shapes its table.

property_title: Villa Franca Hotel: Where Positano Unfolds Below Your Terrace
property_intro: Perched on Positano's upper slopes, Villa Franca Hotel looks out across tumbling pastel houses to the Tyrrhenian Sea beyond. Interiors pair hand-painted Vietri tiles with cool whitewashed arches, while the rooftop pool and Li Galli restaurant frame the coastline at every hour. Days begin with lemon-scented breakfasts and unfold into boat trips to hidden coves or walks along the Path of the Gods. Family-run for generations, it keeps Amalfi craftsmanship and hospitality genuinely close.

property_title: Relais Roncolo 1888: Slow Luxury in Emilia's Vineyard Hillsides
property_intro: Set among the wooded hills above Quattro Castella, a short drive from Reggio Emilia, Relais Roncolo 1888 occupies a restored nineteenth-century estate where frescoed ceilings meet contemporary Italian craftsmanship. Days unfold slowly here: tastings of Lambrusco and aged Parmigiano, walks through the surrounding parkland, cookery lessons rooted in local tradition. The owners' careful restoration has revived original details and supported regional artisans and producers, giving guests a genuine sense of belonging to this quietly compelling corner of Emilia.

property_title: Viesca Toscana: A Restored Tuscan Hamlet in the Chianti Hills
property_intro: Tucked into the hills above the Arno valley, half an hour from Florence, Viesca Toscana gathers restored farmhouses and villas across an estate of olive groves, vineyards and wildflower meadows. Interiors pair honeyed stone and beamed ceilings with quietly contemporary comfort, while days unfold with cookery lessons, olive harvests, cycling through Chianti or long lunches beneath the pergola. The estate's own oil, wine and produce keep local traditions alive, and its craftspeople close at hand.

property_title: The Goethe Hotel: Refined Italian Living, Steeped in Story
property_intro: Named for the poet who wandered Italy in search of light and beauty, The Goethe Hotel invites you to do the same. Interiors pair restored period details with contemporary calm, while sunlit terraces and hushed courtyards encourage lingering. Days unfold through market walks, regional wines and conversations with local artisans whose crafts shape the rooms you sleep in. Family-run and quietly committed to its neighbourhood, it offers the rare pleasure of feeling genuinely at home.

property_title: Hotel Vilon: An Intimate Roman Retreat Beside Palazzo Borghese
property_intro: Tucked into a quiet corner of central Rome, Hotel Vilon occupies a wing of the 16th-century Palazzo Borghese, its eighteen rooms overlooking the family's private garden. Interiors layer hand-painted frescoes and bold contemporary fabrics, the work of Italian artisans whose crafts the hotel actively supports. Days might begin with espresso in the courtyard and end over Roman cooking at Adelaide, before a short stroll delivers you to the Spanish Steps and Via Margutta's galleries.

property_title: Cape of Senses: Lake Garda's Quiet Art of Slow Luxury
property_intro: Perched above Torri del Benaco on Lake Garda's eastern shore, Cape of Senses is an adults-only retreat where olive terraces tumble towards the water and Monte Baldo rises behind. Suites open to lake-facing balconies, the spa draws on local botanicals, and the kitchen leans on Veneto growers and lake-caught fish. Days unfold with cycling through vineyards, sailing at dusk, or simply watching the light shift across the water from a heated infinity pool.

property_title: Castle Elvira: A Restored Puglian Reverie Among Olive Groves
property_intro: Set amid ancient olive groves near San Cesario di Lecce, Castle Elvira is a 19th-century folly brought gently back to life. Frescoed ceilings, salvaged antiques and bold contemporary art fill rooms once left to silence, while long lunches unfold beneath the loggia. Wander Baroque Lecce, swim in the Adriatic, then return for Salentine cooking rooted in local farms. Every restoration decision honoured the building's history and the craftspeople of Puglia who made it possible.

property_title: Hotel Ai Reali: Venetian Grandeur in the Heart of Castello
property_intro: Set within a restored 15th-century palazzo in Venice's Castello district, Hotel Ai Reali sits moments from Rialto Bridge yet feels pleasingly removed from the crowds. Frescoed ceilings, Murano glass and Rubelli fabrics meet a serene spa beneath ancient brick vaults. Days might begin with a canal-side breakfast and end with cicchetti in a neighbourhood bacaro. Family-run and deeply local, the hotel champions Venetian artisans, keeping the city's craft traditions quietly alive.

property_title: Vista Palazzo: Lakeside Elegance in the Heart of Como, Italy
property_intro: Overlooking the shimmering waters of Lake Como, Vista Palazzo occupies a restored nineteenth-century residence in the centre of Como's old town. Eighteen rooms reveal hand-selected antiques, Italian marble and windows framing the Alps beyond. Dine on the rooftop as evening light settles over the water, unwind in the spa, or set out by private boat to villages few visitors reach. Family-run and deeply rooted here, the hotel champions Lombardy's artisans, growers and lakeside traditions with genuine care.

property_title: Shigira Resort: Where Miyako Island's Coral Seas Slow Time Down
property_intro:
On the southern shore of Miyako Island, where sugarcane fields give way to limestone cliffs and startlingly clear water, Shigira Resort unfolds across a headland of subtropical greenery. Villas and suites open to the Pacific, framed by Okinawan craft, quiet materials and hot springs drawn from deep beneath the island. Days drift between coral gardens, island-grown produce and local music, with reef care and Miyako's farming and artisan communities woven gently into every stay.

Come and see for yourself.

property_title: The Hotel Seiryu: Kyoto's Heritage Reawakened in Higashiyama
property_intro: Set on the slopes below Kiyomizu-dera, The Hotel Seiryu occupies a beloved 1933 schoolhouse, its arched windows and terrazzo staircases carefully preserved rather than replaced. Rooms look out over Higashiyama's tiled rooftops, while the rooftop bar frames the pagoda at dusk. Days here unfold slowly: tea with a local master, dawn walks along lantern-lit lanes, kaiseki shaped by Kyoto growers. A building saved by the neighbourhood that once filled it with children.

property_title: Sankara Hotel & Spa: Yakushima's Ancient Cedar Forest Retreat
property_intro: On the subtropical island of Yakushima, where thousand-year-old cedars rise from moss-cushioned slopes, Sankara sits quietly above the Pacific amid its own gardens and groves. Villa-style suites blend Japanese craft with island light, while the spa and kitchen draw on flying fish, citrus and mountain herbs from nearby producers. Guides lead guests into UNESCO-listed forests and along river gorges, and the hotel's conservation work helps protect the very wilderness that shapes every stay here.

property_title: The Namkhan: Riverside Retreat in the Hills of Luang Prabang
property_intro: Set above the Nam Khan river a short drive from Luang Prabang, The Namkhan unfolds across gardens, rice terraces and quiet stretches of forest. Rooms and villas are shaped from timber, stone and local craft, opening to water views and birdsong. Days might mean paddling the river, cycling to nearby villages, or learning from the farm that supplies the kitchen. Guest stays support local education and land regeneration, making the calm here quietly purposeful.

property_title: Velassaru: Barefoot Elegance on a South Male Atoll Island
property_intro: Just twenty-five minutes by speedboat from Male, Velassaru occupies its own slender island in the South Male Atoll, ringed by a house reef that rewards every early morning swim. Interiors lean towards clean lines, pale timber and quiet restraint, while dining moves from a sandbank supper to a bar suspended above the lagoon. Marine biologists guide coral restoration and turtle spotting, and the resort's reef work continues long after guests have dried off their fins.

property_title: Huvafen Fushi: Where Maldivian Reefs Meet Quiet Indulgence
property_intro: Set within its own lagoon in the North Mal\u00e9 Atoll, Huvafen Fushi is a place of considered calm, where forty-three bungalows and overwater villas open straight onto turquoise shallows. Descend to the world's first underwater spa, dine beneath the waterline, or drift over a house reef tended by resident marine biologists working on coral restoration. Barefoot days unfold slowly here \u2014 wine cellar tastings, sunrise yoga, dhoni voyages \u2014 with an intimacy that larger islands simply cannot offer.

property_title: Villa Park: Barefoot Island Living in the Heart of the Maldives
property_intro: Set within the South Ari Atoll, Villa Park occupies a lushly wooded island fringed by a house reef where whale sharks glide year-round. Timber-clad villas open directly onto sand or turquoise shallows, while dive guides, marine biologists and local chefs shape days here. Snorkel at dawn, join reef restoration efforts, or simply retreat beneath the palms. Conservation and island community life run quietly through every corner of the stay.

property_title: Villa Santa Cruz: Barefoot Coastal Living on Mexico's Pacific
property_intro: Set above a wide stretch of Pacific sand, Villa Santa Cruz invites you to slow down among whitewashed adobe walls, hand-carved wood and shaded terraces open to the sea breeze. Days unfold with horseback rides along the shore, estuary paddles among herons, and long lunches drawn from nearby farms and fishing boats. The villa works closely with its village neighbours, supporting local artisans and turtle protection efforts, so your stay leaves something meaningful behind.

property_title: The Bespoke: Considered Luxury in the Heart of Mexico's Coast
property_intro: Tucked between jungle and shoreline, The Bespoke offers a quietly considered take on Mexican hospitality. Interiors draw on local craftsmanship anging from hand-thrown ceramics to woven textiles while open-air spaces invite the breeze and birdsong indoors. Days might begin with a swim before breakfast, unfold through cooking sessions with regional producers, and close beneath a sky untouched by city light. The team works closely with neighbouring communities and conservation partners, ensuring your stay leaves something meaningful behind.

property_title: Wakax Hacienda: A Restored Yucatán Retreat with Its Own Cenote
property_intro: Tucked between Tulum's coast and the sleepy village of Sac Actun, Wakax Hacienda is a 19th-century henequen estate reborn as an intimate eight-suite hideaway. Colonial stonework meets Mayan craft, while a private cenote glimmers beneath the jungle canopy. Days unfold with birdsong breakfasts, guided swims and Yucatecan cooking rooted in the garden. Local families work and share their knowledge here, and much of the surrounding forest remains deliberately, beautifully untouched.

property_title: Villa Geba: Adriatic Serenity Above Montenegro's Coastline
property_intro: Set on a hillside above Montenegro's Adriatic shoreline, Villa Geba looks out across olive groves and glittering water towards Sveti Stefan. Stone terraces, natural textures and locally crafted furnishings give the house a quiet, grounded elegance, while the infinity pool invites long afternoons of doing wonderfully little. Days might begin with a swim in a hidden cove, continue with market produce prepared by a private chef, and end beneath a sky thick with stars.

property_title: Hotel Sahrai: Contemporary Calm Above the Ancient Medina of Fez
property_intro:
Perched on a hillside above Fez, Hotel Sahrai looks out across the rooftops and minarets of the world's oldest living medina. Behind its calm lines lies a dialogue between Moroccan craft and contemporary design: zellige tilework, cedar and cool marble shaped by local artisans. Days unfold between the black-tiled pool, a Givenchy spa and guided walks through tanneries and souks with Fassi hosts who know every hidden doorway.

Evenings belong to the terrace, mint tea in hand.

property_title: La Sultana Hotels: Moroccan Soul, from Medina to Ocean Shore
property_intro: Spanning Marrakech's hushed Kasbah quarter, the ramparts of Oualidia's lagoon and a coastal retreat beside the Atlantic, La Sultana Hotels invite you into a Morocco of carved cedar, tadelakt and courtyard calm. Days unfold with oyster tastings, hammam rituals, horse riding through eucalyptus groves or rooftop suppers above the rooftops. Each address is family-run, employing local artisans and craftspeople, and quietly supporting the lagoon's fragile birdlife and the neighbourhoods that surround it.

property_title: Yemaya Reefs: Barefoot Island Luxury on Nicaragua's Little Corn
property_intro: On the wild eastern edge of Little Corn Island, Yemaya Reefs looks out across the Caribbean from a bluff where the reef breaks white and the trade winds rarely rest. Thatched suites in pale timber and stone open to sea air, while days drift between diving, yoga, spa treatments and long lunches of just-landed fish. There are no cars here, only sand paths, island neighbours who shape the kitchen and the school the lodge helps sustain.

property_title: The Lindenberg: Refined Norwegian Calm Amid Fjord and Forest
property_intro: Set within Norway's quietly dramatic landscape, The Lindenberg invites you to slow down among forested slopes, still water and clear northern light. Interiors pair Scandinavian restraint with warm textures and locally made pieces, while kitchen menus follow the seasons, drawing on nearby farms and foragers. Days might mean lake swims, woodland walks or long conversations beside the fire. Thoughtful energy use and close ties with local craftspeople make each stay feel genuinely rooted here.

property_title: Carmo's Boutique Hotel: Quiet Luxury Above the Lima Valley
property_intro: Set on a hillside above Ponte de Lima, Portugal's oldest town, Carmo's Boutique Hotel is surrounded by vines, granite walls and eucalyptus-scented air. Its suites pair contemporary Portuguese design with hand-chosen art, while the spa, infinity pool and vinho verde tastings encourage unhurried days. The kitchen leans on the estate's gardens and neighbouring smallholders, and solar energy, rainwater harvesting and regional craftsmanship quietly shape the experience. Somewhere to breathe deeply, wander the Minho, and stay longer than planned.

property_title: Hotel Casa Palmela: Timeless Grace in the Wild Arrábida Hills
property_intro: Set within a former 17th-century manor on the edge of the Arrábida Natural Park, Hotel Casa Palmela looks out across vineyards, cork oaks and the shimmer of the Sado estuary. Interiors pair heirloom azulejos with contemporary calm, while days unfold through hillside walks, dolphin-watching in Setúbal Bay and tastings of Palmela's Castelão wines. Local producers supply the kitchen, and the estate's gardens are tended with care for native species and the surrounding wildlife.

property_title: Olive Boutique Hotel: Mediterranean Calm in San Juan's Condado
property_intro: Tucked into a leafy Condado street, moments from the Atlantic and San Juan's lagoon, Olive Boutique Hotel brings a distinctly Mediterranean sensibility to Puerto Rico. Just fifteen rooms, dressed in olive wood, linen and hand-laid tile, open onto a rooftop where sunset cocktails and Sardinian-inspired plates await. Days drift between beach walks, Old San Juan's cobblestones and long lunches sourced from island growers. Staff, many locally born, share their city with genuine pride and quiet, attentive grace.

property_title: Bequia Beach Hotel: Refined Caribbean Calm on Friendship Bay
property_intro: On the gentle southern shore of Bequia, where fishing boats still outnumber cars, Bequia Beach Hotel unfolds across the sands of Friendship Bay. Colonial-style suites and villas open to sea breezes, hand-picked antiques and locally crafted details. Days drift between snorkelling over turtle grass, sailing to neighbouring Grenadine islands and dining on the catch landed that morning. The hotel supports island turtle conservation and schools, so your stay quietly strengthens the community that makes Bequia so beguiling.

property_title: Principe Collection: Rainforest, Ocean and Island Renewal
property_intro: On Príncipe, a small volcanic island adrift in the Gulf of Guinea, the Principe Collection gathers a handful of distinct retreats across a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Stay in a restored plantation house among cacao groves, or wake to surf breaking below a jungle-fringed bay. Guides reveal endemic birds, hidden waterfalls and fishing villages, while much of what you eat is grown nearby. Local employment, schools and reforestation are woven into daily island life here.

property_title: The Cellars-Hohenort Hotel: A Garden Sanctuary in Constantia
property_intro: Set within nine acres of heritage gardens in Cape Town's Constantia Valley, The Cellars-Hohenort unfolds across two historic manor houses beneath the wooded slopes of Table Mountain. Ancient camphor trees, rose terraces and kitchen beds supply the celebrated kitchens, while rooms blend Cape antiques with generous comfort. Days might begin with a guided garden walk and end with wines from neighbouring estates. Local artisans, growers and conservation projects remain woven quietly into everyday hospitality here.

property_title: The Marine Hotel: Whale-Watching Elegance on Hermanus Cliffs
property_intro: Perched above the rocky shoreline of Walker Bay in Hermanus, The Marine Hotel invites you to watch southern right whales surface just beyond your window. Interiors blend antique finds with contemporary South African art, while two restaurants celebrate Overberg produce and Hemel-en-Aarde wines. Days unfold with cliff-path walks, fynbos-scented spa treatments and marine conservation talks led by local guides. It is a place where refined comfort meets genuine care for the coastline and its community.

property_title: The Plettenberg Hotel: Cliffside Grace on the Garden Route
property_intro: Perched on a rocky headland above Plettenberg Bay, this Garden Route landmark looks out across Formosa Cove towards the Tsitsikamma mountains, where southern right whales pass close to shore between June and November. Interiors blend Cape heritage with contemporary calm, while the terrace invites long lunches above the Indian Ocean. Days might involve forest walks, marine safaris or time at the spa, and the hotel's support for local conservation and community projects runs quietly throughout.

property_title: Seda Club Hotel: Granada's Refined Retreat Beneath the Alhambra
property_intro: Set within a restored 19th-century townhouse in the heart of Granada, Seda Club Hotel places you moments from the Cathedral, the Albaicín's winding lanes and the Alhambra rising above. Interiors pair original architectural details with contemporary Andalusian craft, while the rooftop terrace offers Sierra Nevada views at sunset. Expect attentive service, locally sourced cooking and thoughtful introductions to the city's artisans, from silk weavers to guitar makers, in a hotel that quietly champions its neighbourhood.

property_title: Nobu Hotel Ibiza Bay: Barefoot Elegance on Talamanca Bay Shore
property_intro: Set along the sheltered curve of Talamanca Bay, moments from Ibiza Town's Unesco-listed Dalt Vila, this whitewashed retreat pairs Japanese restraint with Balearic ease. Days drift between saltwater pools, Six Senses spa rituals and Nobu's celebrated cuisine, while sunset yoga and Posidonia seagrass conservation initiatives keep the island's fragile waters in focus. Family suites, an art programme and Ibizan makers' markets lend genuine local character to a stay that feels considered rather than showy.

property_title: CoolRooms Hotel: Refined Calm in the Heart of Historic Spain
property_intro: Set within a lovingly restored palace in one of Spain's most storied quarters, CoolRooms Hotel pairs original mouldings and marble with contemporary comfort. Mornings begin with Iberian coffee in a plant-filled courtyard; evenings drift towards the rooftop pool, where terracotta rooftops soften into dusk. Interiors honour local craftsmanship, while kitchens champion producers from nearby markets. Step outside and centuries of architecture, tapas counters and independent galleries await, all within an unhurried walk of your door.

property_title: The Principal Madrid Hotel: Refined Living Above Gran Vía
property_intro: Where Gran Vía meets the elegant Chueca and Salesas districts, The Principal Madrid Hotel occupies a restored 1917 building with quiet confidence. Interiors by Luis Galliussi pair warm woods and considered vintage pieces with generous light, while the rooftop terrace frames the city's tiled domes and Sierra beyond. Dine on seasonal Spanish produce, wander to the Prado on foot, then return for a cocktail as Madrid's evening rhythm unfolds below your window.

property_title: Dwarika's Sanctuary: Himalayan Serenity Above the Clouds
property_intro: High on a forested ridge above the Kathmandu Valley, Dwarika's Sanctuary looks out towards the Himalaya through pine and rhododendron. Rooms draw on Newari craftsmanship, with hand-carved timber and locally woven textiles, while days unfold through meditation with resident monks, Ayurvedic therapies and walks to hillside villages. Meals begin in the organic gardens. Guided by a family legacy of preserving Nepali artistry, the retreat trains local artisans and supports the communities that make this corner of the country quietly extraordinary.

property_title: Anantara Palais Hansen Vienna: Imperial Elegance Reimagined
property_intro: Set on Vienna's grand Ringstrasse, this restored 19th-century palace was designed by architect Theophil Hansen for the 1873 World Exhibition. Today its lofty salons and softly lit corridors blend Habsburg-era detail with contemporary calm, moments from the Danube Canal, the State Opera and the city's coffee houses. Expect thoughtful Austrian cuisine, a serene spa and a team who share Vienna's musical traditions and artisan makers with genuine pride. A stay that feels personal rather than performative.

property_title: Anantara Plaza Nice Hotel: Belle Époque Grace on the Riviera
property_intro: Set between the Jardin Albert 1er and the shimmering Baie des Anges, Anantara Plaza Nice Hotel occupies a restored Belle Époque landmark moments from Vieux Nice and the Promenade des Anglais. Interiors pair Riviera lightness with Mediterranean craftsmanship, while the rooftop pool and terrace frame the old town's terracotta rooftops. Days unfold with market walks, Provençal cookery sessions and Niçois flavours, guided by a team committed to local producers and the city's living heritage.

property_title: Anantara The Marker Dublin Hotel: Docklands Style, Skyline Views
property_intro: Rising in sharp geometric lines above Grand Canal Dock, Anantara The Marker Dublin Hotel brings a quietly theatrical edge to Ireland's capital. Its faceted facade echoes the Giant's Causeway, while inside, Irish craftsmanship meets Thai-inspired hospitality. Spend mornings in the infinity pool, afternoons following the hotel's own city walks, and evenings on the rooftop as the Dublin Mountains fade to violet. Local growers, artists and makers shape the menus, spa rituals and gallery-like interiors throughout.

property_title: Anantara Angkor Resort: Serene Siem Reap Sanctuary Awaits
property_intro: Moments from the temples of Angkor, this intimate retreat holds just 39 suites arranged around a courtyard pool, where frangipani shade and Khmer artistry set a calm, contemplative mood. Days might begin with sunrise at Angkor Wat, followed by a Cambodian cooking class, a spa ritual drawn from local traditions, or a guided cycle through rice fields and village lanes. Warm Khmer hospitality, thoughtful sourcing and support for community initiatives give every stay quiet purpose.

property_title: Anantara Jewel Bagh: Rajasthan's Gardens of Living Heritage
property_intro: Set within Rajasthan's storied landscape, Anantara Jewel Bagh draws on the craft of local artisans, from hand-carved sandstone to mirrorwork that catches the desert light. Days unfold slowly here: courtyard breakfasts, guided walks through nearby villages, conversations with craftspeople who keep centuries-old techniques alive. Water is conserved, ingredients are grown close by, and the surrounding wilderness is quietly protected. It is a place to linger, listen and leave feeling genuinely connected.

property_title: Raffles Jaipur: Where Rajasthani Grandeur Meets Quiet Luxury
property_intro: Set on the edge of Jaipur, with the Aravalli hills rising beyond, Raffles Jaipur unfolds like a private palace of hand-carved marble, frescoed ceilings and courtyards scented with jasmine. Just 45 suites invite unhurried days: astronomy on the rooftop, Ayurvedic rituals, or dawn drives to Amber Fort before the crowds. Artisans from nearby villages shaped much of the craftsmanship here, and the celebrated Raffles Butlers ensure every detail feels considered, personal and quietly generous.

property_name: Devasom Khao Lak Beach Resort & Villas
property_title: Devasom Khao Lak Beach Resort & Villas: Andaman Serenity
property_intro: Set along a quiet stretch of Andaman coastline north of Phuket, Devasom Khao Lak Beach Resort & Villas pairs breezy colonial-inspired architecture with the rhythm of village life. Days unfold between private pools, sea-facing verandas and casuarina-shaded sands, with Similan diving, mangrove paddling and turtle conservation projects close at hand. Kitchens favour Phang Nga growers and day-boat catches, while interiors nod to southern Thai craft. An unhurried retreat for those who prefer discovery over spectacle.

property_title: Aarunya Nature Resort & Spa: Kandy's Hillside Sanctuary
property_intro: Perched on a forested ridge above Kandy, Aarunya Nature Resort & Spa looks out across terraced valleys where mist gathers at dawn and birdsong carries far. Villas built from local stone and timber follow the contours of the hillside, each opening to wide views. Days unfold with Ayurvedic treatments, guided walks to hidden waterfalls and dinners drawn from village growers, while the resort's rewilding of native trees quietly restores the surrounding slopes for generations ahead.

property_title: SAii Laguna Phuket: Barefoot Days on Bang Tao's Golden Sands
property_intro: Set along the eight-kilometre sweep of Bang Tao Beach, SAii Laguna Phuket brings a playful, design-led spirit to Thailand's west coast. Rooms open onto lagoons and gardens, while the beachfront invites long, unhurried afternoons. Days might begin with Muay Thai on the sand and end with Andaman sunsets over cocktails. Within the wider Laguna Phuket estate, once a reclaimed tin mine, restored wetlands and thriving mangroves tell a quietly remarkable story of regeneration.

property_title: Santiburi Koh Samui Resort: Tropical Gardens by the Gulf Sea
property_intro: Set along the quiet northern shore of Mae Nam Beach, Santiburi Koh Samui Resort unfolds across 23 acres of lush tropical gardens, coconut groves and lotus ponds. Thai-style villas draw on traditional teak craftsmanship, while the private stretch of sand faces the calm Gulf waters. Days might involve cookery lessons using herbs from the resort's own garden, coral restoration outings, or simply the pleasure of a slow, unhurried breakfast beneath the palms.

property_title: Capella Shanghai: Heritage Lanes, Quiet Luxury in Jian Ye Li
property_intro: Tucked into the leafy former French Concession, Capella Shanghai occupies Jian Ye Li, a restored 1930s shikumen quarter whose brick lanes once hummed with neighbourhood life. Villas open onto private courtyards, where Jean-Michel Gathy's interiors pair Shanghainese craft with contemporary calm. Your personal Culturist uncovers hidden ateliers, tailors and teahouses beyond the gates, while the spa, lantern-lit gardens and Le Comptoir de Pierre Gagnaire invite unhurried evenings. Heritage here feels lived-in rather than merely preserved.

property_title: The Okura Tokyo: Timeless Japanese Grace in the Heart of the City
property_intro: Set on a quiet rise in Toranomon, moments from the embassies and gardens of central Tokyo, The Okura Tokyo carries forward a legacy first shaped in 1962. Its celebrated lobby lanterns, lacquerwork and plum-blossom motifs have been faithfully reimagined, while a rooftop garden and museum invite unhurried afternoons. Expect kaiseki crafted from seasonal produce, tea ceremony in a hillside pavilion, and service passed down through generations of Japanese hospitality.

property_title: Kahanda Kanda: Tea-Garden Serenity Above Sri Lanka's South
property_intro: Set on a hillside tea estate above Koggala Lake, Kahanda Kanda pairs colonial-era calm with contemporary Sri Lankan design across a handful of individually styled suites. Days unfold slowly here: swimming beside the plantation, learning to temper spices with the kitchen team, or walking the rows where tea is still picked by hand. Galle Fort and the southern beaches lie half an hour away, yet few guests hurry to leave.

property_title: Conrad Osaka: Elevated Calm Above the City's Neon Streets
property_intro: Perched on the upper floors of a glass tower in Nakanoshima, Conrad Osaka looks out across rivers, rooftops and the distant Ikoma mountains. Interiors by Kengo Kuma's contemporaries pair washi textures with sculptural glass, while Atmos Dining serves Kansai produce sourced from nearby markets. Wander to Nakanoshima's museums and willow-lined canals, then return for a soak overlooking the skyline. Staff share their own neighbourhood haunts, and community craft partnerships bring local artistry into every corner.

property_title: Banyan Tree AlUla: Desert Nights Among Ancient Sandstone Cliffs
property_intro: Tucked into the Ashar Valley, where sandstone formations rise like weathered sculpture, Banyan Tree AlUla invites you to slow down beneath a canopy of stars. Tented villas echo Bedouin traditions with contemporary restraint, each opening onto private terraces and pools. Days unfold with guided walks through Hegra's Nabataean tombs, stargazing with local astronomers, or Arabian-inspired treatments at the spa. The resort works closely with AlUla's communities, championing regional craft, cuisine and the valley's careful stewardship.

property_title: Torre de Palma: Vineyard Living in Portugal's Alentejo Plains
property_intro: Set among vines, olive groves and cork oaks in the Alentejo, Torre de Palma occupies a farmhouse whose roots reach back to Roman times. Whitewashed walls, contemporary art and quiet courtyards frame days spent tasting the estate's own wines, baking bread in the old oven or riding Lusitano horses across open country. Local artisans and producers shape much of what you eat and see here, making each stay feel genuinely rooted in its landscape.

property_title: Timber Cove Resort: Wild Sonoma Coast Retreat in California
property_intro: Perched above the churning Pacific on Sonoma's untamed coastline, Timber Cove Resort pairs mid-century timber architecture with the drama of cypress, cliff and fog. Rooms open to ocean or redwood views, fires crackle in the lodge, and Benny Bufano's soaring peace obelisk presides over the headland. Days unfold with tidepooling, kayaking the Russian River and tastings from nearby coastal vineyards, while local makers and conservation partners shape a stay rooted firmly in this remarkable stretch of California.

property_title: Phāea Cretan Malia: Barefoot Luxury on Crete's Northern Shore
property_intro: On Crete's northern coast, where the Malia plain meets the Aegean, Phāea Cretan Malia unfolds across gardens of olive, citrus and native herbs. Rooms open to sea breezes and quiet courtyards, while island-grown menus draw on Cretan farms and fishing boats nearby. Wander to Minoan ruins, swim in warm shallows, or join a foraging walk with local growers. Renewable energy, water stewardship and long-standing village partnerships shape a stay that feels genuinely rooted here.

property_title: Parīlio Hotel: Sunlit Cycladic Serenity in the Heart of Paros
property_intro: Set among olive groves and dry-stone walls a short stroll from Naoussa's fishing harbour, Parīlio is a study in Cycladic restraint: local marble, pale plaster and shaded courtyards that invite slowness. Days drift between the long pool, a Greek-herb spa ritual and dinners drawn from Parian producers and the hotel's own garden. Wander to hidden coves, learn pottery from island artisans, or simply watch the Aegean light shift across the whitewashed terraces.

property_title: Istoria Hotel: Where Santorini's Black Sands Tell Their Stories
property_intro: On the volcanic shoreline of Perivolos, Istoria sits quietly between black sand and the Aegean, a world away from Santorini's crowded caldera paths. Just nine rooms and suites draw on Cycladic craft, weathered timber and antique finds, each one shaped by island history rather than trend. Days unfold with barefoot breakfasts, boat trips to hidden coves and Greek cooking rooted in local growers. It is intimate, unhurried and quietly generous to the community around it.

property_title: XELA: A Barefoot Sanctuary Where Jungle Meets Mexico's Coast
property_intro: Tucked between dense coastal jungle and the warm swell of the Pacific, XELA invites you to slow down entirely. Suites are shaped from lime plaster, native hardwoods and handwoven textiles by Mexican artisans, framing sea breezes rather than shutting them out. Days unfold with sunrise swims, mezcal tastings and guided walks with local naturalists tracking nesting turtles. Rainwater harvesting, solar power and partnerships with nearby villages keep this retreat quietly, genuinely rooted in its place.

property_title: Vila Foz Hotel & Spa: Atlantic Elegance on Porto's Shoreline
property_intro: Where the Douro meets the Atlantic, this restored 19th-century manor house sits along Porto's Foz seafront, moments from tiled promenades and salt-sprayed rocks. Interiors pair original stonework with contemporary craftsmanship, while the spa draws on marine rituals and the ocean's rhythm just beyond the windows. Dine on Michelin-recognised Portuguese cooking rooted in regional producers, then wander into the city's cellars and galleries. A quietly confident address for those who prefer character over convention.

property_title: Mason, Thailand: Considered Living Amid Quiet Coastal Beauty
property_intro: Set within Thailand's gentle rhythms of sea, forest and village life, Mason invites you to slow down and pay attention. Interiors of pale timber, raw stone and handwoven textiles frame views that shift with the light. Days might begin with a market walk beside local growers, drift into open-water swims, and close over dishes drawn from nearby farms. Partnerships with surrounding communities and careful stewardship of the shoreline shape every detail, making each stay quietly meaningful.

property_title: Casa de La Flora: Architectural Calm on Khao Lak's Shoreline
property_intro: Set along the quiet sands of Bang Sak Beach in Khao Lak, Casa de La Flora is a study in sculptural simplicity, where cube-like villas open onto private pools and the Andaman Sea beyond. Days drift between mangrove kayaking, Similan Islands diving and slow mornings in Takua Pa's old town. Thoughtful sourcing, reef-friendly practices and close ties with local artisans give this refined retreat a genuine sense of place and purpose.

property_title: The Surin Phuket: Barefoot Luxury on Pansea Beach's Shores
property_intro: Tucked into a private cove on Phuket's west coast, The Surin scatters its thatched cottages across a wooded hillside above Pansea Beach, where sand meets a black-tiled lagoon pool. Days unfold slowly here: reef snorkelling, Thai cookery lessons, treatments scented with local herbs. The design honours traditional craftsmanship, while beach clean-ups, coral care and support for nearby communities reflect a quieter commitment. Wake to birdsong, breakfast on your terrace, and let the Andaman set the pace.

property_title: The Naka Phuket: Cliffside Serenity Above the Andaman Sea
property_intro: Carved into a forested hillside above Kamala Bay, The Naka Phuket feels pleasingly removed from the island's busier shores. Angular villas of stone, timber and glass step down the slope, each with a private pool framing the Andaman Sea and its evening light. Days unfold slowly here: barefoot breakfasts, treatments scented with local botanicals, dinners overlooking the water. Native planting shelters resident hornbills and monitor lizards, while kitchens draw on Phuket's growers and small fishing communities.

property_title: Witt Hotels: Istanbul Living, Reimagined in Cihangir Style
property_intro: Tucked into Cihangir, one of Istanbul's most creative neighbourhoods, Witt Hotels offers spacious suites where clean lines, warm wood and Bosphorus light meet. Step outside to antique dealers, independent coffee roasters and Turkish bakeries, with Galata and Karak\u00f6y a gentle stroll downhill. Interiors celebrate local designers and craftspeople, while the kitchen leans on Aegean producers and seasonal markets. It is a place to settle in slowly, live like a resident, and discover the city through its own rhythms.

property_title: Form Hotel: Design-Led Living in the Heart of Old Dubai
property_intro: Set in Al Jaddaf, moments from Dubai Creek and the city's historic quarters, Form Hotel brings a considered, design-forward sensibility to a neighbourhood in gentle transformation. Concrete, timber and light shape interiors that feel calm rather than showy, while the rooftop pool looks out across the skyline. Independent coffee, curated art and a knowledgeable team encourage guests to explore the abras, souks and galleries nearby, discovering a Dubai shaped by craft and community.

property_title: El Llorenç: Old Town Soul, Sea Views and Rooftop Sunsets in Palma
property_intro: Tucked into Palma's old quarter, moments from the cathedral and the shimmer of the bay, El Llorenç blends Mallorcan craft with contemporary calm. Handmade tiles, local stone and island artistry set the mood, while the rooftop pool invites long, unhurried afternoons above the rooftops. Sample Balearic produce from nearby growers, wander into artisan workshops with the concierge, or simply linger over sunset. A city retreat that champions its makers and rewards those who arrive curious.

property_title: Cugó Gran Macina: Harbourside Heritage in Malta's Senglea
property_intro: Set within a restored 16th-century crane house on the tip of Senglea, Cugó Gran Macina looks across Grand Harbour to Valletta's honeyed bastions. Fortress walls and vaulted stone meet contemporary Maltese craftsmanship, with suites that open onto water on three sides. Days unfold slowly here: rooftop swims, boat trips between the Three Cities, dinners drawn from island growers and fishermen. The restoration itself has helped revive a neighbourhood long overlooked, giving guests genuine local company.

property_title: Hotel Galery69: Artful Escapes in Poland's Wooded Foothills
property_intro: Set among the wooded foothills of southern Poland, Hotel Galery69 blends contemporary Polish design with a genuine love of local craft. Rooms are hung with works by regional artists, while the kitchen draws on nearby farms and orchards for dishes rooted in seasonal tradition. Days unfold with forest walks, thermal spa rituals and slow conversations over Silesian wine. It's a place where creativity, comfort and community quietly meet, inviting you to linger longer than planned.

property_title: Altis Grand Hotel: Lisbon's Timeless Address Above the City
property_intro: Set moments from Avenida da Liberdade, the Altis Grand Hotel occupies a quietly confident corner of Lisbon, where boulevards lined with jacaranda give way to the tiled lanes of Bairro Alto. Interiors pair Portuguese artistry with mid-century calm, while the rooftop pool and terrace frame the Tejo and the castle beyond. Dine on Michelin-recognised cooking rooted in local producers, unwind in the spa, then step out to galleries, fado houses and markets just beyond the door.

property_title: The Warehouse Hotel: Riverside Heritage Reimagined in Singapore
property_intro: Set along the Singapore River in Robertson Quay, The Warehouse Hotel occupies a trio of 1895 godowns once thick with spice trade, secret societies and river commerce. Today, 37 rooms rise beneath soaring trusses, where industrial pulleys and local craftsmanship meet quiet comfort. Sip a heritage-inspired cocktail at the lobby bar, swim in the cantilevered pool above the water, or wander Tiong Bahru's lanes. A conservation landmark given fresh, thoughtful purpose.

property_title: Schgaguler Hotel: Understated Alpine Elegance in the Dolomites
property_intro: In the village of Castelrotto, where church bells drift across meadows and the Dolomites rise sharply beyond, the Schgaguler Hotel has been shaped by four generations of one South Tyrolean family. Pale stone, oiled oak and vast windows frame the peaks with quiet restraint, while the Alpe di Siusi begins a short walk away. Days unfold with mountain hikes, sauna rituals and produce from nearby farms, served with genuine local warmth.

property_title: Hotel Giardino Mountain: Alpine Calm Above St Moritz's Valley
property_intro: Set in Champfèr, moments from St Moritz, Hotel Giardino Mountain occupies a quiet fold of the Engadin where larch forests meet glacial light. Interiors pair Alpine timber with relaxed Italian elegance, while the kitchens champion regional growers and cheesemakers. Days unfold on cross-country trails, in mountain-facing spa pools, or beside the fire with a slice of Engadin nut tart. Family-run and firmly rooted in its valley, it supports local artisans and welcomes you like an old friend.

property_title: Nira Alpina: Alpine Serenity Above the Engadin's Silver Lakes
property_intro: Perched above Silvaplana in Switzerland's Engadin valley, Nira Alpina sits at the foot of Corvatsch, with a private lift bridging your room and the cable car station. Larch-lined interiors, sheepskin throws and windows framing glacial lakes set a quietly confident mood. Days might mean kite-surfing on the wind-swept water, hiking to mountain huts, or lingering over Alpine dishes made with produce from valley farmers, before the rooftop bar turns golden at sunset.

property_title: Ametis Villa Bali: Rice-Field Serenity Moments from Canggu
property_intro: Set among working rice terraces on the fringes of Canggu, Ametis Villa offers a quieter counterpoint to Bali's coastal buzz. Just fifteen minutes from the surf at Berawa, its pool suites open onto green horizons, with tropical modernist architecture softened by local stone and timber. Days unfold with sunrise yoga, Balinese healing rituals and Indonesian cooking lessons led by neighbouring villagers. Staff drawn from the surrounding community share the customs and rhythms that shape this pocket of the island.

property_title: Azumi Setoda: Island Ryokan Living on Japan's Seto Inland Sea
property_intro: On the citrus-scented island of Ikuchijima, a 140-year-old merchant's residence has been carefully reborn as a 22-room ryokan. Cedar-scented baths, tatami calm and locally grown lemons set the rhythm here, while cycling routes, harbour walks and the artisan workshops of Setoda are moments from the gate. Craftspeople from across Hiroshima shaped the interiors, and the neighbouring public bathhouse remains open to residents — a quiet act of stewardship that keeps island life at the heart of every stay.

property_title: Hotel The Mitsui: Kyoto Heritage Beside Nijo Castle Walls
property_intro: Set across from Nijo Castle in the heart of Kyoto, Hotel The Mitsui occupies land held by the Mitsui family for more than three centuries. Its restored Kajiimiya gate opens onto quiet courtyards, a thermal spring drawn from beneath the city, and rooms where contemporary calm meets craftsmanship from local artisans. Wander the garden at dusk, take tea in the pavilion, then step out to temples, machiya lanes and markets moments away.

property_title: Janu Tokyo: Connected Living Amid the Azabudai Hills Gardens
property_intro: Set within Azabudai Hills, where lawns and orchards soften the city's edges, Janu Tokyo offers a gentler interpretation of urban luxury. Rooms open onto views of Tokyo Tower, while a vast wellness floor, thermal baths and eight dining rooms invite unhurried days. The name means 'soul' in Sanskrit, and the spirit shows: staff greet you like a neighbour, gardeners tend native planting, and chefs draw on small Japanese producers. Curiosity, not formality, guides every stay.

property_title: Six Senses Con Dao: Barefoot Seclusion on Vietnam's Wild Isles
property_intro: Set along a sweep of sand on Vietnam's remote Con Dao archipelago, this hideaway faces the East Sea with forested peaks rising behind. Timber villas, cooled by sea breezes, open to private pools and horizons uninterrupted by crowds. Days unfold with dawn swims, freshly landed seafood and snorkelling above coral gardens. The resort's turtle hatchery and marine conservation work, alongside island community partnerships, make each stay quietly meaningful as well as gloriously restorative.

property_title: Six Senses Samui: Barefoot Luxury on Thailand's Northern Cape
property_intro: Set on a headland at Koh Samui's northern tip, Six Senses Samui looks out across the Gulf of Thailand towards Koh Phangan. Sixty-six villas step down the hillside, timber-clad and open to the breeze, each with its own pool and sweeping sea views. Days unfold with hilltop yoga, Thai cookery lessons and treatments drawing on the resort's own organic garden. A long-standing commitment to plastic-free operations and local schooling projects underpins every stay.

property_title: Six Senses Yao Noi: Barefoot Luxury Amid Phang Nga's Karsts
property_intro: Set on a hillside overlooking the limestone islands of Phang Nga Bay, Six Senses Yao Noi occupies a quiet corner of Koh Yao Noi, where rubber plantations and fishing villages still set the daily rhythm. Pool villas built from local timber open to sweeping sea views, while the organic garden supplies the kitchens. Sail a traditional long-tail at dawn, learn from island cooks, or join reef restoration work with the resident marine biologist.

property_name: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
property_title: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort: Barefoot Elegance on Motu Ome'e
property_intro: Set on its own islet within Bora Bora's luminous lagoon, this resort faces Mount Otemanu across water so clear the coral seems close enough to touch. Villas open onto private gardens and lagoonarium shallows, where marine biologists nurture reef fish and giant clams. Days drift between Polynesian spa rituals, outrigger paddles and dinners drawing on island growers. Timber, thatch and local craftsmanship shape interiors that feel unhurried, generous and quietly connected to place.

property_title: Minos Beach Art Hotel: Where Cretan Shores Meet Sculpture
property_intro: On a private peninsula near Agios Nikolaos, Minos Beach Art Hotel unfolds across gardens of olive, bougainvillea and contemporary sculpture, with the Gulf of Mirabello lapping at its edges. Whitewashed bungalows open directly onto the water, while Greek artists' installations turn a morning stroll into a gallery visit. Days drift between sea-fresh Cretan cooking, seaweed-strewn coves and conversations with local makers. It is Crete at its most quietly cultured, unhurried and genuinely rooted in place.

property_title: Boca de Agua: A Treetop Sanctuary in Holbox's Mangrove Wilds
property_intro: On the sandy edges of Isla Holbox, Boca de Agua raises its timber villas high among the mangroves, leaving the forest floor undisturbed. Conceived by architect Frida Escobedo, each suite frames a shifting view of canopy, lagoon and sky. Days unfold with cenote swims, whale shark encounters in season and long, slow lunches drawn from Yucatecan waters. Solar power, rainwater harvesting and island-led hospitality make this a stay that quietly gives back.

property_title: 21 Carpenter: Where Old Singapore Meets Quietly Modern Luxury
property_intro: Tucked along Carpenter Street, moments from the Singapore River and Chinatown's shophouse lanes, 21 Carpenter occupies a trio of 1930s remittance houses once used to send letters and money home to China. WOHA's sculptural extension crowns the conserved facades, its perforated screens filtering light into 48 calm, timber-warmed rooms. Linger over Peranakan-influenced plates at Kee's, swim beneath the skyline, and let handwritten fragments of the building's past shape a stay rich in quiet meaning.

property_title: The Nautilus Maldives: Barefoot Freedom on Baa Atoll's Shores
property_intro: Set within the UNESCO Biosphere Reserve of Baa Atoll, The Nautilus is an island of just 26 beach and ocean houses, where there are no schedules and no menus \u2014 only what you feel like, whenever you feel like it. Days unfold with manta encounters in Hanifaru Bay, reef restoration alongside resident marine biologists, and dinners arranged on a sandbank at your whim. Design nods to Maldivian craft, while the house reef flourishes under careful watch.

property_title: Hanging Gardens of Bali: Rainforest Villas Above the Ayung River
property_intro: Suspended above the Ayung River gorge near Ubud, this cluster of timber villas is reached by private funicular through dense Balinese jungle. Each pool seems to spill into the canopy, while temple ruins and rice terraces lie within walking distance. Days unfold with river-valley treks, Balinese healing rituals and dining in a restored 19th-century royal residence. The resort supports village artisans, local schooling and reforestation, so your stay quietly sustains the valley that surrounds it.

property_title: Amanoi: Cliffside Serenity in Vietnam's Nui Chua National Park
property_intro: Set where granite peaks tumble into the East Sea, Amanoi occupies a rare pocket of Nui Chua National Park, overlooking the turquoise curve of Vinh Hy Bay. Pavilions and villas echo Vietnamese temple architecture, framed by dry forest where langurs and hornbills still roam. Days unfold with cliff-top yoga, sailing on traditional junks, or forest walks with conservationists protecting nesting turtles. It is a place of considered calm, where luxury feels quietly earned and deeply rooted in place.

property_title: Ananda in the Himalayas: Ancient Wisdom Above the Ganges
property_intro: Set within a former maharaja's palace estate above Rishikesh, Ananda in the Himalayas looks out across the Ganges valley to forested foothills and distant snow peaks. Here, Ayurveda, yoga and Vedanta are practised with genuine rigour, guided by resident physicians who tailor every treatment, meal and meditation to you. Colonial-era architecture meets sal forest calm, while the spa's herbs come from surrounding gardens. Local artisans, musicians and Himalayan communities remain woven into daily life.

property_title: The Retreat Hotel: Lava-Framed Luxury Beside the Blue Lagoon
property_intro: Set into an 800-year-old lava flow on Iceland's Reykjanes peninsula, The Retreat Hotel opens directly onto the mineral-rich waters of the Blue Lagoon. Suites are carved into the volcanic landscape, where moss, basalt and shifting northern light shape every view. Days unfold between the subterranean spa, guided lava walks and Moss Restaurant's Icelandic tasting menus. Geothermal energy powers the estate, while research into the lagoon's algae continues quietly alongside your stay.

property_title: Euphoria Retreat: Mystras Wellbeing Amid Byzantine Hillsides
property_intro: Set on the forested slopes of Mount Taygetos, beneath the Byzantine ruins of Mystras, Euphoria Retreat blends Hellenic and Chinese healing traditions within a restored 19th-century mansion and a sphere-shaped pool carved into the rock. Days unfold with tailored wellbeing programmes, watsu, guided walks through Sparta's olive groves and produce grown nearby. Family-owned and deeply rooted in the Peloponnese, it employs local villagers and supports regional artisans ,, and begin again.

property_title: Paradero Todos Santos: Desert Luxury on Baja's Wild Coast
property_intro: Set among organic farmland on the edge of Baja California Sur's desert, Paradero Todos Santos sits between the Sierra de la Laguna mountains and the Pacific. Raw concrete architecture frames cactus gardens and open sky, while forty-odd suites offer rooftop hammocks and outdoor showers. Days unfold through guided canyon hikes, foraging with local farmers, surf lessons and mezcal tastings. Produce arrives from neighbouring ranches, and the surrounding land is cultivated with genuine care for the region's fragile ecology.

property_title: Amangiri: Desert Stillness Among Utah's Ancient Sandstone
property_intro: Set within 600 acres of protected desert on the edge of Lake Powell, Amangiri rises quietly from the Utah landscape, its concrete and glass forms shaped around a sandstone escarpment millions of years in the making. Suites open to slot canyons and mesas; days unfold with Navajo-guided walks, via ferrata climbs and treatments drawing on Native healing traditions. Local artisans and neighbouring communities remain woven into daily life here, lending the stay unusual depth and quiet meaning.

property_title: Borgo Egnazia: Puglia's Whitewashed Village by the Adriatic
property_intro: Rising from the olive groves of Puglia's Itria Valley, Borgo Egnazia is built in the image of a traditional whitewashed village, complete with courtyards, hidden lanes and tufo stone quarried nearby. Days unfold between the Adriatic shore, kitchen tables laden with local produce, and treatments drawn from Pugliese ritual. Master craftspeople, regional farmers and centuries-old techniques shape every corner, making a stay here feel less like arrival and more like belonging.

property_title: Six Senses Vana: Himalayan Foothills Retreat in Dehradun
property_intro: Set within a sal forest on the edge of Dehradun, Six Senses Vana looks towards the Himalayan foothills with quiet purpose. This is a place of considered stillness: Ayurveda, Tibetan healing and yoga practised over multi-night programmes, guided by physicians who tailor every detail. Interiors favour local stone, wood and daylight, while kitchens serve sattvic dishes grown nearby. Guests wear kurtas, phones stay away, and days unfold at the pace of the forest.

property_title: Château de La Messardière: Hilltop Serenity Above Saint-Tropez
property_intro: Perched on the highest hill above Saint-Tropez, Château de La Messardière surveys vineyards, umbrella pines and the shimmering Bay of Pampelonne from within its own ten-hectare estate. The 19th-century château blends Provençal craftsmanship with contemporary calm, while gardens shelter beehives, olive groves and kitchen plots that supply the restaurants. Spend mornings in the Valmont spa, afternoons on the coastal paths, evenings watching the light soften over the rooftops — village life close by, yet wonderfully removed.

property_title: Suitree Hotel: Rainforest Serenity on Costa Rica's Pacific Coast
property_intro: Tucked into the green hills above Uvita, Suitree Hotel looks out across the treetops to the Pacific, where whales pass offshore and Marino Ballena National Park unfolds below. Adults-only suites open to the canopy, shaped by natural timber, stone and generous light. Days drift between waterfall walks, birdsong at breakfast and unhurried afternoons by the pool. Locally sourced kitchens, reforested grounds and long-standing ties with nearby communities give the stay real substance.

property_title: The Kumaon: Himalayan Horizons Above the Village of Kasar Devi
property_intro: Perched on a forested ridge in Uttarakhand, The Kumaon frames a 300-kilometre sweep of Himalayan peaks from just ten rooms. Built with local stone, slate and hand-woven ringal bamboo by regional artisans, its award-winning architecture sits lightly on the hillside. Days unfold with guided walks to hidden temples, foraging with village cooks, and dinners drawn from nearby farms. Evenings belong to the stars, the deodar scent, and conversations that linger long past dessert.

property_title: Ilora Retreats: Intimate Luxury on the Maasai Mara's Edge
property_intro: Overlooking the plains of the Maasai Mara, Ilora Retreats offers just a handful of tented suites, each with a private plunge pool and uninterrupted views across wildlife-rich grassland. Days unfold with unhurried game drives, walks alongside Maasai guides and dinners under a vast African sky. Interiors blend handcrafted Kenyan artistry with quiet comfort, while the retreat's partnerships with neighbouring communities and conservancies ensure your stay supports the land and people who make this corner of Kenya extraordinary.

property_title: Q92 Noto Hotel: Baroque Sicily, Reimagined with Quiet Grace
property_intro: Tucked within Noto's honey-hued streets, Q92 Noto Hotel occupies a restored townhouse where Sicilian Baroque detail meets pared-back contemporary calm. Days begin with almond granita on the terrace, drift through Val di Noto's stone lanes and end with wine from nearby Nero d'Avola vineyards. Local artisans shaped much of the interiors, and the kitchen draws on growers from the surrounding countryside. Beyond the door: Vendicari's wetlands, Marzamemi's fishing harbour and the slow rhythm of Sicily's south-east.

property_title: L'Apogée Courchevel: Alpine Elegance at the Summit of 1850
property_intro: Perched at the top of Jardin Alpin, L'Apogée Courchevel opens directly onto the slopes of the Trois Vallées, with ski-in, ski-out ease and views across snow-laden pines. Interiors by India Mahdavi and Joseph Dirand balance chalet warmth with playful sophistication, while the spa, ice rink and family ski school invite unhurried days. Chefs draw on Savoyard producers and mountain cheesemakers, and evenings settle into the kind of conviviality that keeps guests returning each winter.

property_title: The Chedi Andermatt: Where Alpine Peaks Meet Eastern Serenity
property_intro: Tucked into the Ursern Valley, high in the Swiss Alps, The Chedi Andermatt reimagines mountain living through an Asian lens u2013 dark timber, soft lantern light and 200 crackling fireplaces. Days here might begin with fresh powder on the Gemsstock and end in the glass-roofed hydrothermal spa, or over sushi and raclette crafted from Alpine cheeses aged on site. Family-run producers supply the kitchens, while the hotel's quiet commitment to the valley keeps local traditions thriving.

property_title: Forestis: Dolomite Stillness High Above Brixen's Valley Floor
property_intro: Perched at 1,800 metres on the Plose plateau above Brixen, Forestis looks out across South Tyrol's spruce forests to the Dolomites beyond. Four slender towers of local timber frame the light, while treatments draw on the mountain's own elements: pine, stone, water and air. Days unfold with forest walks, silent snowshoe trails and dishes shaped by nearby farms. Solar-heated, spring-fed and quietly self-sufficient, it invites you to breathe more slowly.

property_title: Aman Le Mélézin: Alpine Serenity on Courchevel's Slopes
property_intro: Tucked beside the Bellecôte piste in Courchevel 1850, Aman Le Mélézin offers something rare in the French Alps: quiet. Larch-lined interiors and softly lit spaces frame views across the Trois Vallées, while ski butlers see to boots and bindings before you glide directly from the door. Days unfold with off-piste guiding, forest walks and long afternoons in the pool. Savoyard produce shapes the menus, and local artisans lend their craft to every considered detail.

property_title: Ultima Hotel Gstaad: Alpine Seclusion in the Saanenland Hills
property_intro: Tucked into the meadows above Gstaad, Ultima Hotel Gstaad offers just a handful of chalet residences, each with its own spa, pool and uninterrupted view across the Saanenland. Interiors pair Alpine timber with contemporary calm, while private chefs, ski guides and mountain picnics shape days entirely around you. Local artisans and producers inform much of what you'll taste and touch here, grounding the experience in the valley's traditions rather than simply borrowing its scenery.

property_title: Six Senses Crans-Montana: Alpine Calm Above the Rhone Valley
property_intro: Perched on a sunlit plateau above the Rhone Valley, Six Senses Crans-Montana looks across to the Matterhorn and Mont Blanc, with ski slopes and larch forests at the doorstep. Interiors blend pale Swiss timber with locally woven textiles, while the vast spa draws on Alpine botanicals and Nordic bathing rituals. Days might mean ski-touring at dawn, foraging with a local guide, or lingering over cheeses from valley farms. Sustainability runs quietly through every detail here.

property_title: Lefay Resort & Spa Dolomites: Alpine Calm Above Pinzolo
property_intro: Perched above Pinzolo in Trentino's Val Rendena, Lefay Resort & Spa Dolomites looks out across the Brenta peaks and the forests of Adamello Brenta Nature Park. Larch, stone and glass frame interiors that feel more mountain retreat than grand hotel, while the spa blends Classical Chinese medicine with Alpine ritual. Days might mean forest walks, ski touring or slow afternoons by the salt lake. The near-zero-emissions design quietly honours the valley that surrounds it.

property_title: Bürgenstock Hotel & Alpine Spa: Above Lake Lucerne's Shores
property_intro: Perched on a limestone ridge some 500 metres above Lake Lucerne, Bürgenstock Hotel & Alpine Spa looks out across water, meadow and mountain in every direction. Inside, contemporary Swiss design meets a resort legacy stretching back to 1873, while the Alpine Spa's cantilevered infinity pool seems to hover over the lake. Wander the historic Felsenweg cliff path, ride the funicular down to the shoreline, and dine on produce from the estate's own farm and surrounding valleys.

property_title: Tintswalo Boulders: Simon's Town Serenity Beside the Penguins
property_intro: Tucked into the leafy slopes of Simon's Town, Tintswalo Boulders looks out across False Bay, moments from the granite coves where African penguins gather. Interiors layer antique finds, hand-chosen fabrics and deep verandas that invite long, unhurried mornings. Swim in the sheltered sea, walk the Cape Point paths, or follow a chef through the day's market haul. The Tintswalo Foundation supports local schooling and conservation, so your stay quietly gives something back.

property_title: Royal Livingstone Hotel: Where the Zambezi Meets the Falls
property_intro: Set on the banks of the Zambezi, moments upstream from Victoria Falls, the Royal Livingstone Hotel offers a rare kind of stillness before the thunder. Colonial-era elegance meets manicured lawns where zebra graze freely, and private gateways lead straight to the falls' edge. Sip sundowners as the mist catches the light, drift into the spa, or join guided walks with local conservation teams working to protect the river and support surrounding communities.

property_title: Sal Salis Ningaloo Reef: Where White Dunes Meet a Living Reef
property_intro: Tucked into the dunes of Cape Range National Park, where Australia's outback slips straight into the Indian Ocean, Sal Salis is an intimate wilderness camp on the edge of Ningaloo Reef. Swim with whale sharks and humpbacks metres from shore; return to a candlelit dinner and skies thick with stars. Solar-powered and deliberately low-impact, the safari tents are dressed in natural linens, while guides share the reef's fragile brilliance and the science protecting it.

property_name: Anantara Golden Triangle Elephant Camp & Resort
property_title: Anantara Golden Triangle Elephant Camp & Resort: Gentle Giants
property_intro: Set high above the Ruak and Mekong rivers, where Thailand, Laos and Myanmar quietly converge, this hillside retreat looks out across bamboo forests and drifting morning mist. Teak-clad suites and open-air terraces frame the view, while days unfold with rescued elephants, mahout families, river excursions and Thai cookery lessons. Your stay directly funds the Golden Triangle Asian Elephant Foundation, supporting veterinary care, education and the mahout communities who have made these highlands home.

property_title: Mahali Mzuri: Tented Luxury in Kenya's Olare Motorogi Wild
property_intro: Set high on a ridge above the Olare Motorogi Conservancy, Mahali Mzuri looks out across the plains where the Great Migration passes each year. Twelve tented suites rise on stilts, their sculptural forms echoing the escarpment behind them. Days here might mean tracking lion at dawn, sharing tea with Maasai neighbours, or simply watching elephants drift past from your deck. Grazing agreements with local landowners keep this corridor open, making every stay part of something larger.

property_title: Anjajavy Le Lodge: Barefoot Luxury on Madagascar's Wild Coast
property_intro: Reached only by light aircraft, Anjajavy sits where dry deciduous forest tumbles into the turquoise Mozambique Channel. Rosewood villas open onto white sand, while limestone tsingy pinnacles, baobabs and inquisitive Coquerel's sifakas frame the days. Snorkel hidden coves, paddle mangrove channels or walk with naturalists through a private 550-hectare reserve, protected and replanted in partnership with neighbouring villages. Cuisine leans on the day's catch and garden harvest, served with unhurried Malagasy warmth.

property_title: Uga Chena Huts: Wild Luxury on Sri Lanka's Yala Frontier
property_intro: Tucked between the scrub jungle of Yala National Park and a wide sweep of Indian Ocean sand, Uga Chena Huts offers just fourteen thatched villas, each with a private plunge pool shaded by palu trees. Days begin with leopard tracking alongside resident naturalists and end with barefoot dining beneath the stars. Solar power, careful water stewardship and local hiring keep the footprint light, while the surrounding wilderness remains gloriously, unmistakably in charge.

property_title: La Casitas, A Belmond Hotel: Serenity in Peru's Colca Canyon
property_intro: Tucked into the terraced slopes above the Colca Canyon, La Casitas, A Belmond Hotel scatters twenty private casitas across gardens, orchards and streams fed by Andean snowmelt. Days unfold slowly here: harvesting vegetables with the resident gardener, learning to weave alpaca wool alongside local artisans, or watching condors ride the thermals at dawn. Interiors marry adobe warmth with deep soaking tubs and plunge pools, while long-standing partnerships with Colca communities keep traditions thriving.

property_title: Wilderness Bisate Lodge: Volcanoes, Forest and Gorilla Trails
property_intro: Set within the eroded cone of an ancient volcano, Wilderness Bisate Lodge looks out across the peaks of Rwanda's Virunga Massif, where mountain gorillas roam the bamboo slopes. Six thatched, woven villas curve into the hillside, warmed by fireplaces and dressed in Rwandan craftsmanship. Days begin with a gorilla trek and end with stories over dinner. More than a million indigenous trees have been planted here, restoring forest and forging lasting partnerships with neighbouring communities.

property_title: Giraffe Manor: Breakfast Beside Nairobi's Rothschild Giraffes
property_intro: Set within twelve acres of private forest on the edge of Nairobi, Giraffe Manor is an ivy-clad 1930s residence where endangered Rothschild's giraffes lean through the windows at breakfast. Interiors blend Art Deco detail with warm colonial-era character, while the adjoining Giraffe Centre continues decades of conservation and education work with Kenyan schoolchildren. Wander the sanctuary at dusk, sip sundowners on the terrace, and let the city's national park and Karen's galleries fill your afternoons.

property_title: Sacha Lodge: A Rainforest Sanctuary in Ecuador's Amazon Basin
property_intro: Reached by canoe and a boardwalk through flooded forest, Sacha Lodge rests beside a black-water lagoon in Ecuador's Yasuna region. Thatched cabins open onto 5,000 acres of protected rainforest, where a 275-metre canopy walkway brings you eye to eye with toucans and tanagers. Naturalists from neighbouring Kichwa communities read the forest with remarkable fluency, guiding dawn paddles, night walks and visits to parrot clay licks. Conservation here is quiet, considered and genuinely local.

property_title: Daintree Ecolodge: Rainforest Serenity in Tropical Queensland
property_intro:
Tucked into the world's oldest living rainforest, Daintree Ecolodge places just fifteen timber bayans among the canopy, where waterfalls, fan palms and birdsong set the rhythm of the day. Kuku Yalanji knowledge shapes the experience here, from guided walks to the Daintree Wellness Spa's botanical rituals, while the kitchen draws on native ingredients and nearby growers. Solar power, revegetation and local partnerships underpin it all 
tranquil luxury with genuine purpose, moments from Cape Tribulation's reef-fringed shore.

property_title: Cristalino Lodge: Amazon Rainforest Immersion in Southern Brazil
property_intro: On the banks of the Cristalino River in Brazil's southern Amazon, this intimate lodge sits within a private reserve safeguarding thousands of hectares of pristine rainforest.
