Days unfold along blackwater tributaries, up canopy towers at first light and in the company of naturalists who know each birdsong by name. Bungalows are open to the forest, quietly designed and softly lit. Every stay supports research, conservation and the local communities who call this remarkable region home.

property_title: One & Only Nyungwe House: Amid Tea Fields and Ancient Rainforest
property_intro: Set on the edge of one of Africa's oldest rainforests, One & Only Nyungwe House sits within a working tea plantation in southwest Rwanda, where mist drifts through the canopy and chimpanzees call at dawn. Interiors blend Rwandan craftsmanship with quiet contemporary comfort, while days unfold through guided primate treks, canopy walkways and tea tastings. Conservation partnerships and local employment ensure your stay supports the forest and the communities who safeguard it.

property_title: Silky Oaks Lodge: Where Ancient Daintree Meets Mossman River
property_intro: Tucked into the world's oldest living rainforest, Silky Oaks Lodge rests above the clear, tumbling Mossman River in Far North Queensland. Treehouses and suites sit lightly among the canopy, their timber interiors framing green views and birdsong. Days unfold with river swims, guided walks alongside Kuku Yalanji custodians, spa treatments by the water and produce-led dining. Reef and rainforest conservation partnerships underpin it all, making every stay quietly purposeful as well as restorative.

property_title: Anavilhanas Lodge: Where the Rio Negro Meets Amazon Wilderness
property_intro: On the banks of the Rio Negro, facing the labyrinthine islands of the Anavilhanas archipelago, this intimate lodge places you at the threshold of one of the Amazon's richest waterways. Twenty bungalows and chalets blend regional timber with wide verandas and river views, while days unfold through canoe expeditions, night walks with local guides and visits to riverside communities. Family-run and deeply invested in conservation and village livelihoods, it offers rainforest immersion with genuine warmth.

property_title: Shinta Mani Wild: Tented Luxury Deep in Cambodia's Cardamoms
property_intro: Arrive by zipline into 350 hectares of protected rainforest, where the Cardamom Mountains meet a river of waterfalls and swimming holes. Bill Bensley's fifteen tents perch above the water, layered with antiques, art and a touch of theatre. Days unfold with expedition guides, jungle boat trips, wildlife-camera trails and spa treatments beside cascades, while your stay funds ranger patrols protecting this once-threatened valley. Dinner might be served on a riverbank, lanterns glowing overhead.

property_title: Nayara Tented Camp: Rainforest Luxury Beneath Arenal Volcano
property_intro: Set on a rewilded hillside facing Arenal Volcano, Nayara Tented Camp brings safari-style living to Costa Rica's cloud-draped north. Canvas suites open onto private plunge pools fed by volcanic springs, with sloths dozing in the cecropia trees planted by the owners themselves. Days unfold with guided rainforest walks, hot-spring soaks and dinners drawn from nearby farms. Once cattle pasture, this land now shelters returning wildlife \u2013 proof that thoughtful hospitality can restore as well as delight.

property_title: Copal Tree Lodge: Where Belize's Rainforest Meets the Caribbean
property_intro: Set on a ridge above Punta Gorda in Belize's Toledo District, Copal Tree Lodge looks across 12,000 acres of protected rainforest towards the Caribbean. Hardwood suites open to birdsong and canopy views, while the kitchen draws on the estate's own farm, cacao groves and distillery. Days might bring fly-fishing in the flats, Maya village visits or river kayaking, each shaped by local guides whose knowledge sustains both forest and community.

property_title: Awasi Iguazu: Private Guides and Rainforest Calm Near the Falls
property_intro: Hidden within the Atlantic rainforest a short drive from the Iguazú Falls, Awasi Iguazu gathers just fourteen villas among towering trees, each with a private plunge pool and its own guide and 4x4 for excursions shaped entirely around you. Days might mean dawn at the falls before the crowds, birdwatching along quiet trails, or Guaraní encounters nearby. Timber architecture sits lightly on the land, while the lodge's foundation supports jaguar conservation and neighbouring communities.

property_title: Hotel das Cataratas: Awaken to the Thunder of the Iguaçu Falls
property_intro: Set alone within Brazil's Iguaçu National Park, this rose-pink Portuguese colonial landmark grants something no one else can: the falls to yourself, long after the day visitors depart. Mornings begin with coatis on the lawn, toucans overhead and mist rising from the Devil's Throat. Interiors nod to 1950s Brazilian elegance, while guided walks with park naturalists, boat descents and conservation work alongside local communities deepen every stay in this UNESCO-protected rainforest.

property_title: One & Only Gorilla's Nest: Rwanda's Rainforest Sanctuary Awaits
property_intro: Tucked into a towering eucalyptus grove at the foot of the Virunga volcanoes, One & Only Gorilla's Nest sits on the threshold of Volcanoes National Park. Days begin with misty treks to meet mountain gorilla families, guided by trackers whose knowledge spans generations, and end beside a fire with Rwandan coffee. Interiors weave local craft and warm timber, while partnerships with neighbouring communities and conservation teams ensure your stay supports the forest and the people who protect it.

property_title: Delek Tulum: Barefoot Luxury Where Jungle Meets Caribbean
property_intro: Tucked between dense Mayan jungle and the powdery shoreline of Tulum's beach road, Delek invites you to slow down. Suites crafted from local hardwood, stone and woven textiles open onto private terraces, while candlelit dinners drift into the sound of the Caribbean. Days unfold with cenote swims, temazcal ceremonies and yoga beneath the palms. Built with regional artisans and committed to protecting the coastline's turtles and reef, it is a stay with genuine roots.

property_title: Buahan, A Banyan Tree Escape: Jungle Bali Without Walls or Doors
property_intro: Perched above the Ayung River gorge near Ubud, Buahan invites you to live openly: its bale have no walls, no doors, only the breathing green of the Balinese highlands. Mornings arrive with birdsong and river mist; evenings with wood-fired dining shaped by the village harvest. Local artisans built these timber pavilions, and the surrounding community shares its farming, healing and ritual traditions. A rare stay where luxury feels quietly earned and beautifully unguarded.

property_title: Happy House: Himalayan Warmth and Quiet Grace in Nepal
property_intro: Set among terraced fields and pine-scented ridges, Happy House offers a rare kind of welcome in Nepal " hearth-warmed rooms, handwoven textiles and windows framing the snowbound peaks beyond. Days unfold slowly here: village walks with local guides, kitchen-garden feasts, mornings spent watching mist lift from the valley. Restored with regional craftsmanship and run in partnership with neighbouring families, it channels its earnings into schooling and forest care, so your stay quietly sustains the community around it.

property_title: Sujan Sher Bagh: Tented Luxury on Ranthambore's Wild Edge
property_intro: On the fringes of Ranthambore National Park, Sujan Sher Bagh sits within a grove of trees where tigers pad past ancient hunting ruins. Twelve canvas tents recall the 1920s safari camps of Rajasthan, with campaign furniture, leather trunks and hand-stitched detail. Days begin with dawn drives into the park and end beside the fire pit under Aravalli skies. The camp's conservation work and village schools ensure your stay supports both wildlife corridors and the communities beside them.

property_title: Chiva-Som: A Coastal Wellness Sanctuary in Hua Hin, Thailand
property_intro: Set within seven acres of tropical gardens on the Gulf of Thailand, Chiva-Som has quietly shaped the art of holistic retreat in Hua Hin since 1995. Thai-inspired pavilions and ocean-facing rooms frame a rhythm of personalised health programmes, from physiotherapy and holistic spa therapies to mindful movement by the shore. Produce arrives from the resort's own organic farm, plastics have been all but eliminated, and local craftsmanship threads through every considered detail.

property_title: The Nautilus Maldives: Barefoot Freedom on Baa Atoll's Shores
property_intro: Set within the UNESCO Biosphere Reserve of Baa Atoll, The Nautilus Maldives abandons schedules entirely — you decide when to dine, dive or drift. Just 26 houses and residences sit among sand gardens and palms, each with a private pool and a personal Guest Maestro. Snorkel with manta rays in Hanifaru Bay, join marine biologists tending coral, or sail a traditional dhoni at dusk. Design here is quietly handcrafted, drawing on Maldivian artistry and island rhythms.

property_title: Woods at Sasan: Where Gir's Wild Heart Welcomes You Home
property_intro: On the fringes of Gir National Park in Gujarat, Woods at Sasan sits among mango orchards and teak groves, the last refuge of the Asiatic lion. Days begin with jeep safaris at first light and unwind beside the pool as peacocks call from the canopy. Interiors draw on Kathiawari craft and local stone, while the kitchen leans on nearby farms. Staffed largely by villagers from Sasan, the lodge invests directly in the community it belongs to.

property_title: Ahilya By The Sea: Coastal Grace in Goa's Fishing Village
property_intro: Perched above the fishing village of Nerul in North Goa, Ahilya By The Sea gathers a cluster of Portuguese-era villas around gardens, pools and a tidal creek where kingfishers dart at dawn. Rooms layered with antiques, Indian textiles and family heirlooms feel more like a private home than a hotel. Days drift between boat trips along the Mandovi, market wanders in Panjim and long lunches of Goan seafood, prepared with produce sourced from neighbouring growers and fishermen.

property_title: Leeu Estates: Franschhoek Vineyard Living, Refined and Rooted
property_intro: Set among vines and olive groves on the quiet edge of Franschhoek, Leeu Estates gazes out to the jagged peaks of the Cape Winelands. The manor house and garden suites hold an uncommon mix: contemporary South African art, Cape Dutch bones, deep and unhurried gardens. Days unfold through cellar tastings of Mullineux & Leeu Family Wines, long spa hours and walks past proteas, while the estate invests in local schooling and hospitality training across the valley.

property_title: Jackalope Hotel: Art, Vines and Wonder on the Mornington
property_intro: Set among 11 hectares of vines on Victoria's Mornington Peninsula, Jackalope is a study in contrasts \u2014 brooding architecture, bold contemporary art and light-filled rooms that look out across rows of pinot noir. Days unfold slowly here: tastings at Willow Creek Vineyard, dinner at Doot Doot Doot beneath a shimmering canopy of glass, walks through gardens planted with native species. It is a place shaped by imagination, and by deep respect for the land that sustains it.

property_title: Awasi Mendoza: Private Vineyard Living Beneath the High Andes
property_intro: In Argentina's Uco Valley, eight adobe villas sit quietly among Awasi Mendoza's own Malbec vines, each with a plunge pool, wood-fired grill and uninterrupted view of the Andes. A private guide and 4x4 come with every stay, so days unfold as you wish: high-altitude cellars, horseback rides into the foothills, or nothing more strenuous than lunch beneath the poplars. Local artisans, growers and producers shape the experience, and the estate farms with a light, considered touch.',

property_title: Stanly Ranch: Where Napa Valley's Vineyards Meet Slow Luxury
property_intro: Tucked into the southern reaches of Napa Valley, Stanly Ranch unfolds across 712 acres of working farmland, restored wetlands and vines cooled by breezes off San Pablo Bay. Cottages in warm timber and stone open onto rows of grapes, while days drift between soil-to-table dining, horseback rides and treatments at the Halehouse spa. Regenerative farming and native habitat restoration underpin it all, making this a place where indulgence and stewardship sit comfortably together.

property_title: Les Sources de Caudalie: Vineyard Serenity in Bordeaux's Heart
property_intro:
Set among the celebrated vines of Château Smith Haut Lafitte, just south of Bordeaux, Les Sources de Caudalie feels like a village of its own 
interlinked by water, woodland and rows of Sauvignon Blanc. Rooms are dressed in salvaged timber and antique finds, while the spa pioneered vinotherapy, drawing on grape extracts from the estate's own harvest. Dine on produce from the kitchen garden, cycle between rows tended organically, and let the rhythm of the seasons set your pace.

property_title: The Vines Resort & Spa: Andean Vineyard Living in Mendoza
property_intro: Set within a private vineyard in Mendoza's Uco Valley, The Vines Resort & Spa places you between rows of Malbec and the snow-dusted Andes. Villas of stone, timber and glass open onto terraces made for slow evenings and long horizons. Days might involve horseback rides through the foothills, blending your own barrel with a winemaker, or dining at Siete Fuegos, where Francis Mallmann cooks over open flame. Sustainable farming and local craftsmanship shape every detail.

property_title: Castello di Casole: Tuscan Hills, Vineyards and Quiet Luxury
property_intro: Set within 4,200 acres of woodland, olive groves and vineyards near Siena, this restored tenth-century estate offers a rare kind of seclusion. Frescoed ceilings and stone walls meet contemporary comfort, while days unfold with truffle hunting, cellar tastings and long lunches under the pergola. The estate's own wines and olive oil speak of careful stewardship, and its rewilded valleys shelter deer and wild boar. An unhurried, deeply Tuscan retreat that lingers long after departure.

property_title: Vik Hotel: Art, Wine and Andean Light in Chile's Millahue Valley
property_intro: High on a hilltop in the Millahue Valley, two hours south of Santiago, Vik Hotel crowns a vast estate of vineyards, native forest and grazing horses. Its shimmering titanium canopy shelters interiors where contemporary Chilean and Latin American art fills every room. Days unfold with barrel tastings, rides through the hills, thermal spa rituals and dinners drawn from the estate's own harvest, while ongoing reforestation and local employment keep this remarkable valley thriving.

property_title: Castiglion del Bosco: Tuscan Hills, Vineyards and Quiet Luxury
property_intro: Set within a 5,000-acre estate in the Val d'Orcia, Castiglion del Bosco unfolds across restored farmhouses, ancient woodland and Brunello di Montalcino vineyards. Suites and villas balance Tuscan stone with understated comfort, while days might involve pasta lessons with resident nonnas, cellar tastings or riding out through oak forest. The estate's careful restoration revived an abandoned medieval hamlet, safeguarding its 12th-century frescoes and supporting local artisans, farmers and winemakers who give this corner of Tuscany its quiet character.

property_title: Meadowood Napa Valley: Woodland Calm in St Helena's Hills
property_intro: Tucked into 250 wooded acres above St Helena, Meadowood feels less like a resort and more like a private estate shared with friends. Gabled lodges sit among oaks and Douglas firs, overlooking croquet lawns and a vineyard-fringed golf course. Days unfold with forest hikes, tennis, wine study with a resident master sommelier, and long dinners drawn from the kitchen garden. Rebuilt with fire resilience and native planting at its heart, it champions the valley's growers and land alike.

property_title: Little Palm Island Resort & Spa: Barefoot Luxury in the Keys
property_intro: Reachable only by boat or seaplane, Little Palm Island rests on a five-acre outpost in the Florida Keys, where thatched bungalows sit beneath swaying palms and Key deer wander the shoreline. Adults-only and delightfully unhurried, days unfold with paddleboarding over turtle grass flats, spa treatments beside the lagoon and candlelit dinners on the sand. Coral restoration projects and careful stewardship of the surrounding National Wildlife Refuge underpin every barefoot moment here.

property_title: Clayoquot Wilderness Lodge: Rainforest Reverie on Bedwell Sound
property_intro: Reached only by floatplane or boat, this canvas-roofed retreat sits where the Bedwell River meets the sea, cradled by Vancouver Island's ancient rainforest and a UNESCO biosphere region. Days unfold with horseback rides through old-growth cedar, bear-spotting by kayak and long soaks beneath the treetops. Interiors blend antique curiosities with quiet comfort, while ongoing habitat restoration and partnership with the Ahousaht First Nation ensure your stay leaves this remarkable coastline in better health.

property_title: Eko Patagonia: Conscious Luxury in Chile's Wild Southern Frontier
property_intro: Set against the windswept steppe and glacial peaks of Chilean Patagonia, Eko Patagonia offers a rare kind of seclusion. Timber-and-glass suites frame the horizon, warmed by wood fires and locally woven wool, while guides lead you to hidden lagoons, condor lookouts and estancia tables laden with Patagonian lamb. Solar power, rewilded grassland and partnerships with neighbouring farming families ensure your stay gives back. Wake to guanaco crossing the plain, and let the silence settle.

property_title: Few & Far Luvhondo: Wild Luxury in the Soutpansberg Peaks
property_intro: High in the Soutpansberg mountains of South Africa's Limpopo province, Few & Far Luvhondo unfolds across a vast rewilded reserve where leopards roam ancient cliffs and baobabs stand sentinel. Six solar-powered suites are carved into the landscape with restraint and craft, while a solar-powered cable car glides silently above the valley. Guests walk with trackers, share meals shaped by local growers, and help fund an ambitious conservation corridor restoring land, wildlife and livelihoods alike.

property_title: Refugia Chiloé: Island Living Shaped by Sea, Wood and Myth
property_intro: On Chiloé's eastern shore, Refugia stands above the tidal waters of Rilán, its timber-clad form echoing the island's palafitos and shingled churches. Twelve rooms face the archipelago's shifting light, while local cooks draw on curanto traditions and seaweed harvested nearby. Days unfold with island guides: boat crossings to Mechuque, walks through native forest, visits to families weaving wool. Chiloé's culture is not observed here but shared, thoughtfully and on its own terms.

property_title: Posada Ayana: Coastal Calm and Turrell Skies in José Ignacio
property_intro: Set among dunes and wind-shaped pines a short stroll from José Ignacio's Atlantic shoreline, Posada Ayana pairs Scandinavian restraint with Uruguayan warmth. Rooms open onto gardens planted with native species, while Ta Khut, James Turrell's Skyspace and the first in South America, turns dusk into a slow, colour-shifting ritual. Days drift between the pool, seasonal cooking rooted in nearby farms, and rides through lagoon country with guides whose families have lived here for generations.

property_title: Aman Yangyun: Ancient Camphor, Restored Village Near Shanghai
property_intro: Half an hour from Shanghai's skyline, Aman Yangyun unfolds within a rescued Ming and Qing dynasty village, its stone dwellings dismantled in Jiangxi and rebuilt here alongside 10,000 camphor trees saved from a reservoir project. Antique courtyards now hold suites, a Nan Shufang cultural pavilion, and studios for calligraphy, tea and Kunqu opera. Craftsmen spent years restoring every carved beam, and the result feels less like a hotel than a village quietly reawakened.

property_title: Banyan Tree Chongqing Bei Bei: Thermal Springs Below Jinyun
property_intro: Tucked beneath the forested slopes of Jinyun Mountain, where the Jialing River curves quietly through Bei Bei, this retreat draws on thermal waters prized here for centuries. Courtyard villas echo Ba-Yu architecture, with timber screens, private hot-spring pools and gardens that invite unhurried mornings. Guests wander bamboo groves, learn regional tea rituals, or sample Chongqing's fiery flavours reimagined. Conservation work with the surrounding nature reserve and local artisan partnerships give each stay quiet purpose.

property_title: Amandayan: Serene Heights Above Lijiang's Ancient Old Town
property_intro: Perched on Lion Hill above Lijiang's UNESCO-listed Old Town, Amandayan looks across a sea of grey-tiled rooftops towards the snow-capped Jade Dragon Mountain. Stone pathways, timber pavilions and courtyard suites draw on Naxi building traditions, while interiors remain quietly restrained. Days might begin with tai chi at dawn, then unfold through Dongba script calligraphy, visits to local villages and market walks with the chefs. A place to linger, listen and understand Yunnan more deeply.

property_title: Six Senses Qingcheng Mountain: Where Ancient Taoist Calm Endures
property_intro: Set among the misty foothills of Sichuan's sacred Qingcheng Mountain, birthplace of Taoism, this retreat unfolds across courtyards inspired by Qing dynasty villages, with dark timber, grey brick and lantern-lit walkways. Wander tea plantations and bamboo groves, practise qigong with a local master, or learn Sichuanese cooking from village growers. Spa rituals draw on Chinese medicine, while nearby Dujiangyan's ancient waterworks and the giant panda base reward slow, curious days. Wellness here feels quietly earned.

property_title: Badrutt's Palace: Alpine Grandeur Above St Moritz's Frozen Lake
property_intro: Rising above the frozen lake at St Moritz, Badrutt's Palace has welcomed travellers since 1896, when the Badrutt family first tempted visitors to spend winter in the Engadin. Its turreted silhouette conceals lavish salons, family-run warmth and nine restaurants ranging from Japanese refinement to a mountainside chalet. Ski the Corviglia slopes, take tea beneath the vaulted Grand Hall, then retreat to a suite framing the Piz Rosatsch. Five generations on, the same family still sets the tone.

property_title: Caiman, Pantanal: Where Jaguars Roam Brazil's Wild Wetlands
property_intro:
Set within 53,000 hectares of private reserve in Brazil's southern Pantanal, Caiman pairs working cattle ranch heritage with pioneering wildlife protection. Two intimate lodges, styled with regional craftsmanship and shaded verandas, look out across seasonal floodplains alive with hyacinth macaws, giant anteaters and capybara. Days unfold with biologist-led safaris, horseback rides and night drives, while the celebrated Oncafari project brings guests remarkably close to wild jaguars 
inguists and rangers drawn from neighbouring communities.

property_title: Aman-i-Khas: Tented Luxury on the Edge of Ranthambore
property_intro: On the fringes of Ranthambore National Park, Aman-i-Khas gathers ten billowing tents beneath a canopy of dhok trees, each drawing on the grandeur of Mughal campaign quarters with soaring cotton drapes and freestanding baths. Days begin with jeep safaris in search of tigers, and close around a fire pit beneath the Rajasthani stars. The camp supports local schooling and conservation initiatives, while village walks and step-well visits reveal a quieter, deeply rooted side of Rajasthan.

property_title: Bamurru Plains: Wild Floodplain Luxury on the Top End's Edge
property_intro: On the edge of Kakadu, where the Mary River floodplains stretch towards the Timor Sea, Bamurru Plains offers a rare kind of seclusion. Ten safari-style bungalows sit lightly on the land, mesh walls dissolving the boundary between bed and buffalo grass. Days pass on airboats gliding through paperbark swamps, with magpie geese overhead and crocodiles below. Working alongside local rangers and the neighbouring cattle station, the lodge protects this floodplain wilderness while sharing its extraordinary birdlife.

property_title: SUJÁN Jawai: Where Leopards Roam Rajasthan's Granite Wilds
property_intro: Set among ancient granite hills and shepherd country in rural Rajasthan, SUJÁN Jawai places you in one of India's most extraordinary leopard landscapes, where big cats and Rabari herders have long coexisted peacefully. Nine tented suites blend mid-century safari elegance with Rajasthani craft, while days unfold through hill drives, village encounters and evenings beneath vast skies. Guided by a deep commitment to local employment and leopard conservation, this is wilderness lived with genuine respect.

property_title: Château de Fonscolombe: Provençal Grandeur Among the Vines
property_intro: Set within a working wine estate near Aix-en-Provence, Château de Fonscolombe unfolds across centuries-old parkland where plane trees shade ornamental pools and rows of vines stretch towards the Luberon. This restored 18th-century residence pairs frescoed salons with contemporary calm, while its kitchens draw on the estate's own organic harvest. Wander the terraced gardens, taste vintages in the historic cellars, or simply linger over long Provençal lunches as cicadas mark the passing afternoon.

property_title: Suvretta House: Alpine Grandeur Above St. Moritz's Lakes
property_intro: Set apart on a sunlit meadow between St. Moritz and Champfèr, Suvretta House looks out across the Engadin's lakes towards the Piz da la Margna. Family-run for generations, it pairs the ceremony of a grand Alpine hotel with genuine warmth: wood-panelled salons, a private ski lift to Corviglia, and kitchens that favour Graubünden producers. Days might begin with cross-country tracks at the door and end beside the fire, watching light fade over the valley.

property_title: Divine Cave Experience: Santorini's Cliffside Sanctuary Awaits
property_intro: Carved into the volcanic rock of Santorini's caldera, Divine Cave Experience pairs centuries-old cave architecture with a quiet, contemporary calm. Whitewashed curves, handcrafted local textiles and plunge pools open onto the Aegean, where sunsets stretch across the water. Days unfold slowly: wine tastings among Assyrtiko vines, sunrise swims, conversations with island artisans. Traditional building methods keep interiors naturally cool, reducing energy use, while family stewardship ensures your stay supports the craftspeople and producers who shape Santorini's character.

property_title: Kagga Kamma Nature Reserve: Sandstone Sanctuary in the Cederberg
property_intro: Set among the weathered sandstone formations of the Cederberg, Kagga Kamma invites you into a landscape shaped over millennia. Suites are carved into rock or perched beneath open skies, where stargazing feels almost ceremonial. Days unfold with guided walks among ancient San rock art, scenic drives past fynbos and succulents, and quiet hours watching light shift across the ridges. The reserve protects rare flora and fauna while honouring the heritage of the region's first inhabitants.

property_title: Argos in Cappadocia: Where Ancient Stone Meets Starlit Skies
property_intro: Carved into the ridge of Uçhisar village, Argos unfolds across restored cave dwellings, monastic tunnels and terraced courtyards overlooking Pigeon Valley and distant Mount Erciyes. Rooms reveal their original stonework, warmed by kilims, antique timber and quiet craftsmanship. Days might begin with a balloon drifting over the valleys and end with wine from the estate's own vineyard, paired with produce grown nearby. Restoration here has revived local skills, traditions and a village long overlooked.

property_title: Acro Suites: Cliffside Calm Above Crete's Aegean Horizon
property_intro: Carved into the cliffs above Agia Pelagia, Acro Suites looks out across the Cretan Sea from a hillside of wild herbs and warm limestone. Cave-inspired suites, private pools and locally quarried stone reflect the island's raw geology, while the kitchen draws on Cretan growers and centuries-old recipes. Days unfold with sunrise yoga, sea swims from the rocks and slow evenings watching the light shift over the water. Wellbeing here feels unhurried, rooted and quietly generous.

property_title: Desert Rock Resort: A Sanctuary Carved into Ancient Cliffs
property_intro: Tucked within a granite massif in NEOM's mountainous interior, Desert Rock Resort sits where sheer rock walls open onto a hidden valley in north-west Saudi Arabia. Villas and cliff-side suites are set into the landscape rather than upon it, with local stone, shaded terraces and near-silent nights beneath brilliant stars. Days unfold through canyon walks, guided geology and stargazing, while restoration of native flora and Saudi hospitality by resident guides give the setting genuine depth.

property_title: Nine Furlongs: Unhurried Days in India's Rolling Green Hills
property_intro:
Named for the measure of a racecourse, Nine Furlongs invites you to slow to a gentler pace. Set among mist-softened hills and working farmland, the house pairs heritage bones with contemporary calm 
crafted by regional artisans. Days unfold with garden breakfasts, walks through eucalyptus and tea, and evenings by the fire. Produce is grown or sourced within miles, and local families share in the estate's livelihood 
making every stay quietly meaningful.

property_title: KAAV Safari Lodge: Tiger Country Comfort on Kanha's Edge
property_intro: On the quiet fringes of Kanha National Park, KAAV Safari Lodge sits amid sal forest and farmland where villagers still walk the old cattle tracks. Twelve airy suites open onto private verandahs, dressed in Gond-inspired art and local stone. Days begin with dawn drives in search of tigers and barasingha, and close beside the pool with Bagheli-spiced dinners. The lodge trains and employs from surrounding hamlets, keeping conservation and community firmly intertwined.

property_title: Camp Denali: Wilderness, Warmth and Alaska's Vast Horizons
property_intro: Deep within Denali National Park, where the road ends and tundra stretches towards North America's highest peak, Camp Denali has welcomed guests since 1952. Hand-built cabins face Denali itself, warmed by wood stoves and lit by paraffin lamps, powered by solar and hydro. Days unfold on guided hikes across open country, evenings in conversation with naturalists over garden-grown suppers. A family-run retreat where low-impact living and genuine hospitality have always gone hand in hand.

property_title: Samara Karoo Private Reserve: Where the Great Karoo Awakens
property_intro: Set across 67,000 acres of the Great Karoo in South Africa's Eastern Cape, Samara is a landscape of ancient plains, mountain plateaus and sweeping silence. Once farmland, it has been restored over decades, welcoming back cheetah, rhino and elephant. Guests track big cats on foot, picnic high on the Mountain Reserve and return to elegant, unhurried lodgings shaped by family stewardship. Local employment and conservation research underpin every stay, quietly and meaningfully.

property_title: Kisawa Sanctuary: Barefoot Luxury on Mozambique's Benguerra
property_intro: On the southern tip of Benguerra Island, within Mozambique's Bazaruto Archipelago, Kisawa Sanctuary unfolds across three kilometres of private beach, dune forest and grassland. Each bungalow is 3D-printed from local sand and seawater, furnished with pieces made by Mozambican artisans, and comes with its own vehicle and dedicated host. Days drift between dhow sailing, diving with manta rays and long, unhurried lunches. Room revenue supports the neighbouring Bazaruto Center for Scientific Studies, a permanent ocean research base.

property_title: Arijiju: A Handcrafted Retreat in Kenya's Borana Highlands
property_intro: Set high on the slopes of the Borana Conservancy, Arijiju looks out across Laikipia towards Mount Kenya, its stone walls and vaulted ceilings drawing on monastic architecture and local craftsmanship. This private house sleeps up to ten, with a spa, lap pool and squash court alongside riding, tracking rhino on foot and fly-camping under the stars. Conservation fees support anti-poaching teams and neighbouring communities, so every night here holds quiet purpose.

property_title: Borgo Pignano: A Tuscan Estate Where Nature Sets the Pace
property_intro: High on a limestone ridge above Volterra, Borgo Pignano gathers an eighteenth-century villa, restored farm buildings and 750 acres of woodland, wildflower meadows and organic fields. Frescoed rooms and lime-washed walls sit easily alongside horses in the paddocks and beehives in the orchard. Days might mean truffle hunting, bread-making in the bakery, or simply reading beside the pool. The estate farms regeneratively, employs local artisans, and lets the surrounding countryside shape every meal and moment.

property_title: ICEHOTEL: Sculpted Nights Beside Sweden's Torne River
property_intro: On the banks of the Torne River in Jukkasj\u00e4rvi, 200 kilometres above the Arctic Circle, ICEHOTEL is rebuilt each winter from ice harvested locally and returned to the river come spring. Artists from around the world carve suites that exist for a single season, while warm cabins, a Sami-inspired restaurant and an ice bar await. Days are spent dog sledding or tracking the aurora; nights, wrapped in reindeer hides beneath sculpted vaults.

property_title: Yasuragi: Japanese Serenity on Stockholm's Archipelago Shore
property_intro: Set on a pine-fringed slope above the water at Hasseludden, just half an hour from central Stockholm, Yasuragi reinterprets Japanese bathing culture on the Swedish archipelago. Guests trade shoes for a yukata and drift between hot baths, cold plunges and outdoor onsen with views across the bay. Days unfold through shiatsu treatments, quiet tearooms, mindful movement and seasonal Japanese dishes, while low timber architecture and locally sourced ingredients keep the experience grounded in its surroundings.

property_title: Fothergill Island: Where Lake Kariba Meets the Wild Matusadona
property_intro: On the shores of Lake Kariba, where the Matusadona escarpment falls away to drowned forests and open water, Fothergill offers a rare kind of stillness. Airy, thatched suites frame views of elephant crossing the floodplain at dusk. Days unfold by boat, on foot with expert guides, or over sundowners with a fishing rod in hand. Long committed to protecting this wilderness, the lodge supports anti-poaching efforts and neighbouring communities across the valley.

property_title: Casa San Agustín: Colonial Splendour in Old Cartagena's Heart
property_intro: Tucked behind the walls of Cartagena's old town, Casa San Agustín unfolds across three 17th-century mansions, where a 400-year-old aqueduct arches above the pool and coral-stone walls hold the day's warmth. Rooms marry Caribbean light with hand-crafted Colombian details, while the kitchen draws on Bolívar's farmers and fishermen. Wander to the Rosario Islands, learn the city's stories from local historians, or simply linger on the rooftop as the cathedral bells ring out.

property_title: Camp Khwai: Riverside Days at the Wild Heart of the Okavango
property_intro: On the fringes of Moremi, where the Khwai River draws elephants, wild dogs and lion prides to its banks, Camp Khwai offers a rare seat at nature's table. Canvas suites are dressed in muted linens and local craft, opening to floodplain views. Days unfold with guided drives, mokoro glides and walks led by Khwai community guides, whose village holds the concession — your stay directly sustaining their land and livelihoods.

property_title: Anantara Qasr Al Sarab: A Fortress Retreat in the Liwa Dunes
property_intro: Deep within the Liwa Desert, on the edge of the Empty Quarter, this fortress-like retreat rises from apricot dunes that shift with the light. Rooms and villas blend Emirati craftsmanship with quiet comfort, while days unfold through falconry, camel treks, dune walks with Bedouin guides and stargazing far from city glow. Set within a protected conservation area, the resort supports Arabian oryx and gazelle, offering a stay shaped by heritage, stillness and genuine care.

property_title: Dar Tantora The House Hotel: AlUla's Candlelit Mudbrick Soul
property_intro: Tucked within AlUla's Old Town, Dar Tantora occupies a cluster of centuries-old mudbrick houses, patiently restored by local craftspeople using palm wood, stone and lime. Evenings unfold by candlelight, with no electric glare to dim the desert stars. Rooms are hand-painted in the manner of Saudi homes of old, while days bring rooftop breakfasts, oasis walks and the sandstone theatre of Hegra nearby. A living neighbourhood, gently reawakened rather than reinvented.

property_title: Royal Mansour Marrakech: Your Own Riad Beside the Medina Walls
property_intro: Tucked behind the ramparts of Marrakech's medina, Royal Mansour gathers 53 private riads within gardens of orange trees, roses and running water. Each has its own rooftop terrace, plunge pool and quiet courtyard, shaped by Moroccan master craftspeople whose zellige, carved cedar and stucco took years to complete. Days unfold with hammam rituals, Atlas-inspired dining and unhurried wandering through the souks, while the hotel's ateliers keep centuries-old artisanal skills alive for the next generation.

property_title: Amanjena: Timeless Moorish Grandeur in Marrakech's Palm Groves
property_intro: Beyond the ramparts of Marrakech, where olive groves give way to the snow-tipped Atlas, Amanjena rises in warm pisé walls around a centuries-old irrigation basin. Pavilions and domed pavilion suites open to courtyards scented with orange blossom, while artisans trained in local zellige and tadelakt keep age-old crafts alive. Ride through the palmeraie at dawn, wander the souks with a private guide, then retreat to hammam rituals and unhurried candlelit evenings.

property_title: Can Ferrereta: A Restored Mallorcan Manor in Santanyí's Heart
property_intro: Set within a 17th-century manor house in the sandstone village of Santanyí, Can Ferrereta brings southern Mallorca's slower rhythms into focus. Original vaults and beams sit alongside contemporary Mallorcan craftsmanship, local marés stone and works by island artists. Days unfold between the walled garden, the subterranean spa and a kitchen led by produce from nearby farms and fishermen. Beyond the doors, Saturday markets, coastal coves and the Serra de Llevant await discovery.

property_title: Landet Stay: Quiet Swedish Countryside, Thoughtfully Reimagined
property_intro: Set amid the meadows, forests and lake-strewn calm of the Swedish countryside, Landet Stay invites you to slow to the rhythm of the seasons. Interiors pair honest materials with Nordic restraint, while days unfold through forest foraging, wild swimming, wood-fired saunas and long dinners built around produce from nearby growers. Local craftspeople have shaped much of what you touch here, and the surrounding land is tended with care, so your stay quietly supports the landscape that makes it memorable.

property_title: Gleneagles Townhouse: Edinburgh Glamour with a Highland Heart
property_intro: Set within a restored 1840s bank on Edinburgh's St Andrew Square, Gleneagles Townhouse brings the warmth of its Perthshire sibling to the heart of the city. Marble halls and a domed former banking room now hold Lamplighters restaurant, while bedrooms layer soft tartans with contemporary Scottish art. Days unfold with rooftop spa treatments, wellness classes and cocktails at The Spence, all supported by local makers, growers and craftspeople from across Scotland.

property_title: The PuLi: Shanghai's Serene Urban Retreat Above Jing'an
property_intro:
Overlooking the green expanse of Jing'an Park, The PuLi brings a considered calm to central Shanghai. Interiors draw on Chinese scholarly tradition 
i open, contemplative spaces, where dark timber, stone and lantern light temper the city beyond the glass. Days might begin with tai chi, unfold over a long soak in the Anantara Spa, and close with cocktails at the 32-metre Long Bar. Local artisans and seasonal Jiangnan produce shape much of what you'll encounter here.

property_title: Hotel Tugu Bali: Where Art, Ocean and Heritage Entwine
property_intro: On the quiet shoreline of Canggu, where rice fields meet black volcanic sand, Hotel Tugu Bali feels closer to a living museum than a hotel. Antique pavilions, temple carvings and centuries-old Javanese artefacts fill every corner, each with a story its custodians love to share. Days unfold with Balinese cooking lessons, candlelit dinners in a 300-year-old teak hall, and sunset rituals by the sea, all supported by artisans and villages nearby.

property_title: Kalukanda House: Barefoot Luxury on Sri Lanka's Southern Coast
property_intro: Set among coconut groves and paddy fields near Ahangama, Kalukanda House is a six-bedroom villa where whitewashed walls, antique Sri Lankan pieces and a long lap pool invite unhurried days. Surf breaks and sleepy fishing villages lie minutes away, while cinnamon plantations and lagoon backwaters reward slower exploring. A resident team cooks with produce from nearby smallholders, and guests are welcomed into village life rather than kept at arm's length from it.

property_title: Susafa: A Sicilian Wheat Estate Where Time Slows Beautifully
property_intro: Deep in Sicily's golden interior, between Palermo and the Madonie mountains, Susafa rises from a 19th-century wheat farm still worked by the same family. Vaulted grain stores have become serene rooms of bare stone and linen, where nothing competes with the view. Days unfold slowly: bread baked in the old oven, swims beneath open sky, walks through fields humming with bees. Dinner arrives from the kitchen garden, and conversation lingers long after the candles burn low.

property_title: Misool Eco Resort: Raja Ampat's Private Island Marine Sanctuary
property_intro: Set on a remote island in southern Raja Ampat, Misool sits at the heart of a 300,000-acre marine reserve created by the resort's own founders. Timber villas rise over water so clear the reef seems close enough to touch, built by local craftsmen using reclaimed wood. Days drift between dives among manta rays, kayaking through hidden lagoons and lazy afternoons in a hammock, knowing your stay directly sustains rangers, patrols and Papuan communities.......}

property_title: Islas Secas: A Solar-Powered Sanctuary in Panama's Wild Pacific
property_intro: Scattered across the Gulf of Chiriquí, this private archipelago of sixteen islands is reached by air from Panama City, then given over entirely to the rhythm of the sea. Just a handful of casitas overlook the water, powered by sun and shaped from natural materials. Days drift between humpback whale sightings, diving at Coiba, and quiet coves. A working reserve, Islas Secas channels its efforts into marine research and coastal communities nearby.

property_title: Areias do Seixo: Barefoot Luxury Amid Portugal's Wild Dunes
property_intro: Tucked between pine woods and the Atlantic dunes of Povoa de Penafirme, an hour north of Lisbon, Areias do Seixo feels like a secret shared among friends. Each room is a work of craft, shaped from reclaimed timber, clay and candlelight, with fires lit at dusk. Days unfold with surf lessons, horse rides along empty sand and dinners drawn from the hotel's organic gardens, where regenerative farming and local partnerships quietly underpin everything.

property_title: Barracuda Hotel & Villas: Barefoot Refinement on Brazil's Coast
property_intro: Set among the dunes and palm groves of São Miguel do Gostoso, Barracuda Hotel & Villas draws on the rhythms of Brazil's north-eastern coastline, where trade winds draw kitesurfers and fishing boats still work the shore. Villas of raw wood, thatch and local stone open to private pools and ocean horizons. Days unfold with regional cooking, sailing on jangadas and quiet exchanges with the village community that shapes this remarkably unhurried corner of Rio Grande do Norte.

property_title: The Fortress Resort & Spa: Barefoot Luxury on Galle's Coast
property_intro: On Sri Lanka's southern shore near Koggala, The Fortress Resort & Spa rises behind dramatic ramparts inspired by the Dutch architecture of nearby Galle. Inside, cool courtyards, timber shutters and an ocean-facing pool set a gentler pace. Days might begin with surfing lessons or an Ayurvedic ritual, and end with chef-led seafood tastings. The resort works closely with coastal communities and marine conservation projects, while stilt fishermen and tea country lie temptingly close.

property_title: Auberge du Soleil: Sunlit Olive Groves Above the Napa Valley
property_intro: Set high on a Rutherford hillside within a working olive grove, Auberge du Soleil looks out across vineyards that shift colour with the seasons. Terracotta-toned suites open onto private terraces, while the Michelin-starred restaurant draws on produce from neighbouring growers and the estate's own trees. Days unfold with spa rituals, cellar tastings and quiet hours beneath ancient olives. Long-standing partnerships with Napa's sustainable winemakers keep the valley's land, and its stories, thriving.

property_title: Kona Village: Where Hawaii's Ancient Shores Welcome You Home
property_intro: Set along Kahuwai Bay on Hawaii Island's Kona coast, Kona Village unfolds across 81 acres of lava fields, palm groves and anchialine ponds. Thatched hale draw on Polynesian building traditions, standing without televisions or locks, inviting a slower rhythm. Petroglyphs and fishponds trace centuries of habitation, cared for alongside cultural practitioners and marine conservation partners. Days pass with outrigger paddling, reef swims and lava-rock spa rituals, closing with dinner beneath the stars.

property_title: Villa La Coste: Art, Architecture and Vineyards in the Luberon
property_intro: Set among organic vines and olive groves in the Luberon hills, Villa La Coste is a place where contemporary art and Provençal earth meet. Guests wander a sculpture trail past works by Louise Bourgeois and pavilions by Gehry and Ando, before dinner drawn from the estate's biodynamic harvest. Suites open to private terraces, valley views and quiet. Beyond the art, the vineyard's certified organic practices sustain the land and local livelihoods.

property_title: Delaire Graff Estate: Vineyard Luxury Above Stellenbosch
property_intro: Perched on the Helshoogte Pass with the Simonsberg rising beyond, Delaire Graff Estate looks out across the Cape Winelands from its own working vineyards. Ten lodges come with private plunge pools, log fires and an art collection worth lingering over, while two restaurants pair estate wines with produce grown a short walk away. Spend mornings in the spa, afternoons tasting, and evenings watching the light shift across Stellenbosch's peaks. Conservation of indigenous fynbos and skills training for local staff underpin it all.

property_title: VOYA Boutique Hotel: Havana's Refined Corner of Cuban Soul
property_intro: Tucked into a leafy pocket of Havana's Vedado district, VOYA Boutique Hotel pairs mid-century Cuban architecture with contemporary calm. Behind its quiet façade you'll find handcrafted furnishings by local artisans, a shaded courtyard for slow breakfasts and rooftop evenings scented with sea air. Wander to the Malecón at dusk, seek out neighbourhood jazz cellars, or let the team arrange tobacco-farm visits. Staffed and supplied locally, VOYA keeps its rewards firmly within the community it calls home.

property_title: Arctic TreeHouse Hotel: Glass-Fronted Calm in Lapland's Pines
property_intro: Perched on a forested hillside on the edge of Rovaniemi, Arctic TreeHouse Hotel places you level with the treetops, where floor-to-ceiling glass frames pine, snow and the shifting Northern Lights. Nordic timber interiors, locally sourced menus and a design rooted in Sfmi tradition give each suite a quiet intimacy. Days unfold with husky trails, forest foraging and long saunas, while the hotel's careful build preserved the surrounding woodland and supports Lapland's makers.

property_title: Hapuku Lodge + Tree Houses: Kaikōura Treetop Living by the Sea
property_intro: Set within a working deer farm between the Seaward Kaikōura range and the Pacific, Hapuku Lodge + Tree Houses invites you to sleep among the branches of a native kānuka grove. Family-built and architect-designed, its timber, copper and glass interiors frame mountain snow and ocean in equal measure. Days might bring whale watching, vineyard lunches or fly fishing, before dinner drawn from the orchard, garden and coast. Regeneration planting continues quietly around you.

property_title: Tsala Treetop Lodge: Suspended in the Heart of Knysna Forest
property_intro: Raised on stilts within the ancient canopy of the Knysna forest, Tsala Treetop Lodge invites you to live at eye level with the birds. Timber walkways thread between glass-fronted suites and private infinity pools, where indigenous ironwood and yellowwood press close. Days unfold slowly here: forest walks, Garden Route drives, long dinners drawn from local producers. The lodge's careful footprint protects the very woodland that shelters it, and supports the surrounding community.

property_title: Lion Sands Chalkley Treehouse: Sleep Beneath Sabi Sand Stars
property_intro: Raised on a platform beneath a 500-year-old leadwood in the Sabi Sand, Lion Sands Chalkley Treehouse offers a single night entirely your own. Dinner is laid out at dusk, your guide departs, and the Sabie River bushveld takes over: nightjars, distant lion, a sky thick with stars. Days bring game drives through Big Five country, while Lion Sands' conservation work and community partnerships help safeguard this wilderness for generations still to come.

property_title: Free Spirit Spheres: Suspended Serenity in Vancouver Island's Rainforest
property_intro: Suspended among Sitka spruce and cedar on Vancouver Island, Free Spirit Spheres invites you to sleep within the rainforest canopy rather than beside it. Three handcrafted wooden spheres sway gently with the breeze, their curved interiors fitted with built-in beds, small kitchens and round windows framing moss, mist and birdsong. The forest floor remains untouched, protected by a light-footed design philosophy. Wake to filtered green light, wander the trails, and rediscover what stillness sounds like.

property_title: Chewton Glen Treehouses: Canopy Living on the New Forest Edge
property_intro: Perched above a wooded valley on the fringes of the New Forest, Chewton Glen's treehouse suites hover among oak and birch, a short stroll from Hampshire's coast. Breakfast arrives quietly through a hatch; deer graze below as you sink into your private hot tub. Interiors balance timber warmth with deep baths and log fires, while the estate's kitchen garden, beehives and woodland planting shape both the menus and the birdsong that wakes you.

property_title: Kailasha The Himalayan Village: Slow Living in the Foothills
property_intro: Tucked into the terraced slopes of the Kumaon Himalaya, Kailasha The Himalayan Village gathers stone-and-timber cottages around orchards, pine and far-reaching valley views. Days unfold gently here: forest walks with local guides, harvests from the kitchen garden, hearth-cooked Pahadi dishes and evenings under remarkably clear skies. Built using regional craft traditions and run alongside neighbouring villages, it supports hill livelihoods and mountain ecology. Come for the quiet, stay for the sense of belonging.

property_title: Zannier Sonop: 1920s Desert Grandeur Above Namibia's Dunes
property_intro: Perched atop a granite outcrop in Namibia's vast Karas region, Zannier Sonop invites you into the romance of 1920s exploration. Ten canvas tents, dressed in antique furnishings and Persian rugs, look across an ocean of red sand and ancient rock. Days unfold with horse rides, e-fatbike trails, stargazing and champagne at sundown. The surrounding 5,600-hectare reserve is being carefully rewilded, while local artisans and guides share the stories that make this remarkable landscape sing.

property_title: Six Senses Uluwatu: Clifftop Calm Above Bali's Wild Indian Ocean
property_intro: Perched on limestone cliffs at Bali's southern tip, Six Senses Uluwatu gazes across the Indian Ocean towards distant surf breaks and Uluwatu's ancient sea temple. Villas and suites draw on Balinese craftsmanship, with alang-alang thatch, local stone and gardens tumbling towards the water. Days unfold with cliff-edge yoga, wellness rituals rooted in Usada healing, and dining shaped by island growers. Behind the scenes, an on-site water bottling plant and reef restoration work quietly reduce impact.

property_title: Amankila: Cliffside Serenity on Bali's Untamed Eastern Coast
property_intro: Set high on a bluff in Karangasem, Amankila looks out across the Lombok Strait, with three tiered pools stepping down towards the sea like rice terraces. Thatched suites draw on the architecture of Bali's old Karangasem court, while pathways wind through gardens to a secluded beach club. Days unfold with temple visits at Tirta Gangga, salt-making with village families in Kusamba, and dinners shaped by the estate's own gardens.

property_title: Casa Angelina: Amalfi Coast Serenity Above the Tyrrhenian
property_intro: Perched on the cliffs of Praiano, Casa Angelina looks out across the Tyrrhenian towards Positano and the Li Galli islands. Interiors are pure white, deliberately uncluttered, allowing contemporary art and the shifting Mediterranean light to take centre stage. Days unfold slowly here: a lift down to the private beach club, boat trips to hidden coves, kitchen gardens supplying the Michelin-starred table. Family-run and rooted in Campanian craft, it champions local producers and artisans with quiet conviction.

property_title: Hacienda Na Xamena: Ibiza's Cliffside Sanctuary Above the Sea
property_intro: Perched on the pine-clad cliffs of Ibiza's wild northern coast, Hacienda Na Xamena looks out across the Mediterranean from 180 metres above the waves. Whitewashed arches, hand-crafted local materials and terraces carved into the rock frame sunsets over Cala Xarraca. Descend to the cascading Cabin Baths, dine on produce from the estate's own gardens, and wander the surrounding nature reserve. Family-run since 1971, it remains a quietly pioneering retreat where island craftsmanship and landscape shape every moment.

property_title: Canaves Epitome: Santorini Serenity Above the Caldera Breeze
property_intro: Set in the quiet village of Oia, Canaves Epitome offers a calmer side of Santorini, where whitewashed suites open onto private pools and gardens scented with bougainvillaea. Architecture draws on Cycladic craft traditions, using local stone and light in equal measure. Days might involve vineyard walks among ancient assyrtiko vines, cookery lessons with island producers, or simply the long Aegean sunset. The team works closely with Santorini farmers and artisans, keeping island heritage alive on every plate.

property_title: Casa Chameleon at Las Catalinas: Where Tropical Dry Forest Meets Sea
property_intro: Perched above the car-free village of Las Catalinas on Costa Rica's Guanacaste coast, Casa Chameleon offers just 21 adults-only villas, each with its own plunge pool and uninterrupted Pacific views. Wake to howler monkeys in the surrounding tropical dry forest, then wander cobbled lanes to hidden beaches or ride miles of trails through protected woodland. Interiors blend local hardwoods with artisan craft, while the wider community's reforestation work quietly restores one of the planet's rarest habitats.

property_title: Il San Pietro di Positano: Cliffside Grace on the Amalfi Coast
property_intro: Carved into the cliffs just beyond Positano, Il San Pietro drapes itself over terraces of bougainvillaea and lemon groves, with a private beach reached by lift through the rock. Rooms open to the Tyrrhenian on every side, furnished with antiques, hand-painted Vietri tiles and family heirlooms gathered across generations. Days might mean sailing to hidden coves, tennis above the sea, or cookery lessons using produce from the hotel's own kitchen garden and local growers.

property_title: The Maybourne Riviera: Cliffside Serenity Above Monaco's Coast
property_intro: Perched on a rocky promontory at Roquebrune-Cap-Martin, The Maybourne Riviera surveys three countries at once, with Monaco glittering below and the Alps rising behind. Interiors by Bryan O'Sullivan and André Fu frame the Mediterranean like artwork, while kitchens led by Mauro Colagreco and Jean-Georges Vongerichten celebrate Ligurian and Provençal growers. Days unfold between the clifftop pool, coastal walks along the Sentier du Littoral, and spa rituals scented with local citrus and wild herbs.

property_title: The Trillium: Refined Coastal Living Rooted in Mexico's Wild Edge
property_intro: Set where jungle-clad hills lean towards the Pacific, The Trillium offers a considered retreat for those who travel with intention. Sunlit interiors pair local hardwoods and handwoven textiles with quiet, contemporary lines, while terraces open to birdsong and sea breeze. Days might unfold with a guided walk through native forest, a market visit alongside neighbouring cooks, or an unhurried swim. Reforestation projects and partnerships with nearby artisans ensure your stay leaves something meaningful behind.

property_title: Passalacqua: Eighteenth-Century Elegance Above Lake Como's Shores
property_intro: Set above Moltrasio in a terraced garden of citrus, roses and cypress, Passalacqua is an eighteenth-century villa where Bellini once composed and where only a handful of guests share the estate at any time. Frescoed salons, hand-blocked fabrics and family antiques feel lived-in rather than staged. Days unfold with lake swims, vineyard walks, boat outings to hidden shores and cooking with produce from the kitchen garden, all tended by local artisans and gardeners who know every terrace intimately.

property_title: Hotel Il Pellicano: Coastal Elegance on Tuscany's Argentario
property_intro: Perched above the rocks of Porto Ercole, where the Monte Argentario peninsula meets the Tyrrhenian Sea, Hotel Il Pellicano has drawn discerning guests since 1965. Ivy-clad terraces, olive groves and interiors layered with vintage photography and Italian craftsmanship set the mood, while days unfold with saltwater swims, sailing along the coast and Michelin-starred cooking rooted in local produce. Family-run and quietly loyal to its Maremma neighbours, it offers the rare pleasure of a place that has never chased fashion.

property_title: Capella Singapore: Rainforest Calm on Sentosa's Green Edge
property_intro: Tucked into 30 acres of Sentosa rainforest, Capella Singapore unfolds across restored 1880s colonial bungalows and a sweeping Norman Foster-designed curve, with peacocks wandering the lawns and the South China Sea glinting beyond. Cascading pools, a cocooning Auriga Spa and thoughtful heritage conservation set the mood, while butlers arrange forest walks and Peranakan-inspired dining. The city lies fifteen minutes away, yet here the loudest sound is birdsong drifting through the canopy.

property_title: The Inn on Biltmore Estate: Refined Living in Asheville's Hills
property_intro: Set high on a ridge within America's largest private estate, The Inn on Biltmore Estate looks across 8,000 acres of managed woodland, vineyards and pasture in North Carolina's Blue Ridge foothills. Interiors echo the Vanderbilt legacy without stuffiness, while days unfold with guided hikes, winery tastings and dinners drawing on the estate's own farm. Conservation shapes everything here, from restored forests to heritage livestock, making each stay part of a much longer story of stewardship.

property_title: Grand Hotel Fasano: Timeless Lakeside Elegance on Lake Garda
property_intro: On the western shore of Lake Garda, in Gardone Riviera, Grand Hotel Fasano occupies a former Habsburg hunting lodge wrapped in a private park of century-old cedars and palms. Family-run for generations, it pairs Belle Epoque interiors with lake-facing terraces, a garden spa and cuisine drawn from Lombard growers and local fishermen. Days unfold gently here: swimming from the private beach, sailing towards Sirmione, or watching the light shift slowly across the water.

property_name: Castello del Sole Beach Resort & SPA
property_title: Castello del Sole Beach Resort & SPA: Ascona's Lakeside Idyll
property_intro: Set between Lake Maggiore and the palm-fringed lanes of Ascona, Castello del Sole occupies a working estate of vineyards, rice paddies and organic gardens in Switzerland's sun-warmed Ticino. Produce from its own farm shapes the kitchens, while the private beach, cypress avenues and spacious spa invite unhurried days. Interiors blend Lombard elegance with contemporary calm, and generations of the same family continue to tend the land, the wine cellar and every welcome.

property_title: Vila Bled: A Presidential Lakeside Escape in Slovenia's Alps
property_intro: Set above the glassy waters of Lake Bled, this former royal summer house and Tito's presidential retreat still carries the poise of its mid-century past 	houghtful terrazzo floors, original frescoes and lakeside terraces framed by parkland. Days unfold with swims from the private jetty, pletna boat crossings to the island church, and dinners drawing on Slovenian growers and foragers. The gardens are tended without chemicals, and staff gladly share the walking trails that locals keep to themselves.

property_title: Hotel Eden Roc Ascona: Lakeside Serenity in Ticino's Sunlight
property_intro: On the shores of Lake Maggiore, where Switzerland softens into Mediterranean warmth, Hotel Eden Roc Ascona opens directly onto its own beach and marina. Palms shade the terraces, subtropical gardens scent the air, and the Alps rise beyond the water. Days drift between the lakeside spa, sailing, and dining rooms championing Ticino producers and regional wines. Interiors balance contemporary calm with local craftsmanship, while family ownership keeps the hotel closely bound to its community.

property_title: Villa d'Este: Lakeside Grandeur on the Shores of Lake Como
property_intro: On the western shore of Lake Como, Villa d'Este has welcomed guests to its Renaissance halls since 1873, though the villa itself dates to 1568. Frescoed salons, silk-draped suites and a mosaic-tiled nymphaeum open onto twenty-five acres of gardens tended by generations of Cernobbio families. Swim in the floating pool, sail beneath the mountains, or simply take an aperitivo on the Veranda as the lake turns amber at dusk.

property_title: Villa Cortene Palace: Timeless Italian Elegance Reimagined
property_intro: Set among cypress-lined avenues and centuries-old gardens, Villa Cortene Palace invites you to slow down and settle into the rhythm of the Italian countryside. Frescoed salons and restored stonework sit easily beside contemporary comforts, the result of careful conservation work with local artisans. Days unfold with vineyard walks, market visits and long lunches drawn from the estate's own kitchen garden. Evenings belong to the terrace, where the light softens and the valley falls quiet.

property_title: Le Palace De Menthon: Lakeside Serenity in the French Alps
property_intro: On the quieter eastern shore of Lake Annecy, Le Palace De Menthon looks across turquoise water to the Tournette massif, with its own beach and gardens shaded by mature trees. Belle Époque bones meet contemporary Alpine warmth in rooms that frame the view rather than compete with it. Swim before breakfast, cycle the lakeside path to Talloires, or linger over Savoyard produce from nearby growers. A place that rewards slowness, in every season.

property_title: Langdale Chase: Lakeside Grandeur on Windermere's Shore
property_intro: On the eastern shore of Windermere, Langdale Chase occupies a Victorian mansion where oak panelling, carved fireplaces and terraced gardens tumble towards the water. Rooms and lakeside suites frame views across to the Langdale Pikes, while the kitchen draws on Cumbrian growers and producers. Days might begin with a lake swim or a boat trip from the private jetty, and end beside the fire. Restored with care by local craftspeople, it remains quietly connected to its Lakeland surroundings.

property_title: Grand Hotel Tremezzo: Lake Como's Art Nouveau Grande Dame
property_intro: Facing the Bellagio peninsula across Lake Como's shimmering waters, Grand Hotel Tremezzo has welcomed guests since 1910, its Art Nouveau facade framed by camellias and centuries-old plane trees. Days unfold between the floating pool, Ruggero Caverni's terraced gardens and boat trips aboard vintage Riva launches. The kitchens celebrate Lombardy's lake fish and Alpine cheeses from small producers nearby, while the family owners continue to restore the villa's original frescoes, mosaics and heritage craftsmanship with quiet devotion.

property_title: Rosewood Schloss Fuschl: Lakeside Grandeur in the Salzkammergut
property_intro: Set on a wooded peninsula above the emerald waters of Lake Fuschl, this 15th-century castle sits just outside Salzburg, where the Salzkammergut's peaks meet centuries of Habsburg history. Restored with reverence, its vaulted rooms and hand-painted details now frame a lakeside spa, alpine-inspired dining and forest walks guided by local naturalists. Swim from the private jetty, row at dusk, or linger over produce from nearby farms and the estate's own gardens.

property_title: Park Hotel Vitznau: Lakeside Grandeur Beneath Mount Rigi
property_intro: Set on the shores of Lake Lucerne with Mount Rigi rising behind it, Park Hotel Vitznau occupies a restored 1903 palace where every suite tells a different story, from Asian antiquities to contemporary Swiss craft. Days unfold with lake swims, vineyard walks and a wine cellar holding thousands of rare vintages. The kitchen champions regional growers and lake fishermen, while the spa draws on Alpine botanicals. Arrive by steamer, and time slows considerably.

property_title: El Lodge: Timber, Snowfall and Stillness in the Sierra Nevada
property_intro: High in Spain's Sierra Nevada, where snowfields meet the light of Andalusia, El Lodge is a rare thing: a Nordic-inspired retreat of hand-cut timber and open hearths, moments from the piste. Days begin with skis clipped on at the door and end in an outdoor pool steaming beneath the peaks. Interiors layer sheepskin, stone and local craft, while the kitchen draws on Granada's growers and the mountain's own long-held traditions.

property_title: Krallerhof: Alpine Serenity Above the Meadows of Leogang
property_intro: Set on a sunlit plateau above Leogang, Krallerhof looks across the Salzburg Alps with the quiet confidence of a family estate shaped over generations. Its celebrated Atmosphere spa, designed by Hadi Teherani, draws bathers into a lake-fed pool where water meets mountain light. Days unfold with alpine hikes, saddle time at the stables and dishes built around produce from neighbouring farms. Timber, stone and glass frame the landscape, while long-standing local partnerships keep the valley's traditions thriving.

property_title: Riffelalp Resort: Alpine Serenity High Above Zermatt Village
property_intro: Perched at 2,222 metres on a sunlit terrace above Zermatt, Riffelalp Resort is reached only by cogwheel railway and a little red tram 	he ttone for the stay. The Matterhorn fills the windows; larch-clad rooms, an outdoor pool steaming at Europe's highest altitude and a chapel among the pines invite lingering. Run with real care, the house champions Valais producers, alpine craft and the fragile landscape that surrounds it.

property_title: Huka Lodge: Riverside Grace on New Zealand's Wild Waikato River
property_intro: Set among towering poplars on the banks of the Waikato, just upstream from the thundering Huka Falls, this Taupo retreat has drawn discerning guests since 1924. Suites open onto lawns and glacial-blue water, dinner is served wherever the mood takes you, and days unfold with fly fishing, forest walks or a soak beneath the stars. Native planting and long-standing conservation partnerships keep the surrounding river country as compelling as ever.

property_title: Our Habitas AlUla: Desert Living Among Ancient Sandstone
property_intro: Tucked into the Ashar Valley, where sandstone cliffs rise like weathered sculpture, Our Habitas AlUla invites you to settle into the rhythm of Saudi Arabia's desert. Low-impact villas are built from natural materials, each with a private pool framed by rock and sky. Days unfold through stargazing, guided walks to Hegra's Nabataean tombs and conversations with AlUla's makers and farmers. Local hospitality, regenerative design and genuine community partnership shape every moment of your stay here.

property_title: Six Senses Douro Valley: Vineyard Serenity in Northern Portugal
property_intro: Set within a restored 19th-century manor above the terraced slopes of the Douro, this retreat looks out over Portugal's oldest demarcated wine region. Days unfold with river swims, cellar tastings with local winemakers and long treatments in the Alchemy Bar-scented spa. Interiors pair heritage tiles with reclaimed timber, while organic gardens supply the kitchen and regenerative projects support neighbouring villages and vine growers. An invitation to slow down, taste deeply and reconnect with the land.

property_title: Royal Mansour Tamuda Bay: Mediterranean Grace in Morocco
property_intro: Set along Morocco's northern coastline, where the Rif mountains meet the Mediterranean, Royal Mansour Tamuda Bay offers a rare kind of seclusion. Villas and suites open directly onto sand, their interiors shaped by Moroccan craftsmanship — zellige tilework, carved cedar and hand-woven textiles created by artisans from nearby Tétouan. Days unfold with spa rituals, wellness journeys and slow lunches of Andalusian-influenced cuisine, while excursions into the whitewashed medina of Chefchaouen reveal a region few travellers pause to discover.

property_title: Al Zorah Beach Resort: Where Mangroves Meet the Arabian Gulf
property_intro: Tucked between tidal mangroves and a quiet stretch of Ajman shoreline, Al Zorah Beach Resort offers a gentler side of the Emirates. Flamingos wade in the lagoons at dawn, kayaks slip through green channels, and low-slung architecture keeps the focus on water and sky. Days drift between the beach, considered dining and the spa, while ongoing wetland protection and local partnerships ensure this rare coastal habitat thrives long after you leave.

property_title: Nikki Beach Resort & Spa Dubai: Barefoot Glamour by the Gulf
property_intro: Set on Pearl Jumeira with the Gulf on one side and Dubai's skyline shimmering on the other, Nikki Beach Resort & Spa Dubai brings a relaxed, sun-warmed rhythm to the city. Whitewashed interiors, palm-shaded terraces and a private beach invite slow mornings, while live music, spa rituals and Mediterranean dining fill the evenings. It's a place where design feels effortless, service is genuinely personal, and the pace is entirely yours to set.

property_title: Thuwal Private Retreat: Red Sea Seclusion on Arabia's Coast
property_intro: On the Red Sea shore north of Jeddah, Thuwal Private Retreat opens onto coral gardens, mangrove channels and dunes that shift with the light. Interiors draw on Hejazi craft, with mashrabiya screens, woven textiles and shaded courtyards cooled by sea breeze. Days unfold through reef snorkelling with marine researchers, dhow sailing at dusk and long lunches of Saudi coastal cooking. Guides from nearby fishing villages share the traditions and conservation work protecting these waters.

property_title: D Maris Bay: Five Secluded Beaches on Turkey's Wild Datça Coast
property_intro: Tucked into a pine-clad cove where the Aegean meets the Mediterranean, D Maris Bay unfolds across five private beaches on the untamed Datça Peninsula. Rooms open to the water, while sailing, diving and forest trails fill unhurried days. Dining spans Japanese, Italian and Turkish kitchens, sourcing from nearby villages and growers. Marine conservation work protects the surrounding seagrass and reefs, so every swim feels part of something quietly enduring.

property_title: Anantara Santorini Abu Dhabi Retreat: Cycladic Calm by the Gulf
property_intro: On Hudayriyat Island, minutes from the capital yet worlds away in mood, this retreat gathers whitewashed domes and cobalt shutters along a quiet stretch of Gulf shoreline. Private pool villas open to sea breezes, while cliffside dining, wellness rituals and paddleboarding at dawn shape unhurried days. Native planting and reef-friendly practices sit alongside Emirati hospitality and local artistry, so time here feels rooted in place — a Greek-island reverie with a distinctly Arabian heart.

property_title: ROHO Rosenhof Murau: Styrian Calm Amid Alpine Meadows
property_intro: Tucked into the wooded hills above Murau in Austria's upper Styria, ROHO Rosenhof reimagines a traditional farmstead as a quietly contemporary retreat. Timber, loden and local stone shape rooms that open onto meadows grazed by native cattle. Days might begin with a forest walk, a river swim in the Mur, or bread baked from regional grain. Neighbouring farmers supply the kitchen, craftspeople furnish the interiors, and evenings end beside the fire, unhurried and genuinely restorative.

property_title: Tierra Atacama: Desert Stillness Beneath the Vast Andean Skies
property_intro: Set on the edge of San Pedro de Atacama, where old corrals once stood, Tierra Atacama looks out to the Licancabur volcano across a garden reclaimed from the desert. Adobe walls, native timber and open terraces frame days spent riding through salt canyons, walking to high-altitude lagoons or floating in the pool as the sky deepens. Guides from local Atacameño families share their heritage, while solar power and careful water use keep the oasis thriving.

property_title: Pikaia Lodge: Galápagos Wilderness, Reimagined in Comfort
property_intro: Set high on an extinct volcanic crater in the highlands of Santa Cruz, Pikaia Lodge looks out across the Galápagos in every direction. Its fourteen rooms sit within a private tortoise reserve, where restored forest shelters giant tortoises that roam freely past your terrace. Days unfold aboard the lodge's own yacht, exploring outlying islands with resident naturalists, before returning to spa treatments, considered architecture and dinners that celebrate Ecuadorian produce and island conservation.

property_title: Los Cuaquenes Resort & Spa: Argentina's Wild, Serene Retreat
property_intro: Set within Argentina's untamed landscapes, Los Cuaquenes Resort & Spa invites you to slow down among native woodland, birdsong and wide, uninterrupted skies. Interiors marry local stone and timber with quiet contemporary lines, while the spa draws on regional botanicals for treatments that feel genuinely restorative. Days unfold with guided walks, horseback rides and long tables of produce grown nearby. Conservation projects and partnerships with neighbouring communities shape every stay, giving your time here lasting meaning.

property_title: Las Islas: Barefoot Elegance Among Colombia's Rosario Islands
property_intro: Reached by boat from Cartagena, Las Islas rests within the mangroves and coral gardens of the Rosario archipelago. Thatched bungalows stand on stilts above the water or nestle beneath tropical canopy, built with local craftsmanship and native timber. Days unfold with paddleboarding through mangrove channels, snorkelling over reefs and Caribbean cooking rooted in island tradition. The hotel works closely with nearby communities and marine conservation projects, ensuring your stay contributes to the archipelago's long-term protection.

property_title: Fasano Punta del Este: Where Rolling Hills Meet the Atlantic
property_intro: Set across 480 acres of pasture, lagoon and native woodland near La Barra, Fasano Punta del Este pairs Uruguay's gaucho country with the polish of a great Italian table. Isay Weinfeld's low-slung bungalows open to horizons of grazing horses and distant surf. Ride at dawn, play the Arnold Palmer course, then linger over Fasano's coastal cuisine. Reforestation and local sourcing keep the estate quietly rooted in its own remarkable landscape.

property_title: Aramness Gir: Where Asiatic Lions Roam and Gujarat Welcomes
property_intro: On the edge of Gujarat's Gir Forest, the last refuge of the Asiatic lion, Aramness gathers eighteen private houses into a village of its own. Whitewashed walls, hand-carved timber and Kathiawari craft speak of local heritage rather than imported glamour. Days begin with tracking lions alongside naturalists and end with Gujarati thalis drawn from the kitchen garden. Villagers form much of the team here, and their knowledge shapes every encounter with this remarkable landscape.

property_title: Tree of Life Sariska Manor: Aravalli Calm Beside Tiger Country
property_intro: On the fringes of Sariska Tiger Reserve, where the Aravalli hills fold into scrubland and ancient temple ruins, this restored manor holds just a handful of suites. Days unfold with jeep safaris, guided birding walks and unhurried afternoons beside the pool, while dinners draw on Rajasthani recipes and produce from nearby villages. Interiors pair heritage stonework with local craft, and the team works closely with surrounding communities on conservation and livelihoods. Quietly luxurious, genuinely rooted.

property_title: Marufukuro: Kyoto's Playful Heritage Reborn by Tadao Ando
property_intro: Tucked into Kyoto's Shimogyo district, a short stroll from the Kamo River, Marufukuro occupies the 1930s building where Nintendo once made playing cards. Tadao Ando's restoration keeps the original tiled facade and terrazzo staircases intact, pairing them with quiet concrete calm and just eighteen rooms. Guests gather for kaiseki dinners, morning tea in the courtyard and conversations with local artisans, while the neighbourhood's craft workshops and family-run shops remain very much part of the experience.

property_title: Fasano Angra dos Reis: Where Atlantic Forest Meets Quiet Seas
property_intro: Tucked into a private peninsula on Brazil's Costa Verde, Fasano Angra dos Reis looks out across a bay scattered with islands and still, jade-green water. Isay Weinfeld's architecture folds timber, stone and shade into the hillside, framing the Atlantic Forest that surrounds it. Days drift between sailing to hidden coves, forest trails with local guides, and long lunches of coastal seafood. Reforestation and marine care projects keep this fragile stretch of shoreline thriving for years to come.

property_title: Flockhill Lodge: Alpine Solitude in Canterbury's High Country
property_intro: Set within a 36,000-acre working sheep station in Canterbury's Craigieburn Valley, Flockhill Lodge is a study in quiet confidence, its four suites framing limestone tors, tussock and the Southern Alps beyond. Days unfold with fly fishing, heli-picnics, riding or simply the hush of the valley. Architecture in stone and timber echoes the landscape, while ongoing native planting and predator control ensure this remarkable high country endures for generations to come.
