property_title: Alpenresort Schwarz: Family-Run Wellness in the Tyrolean Alps
property_intro: Set above the village of Mieming, with the Mieminger Plateau unfolding towards the Alps, Alpenresort Schwarz has been shaped by the same Tyrolean family for generations. Larch-clad interiors, spring-fed pools and vast spa gardens invite unhurried days, while horse riding, mountain hikes and its own golf course draw you outdoors. Kitchens lean on produce from neighbouring farms and the resort's own gardens, and geothermal energy quietly warms the waters you'll linger in.

property_title: Golf Lodge Andreus: Fairways and Calm in the Passeier Valley
property_intro: Set among the sunlit slopes of South Tyrol's Passeier Valley, near Merano, Golf Lodge Andreus looks out over an 18-hole course framed by orchards, larch woods and the Texel mountains. Interiors pair local stone and untreated timber with quiet, contemporary lines. Days unfold with early tee times, spa hours fed by mountain water, and dinners built around produce from neighbouring farms. Walking trails begin at the door, leading deep into protected alpine parkland.

property_title: Seeleiten Lake Spa Hotel: Serene Lakeside Days in South Tyrol
property_intro: On the sun-warmed shores of Lake Caldaro, where South Tyrolean vineyards slope towards the Alps' warmest bathing lake, Seeleiten invites a slower rhythm. Rooms in larch and local stone open onto orchards, while the spa draws on lake breezes and alpine herbs. Days unfold with cycling through the vines, tastings with neighbouring winemakers and dinners built around small valley producers — a place where quiet indulgence and care for this gentle landscape sit comfortably together.

property_title: Tierra Patagonia: Wild Horizons on the Edge of Torres del Paine
property_intro: Curved low against the shoreline of Lake Sarmiento, Tierra Patagonia rises like driftwood shaped by the Patagonian wind, its weathered timber echoing the steppe beyond. Torres del Paine's granite towers fill the windows, while guides lead riding, hiking and boat journeys tailored to your pace. Local lenga wood, Chilean craftsmanship and regional produce ground the experience, and partnerships with nearby communities and conservation projects help safeguard this remarkable corner of the world.

property_title: Hotel Jökulsárlón: Where Ice, Ocean and Stillness Converge
property_intro: On the fringe of Vatnajökull National Park, Hotel Jökulsárlón sits within sight of Iceland's celebrated glacier lagoon, where centuries-old ice drifts quietly towards the Atlantic. Interiors draw on the surrounding palette of basalt, moss and glacial blue, framing vast windows that catch the northern lights in winter. Guides from nearby farming communities lead ice-cave walks and coastal wanders, while the kitchen champions produce from the region's small growers and fishermen. A refined base for those who travel attentively.

property_title: Bürgenstock Resort: Alpine Heights Above Lake Lucerne's Shore
property_intro: Perched on a limestone ridge 500 metres above Lake Lucerne, Bürgenstock Resort commands one of Switzerland's most storied views. Four hotels, a cliffside spa and an infinity pool suspended over the water sit within a private estate of meadows and forest paths, including the famous Hammetschwand lift and Felsenweg cliff walk. Interiors pair Swiss craftsmanship with restrained contemporary design, while regional producers supply the kitchens. Guests arrive by lake steamer and funicular, leaving the valley behind entirely.

property_title: Aliée: Refined Coastal Living Rooted in Turkey's Wild Beauty
property_intro: Set along Turkey's sun-warmed coast, Aliée invites you into a world where pale stone, linen and light meet the scent of wild herbs on the breeze. Days unfold slowly here: swimming in clear water, wandering olive groves with local growers, or sharing long lunches built around the day's harvest. Thoughtfully designed by regional artisans and committed to protecting the surrounding landscape, Aliée offers a stay that feels quietly generous, unhurried and genuinely of its place.

property_title: JOALI Maldives: An Immersive Art Island in Raa Atoll
property_intro: On the private island of Muravandhoo in the little-visited Raa Atoll, JOALI Maldives brings together contemporary art and barefoot ease. Commissioned installations by international artists sit among coconut palms and beach villas, while overwater retreats open onto a house reef alive with turtles. Days might unfold with coral restoration dives, a treatment inspired by island botanicals, or dinner shaped by Maldivian flavours. Local craftspeople and marine biologists give the island its quietly purposeful character.

property_title: Six Senses Rome: Eternal City Calm in an 18th-Century Palazzo
property_intro: Set within Palazzo Salviati Cesi Mellini, moments from the Trevi Fountain, this is Rome at a gentler pace. Travertine, lime plaster and reclaimed timber shape interiors that feel quietly Roman, while the subterranean bathhouse revives ancient rituals of heat, water and rest. Spend mornings with local artisans, evenings on the rooftop above Santi Apostoli. Restored with upcycled materials and Roman craftsmanship, it's a house that honours its neighbourhood as much as its guests.

property_title: Naturhotel Forsthofgut: Alpine Serenity Rooted in the Forest
property_intro: Set on the edge of Leogang's ancient spruce woods in Austria's Salzburger Land, Forsthofgut has been tended by the same family for generations. Its waldSPA draws the forest indoors — moss, larch and soft daylight — while the working farm supplies the kitchen with milk, herbs and eggs. Days unfold along barefoot trails and mountain paths, then ease into long saunas and quiet evenings beneath the Leoganger Steinberge. Refined, unhurried and genuinely rooted in the valley that shaped it.

property_title: Aman New York: Where Fifth Avenue Yields to Profound Stillness
property_intro: Set within the landmarked Crown Building at Fifth Avenue and 57th Street, Aman New York turns Midtown's energy into something unexpectedly still. Interiors by Jean-Michel Gathy layer warm timber, fireplaces and light-filled calm across residential-scale suites, while a three-storey spa, a garden terrace above Central Park and a jazz club below hold the hours. Restored historic details honour the building's 1921 origins, and every experience is quietly attentive rather than showy \u2014 a hidden refuge, moments from everything.

property_title: The Ranch at Rock Creek: Where Montana's Wild Heart Beats Softly
property_intro: Tucked into a 6,600-acre valley in western Montana, The Ranch at Rock Creek unfolds along four miles of blue-ribbon trout water, framed by the Pintler Mountains. Days here might mean fly-fishing at dawn, riding through wildflower meadows or learning to cast alongside a guide who knows every bend. Restored homesteads and timber-framed barns house interiors of quiet craft, while conservation easements and a working cattle operation keep this landscape thriving for generations to come.

property_title: The Lodge at Blue Sky: Wild Utah Luxury on 3,500 Acres
property_intro: Set across 3,500 acres of high-desert ranchland near Park City, The Lodge at Blue Sky sits where Utah's Wasatch peaks meet open sagebrush country. Just 46 rooms look out over creeks, aspen groves and rescued mustangs roaming freely. Days might involve fly-fishing, horseback riding or whiskey tasting at the on-site distillery, before dinner drawn largely from the surrounding farm. Conservation runs through everything here, from wildlife stewardship to the quiet, timber-and-glass architecture that defers to the land.

property_title: Three Forks Ranch: Refined Wilderness on the Continental Divide
property_intro: Straddling the Coloradou2013Wyoming border, Three Forks Ranch unfolds across 200,000 acres of sage flats, aspen groves and the Little Snake River. Days here might mean fly fishing private waters, riding out at first light, or unwinding in the spa after a long ramble. Interiors are quietly handsome, with stone, timber and open fires. Decades of habitat restoration have revived the river and its wildlife, so every stay supports the landscape you've come to enjoy.

property_title: Paws Up Montana: Wild Luxury on 37,000 Riverside Acres
property_intro: Spread across 37,000 acres of working ranchland in Montana's Blackfoot Valley, Paws Up pairs genuine cattle-country heritage with beautifully considered luxury. Choose a timber-framed home or a safari-style tent above the river, where wood-burning stoves and hand-crafted furnishings feel entirely at home. Days might mean fly-fishing storied waters, riding through pine forest or dining beneath the stars with a chef at the fire. The ranch protects vital wildlife corridors and champions local artisans, ensuring your stay leaves the land richer.

property_title: Casa Yati: Barefoot Luxury on Mexico's Wild Pacific Shore
property_intro: Set between jungle-clad hills and the Pacific's open horizon, Casa Yati is a private retreat where handcrafted design meets the rhythm of the tides. Local artisans shaped its palapa roofs, clay tones and open-air living spaces, while sea turtles nest on the sand below. Days unfold with ocean swims, mezcal tastings and lantern-lit dinners of regional produce. Guests support turtle conservation and nearby village initiatives simply by staying, making every moment quietly meaningful.

property_title: Casona Sforza: Vaulted Sanctuary on Oaxaca's Pacific Shore
property_intro: On a quiet stretch of Puerto Escondido's coastline, Casona Sforza rises in a rhythm of eleven brick vaults, framing the Pacific through sculpted arches. Designed by Alberto Kalach, its parota wood, lime plaster and local craftsmanship feel rooted in Oaxaca rather than imposed upon it. Eleven rooms invite slow mornings, sea swims and mezcal at dusk, while the kitchen draws on nearby farms and fishermen. Barefoot, unhurried, quietly considered.

property_title: Kymaia: Barefoot Luxury Where Jungle Meets the Caribbean Sea
property_intro: Tucked between dense Yucatán jungle and a quiet stretch of Mexican coastline, Kymaia invites you to slow down and listen. Suites of pale limestone, hand-woven textiles and local hardwood open onto gardens alive with birdsong, while cenote swims, guided reef snorkelling and long, unhurried breakfasts fill the days. Regenerative practices and partnerships with nearby Maya communities shape everything here, from the kitchen's ingredients to the artisans behind each room's quietly beautiful details.

property_title: Amanpuri: Coconut Grove Serenity on Phuket's Western Shore
property_intro: Set within a coconut plantation above Pansea Beach, Amanpuri was the first Aman, and its Thai-inspired pavilions still feel remarkably at ease among the palms. Days unfold between a black-granite pool, holistic treatments drawing on Thai healing traditions, and voyages aboard the resort's fleet to the limestone islands of the Andaman. Reef restoration work and support for local schools continue quietly nearby, while sunset from the terrace remains one of Phuket's most unhurried pleasures.

property_title: Hoshinoya Fuji: Japan's Glamping Retreat Above Lake Kawaguchi
property_intro: Set within a red pine forest on a hillside above Lake Kawaguchi, Hoshinoya Fuji reframes the great outdoors as Japan's first glamping retreat. Concrete cabins with generous terraces open directly onto Mount Fuji, while days unfold around morning canoeing, forest walks and venison slowly cooked over the Cloud Terrace fire. Interiors stay deliberately spare, letting the landscape lead, and local producers shape much of what reaches the table. Arrive curious; leave attuned to the mountain's shifting moods.

property_title: Shebara Resort: Futuristic Overwater Calm on the Saudi Red Sea
property_intro: Suspended above the shallows of Sheybarah Island, this collection of mirrored stainless-steel orbs reflects the Red Sea's shifting light, appearing almost weightless against turquoise water. Reached by boat or seaplane, Shebara sits within a protected archipelago where coral gardens, turtles and dugongs thrive. Days unfold with reef dives, dhow sailing and Hejazi-inspired dining, while the resort runs on solar power with a strict no-waste ethos, and local guides share the region's stories....b Then, silence returns.

property_title: Here Maldives: Island Serenity, Reef Life and Barefoot Luxury
property_intro: Set within a quiet corner of the Maldives, Here Maldives unfolds across powdered sand and shallow turquoise lagoons, where villas open directly onto the water. Interiors draw on natural timber, woven textures and soft daylight, creating a sense of calm that lingers. Days pass snorkelling coral gardens with resident marine guides, dining on catch landed by local fishermen, or simply drifting. Reef restoration and island partnerships give every stay a quiet, lasting purpose.

property_title: Castel Badia: A Dolomite Castle Where Centuries Still Speak
property_intro: Perched above the Val Pusteria in South Tyrol, Castel Badia occupies a former Benedictine abbey whose vaulted halls have watched over these valleys for a thousand years. Stone archways and timber-lined rooms open onto orchards, meadows and the pale peaks of the Dolomites beyond. Days here unfold slowly: alpine walks, cycling along the Rienza, hearty Tyrolean cooking and local wines. Careful restoration has preserved the castle's frescoes and character, keeping village craftsmanship and traditions firmly at its heart.

property_title: Zannier Île de Bendor: A Mediterranean Island Reimagined
property_intro: Just moments from Bandol on the Provençal coast, this private island has long attracted artists and dreamers. Zannier Île de Bendor honours that spirit, weaving Mediterranean craftsmanship and Paul Ricard's original vision into interiors that feel unhurried and quietly considered. Days unfold around sheltered coves, vineyard tastings, sailing and the island's revived artisan workshops. Native planting, careful restoration and partnerships with local producers ensure Bendor's character endures for those who arrive after you.

property_title: Hoshinoya Taketomi Island: Where Coral Sands Meet Slow Living
property_intro: On a tiny coral island in Japan's Yaeyama archipelago, Hoshinoya Taketomi Island unfolds as a village of its own \u2\u2014 low red-tiled roofs, sand-strewn lanes and gardens shaped by island craftsmen. Days pass gently here: sanshin melodies at dusk, star-gazing from the shoreline, seasonal Ryukyuan cooking drawn from local waters. Built with island techniques and tended alongside the 350-strong community, it invites you to move at Taketomi's unhurried, deeply rooted pace.

property_title: KAI Tamatsukuri: Beauty Waters, Myths and Craft in Ancient Izumo
property_intro: Set along the Tamayu River in Shimane, KAI Tamatsukuri draws on the spirit of Izumo, land of Japan's oldest myths. Silky hot-spring waters, prized for centuries, flow into baths framed by cedar and stone, while interiors echo the region's magatama bead-making and Yakumo-nuri lacquer. Days unfold with kagura dance performances, Lake Shinji sunsets and seasonal seafood from local waters. Artisan partnerships keep age-old crafts alive, giving every stay a quietly rooted sense of place.

property_title: Rakudo An: A Restored Machiya Retreat in Timeless Japan
property_intro: Tucked along a quiet lane where lantern light pools on old stone, Rakudo An invites you into a lovingly restored machiya where centuries-old timber, washi paper and tatami set a gentle rhythm. Days unfold with tea poured by hand, garden views framed like scrolls, and conversations with local artisans whose crafts keep regional traditions alive. Each careful restoration detail honours the building's past, offering an intimate, considered stay for travellers who value substance over spectacle.

property_title: Hôtel Hermitage Monte-Carlo: Belle Époque Grace Above the Sea
property_intro: Perched above Port Hercule, Hôtel Hermitage Monte-Carlo has welcomed guests since 1900, its Belle Époque façades and Gustave Eiffel-designed glass dome setting a tone of unhurried elegance. Rooms open to balconies above the Mediterranean, while the Thermes Marins spa and Michelin-starred dining invite slow, considered days. Recognised for its sustainability commitments, the hotel champions local producers and low-impact operations, proving that heritage grandeur and mindful hospitality can share the same address on the Riviera.

property_title: Grand Park Hotel Rovinj: Adriatic Elegance Above the Old Town
property_intro: Terraced into a pine-clad hillside above Rovinj's marina, this Istrian retreat looks across the water to a huddle of terracotta rooftops and the bell tower of St Euphemia. Interiors echo the coast in stone, oak and glass, while rooftop pools, an expansive spa and Adriatic tasting menus invite lingering. Days unfold cycling through Zlatni Rt forest park, foraging truffles inland, or meeting the winemakers and fishermen whose craft shapes every plate.

property_title: Windjammer Landing: Hillside Villas Above Saint Lucia's Sea
property_intro: Draped across a green hillside above Labrelotte Bay on Saint Lucia's north-west coast, Windjammer Landing gathers whitewashed villas and terracotta roofs among flowering gardens and sea grape. Days unfold between four beaches, cliffside dining and pools that seem to spill towards the Caribbean. Snorkel over reefs, learn Creole cookery from local chefs, or venture south to the Pitons. Longstanding partnerships with island schools and growers keep the resort rooted in its community and coastline.

property_title: The Legian Seminyak: Beachfront Grace on Bali's Golden Coast
property_intro: Set along Seminyak's sweeping stretch of sand, The Legian Seminyak looks out across the Indian Ocean from a quiet enclave moments from Bali's most inventive kitchens and boutiques. Airy suites in teak and rattan open to sea breezes, while the tiered pool seems to spill towards the surf. Days unfold with Balinese-inspired spa rituals, market-led dining and evenings coloured by sunset. Local artisans and long-standing island partnerships keep the experience genuinely, generously Balinese.

property_title: Paradisus Los Cabos: Desert Serenity Where Two Seas Meet
property_intro: Set along the golden shoreline between San José del Cabo and Cabo San Lucas, Paradisus Los Cabos rests where the Sonoran Desert slips into the Sea of Cortez. Cactus gardens frame open-air lounges, while candlelit dinners unfold beside the water. Days drift between reef snorkelling, agave tastings and long spa afternoons. The resort nurtures its coastline through sea turtle release programmes and works closely with Baja growers, chefs and artisans whose craft shapes every stay.

property_title: The Chedi Katara Hotel & Resort: Serenity on Doha's Coastline
property_intro: Set within Doha's Katara Cultural Village, this beachfront retreat sits between amphitheatres, galleries and mosques, with the Arabian Gulf just beyond the terrace. Interiors blend Qatari craftsmanship with the understated Asian calm The Chedi is known for, while palm-shaded courtyards invite unhurried afternoons. Days might begin with a hammam ritual, drift into dhow sailing, then close over mezze beneath the stars. Local artisans, musicians and chefs shape the experience, keeping Qatari heritage vividly present throughout your stay.

property_title: Vila Vita Parc: Algarve Clifftops, Gardens and Ocean Serenity
property_intro: Perched above the ochre cliffs of Porches, Vila Vita Parc unfolds across subtropical gardens where cobbled lanes lead to whitewashed suites, private villas and hidden terraces above the Atlantic. Days drift between vineyard tastings, Michelin-starred dinners and quiet swims in coves below. Much of what reaches the table comes from the estate's own farm in the Alentejo, while the resort's foundation supports local children and families \u2014 a rare depth beneath the Algarve's easy warmth.

property_title: Principe Forte dei Marmi: Tuscan Coast Elegance and Ease
property_intro: Set between the Apuan Alps and the Versilia shoreline, Principe Forte dei Marmi brings a quiet confidence to Tuscany's most storied stretch of coast. Interiors of Carrara marble and warm walnut nod to local craftsmanship, while the rooftop pool looks towards the marble quarries that shaped Michelangelo. Days drift from spa rituals and seasonal Tuscan cooking to cycling through pinewoods, with the hotel's beach club moments from the sand.

property_title: The Phoenicia: Timeless Grandeur at Valletta's Ancient Gates
property_intro: Standing just beyond Valletta's fortified City Gate, The Phoenicia has welcomed guests since 1947, its Art Deco interiors and seven acres of terraced gardens overlooking Marsamxett Harbour. Gardeners here nurture heritage Maltese plants, while the kitchen draws on island growers and fishermen. Days might begin with coffee among the bougainvillea, drift through the infinity pool carved into the bastion walls, and end with Baroque architecture and limestone lanes waiting a short stroll from your door.

property_title: Princes' Palace Resort: Refined Coastal Living in Turkey
property_intro: Set along Turkey's sun-warmed shoreline, Princes' Palace Resort draws on Ottoman craftsmanship and Aegean light, where hand-carved detail meets cool stone and sea breezes. Days unfold slowly here: hammam rituals, boat trips to quiet coves, and long tables of produce grown by neighbouring farmers. Local artisans shape much of what you touch, from ceramics to woven textiles, while careful water and energy practices protect the coastline. An address for travellers who value substance as much as beauty.

property_title: Asia Gardens Hotel & Thai Spa: Asian Serenity on the Costa Blanca
property_intro: Tucked into the hills of Benidorm's Sierra Cortina, Asia Gardens feels worlds away from the Mediterranean coastline shimmering below. Tropical gardens, lotus ponds and colonial-Asian pavilions frame seven pools and a Thai spa where therapists trained in Bangkok work with time-honoured techniques. Days unfold slowly here: sunrise tai chi, Michelin-calibre Asian-Mediterranean cooking, botanical trails alive with birdsong. Native planting and careful water stewardship keep this lush retreat rooted in its Alicante surroundings.

property_title: The Chedi Lu\u0161tica Bay: Adriatic Calm on Montenegro's Coast
property_intro: Set on a quiet Adriatic peninsula near Tivat, The Chedi Lu\u0161tica Bay looks out across the marina towards limestone hills and open sea. Asian-inspired interiors meet Montenegrin stone and timber, creating rooms that feel grounded rather than showy. Days unfold between the seawater pool, the Peter Harradine-designed golf course and boat trips into hidden coves. The kitchen leans on Bay of Kotor fishermen and nearby farms, while the wider Lu\u0161tica development champions native planting and local craft.

property_title: Crillon-le-Brave: A Provençal Hilltop Village Reawakened
property_intro: Perched on a rocky spur beneath Mont Ventoux, Crillon-le-Brave occupies a cluster of restored stone houses that together form the heart of a medieval Provençal village. Rooms open onto vineyards, lavender fields and terracotta rooftops, while gardens tumble down the hillside towards a pool with far-reaching views. Dine on produce from the kitchen garden and neighbouring farms, cycle the Ventoux foothills, or simply linger over rosé as the valley softens into dusk.

property_title: Domaine de Primard: A Riverside Reverie in France's Eure Valley
property_intro: An hour from Paris, this 18th-century estate unfolds along the banks of the Eure, where wild gardens, ancient trees and meadows recall the light that once drew Monet to nearby Giverny. Rooms feel lived-in rather than staged, with antiques, linen and quiet views. Days pass tending the organic potager, swimming in the river pool, or dining on produce grown steps from the kitchen. Beekeeping, biodiverse planting and local craftsmanship shape everything here.

property_title: Stok Palace Heritage Hotel: Living Royalty in the Indus Valley
property_intro: Set in the Indus Valley just beyond Leh, Stok Palace remains the residence of Ladakh's royal family — and a rare chance to sleep within living heritage. A handful of rooms, once part of the household, retain hand-painted woodwork, thangkas and heirloom furnishings, with the Stok Kangri massif framed in every window. Days unfold through monastery walks, village trails and conversations over butter tea, while the palace museum and its custodians safeguard Ladakhi craft, cuisine and Buddhist tradition.

property_title: Leopard Safaris Yala Campsite: Wild Nights Under Sri Lanka's Stars
property_intro: On the fringes of Yala National Park, Leopard Safaris pitches its elegant canvas beneath spreading palu trees, where leopards pad through the scrub and elephants drift past at dusk. Ten spacious tents blend colonial-era campaigning style with hot bucket showers and lantern-lit dinners around the fire. Guided by naturalists who know these plains intimately, days unfold in open jeeps and quiet observation. The camp leaves no permanent trace, employing local teams and supporting Sri Lanka's ongoing leopard research.

property_title: Wa Ale Private Island Resort: Myanmar's Wild Marine Sanctuary
property_intro: Set within the Lampi Marine National Park, Wa Ale sits among the seldom-visited islands of Myanmar's Myeik Archipelago, where jungle-clad hills meet empty beaches and turtles return each season to nest. Just a handful of tented villas and treetop retreats, crafted from reclaimed timber, open to the Andaman Sea. Days pass kayaking mangrove creeks, diving untouched reefs or joining rangers on patrol, with resort proceeds funding conservation and neighbouring Moken communities.

property_title: Sela Chiang Mai: Northern Thai Serenity Among Rice Fields
property_intro: Tucked into the countryside beyond Chiang Mai's old walls, Sela is a quiet retreat where teak, terracotta and handwoven textiles echo Lanna craft traditions. Days unfold slowly here: barefoot breakfasts overlooking rice paddies, temple visits with local guides, cookery lessons shaped by the morning market. The gardens are tended organically, and much of the team hails from surrounding villages, their knowledge woven into every stay. Come evening, cicadas and distant mountains make conversation feel unhurried.

property_title: Bamboo Nest @ Sanggadee: Rice Fields, Hills and Slow Living
property_intro: Tucked into the hills beyond Chiang Rai's town centre, Bamboo Nest @ Sanggadee sits amid terraced rice fields and forest, where mornings begin with birdsong and mist. Handbuilt bamboo huts, open to valley views, are lit softly at night and warmed by shared meals of Lahu and Northern Thai cooking. Days unfold with hill walks, village visits and time with local farmers, in a place shaped by community partnership and a genuinely light footprint.

property_title: Aava Resort & Spa: Barefoot Serenity on Khanom's Quiet Shore
property_intro: On the Gulf of Thailand's little-visited Khanom coast, Aava Resort & Spa unfolds along a soft sweep of sand where pink dolphins surface offshore and evenings pass without a single beach vendor. Rooms open to gardens and sea breezes, spa treatments draw on local herbs, and the kitchen sources from nearby fishermen and growers. Kayak the shallows, cycle to village markets, or simply let Khanom's unhurried rhythm settle into your days.

property_title: 500Rai Floating Resort: Waking Slowly on Khao Sok's Lake
property_intro: Moored on the jade stillness of Cheow Lan Lake, deep within Khao Sok National Park, 500Rai drifts beneath limestone karsts far older than the rainforest around them. Timber villas open straight onto the water, where mornings begin with mist, hornbills and a swim before breakfast. Guided kayak journeys and ranger-led jungle walks reveal the park's quieter corners, while solar power, plastic-free practices and local hiring help keep this remarkable valley thriving.

property_title: Paresa Resort: Cliffside Serenity Above Phuket's Andaman Sea
property_intro: Perched on the dramatic cliffs of Kamala on Phuket's west coast, Paresa Resort seems suspended between jungle and sea. Private pool villas open to sweeping Andaman views, their contemporary Thai design shaped by natural stone, timber and light. Days unfold with cliff-edge dining, spa rituals drawing on local traditions, and quiet swims high above the shore. The resort works closely with nearby communities and protects the surrounding headland, so every stay leaves something behind.

property_title: Ambong Ambong: A Rainforest Hideaway Above Langkawi's Shore
property_intro: Tucked into the forested hillside above Pantai Tengah, Ambong Ambong is a collection of just a dozen villas built around Langkawi's ancient trees rather than through them. Hornbills and dusky langurs pass by at breakfast; the Andaman Sea glitters beyond the canopy. Days unfold slowly here, with jungle walks, mangrove excursions and spa treatments drawing on local botanicals. Architecture in timber and stone honours the terrain, while the family owners quietly champion island conservation.

property_title: Cove 55: Rainforest, Shoreline and Slow Days in Teluk Bahang
property_intro: Tucked into a fishing village on Penang's north-western tip, Cove 55 sits where jungle-clad hills lean towards the Andaman Sea. Just fifteen suites, shaped from timber, stone and sea breeze, look out over a quiet stretch of shore beside Penang National Park. Days unfold with rainforest walks, turtle-watching at Pantai Kerachut and dishes drawn from village gardens and nearby waters. Local hands built and now run it, keeping Teluk Bahang's rhythms gently, genuinely intact.

property_title: Borneo Rainforest Lodge: Wild Luxury in Ancient Danum Valley
property_intro: Deep within Sabah's Danum Valley Conservation Area, one of the world's oldest rainforests, this lodge sits beside the Danum River amid 130 million years of unbroken wilderness. Timber chalets with open-air bathtubs and private verandahs invite you to listen for gibbons at first light. Walk the canopy bridge, swim beneath waterfalls and track orangutans with resident naturalists, many from nearby communities, whose research and conservation work keeps this extraordinary forest standing.

property_title: MesaStila: Volcano Views and Colonial Charm in Java's Highlands
property_intro: Cradled by eight volcanoes in the highlands of Central Java, MesaStila unfolds across a working coffee plantation, where antique Javanese joglo houses have been carefully rebuilt as private villas. Days might begin with a barefoot walk through the coffee rows, followed by treatments in a converted colonial train station spa. Harvests are picked by neighbouring villagers, guests join the roasting, and the estate's forest planting quietly restores the surrounding hillsides for generations to come.

property_title: Tugu Lombok: Art, Ocean and Old Java on Sire Beach
property_intro: On the quiet sands of Sire Beach, with Mount Rinjani rising behind and the Gili Islands shimmering offshore, Tugu Lombok is part hotel, part living museum. Antique Javanese pavilions, restored temple carvings and centuries-old artefacts fill the grounds, gathered by a collector devoted to Indonesia's heritage. Days drift between candlelit dinners on the shore, Sasak village visits, healing rituals and coral restoration outings, all shaped by local craftspeople and the families who have long called this coast home.

property_title: Papua Paradise Eco Resort: Raja Ampat's Overwater Sanctuary
property_intro: On the tiny island of Birie, at the northern edge of Raja Ampat, Papua Paradise Eco Resort places you above some of the richest reefs on the planet. Timber overwater bungalows open onto turquoise shallows where dugongs graze and wobbegong sharks rest beneath the jetty. Days unfold with dives among coral gardens, treks to spot Wilson's birds-of-paradise, and dinners shared with Papuan hosts whose villages the resort supports through employment and reef protection.

property_title: Silolona Cruise: Sailing Indonesia's Wild Waters in Timber Grace
property_intro: Hand-built from ironwood in the tradition of Sulawesi's seafaring Bugis, Silolona glides between Raja Ampat's coral gardens, Komodo's dragon-guarded shores and the remote Banda Islands. Days unfold with reef dives, village visits and quiet anchorages found only by those who know these waters. Antique textiles and teak interiors give the vessel a collector's warmth, while long-standing partnerships with island communities and marine conservationists ensure your wake leaves something worthwhile behind.

property_title: Slow Villas and Spa: Unhurried Days in Bali's Green Heart
property_intro: Set among Canggu's rice terraces, Slow Villas and Spa invites you to trade the rush for something gentler. Handcrafted timber, local stone and open pavilions frame private pools and gardens where geckos outnumber guests. Days might unfold with yoga at sunrise, a herbal massage drawn from Balinese tradition, or a slow cycle to the coast. The kitchen sources from nearby farmers, while the villas' Javanese artistry supports craftspeople whose skills deserve keeping alive.

property_title: Satri House: Heritage Charm and Quiet Luxury in Luang Prabang
property_intro: Once the residence of Prince Souphanouvong, Satri House sits within strolling distance of Luang Prabang's temples, night market and the slow-moving Mekong. Frangipani-shaded courtyards, lotus ponds and two saltwater pools frame interiors layered with Lao textiles, Indochinese antiques and locally crafted furniture. Days might begin with alms-giving at dawn, then unfold into cookery lessons, weaving visits or riverside excursions. The team is largely local, and guests are gently encouraged to explore the town's living crafts traditions.

property_title: Riverside Boutique Resort: Nam Song Serenity in Vang Vieng, Laos
property_intro: Set along the languid Nam Song in Vang Vieng, this intimate retreat looks out to limestone karsts that shift colour through the day. Interiors draw on Lao and Luang Prabang craft traditions, with handwoven textiles and locally made furnishings throughout. Days might begin with a sunrise kayak, a cookery lesson using produce from nearby gardens, or a cycle through rice fields. The resort employs and trains villagers from the surrounding valley, keeping benefits close to home.

property_title: Heritage Suites Hotel: Colonial Grace in the Heart of Siem Reap
property_intro: Tucked behind the frangipani-shaded lanes of Siem Reap's Wat Polanka quarter, Heritage Suites Hotel offers a quieter counterpoint to the temples that draw travellers here. French colonial architecture meets Khmer craftsmanship across garden villas with private steam rooms, while cuisine celebrates Cambodian produce and local growers. Monks pass by at dawn, Angkor waits minutes away, and the hotel's long-standing commitment to Cambodian training and employment gives every stay a deeper resonance.

property_title: Knai Bang Chatt Resort: Seaside Serenity on Kep's Quiet Coast
property_intro: On the sleepy shoreline of Kep, where the Gulf of Thailand meets pepper farms and jungle-clad hills, Knai Bang Chatt occupies a cluster of restored 1960s villas built in Cambodia's celebrated New Khmer Architecture style. Days unfold slowly here: sailing traditional Hobie cats, cycling to the crab market, or lingering over pepper-laced seafood. The resort trains and employs local villagers, supports nearby schools and champions Kep's modernist heritage, making every stay quietly meaningful.

property_title: Topas Ecolodge: Mountain Serenity Above Sapa's Rice Valleys
property_intro: Perched on two granite hilltops deep in the Hoang Lien mountains, Topas Ecolodge looks out across terraced rice valleys and Red Dao villages far below Sapa. White stone bungalows open onto private balconies where mist drifts through at dawn. Days unfold with guided treks to hill-tribe hamlets, cookery lessons and swims in an infinity pool suspended above the valley. Solar power, local employment and community schooling projects keep this remarkable place rooted in the landscape it celebrates.

property_title: Mekong Princess Cruise: Timeless Voyages Along Cambodia's River
property_intro: Gliding between Phnom Penh and the temple-strewn reaches of northern Cambodia, the Mekong Princess carries just twelve guests along one of Asia's great waterways. Teak-lined suites open onto the river, while days unfold at the pace of the current: silk-weaving villages, sunrise alms-giving, freshwater dolphins near Kratie. Crewed almost entirely by Cambodians, the vessel supports local artisans and schools along its route, turning each journey into something quietly meaningful.

property_title: L'Alya Ninh Van Bay Resort: Barefoot Calm on Vietnam's Coast
property_intro: Reached only by boat across Ninh Van Bay, L'Alya sits where granite boulders meet a quiet crescent of sand, framed by the forested slopes of the Hon Heo peninsula. Timber villas, thatched roofs and open-air bathrooms echo Vietnamese craft traditions, while days unfold with reef snorkelling, herb-garden cookery lessons and hillside yoga. The resort works closely with neighbouring fishing villages and supports marine conservation, so your stay quietly gives something back to this remarkable stretch of coast.

property_title: The Island Lodge: Serene Mekong Days on Vietnam's Unicorn Isle
property_intro: Moored on the Mekong's Unicorn Island, The Island Lodge is a French colonial-style villa where twelve rooms open to river breezes, frangipani gardens and a pool facing the water. Days drift by sampan through coconut groves and fruit orchards, with cooking sessions built around produce from neighbouring smallholdings. The owners work closely with local families, employing islanders and sourcing regionally, so your stay quietly supports the community whose rhythms shape this remarkably unhurried corner of the delta.

property_title: P'apiu Resort: Highland Serenity in Vietnam's Ha Giang Hills
property_intro: Tucked into the terraced valleys of Ha Giang, P'apiu Resort sits where rivers curl between limestone peaks and Dao and Tay villages farm the slopes as they have for generations. Its villas draw on local craft traditions, with hand-woven textiles, timber and stone shaped by artisans from nearby hamlets. Days unfold slowly here: foraging with village cooks, cycling past rice paddies, soaking in herbal baths. A place that gives back to the community that shaped it.

property_title: Jing's Residence: A Qing Dynasty Courtyard Reborn in Pingyao
property_intro: Within the ancient walls of Pingyao, one of China's best-preserved walled cities, a 260-year-old silk merchant's mansion has been coaxed back to life. Jing's Residence pairs weathered grey brick and carved timber with restrained contemporary design, its five courtyards unfolding around quiet gardens. Just 19 rooms mean unhurried days: Shanxi cuisine reimagined by the kitchen, lantern-lit lanes at dusk, artisans and local craftspeople met through the hotel's own guided walks. Heritage here feels lived-in, not staged.

property_title: Rakkojae Seoul: A Hanok Sanctuary Amid Bukchon's Quiet Lanes
property_intro: Tucked into the narrow lanes of Bukchon, where tiled rooftops meet the slopes of Bugaksan, Rakkojae Seoul occupies a lovingly restored hanok more than a century old. Timber beams, hand-papered doors and a courtyard garden frame days of tea ceremonies, calligraphy and evenings in the earthen kiln sauna. Its careful revival helped safeguard Seoul's vanishing wooden houses, and the hosts still share neighbourhood stories over breakfast, drawing you into the rhythm of a living quarter.

property_name: Puri Ganesha Homes by the Beach
property_title: Puri Ganesha Homes by the Beach: Bali's Quiet Northern Shore
property_intro: On the black-sand shoreline of Pemuteran, in Bali's gentle north-west, Puri Ganesha Homes offers just four antique-filled villas set within tropical gardens, each with its own pool and open-air living. Days drift between snorkelling the coral gardens of Menjangan, cooking with produce from the kitchen garden, and walking to the village temple. The owners have long championed reef restoration and local schooling, so your stay quietly supports the community that shaped it.

property_title: Gangga Island Resort & Spa: Barefoot Luxury in North Sulawesi
property_intro: Set on a small island off North Sulawesi, Gangga Island Resort & Spa opens onto white sand, warm shallows and the coral-rich waters of Bangka and Bunaken. Thatched timber bungalows sit among frangipani and coconut palms, furnished with Indonesian craftsmanship and cooled by sea breezes. Days drift between dive briefings, spa rituals and village visits, while reef monitoring and local employment keep the resort closely tied to the community that surrounds it.

property_title: Koh Jum Beach Villas: Barefoot Elegance on a Quiet Thai Isle
property_intro: Set between the Andaman Sea and jungle-clad hills, Koh Jum Beach Villas occupies a car-free island where fishing boats still outnumber visitors. Handcrafted wooden villas, shaded by coconut palms, open onto a three-kilometre stretch of sand. Swim, kayak through mangroves or share a meal with local families in the nearby village. Solar power, rainwater harvesting and long-standing partnerships with island communities underpin every detail, making this a stay that gives quietly back.

property_title: Baba Ecolodge: Barefoot Luxury Rooted in Thailand's Wild Beauty
property_intro: Tucked between tropical forest and quiet water, Baba Ecolodge invites you to slow down and pay attention. Timber pavilions, open-air bathrooms and locally woven textiles reflect a design language shaped by the landscape rather than imposed upon it. Days unfold with kayaking through mangroves, foraging with local cooks, or simply reading in a hammock as hornbills pass overhead. The lodge works closely with neighbouring villages, employing and training residents while funding reforestation across the surrounding hillsides.

property_title: Madulkelle Tea and Eco Lodge: Where the Knuckles Mountains Rise
property_intro: Set high on a working tea estate near Kandy, Madulkelle Tea and Eco Lodge looks out across the Knuckles Mountain Range, a UNESCO-listed wilderness of cloud forest and terraced slopes. Canvas suites stand on stilts among the bushes, each framing the valley through wide verandah doors. Days unfold with tea plucking alongside estate workers, guided walks to hidden waterfalls and Ayurvedic treatments. Solar power, spring water and local employment keep the lodge quietly rooted in its hillside community.

property_title: The Governor's Residence: Yangon's Teak-Shaded Colonial Grace
property_intro: Set within Yangon's leafy embassy quarter, this 1920s teak mansion was once home to a Shan State governor. Ceiling fans turn slowly above polished floorboards, lotus ponds mirror the verandas, and the palm-fringed pool invites long afternoons with a book. Dine on Burmese classics reimagined by local chefs, learn to fold lacquerware or wander to the Shwedagon Pagoda at dusk. Artisan partnerships and staff training keep Myanmar's craft traditions and hospitality heritage thriving.

property_title: Khla Lodge: Wild Cardamom Seclusion in Cambodia's Green Heart
property_intro: Tucked into the forested folds of Cambodia's Cardamom Mountains, Khla Lodge offers a rare kind of quiet. Handsome timber tents open onto river and canopy, where gibbons call at first light and rangers share the day's tracking notes over breakfast. Days unfold with jungle treks, kayaking through mangrove channels and conversations with the communities safeguarding this wilderness. Design is understated and locally crafted, and every stay directly funds forest protection and Khmer livelihoods.

property_title: House of MG: Ahmedabad's Heritage Mansion Reimagined with Soul
property_intro: In the heart of Ahmedabad, this 1920s family mansion opens its carved doors onto a city of textile merchants, stepwells and Gandhi's Sabarmati Ashram. Restored by descendants of its original owners, House of MG keeps craft alive through its in-house weaving and embroidery workshops, while Agashiye serves Gujarati thalis on the rooftop beneath the stars. Join a dawn heritage walk through the walled city, then return to shaded courtyards and quiet, antique-filled rooms.

property_title: Dolkhar Ladakh: Himalayan Heritage Reimagined in Leh Valley
property_intro: Tucked among barley fields and apricot orchards on the edge of Leh, Dolkhar is a family-run retreat where Ladakhi craftsmanship shapes every detail, from hand-carved timber to mud-brick walls that hold the mountain warmth. Eight villas open onto the Stok Kangri range, while the kitchen revives regional recipes using produce grown nearby. Days unfold with monastery walks, textile studios and conversations with local artisans, all part of a livelihood-led approach that keeps Ladakh's traditions thriving.

property_title: Residence Bassac Boutique Hotel: Champasak's Riverside Grace
property_intro: Set beside the Mekong in Pakse, Residence Bassac blends French colonial proportions with Lao craftsmanship, from handwoven textiles to locally milled timber. Mornings begin with Bolaven coffee on the terrace before excursions to Wat Phou, waterfalls and the coffee plantations that shape southern Laos. The kitchen sources from Champasak growers, and staff are recruited and trained locally. Return each evening to quiet courtyards, a shaded pool and river light softening the rooftops.

property_title: The Blackbuck Lodge: Grassland Serenity on Velavadar's Edge
property_intro: On the fringes of Velavadar's rippling grasslands in Gujarat, The Blackbuck Lodge offers a quiet vantage point over one of India's most singular landscapes. Cottages are shaded by native trees, with plunge pools and wide verandahs made for slow afternoons. Days unfold with guided drives in search of blackbuck, wolves and harriers, followed by regional Kathiawadi cooking. Solar power, local employment and close ties with nearby villages keep the lodge rooted in its surroundings.

property_title: House of Tugu: Where Indonesia's Living Heritage Welcomes You
property_intro: Set among the shifting light and sea air of Indonesia, House of Tugu is less a hotel than a private collection you can sleep inside. Antique doors, temple carvings and Javanese portraits fill rooms rescued from vanishing eras, each piece safeguarded rather than merely displayed. Days unfold with candlelit royal dinners, jamu-making rituals and conversations with local artisans whose crafts endure here. For travellers drawn to culture with substance, this is heritage held gently, and generously shared.

property_title: Ahsa Farm Stay: Slow Days Among Thailand's Rice Fields
property_intro: Set among working rice paddies and fruit orchards, Ahsa Farm Stay invites you to settle into the rhythms of rural Thailand. Timber-framed villas open onto water and sky, furnished with local craftsmanship and quiet restraint. Days unfold gently: harvesting vegetables at dawn, learning regional recipes from neighbouring cooks, cycling lanes lined with lotus ponds. The farm champions organic growing and shares its earnings with the surrounding village, so every stay strengthens the community that shapes it.

property_title: The Siam: Art Deco Elegance on Bangkok's Riverside Edge
property_intro: Tucked along a quiet stretch of the Chao Phraya in Bangkok's historic Dusit district, The Siam feels like a private world of monochrome Art Deco, antiques and shaded courtyards. Bill Bensley's design frames three-storey pool villas, a Thai boxing ring and a riverside spa drawing on traditional remedies. Days might begin with market foraging, then Muay Thai or ceramics with local artisans, before slow boat rides past temples the tour crowds rarely reach.

property_title: Reverie Siam: Jazz-Age Romance on the Banks of the Pai River
property_intro: Tucked into a quiet bend of the Pai River in Thailand's mountainous north, Reverie Siam channels the elegance of 1920s Siam through hand-painted tiles, vintage portraits and gardens heavy with frangipani. Days drift between the saltwater pool, riverside spa treatments and slow cycles into Pai's morning market. The family-run team sources from neighbouring farms and supports local artisans, so every detail carries the character of the valley that surrounds you.

property_title: Le Chanthou Boutique Hotel: Siem Reap's Quiet Sanctuary
property_intro: Tucked down a leafy lane moments from Siem Reap's temple road, Le Chanthou Boutique Hotel welcomes guests into a house shaped by Khmer craftsmanship, with hand-woven textiles, timber detailing and a courtyard pool shaded by frangipani. Days begin with fruit from nearby markets and unfold towards Angkor at first light or the artisans' workshops the hotel proudly supports. Staff, largely from surrounding villages, share their Cambodia with genuine, unhurried generosity that lingers long after departure.

property_name: Athita The Hidden Court Boutique Hotel
property_title: Athita The Hidden Court Boutique Hotel: Lanna Grace in Chiang Saen
property_intro: Tucked along the Mekong in ancient Chiang Saen, Athita The Hidden Court occupies a quiet corner of Thailand's far north, where Lanna temples and river traffic set the rhythm of the day. Teak details, handwoven textiles and shaded courtyards reflect craftsmanship from nearby villages, while the kitchen draws on northern recipes and local growers. Cycle to riverside ruins, wander the morning market, or simply watch the water drift towards Laos.

property_title: Villa Song: Riverside Serenity a Sampan Ride from Saigon's Heart
property_intro: Set along the Saigon River in leafy Thao Dien, Villa Song is an Indochine-style retreat of just 23 rooms, where ceiling fans turn slowly above polished timber and frangipani leans towards the water. Glide into the city centre by private sampan, swim beneath tamarind shade, or linger over Vietnamese classics made with produce from nearby growers. The team champions local artisans and river-friendly practices, giving this quietly elegant villa a genuine sense of place.

property_title: Vocabolo Moscatelli: A Restored Umbrian Retreat by the Tiber
property_intro: Set among the oak woods and olive terraces of the upper Tiber Valley, Vocabolo Moscatelli occupies a 13th-century monastery brought gently back to life. Stone vaults meet contemporary craftsmanship, wood-fired cooking and wines from small Umbrian growers. Days unfold with truffle hunts, river walks and slow afternoons by the pool, while the surrounding land is farmed with care and local artisans shape much of what you touch, taste and take home.

property_title: Cap Karoso: Sumba's Wild Coast, Reimagined with Creative Soul
property_intro: On the untamed south-western tip of Sumba, Cap Karoso sits between rice terraces and a broad Indian Ocean beach, where fishing villages still set the rhythm of the day. Two swimming pools, a working farm and a rotating cast of guest chefs anchor a stay that feels part retreat, part creative residency. Interiors blend Sumbanese craft with mid-century calm, while local hiring, ikat weaving partnerships and regenerative growing keep the island's culture firmly at the centre.

property_title: Ultima Gstaad: Alpine Seclusion in the Heart of the Saanenland
property_intro: Tucked into the meadows above Gstaad, Ultima looks out across the Saanenland's timbered chalets and snow-dusted peaks. Suites and private chalets pair blackened wood with open fires, deep soaking tubs and spa rituals shaped around mountain botanicals. Ski straight to the door in winter, then trade skis for hiking boots and cheese-dairy visits come summer. Local artisans, alpine farmers and regional producers underpin the kitchen, making each stay feel quietly rooted in its valley.

property_title: Singita Ebony Lodge: Timeless Safari Elegance in the Sabi Sand
property_intro: Set beneath ancient ebony trees on the banks of the Sand River, Singita Ebony Lodge sits within South Africa's Sabi Sand Reserve, where leopards move through dappled shade and elephants drift down to drink. Twelve suites blend colonial-era romance with contemporary craft, each opening to uninterrupted bushveld views. Days unfold with expert-led game drives, walking safaris and slow afternoons by the pool, while every stay supports Singita's century-long conservation commitment and its neighbouring community partnerships.

property_title: 1 Hotel South Beach: Barefoot Luxury Along Miami's Shoreline
property_intro: Set along a quiet stretch of Collins Avenue, 1 Hotel South Beach turns its back on Miami's glitz in favour of reclaimed driftwood, living greenery and light that pours through every corner. Four pools, a rooftop overlooking the Atlantic and a beach club invite slow days, while filtered water taps, hemp bedding and sea-turtle-friendly lighting reveal a deeper commitment. Step outside and Ocean Drive, Española Way and the dunes are moments away.

property_title: The Brando: Barefoot Luxury on a Private Tetiaroa Atoll
property_intro: On Tetiaroa, the coral atoll Marlon Brando fell for in the 1960s, thirty-five villas rest beneath coconut palms on a private islet north of Tahiti. Days unfold between turquoise lagoon and lush motu, where seabirds nest and green turtles come ashore to lay. Run on solar power and seawater air-conditioning, the resort funds a working research station, so time spent snorkelling, paddling or dining on Polynesian-French cuisine directly supports the atoll's future.

property_title: Equinox Hotel New York: Where Rest Becomes an Art Form
property_intro: Rising above Hudson Yards on Manhattan's revitalised west side, Equinox Hotel New York treats sleep, movement and recovery as the true luxuries. Blackout suites, circadian lighting and cooled bedding are designed for genuine restoration, while a three-storey wellness club, 60-metre pool and Spanish-inspired dining by Electric Lemon await below. The High Line unfurls just outside, and the Hudson glitters beyond floor-to-ceiling glass. Come for the city; leave feeling remarkably, unexpectedly restored.

property_name: The Lodge & Spa at Brush Creek Ranch
property_title: The Lodge & Spa at Brush Creek Ranch: Wyoming's Wild Grandeur
property_intro: Set across 30,000 acres of Wyoming's Medicine Bow foothills, this working cattle ranch pairs saddle-worn authenticity with quietly considered comfort. Days unfold on horseback, casting into spring creeks or climbing into aspen groves; evenings belong to the spa, a crackling hearth and beef raised on the land itself. Interiors of weathered timber and hide feel rooted rather than staged, while ongoing habitat restoration and ranch apprenticeships ensure the valley thrives long after your departure.

property_title: Canouan Estate Resort & Villas: Grenadines Seclusion Redefined
property_intro: Set along the powder-soft shores of Godahl Beach on Canouan, this Grenadine hideaway unfolds across 1,200 acres of hillside, reef and lagoon. Villas and suites in warm coral stone open to trade winds and turquoise horizons, while days drift between sailing, diving the protected barrier reef and dining on island-grown produce. The estate works closely with Canouan's community, supporting local livelihoods and marine conservation, so your stay quietly gives something back.

property_name: Hotel La Vigne by Onko Chishin
property_title: Hotel La Vigne by Onko Chishin: Vineyard Living in Japan
property_intro: Set among the gentle slopes of Japan's wine country, Hotel La Vigne by Onko Chishin invites you to slow down among rows of vines and quiet mountain air. Interiors pair restrained craftsmanship with locally sourced materials, while the kitchen draws on neighbouring farms and cellars. Days might unfold with tastings led by growers, walks through orchards, or simply the pleasure of an unhurried breakfast. It's a stay rooted in place, community and the rhythm of the harvest.

property_title: Eleven Martín Pescador Lodge: Where Patagonia's Rivers Run Wild
property_intro: Tucked between glacial peaks and the turquoise waters of northern Chilean Patagonia, Eleven Martín Pescador Lodge is a fly-fisher's sanctuary with a wider soul. Days unfold on spring creeks and remote rivers, or on horseback and hiking trails through temperate rainforest, before returning to interiors of warm timber, local textiles and long, convivial dinners. Guides are Patagonian born and bred, and the lodge works closely with neighbouring farming families to keep this valley's traditions and waterways thriving.

property_title: Amanemu: Onsen Rituals on Japan's Pearl-Diving Ise-Shima Coast
property_intro: Set above the oyster rafts and inlets of Ago Bay, within Japan's Ise-Shima National Park, Amanemu draws on mineral-rich waters from the nearby Ise Springs. Kerstin Thompson's minimalist suites and villas echo the lines of a traditional ryokan, with private onsen and cedar-scented calm. Days unfold gently: kayaking through quiet coves, meeting the region's ama free-divers, or walking pilgrim paths to Ise Jingu, Shinto's most revered shrine. Wellness here feels rooted, unhurried and quietly restorative.

property_title: Amanwana: Barefoot Seclusion on Indonesia's Moyo Island Shores
property_intro: Reached by boat across the Flores Sea, Amanwana rests on Moyo Island, a forested nature reserve off Sumbawa where deer wander between banyans and hornbills call at dusk. Canvas-roofed tents open onto sand and jungle, their teak interiors quietly luxurious. Days drift between reef dives, hidden waterfall walks and village visits, while the camp's marine conservation work protects the coral gardens and reef life offshore rom evereverything familiar.

property_title: BYAKU Narai: A Storied Sake Town Reawakened in the Kiso Valley
property_intro: Set along the old Nakasend\u014d highway, BYAKU Narai occupies a 200-year-old sake brewery and merchant houses in a post town that time has treated kindly. Behind cedar lattice and earthen walls, sixteen rooms unfold around quiet courtyards, an onsen drawn from Kiso's mountains, and dining that follows the valley's seasons. Guests brew, taste and wander with local artisans, while careful restoration sustains Narai's timber streetscape and the community who have kept it alive for four centuries.

property_title: Hoshinoya Tokyo: A Tower-Top Ryokan Above Otemachi's Streets
property_intro: Slip off your shoes at the door and the financial district falls away. Rising seventeen storeys in Otemachi, Hoshinoya Tokyo reimagines the ryokan for the city: tatami floors, lattice-screened walls and a hot-spring bath open to the Tokyo sky. Each floor gathers around a quiet lounge where tea and seasonal sweets appear unannounced. Kaiseki dinners honour small Japanese producers, while craftsmen from across the country shaped the interiors, keeping centuries-old techniques alive.

property_title: Nishimuraya Honkan: Timeless Onsen Grace in Kinosaki, Japan
property_intro: In the willow-lined streets of Kinosaki Onsen, Nishimuraya Honkan has welcomed bathers for more than 160 years. Behind its wooden facade lie tatami rooms framing camellia gardens, cypress baths fed by mineral springs, and kaiseki dinners built around Tajima beef and winter snow crab. Guests wander the town in yukata, hopping between seven public bathhouses the inn has long helped sustain, before returning to a hush that seems to belong to another century.

property_title: Gora Kadan: Imperial Serenity in the Hills of Hakone, Japan
property_intro: Once the summer retreat of Japan's imperial Kan'in family, Gora Kadan rests on wooded slopes in Hakone, where mineral-rich waters rise from the volcanic earth. Cypress-scented private onsen, tatami suites framing maple and moss, and kaiseki dining shaped by mountain and coast reveal a quieter kind of luxury. Ryokan traditions are kept alive by families who have served here for generations, while forest paths lead to Mount Fuji views and centuries-old shrines nearby.

property_title: Ozu Castle Stay: Become Lord of a Restored Ehime Keep
property_intro: On the banks of the Hijikawa River in western Ehime, Ozu Castle invites you to spend the night within its reconstructed wooden keep 	his you a castle is yours alone. Arriving by horseback to a welcome of drums and banners, you dine on Iyo beef and local citrus, then sleep where feudal lords once did. Guest stays directly fund the castle's upkeep and the craftsmanship of Ozu's artisans, keeping timber traditions and this quiet castle town alive.

property_title: Sala Khaoyai: Where Khao Yai's Wild Green Hills Slow the Pace
property_intro: Set among the vineyards and forested ridges bordering Khao Yai National Park, Sala Khaoyai looks out across Thailand's most storied wilderness, where hornbills glide above the tree line. Architect-designed pavilions frame the valley in glass and warm timber, drawing the landscape indoors. Days unfold with sunrise safaris, cellar tastings and produce gathered from neighbouring farms, while the resort's stewardship supports local growers and forest conservation. Evenings belong to the stars, unhurried and remarkably clear.

property_title: Cape Weligama: Clifftop Serenity on Sri Lanka's Southern Coast
property_intro: Perched on a red-earth headland high above the Indian Ocean, Cape Weligama gathers just a scattering of villas and suites across gardens and terraces on Sri Lanka's southern shore. Days unfold gently here: whale watching beyond the reef, cricket with village children, surfing lessons at nearby breaks, or long hours beside the crescent-shaped moon pool. Interiors nod to Dutch and Sinhalese craft traditions, while local hiring and marine conservation work keep the coastline, and its communities, thriving.

property_title: Six Senses Punakha: Riverside Serenity in Bhutan's Old Valley
property_intro: Set above the Mo Chhu river in Bhutan's former winter capital, Six Senses Punakha occupies a hillside of terraced rice paddies and citrus groves, with the valley's revered dzong within easy reach. The lodge borrows from traditional Bhutanese craftsmanship, its timber and rammed-earth interiors framing views towards the Himalayas. Days might involve a farmhouse lunch with a local family, archery with village teams, or a suspension-bridge walk lined with fluttering prayer flags.

property_title: Palazzo Fuiggi: Timeless Italian Elegance Awaits Your Arrival
property_intro: Set within a lovingly restored historic residence, Palazzo Fuiggi invites you to slow down amid frescoed ceilings, stone archways and sunlit courtyards scented with citrus. Days here unfold gently: mornings spent with local pastries and strong coffee, afternoons exploring nearby vineyards, hilltop villages and family-run trattorias. Artisans from the region shaped much of the interiors, while ingredients arrive from neighbouring growers. It is a place where heritage feels lived-in, hospitality feels personal, and Italy reveals itself quietly.

property_title: Borgo Santo Pietro: A Tuscan Estate Rooted in Land and Craft
property_intro: Set within 300 acres of Tuscan countryside near Chiusdino, Borgo Santo Pietro began life as a 13th-century pilgrims' rest and now unfolds as a working farm estate. Kitchen gardens, beehives and pastures supply the Michelin-starred table, while guests can gather herbs for the on-site distillery, learn to cook in the farmhouse kitchen or simply wander the gardens. Restored with genuine care, it champions regenerative farming, heritage breeds and the artisans of its valley.

property_title: Aman Tokyo: Serene Stillness Above the City's Ceaseless Rhythm
property_intro: Perched across the upper floors of the Otemachi Tower, Aman Tokyo opens onto a soaring lantern-lit atrium of washi, stone and cypress 	he scale of a temple, the hush of a private home. Below, the Imperial Palace gardens unfold; beyond, Mount Fuji on clear mornings. Days might begin with kendo or calligraphy, and close in the 30-metre pool. The tower's own woodland garden, planted with native species, brings the seasons quietly indoors.

property_title: Chem Chem Lodge: Barefoot Luxury on Tanzania's Ancient Plains
property_intro: Set within a private wildlife corridor linking Tarangire National Park with the shores of Lake Manyara, Chem Chem Lodge looks out over shimmering salt flats where elephants pass at dusk. Eight airy tented suites blend linen, timber and Swahili craftsmanship, while walking safaris with Maasai guides reveal the smaller wonders that vehicles overlook. The lodge's conservation work has restored this once-fragmented land, and its partnerships with neighbouring villages ensure your stay leaves the plains richer than you found them.

property_title: Wild Coast Tented Lodge: Where Sri Lanka's Jungle Meets Sea
property_intro: Set between the boulder-strewn shoreline of the Indian Ocean and the leopard-rich wilderness of Yala National Park, Wild Coast Tented Lodge feels quietly extraordinary. Cocoon-like suites, inspired by the shapes of nearby rocks and shaped from bamboo and canvas, open onto private plunge pools where elephants sometimes wander past. Days unfold with dawn safaris, Ayurvedic treatments and long lunches of southern Sri Lankan spice, while the lodge's low-impact build and local employment keep this coast thriving.

property_title: Erebero Hills: Where Uganda's Green Horizons Invite You In
property_intro: Set among the rolling green folds of Uganda's countryside, Erebero Hills offers a gentler pace, where mornings begin with birdsong and mist drifting across the valley. Interiors marry handcrafted local materials with quiet comfort, framing views that shift with the light. Wander forest paths, share a meal grown metres from your table, or sit with a coffee as the hills soften into dusk. Community partnerships and thoughtful land stewardship shape every detail of your stay here.

property_title: Nkasa Linyanti: Floodplain Serenity in Namibia's Zambezi Region
property_intro: On the edge of Nkasa Rupara National Park, where the Linyanti wetlands spill into reed-lined channels, this intimate camp looks out across floodplains grazed by elephant and buffalo. Raised tented suites are dressed in natural linens and timber, framing water views from your bed. Days unfold with boat safaris, guided drives and birding among more than 400 species, while partnerships with neighbouring Wuparo Conservancy ensure your stay supports the communities who safeguard this remarkable corner of Namibia.

property_title: Le Domaine de La Réserve: Barefoot Serenity on Praslin's Shore
property_intro: Tucked along the quiet north coast of Praslin, Le Domaine de La Réserve looks out across Anse Petite Cour to the granite silhouettes of Curieuse and Chauve Souris. Timber-framed villas and thatched roofs sit lightly among takamaka trees, where days drift between snorkelling over coral gardens, sailing to hidden coves and dining on line-caught fish. Family-run for generations, the estate supports island growers and marine protection, offering a stay that feels genuinely rooted in Seychellois life.

property_title: Hoanib Elephant Camp: Wild Solitude in Namibia's Kaokoveld
property_intro: Tucked into the remote Kaokoveld of north-western Namibia, Hoanib Elephant Camp sits beside a dry riverbed where desert-adapted elephants pass through in search of shade and water. Just a handful of canvas tents face the gravel plains, their interiors pared back and quietly comfortable. Days unfold with guided drives, tracking on foot and evenings under remarkably clear skies, while partnerships with local conservancies ensure Damara communities share directly in the rewards.

property_title: Anantara Kafue River Tented Camp: Wild Luxury in Zambia
property_intro: Set on the banks of the Kafue River within Zambia's largest and least-travelled national park, this intimate tented camp places you among lion, leopard and vast floodplains alive with birdsong. Canvas suites open to the water, furnished with quiet craftsmanship and locally made pieces. Days unfold through boat safaris, guided walks and evenings by the fire with skilled Zambian guides, while the camp's partnerships support anti-poaching patrols and neighbouring communities across the Kafue.

property_title: Chetzeron: A Reimagined Gondola Station High Above Crans-Montana
property_intro: At 2,112 metres above Crans-Montana, Chetzeron began life as a gondola station and now welcomes guests into raw stone, larch and glass framing the Valais peaks. Arrive by snowcat, ski or mountain track, then settle into slow days of alpine walks, spa hours and cooking rooted in local producers. Solar power, careful stewardship of the terrain and long-standing ties to the valley's artisans shape a stay that feels both rarefied and genuinely grounded.

property_title: Santre Dolomythic Home: Alpine Myth in the Heart of Dolomites
property_intro: Tucked into the Val di Fiemme, Santre Dolomythic Home draws its character from the legends and forests of the Dolomites. Rooms are dressed in local spruce, wool and stone, crafted by Trentino artisans, while windows frame the pale peaks beyond. Days unfold with mountain walks, alpine wellness rituals and slow dinners built around valley producers. It is a house that listens to its landscape ye invited to do the same.

property_title: Eco Hotel Saltus: Alpine Calm, Crafted with Conscience
property_intro: Tucked into the wooded slopes of northern Italy, Eco Hotel Saltus draws its character from the surrounding forest: local timber, stone and wool shape interiors that feel warm rather than showy. Days unfold slowly here, with mountain walks, seasonal menus built around neighbouring farms and evenings in a sauna scented with pine. Low-impact energy, careful sourcing and long-standing ties to village artisans mean your stay quietly supports the valley that makes it possible.

property_title: Hotellerie de Mascognaz: Alpine Hamlet Reborn in Aosta Valley
property_intro: Tucked into a car-free hamlet above Champoluc, in the shadow of Monte Rosa, Hotellerie de Mascognaz occupies a cluster of Walser farmhouses lovingly rebuilt using local larch, stone and slate. Days unfold slowly here: forest walks, ski trails from the door, thermal baths fed by mountain water, and dishes shaped by Valdostana producers. Restoration work has revived centuries-old building traditions and village life, making every night's stay part of a quietly remarkable preservation story.

property_name: Serras Andorra Luxury Boutique Resort & Spa
property_title: Serras Andorra Luxury Boutique Resort & Spa: Pyrenean Serenity
property_intro: Tucked into the Pyrenean valleys of Andorra, Serras Andorra Luxury Boutique Resort & Spa pairs alpine calm with quietly confident design. Stone, timber and light frame views of forested slopes, while thermal waters and mountain-sourced treatments restore after days spent walking, skiing or exploring Romanesque hamlets nearby. The kitchen leans on Andorran growers and cheesemakers, and local guides share the valley's traditions first-hand. It is a place to slow down, breathe deeply and rediscover mountain hospitality at its most genuine.

property_title: HUUS Gstaad Hotel: Alpine Adventure in the Saanenland Valley
property_intro: Perched above the meadows of Saanen, HUUS Gstaad looks out across the Saanenland valley to peaks that shift from summer green to deep winter white. Interiors blend warm local timber with playful, contemporary touches, while the in-house guides lead guests ski touring, climbing and fat-biking through terrain most visitors never see. Complimentary activities, family-friendly spaces and close ties with Bernese Oberland farmers and craftspeople make this a mountain retreat with genuine character and roots.

property_title: Singita Sabora: Tented Luxury on the Serengeti's Grumeti Plains
property_intro: Set within the Grumeti Reserve on Tanzania's western Serengeti, Singita Sabora is a tented camp with a rare sense of ease. Canvas walls open onto plains crossed by wildebeest and zebra, while interiors blend Persian rugs, brass and pared-back linen. Days unfold through guided game drives, walking safaris and quiet hours by the pool. Every stay supports the Grumeti Fund's anti-poaching work and community education, so your time here leaves the wilderness stronger.

property_title: Dar Ahlam: A Dreamlike Kasbah in Skoura's Ancient Palm Grove
property_intro: Hidden within the palm groves of Skoura, between the High Atlas and the Sahara, Dar Ahlam occupies a restored 19th-century kasbah where days unfold without a printed schedule. Candlelit dinners appear in walled gardens, hammams are drawn at dusk, and journeys lead to Berber villages, rose valleys and dune camps. Interiors by Patrick Jouin marry Moroccan craft with quiet modernity, while the house works closely with local artisans, growers and families nearby.

property_title: J.K. Place Capri: Island Elegance Above the Marina Grande
property_intro: Perched above Marina Grande, J.K. Place Capri looks out across the Bay of Naples from a whitewashed villa that feels more like the home of a well-travelled friend than a hotel. Interiors layer antique mirrors, linen and local craftsmanship with an easy, unfussy confidence. Days drift between the saltwater pool, boat trips to hidden sea caves and long lunches of Campanian produce, before the island's evening quiet settles and Vesuvius fades into dusk.

property_title: Sol y Luna: A Sacred Valley Sanctuary Rooted in Community
property_intro: Set among eucalyptus groves and maize fields near Urubamba, Sol y Luna sits at the heart of Peru's Sacred Valley, framed by the peaks of the Andes. Casitas painted by Peruvian artists open onto gardens where Paso horses graze nearby. Guests ride, hike Inca trails or dine on produce grown metres from the table. Profits support the on-site Sol y Luna school, educating hundreds of children from surrounding Quechua villages.

property_title: Quercus: Where Ancient Oaks Shelter a Slower Kind of Luxury
property_intro: Sheltered among centuries-old oaks, Quercus is a retreat where architecture defers to the landscape rather than competing with it. Timber, stone and generous glass frame the shifting light, while days unfold at the pace you choose: foraging walks, long lunches sourced from neighbouring growers, evenings beneath undimmed stars. The surrounding woodland is actively restored and stewarded with local conservationists, so every stay quietly supports the habitat you have come to admire. Thoughtful, unhurried and genuinely rooted in place.

property_name: The Inn at Rancho Santa Fe
property_title: The Inn at Rancho Santa Fe: Eucalyptus-Shaded Californian Calm
property_intro: Tucked beneath towering eucalyptus in one of Southern California's most discreet villages, The Inn at Rancho Santa Fe has welcomed guests since 1924. Twenty acres of gardens, citrus groves and croquet lawns surround hacienda-style cottages dressed in warm woods and locally made ceramics. Days drift between the heated pool, garden-to-table dining and long walks on the village trails, with the beaches of Del Mar twenty minutes away. Its roots in the community run deep — a local institution, still delightfully unhurried.

property_title: Cataloochee Ranch: Mile-High Mountain Living in Maggie Valley
property_intro: Perched a mile high on the edge of Great Smoky Mountains National Park, Cataloochee Ranch has welcomed riders and wanderers to its North Carolina meadows since the 1930s. Hand-hewn cabins and a thoughtfully revived lodge look out across ridgelines that fade into blue, while horses graze on pastures grazed for generations. Days unfold with trail rides, fly fishing and Appalachian suppers sourced nearby, and the ranch's conservation easements ensure these highlands remain wild for those who follow.

property_title: Alisal Ranch: Where California's Working West Still Breathes
property_intro: Tucked into the oak-studded hills of California's Santa Ynez Valley, Alisal Ranch has been a working cattle ranch since the 1800s \u2013 and still is. Days here unfold on horseback across 10,000 acres, with fly-fishing on a private lake, open-air suppers and evenings by the fire in adobe-walled cottages. Regenerative grazing and land stewardship shape every acre, while the kitchen draws on the ranch's own herd and the valley's growers. Wi-Fi is scarce; conversation is not.

property_title: Lone Mountain Ranch: Montana Wilderness, Timeless Ranch Soul
property_intro: Tucked into 148 acres of meadow and lodgepole pine in Big Sky, Montana, Lone Mountain Ranch has welcomed guests since 1915. Historic log cabins, warmed by wood stoves and quiet craftsmanship, sit within easy reach of Yellowstone's northern wonders. Days unfold with fly fishing, horseback rides and Nordic trails groomed through snowbound forest, before dinners drawn from regional producers. A long-standing commitment to land stewardship keeps this valley wild for those who follow.

property_title: Six Senses Southern Dunes: Desert Wonder on the Red Sea Coast
property_intro: Set among golden dunes and ancient Nabataean trade routes inland from Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast, Six Senses Southern Dunes draws its design language from Hegra's carved stone and Bedouin craft. Villas open to vast skies ideal for stargazing, while days unfold with horse riding, desert foraging and treatments rooted in Arabian wellness traditions. Local artisans shape much of what you see, and native planting and dune restoration quietly safeguard this remarkable landscape for generations to come.

property_title: Amankora: A Journey Through Bhutan's Sacred Valleys and Peaks
property_intro: Amankora unfolds across five valleys in the Bhutanese Himalaya, each lodge a quiet composition of rammed earth, timber and firelight framing dzongs, pine forests and terraced fields. Travel between them by road, threading mountain passes and monasteries, with monks' blessings, archery lessons and hot-stone baths along the way. Interiors are restrained and warm, drawing on local craftsmanship, while community farms, artisans and heritage projects shape each stay. This is Bhutan encountered slowly, valley by valley.

property_title: Ultima Hotel Courchevel: Alpine Seclusion Above the Slopes
property_intro: Perched above Courchevel 1550 with the Trois Vall\u00e9es unfolding below, Ultima Hotel Courchevel offers just a handful of private chalets, each with its own spa, pool and dedicated staff. Interiors pair reclaimed alpine timber with contemporary calm, while ski-in access, guided off-piste descents and dining shaped around Savoyard producers root the stay in its surroundings. Evenings belong to firelight and falling snow \u2014 the kind of quiet luxury that lingers long after departure.

property_title: Ultima Corfu: Ionian Serenity Above the Cypress-Clad Coast
property_intro: Set among olive groves and cypress on Corfu's north-eastern shore, Ultima Corfu looks out across the Ionian towards the mountains of Albania. Villas and suites are shaped from local stone and timber, with private pools, sea-facing terraces and interiors that favour craftsmanship over show. Days unfold with boat trips to hidden coves, wine tastings with island producers and dinners built around Corfiot recipes. Local artisans and growers are woven into everyday life here, quietly and genuinely.
