property_title: Santani Wellness Kandy: A Mindful Retreat in Sri Lanka's Hills
property_intro: Set across 48 acres of regenerated forest and former tea land above Kandy, Santani rests where mountain air, birdsong and a natural spring-fed stream set the rhythm of the day. Minimalist chalets open to valley views, while Ayurveda, yoga and personalised wellness programmes are guided by resident doctors. Solar power, rainwater harvesting and locally sourced kitchens reflect a quiet commitment to the land and the surrounding villages. Come for stillness; leave recalibrated, unhurried and genuinely restored.

property_title: Banyan Tree Mayakoba: Serene Lagoon Life on the Riviera Maya
property_intro: Threaded through freshwater lagoons and mangrove channels south of Playa del Carmen, Banyan Tree Mayakoba feels pleasingly hidden. Thatched villas open onto private pools, reached by boat or bicycle along water-lined pathways where herons fish at dawn. Days drift between Thai-inspired spa rituals, cenote swims and Mayan cookery lessons, while the resort's marine and mangrove conservation work protects the ecosystem you're floating through. Evenings bring candlelit dinners above the water, unhurried and quietly memorable.

property_title: Casa Palop\u00f3: Colour, Craft and Volcano Views in Guatemala
property_intro: Perched on a hillside above Lake Atitl\u00e1n, Casa Palop\u00f3 looks out across still water to three volcanoes and the Mayan villages that ring the shore. Interiors layer hand-painted tiles, local textiles and bold pigment, while terraces invite long afternoons with a book. Days might mean paddling at dawn, weaving with Tz'utujil artisans or hiking to a coffee finca. The house supports village schools and lakeshore conservation, so your stay leaves something behind.

property_title: Casa de Sierra Nevada: Colonial Charm in San Miguel de Allende
property_intro: Set across a cluster of restored 16th-century mansions in the heart of San Miguel de Allende, Casa de Sierra Nevada unfolds through cobbled lanes, hidden courtyards and rooftops framed by the Parroquia's pink spires. Rooms reveal hand-carved beams, local textiles and antique tilework, while the cookery school celebrates Mexican heritage with market visits and family recipes. Artisans from surrounding villages supply much of the craftsmanship, keeping centuries-old techniques alive within these walls.

property_title: Nayara Gardens: Where Arenal's Rainforest Meets Quiet Luxury
property_intro: Set on a hillside facing the Arenal Volcano, Nayara Gardens unfolds within regenerated rainforest that sloths, toucans and tree frogs now call home. Casitas built from tropical hardwoods open onto private plunge pools and volcanic hot-spring terraces, while candlelit dinners follow the day's harvest from local farms. Spend mornings tracking wildlife with resident naturalists, afternoons in the treetop spa, evenings watching mist gather over the summit. A rare place where indulgence and restoration grow side by side.

property_title: Soori Bali: Black Sand Shores and Rice Terraces in Tabanan
property_intro: On Bali's south-western coast, Soori sits where volcanic black sand meets terraced rice fields and the peaks of Tabanan. Architect Soo K. Chan's design frames the landscape in local stone and timber, with private pools opening to the Indian Ocean. Days unfold with temple visits, village walks and cooking sessions led by neighbouring farmers, while the resort's partnerships support local schools, artisans and reef care along this quietly untouched shoreline.

property_title: Katikies Chromata: Caldera Serenity Carved into Santorini
property_intro: Cut into the caldera cliffs of Imerovigli, Katikies Chromata looks out across the volcano and the Aegean's shifting blues. Whitewashed suites follow the contours of the rock, with cave-cool interiors, private plunge pools and terraces angled towards Santorini's long, unhurried sunsets. Days drift between Cycladic cooking rooted in island produce, wine tastings from Assyrtiko vineyards nearby, and quiet swims. It is a place shaped by local craft, where hospitality feels personal rather than performed.

property_title: Constance Lemuria: Praslin's Turtle Shores and Granite Coves
property_intro: On Praslin's north-western shore, Constance Lemuria unfolds across three beaches, including Anse Georgette, reached through groves of coco de mer palms. Villas and suites sit low among the granite boulders, shaded and quietly composed. Days might mean the archipelago's only 18-hole course, Creole cooking with island growers, or dawn on the sand as hawksbill hatchlings emerge, watched over by the resort's long-running turtle conservation team.

property_title: Hotel Royal-Riviera: Belle Époque Grace on Cap Ferrat's Shore
property_intro: Set between Beaulieu-sur-Mer and the pines of Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat, Hotel Royal-Riviera looks out across a private beach and a Mediterranean that shifts from turquoise to ink. Behind its 1904 façade, interiors balance Belle Époque proportions with quiet contemporary calm, while the Orangerie garden shelters olive and citrus trees tended without chemicals. Days drift from sea-water swims to Provençal menus built on local catch and market produce, then coastal walks along the Sentier du Littoral.

property_title: Floating Leaf Eco Retreat: Bali's Quiet Coast and Rice Fields
property_intro: Tucked between rice terraces and the black-sand shore of Bali's south coast, Floating Leaf Eco Retreat offers a gentler rhythm of island life. Bamboo pavilions and open-air suites look out over water gardens, while days unfold through yoga, temple visits, cooking with village families and snorkelling off Nusa Penida. The retreat champions permaculture, reef restoration and local livelihoods, so your stay quietly supports the community whose traditions shape every meal, ceremony and conversation here.

property_title: Le Sereno Hotel: Barefoot Elegance on Grand Cul-de-Sac Beach
property_intro: Set along the calm turquoise lagoon of Grand Cul-de-Sac, Le Sereno feels like a private stretch of St Barth's shoreline. Christian Liaigre's pared-back interiors let sea light, teak and linen do the talking, while villas open straight onto warm sand. Days drift between paddleboarding over protected reef, Italian-inspired dining at Al Mare and treatments scented with island botanicals. The team works closely with local producers and marine conservationists, keeping this shimmering bay as beautiful as they found it.

property_title: AREV St. Tropez: Refined Riviera Living Beside the Vineyards
property_intro: Tucked between the vineyards of the Var and the shimmer of the Gulf of Saint-Tropez, AREV offers a quieter interpretation of Riviera life. Pared-back interiors in stone, linen and pale wood open onto gardens scented with rosemary and pine, while the village's harbour and markets sit within easy reach. Days unfold slowly here: swimming, cycling coastal lanes, tasting Provencal rose from neighbouring estates. Local artisans shape much of what you'll see, touch and taste.

property_title: ESPACIO The Jewel of Waikiki: Oceanfront Living, Perfected
property_intro: Rising above Waikiki's golden shoreline, ESPACIO The Jewel of Waikiki offers just nine residences, each occupying an entire floor with sweeping Pacific views, a private terrace and an outdoor onsen. Honolulu's beaches, surf breaks and Diamond Head sit moments away, yet the atmosphere here is quietly personal: a dedicated concierge, in-residence dining and Miyako Hotels' Japanese sense of hospitality. Interiors blend Italian craftsmanship with island light, while local artisans and producers shape much of what you taste and see.

property_title: Hotel Villa Dubrovnik: Adriatic Serenity Beneath Old Town Walls
property_intro: Tucked into the cliffs east of Dubrovnik's Old Town, this cascading villa faces Lokrum island across water that shifts from turquoise to indigo. Terraces of stone, glass and pale timber step down to a private bathing platform, while the hotel's boat glides guests to the city walls in minutes. Dine on Dalmatian seafood and estate olive oil, retreat to the cliffside spa, and let unhurried afternoons on the Adriatic set the rhythm of your stay.

property_name: La Casa de la Playa Xcaret
property_title: La Casa de la Playa Xcaret: Riviera Maya's Quiet Luxury
property_intro: Set along a sheltered stretch of Riviera Maya shoreline, La Casa de la Playa Xcaret holds just a handful of suites, each opening to the Caribbean. Mexican artisans shaped its interiors, from hand-carved stone to woven textiles, while chefs draw on Yucatecan traditions across intimate dining rooms. Guests roam Xcaret's parks, swim in cenotes and learn about the marine turtle and coral programmes that quietly define this coast's conservation story.

property_title: Bill & Coo Mykonos: Refined Cycladic Calm Above Megali Ammos
property_intro: Perched on a gentle slope above Megali Ammos Bay, Bill & Coo looks out across the Aegean towards Mykonos Town, close enough for evening strolls through its lanes yet pleasingly removed from the bustle. Whitewashed lines, local stone and handcrafted detail set the tone, while the adults-only pool, candlelit dinners and Greek wines invite unhurried days. The kitchen champions small Cycladic producers, and thoughtful water and energy practices reflect a genuine respect for the island.

property_title: Birkenhead House: Whale-Watching Luxury on Wild Hermanus Cliffs
property_intro: Perched on a rocky headland above Walker Bay, Birkenhead House looks out over water where southern right whales gather each winter within earshot of your terrace. Inside, eleven individually styled rooms layer bold art, antiques and deep comfort, while Hermanus's fynbos-clad mountains and celebrated wine valleys wait beyond the gate. Days unfold with shark cage diving, cliff-path walks and cellar visits, and the house supports local schools and conservation projects along this remarkable coastline.

property_title: The Silo Hotel: Cape Town's Art-Filled Heights Above the Bay
property_intro: Rising above the V&A Waterfront in a converted grain silo, The Silo Hotel crowns Zeitz MOCAA, Africa's museum of contemporary art. Faceted pillowed windows frame Table Mountain, the harbour and the Atlantic beyond, while interiors by Liz Biden layer colour, texture and commissioned African works. Days might begin with a rooftop swim and end with wine chosen by a resident sommelier. Downstairs, the museum champions artists from across the continent and its diaspora.

property_title: Emerald Maldives Resort & Spa: Barefoot Elegance in Raa Atoll
property_intro: Set within a UNESCO-listed biosphere reserve in the Raa Atoll, Emerald Maldives Resort & Spa unfolds across a lush island fringed by house reef and lagoon. Beach and overwater villas draw on natural timber and soft light, while eight dining venues range from teppanyaki to Mediterranean. Guests snorkel with manta rays, join the resident marine biologist in coral restoration, or simply drift between spa treatments and the hush of the Indian Ocean.

property_title: Montage Healdsburg: Vineyard Serenity in Sonoma's Hillsides
property_intro: Set across 258 rolling acres above the Russian River Valley, Montage Healdsburg unfolds among oak woodlands and a working Chardonnay vineyard. Bungalow guestrooms step down the hillside, their timber and glass framing long views over Sonoma's ridgelines. Days might mean tasting with winemakers, foraging with the resident chef, or walking trails through restored native habitat. Regenerative farming, wildlife corridors and close ties with local growers shape the experience here, making indulgence feel quietly grounded in place.

property_title: Dunton Hot Springs: A Restored Ghost Town in the Colorado Rockies
property_intro: Tucked into a high valley beneath Colorado's San Juan Mountains, Dunton Hot Springs is a 19th-century mining settlement carefully brought back to life. Hand-hewn log cabins conceal deep baths, wood stoves and quietly considered interiors, while geothermal springs steam beside the Dolores River. Days unfold with heli-skiing, fly-fishing, horseback rides and long lunches at the old saloon. Land conservation, regenerative ranching and close ties with the local community underpin every stay here.

property_title: Wildflower Farms: Hudson Valley Meadows Below the Gunks Ridge
property_intro: Set across 140 acres of meadow, orchard and working farmland in Gardiner, New York, Wildflower Farms unfolds beneath the dramatic cliffs of the Shawangunk Ridge. Timber-clad cottages open onto wildflower fields, while the kitchen draws from the resort's own gardens and apiary. Days might mean foraging walks, cold-water plunges, stargazing or simply an afternoon spent beside the fire. Regenerative farming practices and long-standing Hudson Valley partnerships give this quiet corner of the countryside genuine depth.

property_name: Under Canvas Lake Powell – Grand Staircase
property_title: Under Canvas Lake Powell – Grand Staircase: Desert Stargazing
property_intro: Set on a high plateau between Lake Powell's blue coves and the layered cliffs of Grand Staircase-Escalante, this camp places you in one of Utah's least-crowded corners. Safari-inspired tents open onto slickrock and sagebrush, with wood stoves, hand-pumped showers and no screens to distract from an International Dark Sky Park overhead. Days bring slot canyon hikes and boat trips; evenings, live music and s'mores. Solar power, low-impact design and water conservation keep the desert as you found it.

property_title: Clear Sky Resorts Grand Canyon: Nights Beneath Arizona Stars
property_intro: Set on the high desert plateau near the Grand Canyon's South Rim, Clear Sky Resorts invites you to sleep beneath one of the darkest skies in the United States. Geodesic sky domes frame the constellations from your bed, while thoughtful design keeps the surrounding pinyon and juniper undisturbed. Days unfold with canyon hikes and astronomy sessions led by resident guides; evenings belong to firelight, silence and the slow turning of the Milky Way overhead.

property_title: Wharekauhau Country Estate: Wild Coast, Working Sheep Station
property_intro: Set on a 3,000-acre working sheep station above Palliser Bay, Wharekauhau looks out across windswept coastline to the Kaikōura ranges beyond. Guests wake in Edwardian-inspired cottages, ride horses through native bush, help with mustering, or fish the Wairarapa rivers before dining on estate-reared lamb and Martinborough wines. Ongoing native replanting and wetland restoration sit alongside the farming rhythm here, making this rare corner of New Zealand feel both grandly comfortable and genuinely lived-in.

property_title: The Lindis Lodge: Architectural Sanctuary in the Ahuriri Valley
property_intro: Set within a working high-country station in the Ahuriri Valley, The Lindis rises from the tussock like a sculpted ridgeline, its curved timber roof framing mountains, braided river and vast Central Otago sky. Just five suites, a handful of alpine pods, and days shaped by fly fishing, riding, stargazing and quiet walks. Native planting and predator control restore the valley, while the kitchen draws on Otago growers and the lodge's own garden.

property_title: Mt Cook Lakeside Retreat: Alpine Serenity on Lake Pukaki
property_intro: On the turquoise shore of Lake Pukaki, with Aoraki/Mt Cook rising beyond, this intimate retreat occupies a working high-country estate in New Zealand's Mackenzie Basin. Stone and timber villas frame the peaks, while days unfold with private guiding, heli-picnics on glaciers and stargazing beneath the world's largest dark sky reserve. Native plantings, predator control and long-standing ties to local runholders keep the landscape as compelling as the comforts within.

property_title: Awasi Atacama: Private Journeys Through Chile's High Desert
property_intro: Tucked into the adobe village of San Pedro de Atacama, Awasi pairs fourteen private villas with something rare: your own guide and 4x4, so each day unfolds entirely on your terms. Wander salt flats at dawn, share a table with Likan Antai neighbours, or simply linger by your plunge pool beneath the clearest skies on earth. Built with local stone, wood and thatch, the lodge supports Atacameño families and desert conservation across the surrounding altiplano.

property_title: Kwessi Dunes: Stargazing and Solitude in the NamibRand Reserve
property_intro: Set where russet dunes meet the shadowed peaks of the Nubib Mountains, Kwessi Dunes sits deep within Namibia's NamibRand Nature Reserve, one of Africa's largest private conservation areas. Ten low-slung chalets, shaped in earth tones and canvas, each conceal a star bed for nights beneath one of the world's darkest skies. Days unfold with guided desert walks, oryx sightings and dune drives, while your stay directly funds reserve conservation and local school programmes.

property_title: Wilderness Little Kulala: Desert Dreaming Beneath Sossusvlei Skies
property_intro: On the private Kulala Reserve, moments from the towering dunes of Sossusvlei, Wilderness Little Kulala sits within one of the oldest deserts on earth. Eleven light-filled suites open onto plunge pools and rooftop skybeds made for stargazing beneath famously clear Namib skies. Days unfold with dune walks, quad trails, hot-air balloon flights and encounters with oryx and gemsbok. Solar-powered and closely involved with local conservation, it protects ancient ephemeral riverbeds and supports neighbouring communities.

property_title: Aman Venice: Tiepolo Frescoes and Gardens on the Grand Canal
property_intro: Set within a 16th-century palazzo on the Grand Canal, Aman Venice pairs Tiepolo frescoes and gilded salons with the calm restraint Aman is known for. Two private gardens, rare in this city, offer shade and birdsong just beyond the water traffic. Restoration here has been painstaking, safeguarding centuries of Venetian craftsmanship. Slip out by boat with a curator, dine beneath original stuccowork, then return to silk-lined rooms where the canal light does the rest.

property_title: 7132 Hotel: Thermal Springs and Alpine Artistry in Timeless Vals
property_intro: Tucked into a narrow valley in Graub\u00fcnden, 7132 Hotel rises where quartzite peaks meet the murmur of mountain water. Peter Zumthor's celebrated thermal baths sit at its heart, while guest rooms shaped by Kengo Kuma, Tadao Ando and Thom Mayne reward slow appreciation. Days unfold between candlelit stone pools, alpine hikes and dishes drawn from the surrounding valley, whose community has long safeguarded this village and the springs that sustain it.

property_title: Therasia Resort: Aeolian Horizons on Vulcano's Wild Shoreline
property_intro: Perched on a lava-black headland on Vulcano, Therasia Resort looks across the Tyrrhenian towards Lipari and the smoking cone of Stromboli. Rooms in muted volcanic tones open to terraces where the only soundtrack is the sea. Days drift between thermal-inspired spa rituals, boat trips to hidden coves and dinner at Michelin-starred Il Cappero, where Aeolian capers, island-grown herbs and small-boat fish tell the archipelago's story. A quietly considered retreat that gives back to the community sustaining it.

property_title: Hotel Esencia: Barefoot Grandeur on the Quiet Caribbean Coast
property_intro: Once the private estate of an Italian duchess, Hotel Esencia unfolds across fifty acres of jungle and gardens above the pale sands of Xpu-Ha, between Playa del Carmen and Tulum. Colonial architecture meets contemporary calm here, with sea-facing suites, a Mayan-inspired spa and cuisine drawn from nearby growers and fishers. Days pass slowly: cenote swims, reef snorkelling, tequila tastings. The team protects native flora and supports neighbouring Mayan villages, keeping this coastline authentically alive.

property_name: La Valise San Miguel de Allende
property_title: La Valise San Miguel de Allende: Colonial Charm, Quietly Kept
property_intro: Tucked behind a discreet doorway in the heart of San Miguel de Allende, La Valise offers just a handful of suites, each opening onto sunlit courtyards and rooftop views across pink stone domes. Interiors celebrate Mexican craft: hand-loomed textiles, local ceramics and antiques gathered from nearby workshops. Days unfold slowly here, with breakfast served wherever you please, mezcal tastings after dusk, and the town's galleries, markets and artisan studios a short stroll from your door.

property_title: Casa Polanco: A Refined Retreat in Mexico City's Green Heart
property_intro: Set on a leafy street in Mexico City's Polanco district, Casa Polanco occupies a lovingly restored 1940s mansion moments from Chapultepec Park and the Museo Nacional de Antropolog	textscia. Ten individually designed rooms pair Mexican craftsmanship with European elegance, while breakfast on the terrace and mezcal tastings in the salon invite unhurried afternoons. Local artisans, galleries and family-run kitchens sit within walking distance, and the house champions Mexican makers throughout, from hand-woven textiles to ceramics.

property_name: Cala de Mar Resort & Spa Ixtapa
property_title: Cala de Mar Resort & Spa Ixtapa: Where the Pacific Whispers
property_intro: Carved into a cliffside above Playa Majahua, Cala de Mar looks out across the Mexican Pacific from an adults-only sanctuary of open-air suites, each with its own plunge pool and views that shift with the light. Days unfold slowly here: spa rituals drawn from local traditions, seafood plucked from nearby waters, and sunsets that draw everyone to the terrace. Beyond the resort, the Sierra Madre foothills, sea turtle releases and Zihuatanejo's fishing-village charm await discovery.

property_title: Esperanza: Clifftop Serenity on Mexico's Los Cabos Coastline
property_intro: Perched on a bluff above the Sea of Cortez, between Cabo San Lucas and San Jostheu00e9 del Cabo, Esperanza gathers its casitas among desert gardens and volcanic rock. Terraces open to whale-watching waters, while the spa's hydrotherapy ritual draws on local sea salts and clay. Days unfold with Baja wine tastings, guided marine encounters and dishes shaped by nearby fishing cooperatives and farms 	he rpeninsula's own rhythms, thoughtfully honoured.

property_title: Our Habitas Bacalar: Lagoon Living on Mexico's Seven Shades
property_intro: On the shores of Bacalar's Lagoon of Seven Colours, deep in Mexico's Quintana Roo jungle, Our Habitas Bacalar rests lightly on the land. Suites of timber, stone and woven fibre open to water the colour of raw turquoise, while ancient stromatolites quietly line the shallows. Days drift between paddleboarding at dawn, cacao ceremonies, sound journeys and long dinners drawn from Mayan kitchens. Local artisans, guides and growers shape the experience, and conservation guides every decision made here.

property_title: Eriro: An Earth Hotel in Tirol's Wild Highlands Above Ehrwald
property_intro: Perched at 1,500 metres above Ehrwald, with the Zugspitze rising close by, Eriro is a nine-room retreat built almost entirely from Tirolean stone, larch and loden. Days unfold slowly here: forest walks with the resident guide, herb gathering, saunas warmed by local timber, and a kitchen that cooks only what the surrounding valleys provide. Nothing is flown in, little is wasted, and every craftsman lived within reach \u2013 mountain hospitality, thoughtfully rewritten.

property_title: Rosewood Matakauri: Wild Lakeside Grace in Queenstown's Alps
property_intro: Tucked into a beech-clad shoreline minutes from Queenstown, Rosewood Matakauri gazes across Lake Wakatipu to the jagged Remarkables. Just eleven suites and villas, dressed in schist, timber and sheepskin, frame that view from deep baths and private terraces. Days might begin with a helicopter flight over Fiordland and end beside the fire with Central Otago pinot. Native planting, local growers and Māori storytelling shape a stay that feels rooted in this valley, not merely visiting it.

property_title: Schloss Elmau: Bavarian Alpine Retreat of Music and Stillness
property_intro: Cradled in a private Bavarian valley beneath the Wetterstein peaks, Schloss Elmau has drawn thinkers, musicians and families since 1916. Concerts unfold nightly in its intimate halls, while six spas, forest trails and thermal pools invite slower hours. Wellness and culture sit together here without ceremony, and the estate's own farm, heat-pump warmth and long-standing literary programme reflect a house that has always looked beyond itself. Come for the mountains; stay for the music.

property_title: Grand Forest Metsovo: Pindus Mountain Retreat in Epirus, Greece
property_intro: High in the Pindus range, above the stone-built village of Metsovo, Grand Forest sits among fir forest and alpine meadows where Epirus reveals its quieter character. Rooms in timber and local stone open onto valley views, while the spa, hearth-warmed lounges and mountain cuisine draw on Vlach traditions and regional producers. Days might bring forest walks, winter skiing or visits to village workshops, where centuries of craft and shepherding culture continue to shape daily life.

property_title: Saltmoore: Where the Yorkshire Moors Meet the Restless North Sea
property_intro: Tucked into the Mulgrave Estate near Sandsend, Saltmoore sits where heather moorland tips down towards the North Sea, a short stroll from the sand. Interiors draw on the coast and countryside beyond, all weathered timber, wool and light. Days unfold with sea swims, woodland walks, spa hours and produce grown or landed nearby. The estate's ongoing rewilding and long ties with local makers and fishermen give every stay a quiet sense of belonging.

property_title: Chateau de Fere Hotel & Spa: Champagne's Storied Retreat
property_intro: Set within 300 acres of Picardy woodland, Chateau de Fere Hotel & Spa stands beside the romantic ruins of a 13th-century fortress, its Renaissance viaduct still arching across the valley. Rooms blend period detail with quiet contemporary comfort, while the spa and kitchen garden shape the rhythm of each day. Champagne's vineyards lie within easy reach, yet many guests find themselves lingering here, wandering the parkland at dusk and dining on produce grown just beyond the terrace.

property_intro: In a flower-filled hamlet in the Landes, Les Pr\

property_title: Airelles Gordes: Provençal Splendour Above the Luberon Valley
property_intro: Carved into the hillside of one of Provence's most beguiling villages, Airelles Gordes gazes across the Luberon's lavender fields and dry-stone terraces. Once a bastide, now a house of quiet grandeur, it pairs Pierre Yovanovitch interiors with warm Provençal spirit. Days unfold with truffle hunts, cycling through ochre villages, market mornings in Coustellet and cooking alongside chefs who champion local growers. Cellars, spa and vine-shaded terraces invite lingering ained beautifully close to the land that shaped them.

property_title: Château Saint-Martin & Spa: Hilltop Calm Above the French Riviera
property_intro: Set high in the hills above Vence, this former Templar estate looks out across olive groves and cypress to the shimmer of the Mediterranean below. Thirty-four acres of terraced gardens supply the kitchen, while beekeeping and careful land stewardship shape daily life here. Days unfold slowly: treatments in the light-filled spa, long lunches beneath ancient trees, walks to hilltop villages once painted by Chagall and Matisse. Provençal elegance, quietly confident and refreshingly unhurried.

property_title: La Réserve: A Refined French Retreat Amid Wild, Quiet Beauty
property_intro: Tucked into the folds of the French countryside, La Réserve invites you to slow your pace and settle in. Days unfold gently here: long walks through wildflower meadows, seasonal menus shaped by neighbouring growers, and evenings spent by the fire as the light softens. Interiors pair honest materials with quiet craftsmanship, while careful rewilding and partnerships with local artisans mean your stay leaves the surrounding landscape richer than you found it.

property_title: Airelles Château de Versailles: Evenings Inside Royal Grounds
property_intro: Set within the Grand Contrôle, a 1681 mansion at the edge of the palace gardens, this is the only address where guests can stay on the Versailles estate itself. Christophe Tollemer's interiors echo the 18th century with restored panelling and antiques, while Alain Ducasse oversees the kitchen. Wander the gardens after closing, drift through the Hall of Mirrors privately, and know your stay supports the château's ongoing restoration work.

property_title: Hotel de Crillon: Parisian Grandeur on Place de la Concorde
property_intro: Overlooking the Place de la Concorde, this eighteenth-century palace has welcomed Paris society since 1909, its stonework restored by master artisans over four painstaking years. Inside, Karl Lagerfeld-designed suites sit alongside marble baths, a hushed spa and courtyard dining beneath climbing greenery. Guests wander to the Tuileries in minutes, or linger over cocktails in Bar Les Ambassadeurs. French craft traditions are quietly championed here, from gilders to glassmakers, keeping rare skills alive for another generation.

property_title: Where the Riviera Slows: Hotel du Cap-Eden-Roc, Cap d'Antibes
property_intro: Set within twenty-two acres of pines and terraced gardens on the tip of Cap d'Antibes, Hotel du Cap-Eden-Roc has drawn artists, writers and dreamers since 1870. Days drift between the seawater pool carved into the rocks, cliffside paths and dining beneath parasol pines. Interiors balance Belle Epoque calm with Mediterranean light, while the gardens are tended organically, with beehives, heritage plantings and locally sourced produce shaping each unhurried, quietly indulgent stay.

property_title: Malis Garten: Alpine Calm and Conscious Comfort in Zell am Ziller
property_intro: Tucked into Austria's Zillertal valley, Malis Garten greets guests with timber-warm interiors, a garden that shifts with the seasons and mountains rising just beyond the terrace. Days here move gently: forest walks and ski slopes on the doorstep, spa hours scented with regional herbs, breakfasts built from neighbouring farms. The family behind it champion local craft, low-impact building and produce grown metres from the table, making this a place where refinement feels rooted rather than staged.

property_title: The Murray, Hong Kong: A Modernist Landmark Reborn in Central
property_intro: Set on Cotton Tree Drive, moments from Hong Kong Park and the Peak Tram, The Murray occupies a celebrated 1969 government building, its sculpted arched windows designed to temper the subtropical sun. Ron Arad Architects' sensitive restoration retained the original structure, saving energy and history alike. Inside, light-filled rooms, a rooftop garden and dining that spans Cantonese to Mediterranean invite lingering, while the Niim Mo trail and banyan-shaded streets begin at the doorstep.

property_title: Signiel Seoul: Where the City Unfolds Far Below Your Window
property_intro: Perched on the upper floors of Lotte World Tower in Songpa, Signiel Seoul lifts you above the capital's rhythm, with Namhansanseong's ridgelines and the Han River threading the view. Interiors pair Korean craft traditions with quiet contemporary lines, while the kitchens champion small Korean producers and seasonal harvests. Spend mornings in the sky-high pool, afternoons among Seokchon Lake's cherry trees, and evenings watching the lights come up across a city that never quite settles.

property_title: The Shilla Seoul: Timeless Grace on Namsan's Wooded Slopes
property_intro: Set within 23 acres of private parkland on the slopes of Namsan Mountain, The Shilla Seoul offers a rare stillness moments from the city's markets and palaces. Guests wander a sculpture garden dotted with Korean contemporary works, take breakfast overlooking ancient fortress walls, then slip into the urban hot spring spa. Dining spans revered Korean fine dining to Michelin-recognised kitchens, while the hotel's long-standing support for Korean craft keeps heritage traditions thriving in modern hands.

property_title: Soori Penang: Coastal Calm on Malaysia's Heritage Island Shore
property_intro: On Penang's north-western shore, Soori Penang gathers light, water and volcanic stone into something quietly extraordinary. Architect Soo K. Chan's pavilions frame the Andaman Sea, with private pools, timber screens and locally quarried surfaces that soften as the day turns. Beyond the gates lie George Town's shophouse lanes, spice-scented kitchens and the rainforest ridges of Penang Hill. Spend mornings paddling, afternoons with a local artisan, and evenings tracing the horizon from your terrace, unhurried.

property_title: Awasi Patagonia: Wild Solitude Beneath Torres del Paine Peaks
property_intro: Set on a private reserve at the edge of Torres del Paine, Awasi Patagonia gathers just fourteen villas across the steppe, each with its own hot tub and uninterrupted views of the Paine massif. Every villa comes with a private guide and vehicle, so days unfold at your pace: tracking pumas, riding out with local baqueanos, lingering over Patagonian lamb. Rewilded grasslands and long-term puma conservation quietly underpin it all.

property_title: Camp Sossus: Desert Silence Beneath Namibia's Ancient Dunes
property_intro: Set on a private reserve near the Namib's great dune sea, Camp Sossus gathers a handful of stone-and-canvas suites into a landscape of gravel plains, granite outcrops and endless sky. Days unfold with guided walks among ancient welwitschia, dawn drives towards Sossusvlei and evenings tracing constellations from your veranda. Built with local craftsmen and run largely on solar power, the camp supports desert-adapted wildlife research and nearby communities, so your stay leaves the land quietly better.

property_title: Casa Carolina: Colombia's Coastal Calm, Reimagined with Soul
property_intro: Set along Colombia's Caribbean shoreline, Casa Carolina is a whitewashed retreat where sea breezes drift through open courtyards and handcrafted furnishings tell of local artisanry. Days unfold slowly here: breakfast beneath fruit trees, afternoons in the pool, evenings spent tasting seafood drawn from nearby waters. The house works closely with its village neighbours, supporting fishermen and craftspeople, while thoughtful design keeps its footprint light. A place for those who prefer warmth and authenticity over polish.

property_title: Casa Mãe: Sunlit Courtyards and Slower Days in Old Town Lagos
property_intro: Tucked into the lanes of Lagos, minutes from the Algarve's cliff-backed coves, Casa Mãe gathers a 19th-century townhouse and garden pavilions around courtyards scented with citrus and rosemary. Rooms pair local craftsmanship with pieces by Portuguese makers, while the kitchen cooks from its own garden and nearby smallholdings. Swim between fig trees, learn to shape clay or bake bread, then wander to the marina as the light softens over the water.

property_title: 1 Hotel Mayfair: Nature-Led Luxury in the Heart of London
property_intro: Tucked between Berkeley Square and Green Park, 1 Hotel Mayfair brings a breath of the wild to one of London's most storied districts. Reclaimed timber, living greenery and daylight shape interiors that feel calm rather than showy, while the restaurant celebrates British growers and seasonal produce. Wander to Bond Street, the Royal Academy or Hyde Park, then return to a room where sustainability is quietly considered in every detail.

property_title: Filha Da Lua Ecolodge: Barefoot Serenity on Brazil's Coast
property_intro: Tucked between dunes, lagoons and the warm Atlantic in Brazil's north-east, Filha Da Lua Ecolodge invites you to slow down. Handcrafted bungalows, shaded by palms and shaped from local timber and clay, open to sea breezes and star-filled skies. Days unfold with kitesurfing, horseback rides along empty sands and long lunches of just-caught fish. Solar power, careful water use and close ties with the neighbouring fishing village make every stay quietly meaningful.

property_title: Juvet Landscape Hotel: Silence, Stone and Norway's Wild Gorge
property_intro: Tucked into a birch-clad ravine above the Valldøla river in Valldal, Juvet Landscape Hotel invites you to live briefly inside the Norwegian landscape rather than merely look at it. Each timber-and-glass room stands on stilts, angled so no window meets another, framing rock, water and moss. Meals arrive from nearby farms and fjord waters; days unfold with river swims, mountain walks and sauna heat. The land is left largely untouched, and that restraint is the luxury.

property_title: NATIVE Ballydehob: Where West Cork's Wild Beauty Feels Like Home
property_intro: Tucked into the colourful village of Ballydehob, where West Cork's hills tumble towards Roaring Water Bay, NATIVE offers a considered kind of retreat. Interiors pair local craftsmanship with natural materials and quiet restraint, while days unfold between island-hopping, sea swims, foraged suppers and studio visits with the artists who have long made this corner of Ireland their own. Sustainably run and deeply rooted in the community, it invites you to settle in and linger....**wait**

property_title: Pousada Trijunção: Wild Cerrado Luxury in Brazil's Heartland
property_intro: Set where three Brazilian states meet, Pousada Trijunção sits within a vast private reserve of Cerrado savannah 	aniverse rarely seen by travellers. Maned wolves pad past at dusk, giant anteaters forage in the grasslands and horseback rides trace red-earth trails through flowering campos. Eight airy suites blend regional craftsmanship with quiet comfort, while the kitchen draws on native fruits and local growers. Guided walks and research collaborations support the reserve's ongoing protection of this remarkable, misunderstood biome.

property_title: Roça Sundy: Heritage, Rainforest and Renewal on Príncipe Island
property_intro: On the northern plateau of Príncipe, a restored cocoa plantation looks out across forested hills towards the Atlantic. Roça Sundy pairs colonial-era architecture with airy, light-filled rooms, wide verandas and locally crafted furnishings. Days unfold with rainforest walks, empty beaches, birdlife found nowhere else and long lunches shaped by the island's own harvests. As part of a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, the estate invests in village schools, farming and jobs, so your stay quietly sustains Sundy itself.

property_title: Six Senses Ibiza: Sunset Rituals on Ibiza's Wild North Coast
property_intro:
Set above the quiet coves of Xarraca Bay, in Ibiza's rugged and least-trodden north, Six Senses Ibiza offers a gentler rhythm to island life. Earth-toned suites and cliffside villas open to pine-scented breezes, while the wellness pavilion draws on longevity science and sound healing. Days unfold with organic farm dinners, boat trips to Es Vedrà and sunsets shared at Beach Caves. A LEED Platinum retreat where regenerative farming and local craft quietly shape every stay.

Curious to feel it for yourself?

property_title: Six Senses Zighy Bay: Where Oman's Rugged Peaks Meet the Sea
property_intro: Tucked between the Hajar mountains and the Gulf of Oman on the Musandam Peninsula, Six Senses Zighy Bay is reached by winding mountain road, speedboat or — for the bold — paraglider. Stone-walled villas echo the architecture of the neighbouring fishing village, while days unfold with dhow sailing, wadi hikes and dining above the bay. An organic garden, marine conservation work and long-standing village partnerships keep this remarkable stretch of coast thriving.

property_title: Six Senses Zil Pasyon: Granite Shores and Seychelles Serenity
property_intro: On Félicité, a private granite island in the Seychelles, Six Senses Zil Pasyon unfolds across boulder-strewn shores and forested hills, with just a handful of villas hidden among the rocks. Each has its own pool and views over the Indian Ocean towards neighbouring La Digue. Days might mean snorkelling coral gardens, hiking to viewpoints, or spa treatments in a boulder-framed sanctuary. The island's nursery propagates native plants, restoring habitats for endemic birds and giant tortoises.

property_title: Storfjord Hotel: Handcrafted Calm Above Norway's Fjord Country
property_intro: Set on a wooded hillside above the Storfjord near Ålesund, this timber-built retreat was raised by local craftsmen using traditional Norwegian joinery, and the care shows in every beam and hand-woven textile. Days unfold with forest walks, sea kayaking and hikes into the Sunnmøre Alps, before dinners built around produce from the surrounding farms and fjord. Just twenty-two rooms, deep silence and a garden that rolls towards the water: unhurried, considered, quietly Norwegian.

property_title: Tutka Bay Lodge: Where Alaska's Wild Coast Meets Quiet Comfort
property_intro: Tucked into a sheltered fjord off Kachemak Bay, this floating retreat is reached only by boat or floatplane from Homer. Timber cabins perch above tidal waters, framed by spruce forest and glacier-cut peaks. Days unfold with kayaking, bear viewing and foraging along the shoreline, before dinner in the Widespread Cooking School, where wild Alaskan ingredients take centre stage. Long committed to marine research and local livelihoods, the lodge offers wilderness with genuine warmth.

property_title: Tri Sri Lanka: Lakeside Calm on Koggala's Cinnamon Shores
property_intro: Set on a cinnamon-scented peninsula above Koggala Lake, a short drive from Galle's ramparts, Tri unfolds in a gentle spiral inspired by the Fibonacci sequence. Rooms open to water, treetops and birdsong, while rainwater harvesting, solar power and a chemical-free garden quietly underpin everything. Days might mean lake yoga, Ayurvedic treatments, kayaking past mangroves or lunch drawn from the estate. It is a place designed for slowness, curiosity and unhurried conversation.

property_title: One&Only Aesthesis: Barefoot Glamour on the Athenian Riviera
property_intro: On a pine-shaded stretch of Glyfada shoreline, twenty minutes from the Acropolis, One&Only Aesthesis revives the spirit of the 1960s Asteria beach club with quiet confidence. Villas and bungalows sit among rare protected dunes, carefully restored alongside native flora, while interiors nod to mid-century Greek modernism in stone, timber and linen. Days drift between a private sandy beach, Aegean sailing and slow suppers of island produce, with Athens' galleries and tavernas within easy reach.

property_title: One&Only Kéa Island: Untamed Cycladic Shores, Serene Seclusion
property_intro: An hour from Athens yet worlds apart, One&Only Kéa Island unfolds across the rugged headlands of Kéa, where oak forests meet the Aegean and ancient footpaths trace the hillsides. Stone-and-timber villas echo local craftsmanship, framing views over Vroskopos Bay. Days drift between sea kayaking, wild swimming and hikes with island guides, while kitchens draw on Kéan honey, cheese and herbs. Marine restoration and partnerships with island artisans keep this quiet corner of Greece thriving.

property_title: One&Only Royal Mirage: Arabian Grace on Dubai's Jumeirah Sands
property_intro: Set along a kilometre of private beach in Dubai's Jumeirah, One&Only Royal Mirage unfolds across 65 acres of scented gardens, arcaded courtyards and reflecting pools. Three distinct residences "," each with its own character "," share hammam rituals, candlelit Moroccan dining and views towards the Palm. Arabesque domes and hand-laid mosaics honour Gulf craftsmanship, while the resort's marine and turtle conservation work, alongside local artisan partnerships, gives every stay a quieter, lasting purpose.

property_title: One&Only Reethi Rah: Barefoot Elegance on North Malé Atoll
property_intro: Set on a sculpted island in North Malé Atoll, One&Only Reethi Rah unfolds across twelve powder-soft beaches, each with its own mood and light. Villas of timber and stone open to the lagoon, where reef restoration projects and resident marine biologists invite guests to take part in coral gardening. Days drift between overwater spa rituals, Maldivian-inspired dining and dhoni sails at dusk, with island life never far from your doorstep.

property_title: One&Only Le Saint Géran: Where Mauritius Meets the Indian Ocean
property_intro: Set on a private peninsula between the Indian Ocean and a tranquil lagoon on Mauritius' east coast, One&Only Le Saint Géran feels wonderfully unhurried. Sun-washed suites open to sea breezes, while days drift between snorkelling coral gardens, tennis with a pro, and Creole flavours shaped by island growers. Marine biologists guide guests through coral restoration work, children explore the KidsOnly nature club, and evenings end quietly, with the lagoon glinting beneath a wide southern sky.

property_title: One&Only Mandarina: Cliffside Luxury Above Mexico's Wild Pacific
property_intro: Set within a private reserve on Mexico's Riviera Nayarit, One&Only Mandarina scatters treehouses and clifftop villas across jungle-clad headlands above the Pacific. Howler monkeys wake the canopy, surf breaks below, and design by Rick Joy weaves timber and stone into the forest rather than upon it. Days unfold with horseback rides through the hills, Michelin-starred dining, and treatments drawn from Huichol tradition, while ongoing rewilding and local partnerships keep this coastline thriving for generations.

property_title: One&Only Palmilla: Sunlit Seclusion on Mexico's Baja Peninsula
property_intro: Perched where the desert slips into the Sea of Cortez, One&Only Palmilla occupies a headland of gardens, cactus and quiet coves near San José del Cabo. Whitewashed casitas and a 1950s chapel nod to the resort's storied past, while days unfold with sunrise paddles, sea-turtle releases and menus shaped by local growers and fishermen. Guests dine at Jean-Georges' beachside tables, then retreat to a hilltop spa scented with wild herbs.

property_title: One&Only Portonovi: A Fjord-Framed Haven on Montenegro's Coast
property_intro: Set where the Adriatic slips into the mountain-cradled Bay of Kotor, One&Only Portonovi occupies a stretch of shoreline once known only to sailors. Stone-hued architecture and pale timber echo the surrounding karst peaks, while Europe's first Chenot Espace guides guests through restorative wellness programmes. Days unfold sailing hidden coves, hiking Lustica's wild trails or dining on produce from Montenegrin smallholders. Local craftspeople and marine conservation projects quietly shape the experience, grounding every stay in place.

property_title: One&Only Cape Town: Waterfront Serenity Beneath Table Mountain
property_intro: Set on its own island within Cape Town's V&A Waterfront, One&Only gazes across still marina waters to Table Mountain. Interiors weave South African art, textiles and timber into spaces that feel generous rather than grand, while Nobu and Reuben's celebrate the Cape's larder. Days unfold with wine-country drives, township-led cultural tours and penguin encounters, and the resort's partnerships support local artisans and marine conservation. Return at dusk, when the mountain glows and the island quietens.

property_title: One&Only One Za'abeel: Dubai's Skyline Reimagined in Style
property_intro: Rising above Dubai's World Trade Centre district, One&Only One Za'abeel is linked by The Link, the world's longest cantilevered skybridge, where suspended gardens and a sky pool hover 100 metres above the city. Interiors blend Japanese restraint with Middle Eastern warmth, while restaurants from acclaimed chefs sit alongside a subterranean wellness sanctuary. Locally sourced produce, water conservation systems and partnerships with Emirati artisans anchor this vertical retreat firmly in its place.

property_title: One&Only The Palm: Moorish Seclusion on Dubai's Palm Shore
property_intro: Tucked on a private peninsula at the western crescent of Palm Jumeirah, One&Only The Palm feels worlds away from the city it faces. Moorish courtyards, hand-laid mosaics and shaded colonnades frame a private beach and calm lagoon views, reached by boat or by road. Days unfold with Michelin-recognised dining, treatments at the Guerlain spa and marine conservation walks along the shoreline. It is intimate, unhurried and quietly grand, with skyline lights shimmering across the water each evening.

property_title: Wilderness Mombo: Where the Okavango's Legends Come to Life
property_intro: On the northern tip of Chief's Island, where the Okavango Delta's floodplains meet ancient riverine forest, Wilderness Mombo has earned its reputation as one of Africa's great wildlife sanctuaries. Nine airy suites stand raised above the grasses, their design drawing on collected treasures and open sightlines rather than convention. Days unfold with game drives, mokoro glides and quiet hours watching lions pass beneath your deck. A pioneering rhino reintroduction programme continues here, shaped by decades of conservation commitment.

property_title: Magashi Peninsula: Wild Lakeside Seclusion in Akagera, Rwanda
property_intro: Set on a private peninsula within Rwanda's Akagera National Park, Magashi Peninsula looks across papyrus-fringed Lake Rwanyakazinga, where hippos surface at dusk and fish eagles call overhead. Six tented suites blend contemporary East African craftsmanship with uninterrupted water views. Days unfold with boat safaris, guided game drives tracking lion and black rhino, and time with the naturalists who know these plains intimately. Your stay directly supports Akagera's remarkable revival and the communities living alongside it.

property_title: Usawa Serengeti: Following the Great Migration in Quiet Luxury
property_intro: Usawa Serengeti moves with the herds, its canvas suites relocating through the year to stay close to the migration's shifting rhythm. Days begin with coffee poured beside the acacias and unfold into game drives, walking safaris and long, unhurried evenings under Tanzanian stars. Interiors are pared back and tactile, solar-powered and light on the land, while the camp's Maasai-led team shares knowledge that turns every sighting into something far more personal.

property_title: DumaTau Camp: Waterside Wilderness in Botswana's Linyanti
property_intro: Set along the Linyanti Waterway in northern Botswana, DumaTau Camp overlooks a lagoon where elephants wade at dusk and hippos announce the evening. Eight raised suites of timber, canvas and copper open to the water, their design shaped by the landscape rather than imposed upon it. Days unfold by boat, on game drives or from a sunken hide, while the camp's solar power and partnership with local communities help safeguard one of Africa's great elephant corridors.

property_title: Linkwasha Camp: Art Deco Elegance on Hwange's Wild Ngamo Plains
property_intro: In the south-eastern reaches of Hwange National Park, Linkwasha overlooks the Ngamo Plains, where elephant herds, wild dog and lion move between seeps and open grassland. Nine tented suites blend art deco lines with soft desert tones, framed by uninterrupted views. Days unfold on game drives and guided walks with Zimbabwe's exceptional guides, while the camp's solar power and long-standing partnership with neighbouring communities ensure your stay strengthens the wilderness that surrounds it.

property_title: Tipai Wildlife Luxuries: Tiger Country, Reimagined in Style
property_intro: On the fringes of Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve in Maharashtra, Tipai Wildlife Luxuries sits amid teak forest and bamboo, where langur calls carry through the canopy at first light. Villas open onto private plunge pools, their design drawing on Vidarbha craft traditions and local materials. Days unfold with expert-led safaris, forest walks and Warli-inspired art sessions, while village partnerships and habitat restoration shape everything here. Evenings belong to slow dinners under an unhurried, star-scattered sky.

property_title: Bijapur Lodge: Heritage Calm at the Edge of Wild India
property_intro: Set amid the quiet farmland and teak forests of central India, Bijapur Lodge offers a considered base for those drawn to the region's tigers, temples and long-held rural rhythms. Handcrafted interiors, locally sourced stone and shaded verandahs invite unhurried afternoons between early morning game drives and village walks led by naturalists who grew up here. Meals draw on the kitchen garden and neighbouring farms, while employment and conservation partnerships keep benefits firmly within the community.

property_title: Java Rain: Where Chikmagalur's Coffee Hills Meet Quiet Luxury
property_intro: Set high above Chikmagalur on a working coffee estate, Java Rain looks out across ridges of the Western Ghats, where mist drifts through Baba Budangiri's slopes. Glass-fronted suites and open verandas draw the plantation indoors, while cuisine leans on estate-grown produce and Malnad recipes. Days unfold with sunrise walks among the coffee, waterfall trails and unhurried afternoons watching the valley change colour. Local families form the heart of the team, and native planting keeps this hillside thriving.

property_title: Satya Resort: Where Indian Wilderness Meets Quiet Luxury
property_intro: Set amid rustling groves and open skies, Satya Resort invites you to slow down and settle into the rhythms of rural India. Handcrafted interiors draw on regional craft traditions, while sunlit terraces and shaded courtyards frame views that shift with the light. Wander village pathways with local guides, dine on produce grown nearby, or simply linger over chai as dusk falls. Every stay supports artisans and conservation efforts rooted in the surrounding landscape.

property_title: Chhahari Retreat: Himalayan Calm in Nepal's Timeless Valleys
property_intro:

e a place to pause beneath the Himalaya. Rooms crafted from local stone, timber and handwoven textiles open onto valley views where eagles drift and prayer flags catch the wind. Guest stays support local artisans, farmers and reforestation of the surrounding ridges.

property_title: Xigera Safari Lodge: Artistry in the Heart of the Okavango
property_intro: Set on a private island in the Moremi Game Reserve, Xigera Safari Lodge rises above the Okavango Delta's floodplains on raised walkways, where papyrus channels shift with the seasons. Twelve suites showcase commissioned work by African artists and makers, from hand-forged doors to woven ceilings. Days unfold by mokoro, on foot with expert guides, or in the treehouse beneath the stars. Solar-powered and deeply invested in local craft and conservation, it redefines what a delta stay can be.

property_title: Waldeck Namibia Luxury Lodge: Where the Desert Breathes Slow
property_intro: Set amid the ochre plains and granite outcrops of Namibia's vast interior, Waldeck Namibia Luxury Lodge offers a rare kind of quiet. Suites are shaped by natural stone, timber and light, framing horizons that shift from gold to violet. Days unfold with guided desert walks, wildlife tracking and stargazing beneath famously clear skies, while the lodge works closely with neighbouring communities and conservancies to protect the land. Warm hospitality, thoughtful cuisine and space to simply pause await.

property_title: Herdade da Cortesia: Quiet Days Among the Alentejo Cork Oaks
property_intro: Set within a working estate near Avis, Herdade da Cortesia unfolds across cork oak groves, wheat fields and the still waters of the Maranh\pared back and generous, the interiors favour local stone, linen and light. Days pass with horse rides, birdwatching, cellar tastings and long lunches drawn from the kitchen garden. Cork is harvested by hand here, sheep graze the pastures, and neighbouring villages supply much of what reaches your table.

property_title: Rubondo Island Camp: Wild Seclusion on Lake Victoria's Shores
property_intro: Set within a forested national park in the southwestern reaches of Lake Victoria, Rubondo Island Camp offers a rare kind of quiet. Eight timber-and-canvas bandas open to the water, shaded by ancient trees where chimpanzees, rehabilitated here decades ago, now roam freely. Days unfold with forest walks, birding among 300 species, catch-and-release fishing for Nile perch, and boat trips past otters and sitatunga. Park fees directly support the island's ongoing protection and its resident research team.

property_title: Saline Taiba: Barefoot Serenity on Brazil's Windswept Coast
property_intro: Set among the dunes and salt flats of Taiba, on Cear\u00e1's breezy northeastern shore, Saline Taiba is a quiet retreat where pale architecture meets shifting sand and lagoon light. Days unfold between kitesurfing sessions, horseback rides along empty beaches and long lunches of seafood drawn from local waters. Interiors favour handcrafted pieces by regional artisans, while the owners work closely with the fishing village nearby \u2014 a stay that feels rooted, generous and genuinely unhurried.

property_title: Enchanted Galapagos Lodge: Where Wild Islands Meet Warmth
property_intro: Set among the volcanic contours of the Galapagos, Enchanted Galapagos Lodge opens onto highlands where giant tortoises roam freely and finches chatter in the scalesia trees. Interiors of pale wood and local stone frame views of the Pacific, while guides born on these islands lead snorkelling, kayaking and lava-tunnel walks. Solar power, rainwater harvesting and partnerships with island farmers underpin every stay, so your days here quietly sustain the archipelago that inspires them.

property_title: Keythorpe Hall: Rolling Leicestershire Acres, Unhurried Days
property_intro: Set among the gentle folds of rural Leicestershire, Keythorpe Hall gathers parkland, ancient hedgerows and wildflower meadows around a handsome country house. Interiors balance period proportion with considered comfort: deep armchairs, log fires and long views across grazing pasture. Days unfold through woodland walks, kitchen gardens picked at first light and evenings spent lingering over local produce. Careful rewilding, native tree planting and partnerships with nearby farmers and makers keep this corner of England thriving.

property_title: The Gilded Iguana: Where Nosara's Jungle Meets the Pacific Surf
property_intro: Set among the tropical dry forest of Nosara on Costa Rica's Guanacaste coast, The Gilded Iguana sits moments from Playa Guiones and its dependable, year-round waves. Rooms open onto gardens alive with howler monkeys and parrots, while timber, stone and local craftsmanship shape a relaxed, considered aesthetic. Days unfold with dawn surf lessons, river paddles and yoga, then long lunches of Costa Rican produce. Reef-safe practices and nearby reserve protection keep this stretch of coastline thriving.

property_title: Boardwalk Boutique Hotel Aruba: Casitas Among Tall Coconut Palms
property_intro: Tucked into a former coconut plantation moments from Palm Beach, Boardwalk Boutique Hotel Aruba gathers pastel casitas around gardens shaded by palms and frangipani. Family-run and thoughtfully low-rise, it favours hammocks, outdoor kitchens and bicycles over crowds and formality. Rainwater is harvested, native planting draws hummingbirds and iguanas, and local artisans shape much of the interior detail. Days drift between the beach across the road, the pool terrace and unhurried island conversation.

property_title: Skåbu Fjellhotell: Highland Calm Above Norway's Deepest Valleys
property_intro: Set in one of Norway's highest mountain villages, Skåbu Fjellhotell looks out across the plateaus between Jotunheimen and Rondane, where the air is thin and the light lingers late. Rooms are pared back and timber-warm, the kitchen leans on local lamb, trout and foraged berries, and days unfold on cross-country trails, summer ridges and cloudberry bogs. Family-run and rooted in village life, it offers the rare pleasure of somewhere genuinely lived in.

property_title: Ngalung Kalla: A Wild Sumba Retreat Rooted in Community Spirit
property_intro: On the untamed south-east coast of Sumba, Ngalung Kalla sits above a private bay where surf breaks meet grassland hills and horses graze at dusk. Thatched villas built from local timber and stone open to the ocean breeze, while days unfold with waves, weaving lessons and long lunches of garden produce. Profits support the on-site learning centre, where young Sumbanese train in hospitality, English and enterprise, keeping this coastline's future in local hands.

property_title: Cherero Camp: Wild Serenity in Tanzania's Untamed Heartland
property_intro: Tucked into a quiet corner of Tanzania's northern wilderness, Cherero Camp offers a rare intimacy with the bush. Just a handful of canvas suites, dressed in natural linens and handcrafted timber, open onto grasslands where elephant and lion pass unhurried. Days unfold with guided walks, dawn game drives and long lunches beneath acacia shade. Locally recruited guides share ancestral knowledge, while camp revenue supports nearby villages and anti-poaching patrols across surrounding conservation land.

property_title: The Manta Resort: Pemba Island's Underwater Room Sanctuary
property_intro: On the northern tip of Pemba Island, where the Indian Ocean shifts through every shade of blue, The Manta Resort occupies a stretch of coast fringed by coral reef and mangrove. Its celebrated Underwater Room floats offshore, inviting you to sleep beneath the waterline among passing fish. Days unfold with diving, dhow sailing and visits to nearby villages, while the resort's marine conservation work and locally recruited team keep Pemba's rhythms close.

property_title: Rockhouse Hotel: A Cliffside Sanctuary on Negril's Wild Coast
property_intro: Perched on volcanic rock above Pristine Cove, Rockhouse Hotel occupies one of Negril's most dramatic stretches of coastline, where ladders drop straight into turquoise water. Thatched villas of stone and timber are built into the cliffs, framed by tropical gardens and open to the trade winds. Days pass between spa treatments, reef swims and Jamaican cooking at Pushcart. Profits fund the Rockhouse Foundation, which has transformed local schools 	ravyou might imagest.

property_title: Tranquilo Bay: Rainforest and Reef in Panama's Bocas del Toro
property_intro: On the wild edge of Bastimentos Island, Tranquilo Bay sits where Caribbean reef meets Panamanian rainforest, reachable only by boat. Six timber cabanas open onto a canopy alive with sloths, poison dart frogs and more than 300 bird species. Days unfold with guided paddles through mangroves, snorkelling over coral gardens and conversations with the Ngabe communities nearby. Family-run for two decades, the lodge protects 200 acres of regenerating forest " and shares every discovery within it.

property_title: Virsa Baltistan: Heritage Living in Ladakh's Turtuk Valley
property_intro: In Turtuk, one of the few Balti villages on the Indian side of the Line of Control, Virsa Baltistan opens a window onto a culture shaped by apricot orchards, glacial streams and centuries of Silk Route exchange. Rooms built with local stone, timber and willow reflect Balti craftsmanship, while meals draw on family recipes and village harvests. Wander buckwheat terraces with your host, meet weavers and orchard keepers, and witness tourism sustaining a remarkable mountain heritage.

property_title: The Doksa: Himalayan Stillness, Ladakhi Warmth and Wide Skies
property_intro: High in Ladakh's sun-bleached valleys, The Doksa takes its name from the summer pastures where herding families once gathered. Rammed-earth walls, hand-woven textiles and sunlit courtyards frame views of ridgelines that shift colour through the day. Days unfold slowly here: walks to village monasteries, conversations with local weavers, apricots picked from the orchard. Solar power, spring-fed water and a team drawn from surrounding hamlets keep the mountains, and their traditions, at the heart of every stay.

property_title: Akalki Holistic Sanctuary: Lakeside Healing in Chiapas, Mexico
property_intro: On the shore of Lake Montebello in the Chiapas highlands, Akalki Holistic Sanctuary unfolds among pine forest and turquoise water. Timber cabins stand on stilts above the lake, warmed by fireplaces and hushed by mist at dawn. Days revolve around temazcal ceremonies, hydrotherapy circuits, massage and slow meals prepared with produce from nearby farms. Built and run with local Tojolabal and Mayan families, it offers something quietly rare: restoration that benefits the community sustaining it.

property_title: Villas Flamingos: Where Holbox Lagoons Meet Barefoot Elegance
property_intro: On the sandy lanes of Isla Holbox, where cars give way to bicycles and the Yum Balam reserve breathes all around, Villas Flamingos opens onto a shallow turquoise lagoon. Palapa roofs, driftwood tones and hammocks strung between palms set the rhythm; kayaks, whale shark season and flamingo sightings fill the days. Solar power, local craftsmanship and island-run kitchens keep the place rooted in Holbox itself, quietly generous rather than showy.

property_title: Myconian Ambassador: Aegean Serenity Above Platis Gialos Bay
property_intro: Perched on the hillside above Platis Gialos, Myconian Ambassador looks out across the Aegean with a calm that feels rare on Mykonos. Interiors pair Cycladic simplicity with commissioned art and deep, sea-facing terraces, while the thalassotherapy spa draws on the island's own mineral waters. Family-run for generations, the hotel supports local artisans, growers and marine conservation efforts, so every long lunch and slow swim carries something of the island's living character.

property_title: Myconian Avaton: Cliffside Serenity Above Elia Beach, Mykonos
property_intro: Set high on the cliffs above Elia Beach, Myconian Avaton looks out across the Aegean from a hillside of wild thyme and sun-warmed stone. Cave-like suites, carved timber and locally quarried marble echo the island's vernacular, while private pools catch the afternoon light. Days unfold with Cretan-inspired dining, thalassotherapy rituals and boat trips to quieter coves. Family-run for generations, the hotel supports island artisans and producers, keeping Mykonian craft and hospitality quietly, genuinely alive.

property_title: Myconian Deos: Cycladic Calm Above Mykonos' Elia Shoreline
property_intro: Set into the hillside above Elia Beach, Myconian Deos looks out across the Aegean with an ease that feels entirely Cycladic. Whitewashed lines, handwoven textiles and local stone shape interiors that stay cool and unhurried, while terraced pools follow the slope down towards the water. Days drift between Greek-Mediterranean dining, thalassotherapy rituals and quiet coves reached by boat. Family-run for generations, the hotel champions island producers, artisans and considered, low-impact hospitality.

property_title: Myconian Imperial: Elite Elegance Above Mykonos' Elia Bay
property_intro: Perched on the hillside above Elia Beach, Myconian Imperial looks out across the Aegean from a quieter corner of Mykonos, far from the bustle of Chora. Cubic whitewashed architecture, handcrafted local stone and sculptural interiors frame terraces where the sea seems within reach. Days drift between the thalassotherapy spa, Cycladic-inspired dining and boat trips to hidden coves. The family-run group champions Greek artisans, regional producers and island conservation, giving each stay a genuine sense of place.

property_title: Mykonian Kove: Aegean Serenity Above a Secluded Cycladic Bay
property_intro: Set into the sun-warmed hillside above a quiet cove, Mykonian Kove looks out across the Aegean towards Delos, far from the island's busier shores. Whitewashed forms, handwoven textiles and local stone reflect Cycladic craft traditions, while terraces and private pools invite unhurried afternoons. Days might bring caique sailing, foraging with island cooks, or wine tasting in nearby vineyards. Water is carefully conserved, produce comes from Mykonian growers, and local artisans shape much of what you touch.

property_title: Mykonian Korali: Aegean Serenity Above Elia's Shimmering Bay
property_intro: Perched on the hillside above Elia Beach, Mykonian Korali looks out across the Aegean with quiet confidence. Whitewashed lines, handwoven textiles and driftwood tones echo the island's Cycladic craft traditions, while private plunge pools invite unhurried afternoons. Days might begin with yoga on the terrace and end with Greek small plates built around island produce and local fishermen's catch. Beyond the sun loungers, the owners champion Mykonian artisans and mindful water use, grounding indulgence in genuine care.

property_title: Myconian Kyma: Sunlit Aegean Serenity Above Mykonos Town Bay
property_intro: Perched on the slopes above Mykonos Town, Myconian Kyma looks out across the bay to Delos, with whitewashed terraces stepping down towards the water. Interiors pair island craftsmanship with contemporary calm, while the spa, sea-facing pool and Aegean-inspired dining invite unhurried days. Family-run for generations, the hotel supports local artisans, producers and marine conservation efforts. Wander into the old harbour's lanes at dusk, then return for a quiet cocktail as the Cyclades turn amber.

property_title: O'By Myconian: Refined Cycladic Calm Above the Aegean Blue
property_intro: Perched on Mykonos' sun-warmed slopes, O'By Myconian looks out across the Aegean with an ease that feels entirely unhurried. Whitewashed lines, handcrafted local textiles and stone underfoot reflect a Cycladic sensibility carried forward by a family with deep island roots. Days drift between sea-facing terraces, spa rituals and menus built around Greek growers and fishermen. Come evening, the light softens over the water, and you'll understand why guests find it difficult to leave.

property_title: Myconian Naia: Whitewashed Calm Above Platis Gialos Bay, Mykonos
property_intro: Tucked into the hillside above Platis Gialos, Myconian Naia looks out across the Aegean from a hushed corner of Mykonos, moments from the sand yet worlds from the crowds. property_title: Panoptis Escape: Where Cretan Hillsides Meet Quiet Luxury
property_intro: Set among olive groves on the slopes above Crete's southern coast, Panoptis Escape offers a considered kind of seclusion.
