property_title: Hacienda Pena Pobre: Timeless Calm in Mexico's Highlands
property_intro: Set among the pine-scented highlands south of Mexico City, Hacienda Pena Pobre unfolds behind weathered stone walls, where colonial arches frame courtyards of jacaranda and bougainvillea. Rooms are dressed in local textiles, hand-glazed talavera and antique timber, warmed by open fires on cool evenings. Days might involve horseback rides through ancient woodland, kitchen sessions with regional cooks, or quiet hours in the library. Restoration work here supports neighbouring artisans and safeguards the estate's native forest for generations to come.

property_title: Casa las Tortugas: Barefoot Serenity on Holbox's Sandy Shoreline
property_intro: On the car-free island of Holbox, where sandy lanes replace roads and flamingos wade in the shallows, Casa las Tortugas invites you to slow down. Whitewashed rooms, handwoven textiles and driftwood details open onto a garden shaded by palms, steps from the Gulf. Days drift between kayaking through mangroves, swimming with whale sharks in season and dining on the day's catch, while the owners quietly champion turtle protection and island livelihoods.

property_title: Imanta Resorts Punta de Mita: Where Jungle Meets Pacific Shore
property_intro: Tucked into 300 acres of private jungle on Mexico's Riviera Nayarit, Imanta Resorts Punta de Mita unfolds along a secluded stretch of Pacific coastline. Just thirteen residences, built from local stone and timber, sit lightly among the trees, with the Sierra de Vallejo rising behind. Days might mean turtle releases, tide-pool wandering or long silences on the sand. The resort protects its rainforest and works closely with neighbouring communities, so your stay leaves something behind.

property_title: Las Alamandas Resort: Private Beaches on Mexico's Costalegre
property_intro: Tucked between jungle-clad hills and four secluded beaches on Mexico's Costalegre, Las Alamandas spans 1,500 acres of protected coastline with just a handful of colour-washed villas. Founded by Isabel Goldsmith, it blends folk art, hand-painted tiles and Pacific light with unhurried days of horse riding, river picnics and turtle releases. Kitchen gardens and local artisans shape much of what you taste and touch here, while the wilderness beyond remains gloriously, deliberately untouched.

property_title: Las Ventanas al Paraiso: Desert Calm by the Sea of Cortez
property_intro: Where the Baja desert meets the Sea of Cortez, Las Ventanas al Paraiso unfolds in whitewashed suites, hand-carved stone and rooftop telescopes trained on the stars. Days drift from cactus-lined pathways to warm tidal waters, with grey whale encounters in winter and turtle hatchling releases at dusk. Local artisans shape much of what you touch here, while marine conservation and community projects run quietly alongside. Los Cabos, considered and unhurried, feels made for lingering.

property_title: ME Cabo: Barefoot Glamour on the Golden Sands of Medano Beach
property_intro: Where the Sea of Cortez laps against Medano Beach, ME Cabo sits at the lively heart of Cabo San Lucas, with El Arco rising in the distance. Interiors play with light, linen and desert tones, while days drift from rooftop pools to whale-watching, mezcal tastings and dawn walks past turtle nesting sites protected in partnership with local conservationists. Evenings bring music, coastal cuisine and the easy company of fellow travellers who linger long after sunset.

property_title: Viceroy Los Cabos: Architectural Calm by the Sea of Cortez
property_intro: Set between the desert and the Sea of Cortez on the San José del Cabo coast, Viceroy Los Cabos is a study in water, light and shadow. Floating walkways cross reflecting pools towards suites with private plunge pools, while four restaurants draw on Baja's farms and fishing boats. Days unfold with sunrise yoga, mezcal tastings and turtle releases along the shore, supported by local artisans and community partnerships that give the stay genuine depth.

property_title: La Pause: Candlelit Nights in Marrakech's Wild Agafay Desert
property_intro: Just beyond Marrakech, where the road surrenders to stone and scrub, La Pause unfolds across the Agafay's rolling hills. There is no electricity here  only lanterns, firelight and an extravagant scatter of stars. Berber tents and earthen kasbah rooms are furnished with local craft, while days pass in camel rides, dune golf, long lunches beneath olive trees and slow silence. Run with village families, it keeps desert traditions and Agafay's fragile calm intact.

property_title: Tribal Hotel: Artisanal Colonial Living in the Heart of Granada
property_intro: Tucked behind an unassuming façade in Granada, Tribal Hotel unfolds into a series of leafy courtyards, a jade-green pool and nine rooms dressed in Nicaraguan craft \u00a0hand-thrown ceramics, woven textiles and locally made furniture. Volcanoes and Lake Nicaragua lie moments away, yet mornings here invite lingering over strong coffee before exploring cigar workshops, artisan villages or a hidden crater lagoon. Guests are welcomed by a small local team whose knowledge of the city shapes each stay beautifully.

property_title: Belmond Hotel Monasterio: Cusco's Sacred Colonial Sanctuary
property_intro: Set within a 1592 seminary in the heart of Cusco, Belmond Hotel Monasterio wraps guests in centuries of Andean history. Cloisters frame a courtyard where a three-hundred-year-old cedar still stands, while colonial artworks line stone corridors and Gregorian chant drifts through the air at breakfast. Oxygen-enriched rooms ease the altitude, local weavers and chefs shape the experience, and the hotel's careful stewardship keeps this national monument, and its craftspeople, thriving.

property_title: Rio Sagrado: Riverside Calm in the Sacred Valley of the Inca
property_intro: Cradled by the Urubamba River between Cusco and Machu Picchu, Rio Sagrado unfolds across terraced gardens where hummingbirds outnumber guests. Adobe-walled casitas and Andean textiles echo the surrounding villages, while a riverside spa draws on local herbs and ancestral technique. Days might bring weaving lessons with Quechua artisans, alpaca encounters, or quiet hours watching mist lift from the mountains. The lodge supports nearby communities and native reforestation, so your stay leaves the valley richer.

property_title: Belmond Palacio Nazarenas: Cusco's Most Tranquil Palace Stay
property_intro: Tucked down a quiet lane in Cusco's San Blas quarter, this former convent conceals Inca walls, cloistered courtyards and frescoes uncovered during a painstaking three-year restoration. Just eleven metres above the Plaza de Armas, it offers oxygen-enriched suites, an open-air pool warmed by the Andean sun, and Peru's first Hypnose spa. Guests dine on produce from Sacred Valley smallholders, while local artisans share weaving and ceramics traditions passed through generations, keeping Cusco's living heritage close at hand.

property_title: Belmond Sanctuary Lodge: Wake at the Gates of Machu Picchu
property_intro: Perched on the mountaintop beside Machu Picchu's entrance, Belmond Sanctuary Lodge is the only hotel within touching distance of the citadel, granting you the rare privilege of arriving before the crowds and lingering after they leave. Cloud forest presses close, orchids bloom in the gardens, and hummingbirds visit at breakfast. Rooms are quietly elegant, dinners draw on Andean produce, and resident guides share Inca history while the lodge nurtures native flora and local livelihoods in Aguas Calientes.

property_title: Paraiso Escondido: A Quiet Portuguese Retreat Among the Hills
property_intro: Tucked into the folds of Portugal's sun-warmed countryside, Paraiso Escondido rewards those who venture beyond the familiar. Cork oaks and citrus groves frame low stone buildings, restored with lime plaster, salvaged timber and a light architectural touch. Days unfold slowly here: foraging with local growers, swimming beneath open sky, dining on produce grown metres from the table. The owners work closely with neighbouring farms, keeping traditional land practices and regional craft quietly, purposefully alive.

property_title: Solar do Castelo: A Hidden Mansion Within Lisbon's Castle Walls
property_intro: Tucked inside the ramparts of São Jorge Castle, Solar do Castelo occupies an 18th-century mansion raised on the site of the old royal kitchens. Peacocks wander the courtyard, Alfama's rooftops tumble towards the Tejo below, and archaeological fragments sit quietly alongside contemporary Portuguese design. Mornings begin with pastries and local produce; afternoons invite slow walks through the medieval quarter with guides who grew up here. A rare address where Lisbon's layered past feels genuinely inhabited.

property_title: Molori Safari Lodge: A Private Wilderness Retreat in Madikwe
property_intro: Set high on a rocky ridge in Madikwe Game Reserve, this malaria-free corner of North West South Africa looks out across plains where elephant, lion and wild dog roam freely. Molori welcomes just a handful of guests at a time, with five suites layered in natural textures, art and quiet comfort. Days unfold with expert-led game drives, bush walks and spa treatments, while the lodge's conservation work and community partnerships shape every stay.We hope you'll linger.dine.}Hmm.}}}}

property_title: Ulusaba Rock Lodge: A Cliff-Top Safari Retreat in the Sabi Sand
property_intro: Perched atop a granite koppie in the Sabi Sand Reserve, Ulusaba Rock Lodge surveys the Mabrak riverbed and the untamed reaches of the Greater Kruger. Suites are cut into the rock itself, with private plunge pools and views that stretch for miles. Days unfold with game drives alongside expert trackers, bush walks and stargazing suppers, while Virgin Limited Edition's Pride 'n Purpose initiative supports neighbouring communities in health, education and enterprise.

property_title: Ocho Suites: Refined Andalusian Living, Rooted in Spanish Soul
property_intro: Tucked into a quiet corner of Spain, Ocho Suites offers just eight thoughtfully composed rooms where lime-washed walls, reclaimed timber and locally thrown ceramics set a calm, considered mood. Days unfold slowly here: market mornings, tastings with neighbouring growers, unhurried afternoons beneath the shade of old olive trees. Family-run and firmly connected to its village, the house champions regional artisans and seasonal produce, inviting you to settle in and live, briefly, at the pace of southern Spain.

property_title: The Serras: Gothic Quarter Grace on Barcelona's Waterfront
property_intro: Tucked between the medieval lanes of Barcelona's Gothic Quarter and the yachts of Port Vell, The Serras occupies the building where a teenage Picasso kept his first studio. Interiors by Eva Martinez balance Mediterranean light with contemporary calm, while the rooftop pool and terrace frame the harbour below. Expect Michelin-starred Catalan cooking rooted in local producers, attentive service without formality, and a genuine sense of the city breathing just beyond your shutters.

property_title: Art Hotel Riposo: Where Ascona's Lake Light Meets Artful Calm
property_intro: Perched on the sunlit slopes above Ascona, Art Hotel Riposo looks out across Lake Maggiore towards the Ticino mountains, moments from cobbled lanes and lakeside promenades. Once a haven for painters drawn to the region's extraordinary light, the house still carries that creative spirit through original artworks, hand-picked furnishings and quietly considered interiors. Days unfold slowly here: breakfast on the terrace, a swim in the garden pool, walks to Monte Verit	tinyà's storied hillside, and evenings scented with Mediterranean blooms.

property_title: Eastwest Hotel: Understated Elegance a Few Steps from Lake Geneva
property_intro: Tucked into Geneva's lively Pâquis quarter, moments from the lake and the old town, Eastwest Hotel offers a considered retreat behind a discreet façade. Dark wood, natural stone and softly lit corners set a hushed, contemporary mood, while the leafy inner courtyard becomes a favourite spot for breakfast. Family-run and deeply rooted in the neighbourhood, the hotel champions local producers and small artisans, inviting you to explore the city slowly, at your own rhythm.

property_title: Muyuna Amazon Lodge: Rainforest Living Deep in Peru's Amazon
property_intro: Reached by boat along the Yanayacu River, Muyuna Amazon Lodge sits within a flooded forest reserve some 140 kilometres from Iquitos, far beyond the reach of roads. Thatched bungalows stand on stilts above the waterline, screened yet open to the dawn chorus of macaws and howler monkeys. Expert local guides lead canoe excursions, night walks and visits to the neighbouring village of San Juan, where the lodge's long-standing partnership supports schooling, healthcare and forest protection.

property_title: Why House: Barefoot Elegance on Sri Lanka's Southern Coast
property_intro: Tucked between coconut groves and paddy fields near Talpe, Why House sits a short stroll from the Indian Ocean and a gentle drive from Galle's ramparts. Whitewashed pavilions open onto lawns, lotus ponds and a 25-metre pool, while interiors blend colonial antiques with contemporary Sri Lankan craft. Days unfold with cookery lessons, surf trips and turtle-hatchery visits, and the kitchen leans on produce grown on site and gathered from neighbouring smallholders.

property_name: Zanzibar White Sand Luxury Villas & Spa
property_title: Zanzibar White Sand Luxury Villas & Spa: Barefoot Refinement
property_intro: Set along the powdery shoreline of Paje on Zanzibar's south-east coast, this intimate collection of thatched villas sits between swaying palms and a lagoon where kitesurfers skim the shallows. Each villa has its own pool and garden, shaded by makuti roofs and dressed in Swahili craftsmanship. Days drift between the spa, dhow sailing and long lunches, while the resort's foundation supports local schools and village initiatives just beyond the garden gate.

property_title: 137 Pillars House: Colonial Charm in the Heart of Chiang Mai
property_intro: Tucked into the leafy Wat Gate quarter beside Chiang Mai's Ping River, 137 Pillars House unfolds around a 19th-century teak residence once home to the Borneo Company. Thirty suites open onto shaded verandas, where mornings begin with birdsong and locally sourced breakfasts. Wander to neighbourhood temples and artisan workshops, join a Lanna cooking lesson, or simply linger by the pool. Heritage restoration and long-standing community partnerships give this quietly elegant retreat genuine depth.

property_title: Another Place, The Lake: Barefoot Luxury on Ullswater's Shore
property_intro: On the quiet western shore of Ullswater, this reimagined Victorian house looks across water to the fells beyond. Eighteen acres of meadow and woodland lead to a private jetty, where guests slip into the lake before warming up in the glass-walled pool. Interiors are unfussy and tactile, food is locally sourced and generous, and the team works closely with Lake District conservation projects. Wild swimming, paddleboarding and long, unhurried evenings await.

property_title: Flemings Mayfair Hotel: Georgian Charm in the Heart of London
property_intro: Tucked along Half Moon Street, moments from Green Park and the boutiques of Piccadilly, Flemings Mayfair occupies a row of Georgian townhouses that have welcomed guests since 1851. Interiors balance heritage detail with quiet contemporary comfort, while Ormer Mayfair serves inventive seasonal cooking rooted in Channel Islands produce. Sip a bespoke cocktail in the Manetta's Bar, retreat to a private apartment, and discover a hotel where thoughtful service and sustainable practice sit naturally together.

property_title: Halepuna Waikiki by Halekulani: Refined Calm Beside the Sea
property_intro: A short stroll from Waikiki Beach, Halepuna Waikiki by Halekulani offers a quieter interpretation of Honolulu luxury. Interiors nod to island craft, with woven textures, hand-painted murals and locally made ceramics gathered through partnerships with Hawaiian artisans. Days might begin with sunrise yoga on the eighth-floor terrace, drift into an afternoon by the infinity-edge pool, then close with Pacific views from your lanai. Cultural programming, from lei-making to ukulele, connects guests meaningfully with O'ahu's living traditions.

property_title: Hotel Valencia Santana Row: Mediterranean Soul in Silicon Valley
property_intro: Set along the tree-lined promenade of Santana Row in San Jose, Hotel Valencia brings a touch of Andalusian romance to the heart of Silicon Valley. Wrought-iron balconies, hand-carved wood and a candlelit courtyard invite you to slow down, while Citrus restaurant and the rooftop Cielo bar draw locals and travellers alike. Boutiques, farmers' markets and vineyards in the Santa Cruz Mountains sit close by, and the hotel's partnerships with neighbourhood makers keep its spirit firmly Californian.

property_title: Hotel ZaZa Dallas Uptown: Bold Design in the Heart of Texas
property_intro: Set along tree-lined Uptown, moments from the Katy Trail and the galleries of the Arts District, Hotel ZaZa Dallas brings theatrical flair to Texan hospitality. Each Concept Suite tells its own story through curated antiques, commissioned artwork and layered textures, while the palm-shaded Urban Oasis pool invites slow afternoons. Dine at Dragonfly, where seasonal produce from regional growers shapes the menu, then wander into neighbourhood boutiques and independent coffee houses just beyond the door.

property_title: Hotel ZaZa Austin Downtown: Bold Art, Warm Texan Welcome
property_intro: Set beside Lady Bird Lake in the heart of Austin's Rainey Street district, Hotel ZaZa Downtown pairs theatrical interiors with genuine Texan hospitality. Rooms and Concept Suites are layered with commissioned artwork and collected antiques, while the terrace pool and lively bar draw locals as readily as guests. Live music venues, hike-and-bike trails and independent kitchens sit within walking distance, and the hotel champions Austin artists and makers throughout its spaces.

property_title: Los Poblanos: Lavender, Legacy and New Mexico's Rio Grande Valley
property_intro: Set among 25 acres of lavender fields, orchards and organic farmland in Albuquerque's North Valley, Los Poblanos occupies a 1930s hacienda designed by John Gaw Meem, New Mexico's celebrated regionalist architect. Cottonwoods shade the acequias, peacocks wander the courtyards, and the farm shop distils lavender grown just beyond your door. Dine on field-to-fork cooking at Campo, join a bread-making class, and settle into rooms where Pueblo craft meets considered comfort and genuine agricultural stewardship.

property_title: R Inn Napa: Vineyard Calm at the Heart of Wine Country
property_intro: Set among the vine-stitched slopes and oak-shaded lanes of California's Napa Valley, R Inn Napa offers an unhurried welcome just moments from celebrated cellars and farm-to-table kitchens. Interiors pair warm timber, natural linens and locally made pieces with quiet comfort, while mornings begin with regional produce and conversation. Spend days cycling the valley floor, tasting with growers who tend their soils thoughtfully, then return for golden light on the terrace and the scent of rosemary drifting through.

property_title: The River Station: Riverside Living on Uganda's Wild Nile
property_intro: Set on the banks of the Nile in Uganda, The River Station gathers a handful of elegantly pared-back suites beneath riverine trees, where kingfishers dart and hippos surface at dusk. Days unfold with boat safaris towards thundering falls, guided walks with local naturalists and long, unhurried lunches above the water. Interiors favour local craftsmanship and honest materials, while partnerships with neighbouring communities and conservation teams ensure your stay leaves the river and its wildlife the better for it.

property_title: Silverback Lodge: Where Uganda's Misty Forest Comes Alive
property_intro: Perched on a ridge above Bwindi Impenetrable Forest, Silverback Lodge looks across a canopy where mountain gorillas move unseen. Rooms are quietly considered, with private verandas, local hardwoods and windows framing the Virunga volcanoes beyond. Days begin early with trackers and guides from neighbouring Buhoma village, whose community benefits directly from every stay. Return to hot water, unhurried dinners and the sound of the forest settling as evening mist gathers below.

property_title: The Peninsula Tokyo: Imperial Gardens, Ginza Glamour Awaits
property_intro: Standing where the Imperial Palace gardens meet the shopping avenues of Ginza, The Peninsula Tokyo folds the city's contrasts into one address. Rooms echo Japanese craft traditions, from lacquer detailing to washi-inspired screens, while the rooftop Peter bar frames Hibiya Park below. Guests borrow bicycles, join calligraphy sessions or slip into the spa's quiet. Local artisans supply much of the interior artistry, and seasonal menus lean on producers from nearby prefectures, grounding this refined tower firmly in its neighbourhood.

property_title: Amanfayun: Tea Fields, Temples and Timeless Hangzhou Calm
property_intro: Set within a restored village on the fringes of Hangzhou's West Lake, Amanfayun occupies a cluster of century-old dwellings threaded by a stone-paved pathway. Camphor trees, terraced tea fields and seven working Buddhist temples surround you, with monks' chanting drifting through the morning mist. Village houses have been sensitively reworked with timber, lime-washed walls and local craftsmanship, while villagers remain neighbours. Walk ancient pilgrim trails, pick Longjing tea in spring, or dine on Hangzhou dishes beside a lantern-lit lane.

property_title: The Lalu Hotel: Lakeside Serenity Above Taiwan's Sun Moon Lake
property_intro: Perched on a wooded promontory above Sun Moon Lake, The Lalu occupies land once reserved for Taiwan's presidents, and the sense of privilege lingers. Minimalist teak interiors frame water and mountain views, while infinity pools seem to spill into the lake below. Days unfold with tea tastings, cypress-scented spa rituals and boat trips to Thao indigenous villages, whose culture and craft the hotel actively supports. Mornings here arrive slowly, wrapped in mist and birdsong.

property_title: Aman Kyoto: A Hidden Garden in Kyoto's Forested Northern Hills
property_intro: Tucked against the wooded slopes of Mount Hidari Daimonji, Aman Kyoto occupies a secret garden once destined for a textile magnate's private museum, its mossy stone pathways rediscovered after decades of quiet. Pavilions of dark timber and washi light sit lightly among maples and cedars, while onsen waters draw from the hillside. Days unfold with temple visits before the crowds, forest walks with local guides, and kaiseki shaped by Kyoto's farmers and artisans.

property_title: Botanic Sanctuary Antwerp: Where Medieval Gardens Still Heal
property_intro: Tucked behind ancient walls in Antwerp's diamond quarter, this former monastery and hospital has tended to the city's wellbeing since the twelfth century. Today, five restored heritage buildings encircle a walled botanical garden, where herbs once used by Augustinian sisters still perfume the air. Expect deeply considered design, six restaurants led by acclaimed chefs, and a spa drawing on centuries of healing practice. Restoration here has revived craft traditions and returned a treasured landmark to Antwerp.

property_title: Hotel AWA: Contemporary Lakeside Calm Beneath the Osorno Volcano
property_intro: On the shore of Lake Llanquihue, with the snow-tipped Osorno volcano rising across the water, Hotel AWA is a quietly confident retreat near Puerto Varas. Floor-to-ceiling glass, native timbers and works by Chilean artists frame the changing light, while the kitchen draws on Patagonian produce and local fishermen's catch. Days unfold with guided hikes through temperate rainforest, kayaking and volcano ascents, led by guides who know these valleys intimately and champion their protection.

property_title: ARIA Retreat & SPA: Serene Tuscan Luxury Above San Gimignano
property_intro: Set among cypress-lined hills within sight of San Gimignano's medieval towers, ARIA Retreat & SPA is an adults-only hideaway where Tuscany slows to a gentler rhythm. Fourteen individually styled rooms blend contemporary calm with restored stone, while the spa, infinity pool and panoramic terrace invite long, unhurried days. Dine on produce from neighbouring farms, walk the vineyards at dusk, or simply linger over Vernaccia as the valley turns golden. Small in scale, generous in spirit.

property_title: Alpin Resort Sacher: Alpine Serenity Above Zell am See
property_intro: Perched above the shimmering waters of Zell am See, Alpin Resort Sacher looks out across the Kitzsteinhorn glacier and the peaks of the Hohe Tauern. Interiors blend Austrian craftsmanship with contemporary calm, while the spa, sun terraces and mountain-inspired kitchen invite unhurried days. Ski from the doorstep in winter, or wander lakeside trails and high pastures come summer. Local producers, regional artisans and generations of Salzburg hospitality shape a stay that feels genuinely rooted in its landscape.

property_title: Hotel K\u00e4mp: Helsinki's Storied Grand Dame on Esplanadi
property_intro: Overlooking the linden-lined Esplanadi in the heart of Helsinki, Hotel K\u00e4mp has welcomed artists, composers and statesmen since 1887. Behind its stately fa\u00e7ade, Nordic restraint meets Belle \u00c9poque flourish: sweeping staircases, deep armchairs and a rooftop spa where you can unwind after a day exploring design studios and harbour markets. Sibelius once debated here until dawn; today, the kitchen champions Finnish growers and foragers, while the hotel supports local craft traditions. Arrive curious, linger longer.

property_title: Nayara Hangaroa: Easter Island's Rapa Nui Retreat Awaits You
property_intro: On the windswept edge of Easter Island, Nayara Hangaroa rises from volcanic rock in curved forms inspired by ancestral Rapa Nui ceremonial villages. Local stone, native timber and craftsmanship by island artisans shape every suite, while cliffside pools face the Pacific. Days unfold with guides tracing moai statues, sacred caves and crater lakes, and evenings bring Polynesian-influenced cooking. Staffed almost entirely by islanders, the hotel channels its efforts into preserving Rapa Nui heritage and fragile landscapes.

property_title: Corona Island: Barefoot Luxury in Colombia's Rosario Isles
property_intro: Set within the Rosario Islands, an hour by boat from Cartagena, Corona Island is Colombia's first sustainability-certified island retreat. Palm-thatched suites rise on stilts above mangroves and coral gardens, built with reclaimed timber and powered with care for the reef below. Days unfold slowly: snorkelling turquoise shallows, learning from marine biologists restoring coral nurseries, dining on Caribbean cooking shaped by island growers. Evenings belong to hammocks, birdsong and the quiet rhythm of the sea.

property_title: Rosewood San Miguel de Allende: Sunlit Courtyards and Artistry
property_intro: Set among the rose-hued domes and cobbled lanes of San Miguel de Allende, this hacienda-style retreat opens onto shaded courtyards, fountains and gardens scented with citrus. Interiors celebrate Mexican craft, from Talavera tiles to hand-woven textiles by local artisans. Days might begin with a hot-air balloon over the Bajío highlands and end with mezcal at Luna rooftop bar, watching the Parroquia glow. Cooking classes, gallery walks and community-led craft workshops connect guests with the town's living heritage.

property_title: Le Agavi: Cliffside Serenity Above Positano's Shimmering Bay
property_intro: Tucked into the terraced cliffs between Positano and Praiano, Le Agavi cascades down towards the Tyrrhenian in a series of sun-warmed levels, linked by a private funicular that glides guests to a rocky beach club below. Rooms open onto lemon-scented gardens and wide sea views, while the kitchen draws on produce from the hotel's own hillside plots and neighbouring Amalfi growers. Days unfold slowly here: swimming before breakfast, boat trips along the coast, evenings lit by candlelight and cicadas.

property_title: Dusit Thani Kyoto: Thai Warmth Woven into Kyoto's Ancient Soul
property_intro: Moments from Nishi Hongan-ji and the lantern-lit lanes of Shimogyo, Dusit Thani Kyoto brings Thai hospitality into quiet conversation with Japanese craft. Rooms frame courtyard gardens, while cedar, washi and hand-thrown ceramics from local artisans soften every corner. Days unfold slowly here: temple walks at dawn, a Thai-Kyoto tasting menu, or tea prepared with unhurried ceremony. The kitchen champions Kansai growers and seasonal produce, and staff share the neighbourhood's stories as warmly as they welcome you home.

property_title: Hotel Le Temple Borobudur: Serene Mornings in Central Java
property_intro: Set among rice terraces and volcanic ridges in Central Java, Hotel Le Temple Borobudur rests moments from the ninth-century Buddhist monument that gives it its name. Javanese craftsmanship shapes the interiors, from carved teak to locally woven textiles, while gardens open towards Menoreh Hills. Rise before dawn for the temple's first light, cycle through neighbouring villages, or learn batik from artisans nearby. Staff are drawn from surrounding communities, and produce arrives from farms within walking distance.

property_title: The Newman: Refined Fitzrovia Living in the Heart of London
property_intro: Tucked along a quiet street in Fitzrovia, The Newman brings a considered calm to one of London's most creative quarters. Georgian bones meet contemporary craftsmanship here, with locally made furnishings, natural materials and light-filled rooms that reward slow mornings. Below, the restaurant and bar draw neighbours as readily as guests, championing British growers and small producers. Step outside and Soho, Marylebone and the galleries of Bloomsbury are all within an easy wander.

property_title: Union Øye: A Storied Alpine Retreat by Norway's Hjørundfjord
property_intro: Tucked between the Sunnmøre Alps and the still waters of the Hjørundfjord, Union Øye has welcomed mountaineers, artists and royalty since 1891. Behind its timber façade, restored interiors hold antiques, curiosities and open fires, while guides lead walks to Slogen's summit and fjord crossings by wooden boat. Dinners draw on the valley's farms and foraged larder, and the hotel's careful stewardship keeps this small mountain community, and its history, quietly thriving.

property_title: Le Petit Pali St. Helena: Napa Valley's Quiet Coastal Charm
property_intro: Set on a leafy street in the heart of St. Helena, Le Petit Pali brings a breezy Californian coastal spirit to the vineyards of Napa Valley. Rooms are dressed in soft linens, rattan and warm timber, opening onto a courtyard where mornings begin with pastries and freshly brewed coffee. Cellar doors, olive groves and family-run kitchens sit within strolling distance, while bicycles wait for slower afternoons spent exploring the valley's celebrated growers and makers.

property_title: Rhinefield House Hotel: New Forest Grandeur Among Ancient Oaks
property_intro: Set at the end of an ornamental drive lined with towering conifers, Rhinefield House rises from 40 acres of formal gardens deep in Hampshire's New Forest. This Victorian mansion borrows from the Alhambra and Tudor England alike, with carved panelling, stained glass and an intricate Moorish hall. Wander maze and knot gardens, spot ponies grazing beyond the ha-ha, then return for spa treatments and dining that draws on Hampshire's growers and forest larder.

property_title: Norton House Hotel & Spa: Woodland Calm Near Edinburgh's Heart
property_intro: Set within 55 acres of parkland and mature woodland at Ingliston, Norton House feels worlds away from the city, yet Edinburgh's Old Town is barely twenty minutes distant. The Victorian mansion pairs original detail with an airy contemporary spa, where hydrotherapy pools and a rooftop hot tub look out over the trees. Dine on Scottish produce sourced from nearby growers and estates, wander the wildlife-rich grounds, then retreat to rooms designed for genuine, unhurried rest.

property_title: Les Hayes en Sologne: Woodland Calm in the Loire's Wild Heart
property_intro: Tucked between the lakes, heathland and oak forests of the Sologne, Les Hayes sits within easy reach of the Loire's great châteaux yet feels wonderfully removed from them. Interiors pair honest local materials with quiet contemporary comfort, while days unfold at their own pace: foraging walks, cycling through the woods, birdwatching at dawn or long tables shared with neighbours. Estate woodland is carefully managed, and much of what reaches the kitchen is grown or gathered nearby.

property_title: Mharo Khet: Rajasthan's Farmstay Where Slow Living Blossoms
property_intro: Set among mustard fields and orchards on the outskirts of Jaipur, Mharo Khet invites you into the rhythms of a working Rajasthani farm. Earth-toned cottages, hand-crafted by local artisans, open onto kitchen gardens where your dinner begins. Join millet harvests, learn ancestral recipes from village women, or simply watch peacocks cross the fields at dusk. Regenerative farming and fair employment shape everything here, offering a stay that nourishes both guest and the community around it.

property_title: The Shelborne By Proper: Art Deco Soul on Miami Beach Sands
property_intro: Rising above Collins Avenue since 1940, The Shelborne By Proper carries its Art Deco heritage lightly, pairing restored period detail with interiors by Kelly Wearstler that feel playful rather than precious. Steps from the Atlantic, days drift between the palm-fringed pool, South Beach's galleries and the Española Way promenade. Locally sourced menus, thoughtful partnerships with Miami makers and a genuine sense of neighbourhood make this a place to settle into, not simply pass through.

property_title: Harmony Seljalandsfoss: Waterfall Views on Iceland's South Coast
property_intro: Set beneath the mossy cliffs of Iceland's south coast, Harmony Seljalandsfoss looks out towards the famous falls you can walk behind. Timber-clad interiors, wide glazing and geothermal warmth frame a landscape of glaciers, black sand and birdsong, while soaking in the outdoor hot tub under shifting skies feels quietly ceremonial. Locally sourced breakfasts, guides from nearby farms and low-impact building choices keep the stay rooted in its valley or slow days and long, luminous evenings.

property_title: Braccialieri Luxury Resort: Italy's Quiet Art of Living Well
property_intro: Set among olive groves and centuries-old stone terraces, Braccialieri Luxury Resort invites you to slow down in one of Italy's most unhurried corners. Interiors pair restored local craftsmanship with contemporary calm, while days unfold through vineyard walks, kitchen sessions with regional producers and long afternoons by the water. The estate works closely with neighbouring farms and artisans, protecting native planting and traditional skills, so every stay quietly sustains the landscape and community that shape it.

property_title: Amina Wind Resort: Kite, Sea and Stillness in Baja Mexico
property_intro: On the shores of La Ventana, where the Sea of Cortez meets the desert mountains of Baja California Sur, Amina Wind Resort welcomes those drawn to wind and water. Days begin with kitesurfing across turquoise swells and end beneath a sky thick with stars. Adobe-toned suites, shaded terraces and locally crafted interiors reflect a quiet respect for place, while the resort supports Baja's fishing communities and marine conservation efforts.

property_title: L'EssenCiel: Where French Skies Meet Considered Alpine Calm
property_intro: Tucked into the folds of the French countryside, L'EssenCiel invites you to slow to the rhythm of the seasons. Interiors pair reclaimed timber with soft natural light, while wide windows frame meadows, forest and an unpolluted night sky. Days unfold gently here: foraging walks with local growers, wood-fired suppers built around neighbouring farms, evenings spent stargazing. Thoughtful stewardship of the land underpins everything, from rainwater harvesting to wildflower planting that draws bees and butterflies back.

property_title: Prospect Berkshires: Woodland Calm in Western Massachusetts
property_intro: Set among the rolling hills and hardwood forests of western Massachusetts, Prospect Berkshires invites you to slow to the rhythm of the seasons. Interiors pair warm timber and natural textures with quiet contemporary lines, while the surrounding land offers trails, swimming holes and starlit evenings by the fire. Days unfold gently here: farm-driven suppers, local makers and artists, and easy access to the region's celebrated galleries, gardens and concert halls just beyond the treeline.

property_title: VALO Ice Cube Villas: Lapland Nights Beneath Glass Skies
property_intro: Set among the snow-laden pines of Finnish Lapland, VALO Ice Cube Villas invites you to sleep beneath glass, where the aurora unfurls above your bed. Each villa balances Nordic restraint with genuine warmth: pale timber, private sauna, and quiet views across frozen forest. Days might bring husky trails, ice fishing or a slow walk on snowshoes, guided by locals who know these lands intimately. Built with low-impact heating and regional craftsmanship, it is luxury measured in stillness.

property_title: The Retreat Costa Rica: Wellness at the Foot of a Sacred Peak
property_intro: Set on the slopes of Cerro Atenas, one of the planet's few crystalline mountains, The Retreat Costa Rica looks out across the Central Valley towards distant volcanoes. Twelve individually designed suites sit among organic gardens, medicinal plant trails and forest restored by the owners themselves. Days unfold with sunrise yoga, plant-based cuisine grown metres from the table, and treatments drawing on local healing traditions. Guests leave lighter, having supported reforestation and the neighbouring Atenas community.

property_title: Xanadu Luxury Villas & Retreat: Barefoot Elegance in Zanzibar
property_intro: On Zanzibar's south-east coast, where the Indian Ocean shifts from jade to sapphire, Xanadu Luxury Villas & Retreat offers ten thatched villas set within tropical gardens above a quiet stretch of Michamvi sand. Interiors blend Swahili craftsmanship with contemporary calm, while days unfold through dhow sailings, spa rituals and slow lunches of just-landed seafood. The retreat works closely with neighbouring villages, employing local artisans and supporting island schools, so your stay leaves something meaningful behind.

property_title: Theros All Suite Hotel: Suite Serenity by the Aegean Shore
property_intro: Set along the sunlit coast of Greece, Theros All Suite Hotel offers a collection of generous suites where pared-back Cycladic design meets considered comfort. Days unfold slowly here: sea-facing terraces, private pools, and menus built around produce from nearby growers and fishermen. Wander to the shoreline at dusk, or let the concierge arrange a boat trip beyond the usual routes. Locally sourced materials, island craftsmanship and a small, dedicated team give this retreat its quietly distinctive character.

property_title: Fowlescombe Farm: Regenerative Luxury in the Devon Hills
property_intro: Tucked into a fold of the South Devon hills, Fowlescombe Farm occupies 400 acres of organic pasture, ancient hedgerows and wildflower meadows on the edge of Dartmoor. Six characterful suites and cottages blend Elizabethan stone with unfussy, considered interiors. Days here might mean foraging with the head chef, wild swimming, tending the market garden or simply watching the Ruby Red cattle graze. Every meal, every acre reflects a genuine commitment to regenerative farming and the community that sustains it.

property_title: Riad Botanica: Marrakech's Garden Sanctuary Within the Medina
property_intro: Tucked down a quiet derb in Marrakech's old medina, Riad Botanica opens onto courtyards shaded by citrus, fig and jasmine, where water murmurs and swifts wheel overhead. Rooms are dressed in tadelakt, hand-loomed wool and lamps beaten by artisans a few streets away. Days unfold slowly: rooftop breakfasts, herbal workshops with local growers, guided walks through the souks. Rainwater is harvested, produce sourced from nearby smallholders, and staff drawn from the neighbourhood itself.

property_title: Riad Rosemary: A Serene Marrakech Sanctuary Behind Medina Walls
property_intro: Tucked down a quiet derb in the heart of Marrakech's medina, Riad Rosemary opens onto a courtyard of citrus trees, zellige tilework and cool shade. Rooms are dressed in tadelakt, handwoven textiles and lanterns made by artisans a few streets away. Days unfold slowly here: rooftop breakfasts above the rooftops, souk walks with a local guide, hammam rituals at dusk. The kitchen sources from nearby growers, and staff are hired and trained from the surrounding neighbourhood.

property_title: Lizard Island Resort: Barefoot Luxury on the Great Barrier Reef
property_intro: Set on a granite island fringed by 24 powder-soft beaches, Lizard Island Resort sits where the Great Barrier Reef meets the Coral Sea, an hour's flight north of Cairns. Just 40 suites and villas open to sea breezes, with interiors shaped by natural timber, stone and light. Snorkel giant clam gardens, picnic on a private beach, or visit the on-island research station, whose scientists have studied and safeguarded these waters for decades.

property_title: Uga Ulagalla: Wild Seclusion in Sri Lanka's Ancient Heartland
property_intro: Set across 58 acres of paddy fields, lakes and woodland near Anuradhapura, Uga Ulagalla centres on a 150-year-old chieftain's manor, with private villas scattered among the trees and their own plunge pools. Days unfold slowly here: horse riding at dawn, birdwatching by the tank, cycling to ancient stupas, or dining beneath the stars. Solar power, on-site farming and close ties with neighbouring villages ensure your stay quietly benefits this remarkable corner of the North Central Province.

property_title: Uga Riva: Colonial Charm on Negombo's Sunlit Palm-Fringed Coast
property_intro: Just north of Colombo, Uga Riva unfolds across a former coconut estate where the Indian Ocean meets Negombo's fishing traditions. Twenty-two suites and villas blend Dutch colonial lines with contemporary calm, each opening onto gardens or a private plunge pool. Days drift between lagoon boat rides, catamaran outings with local fishermen and unhurried Ayurvedic treatments. Menus favour catch landed that morning and produce from nearby smallholdings, supporting the communities who have shaped this shoreline for generations.

property_title: Uga Prava: Riverside Calm and Ocean Air in Bentota, Sri Lanka
property_intro: On the slender strip of land where the Bentota River slips into the Indian Ocean, Uga Prava gathers just a handful of suites around palm-shaded pools and wide verandas. Days unfold slowly here: mangrove paddles at first light, Ayurvedic rituals, spice-scented Sri Lankan cooking drawn from village markets. Design leans on local craft and timber, while turtle conservation and coastal community projects nearby give your stay a quieter, more lasting purpose.

property_title: Uga Halloowella: A Tea Planter's Retreat in Sri Lanka's Hills
property_intro: Set among the emerald contours of a working tea estate near Balangoda, Uga Halloowella is a restored planter's bungalow where colonial character meets quiet contemporary comfort. Wake to mist rising over the plantation, walk the rows with pluckers who know every bush, and end the day beside the fire with estate-grown tea. Only a handful of rooms, a spring-fed pool and cuisine drawn from village gardens make each stay feel wonderfully unhurried and genuinely rooted in its community.

property_title: Uga Chena Huts: Wild Luxury on Yala's Untamed Coastline
property_intro: Where Yala National Park meets the Indian Ocean, Uga Chena Huts settles quietly into scrubland and dune, its thatched villas turned towards the sea. Each has a private plunge pool, an outdoor shower and the possibility of leopard tracks at dawn. Days unfold with guided safaris, coastal walks and Sri Lankan cooking rooted in the region's produce. Solar power, careful water use and local employment keep the footprint light, while the wilderness remains gloriously in charge.

property_title: Asbury Ocean Club: Coastal Calm on New Jersey's Creative Shore
property_intro: Rising gently above the boardwalk in Asbury Park, New Jersey, this glass-clad retreat looks out across the Atlantic while keeping one foot in the city's storied music scene. Interiors by Anda Andrei balance pale timber, linen and light, and days drift between the saltwater pool, the spa and independent galleries a short stroll away. Breakfast leans local, staff know their neighbours, and the hotel's support for Asbury's arts community gives every stay a deeper resonance.

property_title: Riad F\u00e8s: Andalusian Elegance in the Heart of the Medina
property_intro: Tucked within the labyrinthine lanes of Fez's ancient medina, Riad F\u00e8s unfolds around tranquil courtyards where reflecting pools, carved cedar and zellige tilework speak of centuries of Moroccan craftsmanship. Rooftop terraces frame views across minarets to the Atlas foothills, while candlelit dinners celebrate Fassi culinary traditions. Artisans from the surrounding souks maintain the riad's intricate detail, sustaining skills passed through generations. Days here might begin at the tanneries and end in the hammam's fragrant steam.

property_title: Miracle Manor Boutique Hotel & Spa: Desert Hot Springs Serenity
property_intro: Set on the quiet edge of Desert Hot Springs, with the San Jacinto mountains rising beyond the creosote, Miracle Manor is a restored 1948 hideaway of just six rooms. Mineral water rises naturally into the pool and tubs, while the spa offers unhurried treatments and yoga beneath desert skies. Pared-back interiors, a wood-burning fire and starlit silence encourage genuine rest, with Joshua Tree National Park an easy morning's drive away.

property_title: Dimora delle Balze: Sicilian Serenity Amid Ancient Stone
property_intro: Set within the Val di Noto's baroque heartland, Dimora delle Balze occupies a nineteenth-century masseria surrounded by olive groves, dry-stone walls and the wild Cavagrande gorges. Restored with reverence, its vaulted rooms pair honeyed limestone with contemporary calm. Days unfold slowly here: swimming beneath carob trees, foraging with local growers, or wandering to Noto's golden facades. The estate champions Sicilian artisans and native planting, offering a stay that feels rooted, unhurried and quietly generous.

property_title: Les Etangs de Corot Hôtel: Painterly Calm Near Ville-d'Avray
property_intro: Just beyond Paris, in the wooded village of Ville-d'Avray, Les Etangs de Corot gathers a cluster of pastel-shuttered houses around the ponds that once captivated the painter Corot. Days unfold slowly here: forest walks before breakfast, treatments at the Caudalie vinotherapy spa, long lunches of seasonal French cooking. Interiors nod to nineteenth-century landscape artists without pastiche, while the surrounding parkland and protected waters remain quietly tended, a rare pocket of stillness minutes from the capital.

property_title: Lupaia: A Tuscan Farmhouse Retreat Above Montepulciano
property_intro: Set among the rolling farmland of southern Tuscany, within sight of Montepulciano's honeyed hilltop, Lupaia is a restored hamlet where centuries-old stone meets linen, antique timber and quiet, considered comfort. Just ten suites look out across vineyards and cypress-lined ridges. Days unfold slowly here: kitchen-garden dinners drawn from the surrounding land, cellar visits with local growers, long afternoons beside the pool. The family behind it farms sustainably, championing regional producers and the artisans who shaped every room.

property_title: Hôtel Grand Cœur Latin: Parisian Soul in the Latin Quarter
property_intro: Tucked among the bookshops and bistros of Paris's Latin Quarter, Hôtel Grand Cœur Latin offers a quietly considered welcome moments from the Panthéon and the Seine. Interiors pair restored Haussmannian details with contemporary craftsmanship, much of it sourced from French ateliers. Mornings begin with pastries from the neighbourhood boulangerie; evenings invite conversation in the salon. Staff share their own favourite walks, hidden courtyards and vineyard-lined lanes, making this feel less like a hotel and more like a Parisian address of your own.

property_title: Muare Tulum Hotel: Barefoot Sophistication by the Caribbean
property_intro: Set between the jungle's green hush and Tulum's turquoise shallows, Muare Tulum Hotel offers a quieter interpretation of coastal living. Rooms are shaped from local wood, stone and lime plaster, with breezes doing the work of air conditioning. Days unfold slowly: cenote swims, cycling to the Mayan ruins, long dinners of Yucatecan cooking sourced from nearby growers. The hotel supports regional reef monitoring and hires locally, so your stay quietly sustains the coastline that makes it so compelling.

property_title: Ad Astra: Starlit Italian Escapes Rooted in Land and Craft
property_intro: Set within the quiet folds of the Italian countryside, Ad Astra invites you to slow down beneath famously clear night skies. Restored stonework, handwoven textiles and locally made furnishings give the interiors a gentle, lived-in warmth. Days might unfold with olive groves and village markets, evenings with regional wines poured by those who made them. Working closely with neighbouring farmers and artisans, the house supports the traditions that shape this landscape, and welcomes you into them.

property_title: Karawan Riad: Fez's Artisan Heart, Reimagined in Quiet Luxury
property_intro: Tucked within the labyrinthine lanes of Fez's ancient medina, Karawan Riad occupies a lovingly restored 19th-century townhouse where zellige tilework, carved cedar and hand-cut plaster have been revived by local maalems. Courtyards open to the Moroccan sky, rooftop terraces frame the Atlas foothills, and mornings begin with mint tea and warm msemen. Guests are invited into the medina's living traditions, from tannery visits to slow suppers, with craftsmanship sustained through every stay.

property_title: OPUS Vancouver: Spirited Design in Yaletown's Creative Heart
property_intro: Set among the red-brick warehouses and waterfront promenades of Yaletown, OPUS Vancouver brings colour and character to one of the city's most spirited neighbourhoods. Rooms are shaped around distinct personalities, with bold palettes, curated art and windows framing False Creek and the North Shore mountains. Days might begin with a cycle along the seawall and end with cocktails poured by locals who know every hidden gem. Independent makers, chefs and artists are championed throughout, keeping the hotel rooted in its community.

property_title: White Desert Camp: Luxury Amid Antarctica's Endless Ice
property_intro: Set beside the Wolf's Fang runway in Queen Maud Land, White Desert Camp places you within a landscape of granite spires, wind-carved blue ice and light that never quite fades. Heated fibreglass pods echo the form of Antarctic snow drifts, while chefs, guides and mountaineers make the interior feel improbably warm. Days bring ice tunnels, summit climbs and emperor penguin colonies. The camp runs carbon-neutral, leaving nothing behind but footprints in the snow.

property_title: andBeyond Sossusvlei Desert Lodge: Namibia's Starlit Sands
property_intro: Set within the vast Namib Rand Reserve, andBeyond Sossusvlei Desert Lodge looks out across ancient dunes and quartz-strewn plains shaped over millions of years. Ten glass-fronted suites frame the shifting light, each with a private plunge pool and skylight above the bed for nights spent watching one of the world's darkest skies. Days bring guided dune walks, e-fat-bike rides and stargazing through the lodge's observatory, while conservation work protects this fragile desert and supports neighbouring communities.

property_title: Mt Isthmus Villa: Alpine Serenity Above Lake Wānaka's Shores
property_intro: Set high on a tussock ridge with Lake Wānaka glinting below and the Southern Alps rising beyond, Mt Isthmus Villa offers a rare kind of quiet. Architect-designed with schist, timber and vast glazing, the villa frames the landscape rather than competing with it. Days unfold with guided high-country walks, vineyard visits and lakeside swims, while ongoing native planting and predator control on the surrounding station help this remarkable corner of Otago flourish for generations.

property_title: Sheldon Chalet: A Glacier Eyrie in Alaska's Denali Wilderness
property_intro: Perched on a granite outcrop within Denali National Park, Sheldon Chalet is reached only by helicopter, settling guests onto the Ruth Glacier amid mile-deep ice and cathedral peaks. Five rooms, warm timber and vast windows frame the aurora and midnight sun. Days unfold with glacier trekking, crevasse exploring and storytelling shaped by the Sheldon family's decades of Alaskan stewardship, while chefs, guides and conservation partners keep this remarkable wilderness quietly protected.

property_title: Pumphouse Point: Wilderness Stillness on Lake St Clair, Tasmania
property_intro: Suspended above the glacial waters of Lake St Clair, this reimagined 1940s hydro-electric pumphouse sits at the end of a 250-metre flume in Tasmania's World Heritage wilderness. Industrial bones meet considered comfort here: honest concrete, Tasmanian timber and an honesty larder stocked with island produce. Days unfold with lakeside walks, wallaby sightings and swims in impossibly clear water, while evenings belong to fireside conversation. No televisions, little signal deep, restorative quiet instead.

property_title: Velaa Private Island Maldives: Barefoot Elegance, Perfected
property_intro: Cradled by the turquoise waters of Noonu Atoll, Velaa Private Island is a quietly confident retreat where Maldivian craftsmanship meets Czech artistry. Thatched villas curve around a private lagoon, while a submerged wine cellar, golf academy and Aquum spa reward the curious. Dine above the water at Aragu, glide over coral gardens with resident marine biologists, or simply let the tides set your pace. Reef restoration and island-grown produce underpin every gracious detail here.

property_title: Keemala: Treetop Living in Phuket's Emerald Rainforest Hills
property_intro: Set on a forested hillside above Kamala village, Keemala reimagines Phuket beyond its beaches. Clay cottages, tented villas and bird's-nest pavilions draw on the folklore of four fictional clans, each dwelling cradled by rainforest and framed by views to the Andaman Sea. Days unfold with holistic spa rituals, plant-led dining and forest walks, while the resort's organic gardens, water recycling and support for Kamala's community give this hillside hideaway genuine depth.

property_title: Acre Resort: Treehouse Living Among Baja's Verdant Palm Groves
property_intro: Tucked into a 25-acre palm grove in the San Josu00e9 del Cabo valley, Acre Resort feels worlds away from the Baja coastline just minutes down the road. Treehouse suites rise on stilts among the fronds, shaded and quiet, while the kitchen draws on the property's own farm and the day's catch from nearby fishermen. Days drift between the mezcal bar, horseback rides through the arroyo and the animal sanctuary, tended by the local team.

property_title: Mandai Rainforest Resort: Where Singapore's Wild Heart Beats
property_intro: Tucked into the green folds of Singapore's Mandai Wildlife Reserve, this treehouse-inspired retreat rises on stilts above the forest floor, leaving root systems and rainwater channels undisturbed. Rooms open onto canopy views, some with private pools that seem to spill into the trees. Wander to neighbouring wildlife parks, join guided nature walks at dawn, or simply listen as hornbills and cicadas take over from the city. Conservation funding is woven into every stay.

property_title: EOLO – Patagonia's Spirit: Where the Steppe Meets Quiet Luxury
property_intro: Set on a 4,000-hectare estancia between El Calafate and the Perito Moreno glacier, EOLO stands alone on the open Patagonian steppe, with Lago Argentino shimmering in the distance. Just seventeen rooms occupy this restored ranch house, where sheepskin, weathered timber and vast windows frame the horizon. Ride with the estancia's gauchos, walk to hidden lagoons alive with flamingos, then return for Patagonian lamb and Argentine wine. Land, wildlife and local craft are quietly protected here.

property_title: Amanjiwo: Sunrise Over Borobudur in Java's Sacred Kedu Valley
property_intro: Cradled by four volcanoes and the emerald terraces of Java's Kedu Valley, Amanjiwo gazes directly towards Borobudur, the world's largest Buddhist monument. Ed Tuttle's rotunda and limestone suites echo the temple's own geometry, opening to rice fields worked as they have been for centuries. Wander to dawn ceremonies, learn gamelan or shadow puppetry with village artisans, and cycle lanes where the resort supports local schools, farmers and craftspeople. Refined, unhurried and quietly rooted in place.

property_title: Hoanib Skeleton Coast Camp: Where the Desert Meets the Sea
property_intro: Set deep in the Kaokoveld between the Hoanib riverbed and Namibia's fog-bound Skeleton Coast, this remote camp offers solitude on a remarkable scale. Eight canvas suites sit lightly on the gravel plains, cooled by desert breezes and solar-powered throughout. Track desert-adapted lions and elephants with researchers, fly to the coast to meet the Cape fur seal colonies, and share stories with Himba and Herero neighbours who co-own the surrounding conservancies with genuine pride.

property_title: Nayara Bocas del Toro: Overwater Living on Panama's Caribbean
property_intro: Reached only by boat, Nayara Bocas del Toro floats above the turquoise shallows of Bahia Honda, where dolphins pass beneath the villas and the rainforest of Isla Bastimentos rises behind. Thatched suites, crafted with local materials and artisan skill, open straight onto the sea. Days drift between snorkelling coral gardens, kayaking mangrove channels and visiting the Ngabe community whose knowledge shapes the resort's reforestation and sloth conservation work. Barefoot, unhurried and quietly extraordinary.

property_title: Six Senses Krabey Island: Cambodia's Private Isle Sanctuary
property_intro: Just off Sihanoukville, Six Senses Krabey Island occupies a forested private isle in the Gulf of Thailand, reached by a short boat ride. Forty villas sit among tamarind and banyan trees, built from reclaimed timber and local stone, many with pools facing the water. Days unfold through Khmer cookery classes, kayaking to nearby fishing villages, treatments in the cliffside spa and reef restoration with the resident marine team. Rainwater is harvested on site; produce comes from neighbouring farms.

property_title: Nomade Holbox: Barefoot Rituals on Mexico's Wild Island Shore
property_intro: On a car-free island north of the Yucat\n

property_title: Chale Island Resort: A Private Coral Isle Off Kenya's South Coast
property_intro: Just south of Diani, a shallow lagoon separates the mainland from Chale Island, a coral outcrop fringed by mangroves and a sacred forest still tended by Digo elders. The resort's thatched suites open onto white sand, with kayaks, dhow sails and reef dives filling unhurried days. Marine conservation work protects the surrounding sanctuary, while the kitchen draws on Swahili coastal traditions and nearby villages. Arrive at low tide and the island feels entirely your own.

property_title: Chole Mjini Treehouse Lodge: Barefoot Living in Mafia's Baobabs
property_intro: On the tiny island of Chole, off Mafia's mangrove-fringed coast, seven open-sided treehouses rest among ancient baobabs and the ruins of a Swahili trading settlement. Days here move to the tide: snorkelling coral gardens, sailing by dhow, drifting past flying foxes at dusk. Built with local craftsmanship and no electricity, the lodge channels its income into the island's school, clinic and marine protection, so your stay quietly sustains the community that shapes it.

property_title: Mwiba Lodge: Wild Serenity on Tanzania's Southern Serengeti
property_intro: Tucked into a granite-strewn valley on the edge of the Serengeti's southern plains, Mwiba Lodge overlooks the Arugusinyai River, where elephants drift through shaded woodland and leopards rest on warm rock. Suites of timber, stone and canvas open to sweeping views, while days unfold with guided walks, night drives and time with the Hadzabe community. Set within a 50,000-hectare private reserve, your stay directly supports its rewilding, anti-poaching patrols and neighbouring Maasai livelihoods.

property_title: Bwindi Lodge: Mist, Mountain Gorillas and Impenetrable Forest
property_intro: Perched on a ridge facing Bwindi Impenetrable Forest, this intimate lodge places you within earshot of one of the world's last mountain gorilla strongholds. Eight banda-style cottages, crafted from local timber and stone, open onto a tangle of green where hornbills call at dawn. Days begin with a guided trek into ancient forest and end beside the fire, tea in hand. Your stay supports Batwa community projects and gorilla conservation across the region.

property_title: Airelles Pan Deï Palais: A Provençal Romance in Saint-Tropez
property_intro: Tucked into a quiet lane in the heart of Saint-Tropez, Airelles Pan Deï Palais began as a love story: a palace built for an Indian princess in 1835. Today, its twelve rooms and suites blend Mughal detail with Provençal calm, opening onto a fragrant garden and pool moments from the harbour. Expect Ayurvedic-inspired treatments, market strolls with the chef and vineyard visits nearby, alongside a genuine commitment to local artisans and producers.

property_title: Cap Estel: A Private Riviera Peninsula Between Sea and Sky
property_intro: Set on its own peninsula between Nice and Monaco, Cap Estel occupies two hectares of terraced gardens that slip gently towards the Mediterranean. Once a private villa, this intimate retreat holds just a handful of suites, each opening to sea views and the scent of citrus and pine. Days unfold slowly here: swimming in the seawater pool, dining on produce from nearby Provençal growers, or wandering coastal paths favoured by Èze villagers long before the Riviera found fame.

property_title: Ambiente Sedona: Mirrored Cubes Amid Red Rock Wilderness
property_intro: Set among the juniper and red rock of Sedona, Arizona, Ambiente invites you into forty mirrored cubes raised above the desert floor, each reflecting the shifting light of the canyons. Floor-to-ceiling glass frames the sandstone spires, while rooftop decks open to some of the darkest skies in the American Southwest. Built with minimal disturbance to the land and guided by dark-sky principles, it pairs spa rituals and Sonoran-inspired dining with genuine reverence for its surroundings.

property_title: Hassler Roma: A Storied Grande Dame Crowning the Spanish Steps
property_intro: Perched at the top of the Spanish Steps, the Hassler has welcomed guests since 1893 and remains in the hands of the Wirth family, whose sixth-generation stewardship shows in every detail. Rooms are individually dressed in Roman antiques and hand-loomed silks, while Imàgo's Michelin-starred kitchen looks out over a sea of terracotta rooftops. Slip into Trinità dei Monti at dawn, browse Via Condotti with a private guide, then retreat to the fragrant rooftop garden.

property_title: Grantley Hall: Georgian Splendour by Yorkshire's River Skell
property_intro: Set in 30 acres of gardens and woodland on the edge of the Yorkshire Dales, Grantley Hall pairs a lovingly restored 17th-century house with a spirit of quiet ambition. Fountains Abbey lies moments away, while inside you'll find three distinct restaurants, an ELITE performance spa and interiors that reward slow exploration. Kitchen gardens supply the menus, local makers and producers shape the experience, and Ripon's countryside stays gloriously close at hand.

property_title: Palazzo Avino: Ravello's Pink Palace Above the Amalfi Coast
property_intro: Perched high above Amalfi's shimmering water, Palazzo Avino occupies a 12th-century villa in Ravello, a hillside town long favoured by composers and writers. Family-run for four decades, it blends antique majolica, frescoed ceilings and lemon-scented terraces with warm, unhurried hospitality. Days might mean cookery lessons with local producers, a boat trip along the coast, or lazy hours at the Clubhouse beach club below. Michelin-starred dining celebrates Campanian growers, while the Avino family's patronage keeps Ravello's artisan traditions thriving.

property_title: Palais Coburg: Viennese Grandeur Above Legendary Wine Cellars
property_intro: Perched on Vienna's old city bastion, Palais Coburg looks over the Stadtpark and the Ringstrasse, moments from the State Opera. Behind its columned facade, 35 generous suites blend restored 19th-century detail with quiet contemporary calm. Beneath your feet lie six historic cellars holding one of the world's most remarkable wine collections, explored through tastings led by resident sommeliers. Kitchen gardens, thoughtful sourcing and careful stewardship of the building itself shape every stay here.

property_title: The Ashbee Hotel: Timeless Sicilian Grace Above the Ionian Sea
property_intro: Perched on Taormina's clifftop, The Ashbee Hotel occupies a 1908 villa designed by British architect Charles Robert Ashbee, its Arts and Crafts spirit still shaping every terrace and tiled corridor. Below, the Ionian Sea shifts colour through the day; behind, Etna smoulders quietly. Days unfold with Sicilian cooking rooted in nearby farms, garden swims among century-old cypresses, and walks into town along ancient lanes. Restored with care, it remains a house that rewards slow, curious guests.

property_title: Royal Champagne Hotel & Spa: Vineyard Views and Quiet Luxury
property_intro: Set into the hillside above Champillon, this former coaching inn looks out across a sweep of Grand Cru vineyards towards \u00c9pernay. Terraced rooms open to those views, while the subterranean spa draws on thermal-inspired waters and long, unhurried afternoons. Menus follow the seasons and the region's growers, and cellar visits are led by neighbours who tend these slopes. Come for the Champagne, stay for the stillness, the birdsong and the light shifting over the valley.

property_title: Hôtel Barrière Le Royal: Belle Époque Grace by Deauville Sea
property_intro: Overlooking the English Channel on Deauville's celebrated seafront, Hôtel Barrière Le Royal has welcomed guests since 1913, its Belle Époque façade softened by Normandy light. Interiors balance heritage detail with easy comfort, while a spa, sea-facing terraces and kitchens led by regional producers invite lingering. Beyond the boardwalk lie horse country, apple orchards and cliff paths, and the hotel's commitment to local suppliers and coastal preservation keeps Deauville's character intact. Arrive curious; leave unhurried.

property_title: Le K2 Chogori: Himalayan Soul in the Heights of Val d'Isere
property_intro: Perched above Val d'Isere with the Bellevarde slopes at its threshold, Le K2 Chogori draws its spirit from the Karakoram: hand-carved Nepalese woodwork, Tibetan textiles and warm alpine timber shape interiors that feel collected rather than styled. Days unfold between fresh powder, the mountain-view spa and dining that celebrates Savoyard producers. Locally sourced materials, family stewardship and long-standing ties to Himalayan artisans give this retreat a rare sense of place and purpose.

property_title: Relais San Maurizio: Piedmont's Vineyard Monastery Retreat
property_intro: Set within a 17th-century monastery above the vine-striped hills of Langhe, Relais San Maurizio looks out across Piedmont's Barolo and Barbaresco country. Cloisters and frescoed halls now shelter serene rooms, a truffle-scented kitchen and a spa carved into the former cellars. Days unfold with harvest walks, tastings with neighbouring growers and slow lunches sourced from the estate garden. It is a place where restoration, regional craft and quiet hospitality meet, and where UNESCO-listed landscapes begin at the doorstep.

property_title: A Bavarian Welcome in the Heart of the Rockies: Sonnenalp Vail
property_intro: Tucked beside Gore Creek in the heart of Vail Village, Sonnenalp has been cared for by the same Bavarian family for generations. Hand-carved timber, warm woollen textures and a spring-fed spa set a tone of unhurried comfort, with the Gore Range rising just beyond the door. Ski mornings ease into long afternoons; summer brings golf, fly-fishing and mountain trails. Family-run and community-minded, the hotel invests quietly in Vail's people and landscapes.

property_title: El Palace Hotel Barcelona: Belle Époque Splendour on Gran Via
property_intro: Set on the elegant Gran Via, moments from the Passeig de Gràcia's Modernista façades, El Palace has welcomed guests since 1919 with a particular kind of Catalan grace. Marble staircases and hand-painted frescoes meet a rooftop garden with Mediterranean views, while the spa offers Barcelona's original Mayan ritual. Expect gin-tasting in the storied bar, produce from local growers in the kitchens, and long-standing partnerships with city charities that quietly shape the neighbourhood.

property_title: Hotel Bayerischer Hof: Munich's Grand Address Reimagined
property_intro: In the heart of Munich, moments from Marienplatz and the Residenz, Hotel Bayerischer Hof has welcomed guests since 1841 while remaining resolutely family-run. Behind its historic facade, interiors by Axel Vervoordt and Antonio Citterio sit alongside a rooftop spa, six restaurants and a cinema and jazz club that draw locals as readily as travellers. Bavarian produce shapes the menus, and generations of the Volkhardt family continue to champion the city's cultural life.

property_title: Aleenta Retreat Chiang Mai: Riverside Calm in Northern Thailand
property_intro: Set beside the Ping River amid rice fields and distant hills, Aleenta Retreat Chiang Mai offers just a handful of suites and villas, each opening to water, garden or sky. Days unfold with Ayurah spa rituals, yoga on the lawn, cycling through nearby villages and market visits with the kitchen team. Lanna craftsmanship shapes the interiors, while the retreat's Pure Blue Foundation supports local reforestation and community projects across northern Thailand.

property_title: H\u00f4tel Le Grand Mazarin: Theatrical Splendour in the Marais
property_intro: Tucked into a quiet street in the heart of the Marais, H\u00f4tel Le Grand Mazarin brings a sense of playful grandeur to Paris. Interiors layer Venetian colour, hand-painted motifs and antique curiosities into rooms that feel collected rather than decorated. Downstairs, Boubal\u00e9 serves warm, generous Jewish-inspired cooking, while the vaulted pool and hammam offer respite from the cobbles. Galleries, bakeries and independent boutiques wait just beyond the door, inviting unhurried wandering.

property_name: Aleenta Phuket - Phang Nga Resort & Spa
property_title: Aleenta Phuket - Phang Nga Resort & Spa: Barefoot Coastal Calm
property_intro: Set along a quiet stretch of Natai Beach, just north of Phuket, Aleenta Phuket - Phang Nga Resort & Spa trades crowds for eight kilometres of soft sand and uninterrupted Andaman sunsets. Suites and villas open directly to the shore, with pared-back design and private pools framing the horizon. Days drift between the Ayurah spa, seafood shaped by local growers, and turtle conservation work supported by the resort's own marine foundation.

property_title: Six Senses Bhutan: Five Himalayan Valleys, One Soulful Journey
property_intro: Strung across five valleys, from Thimphu's pine-clad ridges to the rice terraces of Punakha and Bumthang's ancient temples, Six Senses Bhutan invites you to travel slowly through the kingdom's heart. Each lodge takes its cue from local craft and dzong architecture, framing views of fortresses, farmhouses and forest. Days might bring archery with villagers, hot stone baths, or a hike to a cliffside monastery, while guides, growers and artisans from nearby communities share their world with you.

property_title: Cap Karoso: Where Sumba's Untamed West Coast Meets Slow Luxury
property_intro: On the far west shore of Sumba, where rice terraces tumble towards a wide grey-sand beach, Cap Karoso occupies a stretch of coast few travellers have yet discovered. Its architecture is spare and sculptural, softened by rattan, timber and Indonesian craft. Days unfold between two pools, a working farm supplying the kitchens, surf breaks and visiting chefs. Village partnerships, local hiring and regenerative growing give the place its quiet purpose, and its considerable charm.

property_title: Lengishu: An Exclusive-Use Home in Kenya's Borana Conservancy
property_intro: High on a hillside in Kenya's Borana Conservancy, Lengishu looks across rolling grassland to the snow-flecked peaks of Mount Kenya. This six-bedroom house is yours alone, shaped from local stone and timber with an easy, uncluttered elegance. Days unfold on horseback, on foot with Samburu guides, or tracking black rhino across the Borana-Lewa wilderness. Your stay directly supports the conservancy's rhino protection and the schools and clinics of neighbouring communities.

property_title: Bawah Reserve: Barefoot Luxury Among Indonesia's Anambas Isles
property_intro: Reached by seaplane from Singapore, Bawah Reserve unfolds across six islands in the remote Anambas archipelago, where thirteen beaches and three lagoons lie within a protected marine park. Suites and overwater bungalows are crafted by hand from reclaimed timber, bamboo and copper, without a single nail. Days drift between snorkelling coral gardens, jungle treks and treatments at the Aura spa, while reef restoration and local employment keep this rare corner of Indonesia thriving.

property_title: Das Kranzbach: Alpine Stillness in a Bavarian Meadow Retreat
property_intro: Set at 1,000 metres in a sunlit clearing beneath the Wetterstein range, Das Kranzbach began life as an English countess's mountain manor and still carries that quiet, eccentric charm. Arts and Crafts interiors meet locally sourced larch and spruce, while the vast spa draws on mountain spring water. Days unfold with meadow walks, forest bathing and Bavarian dishes made from neighbouring farms' produce. Adults only, blissfully phone-free in the lounges, and refreshingly unhurried throughout.

property_title: Fontsanta Hotel Thermal Spa: Mallorca's Ancient Thermal Springs
property_intro: Tucked between the salt flats of Es Trenc and the quiet farmland of Campos, this restored 19th-century estate guards the only thermal spring on Mallorca, its mineral waters rising warm from the earth as they have for centuries. Days unfold slowly here: salt-water treatments, garden-grown suppers, cycling through almond groves. Interiors pair honeyed stone with understated Balearic craft, while the surrounding nature reserve is carefully protected, keeping the birdsong and the starlight beautifully intact.

property_title: The Golden Door: A Californian Sanctuary of Quiet Renewal
property_intro: Set across 600 acres of citrus groves and chaparral-covered hills in San Marcos, California, The Golden Door welcomes just 40 guests each week. Japanese-inspired architecture, koi ponds and raked gardens frame days of mountain hiking, bathhouse rituals and produce gathered that morning from the organic farm. Programmes are shaped around your own pace rather than a fixed schedule. Remarkably, all profits support charities working to protect children from abuse and exploitation.

property_title: &Beyond Punakha River Lodge: A Himalayan Riverside Sanctuary
property_intro: Set along the banks of the Mo Chhu in Bhutan's temperate Punakha Valley, this intimate lodge pairs six tented suites and a handful of villas with views of rice terraces and forested ridges. Days unfold with river rafting, valley hikes to hilltop temples and unhurried conversations with local farmers and monks. Interiors draw on Bhutanese craft and natural materials, while the lodge supports village livelihoods, regional artisans and the kingdom's remarkable commitment to carbon-negative living.

property_title: Amrit Bhawan: A Graceful Heritage Retreat in Rural India
property_intro: Set among mustard fields and slow village lanes, Amrit Bhawan is a restored family residence where hand-carved sandstone, block-printed textiles and shaded courtyards tell of generations past. Days unfold gently here: dawn birdsong from the terrace, cooking with produce from the kitchen garden, and walks with local artisans who keep regional crafts alive. Solar power, rainwater harvesting and fair employment for neighbouring households underpin every stay, making comfort feel quietly considered rather than merely indulgent.

property_title: Anopura: A Rajasthani Retreat Where Stillness Feels Sacred
property_intro: Set among the boulder-strewn hills outside Jaipur, Anopura is a gathering of hand-built cottages where lime-washed walls, local sandstone and Rajasthani craftsmanship meet a landscape of scrub, peacocks and long horizons. Days unfold slowly here: village walks with the family who built it, cooking over wood fires, star-lit dinners in the courtyard. Rainwater harvesting, native planting and lasting village partnerships underpin it all, making this less a hotel than an invitation into rural Rajasthan's quiet rhythm.

property_title: Chunda Shikar Oudi: A Royal Hunting Retreat Above Udaipur
property_intro: Perched on a ridge in the Aravalli hills above Udaipur, Chunda Shikar Oudi began life as a Mewar hunting lodge and now welcomes guests as an intimate retreat of just a handful of suites. Days unfold with leopard-spotting drives in Sajjangarh Sanctuary, village walks and dinners beneath the stars, while heritage craftsmanship fills every corner. The family-run estate employs and trains villagers from surrounding hamlets, keeping Rajasthani artistry and hospitality traditions genuinely alive.

property_title: Daspan House: Heritage, Wilderness and Warmth in Rajasthan
property_intro: Set amid the scrub and rocky outcrops of rural Rajasthan, Daspan House is a family-owned fort turned intimate retreat, where generations of hosts still welcome guests in person. Rooms are dressed in hand-blocked textiles and antique furniture, while courtyards catch the late light. Days unfold with village walks, birdwatching in the surrounding hills, and cooking sessions with local women. Water conservation and craft revival underpin everything, making each stay quietly consequential as well as deeply comfortable.

property_title: Devshree Deogarh: Rajasthan's Aravalli Hills, Quietly Regal
