property_intro: Set above the village of Deogarh in Rajasthan's Aravalli hills, Devshree is a nobleman's home turned intimate retreat, where eight rooms open onto gardens, a pool and views towards distant temples. Days unfold with birdwatching by the lake, walks to Rabari shepherd settlements and long lunches drawn from the kitchen garden. Family heirlooms and hand-blocked textiles fill the rooms, while local guides, artisans and farmers share in the hospitality that sustains this corner of the countryside.

property_title: Fort Rajwada: Golden Sandstone Splendour in the Thar Desert
property_intro: On the fringes of Jaisalmer, where the Thar Desert meets a skyline of honey-hued ramparts, Fort Rajwada rises in locally quarried sandstone, shaped by craftsmen versed in Rajasthan's traditional building arts. Carved jharokhas, hand-painted frescoes and a soaring courtyard set the mood for evenings of folk music beneath the stars. Days unfold with camel rides across dunes, heritage walks through the living fort, and Marwari cuisine prepared with produce and skills drawn from surrounding villages.

property_title: Coco Tangalle: Barefoot Elegance on Sri Lanka's Southern Shore
property_intro: Tucked between a coconut grove and the wide sweep of Tangalle's coastline, Coco Tangalle is a small collection of villas where the Indian Ocean sets the rhythm of the day. Interiors blend Sri Lankan craftsmanship with cool, uncluttered calm, while the kitchen draws on the morning's catch and produce from nearby smallholdings. Spend your days watching turtles nest, wandering to Rekawa lagoon, or simply lingering under the palms with something cold in hand.

property_title: Mela Kothi Chambal Safari Lodge: Ravines, Rivers and Rare Life
property_intro: Set within a family-grown forest on the edge of the National Chambal Sanctuary in Uttar Pradesh, Mela Kothi is a restored farmhouse of whitewashed verandahs, heirloom furniture and unhurried afternoons. Days begin with boat journeys along the Chambal in search of gharial, river dolphins and skimmers, and end beside ravines glowing amber at dusk. Run by conservationists who helped protect this river, the lodge supports local communities, guides and craftspeople throughout.

property_title: Mosvold Villa: Refined Coastal Seclusion in Southern Sri Lanka
property_intro: Set among swaying coconut palms on Sri Lanka's southern coast, Mosvold Villa offers a rare kind of quiet. Restored with Scandinavian restraint and local craftsmanship, its airy rooms open onto gardens where paddy birds gather at dawn. Days unfold with slow breakfasts, surf breaks nearby, and cookery lessons led by neighbours who supply the kitchen. The villa supports village schooling and coastal conservation, so your stay leaves something meaningful behind.

property_title: Sundara By Mosvold: Barefoot Luxury on Sri Lanka's Wild Coast
property_intro: Set among coconut groves on Sri Lanka's untamed south-eastern shore, Sundara By Mosvold pairs breezy, light-filled villas with the rhythm of the Indian Ocean. Days unfold slowly here: surfing at dawn, leopard-spotting in nearby Yala, long lunches drawn from the kitchen garden. Handcrafted interiors celebrate local artisans, while the family behind it invests in coastal conservation and village livelihoods. It's a place where indulgence feels quietly purposeful, and the shoreline remains delightfully your own.

property_title: Flameback Eco Lodge: Barefoot Luxury Beside Sri Lanka's Wilds
property_intro: On the fringes of Udawalawe National Park, Flameback Eco Lodge sits amid paddy fields, tamarind trees and birdsong, where elephants pass along ancient corridors at dusk. Rooms are built from local timber and stone, cooled by breezes rather than machinery, with verandas made for slow mornings. Days unfold with guided safaris, village walks and dinners drawn from nearby smallholdings. Solar power, rainwater harvesting and local employment quietly underpin every stay here.

property_title: The Capoe House: Barefoot Elegance on Sri Lanka's Coast
property_intro: Set among swaying coconut palms on Sri Lanka's southern coastline, The Capoe House pairs colonial-era proportions with a relaxed, barefoot rhythm. Days unfold slowly here: breakfast on the veranda, a swim before the heat, then leisurely afternoons in shaded corners scented with frangipani. Interiors marry locally crafted teak, handloom textiles and antique finds, while the kitchen draws on village gardens and the morning catch. Nearby beaches, turtle sanctuaries and tea country reward the curious, unhurried traveller.

property_title: Rosewood Manor: Refined Colonial Calm in Sri Lanka's Hills
property_intro: Set among tea gardens and mist-softened ridges, Rosewood Manor is a restored colonial residence where polished teak floors, planter's chairs and hand-stitched linens invite unhurried days. Wander estate paths with a resident guide, learn the art of Ceylon tea tasting, or dine on produce grown in the kitchen garden. The Manor works closely with neighbouring villages, supporting local craftspeople and schooling, so every stay quietly strengthens the community that shapes its character.

property_title: Clingendael Weligama: Coastal Calm Above Sri Lanka's South
property_intro: Set on a breezy hillside above Weligama Bay, Clingendael is a private villa where colonial-era proportions meet the rhythms of Sri Lanka's southern coast. Days unfold slowly here: breakfast on the veranda, surf lessons in the bay below, then afternoons drifting between the pool and the garden's birdsong. Antique teak, handwoven textiles and local craftsmanship shape the interiors, while a small resident team, drawn from nearby villages, cooks, guides and shares the stories behind every dish.

property_title: Clingendael Kandy: A Hillside Retreat Above Sri Lanka's Lake
property_intro: Set high on a forested ridge above Kandy, Clingendael looks out across the sacred lake and the temple rooftops below. This colonial-era residence, thoughtfully restored, pairs antique teak and heirloom furnishings with wide verandahs made for slow mornings. Wander the terraced gardens, share stories with hosts who know every corner of the hill country, and return from Peradeniya or the Temple of the Tooth to home-cooked Sri Lankan dishes grown nearby.

property_title: The Last House: Geoffrey Bawa's Final Vision on Sri Lanka's Coast
property_intro: Set above a wide sweep of sand near Tangalle, on Sri Lanka's southern shore, The Last House was the final residence designed by celebrated architect Geoffrey Bawa. Six rooms sit around a courtyard of frangipani and cool terrazzo, where sea breezes do the work of air conditioning. Days unfold with lagoon boat trips, turtle hatchery visits and Sri Lankan cookery led by local chefs, while nearby fishing communities remain part of everyday life here.'}

property_title: Niravi: Barefoot Luxury Amid India's Green Coastal Calm
property_intro: Tucked between swaying palms and slow-moving backwaters, Niravi invites you to trade haste for something far more rewarding. Handcrafted interiors draw on local artistry, with reclaimed teak, terracotta and open verandahs framing the surrounding greenery. Days unfold with river paddles, market visits and kitchens fragrant with produce grown nearby or sourced from neighbouring farms. Rainwater harvesting and village partnerships underpin every stay, so your time here quietly strengthens the community that makes this place so distinctive.

property_title: Outpost 12: Where India's Wild Forest Frontier Feels Like Home
property_intro: Set on the fringes of tiger country, Outpost 12 is a small collection of tented rooms where lantern light, hand-woven textiles and locally quarried stone meet the hush of the surrounding forest. Days unfold with tracking walks led by naturalists raised in these villages, slow breakfasts under old trees and conversations with the guides who protect these corridors. Guest stays fund forest patrols and school programmes, so your quiet retreat leaves something lasting behind.

property_title: Pemako Thimphu: Riverside Serenity in Bhutan's Capital Valley
property_intro: Set along the Chuu river on the quiet fringes of Thimphu, Pemako unfolds across terraces of pine and blue poplar, moments from the capital's markets, monasteries and archery grounds. Interiors marry Bhutanese craftsmanship with contemporary calm, while the spa draws on hot-stone traditions and Himalayan herbs. Days might bring a dawn hike to Tango Monastery, a cookery lesson with local farmers, or slow evenings by the water. Artisans, growers and guides from surrounding villages shape every stay.

property_title: Raga Svara: Ayurveda & Wellness Retreats in the Himalayan Foothills
property_intro: Set above the Ganges near Rishikesh, Raga Svara unfolds across terraced gardens where Himalayan foothills meet forest and river light. Here, classical Ayurveda is practised with quiet precision: personalised panchakarma, yoga at dawn, and sattvic meals drawn from the estate's own harvest. Interiors favour local stone, handwoven textiles and craftsmanship from nearby villages, whose artisans and growers share in the retreat's work. Guests leave recalibrated, carrying something steadier than rest.

property_title: Saraca Resort & Spa, Corbett: Where the Wild Whispers Close
property_intro: On the fringes of Corbett's sal forests, where the Kosi River carves its way through the Kumaon foothills, Saraca Resort & Spa offers a considered kind of calm. Interiors draw on local craft and stone, opening onto gardens alive with birdsong. Days might begin with a jungle safari and close with an Ayurvedic ritual in the spa. The kitchen leans on Kumaoni growers, while conservation partnerships help protect the tigers and terrain just beyond your veranda.

property_title: Sarangkot Mountain Lodge: Himalayan Dawns Above Pokhara Valley
property_intro: Perched on the Sarangkot ridge above Pokhara, this intimate stone-and-timber lodge looks directly onto Annapurna and the fishtail peak of Machhapuchhre. Terraced gardens fall away towards the valley, where kites circle and village paths lead to hidden tea houses. Rooms are quietly considered, with local craftsmanship and wide windows framing the ranges. Days unfold with sunrise walks, Gurung home-cooking and guided ridge treks led by neighbours, whose families share in the lodge's earnings and forest care.

property_title: The Bamboo Forest Safari Lodge: Wild Luxury in Central India
property_intro: On the fringes of Pench Tiger Reserve in Madhya Pradesh, The Bamboo Forest Safari Lodge sits amid teak and bamboo groves where langurs call at first light. Earth-toned suites open onto private verandahs, while candlelit dinners draw on produce from surrounding villages. Days unfold with expert-led game drives, walks with naturalists and encounters with local Gond communities. Employing and training villagers from nearby hamlets, the lodge gives tangible weight to its conservation promise.

property_title: Rumbak Wildlife Lodge: Snow Leopard Country in Ladakh's Hills
property_intro: High in Ladakh's Rumbak Valley, within the folds of Hemis National Park, this intimate lodge sits among barley terraces and wind-scoured ridges where snow leopards move unseen. Rooms are warmed by local stone, timber and handwoven textiles, while village-run kitchens serve dishes rooted in Ladakhi tradition. Days unfold with expert trackers, monastery walks and long silences broken only by chough calls. Your stay supports the herding families who protect these mountains and their elusive residents.

property_title: The Riverwood Forest Retreat, Kanha: Where Sal Forests Whisper
property_intro: On the fringes of Kanha National Park, The Riverwood Forest Retreat sits among towering sal trees and quiet stream beds, a short drive from tiger territory. Villas open onto private verandas where langurs pass at dawn and the forest sets the rhythm of the day. Days unfold with guided safaris, birdsong walks and slow meals drawn from village farms nearby. Local naturalists share generational knowledge, while the retreat supports Baiga and Gond communities living alongside these woodlands.

property_title: The Serai Bandipur: Refined Wilderness on Karnataka's Forest Edge
property_intro: On the fringes of Bandipur Tiger Reserve, where the Western Ghats soften into coffee country, The Serai Bandipur sits quietly among mango orchards and lantana-fringed trails. Rooms open to birdsong and distant hills, their design drawing on local stone, timber and craft. Days unfold with safaris in search of tigers and elephants, guided walks with naturalists, and slow meals rooted in Karnataka's kitchens. The estate works closely with neighbouring villages, supporting livelihoods alongside habitat protection.

property_title: The Serai Chikmagalur: Coffee Country Calm in the Western Ghats
property_intro: Set within a working coffee estate in Karnataka's Western Ghats, The Serai Chikmagalur unfolds across hillsides scented with arabica blossom and wild pepper. Glass-fronted villas open onto plantation views, while private pools catch the mist that drifts down from Mullayanagiri. Days here might involve walking the estate with a planter, tracing the bean from cherry to cup, or simply listening to birdsong. Thoughtful design, local employment and careful stewardship shape every stay.

property_title: The Serai Kabini: Riverside Calm on Nagarhole's Wild Edge
property_intro: On the banks of the Kabini, where Karnataka's forests fold towards Nagarhole National Park, The Serai offers a quieter kind of luxury. Suites and villas of stone, teak and glass open to river light, while coracle rides, guided safaris and tribal village walks reveal a landscape shaped by elephants, leopards and the communities who have long lived alongside them. Local craftsmanship, regional cooking and thoughtful conservation partnerships give every stay a sense of place and purpose.

property_title: Kahani Paradise: A Hillside Retreat Above Karnataka's Coast
property_intro: Set high on a boulder-strewn hillside above Gokarna, Kahani Paradise looks across forest canopy to the Arabian Sea. This eight-room villa marries Indo-Portuguese craftsmanship with contemporary calm, its terraces shaded by mango and cashew trees. Days unfold with yoga at sunrise, cookery lessons in the open kitchen, or barefoot walks to near-empty beaches. The owners have replanted native species across the ridge and support local schooling, so your stay quietly nourishes the community that surrounds it.

property_title: Kumarakom Lake Resort: Backwater Living on Vembanad's Shore
property_intro: On the palm-fringed edge of Vembanad Lake in Kerala, Kumarakom Lake Resort unfolds like a heritage village, its tharavadu-style villas rescued from demolition and rebuilt beam by beam beside meandering water channels. Days pass slowly here: Ayurvedic therapies rooted in local tradition, meals of toddy-shop cooking and lake fish, and houseboat drifts past paddy fields. Bird sanctuaries lie moments away, and village artisans keep Kerala's crafts alive within the grounds themselves.

property_title: Coorg Wilderness Resort & Spa: Misty Mornings in Coffee Country
property_intro: Tucked into the forested folds of Karnataka's Western Ghats, Coorg Wilderness Resort & Spa looks out across coffee estates, cardamom groves and hills that hold the morning mist long past sunrise. Colonial-inspired interiors meet locally quarried stone and Kodava craftsmanship, while spacious suites open to birdsong and rain-washed greenery. Wander plantation trails with a resident naturalist, unwind with Ayurvedic therapies, and taste Kodava cuisine prepared with produce from neighbouring farms and estate-grown coffee.

property_title: Spicetree Munnar: Cloud-Level Calm Above Kerala's Tea Hills
property_intro: Perched high on a ridge in Kerala's Western Ghats, Spicetree Munnar looks out across tea gardens, cardamom slopes and valleys that fill with mist by mid-afternoon. Rooms open onto private plunge pools and vast views, while stonework and timber echo the plantation heritage around them. Days here unfold slowly: guided walks through spice country, conversations with local growers, Ayurvedic treatments and cuisine drawn from nearby farms. It is Munnar at its most considered, quietly rooted in its landscape.

property_title: Spicetree Chinnar: Riverside Calm at the Edge of the Wild
property_intro: Set along the Chinnar river where Kerala meets the Tamil Nadu border, Spicetree Chinnar sits within touching distance of a wildlife sanctuary known for its grizzled giant squirrels and elephant herds. Rooms open to birdsong and water, with interiors that favour local craft and quiet restraint over ornament. Days unfold with guided forest walks led by tribal naturalists, river dips and slow Kerala cooking, while the resort's conservation work supports the communities who call these hills home.

property_title: Rainforest Athirapally: Where Kerala's Waterfalls Set the Rhythm
property_intro: Perched at the edge of the Athirapally Falls in Kerala's Western Ghats, Rainforest Athirapally places you within earshot of thundering water and the calls of hornbills in the canopy beyond. Rooms open to a wall of green, while treehouse-style stays and riverside seating invite unhurried hours. Guided walks with local naturalists reveal the Sholayar forest's quieter secrets, and much of the kitchen's produce and craftsmanship comes from neighbouring villages, keeping the region's traditions thriving.

property_title: Indian Summer House: Coastal Calm and Colour in Goa, India
property_intro: Tucked between palm groves and the Arabian Sea, Indian Summer House invites you into a quieter side of Goa. Sunlit verandahs, antique Portuguese tiles and locally crafted furnishings set the tone, while breakfasts of seasonal fruit and hot poi arrive at your own pace. Wander to fishing villages, join Konkani cooking sessions, or swim at dawn. The house works closely with neighbouring artisans and beach-clean initiatives, so your stay leaves something behind.

property_title: Java Rain Resorts: A Hilltop Sanctuary in Chikmagalur's Hills
property_intro: Perched high above Chikmagalur on a ridge fringed by coffee plantations, Java Rain Resorts looks out towards Mullayanagiri, Karnataka's tallest peak. Days here unfold slowly: plantation walks with estate growers, cupping sessions that trace the bean from blossom to brew, and evenings wrapped in hill mist. Interiors favour local stone, timber and craft, while much of the team is drawn from surrounding villages, keeping the estate's rhythms and rainforest edges thoughtfully intact.

property_title: Spice Routes: Kerala's Backwaters, Spice Gardens and Slow Days
property_intro: Moored where Kerala's waterways slip past coir villages and pepper vines, Spice Routes gathers a handful of heritage-timber suites around courtyards scented with cardamom. Days unfold gently here: dawn canoe rides with local fishermen, Ayurvedic treatments, and cookery sessions led by neighbourhood matriarchs. Much of the produce arrives from the property's own organic plots, while a share of every stay supports backwater conservation and village schooling. Refined, unhurried, and quietly rooted in the place it calls home.

property_title: Brij Atmanya: A Deodar Hideaway High in the Garhwal Himalayas
property_intro: Set above Kanatal in Uttarakhand, Brij Atmanya rests among deodar and apple orchards, with the snow line of the Garhwal Himalayas rising beyond the valley. Days unfold gently here: forest walks with local guides, yoga on dew-cool terraces, Ayurvedic therapies and slow meals drawn from mountain kitchens. Interiors borrow from Pahari craft, warmed by stone and timber, while village partnerships and careful stewardship of the hillside keep the retreat rooted in its surroundings.

property_title: Brij Paraiso: Where Goa's Portuguese Heritage Meets Slow Luxury
property_intro: Tucked among the laterite lanes and leafy quiet of Goa's hinterland, Brij Paraiso is a restored Portuguese-era home where sunlight falls across azulejo tiles, high-ceilinged verandahs and a garden pool. Days unfold gently here: Goan-Saraswat cooking with local families, cycling to village bakeries, evenings scented with frangipani. The restoration keeps original craftsmanship and artisans' skills alive, while menus lean on neighbourhood farmers and fishermen. It is Goa at its most unhurried and quietly characterful.

property_title: Brij Sone Bagh — Where Rajasthan's Golden Gardens Welcome You
property_intro: Set within walled gardens in the Rajasthani countryside, Brij Sone Bagh unfolds slowly: shaded courtyards, birdsong at first light and interiors that pair hand-blocked textiles with quiet, contemporary calm. Days here might mean a cycle through farming hamlets, an unhurried lesson in regional cooking, or conversations with artisans whose crafts shape the rooms around you. Local families tend the kitchens and gardens, and heirloom produce reaches your table. Come for stillness; leave with a sense of belonging.

property_title: Uga Jungle Beach: Barefoot Elegance on Sri Lanka's Wild Coast
property_intro: Tucked between dense jungle and a private stretch of shoreline near Trincomalee, Uga Jungle Beach occupies one of Sri Lanka's least-trodden coastlines. Cabanas of timber, stone and clay sit beneath the canopy, opening towards the Indian Ocean's warm shallows. Days unfold with snorkelling at Pigeon Island, blue whale encounters, Ayurvedic treatments and cooking rooted in nearby villages. Coral regeneration and local employment quietly underpin it all, with luxury measured in birdsong, sea breeze and space to breathe.

property_title: Uga Bay: Coral-Fringed Serenity on Sri Lanka's Eastern Shore
property_intro: On the gentle curve of Passekudah Bay, where the Indian Ocean shallows for hundreds of metres and the water warms to bathwater calm, Uga Bay unfolds in whitewashed pavilions and sea-facing suites. Days drift between reef snorkelling, sunrise paddles and Sri Lankan cookery led by local chefs. Design nods to the island's maritime past, while coral restoration and partnerships with nearby fishing villages keep this quieter east coast thriving long after you leave.

property_title: Azuma Farm: Slow Living Among Japan's Orchards and Mountains
property_intro: Set among fruit orchards and rice terraces beneath Japan's mountain ridges, Azuma Farm invites you into the quiet rhythm of rural life. Timber-framed rooms open onto working fields, where guests gather produce at dawn, learn to ferment miso, or simply linger over tea as mist lifts from the valley. The farm supports neighbouring growers and revives heritage seed varieties, so every meal carries the story of the land and the hands that tend it.

property_title: Apukka Resort: Glass-Roofed Aurora Nights in Rovaniemi, Lapland
property_intro: Set on the shores of Lake Olkkajarvi, a short drive from Rovaniemi, Apukka Resort places you on the Arctic Circle where pine forest meets frozen water. Glass-roofed suites and timber cabins frame the aurora from bed, while days unfold through husky trails, reindeer herding with local Sami partners and ice fishing under low winter light. Small-group guiding, careful land stewardship and honest Lappish cooking keep the experience intimate rather than staged.

property_title: Sterrekopje Farm: A Restorative Retreat in the Franschhoek Valley
property_intro: Cradled by the mountains of the Franschhoek Valley, Sterrekopje Farm is a 300-year-old working farm reimagined as a place of healing. Eleven chambers are dressed in handwoven textiles, antiques and earthy tones, while regenerative gardens supply the kitchen table. Days unfold gently: harvesting vegetables, soaking in the hammam, riding horses through vineyards or simply resting. Run largely by women from the surrounding community, it is farming, artistry and care held in beautiful balance.

property_title: Spirit of Son Fuster: A Mallorcan Estate Between Mountains
property_intro: Tucked beneath the Tramuntana peaks near Alaró, Spirit of Son Fuster occupies a centuries-old Mallorcan finca surrounded by olive groves, almond trees and grazing sheep. Vaulted stone interiors meet contemporary Iberian craftsmanship, while the kitchen draws from the estate's own gardens and neighbouring farms. Days unfold with mountain walks, wine tastings and slow afternoons by the pool. Regenerative farming and long-standing island partnerships give this quietly confident retreat a genuine sense of place and purpose.

property_title: Åmot: Riverside Calm and Quiet Luxury in Rural Norway
property_intro: Set where forest meets river in Norway's gentle interior, Åmot invites you to slow to the rhythm of the water. Timber interiors, warm wool and generous windows frame birch groves and shifting northern light, while days unfold with wild swims, foraging walks and evenings beside the wood-fired stove. The estate works closely with local craftspeople and farmers, restoring old buildings with regional materials, so your stay quietly sustains the landscape and community that shape it.

property_title: Palás Cerequio: Barolo Suites Among Piedmont's Greatest Vines
property_intro: Set within the celebrated Cerequio cru at La Morra, this intimate Langhe retreat looks out over corduroy rows of Nebbiolo vines and the hilltop villages beyond. Nine suites, each named for a Barolo vineyard, pair contemporary calm with the warmth of the surrounding countryside. Days unfold with cellar tastings, walks between neighbouring wineries and slow Piedmontese cooking rooted in local producers. It is a place to understand Barolo from the inside, glass in hand, unhurried.

property_title: The Louise: Vineyard Seclusion in Australia's Barossa Valley
property_intro: Set among the ancient vines of South Australia's Barossa Valley, The Louise offers fifteen private suites, each with its own terrace framing rows of shiraz and distant ridgelines. Days unfold slowly here: cellar-door visits with fifth-generation winemakers, morning walks through the estate, and dinners at Appellation, where the kitchen draws on neighbouring growers and producers. The architecture stays low and unhurried, letting the valley speak. It is a place that rewards lingering, glass in hand, as the light shifts.

property_title: Domaine Les Crayères: Champagne Elegance Among the Vines
property_intro: Set within walled gardens on the edge of Reims, Domaine Les Crayères looks out across the chalk slopes that give Champagne its finesse. The château's high-ceilinged rooms pair antique detail with quiet comfort, while the kitchen draws on regional growers and the estate's own kitchen garden. Days unfold slowly here: tastings with small family houses, walks beneath ancient cedars, unhurried dinners as evening light shifts across the park. An address that rewards those who linger.

property_title: Copacabana Palace: Rio's Timeless Beachfront Grande Dame
property_intro: Facing the sweeping curve of Copacabana beach, this 1923 Art Deco landmark has shaped Rio's social life for a century, hosting artists, royalty and Hollywood alike. Marble corridors, hand-painted tiles and a famed poolside terrace set the scene, while Cipriani's kitchen and rooftop tennis fill the days. Beyond the facade, the hotel champions Brazilian craft, cuisine and local hiring, and guests can slip easily into Ipanema's galleries or Tijuca's forested trails.

property_title: Domaine des Etangs: A Storied Château Amid Charente's Wild Lakes
property_intro: Deep in the Charente countryside, Domaine des Etangs unfolds across a thousand hectares of woodland, meadow and mirror-still lakes. A restored medieval château and its cluster of farmhouses hold rooms where contemporary art meets stone and linen, quietly elegant rather than showy. Days pass with lake swims, forest walks, horses, and produce gathered from the kitchen garden for the Michelin-starred table. Rewilded land, revived crafts and local livelihoods make this a place with genuine roots.

property_title: Marbella Club: Andalusian Gardens Beside the Golden Coast
property_intro: Set between the Sierra Blanca foothills and the Mediterranean shore, Marbella Club unfolds across subtropical gardens where jasmine, citrus and century-old palms shade whitewashed villas. Days drift from beachfront swims to Andalusian cookery lessons, horse riding through cork oak forest, or slow afternoons in the hammam. Interiors nod to local craftsmanship, with hand-painted tiles and woven textiles from nearby workshops. The gardens are tended without chemicals, and kitchens draw on produce from small farms across the Guadalhorce valley.

property_title: Tschuggen Grand Hotel: Alpine Serenity Above Arosa's Peaks
property_intro: Perched above Arosa at 1,800 metres, Tschuggen Grand Hotel sits where pine forest meets open mountain air. Mario Botta's glass-and-steel Bergoase spa glows like sails against the snow, while the hotel's private railway carries guests straight to the slopes. Inside, quiet luxury unfolds through light-filled suites, thoughtful Alpine cuisine and treatments drawing on mountain botanicals. Family-run for generations, it champions regional producers and Arosa's fragile high-altitude landscape, where bears roam a nearby sanctuary.

property_title: Grand Hotel Kronenhof: Alpine Grandeur in Pontresina's Peaks
property_intro: Rising above the village of Pontresina, Grand Hotel Kronenhof looks out across the Roseg Valley towards glaciers that have shaped this corner of the Engadin for millennia. Behind its neo-Baroque facade, frescoed salons and a light-filled spa invite unhurried days, while guides lead guests onto high trails and cross-country tracks. Kitchens draw on Graubünden producers, and long-standing ties with local families keep mountain traditions alive. Come evening, the terrace glows against darkening summits.

property_title: Villa Igiea: Palermo's Belle Epoque Jewel Beside the Sea
property_intro: Perched above the Gulf of Palermo, Villa Igiea has welcomed artists, royalty and restless souls since 1908. Behind its ochre facade, Art Nouveau frescoes and terrazzo floors have been painstakingly revived, while terraced gardens tumble towards the Tyrrhenian. Days drift between the cliffside pool, Sicilian cooking with market produce from Ballaro, and evenings on the loggia as Monte Pellegrino turns rose-gold. Local artisans, growers and restorers have shaped every corner of this reawakened grande dame.

property_title: Romazzino, A Belmond Hotel: Sardinia's Whitewashed Coastal Gem
property_intro: Set above the juniper-scented shores of Sardinia's Costa Smeralda, Romazzino rises like a whitewashed village, its terraces spilling towards two private beaches and water of astonishing clarity. Days unfold slowly here: sailing to hidden coves, tasting Gallurese recipes rooted in island tradition, or wandering gardens planted with native Mediterranean species. Interiors marry handcrafted Sardinian textiles with cool, breezy simplicity, while the hotel's care for its dunes and marine habitats quietly protects the coastline guests come to cherish.

property_title: Borgo Santandrea: Handcrafted Amalfi Coast Elegance by the Sea
property_intro: Terraced into the cliffs between Amalfi and Conca dei Marini, Borgo Santandrea unfolds over seven levels down to a private beach and a lift carved through the rock. Interiors celebrate southern Italian craft: hand-painted majolica tiles, vintage finds and locally woven textiles, all made by artisans from nearby villages. Days drift between the seawater pool, lemon-scented gardens and a kitchen led by the coast's own growers and fishermen. Sail out at dusk, or simply watch the light shift across the Tyrrhenian.

property_title: Six Senses Ninh Van Bay: Barefoot Luxury on Vietnam's Coast
property_intro: Reachable only by boat, Six Senses Ninh Van Bay unfolds beneath towering granite boulders on a secluded stretch of Vietnamese coastline near Nha Trang. Timber-and-thatch villas rise on stilts above the water or nestle into the hillside, each with its own pool and views across the East Vietnam Sea. Days drift between reef snorkelling, earth-lab workshops and the resort's organic gardens, while coral restoration and local hiring initiatives ensure your stay leaves the bay flourishing.

property_title: Capella Hanoi: Where Hanoi's Golden Opera Era Takes Centre Stage
property_intro: Steps from Hanoi's century-old Opera House, Capella Hanoi unfolds like a love letter to the city's theatrical past. Bill Bensley's exuberant design fills every corridor with archival portraits, velvet and curiosity, while Hoan Kiem Lake and the Old Quarter's noodle stalls wait just beyond the door. Days drift between the rooftop pool, a spa hidden in the wings and cocktails at Backstage, where local musicians and artisans keep Hanoi's living heritage delightfully close.

property_title: Zannier Bãi San Hô: Barefoot Luxury on Vietnam's Wild Coral Bay
property_intro: Tucked into a secluded stretch of Phu Yen's coastline, Zannier Bãi San Hô unfolds across ninety-eight hectares of rice paddies, hills and a private beach fringed by coral. Just seventy-three villas, shaped by local craft traditions and thatched in the vernacular of fishing and hill-tribe homes, sit lightly on the land. Days drift between reef snorkelling, buffalo-cart rides through the neighbouring village and long lunches of Phu Yen seafood, while the resort's foundation supports schooling and reef protection nearby.

property_title: Manshausen Island Resort: Arctic Solitude Above the Steens Fjord
property_intro: Set on a private island in Norway's Steigen archipelago, Manshausen is a place of granite, sea and shifting Arctic light. Glass-fronted cabins reach out over the water on old stone quays, framing views of the Lofoten peaks and, in winter, the aurora. Days unfold with sea kayaking, mountain hikes and diving in clear northern waters, before dinners built around local catch and foraged produce. Restoration of the historic trading post keeps island heritage quietly alive.

property_title: Piaule Catskill: Quiet Luxury Among the Mountains of New York
property_intro: Set across 50 acres of meadow and woodland near Catskill, New York, Piaule is a collection of glass-fronted cabins arranged so that each one faces the mountains rather than its neighbours. Minimalist interiors in oak and stone give way to broad views, while the spa, wood-fired sauna and seasonal kitchen draw on what the land and local farms provide. Native plantings and restored habitat continue to shape the property's evolving landscape.

property_title: Estelle Manor: Jacobean Splendour in the Oxfordshire Countryside
property_intro: Set within 3,000 acres of Oxfordshire parkland, Estelle Manor occupies a restored Jacobean-revival house near Eynsham, where ancient woodland and wildflower meadows are being carefully rewilded. Interiors layer antique finds with playful contemporary commissions, while the Roman-inspired Eynsham Baths invite long, unhurried afternoons. Days might drift from falconry and forest walks to fireside dining on produce grown a short stroll away. It is a country retreat that feels lived-in, generous and quietly connected to its surroundings.

property_title: Farris Bad: Where Norway's Mineral Springs Meet the Salt Air
property_intro: Set along Larvik's pebbled shoreline, where the Skagerrak breathes against wide windows, Farris Bad continues a bathing tradition begun here in the 1880s. Its celebrated spa draws on local mineral waters and seawater pools, while interiors in pale timber and stone echo the beach beyond. Days unfold with coastal walks through Bøkeskogen's beech woods, Norwegian dishes rooted in nearby farms and fjords, and long, unhurried evenings watching the light shift over the water.

property_title: Zaborin Ryokan: Silence, Snow and Private Onsen in Niseko's Woods
property_intro: Set within a silver birch forest at the foot of Mount Yotei, Zaborin invites you to slow down. Each of its fifteen villas pairs a private indoor and outdoor onsen with tatami warmth, floor-to-ceiling glass and Hokkaido craftsmanship. Days unfold around kaiseki dinners drawn from Niseko's farms and forests, quiet walks between snow-laden trees, and long soaks under falling flakes. It is a place shaped by stillness, season and remarkable attention to detail.

property_title: The Ranch Malibu: Wellness Reimagined in the Santa Monicas
property_intro: Tucked into 200 acres of the Santa Monica Mountains above Malibu, The Ranch turns an old citrus and horse property into a retreat built around movement, plant-based cooking and genuine rest. Days begin with mountain hikes on trails only guests walk, followed by yoga, massage and produce grown in the organic garden. Interiors are unfussy and warm, all reclaimed wood and canvas, while the surrounding chaparral is carefully protected and left to flourish.

property_title: Wilderness Hotel Inari: Lakeside Calm in Finnish Lapland
property_intro: On the shores of Lake Inari, deep in Finland's Sámi heartland, Wilderness Hotel Inari pairs timber-warm interiors with glass-roofed aurora cabins where the northern sky becomes your ceiling. Days unfold with husky sledding, ice fishing and quiet snowshoe trails through pine forest; evenings bring smoked local fish beside an open fire. Guides share Sámi traditions with genuine respect, while small-scale operations, regional produce and careful stewardship of this fragile Arctic wilderness underpin everything here.

property_title: Arctic Bath: Floating Sanctuary on the Lule, Swedish Lapland
property_intro: Moored on the Lule River in Harads, Arctic Bath rises like a tangle of timber logs \u2013 a nod to the river's log-floating past. In summer it drifts on the water; in winter it freezes into the ice. Cold-plunge rituals, saunas and quiet cabins are paired with foraged Nordic cooking, husky trails and aurora watching. Built with local craftsmanship and low-impact design, it invites you to slow to the rhythm of Lapland's seasons.

property_title: Amandari: Ubud's Sacred Valley Retreat Above the Ayung River
property_intro: Perched above the Ayung gorge in the village of Kedewatan, Amandari borrows its form from a Balinese settlement \alang-alang thatch, paras stone and a village lane opening onto terraced rice fields. Days unfold gently: temple visits, river walks, offerings prepared alongside neighbours whose families have shaped the resort since 1989. Young dancers rehearse in the village hall Amandari built, while the emerald pool mirrors the valley's shifting light from dawn to dusk.

property_title: Amanyara: Serene Seclusion on Providenciales' Wild North Coast
property_intro: On the untamed northwest shore of Providenciales, Amanyara sits beside the Northwest Point Marine National Park, where reef walls drop away just offshore. Timber pavilions frame reflecting ponds and sea grape, drawing the Turks and Caicos light indoors. Days unfold slowly: diving pristine coral gardens, kayaking mangrove channels, or joining the resort's marine conservation and turtle monitoring efforts. With only a handful of villas and pavilions, the quiet here feels genuinely earned rather than arranged.

property_title: Amanpulo: Private Island Serenity in the Philippine Sulu Sea
property_intro: Reached by private flight from Manila, Amanpulo occupies the whole of Pamalican, a slender coral-fringed island adrift in the Sulu Sea. Thatched casitas echo the local bahay kubo, shaded by palms and steps from powder-soft sand. Days unfold with reef dives, turtle hatchling releases, sailing aboard a traditional paraw and tables set beneath the stars. The island's marine sanctuary and long-standing support for neighbouring Cuyo communities mean your stay quietly sustains the waters and people who make this place remarkable.

property_title: Amanbagh: Rajasthan's Palatial Retreat Among Ancient Ruins
property_intro: Set within a walled garden of eucalyptus and fruit trees in rural Rajasthan, Amanbagh occupies the site of a former Maharaja's hunting encampment. Domed pavilions and green marble bathing pools echo Mughal craftsmanship, while beyond the gates lie the abandoned city of Bhangarh, Ajabgarh's stepwells and villages where herders still walk their cattle home at dusk. Days unfold with Ayurvedic treatments, guided walks through the Aravalli hills and quiet encounters with local communities the resort has long supported.

property_title: Vila da Santa Hotel: Búzios Hillside Calm Above the Atlantic
property_intro: Set on a quiet hillside above Ferradura Bay, Vila da Santa looks out across the peninsula that made Búzios famous, yet keeps its own unhurried rhythm. Whitewashed walls, handcrafted Brazilian pieces and shaded terraces frame days spent between the pool, nearby coves and boat trips along the coast. Family-run and closely tied to local artisans and producers, it offers the rare pleasure of feeling at home in a place you have only just discovered.

property_title: Zendaya Resort: Barefoot Luxury on Brazil's Untamed Coast
property_intro: Set between Atlantic forest and a sweep of pale Brazilian sand, Zendaya Resort invites you to slow down. Suites of raw timber, woven fibres and local stone open to the breeze, while days unfold with reef swims, horseback rides along empty shoreline and long lunches built around the day's catch. The kitchen garden and craft studio are tended by neighbouring families, and a dune restoration project quietly reshapes the coast for the better.

property_title: Belmond Hotel das Cataratas: Dawn Beside Iguassu's Falls
property_intro: Set within Brazil's Iguassu National Park, this rose-pink Portuguese colonial landmark is the only hotel inside the reserve, granting guests the falls at first light and long after the day's crowds have gone. Toucans cross the gardens, trails lead into Atlantic rainforest, and evenings bring regional cooking drawn from local producers. Conservation partnerships protect the surrounding wilderness, while guided walks with park naturalists reveal a landscape few travellers ever experience in such unhurried company.

property_title: Ibiti Engenho Lodge: Atlantic Forest Sanctuary in Minas Gerais
property_intro: Set within a vast private reserve on the edge of Ibitipoca in Minas Gerais, Ibiti Engenho Lodge occupies a restored colonial mill where stone, timber and Brazilian craft meet mountain light. Days unfold on horseback, along waterfall trails or in conversation with the neighbouring village, whose families are partners in the project. Rewilded pastures, regenerated forest and an inspired kitchen make this a rare place to slow down and belong.

property_title: Skylodge Adventure Suites: Sleep Among Peru's Sacred Cliffs
property_intro: Suspended on a granite cliff high above Peru's Sacred Valley, Skylodge Adventure Suites invites you to rest within transparent capsules reached by via ferrata or zip line. Below, the Urubamba River threads through terraced Andean farmland; above, constellations fill your glass ceiling. Each suite is handcrafted from aluminium and polycarbonate, with dry toilets and solar-warmed water minimising impact. Local guides from nearby villages lead the climb, sharing Quechua traditions over dinner served at altitude.

property_title: Picnic Island: A Private, Rugged Isle on Tasmania's East Coast
property_intro: Anchored in Great Oyster Bay, moments from Freycinet's granite peaks, Picnic Island is a two-hectare world of your own. The timber-and-steel lodge, shaped by John Wardle Architects, folds into the rock, framing weather, water and the comings and goings of little penguins. Days pass swimming, foraging oysters and watching sea eagles; evenings gather around long shared tables. Revegetation and seabird protection continue quietly here, restoring the island for the colonies that came first.

property_title: Le Couvent des Minimes: Provence's Fragrant Hillside Retreat
property_intro: Set among lavender fields and olive groves in the Haute-Provence village of Mane, this 17th-century convent has been reimagined with quiet confidence: vaulted stone corridors, sun-warmed cloisters and rooms dressed in soft Provencal hues. Days unfold with herbal treatments in the spa, kitchen gardens tended alongside local growers, and menus shaped by neighbouring farms. Walk the Luberon's footpaths, learn the craft of distilling immortelle, and let the region's rhythms slow yours.

property_title: Villa Gallici: An Elegant Provençal Retreat in Aix-en-Provence
property_intro: Set on a cypress-lined hillside moments from the fountains and cafés of Aix-en-Provence, Villa Gallici feels like the private residence of a well-travelled Provençal family. Toile fabrics, antique mirrors and shuttered windows open onto lavender terraces, while the pool rests beneath century-old plane trees. Dine on garden-grown produce and regional wines, wander to Cézanne's studio, or simply linger over breakfast in the shade. Local artisans and growers shape much of what you'll taste and touch here.

property_title: Villa Saint-Ange: Provencal Serenity in the Heart of Aix
property_intro: Set behind wrought-iron gates in Aix-en-Provence, Villa Saint-Ange occupies a 19th-century residence where plane trees shade a garden pool and Cezanne's countryside begins just beyond. Interiors pair Provencal antiques with contemporary calm, while the kitchen draws on nearby market growers and olive producers. Days might begin with pastries beneath the loggia and end with wine from Coteaux d'Aix vineyards. The old town's fountains, ateliers and Saturday markets lie a gentle stroll away.

property_title: Baumanière: Provençal Splendour Beneath Les Baux's Cliffs
property_intro: Tucked into the limestone folds of the Alpilles, beneath the medieval village of Les Baux-de-Provence, Baumanière unfolds across a cluster of honey-stoned farmhouses, olive groves and shaded courtyards. Generations of the Charial family have shaped it, from the kitchen garden feeding two celebrated restaurants to interiors layered with antiques and contemporary art. Days pass slowly here: truffle hunts, cookery lessons, a spa scented with local herbs, and evenings when the cicadas quieten and the cliffs glow amber.

property_title: Adler Spa Resort Dolomiti: Alpine Calm in Val Gardena's Heart
property_intro: Set in the meadows of Ortisei, where the Dolomites rise in pale limestone spires, Adler Spa Resort Dolomiti has welcomed guests for generations of family stewardship. Days unfold between guided hikes across Alpe di Siusi, riding lessons, and a vast spa fed by mountain water. Interiors pair Ladin craftsmanship with warm larch and loden, while kitchens draw on South Tyrolean farms and forests. Come evening, the valley quietens and the peaks glow rose.

property_title: Miramonti Boutique Hotel: Alpine Calm Above the Adige Valley
property_intro: Perched on a forested ledge high above Merano, Miramonti Boutique Hotel looks out across the Adige Valley to the Dolomites beyond. Interiors of local larch, stone and glass frame the view rather than compete with it, while the panoramic pool seems to hover among the treetops. Days unfold with woodland walks, South Tyrolean wines and produce from nearby farms, before a wood-fired sauna and long, quiet evenings watching the mountains fade to violet.

property_title: Aman Rosa Alpina: Dolomite Serenity in the Heart of Alta Badia
property_intro: Tucked into the village of San Cassiano, where the pale peaks of the Dolomites catch the last of the evening light, Aman Rosa Alpina carries a century of Ladin hospitality into a quieter, more considered era. Larch, loden and local stone shape interiors that feel unmistakably of these valleys. Ski straight onto the Sellaronda, forage with mountain guides, then linger over cuisine rooted in Alpine farms and generations of family craft.

property_title: Hotel La Perla: Dolomite Days, Ladin Soul and Alpine Grace
property_intro: Tucked into the Ladin village of Corvara, beneath the pale spires of the Dolomites, Hotel La Perla has been shaped by one family across generations. Rooms panelled in reclaimed alpine timber open to meadows and ski trails, while the wine cellar dug into the mountain rewards slow evenings. Expect mountain guides who know every col, cuisine rooted in South Tyrolean growers, and a genuine commitment to Ladin language, craft and the valley's fragile landscapes.

property_title: San Luis: Lakeside Treehouses Amid South Tyrol's Larch Woods
property_intro: High above Merano, where larch forests meet alpine meadows, San Luis unfolds around a still lake in South Tyrol's Avelengo highlands. Chalets and treehouses stand on stilts among the branches, built in timber and stone with quiet reverence for the woodland. Days pass riding Haflinger horses, foraging with the resident herbalist, or drifting between lake and sauna. Local craftspeople, mountain farms and careful forest stewardship keep the place rooted in its valley.

property_title: Umi Hotel: Glacier Horizons and Quiet Luxury in South Iceland
property_intro: Set among the hayfields of Iceland's south coast, Umi Hotel looks out towards Eyjafjallajfokull's white shoulders and the wide Atlantic beyond. Rooms are pared back and warm, with timber, wool and windows framing the weather as it moves across the plain. Skogafoss and the black sands of Vik lie minutes away, while evenings bring locally sourced dinners and, in winter, aurora watching from the doorstep. A family-run retreat rooted firmly in its landscape.

property_title: Hótel Búðir: Quiet Luxury on Snæfellsnes' Black Shoreline
property_intro: Standing alone between lava fields and the Atlantic on Iceland's Snæfellsnes peninsula, Hótel Búðir looks out to Snæfellsjökull glacier and a tiny black church surrounded by golden beaches. Rooms are calm and understated, letting the shifting light do the work, while the kitchen draws on local lamb, seaweed and freshly landed fish. Days unfold with coastal walks, birdlife and seal-watching; evenings belong to the fireside, the northern lights and the sound of the sea.

property_title: Highland Base at Kerlingarfjöll: Iceland's Wild Heart Awaits
property_intro: Set deep within Iceland's central highlands, Highland Base at Kerlingarfjöll rests among rhyolite peaks streaked with ochre and steam. Once a modest mountain hut, it has been reimagined with timber-lined rooms, geothermal bathing pools and a restaurant championing Icelandic growers and fishers. Days unfold across hiking trails, glacier ridges and hot springs; evenings belong to the aurora. Built with care for this fragile landscape, it offers rare access to a region few travellers ever reach.

property_title: PUQIO by Andean: Sacred Valley Living Rooted in Andean Soil
property_intro: Set among the terraced fields and adobe villages of Peru's Sacred Valley, PUQIO by Andean draws its name from the springs that have sustained these highlands for centuries. Earthen walls, handwoven textiles and locally quarried stone frame views of the Urubamba range, while days unfold through weaving workshops with Quechua artisans, harvests in the kitchen garden and quiet hikes to little-visited ruins. Guest stays support neighbouring farming families, native seed conservation and Andean water stewardship.

property_title: Angama Mara: Suspended Above the Maasai Mara's Endless Plains
property_intro: Perched high on the Oloololo Escarpment, Angama Mara floats above the Mara Triangle, where the plains unfurl for miles below your glass-fronted tent. Days here move gently: game drives with expert Maasai guides, picnics in the spot made famous by Out of Africa, or an afternoon in the photographic studio. Locally crafted interiors, a thriving shamba and the Angama Foundation's work with neighbouring communities give every stay quiet purpose.

property_title: El Fenn Hotel: Colour, Craft and Calm in Marrakech's Old Medina
property_intro: Tucked behind an unassuming door near Bab el Ksour, El Fenn unfolds as a cluster of riads wrapped around courtyards of orange trees, plunge pools and shaded terraces. Rooms glow with tadelakt, hand-woven textiles and contemporary art, all made by Marrakech's own artisans. Days drift between the hammam, the rooftop's Atlas views and the souks moments away. A committed employer and supporter of local craft, it offers Moroccan hospitality with genuine substance.

property_title: Rancho Pacifico: Rainforest Seclusion Above Costa Rica's Coast
property_intro: High in the hills above Playa Dominical, Rancho Pacifico rests within a private rainforest reserve where the Pacific unfolds far below. Adults-only villas open to birdsong, waterfall pools and toucans at breakfast. Days pass with jungle spa treatments, guided hikes to hidden cascades, and farm-to-table dinners drawn from the surrounding valley. The owners protect hundreds of acres of regenerating forest and employ locally, so your stay quietly sustains both the wildlife and the community below.

property_title: Lesante Blu: Adults-Only Elegance Above the Ionian, Zakynthos
property_intro: Perched on the cliffs of Tragaki, on Zakynthos' quieter north-eastern coast, Lesante Blu looks out across the Ionian towards Kefalonia. This adults-only retreat pairs pale stone, driftwood tones and deep blues with private pools and terraces that seem to hover above the water. Days unfold with sunrise swims, sailings to hidden coves, Zakynthian wines and cooking rooted in island produce. The hotel supports loggerhead turtle protection and local growers, so pleasure here carries purpose.

property_title: Hotel Van Zandt: Austin's Rhythm, Rendered in Rainey Street
property_intro: Set on Rainey Street, where bungalow bars spill onto porches and the Lady Bird Lake trail begins, Hotel Van Zandt takes its cue from Austin's musical soul. Art deco flourishes, brass detailing and instrument-inspired motifs fill rooms overlooking the water, while Geraldine's serves Gulf Coast plates alongside live sets from local performers. Cycle the boardwalk at dawn, swim in the rooftop pool by dusk, and discover a hotel genuinely woven into its neighbourhood.

property_title: ADLER Lodge Ritten: Pine-Scented Calm and Dolomite Panoramas
property_intro: High on the Renon plateau above Bolzano, ADLER Lodge Ritten rests among larch and spruce woods, with the Dolomites rising beyond the meadows. Chalets of local timber and stone open onto sun-warmed terraces, while the lake-fed pool, forest sauna and mountain spa invite unhurried days. Guided hikes, foraging walks and South Tyrolean cooking rooted in nearby farms bring the landscape closer. Reachable by cable car, it is a place shaped by quiet respect for its surroundings.

property_title: Grand Hotel Victoria Concept & Spa: Lake Como, Reimagined Calm
property_intro:
Facing the water in Menaggio, on Lake Como's quieter western shore, this nineteenth-century villa has been coaxed into something quietly contemporary. Interiors pair salvaged timber and local stone with soft Alpine light, while the vast Erre Spa draws on lake water and mountain botanicals. Days unfold with sailing, hiking the Sentiero del Viandante, or lingering over Michelin-recognised cooking built around producers from the surrounding valleys. Sustainability here is structural, not decorative 
invest in the place, and it repays you.

property_title: Château Eza: A Medieval Eyrie Above the French Riviera
property_intro: Perched within the stone ramparts of Èze village, some 400 metres above the Mediterranean, Château Eza occupies a 14th-century residence once home to a Swedish prince. Its ten rooms and suites pair vaulted ceilings and open fireplaces with terraces that fall away to the sea. Dine on Riviera produce at the panoramic restaurant, wander the medieval lanes and exotic garden at dawn, and discover a house that keeps local craftsmanship and hillside heritage very much alive.

property_title: Château de Théoule: Riviera Serenity Above the Esterel Coast
property_intro: Set among umbrella pines on the red rock shoreline between Cannes and Saint-Raphaël, Château de Théoule looks out across the Bay of La Napoule towards the Lérins islands. Once a soap works, the building has been reimagined with restrained elegance, its vaulted interiors softened by Mediterranean light. Days unfold with swims from the private coves, walks in the Esterel massif and dishes shaped by nearby growers and fishermen, in a place quietly attentive to its coastline.

property_title: Les Roches Rouges: Barefoot Riviera Living on Provence's Coast
property_intro: Set between Saint-Raphaël and Agay, where the Estérel's red porphyry cliffs slip into the Mediterranean, Les Roches Rouges reimagines the Riviera without the fuss. Mid-century lines, natural materials and a saltwater pool carved into the rock set the mood, while days drift between sea swims, coastal walks and Provençal cooking rooted in nearby producers. Bedrooms frame the water; evenings bring long, unhurried dinners. It is the Côte d'Azur at its most quietly confident, with sand still on your feet.

property_title: Althoff Villa Belrose: Hilltop Serenity Above Saint-Tropez
property_intro: Perched on a pine-clad hillside above the Bay of Saint-Tropez, Althoff Villa Belrose looks out across the Gulf towards Sainte-Maxime and the Massif des Maures. Interiors echo the Riviera in soft linens, terracotta and sunlit stone, while the Michelin-starred kitchen draws on Provençal growers and Mediterranean day boats. Spend mornings in the vineyards, afternoons by the cliffside pool, evenings watching the light shift over the water. Gardens are tended without pesticides, and beehives hum among the lavender.

property_name: Hôtel Château de La Chèvre d’Or
property_title: Hôtel Château de La Chèvre d'Or: Èze's Cliff-Top Enchantment
property_intro: Perched within the medieval walls of Èze, this collection of stone houses tumbles down the hillside some 400 metres above the Mediterranean. Vaulted ceilings, antique tiles and terraced gardens speak of centuries of craftsmanship, carefully preserved rather than reinvented. Days unfold slowly here: swimming beside the cliff edge, wandering car-free lanes with local artisans, dining on Riviera produce shaped by Michelin-starred kitchens. Come evening, the coastline glitters below and the village falls quietly, wonderfully still.

property_title: Hotel de Paris Monte-Carlo: A Belle Époque Legend Reimagined
property_intro: Overlooking Place du Casino, with the Mediterranean glinting beyond, Hotel de Paris Monte-Carlo has welcomed guests since 1864 — and its recent restoration has given the Belle Époque grande dame fresh light, airy suites and a courtyard garden at its heart. Dine with Alain Ducasse at Le Louis XV, descend into the legendary wine cellar, then unwind at the seawater spa. Sustainability runs quietly throughout, from local sourcing to Monaco's own commitments to protecting the sea it overlooks.

property_title: Cheval Blanc St-Tropez: Riviera Elegance on the Water's Edge
property_intro: Tucked into the fishing village heart of St-Tropez, Cheval Blanc St-Tropez opens directly onto the Baie de Pampelonne's shimmering horizon, moments from the old port's cobbled lanes. Interiors by Jean-Michel Wilmotte are washed in maritime blues and soft linen, while the three-Michelin-starred kitchen of La Vague d'Or celebrates Provençal producers and line-caught fish. Days drift between the Dior spa, sailing the gulf and long lunches beneath the pines, with sunsets arriving over the water like an encore.

property_title: La R\u00e9serve Ramatuelle: Clifftop Calm Above the C\u00f4te d'Azur
property_intro: Perched on a pine-clad hillside above Pampelonne's shoreline, La R\u00e9serve Ramatuelle looks out across the Mediterranean from within a protected coastal landscape. Jean-Michel Wilmotte's low-slung architecture settles into the maquis, its villas and suites framed by olive trees and sea light. Days unfold between the celebrated wellness centre, garden-led Proven\u00e7al cooking and long swims, while local producers and conservation of the surrounding scrubland shape the experience. Refined, unhurried, and quietly attuned to its setting.

property_title: Rixos Premium Dubrovnik: Adriatic Calm on the Lapad Peninsula
property_intro: Set along the pine-fringed shoreline of Lapad Bay, Rixos Premium Dubrovnik looks out across the Adriatic towards the Elaphiti Islands, a short stroll from the promenade and minutes from the walled Old Town. Interiors balance Dalmatian stone and soft coastal light, while days unfold between the private beach, thermal spa rituals and menus built around Konavle producers. Local guides lead island sailings and vineyard visits, connecting guests with the region's craftspeople and quiet corners.

property_title: The Roundtree Amagansett: Quiet Luxury on the East End
property_intro: Tucked into the gentle hush of Amagansett, moments from Atlantic dunes and Napeague's salt marshes, The Roundtree offers a considered take on Hamptons living. Bungalows and suites are dressed in pale timber, natural linens and locally made ceramics, with private terraces and outdoor showers. Borrow a bicycle for the farm stands and fish markets, or linger by the saltwater pool. Partnerships with East End growers and artisans keep the experience rooted in its coastal community.

property_title: Martinhal Sagres Family Resort: Where Atlantic Wilds Meet Calm
property_intro: On Portugal's south-westernmost tip, where the Costa Vicentina Natural Park meets a sweep of golden sand, Martinhal Sagres sits gently within its windswept surroundings. Airy villas and suites in pale timber and stone open to sea breezes, while children roam freely between rock pools, tennis courts and kids' clubs. Days might bring surf lessons, cliff-top walks or seafood grilled over coals. The resort works closely with local producers and conservation projects, keeping this untamed coastline as it should be.

property_title: Hotel La Villa Douce: Riviera Calm in the Heart of Saint-Tropez
property_intro: Tucked into a quiet residential pocket moments from Saint-Tropez's old port, Hotel La Villa Douce feels more like a friend's Provençal home than a hotel. Sunlight moves across pale stone, vintage finds and locally made furnishings, while the walled garden and pool offer shade beneath pines. Cycle to Pampelonne, browse the Place des Lices market with the kitchen team, or simply linger over Var wines as the evening softens. Small, personal and quietly generous.

property_title: Santa Casa by Tasman: Barefoot Refinement on Mexico's Coast
property_intro: Set where jungle gives way to the Pacific, Santa Casa by Tasman is a private retreat shaped by local craft: lime-washed walls, hand-carved parota wood and shaded terraces that catch the sea breeze. Days unfold slowly here, whether you are swimming in the pool, walking the shoreline at dawn or joining the chef at the market. The house works closely with nearby artisans and turtle conservation efforts, giving each stay a quiet sense of belonging.

property_title: The Agora Hotel: Old Town Charm in the Heart of Cyprus
property_intro: Tucked into the lanes of a Cypriot old town, The Agora Hotel occupies a lovingly restored stone building where sandstone arches, handmade tiles and locally crafted furnishings set a quietly confident tone. Mornings begin with village honey and halloumi on the courtyard terrace; afternoons drift towards nearby markets, hammams and coastal paths. Family-run and deeply rooted in its neighbourhood, the hotel works with island artisans and growers, offering a stay that feels genuinely, generously Cypriot.

property_title: Toile Blanche: Provençal Calm Amid Saint-Paul-de-Vence Hills
property_intro: Set among cypress and olive groves above Saint-Paul-de-Vence, Toile Blanche is a former artist's retreat where Provence's light still shapes the day. Pared-back interiors, original artworks and sun-warmed stone frame views across the Riviera hinterland. Days unfold slowly: a swim before breakfast, a wander through the village's galleries, an evening spent with wines from neighbouring vineyards. Family-run and deeply rooted in its terroir, it offers a considered, unhurried version of southern French living.

property_title: Chapung Sebali: A Cliffside Sanctuary Above Ubud's Ayung River
property_intro: Perched on a ridge above the Ayung River, a short drive from Ubud, Chapung Sebali looks out across terraced rice fields and dense valley greenery. Villas of timber, stone and thatch open to private pools, while yoga at dawn, river treks and Balinese cooking classes fill unhurried days. The kitchen draws on the estate's own gardens, and long-standing ties with neighbouring Sebali village keep local craft, culture and livelihoods thriving.

property_title: Arimasansoh Goshobessho: Arima's Ancient Golden Spring Ritual
property_intro: Tucked into the wooded hills above Kobe, this intimate ryokan draws on Arima Onsen's storied kinsen waters, iron-rich and amber-gold, poured into private open-air baths where only birdsong intrudes. Rooms pair understated Japanese craftsmanship with quiet comfort, while kaiseki dinners follow the Rokko mountains through the seasons, using produce and Tajima beef from nearby farms. Wander lantern-lit lanes, meet potters and sake brewers, then return to steam rising gently at dusk.

property_title: Quay17: Canal-Side Calm and Quiet Character in Belgium
property_intro: Moored along one of Belgium's most graceful waterways, Quay17 occupies a handsomely restored merchant's house where original beams and brickwork meet considered contemporary design. Mornings begin with bread from the baker two doors down; afternoons invite slow cycling through the polders or a barge trip past shuttered warehouses. Local craftspeople furnished the interiors, and the kitchen sources from growers within a few miles. It is the sort of address that rewards lingering rather than rushing.

property_title: Le Marne Relais: Slow Living Among Italy's Quiet Vineyards
property_intro: Set among rolling farmland and centuries-old vines, Le Marne Relais invites you to settle into the unhurried rhythm of rural Italy. Restored stone buildings hold rooms where handmade textiles and locally crafted furniture meet wide countryside views. Days unfold with cellar tastings, kitchen-garden harvests and long lunches shared at communal tables. The estate works closely with neighbouring producers and tends its land organically, so every meal carries the character of the surrounding hills.

property_title: Mastrojanni Relais: Where Brunello Meets Val d'Orcia Sunlight
property_intro: Set among the organic vineyards of Castelnuovo dell'Abate, Mastrojanni Relais looks out over the Romanesque abbey of Sant'Antimo and the wild southern reaches of the Val d'Orcia. Restored farmhouses hold quiet, light-filled rooms where stone and linen speak louder than ornament. Days unfold with cellar tastings of celebrated Brunello, walks through Monte Amiata's woodland and long lunches drawn from the estate's own harvest. Biodiversity is nurtured here, and local craft quietly celebrated.

property_title: Le Sirenuse: Positano's Cliffside Icon Above the Amalfi Coast
property_intro: Draped across the cliffs of Positano, Le Sirenuse has welcomed guests since 1951, when the Sersale family opened their summer home to travellers. Bougainvillea spills over terraces, majolica tiles cool bare feet, and antiques gathered over generations lend each room its own character. Days drift between the pool, Michelin-starred dining and boat trips along the coast, while the family's championing of local artisans and Amalfi's craft traditions keeps this a place with genuine roots.

property_title: L'oscar London: Baroque Splendour in the Heart of Bloomsbury
property_intro: Set within a former Baptist headquarters in Bloomsbury, L'oscar London is a study in theatrical restraint. Jacques Garcia's interiors bring peacock motifs, silk damask and gilded flourishes to Grade II-listed rooms, while the original chapel now houses a soaring, candlelit bar. Steps from Covent Garden and the British Museum, it offers literary London on the doorstep, thoughtful restoration of historic craftsmanship, and a residents' library made for slow, unhurried evenings.

property_title: The Sanubari: Barefoot Luxury Amid Bali's Emerald Rice Fields
property_intro: Tucked into the gentle folds of Tabanan's countryside, The Sanubari gathers a handful of thatched villas among terraced rice fields, coconut groves and river valleys where herons still gather at dusk. Days unfold slowly here: yoga beneath open rafters, spring-fed pools, market walks with the village cook, and dinners drawn from the surrounding smallholdings. Built by local artisans using bamboo, alang-alang and reclaimed timber, it channels its earnings back into the community that shaped it.

property_title: LILLØY Lindenberg: Where Norway's Coastline Slows Right Down
property_intro: Set on a small island off Norway's southern shore, LILLØY Lindenberg gathers weathered timber buildings, rock pools and sea breezes into something quietly remarkable. Days unfold slowly here: swimming from smooth granite, wandering the shoreline, gathering around long tables for produce drawn from nearby waters and farms. Interiors favour honest materials and craft over ornament, while the team works closely with local fishermen and growers, preserving both island heritage and the fragile coastal landscape that surrounds it.

property_title: Botanique Hotel Experience: Mantiqueira's Quiet Luxury Retreat
property_intro: Set within 250 hectares of Atlantic Forest in Brazil's Mantiqueira mountains, Botanique Hotel Experience feels less like a hotel and more like a private estate shared with hummingbirds and waterfalls. Glass, stone and reclaimed timber frame views across the valley, while menus draw on the kitchen garden and neighbouring farms in Camanducaia. Days unfold with forest trails, thermal pools and horseback rides, supported by ongoing reforestation and partnerships that keep local craft and livelihoods thriving.

property_title: Minaret Station: Alpine Seclusion in New Zealand's High Country
property_intro: Reachable only by helicopter, Minaret Station rests in a hanging valley high above Lake Wanaka, where four canvas-and-timber chalets look out over tussock ridges and snow-fed streams. This is a working high-country farm run by the Wallis family, who share their world through heli-fishing, glacier landings and long lunches on the mountainside. Days end with a soak in the wood-fired hot tub, venison from the valley on the table, and silence broken only by the wind.

property_title: Ca’n Beneït: A Mallorcan Finca Where Stone and Silence Meet
property_intro: Tucked into the folds of Mallorca's Tramuntana foothills, Ca’n Beneït is a restored country finca where centuries-old stone walls frame olive groves, drystone terraces and long views towards the sea. Interiors pair local craftsmanship with quiet, contemporary calm. Days unfold slowly here: harvesting olives with the family who tend the land, swimming beneath the pines, or following goat paths into the hills. A place that gives back to its valley, and to those who linger., warmly.

property_title: Predi Son Jaumell: Mallorcan Finca Living Among Ancient Olives
property_intro: Set in the hills above Capdepera, in Mallorca's wild north-east, this 17th-century manor house looks out across olive groves towards the Serra de Llevant and the sea beyond. Honey-coloured stone, cool vaulted ceilings and just twenty-four rooms make for an unhurried sort of luxury. Days drift between the garden pool, coastal walks to hidden coves and dinners built around produce grown metres from the kitchen, prepared with quiet reverence for Mallorcan tradition.

property_title: Castell Son Claret: A Mallorcan Estate Rooted in Tramuntana
property_intro: Set across 326 hectares at the foot of Mallorca's Tramuntana mountains, Castell Son Claret occupies a centuries-old estate near the village of Es Capdellà. Ancient olive groves, citrus terraces and dry-stone walls surround suites where original stonework meets restrained contemporary design. Days unfold with garden-to-table dining, spa rituals drawn from island botanicals and walks through land farmed without chemicals. Bees, sheep and heritage crops are quietly tended here, keeping local craft and agricultural traditions very much alive.

property_title: Es Figueral Nou: A Mallorcan Finca Rooted in Land and Time
property_intro: Set among almond groves and dry-stone walls in the Mallorcan countryside, Es Figueral Nou is a working finca where centuries-old buildings have been revived with restraint \linen, lime-washed walls and locally quarried stone. Days unfold slowly here: harvesting olives, tasting estate wines, or wandering the Tramuntana foothills at dusk. The family behind it farm organically and employ neighbours from the nearby village, so every meal carries the flavour of this particular patch of land.

property_title: Finca Can Estades: Mallorcan Calm Beneath the Tramuntana
property_intro: Tucked between olive terraces and the limestone ridges of the Serra de Tramuntana, Finca Can Estades is a restored Mallorcan estate where centuries-old stone meets soft linen, lime-washed walls and locally made ceramics. Days unfold slowly here: barefoot mornings by the pool, wandering the orchards with the gardener, cycling to hidden coves. The kitchen leans on the island's small producers, while ongoing tree-planting and water stewardship keep this quiet corner of Mallorca thriving for generations to come.

property_title: Akademie Street Boutique Hotel: A Garden Retreat in Franschhoek
property_intro: Tucked behind old oak trees on a quiet village lane, Akademie Street Boutique Hotel offers a handful of private suites and cottages set within lush gardens, framed by the Franschhoek mountains. Cape Dutch heritage meets collected art and deep, restful comfort here. Days unfold slowly: breakfast beneath the vines, a swim in the saltwater pool, then a stroll to the valley's celebrated kitchens and wine farms just moments from your door.

property_title: The Saxon Hotel: Sanctuary and Soul in Leafy Johannesburg
property_intro: Tucked into six acres of indigenous gardens in Sandhurst, one of Johannesburg's most tranquil suburbs, the Saxon Hotel, Villas and Spa is a place of quiet consequence — Nelson Mandela edited his memoir within these walls. African artistry shapes every interior, from hand-beaded details to sculptural stonework, while the celebrated kitchens champion small-scale South African growers. Days unfold with spa rituals, private art tours and long swims, and the hotel's foundation supports young local talent through culinary apprenticeships.

property_title: GweGwe Beach Lodge: Where the Wild Coast Meets the Indian Ocean
property_intro: Perched above a secluded stretch of the Eastern Cape's Wild Coast, GweGwe Beach Lodge sits within Mkhambathi Nature Reserve, where grassland plateaus fall away to waterfalls, forested gorges and an empty shoreline. Suites frame the ocean in timber, stone and glass, drawing the outdoors close. Days unfold with guided walks, river paddles and whale watching, while the lodge's partnership with local Mpondo communities ensures your stay supports conservation and livelihoods along this remarkable coast.

property_title: Babylonstoren: Cape Winelands Living Rooted in the Garden
property_intro: Set beneath the Simonsberg in South Africa's Cape Winelands, Babylonstoren is a working farm with Cape Dutch roots dating to 1692. Whitewashed cottages open onto an eight-acre fruit and vegetable garden that shapes every plate served here. Days might involve pressing olive oil, foraging with the gardeners, tasting wines in the sculptural cellar or drifting through the spa's healing herb beds. Restoration, regenerative farming and long-standing care for the farm's community underpin it all.

property_title: Future Found Sanctuary: Fynbos Retreat Above Hout Bay, Cape Town
property_intro: Set high on a mountainside above Hout Bay, Future Found Sanctuary looks out across fynbos-clad slopes towards the Atlantic. Timber, stone and glass frame the landscape rather than compete with it, while sound healing, forest walks and long, unhurried meals invite you to slow your pace. Indigenous replanting and partnerships with local makers and conservation projects shape every stay here, leaving you restored, quietly connected and reluctant to head back down the mountain.

property_title: Domaine de Murtoli: Wild Corsican Shores and Ancient Stone
property_intro: Spread across 2,500 hectares of southern Corsica, Domaine de Murtoli gathers restored shepherds' houses among maquis, granite outcrops and a river that meets three private beaches. Each bergerie is furnished with quiet restraint, its thick walls and open hearths speaking of the island's pastoral past. Days might mean sea fishing, riding through the valley or dining in a cave by candlelight. The estate farms its own produce, tends native woodland and keeps Corsican craft traditions alive.

property_title: Juntos Farm: Regenerative Living in the Spanish Countryside
property_intro: Set amid olive groves and sun-warmed hills, Juntos Farm invites you to slow down and settle into the rhythm of rural Spain. Rooms are pared-back yet quietly refined, shaped from local stone, lime and timber. Days unfold with harvests from the kitchen garden, long lunches beneath the trees and walks through land being carefully restored. Working closely with neighbouring growers and artisans, the farm offers something increasingly rare: a stay that gives back to the soil that sustains it.

property_title: Timeless Stone and Slow Alentejo Days at São Lourenço do Barrocal
property_intro: In the plains near Monsaraz, this ancient farming estate has belonged to one family for two centuries. Its whitewashed cottages, threshing floors and vaulted stables have been gently restored by architect Eduardo Souto de Moura, leaving the patina of rural life intact. Days unfold among cork oaks and vineyards: riding, foraging, tasting wines made on site, or simply drifting between olive groves and pool. Local craft, regenerative farming and village life quietly shape everything here.

property_title: Tiger Tops Karnali Lodge: Wild Heart of Nepal's Bardia
property_intro: On the fringes of Bardia National Park, where the Karnali river carves through Nepal's westernmost wilderness, this intimate lodge offers a rare kind of quiet. Handcrafted Tharu-inspired cottages sit among mango and sal trees, while days unfold on foot or by jeep in search of tigers, rhinos and Gangetic dolphins. Guided by local naturalists and rooted in decades of conservation work, Karnali Lodge invites you to travel slowly, attentively and in genuine partnership with its community.

property_title: Les Frères Ibarboure: A Basque Haven of Gardens and Gastronomy
property_intro: Tucked between Biarritz and the Spanish border, Les Frères Ibarboure sits within wooded grounds in Bidart, where two brothers built their reputation on the produce of the Basque country. Rooms open onto pines and rolling parkland, blending pale timber, linen and light. Days unfold slowly: sea air before breakfast, a swim, then dinner shaped by neighbouring farmers, fishermen and cheesemakers. A family address where hospitality feels inherited rather than staged.

property_title: Les Hortensias du Lac: Lakeside Calm in Pine-Clad Hossegor
property_intro: On the still waters of Lake Hossegor, where maritime pines lean towards the Atlantic, Les Hortensias du Lac gathers a cluster of 1930s villas restored with restraint \ bleached timber, linen and Landes craftsmanship.
