Interiors favour local stone, linen and craftsmanship over spectacle, while regenerative farming and island partnerships keep the retreat firmly rooted in its Cycladic surroundings.

property_title: El Santuario: Lakeside Serenity in Mexico's Sacred Highlands
property_intro: Cradled in the wooded hills above Lake Valle de Bravo, El Santuario looks out across mirrored water where sailboats drift and monarch butterflies pass on their winter migration. Interiors blend Mexican craftsmanship with warm stone and timber, while spa rituals, forest trails and boat outings shape unhurried days. The retreat works closely with local artisans and conservation projects protecting the surrounding watershed, so your stay quietly supports the landscape that makes it so beguiling.

property_title: Terme di Vulci: Thermal Springs Amid Etruscan Maremma Wildlands
property_intro: Set between Lazio and Tuscany, where the Fiora river carves through Etruscan tombs and grazing land, Terme di Vulci gathers naturally warm mineral pools beneath open skies. Days drift between long soaks, archaeological walks and lunches drawn from the surrounding farms. Interiors are quietly considered, favouring local stone, timber and light, while the estate protects its springs and native habitat. Come for the water; stay for the extraordinary stillness of this little-visited corner of Italy.

property_title: Tannerhof: Bavarian Mountain Calm in Reimagined Farmhouses
property_intro: Tucked into the Bavarian foothills above Bayrischzell, Tannerhof has welcomed guests seeking mountain air and quiet restoration since 1904. Historic farmhouses sit alongside striking timber huts on stilts, where wood, linen and light replace excess. Days unfold with forest walks, sauna rituals, fasting cures and long soaks, followed by garden-led cooking rooted in the valley. Family-run across generations, it champions regional craft, local producers and a slower rhythm that lingers long after departure.

property_title: Haus Hirt: Alpine Warmth and Thermal Calm in Bad Gastein
property_intro: Perched above the Belle Époque rooftops of Bad Gastein, Haus Hirt has welcomed guests since 1946 with the ease of a family home rather than a hotel. Rooms pair mid-century Austrian craft with soft wool, warm timber and views across the Hohe Tauern peaks. Days unfold with thermal spring bathing, mountain walks and long lunches of produce from nearby farms, while evenings bring live jazz, wood fires and conversation that lingers well past dessert.

property_title: KRAFTalm: Alpine Seclusion and Quiet Luxury in the Tyrol
property_intro: High above the Wildschönau valley, KRAFTalm sits among Tyrolean meadows where cowbells still mark the hours. These handcrafted chalets are built from local spruce and stone, warmed by wood-fired saunas and private outdoor baths with views across the Kitzbühel Alps. Days unfold slowly here: forest walks with a herbalist, farm-fresh breakfasts left at your door, evenings under startlingly clear skies. Family-run and rooted in regional craft, it offers privacy without pretence.

property_title: Kamalaya Wellness Sanctuary: Healing Amid Koh Samui's Hills
property_intro: Set into a granite hillside on the southern shore of Koh Samui, Kamalaya grew around a cave once used by Buddhist monks for meditation "a presence still felt in its quiet terraces and shaded pathways. Thatched pavilions descend towards a private beach, while therapists blend traditional Asian practices with contemporary naturopathy. Meals draw on the sanctuary's own gardens, and long-standing partnerships with island communities and marine conservation projects give every stay a deeper resonance.

property_title: Hotel Schwarzschmied: Orchard Calm in South Tyrol's Lana
property_intro: Set among the apple orchards of Lana, minutes from Merano, Hotel Schwarzschmied pairs alpine warmth with a quietly contemporary hand. Interiors favour local larch, loden and stone, while the garden pool and panoramic sauna look towards the Texel peaks. Days unfold with vineyard walks, cycling along the Adige, and kitchen produce drawn from neighbouring growers and the hotel's own orchard. A family-run house where South Tyrolean craft, seasonal cooking and unhurried hospitality feel genuinely at home.

property_title: Elephant Watch Camp: Where Samburu's Elephants Lead the Way
property_intro: Set beneath doum palms on the banks of the Ewaso Nyiro River, Elephant Watch Camp sits within Kenya's Samburu National Reserve, a landscape of red earth and rugged hills. Six handcrafted tents, shaped by local artisans from fallen wood and recycled materials, open to elephant-crossed plains. Guided by Samburu trackers who know individual herds by name, days unfold slowly here. The camp's roots in elephant research and its Samburu-run team make every stay quietly consequential.

property_title: Sashwa River of Stars: Wild Luxury Beneath South African Skies
property_intro: Set along a seasonal riverbed in South Africa's bushveld, Sashwa River of Stars invites you into a landscape where elephants pass at dawn and the Milky Way seems close enough to touch. Suites are shaped from timber, stone and canvas, opening onto uninterrupted wilderness. Days unfold with tracking on foot, quiet hours by the water and dinners under lantern light, while your stay supports habitat restoration and the surrounding communities who guide it.

property_title: Eumelia: Organic Living Among the Olive Groves of Laconia
property_intro: Set amid olive groves and vineyards in the rolling Laconian countryside of the Peloponnese, Eumelia is an organic farm and agritourism retreat where days unfold at a gentler rhythm. Stone-and-earth guesthouses, built with local materials and powered by the sun, open onto fields worked without chemicals. Press your own olive oil, forage for wild herbs, learn to make pottery, or simply linger over dinner drawn from the garden, shared with the family who tend it.

property_title: Breac House: A Quiet Donegal Retreat on the Wild Atlantic Way
property_intro: Set into the hillside beneath Horn Head, Breac House looks across Sheephaven Bay to Muckish Mountain, with only bog, sea and shifting Donegal light for company. Four rooms, crafted from concrete, oak and local stone, frame the view like paintings. Days unfold with foraging walks, boat trips and long conversations over breakfasts of Irish produce. Owners Cathrine and Niall champion regional makers, artists and food producers, making every stay quietly rooted in place.

property_title: Bodhi Khaya Nature Retreat: Stillness Among Fynbos and Forest
property_intro: Tucked into the Overberg's rolling fynbos near Stanford, Bodhi Khaya spreads across a working farm where indigenous forest, vineyards and a labyrinth of ancient trees invite slow days. Stay in thoughtfully restored cottages and light-filled rooms, join yoga and silent meditation retreats, or wander trails alive with birdsong. Much of the land is under rehabilitation, with alien clearing and local employment at its heart, so your stay quietly restores rather more than yourself.

property_title: Soulshine Bali: Ubud's Rice-Field Retreat with Heart and Soul
property_intro: Set among the rice terraces of Ubud, Soulshine Bali was founded by musician Michael Franti as a place where creativity, wellbeing and community meet. Days unfold with yoga on the open-air shala, cycling through village lanes, treatments drawing on Balinese healing traditions, and long, unhurried swims. Handcrafted interiors celebrate local artistry, while partnerships with nearby schools and clean-water projects extend the warmth beyond the gates. Expect live music, shared tables and a genuine sense of belonging.

property_title: Willka Tika: A Sacred Valley Garden Retreat in the Andes
property_intro: Cradled by the Andes in Peru's Sacred Valley, Willka Tika unfolds across seven flower-filled Chakra Gardens, each planted for reflection and quiet renewal. Adobe guest rooms are dressed in handwoven Quechua textiles, while meals draw on organic harvests from the kitchen garden. Days might bring a coca leaf reading, a master weaver's demonstration, or a walk to nearby Inca terraces. Guest stays directly support local schools and the Quechua families who tend these grounds.

property_title: Haramara Retreat: Barefoot Serenity Above Mexico's Pacific Coast
property_intro: Perched on a jungle-clad clifftop near Sayulita, on Mexico's Nayarit coast, Haramara Retreat invites you to slow down entirely. Fifteen open-air casitas, hand-built from local stone and palm thatch, have no doors or windows "only ocean breezes, birdsong and the sound of surf below. Days unfold with yoga on shaded platforms, cacao-rich vegetarian feasts and swims in a cliffside pool. Solar power, rainwater harvesting and local craftsmanship keep this sanctuary gently rooted in its surroundings.

property_title: The Gleneagles: Perthshire's Grand Country Estate Reimagined
property_intro: Set across 850 acres of Perthshire countryside, The Gleneagles has welcomed guests since 1924 — and still feels wonderfully alive. Beyond its celebrated championship golf, days here might mean falconry among the pines, riding out across the glen, or casting a line on the River Tay. Interiors nod to the estate's Jazz Age beginnings without a hint of pastiche, while kitchen gardens, native woodland planting and long-standing local partnerships quietly shape every stay.

property_title: The Newt in Somerset: Georgian Grandeur, Orchards and Cyder
property_intro: Set within a Georgian estate near Bruton, The Newt in Somerset unfolds across woodland, walled gardens and orchards where hundreds of apple varieties grow. Days might mean tasting your way through the cyder press, exploring the Roman villa recreation, or swimming in a pool set among treetops. Rooms pair antique warmth with quiet craftsmanship, while the estate's farming, rewilding and beekeeping feed both kitchen and countryside. Somerset, generously interpreted and thoroughly lived in.

property_title: Ashford Castle: Ireland's Storied Retreat on Lough Corrib
property_intro: On the shores of Lough Corrib, where County Mayo meets Galway, Ashford Castle has welcomed guests since the 13th century. Woodland trails, walled gardens and 350 acres of parkland surround interiors rich with Irish craftsmanship, antiques and commissioned art. Days here might involve falconry with Harris hawks, casting for brown trout, or learning about the estate's tree-planting and native woodland restoration. Local artisans supply the kitchens, and the village of Cong waits just beyond the gates.

property_title: Baur au Lac: Timeless Lakeside Elegance in the Heart of Zurich
property_intro: Set within its own private park where Lake Zurich meets the city's banking quarter, Baur au Lac has been guided by the same family since 1844. Interiors blend Swiss craftsmanship with contemporary calm, while the garden terrace and Michelin-starred dining draw locals as readily as guests. Alpine views stretch beyond the water, the Bahnhofstrasse waits moments away, and seasonal menus champion regional growers. A rare address where discretion, heritage and genuine warmth still shape every stay.

property_title: The Goring: London's Last Family-Run Grand Hotel in Belgravia
property_intro: Tucked down a quiet Belgravia lane moments from Buckingham Palace, The Goring has been cared for by four generations of the same family since 1910 \u2013 a rarity in London. Expect Gainsborough silk, Nina Campbell interiors and a private garden where afternoon tea unfolds beneath the plane trees. The kitchen champions British growers and heritage produce, while long-serving staff greet returning guests by name. Royal Mews, Hyde Park and the King's Road all sit within an easy stroll.

property_title: Reschio Hotel: Umbrian Hills, Ancient Castle, Timeless Grace
property_intro: Set within a 3,700-acre estate on the border of Umbria and Tuscany, Reschio occupies a thousand-year-old castle restored over decades by the Bolza family. Antonio Bolza's designs pair hand-forged furniture with frescoed walls and deep, quiet corners. Days unfold with horses schooled in the classical tradition, olive groves and vineyards tended without haste, cookery lessons drawn from the kitchen garden, and woodland paths where wildlife thrives. Craftsmanship, farming and forestry continue here as living traditions.

property_title: Hotel Sacher: Timeless Viennese Elegance Beside the Opera House
property_intro: Facing the Vienna State Opera, Hotel Sacher has welcomed composers, diplomats and curious travellers since 1876. Behind its stately facade, rooms dressed in silk, damask and original artworks open onto a city of coffee houses and concert halls. Linger over the legendary Sacher-Torte, still made by hand each morning, or retreat to the rooftop spa. Family-owned across generations, the hotel champions Austrian craftsmanship, regional producers and the artisans who keep Viennese tradition quietly alive.

property_title: Gstaad Palace: Alpine Grandeur Above Switzerland's Saanenland
property_intro: Crowning a wooded hill above Gstaad, this turreted landmark has been guided by the same family since 1938 \u2014 a rare continuity you feel in every welcome. Bernese peaks frame the windows, while below, the Saanenland's timber chalets and working farms shape the seasons. Days might mean glacier skiing, forest trails or the vast Palace Spa; evenings, candlelit dining rooms and a legendary nightclub. Local producers, alpine artisans and village traditions remain quietly central throughout.

property_title: Tinajani Canyon: Stone Giants and Boundless Altiplano Nights
property_intro: High on Peru's southern altiplano, Tinajani sits among wind-carved rock towers that glow amber at dusk, an hour's drive from Ayaviri and the wide grasslands of Puno. Rooms are pared back and tactile, warmed by alpaca wool and local stone, framing views of the canyon's sandstone sentinels. Ride out with Quechua horsemen, trace condor flight paths, or stargaze in near-total silence. Grazing agreements with neighbouring communities help protect this remarkable, little-visited landscape.

property_title: Titilaka: A Contemporary Sanctuary on Lake Titicaca's Shore
property_intro: Set on a private peninsula reaching into Lake Titicaca, Titilaka stands alone amid reeds, water and the vast Altiplano light. Its eighteen rooms pair Andean textiles and local stone with floor-to-ceiling windows framing the lake's changing moods. Days unfold at your own pace: kayaking at dawn, visiting Uros and Taquile communities, or cycling to hillside chullpas. The lodge works closely with surrounding villages, employing and training neighbours while championing Peruvian craft and produce.

property_title: Eha Retreat: Estonia's Quiet Sanctuary Among Pine and Bog
property_intro: Tucked between whispering pine forest and ancient bogland, Eha Retreat invites you to slow down to the rhythm of Estonia's long northern light. Timber-clad cabins, warmed by wood-fired saunas and dressed in local linen, open onto still water and birdsong. Days unfold with forest foraging, dawn swims and candlelit dinners drawn from nearby smallholdings. Built with regional craftspeople and committed to protecting the surrounding wetlands, it is a place that restores more than the traveller.

property_title: Bahía Bustamante: Patagonia's Wild Coast, Quietly Reimagined
property_intro: On a remote stretch of Argentina's Atlantic Patagonia, Bahía Bustamante began life as a seaweed harvesting village and remains a working family estancia. Six simple, sun-washed houses face a bay alive with sea lions, penguins and petrified forests, while guanacos roam the steppe behind. Days unfold with guided kayaking, coastal walks, birdwatching and long lunches of lamb and shellfish. Solar power, careful stewardship and local employment keep this extraordinary place thriving, largely unchanged.

property_title: BE Agafay: Desert Stillness Beneath Marrakech's Atlas Skies
property_intro: Set in the stone desert of Agafay, an hour from Marrakech, BE Agafay unfolds across sun-bleached hills with the snow-topped Atlas as its horizon. Tented suites in earthen tones sit lightly on the land, powered with care and built with local craft. Days pass with hammam rituals, horseback rides through the dunes, stargazing dinners and visits to neighbouring villages, where the camp's partnerships support Berber artisans, schooling and water projects.

property_title: Dragsholm Slot: Storied Castle Living on Odsherred's Wild Coast
property_intro:
Rising above the reclaimed marshes of Odsherred, Dragsholm Slot has watched over this corner of Zealand for some 800 years 
counting kings, prisoners and, they say, a lingering ghost or two among its guests. Today the whitewashed castle is a place of quiet indulgence: rooms layered with Nordic craft and antiquity, dining shaped by the estate's own fields, forests and shoreline, and a kitchen team who forage what the season offers, championing local growers throughout.

property_title: The Thief: Contemporary Art and Fjord Calm in Oslo's Harbour
property_intro: Set on Tjuvholmen, a reclaimed islet once known for smugglers, The Thief looks out across Oslo's harbour towards the fjord's open water. Next door sits the Astrup Fearnley Museum, and the spirit carries indoors: original works by Warhol and Vasarely hang beside Norwegian craftsmanship and softly lit Scandinavian interiors. Days drift between the rooftop terrace, the spa and locally sourced dining, while the city's galleries, saunas and island ferries wait a short stroll from the door.

property_title: Amerikalinjen: Where Oslo's Maritime Heritage Meets Modern Ease
property_intro: Once the headquarters of the Norwegian America Line, this handsome 1919 building beside Oslo Central Station now welcomes travellers rather than emigrants bound for New York. Rooms layer Nordic restraint with walnut, brass and soft wool, while the inner courtyard, jazz cellar and cocktail bar draw locals as readily as guests. Breakfast celebrates small Norwegian producers, and the opera house, fjord promenade and Barcode district lie within an easy stroll of the door.

property_title: Walaker Hotel: Nine Generations on the Shores of Lustrafjord
property_intro: In the orchard village of Solvorn, where the Lustrafjord narrows beneath steep green slopes, Walaker Hotel has welcomed travellers since 1640 — cared for by the same family across nine generations. Rooms in the old timber wing sit alongside a gallery of Norwegian art, while dinners draw on fjord fish, farm produce and the hotel's own garden. Row out to Urnes stave church, hike glacier valleys, then return for coffee on the lawn.

property_title: Kviknes Hotel: Timbered Grandeur on Norway's Sognefjord Shore
property_intro: On the shore of the Sognefjord, in the village of Balestrand, Kviknes Hotel has welcomed travellers since 1877 and remains in the hands of the same family. Dragon-carved gables, panelled salons and an art collection gathered over generations set the tone, while glaciers and orchards frame the water beyond. Arrive by fjord ferry, kayak at dusk, dine on produce from neighbouring farms, and settle into a house that has quietly shaped its community for five generations.

property_title: Lyngen Lodge: Arctic Wilderness and Quiet Luxury in Norway
property_intro: Tucked along a remote shoreline in Norway's Arctic north, Lyngen Lodge faces the snow-draped Lyngen Alps across still fjord water. This intimate timber lodge sleeps just twenty, with sheepskins, open fires and a wood-fired hot tub beneath the northern lights. Days unfold with husky sledding, ski touring and boat trips in search of whales, guided by locals who know these mountains intimately. Meals draw on Arctic ingredients, prepared with care and served among fellow guests turned friends.

property_title: Lydmar Hotel: Stockholm's Waterfront Rhythm and Quiet Style
property_intro: Overlooking Nybroviken's boats and the Royal Palace across the water, Lydmar Hotel occupies a stately Blasieholmen address with an unhurried, music-loving soul. No two rooms are alike; each is layered with contemporary art, vintage finds and deep windows framing the harbour. Live sessions drift through the bar, the lift doubles as a listening room, and breakfast lingers. Beyond the door, Stockholm's galleries, islands and archipelago ferries begin within a few unhurried steps.

property_title: Brändön Lodge: Swedish Lapland Where Forest Meets Frozen Sea
property_intro: On a quiet stretch of Lapland coastline near Luleå, Brändön Lodge sits between pine forest and the shallow, brackish waters of the Bothnian Bay. Timber cabins face the archipelago, warmed by wood fires and long Nordic light. Days unfold with husky sledding, ice fishing on the frozen sea or hovercraft rides to uninhabited islands. Family-run for decades, the lodge works closely with local guides and serves the North's own produce, simply and generously.

property_title: Siggesta Gård: Archipelago Living on a Working Swedish Farm
property_intro: Set on Värmdö in Stockholm's archipelago, Siggesta Gård gathers meadows, forest and shoreline around a working farm just forty minutes from the capital. Rooms and cottages are dressed in pale timber and heritage hues, while stables, kitchen gardens and grazing cattle shape the rhythm of each day. Ride out along woodland trails, paddle the bays, then linger over dishes drawn from the farm's own harvest and neighbouring producers. A quietly rooted retreat where rural craft and coastal calm meet.

property_title: Stamba Hotel: Tbilisi's Storied Printing House Reborn in Style
property_intro: Set within a Soviet-era publishing house on Tbilisi's leafy Vera district, Stamba keeps its industrial bones intact \u2014 concrete beams, original presses and soaring ceilings softened by leather, brass and hanging greenery. Rooms open onto a vertical farm supplying the kitchen, while the courtyard hums with local designers, roasters and thinkers. Wander to Rustaveli Avenue, linger over Georgian wine, then return to a hotel that champions the city's makers rather than merely hosting its visitors.

property_title: Lopota Lake Resort & Spa: Kakheti's Lakeside Wine Retreat
property_intro: Cradled in Georgia's Kakheti wine country, Lopota Lake Resort & Spa rests beside a still lake with the Caucasus rising behind it. Vineyards, orchards and walnut groves supply the kitchens, while the spa draws on thermal waters and local herbs. Days might mean horse riding through the valley, cellar visits with Kakhetian winemakers, or simply watching mist lift from the water. Family-run and rooted in its region, it champions local growers, artisans and time-honoured hospitality.

property_title: Tsinandali Estate: Wine, Music and Kakheti's Living Heritage
property_intro: In the heart of Kakheti, Georgia's winemaking heartland, Tsinandali Estate unfolds across nineteenth-century gardens once tended by Prince Alexander Chavchavadze. Vines climb towards the Caucasus, while restored manor rooms and the estate's own concert hall host chamber music beneath ancient trees. Descend to the historic cellar, where qvevri and rare vintages tell of Georgia's 8,000-year wine story, then linger over Kakhetian cooking made with produce from neighbouring farms and family kitchens. It is a place that rewards slow days.

property_title: The Chedi Muscat: Serene Omani Elegance Beside the Sea
property_intro: Set within 21 hectares of manicured gardens between the Hajar mountains and the Gulf of Oman, The Chedi Muscat pairs Omani craftsmanship with clean, contemplative Asian-inspired design. Days unfold along a 103-metre adults-only pool, on a private beach, or beneath the lantern-lit ceiling of The Restaurant, where six kitchens cook in full view. Spa rituals draw on regional botanicals, while local artisans and produce shape much of what you'll taste, touch and take home.}

property_title: Anantara Al Jabal Al Akhdar: Oman's Canyon-Edge Sanctuary
property_intro: Perched 2,000 metres above sea level on the rim of a vast canyon, Anantara Al Jabal Al Akhdar sits among the terraced rose gardens and juniper slopes of Oman's Green Mountain. Stone-clad villas echo the fortresses of the Hajar range, while cool mountain air invites long evenings by the fire. Wander ancient falaj channels with local guides, greet villagers in Wadi Bani Habib, and taste damask rosewater distilled just beyond your terrace.

property_title: Thousand Nights Camp: Desert Serenity in Oman's Wahiba Sands
property_intro: Tucked deep within the amber dunes of the Wahiba Sands, Thousand Nights Camp offers a rare kind of stillness. Canvas suites and stone-built rooms open onto shifting sands, lit by lanterns and an unhindered canopy of stars. Days unfold with camel rides, dune walks and Bedouin coffee poured by hosts whose families have long read this landscape. Local craftsmanship shapes the interiors, while the camp employs and supports the surrounding desert communities.

property_title: Old Cartagena's Timeless Colonial Splendour at Casa Pestagua
property_intro: Behind coral-stone walls in Cartagena's historic centre, Casa Pestagua unfolds around shaded courtyards where bougainvillaea spills over 18th-century arcades. Once a count's residence, this restored mansion pairs original mahogany beams and hand-laid tiles with a rooftop plunge pool overlooking terracotta rooftops and the Caribbean beyond. Days drift between candlelit Caribbean dinners, guided walks through Getsemaní's murals and boat trips to the Rosario Islands. Local artisans, growers and craftspeople shape much of what you'll taste, touch and take home.

property_title: Bastión Luxury Hotel: Colonial Charm Within Cartagena's Walls
property_intro: Tucked into a quiet corner of Cartagena's walled Old Town, Bastión Luxury Hotel occupies a restored colonial mansion where balconies spill with bougainvillea and courtyards echo with the trickle of water. Interiors pair Caribbean craftsmanship with contemporary calm, while the rooftop pool looks out across terracotta roofs to the sea. Days might begin with local coffee and end with ceviche at Bastión Alto, prepared with produce from nearby growers and fishermen who supply the kitchen daily.

property_title: The Charlee: Design, Rooftop Views and Medell\u00edn's Warm Pulse
property_intro: Tucked into the leafy streets of El Poblado, moments from Parque Lleras, The Charlee brings a considered kind of glamour to Medell\u00edn. Interiors blend sculptural detail with Colombian craftsmanship, while the rooftop pool frames the Aburr\u00e1 Valley and its ring of green mountains. Days might begin with a coffee tasting or a cycle through Comuna 13's murals, guided by locals whose stories shape the city. Service here is generous, intuitive and quietly proud of its roots.

property_title: Hacienda Bambusa: Coffee Country Living in Colombia's Quindío
property_intro: Set amid 44 hectares of cacao, bamboo and grazing land in Colombia's coffee region, Hacienda Bambusa is a restored working farm where guests wake to birdsong and the scent of guadua. Six characterful rooms open onto wide verandas, while days unfold with horseback rides, cacao harvesting and tastings of estate-grown chocolate. Family-run and deeply local, the hacienda employs neighbouring villagers and protects the wetlands and wildlife that thrive along its boundaries.

property_title: Lot Boutique Hotel: Refined Albanian Charm in the Old Town
property_intro: Tucked within Albania's storied streets, Lot Boutique Hotel welcomes you with quiet confidence. Stone walls, local craftsmanship and softly lit interiors set the tone, while sun-warmed terraces invite slow mornings over strong coffee and honeyed pastries. Family-run and rooted in its neighbourhood, the hotel champions regional producers, artisans and guides who share the area's history first-hand. Wander to nearby markets, castles and coastline, then return to a room where every detail feels considered rather than staged.

property_title: La Gazelle d'Or Resort & Spa: Algeria's Golden Desert Calm
property_intro: Set where Algeria's cultivated gardens give way to open desert, La Gazelle d'Or Resort & Spa offers a gentler rhythm. Ochre walls, hand-carved cedar and shaded courtyards draw on regional craft traditions, while the spa turns to argan, rose and local clay. Days might mean riding at dawn, learning to prepare a slow-cooked tagine, or simply watching light shift across the palms. Local artisans and growers supply much of what you'll admire and taste here.

property_title: Hotel de Sal Luna Salada: Salt-Carved Calm Above the Uyuni Flats
property_intro:
Perched on a rise at the edge of the Salar de Uyuni, Luna Salada is built almost entirely from blocks of salt drawn from the plain below. Walls, floors and furnishings glow softly by candlelight, while windows frame a horizon that shifts from blinding white to mirrored sky. Days bring sunrise crossings, stargazing and visits to nearby Colchani, where local families and quinoa growers share in the hotel's story.

Solar power and careful water stewardship keep this remote retreat gentle on its surroundings.

property_title: Palacio de Sal: A Salt-Carved Retreat on Bolivia's Great Flat
property_intro: On the eastern edge of the Salar de Uyuni, Palacio de Sal is built almost entirely from blocks of salt hewn from the flats themselves ",

property_title: Mallku Cueva: Andean Stillness Carved into Bolivia's Highlands
property_intro: Set within Bolivia's sculpted highlands, Mallku Cueva shelters beneath rock formations shaped by wind and centuries. Interiors of adobe, stone and handwoven textiles echo the surrounding valleys, while wide windows draw in the clarity of Andean light. Days unfold with guided walks to petroglyphs, condor-watching at dawn and long conversations with Quechua weavers whose craft sustains the region. Locally sourced meals, solar warmth and community partnerships make this a retreat where comfort and conscience sit easily together.

property_title: Anantara Uluwatu Bali Resort: Clifftop Calm Above the Surf
property_intro: Perched on the limestone cliffs of Bali's Bukit Peninsula, Anantara Uluwatu overlooks Impossibles Beach, where surfers trace the swell far below. Suites and pool villas open to the Indian Ocean, their teak, stone and woven detailing drawn from Balinese craft traditions. Days might begin with a cliffside yoga session, drift into a Balinese healing ritual, then close over grilled seafood at sunset. The resort supports local artisans and coastal clean-ups, keeping this stretch of shoreline thriving.

property_title: Anantara Guiyang Resort: Lakeside Calm in Guizhou's Highlands
property_intro: Cradled by the forested karst hills above Baihua Lake, Anantara Guiyang Resort offers a gentler pace within one of China's least-hurried provinces. Interiors draw on Miao and Buyi craft traditions, with silverwork, indigo batik and timber detailing shaping quietly elegant spaces. Days unfold with lakeside walks, tea tastings from nearby plantations and visits to hillside villages where artisans still work by hand. Return for spa rituals, Guizhou-inspired dining and long, mist-softened evenings.

property_title: Anantara Palazzo Naiadi Rome Hotel: Where Antiquity Awakens
property_intro: Overlooking Piazza della Repubblica, this 19th-century palazzo rises above the remains of the Baths of Diocletian, its Roman foundations still visible beneath the floors. Frescoed ceilings and marble colonnades meet contemporary calm, while the rooftop pool and terrace frame domes and rooftops at golden hour. Wander to Termini, the Trevi Fountain or Villa Borghese within minutes, then return for Mediterranean dining, thoughtful spa rituals and a heritage carefully preserved by Italian artisans and conservators.

property_title: Anantara Desaru Coast Resort & Villas: Johor's Quiet Shoreline
property_intro: On Johor's south-eastern edge, where the South China Sea meets a tranquil stretch of forested coast, Anantara Desaru Coast Resort & Villas unfolds across lagoons, palms and sand. Interiors draw on Malay craftsmanship, while private pool villas invite unhurried days. Join turtle conservation efforts along the shore, learn regional recipes from local cooks, or paddle the mangroves at dawn. Nearby fishing villages and rainforest trails reward those curious enough to wander beyond the gates.

property_title: Anantara Dhigu Maldives Resort: Barefoot Luxury on the Lagoon
property_intro:
Set on a slender island in South Male Atoll, Anantara Dhigu is cradled by one of the Maldives' widest lagoons

property_title: Niyama Private Islands: Barefoot Elegance in the Dhaalu Sea
property_intro: Two linked islands in the Maldives' Dhaalu Atoll, Niyama pairs Play with Chill \u2014 one alive with music and discovery, the other hushed beneath swaying palms. Villas rest over turquoise lagoons or tucked into jungle, while Subsix hosts dinners six metres beneath the waves. Snorkel reefs nurtured by the resident marine biologist, join coral restoration dives, or drift home by dhoni as frigatebirds circle. Warm, unhurried and quietly conscious of its island home.

property_title: Naladhu Private Island: Barefoot Seclusion in the Maldives
property_intro: Tucked within the South Male Atoll, Naladhu Private Island holds just twenty houses, each with a private pool and a stretch of shoreline that feels entirely your own. There are no schedules here, only a dedicated House Master who arranges reef snorkelling, sunset dhoni sailings or dinner beneath the coconut palms. Interiors nod to Maldivian craft in timber and coral tones, while coral restoration and marine research quietly shape the island's future beyond your stay.

property_title: Anantara Veli Maldives Resort: Barefoot Luxury on a Quiet Lagoon
property_intro: Just 35 minutes by speedboat from Mal\uives, Anantara Veli rests on a slender South Male Atoll island reserved for adults. Thatched over-water bungalows perch above a luminous lagoon, reached by timber walkways that seem to float. Days unfold with sunrise yoga, dives among coral gardens tended by the resort's marine biologists, and dinners at an over-water Thai restaurant. Guests can help plant coral frames, leaving something quietly enduring behind.

property_title: Six Senses La Sagesse: Barefoot Luxury on Grenada's Wild Shores
property_intro: Set across three bays on Grenada's untamed south coast, Six Senses La Sagesse unfolds between mangroves, cocoa groves and a crescent of quiet sand. Rooms in soft timber and local stone open to sea breezes, while spa rituals draw on island botanicals. Snorkel the underwater sculpture park, forage with the chef, or meet the growers behind Grenada's celebrated chocolate. Reef restoration and island partnerships mean your stay leaves something lasting behind.

property_title: Six Senses Kaplankaya: Aegean Wellness on Turkey's Wild Coast
property_intro: Set on a rugged headland where pine forest meets the Aegean, Six Senses Kaplankaya looks out across turquoise bays near the ancient ruins of Iasos. Rooms in pale stone and timber frame the horizon, while the vast wellness centre draws guests into longevity programmes, sound therapy and sunrise swims. Meals lean on the organic garden and nearby villages, and marine conservation work protects the seagrass below. Days here unfold slowly, guided by water, light and appetite.

property_title: SUJÁN The Serai: Desert Luxury in the Dunes of Jaisalmer
property_intro: Set within a private wilderness on the fringes of the Thar Desert, SUJÁN The Serai recalls the royal encampments of Rajasthan's warrior princes. Handcrafted tents in cream canvas open onto sculpted gardens, stone courtyards and a horizon of sand and scrub. Days unfold with camel expeditions, desert dining beneath the stars and visits to the golden fort of Jaisalmer. Behind the elegance lies genuine commitment to local artisans, village schools and the fragile desert ecosystem.

property_title: Eden Boutique Hotel: A Refined Moroccan Retreat Reimagined
property_intro: Tucked within Morocco's sun-warmed streets, Eden Boutique Hotel welcomes you into a house shaped by local craft: hand-cut zellige, carved cedar and courtyards cooled by citrus trees. Days unfold slowly here, with rooftop breakfasts, hammam rituals and walks guided by neighbours who know every hidden doorway. Artisans from nearby workshops furnished each room, and the kitchen sources from surrounding smallholdings. It is an intimate address for travellers who value quiet beauty, genuine hospitality and a lighter footprint.

property_title: Morgan's Rock Hacienda: Wild Pacific Coast Living in Nicaragua
property_intro: Tucked into 4,000 acres of tropical dry forest above a private Pacific beach, Morgan's Rock Hacienda pairs barefoot ease with genuine purpose. Hardwood bungalows stand open to the treeline, where howler monkeys announce the morning and turtles nest on the sand below. Days might mean riding through the reforestation project, gathering eggs on the working farm, or paddling the estuary at dusk. Much of what reaches your table is grown here, tended by neighbouring families.

property_title: Fox on the Rocks: A Wild Alpine Hideaway in the Slovenian Hills
property_intro: Tucked into the karst uplands of Slovenia, where limestone ridges give way to beech forest and grazing meadows, Fox on the Rocks is a retreat built for slow days and long views. Timber, stone and glass frame the changing light, while foraging walks, mountain trails and unhurried suppers of neighbours' produce shape the rhythm here. Rainwater, solar warmth and local craftsmanship quietly underpin it all. Wake to woodsmoke, birdsong and the promise of somewhere genuinely unspoilt.

property_title: Ceylon Tea Trails: Colonial Bungalow Living in Sri Lanka's Hills
property_intro: High in Sri Lanka's Bogawantalawa Valley, Ceylon Tea Trails gathers five restored planters' bungalows among emerald tea terraces and mist-wrapped peaks. Each house keeps its own butler, cook and garden, with afternoon tea served on lawns above Castlereagh Lake. Walk the paths between them, tour a working tea factory, or trace the day's leaf from plucking to cup. The estates remain productive, supporting the plucking communities whose knowledge shapes every harvest here.

property_title: Wild Coast Tented Lodge: Where Sri Lanka's Wilderness Awaits
property_intro: On the fringes of Yala National Park, where jungle gives way to the Indian Ocean, Wild Coast Tented Lodge unfolds as a cluster of cocoon-like suites shaped from bamboo, teak and canvas. Leopards prowl beyond the boulders; elephants pass at dusk. Days drift between dawn safaris, ocean-fed pools and slow dinners under the stars. Built lightly on the land, the lodge supports local livelihoods and habitat protection, making indulgence feel genuinely purposeful.

property_title: Cape Weligama: Clifftop Serenity Above Sri Lanka's Southern Sea
property_intro: Perched on a red-earth headland high above the Indian Ocean, Cape Weligama gathers just a handful of villas and suites across twelve hectares of gardens on Sri Lanka's southern coast. Days unfold with whale-watching voyages, stilt fishermen at dawn and Ayurvedic treatments scented with local herbs. Geoffrey Bawa-inspired architecture frames sweeping horizons, while the resort supports nearby marine research and village crafts, so your stay quietly strengthens the community that makes this coastline so compelling.

property_title: Helvetia & Bristol Firenze: Where Old Florence Whispers Luxury
property_intro:
Steps from the Duomo and the Arno, this 19th-century Florentine townhouse has welcomed writers, composers and curious travellers since 1894. Frescoed salons, antique furnishings and a subterranean spa built around Roman-era foundations sit alongside a restaurant championing Tuscan growers and small producers. Artisan workshops, private gallery visits and quiet mornings in the winter garden reveal a city beyond its crowds 
together with a hotel that treats heritage as something to be lived in, not merely admired.

property_title: Andara Resort & Villas: Phuket's Hillside Haven Above the Sea
property_intro: Set into a forested hillside above Kamala Bay, Andara Resort & Villas looks out across the Andaman Sea from Phuket's quieter west coast. Teak-clad pavilions and private pool villas draw on traditional Thai craftsmanship, with local artisans shaping much of the woodwork. Days unfold slowly here: long-tail boat trips to nearby islands, Thai cookery lessons with market visits, and treatments guided by herbal traditions. The team supports Kamala's schools and beach-care initiatives, keeping the community close.

property_title: Parklane Resort & Spa: Limassol's Coastal Sanctuary of Calm
property_intro: Set along Limassol's shoreline, where the Mediterranean meets landscaped gardens and a private stretch of beach, Parklane Resort & Spa blends contemporary Cypriot design with an unhurried rhythm. Days unfold between the Kalloni Spa's thermal circuit, olive-grove dining and sailing lessons at the marina. The resort nurtures sea turtle habitats, sources produce from nearby villages and champions local craftsmanship, so every stay quietly supports the island's landscapes and communities beyond the garden walls.

property_title: Ayan Zalaat: Wild Steppe Serenity Beneath Mongolia's Skies
property_intro: Set amid the rolling grasslands and granite outcrops of Mongolia's steppe, Ayan Zalaat offers a rare kind of quiet. Handcrafted gers blend nomadic craftsmanship with considered comfort, while days unfold on horseback, beside herders' fires or beneath skies unmarred by light. Meals draw on the surrounding valleys and local producers, and the camp works closely with neighbouring families to safeguard grazing traditions. Come evening, the wind settles, the stars gather, and time seems generously unhurried.

property_title: Amanera: Cliffside Calm on the Dominican Republic's North Coast
property_intro: Perched above Playa Grande on the Dominican Republic's wilder northern shore, Amanera looks out across the Atlantic from a bluff fringed with tropical forest. Casitas of warm coralline stone and local hardwood open to sea breezes and private pools, while below, surfers trace the bay's long right-hand break. Days might mean riding through cacao plantations, swimming in freshwater caves, or playing a coastline golf course. Local artisans, farmers and reforestation projects are woven quietly into daily life here.

property_title: Fasano Trancoso: Barefoot Elegance on Bahia's Wild Coastline
property_intro: Set between the Atlantic and a protected sweep of Bahian rainforest, Fasano Trancoso unfolds across hectares of native mata atlântica, its low-slung bungalows shaded by cashew and jackfruit trees. Days drift between the clifftop pool, a coastal golf course and horseback rides along near-empty sand. Interiors marry Brazilian hardwoods with local craftsmanship, while ongoing reforestation and close ties with Trancoso's Quadrado community keep the surrounding ecosystem, and its people, at the heart of every stay.

property_title: Fasano Belo Horizonte: Refined Calm in Minas Gerais' Heart
property_intro: Set in the leafy Lourdes district, Fasano Belo Horizonte brings quiet sophistication to Brazil's most understated capital. Interiors by Isay Weinfeld pair warm timber and Brazilian craftsmanship with generous light, while the rooftop pool frames views towards the Serra do Curral. Downstairs, Fasano's kitchen honours mineiro cooking with produce from surrounding farms. Beyond the door lie Niemeyer's Pampulha, artist-run galleries and the mountain trails that lead towards Inhotim's extraordinary gardens.

property_title: Fasano Boa Vista: Where the Paulista Countryside Slows Right Down
property_intro: An hour or so beyond S\u00e3o Paulo, near Porto Feliz, Fasano Boa Vista unfolds across a vast working estate of pasture, lakes and regenerating Atlantic Forest. Isay Weinfeld's architecture nods to colonial farmhouses while feeling wholly contemporary: deep verandas, cool stone, long views. Days drift between the equestrian centre, golf, canoeing and unhurried lunches drawn from the farm's own gardens. Native replanting and local employment keep the estate rooted in its community, and quietly thriving.

property_title: Fasano Fifth Avenue: Brazilian Warmth in the Heart of Manhattan
property_intro: Overlooking Fifth Avenue near Madison Square Park, Fasano Fifth Avenue brings a distinctly Brazilian sensibility to Manhattan. Housed in a restored landmark, its interiors pair rich timber, marble and mid-century Brazilian design with the quiet confidence of a private residence. Days unfold slowly here: espresso in the salon, dinner shaped by the family's celebrated Italian kitchens, evenings spent watching the city shift below. Independent galleries, Flatiron bookshops and the Hudson's waterfront paths all sit within an easy stroll.

property_title: Fasano Rio de Janeiro: Modernist Glamour Above Ipanema Beach
property_intro: Facing the surf of Ipanema, Fasano Rio de Janeiro channels the city's 1960s spirit through Philippe Starck's playful, sculptural interiors and rosewood warmth. Days drift between the rooftop pool, where Corcovado rises beyond the horizon, and Fasano al Mare's seafood, sourced from Brazilian waters. Step outside for barefoot mornings on the sand, cycling the beachfront, or trails through Tijuca's protected rainforest. Local artisans, growers and musicians shape the experience, grounding refined comfort in genuine carioca character.

property_title: Fasano Salvador: Art Deco Grandeur Above the Bay of All Saints
property_intro: Set within the 1930s former headquarters of Bahia's oldest newspaper, Fasano Salvador brings new life to the historic Pelourinho quarter, its restored Art Deco lines framing wide views across the Bay of All Saints. Rooftop pool afternoons drift into candomble-inflected evenings, with Bahian flavours reworked at the restaurant and craftspeople from the surrounding streets shaping much of the interior. A stay here places you at the heart of Salvador's living Afro-Brazilian culture.

property_title: Fasano São Paulo: Where Jardins Meets Timeless Italian Grace
property_intro: Set on a leafy street in Jardins, moments from Rua Oscar Freire's ateliers and the greenery of Parque Trianon, Fasano São Paulo brings a quiet confidence to Brazil's most restless city. Isay Weinfeld's interiors pair dark wood, marble and soft lighting for a mood closer to a private club than a hotel. Dine on celebrated Italian cooking, retreat to the spa, and drift into the city's live music scene downstairs at Baretto.

property_title: Time + Tide Chongwe Suites: Riverside Living in Lower Zambezi
property_intro: Where the Chongwe River meets the Zambezi, two open-fronted suites sit beneath ancient winterthorn trees on the edge of Zambia's Lower Zambezi National Park. Sculpted from local stone and copper, each has its own plunge pool, private chef and guide, so days unfold at your pace \u2014 canoeing past pods of hippo, walking with elephants nearby, or simply watching the escarpment change colour. Your stay supports anti-poaching patrols and conservation education across the valley.

property_title: Time + Tide Luwi: Walking Safaris in South Luangwa's Wild Heart
property_intro: Tucked beside a seasonal river in a remote corner of South Luangwa, Time + Tide Luwi feels wonderfully unhurried. Six grass-and-thatch chalets are rebuilt each season using local materials, leaving barely a trace on the land. Days begin on foot with expert guides tracking lion and wild dog, and end at the hippo-filled lagoon with a sundowner in hand. Your stay supports community schools, clinics and conservation work across the valley.

property_title: Time + Tide Nsolo: Barefoot Bush Living in South Luangwa Valley
property_intro: Tucked beneath ebony and mahogany trees on the banks of the seasonal Luwi River, Nsolo is a small camp with a big heart in Zambia's South Luangwa. Four thatched chalets open to the bush, lit by lantern and lulled by hyena and owl calls. Days unfold on foot with expert walking guides, tracking lion and leopard through the sand rivers, while guest contributions support local conservation and community schooling across the valley.

property_title: Time + Tide Kakuli: Wild Riverbanks in Zambia's South Luangwa
property_intro: Set where the Luangwa and Luwi rivers meet, Time + Tide Kakuli is a tented camp of quiet confidence, named after the old buffalo bulls who wander close to camp. Four canvas suites open to the sandy riverbed, shaded by ebony trees. Days here belong to walking safaris led by Zambia's finest guides, with night drives revealing leopard and honey badger. Guest stays support local schools and conservation work across the valley.

property_title: Time + Tide Mchenja: Under Ebony Groves by the Luangwa River
property_intro: Set beneath a cathedral of ebony trees on a curve of the Luangwa River, Mchenja is intimate by design — just five airy tented suites, each with an open-air bathtub angled towards the water. Days unfold with walking safaris, night drives and lagoons crowded with hippo and heron. Solar-powered and seasonally light on the land, the camp channels support into Zambian conservation and village schools, so your stay quietly strengthens the wilderness beyond your veranda.

property_title: Time + Tide Chinzombo: Riverside Luxury in Zambia's Valley
property_intro: On a private bend of the Luangwa River, opposite Zambia's celebrated South Luangwa National Park, Chinzombo's six villas rest beneath ancient ebony trees. Canvas, timber and glass frame the water, where hippos gather at dusk and leopards move through the shadows. Walking safaris pioneered in this valley remain the heart of the experience, guided by trackers whose knowledge spans generations. Time + Tide's partnerships with local schools and conservation teams ensure your stay leaves the valley stronger.

property_title: &Beyond Mnemba Island: Barefoot Luxury on Zanzibar's Reef
property_intro: Drifting off Zanzibar's north-eastern shore, this tiny coral island is ringed by a marine reserve where green turtles nest and reef fish shimmer in the shallows. Twelve airy bandas, woven from palm and driftwood tones, sit tucked among casuarina trees just steps from the sand. Days unfold with diving, dhow sailing and long, unhurried lunches, while conservation work with local communities protects nesting beaches and reef life for generations still to come.

property_title: Belmond Hotel Caruso: Ravello's Cliffside Palace Above the Sea
property_intro: Perched high above the Amalfi Coast in Ravello, Belmond Hotel Caruso occupies an 11th-century palazzo where frescoes, vaulted ceilings and centuries-old marble meet the blue expanse of the Tyrrhenian. Days unfold slowly here: swimming in the infinity pool that seems to spill into the gulf, wandering terraced gardens scented with lemon and jasmine, or sailing the coastline by vintage boat. Local artisans, growers and traditions shape every plate, garden bed and quiet detail.

property_title: Belmond Hotel Splendido: Portofino's Cliffside Italian Icon
property_intro: Perched above Portofino's harbour in a former 16th-century monastery, Belmond Hotel Splendido looks out across the Ligurian Sea through terraces of olive, lemon and cypress. Days drift between the saltwater pool, boat trips to San Fruttuoso abbey and coastal walks in the protected marine park. Interiors carry generations of Riviera glamour without fuss, while kitchens draw on Ligurian growers and fishermen, and the gardens are tended with the region's fragile ecology in mind.

property_title: Maroma Resort & Spa: Where the Riviera Maya Truly Slows Down
property_intro: Set on a crescent of pale sand between jungle and the Caribbean, Maroma Resort & Spa has drawn wanderers to Mexico's Riviera Maya since 1995. Its whitewashed casitas, shaded by palms and dressed in Mexican craft, sit within protected dunes where turtles nest each summer. Days drift from cenote swims to temazcal ceremonies led by local healers, before spa rituals and long, unhurried dinners beneath the stars. Luxury here is measured in quiet, not excess.

property_title: Belmond Splendido Mare: Life on Portofino's Storied Piazzetta
property_intro: Right on Portofino's famous piazzetta, Belmond Splendido Mare sits where fishing boats still bob beside polished yachts. Just fourteen rooms, dressed by Martin Brudnizki in sunlit stripes and Ligurian craftsmanship, open onto the harbour's gentle theatre. Days drift between DaV Mare's seafood, hillside walks through the protected Portofino park and swims from sun-warmed rocks. Local artisans, growers and fishermen shape the experience, making this feel less like a hotel and more like belonging to the village.

property_title: Hotel Cipriani: Venetian Calm on the Shores of Giudecca Island
property_intro: A short launch across the water from St Mark's, Hotel Cipriani occupies the tip of Giudecca, where walled gardens, olive trees and a saltwater pool replace the crowds. Rooms look towards the lagoon, breakfast arrives with birdsong, and the kitchen draws on produce grown in the hotel's own vineyard and vegetable garden. Guests can row with local masters, learn Venetian glasswork, or simply watch the tide shift colour from the terrace.

property_title: Miraflores Park: Where Lima Meets the Pacific in Refined Style
property_intro: Perched above the cliffs of Miraflores, this Belmond retreat looks out across the Pacific while Lima's galleries, ceviche counters and pre-Columbian treasures wait a short stroll away. Interiors blend Peruvian craftsmanship with quiet contemporary calm, and the rooftop pool offers front-row seats to the sunset. Days might begin with a market walk beside the chef, sourcing produce from Andean smallholders, and end with pisco in hand, watching paragliders drift along the shoreline.

property_title: The Cadogan Hotel: Refined Belgravia Living in Knightsbridge
property_intro: Tucked between Sloane Street's boutiques and the leafy calm of Cadogan Gardens, The Cadogan Hotel occupies a storied corner of Knightsbridge once frequented by Oscar Wilde and Lillie Langtry. Behind its red-brick façade, interiors balance Victorian character with contemporary ease, while guests enjoy private access to Cadogan Place Gardens and tennis courts. Dine on seasonal British produce at the Hans' Bar & Grill, then wander to Sloane Square, Chelsea's galleries and the Saatchi's changing exhibitions.

property_title: Mount Nelson: Cape Town's Pink Icon Beneath Table Mountain
property_intro: Set within nine acres of gardens at the foot of Table Mountain, Mount Nelson has welcomed guests through its palm-lined avenue since 1899. The famous pink walls hold light-filled rooms, a spa among the trees and afternoon tea that has become a Cape Town ritual. Beyond the gates, the city's vineyards, galleries and coastline await. Long-standing partnerships with local growers, artists and conservation projects keep this grand old address firmly rooted in its community.

property_title: Grand Hotel Timeo: Timeless Sicilian Grandeur Above Taormina
property_intro: Perched beside Taormina's Greek Theatre, Grand Hotel Timeo looks out across the Ionian Sea with Etna smouldering gently in the distance. Sicily's first hotel, opened in 1873, it still welcomes guests with frescoed salons, jasmine-scented terraces and a garden of century-old trees. Spend mornings exploring the ancient amphitheatre, afternoons among citrus groves, evenings over Sicilian wines chosen from local estates. Family-run kitchens, island artisans and slow, considered service make each stay feel genuinely rooted here.

property_title: Villa San Michele: Tuscan Hillside Serenity Above Florence
property_intro: Set among cypress groves on the slopes of Fiesole, Villa San Michele looks out across Florence and the Arno valley from a former fifteenth-century monastery. Vaulted loggias, frescoed corners and quiet cloisters remain intact, while the kitchen garden shapes menus rooted in the surrounding hills. Days unfold with truffle walks, olive harvests and lessons from local artisans, and evenings settle into candlelit dinners beneath the arches, with the city's domes glowing far below.

property_title: Villa Sant' Andrea: Sicilian Shores Beneath Taormina's Cliffs
property_intro: Tucked into the cove of Mazzar\u00f2, Villa Sant' Andrea began life as a 19th-century English family's seaside retreat, and that unhurried domesticity still lingers. Terraced gardens of bougainvillea and citrus tumble towards a private beach, with Taormina reachable by cable car above. Days drift between Ionian swims, boat trips to Isola Bella's nature reserve and Sicilian dishes drawn from island growers. Antique furnishings, family portraits and shuttered windows framing Calabria complete the picture.

property_title: Jimbaran Puri: Beachfront Serenity on Bali's Southern Shore
property_intro: Set along a curve of pale sand on Bali's south-west coast, Jimbaran Puri gathers thatched cottages within tropical gardens where fishing boats still drift past at dawn. Days unfold gently here: reef swims, Balinese healing rituals, and grilled seafood served barefoot as the sun slips behind the water. Local artisans shape much of the interiors, while nearby fishing families supply the kitchens, keeping this village rhythm alive. An unhurried retreat, moments from Bali's temples and surf breaks.

property_title: Reid's Palace: Clifftop Grandeur Above Madeira's Blue Atlantic
property_intro: Perched on a headland above Funchal Bay, Reid's Palace has welcomed guests to Madeira since 1891, its rose-pink façade framed by ten acres of subtropical gardens tended by resident horticulturists. Afternoon tea on the terrace remains a ritual, while cliff-cut lidos, Michelin-starred dining and Atlantic swims fill the hours between. Interiors marry colonial-era detail with island craftsmanship, and the gardens nurture rare endemic species alongside local growers, giving this celebrated address a quietly rooted sense of place.

property_title: Belmond La Residencia: Mallorca's Artful Escape in Deia
property_intro: Cradled in the Tramuntana mountains above the village of Deia, Belmond La Residencia occupies two 16th-century manor houses surrounded by olive groves and citrus terraces. Mallorca's artistic soul runs deep here: hundreds of original works line the walls, a studio invites guests to paint alongside local artists, and resident donkeys wander the grounds. Days drift between sea-facing pools, hidden coves at Cala Deia, and dinners shaped by the estate's own harvest.

property_title: &Beyond Phinda Mountain Lodge: Where KwaZulu-Natal Unfolds
property_intro: Set high on the slopes of the Ubombo Mountains, &Beyond Phinda Mountain Lodge overlooks a private reserve where seven distinct habitats meet, from sand forest to open savannah. Glass-fronted suites frame the valley below, while cheetah tracking, black rhino conservation drives and Zulu community visits fill the days. Phinda's story is one of restored farmland returned to wilderness, and of schools and clinics supported by every guest who stays here.

property_title: Duba Plains Camp: Wild Water and Wonder in the Okavango
property_intro: Tucked onto a palm-shaded island deep within a private concession in the Okavango Delta, Duba Plains Camp welcomes just twelve guests to a landscape of floodplains, buffalo herds and famously formidable lions. Six tented suites channel 1920s safari elegance, with brass fittings, canvas and leather softened by delta light. Days unfold by mokoro, boat or open vehicle, guided by trackers who know these waters intimately, while your stay supports Great Plains' conservation work across Botswana's wildest reaches.

property_title: Singita Pamushana: Ancient Wilderness in Zimbabwe's South-East
property_intro: Set high on a sandstone ridge above Malilangwe's lake and mopane woodland, Singita Pamushana looks out over one of Zimbabwe's least-travelled corners. Five suites and a private villa draw on Shona artistry and Zimbabwean stone, while days unfold through big-game drives, boat safaris, rock-art walks and rhino tracking. Every stay supports the Malilangwe Trust, which safeguards black rhino and feeds thousands of local children daily \u2014 conservation you can feel from your veranda.

property_title: Vumbura Plains: Where the Okavango Delta's Wild Heart Beats On
property_intro: Set on a private concession in the northern Okavango Delta, Vumbura Plains looks out across floodplains, palm islands and open savannah shared with lion, elephant and red lechwe. Raised timber suites, dressed in natural fibres and soft light, sit lightly on the land. Days move between mokoro glides, walking safaris and unhurried game drives, while the concession is leased from five local villages, whose communities share directly in its success.

property_title: Campi ya Kanzi: Maasai Wilderness, Kenya's Chyulu Hills Retreat
property_intro: Set within the Chyulu Hills, on Maasai group ranch land between Amboseli and Tsavo, Campi ya Kanzi looks out to Kilimanjaro across cloud forest and lava-strewn plains. Just a handful of tented cottages, built by Maasai hands from local stone and thatch, are run entirely on solar power. Days unfold with Maasai guides tracking lion and elephant on foot, while your stay directly funds the Maasai Wilderness Conservation Trust's rangers, schools and clinics.

property_title: Sarara Camp: Wild Northern Kenya, Guided by Samburu Hands
property_intro: Tucked beneath the Mathews Range in Kenya's Namunyak Wildlife Conservancy, Sarara Camp sits on land owned and cared for by the Samburu community. Six tented rooms open to forested hills, with a rock pool fed by natural springs and evenings shaped by singing wells, walking safaris and elephant sightings at the waterhole. Design leans on local craft and quiet restraint, while every stay supports conservancy rangers, schooling and the wildlife corridors beyond.

property_title: Sarara Treehouses: Suspended Above Kenya's Wild Mathews Range
property_intro: Set high in the Mathews Range, within the Samburu-owned Namunyak Conservancy, Sarara Treehouses are three open-fronted platforms cradled among ancient fig trees. Days unfold with elephants drifting to the waterhole below, walks led by Samburu warriors, and cool swims in granite rock pools. Handcrafted interiors and canvas walls keep you close to the forest, while your stay directly supports community conservation, wildlife protection and the pastoralist families who call these hills home.

property_title: Reteti House: Where Northern Kenya's Wild Heart Welcomes You
property_intro: Set within the sunlit expanse of Namunyak Conservancy in northern Kenya, Reteti House sits beside the celebrated Reteti Elephant Sanctuary, where orphaned calves are raised by Samburu keepers before returning to the wild. Days unfold with guided walks across lava ridges, unhurried afternoons on the terrace and conversations with the community whose land and stewardship shape everything here. The interiors are pared-back and tactile, drawing on local craft, and every stay directly supports the sanctuary's work.

property_title: Sarara Wilderness: Where Northern Kenya's Wild Heart Beats On
property_intro: Set within the Namunyak Conservancy in Kenya's Mathews Range, Sarara Wilderness looks out across valleys where elephants drift down to drink at dusk. Owned in partnership with the Samburu community, it offers walking safaris led by warriors, visits to the celebrated Reteti elephant sanctuary and swims in cool rock pools. Interiors blend hand-crafted local materials with quiet comfort, while your stay directly supports conservation and the pastoralists who have long called these hills home.

property_title: Verdala Wellness Hotel: Hilltop Calm Above Historic Malta
property_intro: Set on a wooded ridge above Rabat, Verdala Wellness Hotel looks out towards Mdina's honeyed bastions and the shimmer of the Mediterranean beyond. Pine-shaded gardens, limestone interiors and quiet terraces set the tone for slow mornings and unhurried spa afternoons. Days might begin with breathwork beneath the trees, continue with a walk through the Buskett woodland, and end over Maltese wines and produce from nearby growers. It is an address that rewards curiosity, and a genuine sense of place.

property_title: THE FLAG Costa del Sol: Andalusian Living, Reimagined Daily
property_intro: Set between the Mediterranean and the Sierra de Mijas, THE FLAG Costa del Sol offers serviced apartments designed for those who prefer to settle in rather than simply pass through. Sunlit interiors, generous kitchens and shaded terraces invite slow mornings, while Fuengirola's markets, beach paths and neighbourhood bars sit within easy reach. Cycle to the shore, cook with produce from local growers, or spend an afternoon poolside. A refined base for unhurried, quietly independent travel.

property_title: &Beyond Suyian Lodge: Wild Laikipia, Reimagined in Comfort
property_intro: Set within a vast private conservancy on Kenya's Laikipia Plateau, &Beyond Suyian Lodge looks out across rolling grasslands towards the distant silhouette of Mount Kenya. Just a handful of light-filled suites, shaped by natural stone and canvas, open onto uninterrupted plains where elephant, wild dog and rare Grevy's zebra roam. Ride on horseback, track wildlife on foot, or spend time with the Samburu community whose stewardship, alongside pioneering rewilding work, keeps this remarkable landscape thriving.

property_title: COMO Le Beauvallon: Riviera Grace Above Saint-Tropez Bay
property_intro: Set within twenty hectares of pine and olive groves above the Bay of Saint-Tropez, COMO Le Beauvallon occupies a restored Belle Epoque estate where Riviera history meets considered calm. Rooms open to sea light and terraces, while private beach club days, Mediterranean gardens and COMO Shambhala treatments shape the rhythm of a stay. Kitchens draw on Provençal growers, and the grounds are tended with local biodiversity in mind, so mornings arrive with birdsong rather than bustle.

property_title: Hôtel Villa Colette: Garden Serenity Moments from Cannes Bay
property_intro: Tucked into a leafy residential pocket a short stroll from the Croisette, Hôtel Villa Colette offers a gentler side of Cannes. Mediterranean gardens shelter a heated pool, while interiors blend Provençal craftsmanship with contemporary calm and locally sourced materials. Days unfold slowly here: breakfast beneath the pines, a spa treatment, then aperitifs as cicadas begin. The family owners champion regional producers and low-impact practices, so every detail feels considered, personal and quietly rooted in the Riviera it calls home.

property_title: Amanvari: Desert Serenity on Mexico's Sea of Cortez Shore
property_intro: Where the Sierra de la Laguna meets the Sea of Cortez, Amanvari settles quietly into Baja California Sur's Costa Palmas, a stretch of shoreline still shaped by fishing traditions and desert stillness. Pale stone villas open to gardens of native cardón and citrus, while days drift between swimmable waters, marine explorations and long, unhurried lunches. The resort supports mangrove restoration and local artisans, so time spent here gently sustains the coastline and communities that make it remarkable.

property_title: COMO The Treasury: Heritage Grandeur in Perth's Historic Heart
property_intro: Set within Perth's meticulously restored 19th-century State Buildings, COMO The Treasury pairs soaring heritage architecture with a calm, contemporary hand. Just 48 rooms open onto Cathedral Square, with the Swan River, Kings Park and Western Australia's wine country within easy reach. Days might begin with COMO Shambhala therapies, drift into long lunches led by local growers and fishers, and end on a rooftop above the city. Indigenous art and craftsmanship thread quietly throughout.

property_title: Cap Juluca, A Belmond Hotel: Where Anguilla's Sea Meets Calm
property_intro: Set along a mile of powder-soft sand on Anguilla's Maundays Bay, Cap Juluca unfolds in whitewashed, Moorish-inspired villas framed by turquoise water and turtle-grass shallows. Days drift between reef snorkelling, sailing on a traditional Anguillian boat and long lunches of just-landed crayfish. The resort nurtures its coastline through marine and turtle protection work, while local artisans, chefs and musicians shape the experience, making each stay feel genuinely rooted in this quietly confident Caribbean island.

property_title: Ellerton Bungalow: Highland Calm Amid Sri Lanka's Tea Country
property_intro: Set among the emerald folds of Sri Lanka's hill country, Ellerton Bungalow is a restored planter's residence where wood fires crackle against cool mountain evenings. Wide verandas look over working tea gardens, and days unfold with guided plucking walks, cycling through village lanes and unhurried afternoons in the garden. Interiors marry colonial bones with local craftsmanship, while the estate supports the surrounding community and the forest corridors that shelter its birdlife.

property_title: COMO The Halkin: Belgravia's Quietly Refined London Retreat
property_intro: Tucked into a leafy Belgravia street, moments from Hyde Park and the boutiques of Knightsbridge, COMO The Halkin feels more like a private townhouse than a hotel. Just 41 rooms unfold in calm Italian tailoring and Asian-inspired detail, while Michelin-starred Ametsa brings Basque artistry to the table. Wellness runs deep here, from COMO Shambhala nutrition to bespoke treatments, and staff who remember your preferences before you mention them. Central London, softened to a whisper.

property_title: COMO Metropolitan London: Mayfair Calm on Hyde Park's Doorstep
property_intro: Set on Old Park Lane, moments from Hyde Park's green expanse and Mayfair's galleries, COMO Metropolitan London brings a quiet clarity to the city. Interiors are pared-back and light-filled, while the Nobu restaurant and COMO Shambhala treatments invite you to slow down. Wellness menus draw on seasonal British produce, and the hotel's long-standing support of the COMO Foundation extends its care far beyond the front door. A thoughtful retreat within London's happy chaos.

property_title: COMO Le Montrachet: A Refined Retreat in Burgundy's Vineyards
property_intro: Set on the village square of Puligny-Montrachet, in the heart of the Côte de Beaune, COMO Le Montrachet places you among some of the world's most storied white-wine vineyards. Stone walls and soft, contemporary interiors frame a stay built around the seasons: cycling between grand cru parcels, tastings in candlelit cellars, and menus shaped by neighbouring growers and market gardeners. Days end quietly in the courtyard garden, glass in hand, as Burgundy settles into dusk.

property_title: COMO Cordeillan-Bages: Vineyard Sanctuary in Bordeaux's Médoc
property_intro: Set among the gravel soils of Pauillac, this 17th-century chartreuse sits encircled by the celebrated vines of the Médoc, moments from the Gironde estuary. Rooms are quietly contemporary, framing rows of Cabernet Sauvignon that stretch to the horizon. Days unfold with cellar visits to neighbouring châteaux, cycling through Bages village, harvest-time tastings and menus shaped by Aquitaine's growers and fishermen. It is a place for lingering conversation, considered wine and the unhurried rhythm of the vineyard year.

property_title: COMO Castello Del Nero: A Renaissance Estate in Chianti Hills
property_intro: Set among the vineyards and olive groves of Chianti, COMO Castello Del Nero occupies a 12th-century estate where frescoed ceilings and stone archways meet a quiet, contemporary calm. Days unfold slowly: cookery lessons with the kitchen garden's harvest, cycling between hilltop villages, treatments at COMO Shambhala. The estate's own wines and oils speak of long-standing craft, while careful restoration has preserved centuries of Tuscan detail. Evenings arrive with cypress silhouettes, birdsong and dinner beneath the loggia.

property_title: COMO Alpina Dolomites: Where the Dolomites Meet Quiet Luxury
property_intro: Perched at 1,800 metres on the Alpe di Siusi, Europe's largest high-altitude meadow, COMO Alpina Dolomites sits within a UNESCO-protected landscape of limestone spires and wildflower pasture. Larch, glass and local stone frame views that shift with the light. Days unfold with guided hikes, ski-touring and COMO Shambhala treatments, followed by South Tyrolean cooking rooted in nearby farms. Cars are left behind, silence is honoured, and the mountains set the pace entirely.

property_title: COMO Metropolitan Singapore: Considered Calm off Orchard Road
property_intro: Tucked between the shophouses of Bideford Road and the buzz of Orchard, COMO Metropolitan Singapore offers a quieter register of city living. Interiors by Paola Navone pair pale timber with tropical light, while COMO Shambhala therapies and nourishing cuisine restore after long days. Rooftop swims look out over the skyline; Michelin-recognised Cantonese dining sits downstairs. Staff share their favourite hawker haunts and heritage lanes, and sustainability runs quietly through everything, from sourcing to the wellness kitchen.

property_title: COMO Point Yamu: Cape Serenity Above Thailand's Phang Nga Bay
property_intro: Perched on the tip of Cape Yamu, this Phuket retreat looks east across the limestone islands of Phang Nga Bay rather than the busier west coast. Paola Navone's playful interiors draw on Sino-Portuguese heritage, while COMO Shambhala therapies and Nahm's Thai cooking restore in their own quiet way. Days unfold with yoga, boat trips to hidden lagoons and time spent with the resort's coral and mangrove conservation partners nearby. Sea breezes included.

property_title: COMO Metropolitan Bangkok: Urban Calm in Thailand's Capital
property_intro: Tucked behind a leafy courtyard on South Sathorn Road, COMO Metropolitan Bangkok offers a quieter rhythm within the city's diplomatic quarter. Interiors are pared back and light-filled, while the celebrated Nahm restaurant reinterprets historic Thai recipes with remarkable precision. Days might begin with yoga on the terrace, unfold at COMO Shambhala's treatment rooms, then drift towards riverside temples nearby. Sustainability shapes the kitchens and spa alike, with locally sourced produce and thoughtfully chosen wellness ingredients throughout.

property_title: COMO Maalifushi: Wellness and Wild Waters of the Thaa Atoll
property_intro: The only resort in the Maldives' remote Thaa Atoll, COMO Maalifushi sits amid reefs that few travellers ever see. Pale timber interiors and open pavilions frame the lagoon, while COMO Shambhala therapists, free-diving guides and surf breaks just offshore shape unhurried days. Dine on nutrient-rich cuisine, join marine biologists monitoring coral regeneration, or sail to sandbanks with local captains. It is a place to slow down, swim deeply and feel genuinely far away.

property_title: COMO Uma Canggu: Surf, Sea and Slow Living on Bali's Wild Coast
property_intro: Set above the dark volcanic sands of Echo Beach, COMO Uma Canggu looks straight out to Bali's most celebrated surf breaks, with rice fields and village lanes just behind. Rooms and loft-style suites are pared back and light-filled, while COMO Shambhala therapists, dawn yoga and nourishing cuisine restore balance after a day in the water. Surf coaching, temple visits and local artisan encounters draw you gently into Canggu's creative, ever-shifting rhythm.

property_title: COMO Uma Ubud: Balinese Serenity Above the Tjampuhan Valley
property_intro: Perched above the Tjampuhan Valley, COMO Uma Ubud looks out across terraced rice fields and forested ridgelines, moments from Ubud's temples, artisan workshops and markets. Rooms and private pool villas draw on Balinese craftsmanship, while COMO Shambhala therapies, riverside yoga and nourishing cuisine restore quietly and thoroughly. Days might unfold with a sunrise walk through neighbouring villages, a lesson in offerings-making, or cycling past farmers tending their fields, guided by locals who know every path.

property_title: COMO Uma Paro: Himalayan Serenity in Bhutan's Sacred Valley
property_intro: Set among blue pine forests above the Paro Valley, COMO Uma Paro looks out towards monasteries, prayer flags and the peaks beyond. Traditional Bhutanese craftsmanship meets calm, contemporary interiors, while the kitchen draws on Himalayan ingredients and Ayurvedic principles. Days might begin with a guided trek to Tiger's Nest, a hot stone bath, or archery alongside local villagers. Guides born in these valleys share their heritage, and community partnerships ensure your visit leaves something lasting behind.

property_title: COMO Uma Punakha: Riverside Stillness in Bhutan's Hidden Valley
property_intro: Set above the Mo Chhu river in western Bhutan, COMO Uma Punakha is an intimate retreat of just eleven rooms and villas, framed by terraced rice fields and forested ridges. Days unfold with river rafting, farmhouse visits and walks to the revered Khamsum Yulley Namgyal Chorten, before Bhutanese-inspired interiors and restorative COMO Shambhala treatments welcome you back. Meals draw on local produce, while close ties with valley communities lend every stay genuine warmth and meaning.

property_title: Mara Plains Camp: Where Kenya's Wildest Plains Truly Come Alive
property_intro: Set on the banks of the Ntiakitiak River in the Olare Motorogi Conservancy, Mara Plains Camp places you at the heart of the greater Maasai Mara, where lion prides and migrating herds move freely across open grassland. Seven raised tents blend brass, leather and vintage safari finds with quiet comfort. Game drives run with expert Maasai guides, while conservancy leases and local employment ensure your stay supports both wildlife corridors and the communities who steward them.

property_title: Mara Nyika Camp: Riverside Seclusion in Kenya's Naboisho
property_intro: Tucked beneath a canopy of ancient trees on the banks of a seasonal stream, Mara Nyika Camp sits within the Naboisho Conservancy, a Maasai-owned wilderness bordering the Maasai Mara. Five tented suites blend campaign-style furniture with contemporary comfort, each with its own plunge pool and views over the plains. Days unfold with guided walks, night drives and time alongside Maasai guides whose families lease this land, ensuring your stay directly supports both wildlife and community.

property_title: ol Donyo Lodge: Kilimanjaro Views Across the Wild Chyulu Hills
property_intro: Set on the lava-strewn slopes of Kenya's Chyulu Hills, ol Donyo Lodge looks out across Maasai-owned wilderness towards the snows of Kilimanjaro. Seven suites blend swahili craftsmanship with rooftop star beds, private plunge pools and cool, uncluttered interiors. Days unfold on horseback, by mountain bike, on foot with Maasai guides, or in a photographic hide at eye level with elephants. Your stay directly supports the Mbirikani community and one of East Africa's most ambitious predator conservation programmes.

property_title: Mara Toto Tree Camp: Wild Treetop Living in Kenya's Maasai Mara
property_intro: Tucked into a riverine grove along the Ntiakitiak in Kenya's Mara North Conservancy, Mara Toto Tree Camp holds just a handful of raised tented rooms, reached by walkways through the canopy. Days unfold with unhurried game drives, walks alongside Maasai guides and long lunches shaded by ancient trees.
