Interiors marry campaign-style antiques with soft linens and lantern light, while conservancy leases and local employment keep this corner of wilderness, and its communities, thriving.

property_title: Selinda Camp: Wild Waterways and Quiet Luxury in Botswana
property_intro: Set along the Selinda Spillway in the private northern reaches of Botswana, Selinda Camp welcomes just eight guests to a stretch of wilderness where elephants wander the treeline and lions call across the floodplain. Days unfold at your own pace: walking safaris, boating when the waters rise, and slow evenings beneath the fig trees. Interiors blend collected antiques with soft canvas and copper, while the surrounding reserve remains protected through pioneering community partnerships and anti-poaching work.

property_title: Zarafa Camp: Wild Luxury on Botswana's Selinda Reserve
property_intro: Tucked beneath ebony and jackalberry trees on the edge of the Zibadianja Lagoon, Zarafa Camp opens onto one of Botswana's most game-rich private reserves. Just four vast tented pavilions, dressed in reclaimed timber and campaign-era antiques, come with copper baths, private plunge pools and a Canon camera kit for each guest. Days unfold by boat, vehicle or on foot across the Selinda Reserve, where solar power and long-standing conservation work quietly shape every stay.

property_title: Sitatunga Private Island: A Secluded Okavango Delta Sanctuary
property_intro: Tucked into a quiet channel of Botswana's Okavango Delta, Sitatunga Private Island is reached by boat and shared with hippo, kingfishers and the shy antelope it's named for. Just a handful of tented suites sit beneath riverine trees, furnished with natural textures and lit by soft lantern glow. Days drift between mokoro paddles, walking safaris and fireside suppers, while the camp's low-impact build and local guiding partnerships keep this wilderness thriving for generations.

property_title: Tembo Plains Camp: Elephants, Escarpments and the Wild Zambezi
property_intro: Set within Zimbabwe's remote Sapi Reserve, Tembo Plains Camp looks out across the Zambezi River towards the blue folds of the escarpment beyond. Five glass-fronted suites, shaped from stone, timber and canvas, sit lightly in ancient mopane and baobab country. Days unfold on walking safaris, boat cruises and unhurried game drives among elephant herds. Your stay directly funds the reserve's anti-poaching teams and neighbouring communities, restoring one of Africa's great wildernesses.

property_title: Singita Kilima: Serengeti Grasslands, Quietly and Beautifully Lived
property_intro: Set on a gentle rise above the Serengeti's Grumeti plains, Singita Kilima looks out across grasslands crossed by wildebeest, elephant and lion. Interiors blend earthy textures with East African craftsmanship, opening onto verandas made for slow mornings and unhurried conversation. Days unfold through guided drives, walking safaris and time with the conservation teams who protect this vast wilderness. Every stay supports anti-poaching work, community education and the long-term recovery of the Grumeti reserves.

property_title: Boulders Lodge: Granite, Riverine Forest and Big-Cat Country
property_intro: Set along the Sand River in the Sabi Sand Game Reserve, Boulders Lodge is built around the granite domes that give it its name, with glass-fronted suites opening to elephants drinking below. Interiors blend timber, stone and hand-crafted African artistry. Days unfold with expert-led game drives across leopard-rich terrain, wine tastings and walks with trackers. Singita's conservation work protects vast wilderness while nurturing neighbouring communities through training, enterprise and education: luxury with genuine purpose.

property_title: Singita Castleton: A Private Bushveld Homestead in Sabi Sand
property_intro: Tucked into the Sabi Sand Reserve, Singita Castleton is a wholly private homestead reserved for one group at a time. Six rooms open onto lawns and low hills where elephant and leopard roam freely, while interiors blend farmhouse warmth with collected antiques and quiet craftsmanship. Days unfold at your own pace: unhurried game drives, wine tastings, treatments in the spa, or bread-making with the chef. Every stay supports Singita's long-term conservation work and neighbouring community enterprises.

property_title: Lebombo Lodge: Kruger's Riverbank Sanctuary of Light and Wild
property_intro: Perched above the N'wanetsi River in Kruger's Singita Lebombo concession, this glass-and-steel retreat feels suspended between granite hills and open savannah. Suites float among the treetops, their airy interiors framing elephant crossings and lion calls at dusk. Days unfold with expert-led game drives, walking safaris and quiet hours by the cliffside pool. Behind it all lies decades of conservation work and partnerships that place local communities at the heart of the wilderness they protect.

property_title: Sweni Lodge: Quiet Riverbank Luxury in the Kruger Wilderness
property_intro: Tucked along the reed-lined banks of the Sweni River in a private concession within Kruger National Park, Sweni Lodge holds just a handful of glass-fronted suites, each one opening onto grasslands where lion, elephant and buffalo pass unhurried. Interiors layer woven textures and warm timber with hand-crafted detail, while guided drives and walks reveal the region's geology and birdlife. Your stay supports anti-poaching teams and neighbouring communities, making the wild here genuinely enduring.

property_title: Sasakwa Lodge: Grand Serengeti Living on A Private Hilltop
property_intro: Perched high on a grassy hill within the private Grumeti reserves, Sasakwa Lodge surveys the western Serengeti's endless plains, where wildebeest columns move with the seasons. Edwardian-inspired cottages hold antique furnishings, deep verandas and private pools, while riding stables, tennis and a spa temper the day's game drives. Every stay supports the Grumeti Fund's anti-poaching teams, wildlife research and neighbouring village schools, making this rather more than a beautiful place to wake up in Tanzania.

property_title: Faru Faru Lodge: Wild Serengeti Luxury on the Grumeti River
property_intro: Set on a gentle rise above the Grumeti River in Tanzania's Singita Grumeti reserve, Faru Faru Lodge looks out across plains crossed by the annual migration. Nine light-filled suites blend stone, canvas and timber, opening to views where elephants gather at the waterhole below. Days unfold with guided walks, river-bend game drives and unhurried afternoons by the pool. Your stay directly supports anti-poaching teams and neighbouring communities restoring this once-depleted wilderness.

property_title: Singita Milele: A Private Serengeti Sanctuary Made for Forever
property_intro: High on a ridge in Tanzania's Grumeti Reserve, Singita Milele looks out over grasslands where wildebeest, elephant and lion move with the seasons. Taken exclusively, this five-suite house feels like a friend's home: sunlit rooms, a chef who cooks to your mood, a guide who knows every thicket. Days unfold at your pace, whether tracking on foot or drifting in the pool. Your stay directly funds the reserve's anti-poaching work and neighbouring community programmes.

property_title: Kataza House: A Warm, Woman-Led Retreat in Kigali's Nyamirambo
property_intro: Tucked into Nyamirambo, Kigali's most characterful quarter, Kataza House offers a graceful counterpoint to the city's hum. Rooms are dressed in handwoven textiles and locally crafted furniture, opening onto a garden terrace where hillside views unfold at dusk. Run in partnership with the Nyamirambo Women's Centre, every stay supports training and fair wages for local women. Join a neighbourhood walk, a cookery lesson, or simply linger over Rwandan coffee.

property_title: Serengeti House: Your Private Retreat in Tanzania's Wild Heart
property_intro: Set on a kopje in the Grumeti Reserves, Serengeti House looks out across plains where wildebeest thunder past and lions doze in the shade. This exclusive-use villa sleeps eight, with a swimming pool, tennis court and private guiding team at your disposal. Interiors blend contemporary African craft with deep comfort, while your stay directly supports the Grumeti Fund's anti-poaching work and neighbouring communities. Days unfold at your pace: dawn drives, riverside lunches, evenings beneath extraordinary stars.

property_title: Singita Explore: Private Tented Camping in Tanzania's Serengeti
property_intro: Set within the Grumeti reserves on the western edge of the Serengeti, Singita Explore is a mobile tented camp reserved exclusively for your party. Six canvas suites are pitched in quiet wilderness, styled with campaign furniture, brass fittings and lantern light ef{eq:1} understated rather than showy. Days unfold with walking safaris, night drives and fireside dinners under an uninterrupted sky, while your stay supports the Grumeti Fund's anti-poaching work and community education across more than 350,000 acres.

property_title: Mara River Tented Camp: Where Tanzania's Wild Heart Flows
property_intro: Set on the northern reaches of the Serengeti, close to the Mara River's storied crossings, this intimate camp places you within one of Africa's great wildlife theatres. Canvas suites are furnished with quiet restraint, opening to grassland horizons and the sounds of the plains after dark. Days unfold with guided drives, walking safaris and unhurried breakfasts beneath acacias. The camp works closely with neighbouring Maasai communities and local conservation partners, ensuring your stay leaves the wilderness richer.

property_title: Necker Island: Barefoot Luxury in the British Virgin Islands
property_intro: Encircled by coral reef in the British Virgin Islands, Necker Island is Sir Richard Branson's private retreat, where Balinese-inspired pavilions open to trade winds and the Caribbean stretches in every direction. Days unfold with tennis at dawn, kitesurfing across the flats, or quiet hours beside flamingo-dotted lagoons. Conservation runs deep here: endangered scarlet ibis, giant tortoises and lemurs share the island, while solar and wind power much of it. Yours to share with family, friends or fellow travellers.

property_title: Kokomo Private Island Resort: Barefoot Luxury in Fiji's Reefs
property_intro: Set within Fiji's Kadavu archipelago, Kokomo Private Island Resort rises from a coral atoll edged by the Great Astrolabe Reef. Thatched villas and hilltop residences draw on Fijian craftsmanship, while gardens and reef supply the kitchens. Days unfold with manta ray snorkelling, sport fishing or unhurried spa hours above the lagoon. The resort's marine biologists nurture coral nurseries and turtle hatchlings, and neighbouring island villages share in its work, giving every stay quiet purpose.

property_title: The Mudhouse Marayoor: Earthen Living Amid Kerala's Highlands
property_intro: Tucked between sugarcane fields and the sandalwood forests of Marayoor, in Kerala's Anamalai highlands, The Mudhouse is a study in gentle simplicity. Cottages of mud, stone and thatch open to birdsong, river walks and the distant call of elephants in the Chinnar reserve. Days unfold slowly here: foraged breakfasts, treks with local guides, conversations by firelight. Built with village hands and regional materials, it offers a quiet, deeply considered kind of luxury rooted in place.

property_title: Shel Ladakh: Himalayan Serenity Among Orchards and Peaks
property_intro: Tucked into the Indus Valley near Leh, Shel Ladakh unfolds across apricot orchards and barley fields, framed by the bare, luminous ridges of the Himalaya. Rooms built from local stone and timber echo Ladakhi craft traditions, while wide windows draw in mountain light. Days might bring monastery visits, walks through village lanes, or slow afternoons with butter tea. Solar heating, local sourcing and partnerships with Ladakhi artisans keep the mountains, and their communities, thriving.

property_title: Monticle Glamps: Refined Hillside Living Beneath Indian Skies
property_intro: Set among gentle hills where morning mist lingers over terraced slopes, Monticle Glamps offers a considered take on life under canvas. Each tented suite is styled with natural textures and local craftsmanship, opening onto uninterrupted valley views. Days unfold with guided forest walks, conversations with nearby farming families and slow meals built around regional produce. Solar power, rainwater harvesting and village partnerships underpin it all, making comfort here feel quietly purposeful rather than performative.

property_title: The Tamara: Coorg's Coffee Estate Sanctuary in the Western Ghats
property_intro: Tucked into a working coffee and spice plantation in Karnataka's Coorg hills, The Tamara sits within one of the Western Ghats' most biodiverse pockets. Timber-clad cottages rise on stilts among the canopy, linked by elevated walkways where birdsong replaces traffic. Guests wander plantation trails with resident naturalists, trace the journey from bean to cup, and follow forest paths to the Mallalli Falls. Local employment, rainwater harvesting and estate-grown produce underpin a stay that feels genuinely rooted in its landscape.

property_title: Tachibanaya: Riverside Ryokan Serenity in Timeless Japan
property_intro: Tucked beside a quiet river where mountain mist gathers at dawn, Tachibanaya carries the unhurried rhythm of a traditional ryokan into the present. Tatami-floored rooms open onto cedar and maple, private onsen baths draw on mineral-rich springs, and kaiseki dinners honour the season's harvest from nearby farms and waters. Generations of local craftspeople have shaped its timber, ceramics and textiles. Slip into a yukata, listen to the water, and let time loosen its grip.

property_title: Denis Private Island: Barefoot Seclusion on a Coral Frontier
property_intro: Adrift on the edge of the Seychelles plateau, Denis Private Island is a coral cay ringed by white sand and steep blue drop-offs prized by fishermen and divers alike. Twenty-five timber cottages sit beneath takamaka trees, moments from the shore. The island's farm supplies much of the kitchen, while conservationists nurture nesting turtles and rare endemic birds returned to the island. Days unfold slowly here: cycling sandy paths, snorkelling reefs, dining wherever the mood takes you.

property_title: Mwiba Plains: Wild Seclusion on the Southern Serengeti Plains
property_intro: On the southern edge of the Serengeti ecosystem, Mwiba Plains sits within a private wildlife reserve of granite kopjes, acacia woodland and grasslands crossed by the great migration. Just a handful of light-footed tents look out over open country, furnished with quiet restraint and warm textures. Days unfold with guided walks, night drives and time alongside Hadzabe communities, while your stay directly supports anti-poaching patrols, local employment and the protection of this remarkable corner of Tanzania.

property_title: Mila Tented Camp: Wild Serenity in Tanzania's Untamed Heart
property_intro: Set within Tanzania's golden grasslands, Mila Tented Camp offers a rare intimacy with the wild. Just a handful of canvas suites rest beneath acacia shade, furnished with handwoven textiles and locally crafted timber that echo the landscape beyond. Days unfold with guided game drives, walking safaris led by Maasai trackers and unhurried afternoons watching herds drift past. The camp employs and trains from neighbouring villages, channelling revenue into wildlife corridors and schools, so your stay quietly sustains what surrounds it.

property_title: Nyasi Tented Camp: Canvas Comfort Beneath Wide Tanzanian Skies
property_intro: Tucked into golden grasslands where elephants drift past at dawn, Nyasi Tented Camp offers a gentler way to meet the Tanzanian bush. Canvas suites are dressed in natural linens and locally crafted timber, opening onto views that shift with the light. Days unfold through guided walks, unhurried game drives and conversations with the guides who grew up here. A share of every stay supports neighbouring communities and the wildlife corridors they protect.

property_title: Songa Migrational Camp: Following Tanzania's Wild Rhythms
property_intro: Moving with the seasons across Tanzania's northern wilderness, Songa Migrational Camp settles where the game gathers, from the Serengeti's shifting plains to quieter corners few guests ever see. Canvas suites are furnished with restraint and craft, lit by lantern and warmed by conversation around the fire. Days unfold with guided walks, tracking on foot alongside Maasai naturalists and unhurried drives. Low-impact by design, the camp leaves little behind but supports the communities and wildlife corridors that make such journeys possible.

property_title: Legendary Lodge: Coffee Plantation Calm in Mount Meru's Shadow
property_intro: Set within a working coffee plantation on the edge of Arusha, Legendary Lodge gathers a handful of private cottages beneath jacaranda and flame trees, with Mount Meru rising beyond the fields. Verandas open onto lawns and birdsong; interiors marry colonial-era character with easy comfort. Wander the coffee rows with a grower, dine beneath the stars, then set off for the Serengeti or Ngorongoro. Local employment and estate stewardship keep this quiet corner thriving.

property_title: Ulaman Eco Luxury Resort: Bamboo Sanctuary in Bali's Jungle
property_intro: Tucked between rice terraces and jungle in Tabanan, western Bali, Ulaman Eco Luxury Resort is a study in what architecture can achieve when it works with nature rather than against it. Bamboo domes, earth-formed walls and villas suspended above a river-fed valley set the scene for treatments at the cave-like spa, plant-led dining and quiet mornings of yoga. Local craftspeople shaped every curve, and the surrounding village community remains part of the story.

property_title: Hideout Bali: Handcrafted Bamboo Retreats by a Wild Jungle River
property_intro: Tucked into the emerald folds of East Bali, beneath the shoulders of Mount Agung, Hideout Bali is a collection of handcrafted bamboo homes shaped by local artisans and set beside a rushing jungle river. Days unfold slowly here: cold-water plunges, guided walks through rice terraces, cooking with produce from neighbouring farms. Built with reclaimed timber and thatch, and run alongside the village of Selat, it is a stay that gives quietly back.

property_title: Veluvana Bali: A Bamboo Sanctuary Amid Bali's Green Highlands
property_intro: Tucked into Bali's green highlands, where rice terraces fold into river valleys, Veluvana is a cluster of handcrafted bamboo villas built by local artisans using sustainably grown timber. Days unfold slowly here: sunrise yoga above the canopy, spring-fed pools, dinners drawn from village farms. Guests are welcomed into community life rather than screened from it, with reforestation and craft initiatives quietly supported by every stay. A retreat for those who travel thoughtfully.

property_title: Unique Garden Hotel & Spa: Atlantic Forest Wellness Sanctuary
property_intro: An hour from São Paulo, Unique Garden Hotel & Spa unfolds across a private reserve of Atlantic Forest in the hills of Mairiporã. Modernist pavilions by Brazilian masters sit lightly among ancient trees, streams and orchid gardens, while the spa draws on plants grown metres from the treatment rooms. Days pass with forest walks, seasonal tasting menus and long silences. Reforestation projects and local partnerships keep this quiet corner of Mata Atlântica thriving.

property_title: A&K Gorilla Forest Lodge: Where Bwindi's Wild Heart Beats
property_intro: Set within the mist-laced folds of Bwindi Impenetrable Forest, A&K Gorilla Forest Lodge sits close enough to hear gorillas moving through the undergrowth at dawn. Eight airy suites blend local stone, timber and handwoven textiles, opening onto canopy views and a garden where sunbirds gather. Days begin with guided treks to habituated families and end beside the fire, swapping stories. Trekking permits and lodge partnerships directly support Batwa communities and forest conservation.

property_title: Ol Lentille: A Private Hilltop Sanctuary in Wild Laikipia, Kenya
property_intro: High on a ridge in Kenya's Laikipia, Ol Lentille looks out over Maasai and Samburu rangelands where elephants drift through acacia scrub below. Four individually designed houses come with their own guide, chef and private vehicle, so days unfold entirely on your terms: walking safaris, camel treks, riverside picnics or afternoons beside your own pool. Owned in partnership with the local community, it channels revenue into schools, clinics and conservancy protection across these remarkable hills.

property_title: Sindabezi Island Camp: Barefoot Luxury on the Zambezi
property_intro: Set on a private island in the Zambezi, a short drift downstream from Victoria Falls, Sindabezi holds just six open-sided chalets lit by lantern and cooled by the river breeze. Elephants wade the channels at dusk; dinner arrives beneath a canopy of stars. Solar-powered and entirely off-grid, the camp funds local schools and conservation work in the neighbouring national park, making every night here quietly consequential as well as deeply restorative.

property_title: Tongabezi Lodge: Riverside Romance Above the Zambezi's Edge
property_intro: Perched on the banks of the Zambezi just upstream of Victoria Falls, Tongabezi is a place of open-sided houses, ebony trees and long, unhurried afternoons. Each cottage and treehouse is handcrafted and distinct, framing river views from stone baths and private decks. Drift by dugout canoe, breakfast on Sindabezi Island, or dine on a sandbank by candlelight. The lodge's Tujatane School educates hundreds of local children, making every stay quietly consequential.

property_title: Ila Safari Lodge: Riverside Wilderness in Zambia's Lower Zambezi
property_intro: Set on the banks of the Zambezi in Zambia's Lower Zambezi National Park, Ila Safari Lodge blends solar-powered comfort with genuine wilderness. Canvas suites open to the river, where elephants wade at dusk and hippos announce the evening. Explore by electric game vehicle, boat or canoe, then return to a plunge pool shaded by riverine forest. Behind it all, anti-poaching patrols and local employment ensure your stay supports the landscape that surrounds you.

property_title: Chisa Busanga Camp: Nest Above Zambia's Busanga Plains
property_intro: Perched on stilts above the seasonal floodplains of Kafue National Park, Chisa Busanga's four woven nests echo the architecture of weaver birds, cradling guests amid one of Zambia's least-visited wildernesses. Days unfold with lion prides on the Busanga Plains, red lechwe scattering through shallow water and hot-air balloon flights at first light. Handwoven interiors, solar power and close partnership with local communities and park conservation efforts make this a stay of genuine consequence.

property_title: Shawa Luangwa Camp: Where Zambia's Luangwa Valley Comes Alive
property_intro: Set on a quiet bend of the Luangwa River in Zambia's celebrated South Luangwa, Shawa Luangwa Camp pairs raised timber suites with sweeping views of ebony groves and passing elephant. Days unfold at your own pace: walking safaris with expert Zambian guides, night drives in search of leopard, and long lunches above the water. Locally crafted interiors, solar power and close partnerships with neighbouring communities give the camp its quietly purposeful character.

property_title: Sausage Tree Camp: Riverside Wilderness in Zambia's Lower Zambezi
property_intro: On a quiet bend of the Zambezi, deep within Zambia's Lower Zambezi National Park, Sausage Tree Camp opens onto water, woodland and wide skies. Billowing white tented suites sit beneath ancient trees, each with a private plunge pool and views across the river to the Zimbabwean escarpment. Days unfold through canoeing past pods of hippo, catch-and-release tiger fishing, walking safaris and long lunches on sandbanks. The camp's earnings help fund anti-poaching patrols and local schooling.

property_title: Potato Bush Camp: Barefoot Riverside Luxury on the Lower Zambezi
property_intro: Tucked beneath ancient winterthorns on the banks of the Lower Zambezi, Potato Bush Camp holds just four riverfront suites ed of the world. Days unfold slowly here: canoeing past pods of hippo, tiger fishing in the current, walking with guides who know every track. Interiors blend natural timber, canvas and soft light, while long-standing anti-poaching and community schooling partnerships ensure your stay leaves the valley richer than you found it.

property_title: Kaya Mawa: Handcrafted Island Living on Lake Malawi's Shores
property_intro: On the granite-strewn edge of Likoma Island, Kaya Mawa sits where Lake Malawi's clear water meets baobabs and fishing villages. Ten stone-and-thatch rooms, built by local craftsmen, open straight onto private coves. Days drift between snorkelling among cichlids, sailing dhows at dusk and wandering to the island's improbable cathedral. Much of what you spend supports the neighbouring community's schools, clinic and enterprises, making this rare corner of Malawi quietly rewarding to visit.

property_title: Cayo Espanto Private Island: Barefoot Seclusion in Belize
property_intro: Three miles off the coast of San Pedro, Cayo Espanto occupies its own island, where seven villas open directly onto the Caribbean and the world's second-largest barrier reef lies moments offshore. Each villa comes with a private plunge pool, a dedicated houseman and meals served wherever you please. Days pass snorkelling with rays, fly-fishing the flats or drifting in a hammock. The island works closely with Belizean communities and reef conservation partners, keeping this quiet corner flourishing.

property_title: Greystoke Mahale: Chimpanzee Days on Lake Tanganyika's Shore
property_intro: Reached by dhow across the vast blue of Lake Tanganyika, Greystoke Mahale rests where forested peaks tumble to a beach of pale sand. Six driftwood-and-thatch bandas open to the water, their upper decks made for slow mornings and long swims. Days begin with tracking the chimpanzees of Mahale Mountains, whose lives have been studied here for decades, and end beside a fire with the lake glinting. Remote, gently luxurious, and quietly committed to protecting this extraordinary forest.

property_title: Chada Safari Camp: Wild Solitude in Tanzania's Katavi Plains
property_intro: Deep in Katavi National Park, where floodplains shimmer and tamarind trees shade the Chada plain, this intimate camp welcomes only a handful of guests at a time. Canvas tents are furnished with quiet craftsmanship, lantern-lit and open to the sounds of hippo and lion. Days unfold on foot, by vehicle or beside the river, guided by trackers who know every hoofprint. Your stay directly supports anti-poaching patrols and the communities bordering this remarkable wilderness.

property_title: Kigelia Camp Ruaha: Wild Seclusion Beneath Ancient Sausage Trees
property_intro: Tucked into a grove of kigelia trees along the Ifuguru sand river, this intimate camp sits at the heart of Ruaha, Tanzania's vast and little-visited wilderness. Six canvas tents, simply and beautifully dressed, open onto elephant paths and baobab country. Days unfold on foot or by vehicle with guides who read the bush fluently. Seasonal by design, the camp treads lightly, leaving the landscape and its lion prides undisturbed.

property_title: Kiba Point: Riverside Seclusion in Tanzania's Wild Selous
property_intro: Set on a private stretch of the Rufiji River in the vast Nyerere wilderness, Kiba Point welcomes just one party at a time. Four airy bandas, shaded by borassus palms and dressed in local textiles and driftwood, open directly onto the water. Days unfold at your own pace: boating past pods of hippo, walking with expert guides, fishing for tigerfish, or simply watching elephants drink below. Your stay supports anti-poaching patrols and the communities bordering this remarkable reserve.

property_title: Sand Rivers Safari Camp: Riverbank Seclusion in Nyerere Park
property_intro: Set above a bend of the Rufiji River in Tanzania's Nyerere National Park, Sand Rivers occupies one of Africa's least-travelled wildernesses. Eight open-fronted stone-and-thatch suites face the water, where hippos grumble and elephants cross at dusk. Mornings begin with coffee at the river's edge. Days unfold by boat, on foot with expert guides, or fly-camping beneath the stars. Long-standing partnerships with neighbouring communities and anti-poaching teams help safeguard this vast reserve, a place that rewards those who linger.

property_title: Kuro Safari Camp: Wild Seclusion in Tanzania's Tarangire
property_intro: Tucked beneath ancient baobabs in the quiet southern reaches of Tarangire, Kuro Safari Camp offers a rare kind of privacy. Just a handful of canvas suites open onto the riverbed, where elephant herds drift past at dusk. Days unfold with walking safaris led by Maasai guides, night drives and unhurried breakfasts in the bush. Solar-powered and lightly built, the camp supports local conservation and employment, leaving the landscape much as it found it.

property_title: Entamanu Ngorongoro: Where the Crater Rim Meets the Endless Sky
property_intro: Perched on the little-visited western rim of the Ngorongoro Crater, Entamanu looks out across the caldera on one side and the Serengeti plains on the other. Six light-footed suites, built from canvas, timber and reclaimed materials, are warmed by wood stoves as the highland mist rolls in. Days unfold with Maasai-guided walks, crater descents and picnics among wildflowers, while your stay supports Nainokanoka's community and the wider conservation of this remarkable highland landscape.

property_title: Kusini: Barefoot Seclusion on Tanzania's Untamed Shoreline
property_intro: Tucked between whispering casuarina trees and a sweep of pale sand, Kusini offers a rare kind of quiet on Tanzania's coast. Its handful of thatched villas are shaped by local craftsmanship, with coral stone, carved timber and cool linen framing views of the Indian Ocean. Days unfold gently: dhow sailing at dusk, snorkelling over reefs protected through community-led marine work, or long lunches of just-landed seafood. Staffed almost entirely by neighbouring villagers, it feels genuinely rooted.

property_title: Mkombe's House: Barefoot Luxury on Tanzania's Wild Coast
property_intro: Tucked between coastal forest and the warm Indian Ocean, Mkombe's House is an exclusive-use retreat where the beach belongs to you alone. Rooms open to sea breezes, driftwood and natural textures shape the interiors, and days unfold at your own rhythm: dhow sailing, snorkelling reefs, or simply reading in the shade. Part of the Ras Kutani conservation story, your stay supports forest protection and neighbouring village projects, making time here quietly meaningful as well as memorable.

property_title: Lamai Serengeti: Life Among the Kopjes of the Northern Serengeti
property_intro: Tucked into the granite kopjes of Kogakuria, in the Serengeti's remote northern reaches, Lamai sits within walking distance of the Mara River and the wildebeest crossings that define this landscape. Rooms are built around the rocks themselves, open to the breeze and the plains beyond. Days unfold with walking safaris, game drives and unhurried afternoons watching the horizon. Guiding is exceptional, and your stay supports conservation and community partnerships across the wider ecosystem.

property_title: Mount Gahinga Lodge: Where Uganda's Volcanoes Meet Warm Welcome
property_intro: Cradled between the Virunga volcanoes in Uganda's far south-west, Mount Gahinga Lodge sits at the edge of Mgahinga Gorilla National Park, where bamboo forest gives way to golden monkeys and mountain gorillas. Eight stone-and-thatch bandas open onto volcano views, with crackling fires and locally woven textiles within. Days begin with forest treks and end in conversation with the Batwa community, whose village partnership and craft cooperative are woven into the lodge's story.

property_title: &Beyond Benguerra Island Lodge: Barefoot Days in the Indian Ocean
property_intro: Set within Mozambique's Bazaruto Archipelago National Park, &Beyond Benguerra Island Lodge occupies a sliver of soft sand between casuarina forest and a translucent, dugong-rich sea. Thatched casinhas and cliff-top villas open to the breeze, their interiors shaped by local craftsmanship. Days pass sailing traditional dhows, snorkelling coral gardens, riding horses along empty shorelines or visiting island villages. Marine research and community partnerships underpin it all, so time here quietly supports the archipelago's fragile, extraordinary ecosystems.

property_title: Jnane Tamsna: A Garden Retreat in Marrakech's Palmeraie
property_intro: Set among nine acres of organic gardens in Marrakech's Palmeraie, Jnane Tamsna is the creation of an ethnobotanist and an anthropologist, and it shows in every considered detail. Five houses blend Moroccan craftsmanship with bold colour and family heirlooms, while kitchen gardens supply the table each evening. Days might involve cookery lessons, medina wanderings or simply the shade of an olive tree. The owners' foundation supports women's cooperatives and rural schooling across the region.

property_title: Discovery Bedu: Wadi Rum's Desert Under Boundless Skies
property_intro: Set within the sandstone amphitheatres of Wadi Rum, Discovery Bedu invites you into Jordan's protected desert with quiet confidence. Tented suites are shaped by Bedouin craft and warmed by wool, lantern light and long views across the valley floor. Days unfold with local guides who read the land like a familiar page, tracing rock inscriptions, sharing zarb cooked beneath the sand and returning at dusk for tea. Solar power, careful water use and Bedouin-led hospitality keep this landscape thriving.

property_title: Virunga Lodge: Ridgetop Retreat Among Rwanda's Volcanoes
property_intro: Perched on a ridge between the twin lakes of Burera and Ruhondo, Virunga Lodge looks out towards the Virunga volcanoes, home to Rwanda's mountain gorillas. Ten bandas blend local craftsmanship with deep verandas and open fires for cool highland evenings. Days begin early with gorilla or golden monkey trekking, then unwind with village visits, canoe paddles and hilltop sundowners. A share of every stay supports the neighbouring communities and conservation of these remarkable forests.

property_title: Kibale Lodge: Chimpanzee Country from a Hilltop Retreat
property_intro: Set on a breezy ridge above Uganda's Kibale Forest, Kibale Lodge looks across crater lakes and tea fields towards the Rwenzori peaks. Eight thatched cottages blend handcrafted furnishings with deep verandas and private plunge pools, while days begin early with chimpanzee tracking beneath the canopy. Return for volcanic-soil coffee, walks through neighbouring villages and quiet hours in the gardens. Local guides, growers and craftspeople shape the experience, ensuring the forest's future remains woven into community life.

property_title: Pacific Resort Aitutaki: Barefoot Luxury on a Storied Lagoon
property_intro: Set on Aitutaki's western shore, this adults-only retreat looks out across one of the South Pacific's most luminous lagoons, where sandbars shift with the tide and motu drift on the horizon. Just twenty-seven bungalows and villas, dressed in island timber and woven detail, sit within gardens tended by local hands. Days unfold with lagoon cruises, coral-planting outings and Cook Islands cuisine, while the resort's community partnerships and reef conservation work quietly shape every stay.

property_title: Etu Moana: Adults-Only Villa Serenity on Aitutaki's Blue Lagoon
property_intro: On Aitutaki's western shore, where the lagoon shifts through impossible shades of turquoise, Etu Moana gathers just ten thatched villas among frangipani and coconut palms. This adults-only retreat is family-run, with Cook Islands craftsmanship in every carved detail and reef-friendly practices woven quietly into daily life. Days unfold with kayaks, snorkels and lagoon cruises to uninhabited motu, then close over island-grown produce and a sky thick with stars. Barefoot, unhurried and genuinely welcoming.

property_title: Fond Doux Eco Resort: Cocoa Estate Living Beneath the Pitons
property_intro: Set within a working cocoa plantation near Soufrière, Fond Doux unfolds across 250 acres of tropical gardens framed by the Pitons. Timber cottages, many salvaged from historic Saint Lucian homes, sit among breadfruit and heliconia, with plunge pools and hammocks for slow afternoons. Guests walk the estate with growers, follow trails to hidden beaches, and dine on produce grown steps away. Solar power, spring water and local employment keep the land and village thriving.

property_title: Cruachan Hotel: Timeless Warmth Beneath Argyll's Wildest Peaks
property_intro: Set in the heart of Argyll, where Loch Awe glimmers beneath the brooding slopes of Ben Cruachan, this family-run retreat offers a quietly refined welcome. Log fires, locally sourced menus and thoughtfully restored interiors reflect a genuine sense of place, while walking trails, glens and ancient castles wait just beyond the door. Long-standing ties with Highland producers and crofters mean every stay supports the community that makes this corner of Scotland so quietly remarkable.

property_title: Bucuti & Tara Beach Resort: Aruba's Adults-Only Eagle Beach
property_intro: Set along the powder-soft sands of Eagle Beach, Bucuti & Tara is an adults-only retreat where the pace slows to match the rhythm of the Caribbean. Rooms open to sea breezes and wide horizons, while dinner arrives by candlelight at the water's edge. As the world's first certified carbon-neutral resort, it pairs quiet luxury with genuine environmental stewardship, from reef protection to island-wide clean-ups, proving indulgence and responsibility can share the same shoreline.

property_title: Golden Rock Resort: Where Statia's Wild Beauty Unfolds Slowly
property_intro: High on Signal Hill on the little-known island of St Eustatius, Golden Rock Resort looks out to the dormant Quill volcano and a sea streaked with reef. Suites are pared back and sunlit, opening to terraces where tropicbirds drift past. Days here mean diving historic wrecks, hiking crater rainforest or wandering Oranjestad's cobbled ruins, then returning to island-sourced cooking. The resort supports local marine conservation and hires from the community, making every stay quietly consequential.

property_title: Wa Ale Island Resort: Wild Luxury in Myanmar's Mergui Sea
property_intro: Set within the Lampi Marine National Park, Wa Ale Island Resort occupies a remote isle in Myanmar's Mergui Archipelago, where jungle-clad hills meet sand shaped by nesting turtles. Timber-and-canvas tented villas and treetop retreats sit lightly on the land, powered by solar and built with reclaimed materials. Days unfold through kayaking mangrove creeks, snorkelling reefs and hiking to hidden waterfalls, while the resort's foundation funds local schools, healthcare and marine protection across the archipelago.

property_title: Japamala Resort: Rainforest Seclusion on Tioman's Wild Shore
property_intro: Tucked into the jungled hillside of Tioman Island, Japamala Resort is a cluster of timber chalets and treetop sanctuaries reached by winding forest paths. Days unfold slowly here: snorkelling above coral gardens, dining on Malay-inspired plates at the water's edge, or simply listening to hornbills at dusk. Built around the trees rather than through them, the resort supports reef restoration and works closely with island villagers, offering a rare, unhurried intimacy with the South China Sea.

property_title: Estancia Los Potreros: Horseback Days in Córdoba's Highlands
property_intro: High in the Sierras Chicas of Córdoba, Estancia Los Potreros has been in the same family for four generations, a working cattle ranch of 6,000 acres where Peruvian Paso horses carry guests across grassland ridges and river valleys. Days unfold at a gaucho's pace: riding out with local horsemen, polo on the home field, long lunches beneath the trees. Rooms are quietly characterful, filled with heirlooms, while native woodland regeneration and rural employment underpin everything here.

property_title: Alphonse Island Lodge: Where the Seychelles Turn Wild and Blue
property_intro: Some 400 kilometres south of Mahé, Alphonse Island rises from an atoll ringed by flats and coral drop-offs, reachable only by a small plane across open water. The lodge's timber suites and beach bungalows sit lightly beneath casuarina trees, shaped for shade, breeze and privacy. Days drift between fly fishing on Saint François lagoon, diving walls thick with life, and turtle surveys alongside the island's conservation team, whose research quietly guides everything here.

property_title: Cousine Island: A Private Seychelles Sanctuary for Just Ten
property_intro: Set within a granite-fringed nature reserve in the Seychelles, Cousine Island welcomes no more than ten guests at a time. Colonial-style villas open onto a beach shared with nesting hawksbill turtles, while endemic magpie robins and fodies move freely through restored native forest. Days unfold at your own pace: guided conservation walks with resident ecologists, spa treatments beneath takamaka trees, or dinner served wherever you please. Every stay funds ongoing island rewilding and species protection.

property_title: Kep Merli: Wild Cliffs and Quiet Luxury on Albania's Riviera
property_intro: Perched where pine and olive groves tumble towards the Ionian, Kep Merli occupies a stretch of the Albanian coast that few travellers have discovered. Stone-and-timber suites echo the headland's own palette, opening to sea breezes and long, unhurried views. Days drift between hidden coves, boat trips along the cliffs and dinners built around produce from neighbouring villages. Guided by a light-touch ethos, the retreat works closely with local families to protect this remarkable shoreline.

property_title: Masoala Forest Lodge: Where Madagascar's Wild Rainforest Meets the Sea
property_intro: Reached only by boat, Masoala Forest Lodge sits where dense rainforest tumbles into the Bay of Antongil, on Madagascar's remote north-eastern coast. Seven safari-style tents, hand-built from local timber and canvas, open onto a canopy alive with lemurs, chameleons and birdsong found nowhere else on earth. Days unfold with guided forest walks, kayaking and snorkelling, while humpback whales pass offshore in season. Community-run and conservation-led, your stay directly protects one of the island's last great wildernesses.

property_title: Azara Beach House: Barefoot Luxury on Goa's Quiet Coastline
property_intro: Set behind a sweep of soft sand on Goa's gentler shore, Azara Beach House invites you to slow down. Sunlight moves through pared-back interiors of lime plaster, cane and reclaimed teak, while the Arabian Sea provides the soundtrack. Days unfold with Ayurvedic treatments, coastal Goan cooking with local fishermen's catch, and dawn walks to turtle nesting grounds. Staffed and supplied by neighbouring villages, it feels less like a hotel and more like a well-loved home.

property_title: Ol Jogi Wildlife Conservancy: Laikipia's Private Wild Heart
property_intro: Set across 58,000 acres of Laikipia's plains, Ol Jogi is a private family home turned exclusive-use retreat, where black rhino graze beneath Mount Kenya's silhouette. Only one party stays at a time, with a wildlife hospital, veterinary team and anti-poaching rangers at work nearby. Days unfold on horseback, at a hidden waterhole hide, or in art-filled rooms where quirky heirlooms meet remarkable comfort. Local schools and clinics thrive through the conservancy's long-standing community programmes.

property_title: Laguna Lodge Atitl\u00e1n: Volcano Views on Guatemala's Wild Shore
property_intro: Reached only by boat, Laguna Lodge sits within a private nature reserve on the shore of Lake Atitl\u00e1n, three volcanoes rising beyond the water. Just six suites, hand-built from local stone and adobe and dressed in Mayan textiles, invite slow mornings and long, candlelit dinners of garden-grown produce. Kayak at first light, hike the reserve's cloud forest trails, or visit weaving cooperatives in nearby villages, where the lodge's conservation work quietly takes root.

property_title: Blue Zebra Island Lodge: Barefoot Luxury on Lake Malawi
property_intro: Set on Nankoma Island within Lake Malawi National Park, Blue Zebra Island Lodge is reached by boat across water so clear you can count the cichlids below. Thatched tented chalets sit among baobabs and granite boulders, each opening to its own stretch of shoreline. Days drift between snorkelling, kayaking and sundowners on the rocks, while the lodge's fish sanctuary and island community projects quietly safeguard this remarkable freshwater world for generations to come.

property_title: Anabezi Tented Camp: Elevated Luxury on the Lower Zambezi River
property_intro: Set where the Zambezi meets the Mushika floodplains, Anabezi occupies a remote corner of Zambia's Lower Zambezi National Park, shaded by ancient winterthorn trees. Twelve raised tents open to river views, each with private plunge pool and outdoor bath. Days unfold through canoe safaris, walking trails and boat cruises among elephant and carmine bee-eaters. Solar power, careful anti-poaching partnerships and local employment ensure your stay supports the wilderness that surrounds you.

property_title: Chundukwa River Lodge: Riverside Calm Above the Zambezi
property_intro: Set on the Zambezi's palm-fringed banks upstream of Victoria Falls, Chundukwa River Lodge offers a gentler rhythm than the town beyond. Six open-fronted thatched chalets stand on stilts above the water, their timber decks placed for morning birdsong and unhurried sundowners. Days unfold with canoeing between islands, riding horses through the bush, or drifting out to fish. Family-run for decades, the lodge supports its neighbouring village school and local guides with quiet, lasting commitment.

property_title: Camp Kuzuma: Quiet Luxury on Botswana's Chobe Elephant Trail
property_intro: Set on a private concession between Kasane and the Zambezi, Camp Kuzuma looks out over a waterhole where elephant herds arrive in the golden hours. Just eight thatched suites, crafted from local timber and stone, open to teak woodland and immense skies. Days unfold with guided drives, walks and river excursions into Chobe, while the camp's anti-poaching support and village partnerships ensure your stay leaves this wilderness, and its people, stronger.

property_title: Mankwe Tented Retreat: Wild Serenity on Botswana's Edge
property_intro: Tucked into a private wilderness beside the Okavango's eastern reaches, Mankwe Tented Retreat invites you to slow down among mopane woodland and open floodplain. Canvas suites are dressed in natural linens and handcrafted timber, framing views where elephants pass at dusk. Days unfold with guided game drives, walks led by local trackers and quiet hours reading in the shade. The camp works closely with neighbouring villages and funds anti-poaching patrols, so your stay leaves the landscape stronger.

property_title: Mogotlho Safari Lodge: Where Khwai's Wildlife Comes to Drink
property_intro: On the banks of the Khwai River, where the Okavango Delta gives way to the Moremi wilderness, Mogotlho Safari Lodge invites you to settle into thatched, canvas-walled suites raised above the floodplain. Days unfold with game drives, guided walks and mokoro glides led by guides raised in this landscape. The lodge works hand in hand with the Khwai community, channelling tourism into conservation, employment and the elephant corridors that pass quietly beneath your deck.

property_title: Camelthorn Bush Camp: Wild Seclusion in Botswana's Heartland
property_intro: Tucked beneath the shade of ancient camelthorn trees, this intimate camp sits where Botswana's grasslands meet a wilderness roamed by elephant, lion and wild dog. Canvas suites are furnished with quiet craftsmanship, letting the landscape hold your attention. Days unfold with tracker-led game drives, walking safaris and evenings around the fire beneath extraordinary skies. Run in partnership with neighbouring communities and dedicated to protecting migration corridors, it is a place where comfort and conservation sit easily together.

property_title: Amava River Lodge: Riverside Calm in the Heart of the Wild
property_intro: Set along a slow-moving river where kingfishers dart between the reeds, Amava River Lodge invites you to settle into the rhythm of the South African bush. Suites open onto water and woodland, their interiors shaped by local craftsmanship and natural texture. Days unfold with guided game drives, walking safaris and long lunches under the trees, while partnerships with neighbouring communities and ongoing habitat restoration ensure your stay leaves the landscape richer than you found it.

property_title: Cape Point Hideaway: Where Fynbos Meets the Wild Atlantic
property_intro: At the southern tip of the Cape Peninsula, where fynbos-clad slopes tumble towards two oceans, Cape Point Hideaway offers a quieter way to know this remarkable coastline. Interiors of pale timber, linen and locally thrown ceramics frame views of breaking surf and passing whales. Days unfold with guided walks through endemic flora, tidal-pool swims and suppers built around Cape produce. The owners work alongside neighbouring conservancies to restore indigenous habitat and support local livelihoods.

property_title: Mariners Moon: Coastal Calm Where the Cape Meets the Tide
property_intro: Perched along South Africa's wave-carved shoreline, Mariners Moon invites you to slow to the rhythm of the tides. Interiors pair pale timber, linen and locally made ceramics with wide windows framing the Atlantic, while mornings might bring whale sightings, rock-pool wandering or a walk through fynbos-scented dunes. Meals draw on nearby farms and small fisheries, and the house supports coastal conservation efforts led by the community. A refined, unhurried retreat for those who travel thoughtfully.

property_title: Tafika Main Camp: Wild Heart of Zambia's Luangwa Valley
property_intro: On the banks of the Luangwa River, at the edge of Zambia's South Luangwa National Park, Tafika is a family-run camp where thatch, reed and river breeze replace fuss and formality. Days unfold on walking safaris led by legendary guides, microlight flights above the floodplain and visits to nearby Mkasanga village, where the camp's support for schools and clinics runs deep. Evenings belong to the fire, the frogs and the astonishing dark of an African sky.

property_title: Big Lagoon Walking Camp: Zambia's Wild Rhythms on Foot
property_intro: Set beside a lagoon in Zambia's game-rich wilderness, Big Lagoon Walking Camp invites you to travel at the pace of the bush. Days begin with a guided walk among hippo pools and ebony groves, tracking elephant and buffalo alongside expert local guides. Canvas tents are simply and thoughtfully appointed, with breezy verandas and lantern-lit dinners under acacias. Seasonal in footprint and community-run in spirit, the camp supports conservation while sharing the region's living traditions.

property_title: Chikoko Tree Walking Camp: Discover Luangwa's Wild Heart on Foot
property_intro: Deep in Zambia's South Luangwa, reached only on foot, Chikoko Tree Walking Camp sits among ebony and mahogany groves where elephants pass beneath your raised thatch chalet. Built each season from local grass, reeds and timber, then returned to the bush, it leaves barely a trace. Days unfold with expert guides reading tracks and birdsong, while your stay supports community schooling and anti-poaching work across this remarkable, little-trodden corner of the valley.

property_title: Olimba Camp: Wild Seclusion in Zambia's Untamed Heartland
property_intro: Tucked into a quiet corner of Zambia's bush, Olimba Camp offers a rare kind of solitude, where days unfold to the rhythm of the river and the calls of resident wildlife. Canvas suites are furnished with restraint and craft, opening onto floodplains grazed by antelope. Walk with expert guides, track lion on foot, or drink in the stillness after dark. Revenue supports local conservation teams and neighbouring villages, making every stay quietly consequential.

property_title: Takwela Main Camp: Wild River Seclusion in North Luangwa
property_intro: Perched above the confluence of the Mwaleshi and Luangwa rivers, Takwela Main Camp sits in one of Zambia's least-visited wildernesses. Four open-fronted chalets, built from thatch, reed and local stone, look out over water where hippos gather and elephants cross at dusk. Days unfold on foot with expert guides, tracking lion and buffalo through North Luangwa's remote bush. Your stay directly supports the park's rhino protection work and the communities living alongside it.

property_title: Mwaleshi Walking Camp: On Foot Through Wildest North Luangwa
property_intro: Set where the Mwaleshi River spills over shallow falls in Zambia's little-visited North Luangwa National Park, this intimate camp holds just a handful of thatched, open-fronted chalets built by hand from grass and reed. Days begin on foot, tracking buffalo and lion with expert guides in a wilderness closed to vehicles. Family-run for decades, the camp supports anti-poaching patrols and the park's remarkable black rhino recovery. Evenings bring riverside fires and extraordinary silence.

property_title: Bumbusi Wilderness Camp: Hwange's Untamed Northern Secret
property_intro: Tucked into the remote north of Hwange National Park, Bumbusi Wilderness Camp sits beside ancient rock engravings and the ruins of a pre-colonial settlement, in a corner of Zimbabwe few travellers ever reach. Four canvas-and-timber suites open onto mopane woodland where elephants drift past at dusk. Days unfold with walking safaris, tracking lessons and starlit dinners, while your stay directly funds anti-poaching patrols and the neighbouring communities who safeguard this extraordinary wilderness.

property_title: Mhara River Camp: Riverside Seclusion in Wild Zimbabwe
property_intro: Set along a quiet stretch of river in Zimbabwe's untamed bushveld, Mhara River Camp invites you to slow your pace. Canvas suites open to water and woodland, furnished with natural textures and handcrafted pieces from nearby villages. Days unfold with walking safaris led by expert local guides, canoe drifts and long lunches beneath ancient trees. Anti-poaching partnerships and community employment underpin every stay, so your presence here quietly strengthens the wilderness that surrounds you.

property_title: Nantwich Lodge: Elevated Seclusion in Hwange's Northern Wilds
property_intro: Set on a rise above the Deka plains in a quiet northern corner of Hwange National Park, Nantwich Lodge looks out over grasslands where elephant, sable and roan drift between waterholes. Three private villas blend understated comfort with sweeping verandah views, while guided drives, walking safaris and hide sittings unfold far from other vehicles. Long-standing support for anti-poaching patrols and nearby communities means your stay helps sustain one of Africa's great wilderness areas.

property_title: Phinda Rock Lodge: Cliffside Calm in KwaZulu-Natal's Wilds
property_intro: Perched on a rocky ledge above the Leopard Rock gorge, Phinda Rock Lodge looks out across Zululand's wooded valleys, where cheetah, rhino and elephant move through &Beyond's celebrated reserve. Six split-level suites, shaped in earth-toned stone and thatch, open to private plunge pools and views that stretch for miles. Days unfold with expert-led game drives, black rhino tracking and community visits in nearby Mduku, where conservation and local partnership underpin everything Phinda does.

property_title: Playa Cativo Lodge: Rainforest Seclusion on the Golfo Dulce
property_intro: Reached only by boat, Playa Cativo Lodge sits where primary rainforest meets the tranquil waters of Costa Rica's Golfo Dulce. Solar power, spring water and produce from the lodge's own gardens sustain days spent kayaking mangroves, tracking scarlet macaws with resident naturalists or simply reading beneath a ceiling fan. Handcrafted timber interiors open to the shoreline, while long-standing partnerships with Osa communities help protect one of the planet's most biodiverse corners.

property_title: Origins Floral: Costa Rica's Quietly Blooming Rainforest Retreat
property_intro: Tucked into Costa Rica's green interior, Origins Floral gathers a handful of light-filled sanctuaries beneath a canopy alive with birdsong. Days unfold gently here: barefoot walks through flowering gardens, cacao tastings with neighbouring growers, and long afternoons beside water that mirrors the treetops. Interiors favour local hardwoods, handwoven textiles and open air over ornament. Regeneration guides everything, from reforested land to partnerships with nearby families, making each stay quietly consequential as well as restorative.

property_title: Origins Astral: Stargazing Sanctuary in Costa Rica's Wild Hills
property_intro: Set among the forested ridges of Costa Rica, Origins Astral invites you to slow down beneath one of the clearest night skies in the tropics. Architecture of timber, stone and glass frames the surrounding canopy, while days unfold through guided stargazing, forest walks, farm-to-table dining and wellness rituals drawn from the land. Regenerative practices and close partnerships with neighbouring communities shape every detail, so your stay quietly supports the wilderness that surrounds it.

property_title: &Beyond Vira Vira: Chile's Lakeside Farm Retreat in Patagonia
property_intro: Set on a working dairy farm beside the Liucura River in Chile's Lake District, &Beyond Vira Vira pairs volcano views with a genuine sense of place. Cheese is made on site, vegetables come from the garden, and dinner reflects whatever the day has offered. Days might involve fly fishing, riding with local huasos, or paddling glacial waters before the sauna. Rooms are quietly handsome in timber and stone, with Villarrica smouldering gently on the horizon.

property_title: Kichwa Tembo Tented Camp: A Classic Safari on the Mara's Edge
property_intro: Set at the foot of the Oloololo Escarpment, where the Mara Triangle unfolds in golden plains, Kichwa Tembo occupies one of Kenya's most storied stretches of wilderness. Tents open onto grassland grazed by elephant and zebra, while interiors nod to the golden age of safari with campaign furniture and soft linens. Days move between game drives, balloon flights and conversations with Maasai neighbours, whose partnership underpins the camp's conservation and community work.

property_title: Bateleur Camp: Vintage Safari Grace on the Great Mara Plains
property_intro: Tucked beneath the Oloololo Escarpment, where forest gives way to the Maasai Mara's open grasslands, Bateleur Camp recalls the golden age of safari with campaign furniture, Persian rugs and butler service beneath billowing canvas. Just eighteen guests share this hidden setting, waking to wildebeest on the horizon and drifting over the plains by balloon. AndBeyond's conservation and community partnerships across the Mara ensure your stay leaves the wilderness measurably richer.

property_title: Grumeti Serengeti Tented Camp: Wild Luxury on the Migration Path
property_intro: Set along the banks of the Grumeti River in Tanzania's private Singita Grumeti reserve, this intimate camp places you at the heart of the western Serengeti's great migration corridor. Ten airy tented suites blend 1920s safari romance with contemporary comfort, opening onto riverine forest where hippos wallow below. Days unfold with guided game drives, walking safaris and conversations with the anti-poaching teams and community programmes safeguarding 350,000 acres of restored wilderness for generations to come.

property_title: Klein's Camp: Hilltop Seclusion on the Serengeti's Wild Frontier
property_intro: Perched high on the Kuka Hills, Klein's Camp overlooks the Grumeti River valley where the northern Serengeti unfolds towards Kenya. Ten stone-and-thatch cottages sit within a private concession leased from the local Maasai community, allowing night drives, guided walks and unhurried game viewing far from other vehicles. Days might begin with sunrise on the escarpment and end beside the fire, with village visits offering genuine insight into Maasai life and the conservation it sustains.

property_title: Serengeti Under Canvas: Follow the Herds Across Tanzania
property_intro: Pitched in the path of the great migration, Serengeti Under Canvas moves several times each year to keep pace with the herds, placing you within earshot of hooves and lion song. Nine airy tents pair brass fittings and Persian rugs with bucket showers and lantern light, while guides lead walking safaris, dawn game drives and balloon flights above the plains. Solar power, water conservation and Serengeti-wide community partnerships keep this remarkable wilderness thriving.

property_title: Lake Manyara Tree Lodge: Secluded Forest Luxury in Tanzania
property_intro: Tucked deep within a mahogany forest in the southern reaches of Lake Manyara National Park, this intimate lodge places just ten stilted treehouse suites among ancient branches, with only birdsong and distant elephants for company. Days unfold on game drives in search of tree-climbing lions, guided walks with Maasai companions and night drives beneath vast skies. Crafted from local timber and thatch, the lodge supports neighbouring communities and conservation of this remarkable, little-visited corner of Tanzania.

property_title: Chobe Under Canvas: Mobile Camping on Botswana's Wild Frontier
property_intro: Set within Chobe National Park, this seasonal mobile camp moves with the herds, pitching in private wilderness sites where elephants gather in their hundreds along the river. Canvas tents are pared back yet quietly comfortable, with bucket showers, hand-poured drinks at the fire and starlit dinners under acacias. Days unfold on game drives and river cruises, guided by expert local trackers. Low-impact by design, the camp leaves nothing behind but footprints, supporting Botswana's conservation-led approach to tourism.

property_title: Rawla Narlai: A Storied Village Retreat in the Aravalli Hills
property_intro: Halfway between Jodhpur and Udaipur, this 17th-century nobleman's residence sits at the foot of a vast granite hill, wrapped in the quiet rhythms of Narlai village. Frescoed courtyards, hand-carved jharokhas and shaded verandas invite unhurried days; evenings might mean a candlelit dinner in an ancient step-well or a dawn walk past Jain temples and leopard country. Family-run for generations, it supports local artisans, farmers and schools with genuine care.

property_title: Ahilya Fort: Riverside Serenity on the Sacred Narmada, India
property_intro: Perched above the Narmada in the temple town of Maheshwar, Ahilya Fort remains the ancestral home of the Holkar family, opened with genuine warmth to a handful of guests. Days unfold with river swims, boat rides past bathing ghats and dinners in candlelit courtyards, drawn from the fort's own gardens. The estate has revived Maheshwari handloom weaving, and you may watch artisans at their looms before wandering ramparts scented with frangipani and jasmine.

property_title: Zang'ser Sarai: A Himalayan Retreat Among Ladakh's Apricot Groves
property_intro: Set within the high desert folds of Ladakh, Zang'ser Sarai gathers guests into a courtyard of sun-warmed mud brick, poplar beams and apricot trees. Days unfold slowly here: walks to whitewashed monasteries, conversations with village weavers, meals shaped by what the fields and orchards offer. Built using traditional Ladakhi craft and passive solar design, the house supports local artisans and stewards scarce water. Nights belong to the mountains, silent beneath an immense, star-strewn sky.

property_title: Fort Tiracol Heritage Hotel: Goa's Clifftop Portuguese Retreat
property_intro: Perched on a headland where the Tiracol River meets the Arabian Sea, this restored 17th-century Portuguese fort marks Goa's northernmost tip. Just seven rooms, each named after a day of the week, open onto whitewashed terraces above a working chapel and a courtyard shaded by frangipani. Arrive by ferry, swim at quiet Querim beach, dine on Goan seafood, and wake to birdsong. Restoration work here has kept local craft traditions and village livelihoods thriving.

property_title: Alsisar Mahal: A Shekhawati Palace Reborn in Rajasthan's Sands
property_intro: In the frescoed heartland of Shekhawati, three hours from Jaipur, Alsisar Mahal has stood since the 18th century as the seat of a Rajput thakur. Its jharokhas, courtyards and hand-painted arches remain in the family's care, restored rather than reinvented. Days unfold with camel rides through dunes, village walks past merchant havelis and dinners beneath the stars. The palace also hosts the Magnetic Fields festival, drawing artists and locals together each winter.

property_title: Deogarh Mahal: A Living Rajput Palace in the Aravalli Hills
property_intro: Rising above a lake in the Aravalli hills, midway between Udaipur and Jodhpur, Deogarh Mahal has been home to the same family for seventeen generations. Frescoed chambers, cupolas and courtyards remain wonderfully lived-in rather than restored into stiffness. Days unfold with village walks, birdwatching by the water, heritage train journeys and cooking with recipes from the royal kitchen. Local craftspeople and farmers supply the estate, keeping the surrounding community woven into every stay.

property_title: Forsyth Lodge: Wild Satpura Awaits Beyond Your Verandah
property_intro: On the fringes of Satpura Tiger Reserve in Madhya Pradesh, Forsyth Lodge sits within 44 acres of regenerating forest, where sal trees and birdsong replace the hum of the everyday. Days unfold on foot, by canoe along the Denwa backwaters, or tracking sloth bears with naturalists who know each ridge intimately. Rooms are unfussy and locally built, staff are drawn from neighbouring villages, and every stay quietly supports the wilderness beyond your doorstep.

property_title: Wanosato Ryokan: Thatched Farmhouse Serenity in Hida's Hills
property_intro: Tucked into a wooded valley outside Takayama, Wanosato gathers a handful of centuries-old thatched farmhouses beside the Miyagawa river. Relocated and lovingly restored, their blackened beams and irori hearths now frame quiet nights of Hida beef, foraged mountain vegetables and river-stone baths under the stars. Days unfold slowly here: birdsong, cedar-scented air, a walk to nearby hot springs. It is a rare living record of Japanese rural craft, kept alive by the family who tend it.

property_title: Asaba Ryokan: Centuries of Quiet Ritual in Izu's Green Hills
property_intro: Tucked into the wooded hills of Shuzenji on Japan's Izu Peninsula, Asaba has welcomed guests for some five centuries. Rooms open onto a mirror-still pond, where a Noh stage hosts performances beneath the cedars — a tradition the family continues to support. Days unfold slowly: hot-spring bathing, kaiseki dinners drawn from local waters and mountain vegetables, and mornings spent watching mist lift from the garden. Here, restraint feels like the greatest indulgence.

property_title: Azuma Farm Koiwai: Pastoral Calm Beneath Iwate's Mountains
property_intro: Set among the meadows and woodland of Iwate, Azuma Farm Koiwai unfolds beneath the volcanic silhouette of Mount Iwate. Days here follow the rhythm of the land: dairy herds at pasture, seasonal harvests, and long walks through larch groves. Interiors pair timber warmth with quiet restraint, while meals draw on the farm's own milk, eggs and vegetables. Guests leave with a deeper sense of rural Japan, and of the families who sustain it.

property_title: Iwaso: Generations of Quiet Ritual in Miyajima's Maple Valley
property_intro: Tucked into Momijidani's maple-shaded valley on the sacred island of Miyajima, Iwaso has welcomed guests since 1854 with an unhurried grace that feels entirely its own. Wander to Itsukushima Shrine before the ferries arrive, soak in mineral baths, then savour Setouchi seafood in rooms of timber, paper and lacquer. Deer graze beyond the garden bridge, and the family's careful stewardship of the surrounding woodland keeps this rare stillness intact for those who follow.

property_title: Zannier Phum Baitang: Siem Reap's Green Village Sanctuary
property_intro: Set among eight hectares of lemongrass fields on the edge of Siem Reap, Zannier Phum Baitang gathers forty-five wooden stilted villas into a village of its own. Angkor's temples wait a short drive away, yet mornings here belong to buffalo grazing beyond the rice paddies. Reclaimed timber, hand-laid stone and locally trained artisans shape the experience, while spa rituals, Khmer cookery classes and quiet swims in the saltwater pool invite you to linger longer than planned.

property_title: Zannier Omaanda: Namibian Wilderness, Owambo Warmth and Grace
property_intro: Set within a private reserve just beyond Windhoek, Zannier Omaanda gathers ten thatched huts inspired by traditional Owambo architecture across rolling bushveld where giraffe, oryx and zebra roam. Days unfold with guided game drives, bush walks and quiet hours beside the pool, watching the light shift across the hills. The lodge supports the neighbouring N/a'an ku sê Foundation, whose wildlife sanctuary and community clinic serve San families, giving every stay a purpose beyond the extraordinary.

property_title: Zannier Le Chalet: Timeless Alpine Living Above Megève, Savoie
property_intro: Tucked into the wooded slopes above Megève, Zannier Le Chalet gathers just a handful of rooms behind weathered timber and reclaimed stone. Log fires, sheepskins and Savoyard craftsmanship set the mood, while mountain guides, forest walks and long lunches shape unhurried days. The kitchen leans on producers from the surrounding valleys, and salvaged materials give the house its lived-in soul. Come winter or high summer, it feels less like a hotel than a friend's private retreat.

property_title: Mia Resort Nha Trang: Cliffside Calm Above Vietnam's Sea
property_intro: Tucked into a private cove on Nha Trang's southern coast, Mia Resort Nha Trang cascades down a terraced hillside towards its own stretch of sand. Villas and condos frame the East Sea through timber, stone and thoughtful shade, while Sandals restaurant draws on Vietnamese produce and local fishing catches. Days unfold with sunrise swims, hillside spa treatments and boat trips to nearby islands. Staff hail largely from surrounding villages, keeping hospitality here genuinely rooted in place.

property_title: Azerai Ke Ga Bay: Coastal Calm Beneath a Storied Lighthouse
property_intro: Set along Vietnam's south-central coast, a short drive from Phan Thiet, Azerai Ke Ga Bay gazes out to a granite islet crowned by a 19th-century French lighthouse. Boulder-strewn sands, casuarina groves and generous pools shape unhurried days, while pared-back interiors of timber, stone and local craft keep the focus outward. Sail a traditional basket boat, cycle through fishing hamlets, or join dragon fruit farmers whose families have tended this shoreline for generations.

property_title: Pimalai Resort & Spa: Barefoot Luxury on Koh Lanta's Shores
property_intro: Tucked into 100 acres of tropical hillside on Koh Lanta, Pimalai Resort & Spa opens onto a quiet stretch of Ba Kan Tiang Bay in the Andaman Sea. Villas sit among mature jungle, reached by winding paths where hornbills call at dawn. Sail a traditional junk to Koh Rok's coral gardens, learn Thai cookery with island produce, or unwind in the hilltop spa. The resort supports local schools, mangrove replanting and reef protection year-round.

property_title: Kayumanis Jimbaran: Private Villa Living by Bali's South Coast
property_intro: Tucked into a tranquil pocket of Jimbaran, moments from the bay's fishing boats and sunset shoreline, Kayumanis Jimbaran offers just a handful of walled private villas shaded by frangipani and tropical greenery. Each has its own pool, garden pavilion and attentive butler, while Balinese craftsmanship shapes every carved detail. Days might bring a cookery lesson with market-fresh produce, a temple visit with a local guide, or simply the quiet luxury of unhurried privacy.

property_name: Kayumanis Nusa Dua Private Villa & Spa
property_title: Kayumanis Nusa Dua Private Villa & Spa: Bali's Quiet Luxury
property_intro: Tucked within tropical gardens moments from Nusa Dua's shoreline, Kayumanis Nusa Dua offers just twenty walled villas, each with its own pool and shaded pavilion. Balinese craftsmanship shapes every detail, from carved timber to hand-woven textiles, while butlers arrange private dinners, spa rituals and market visits with local cooks. Guests are invited to appreciate Balinese ceremony and cuisine as living traditions, supported by the resort's long-standing ties to nearby villages and artisan communities.

property_title: Kayumanis Sanur Private Villa & Spa: Quiet Luxury in Old Bali
property_intro: Tucked down a lane in Sanur, Bali's gentlest coastal town, Kayumanis hides twenty walled villas behind frangipani and coral stone. Each has its own pool, shaded pavilion and butler who remembers how you take your coffee. Days drift from sunrise walks along the fishing beach to spa rituals scented with local spices, or cooking lessons using produce from nearby growers. Thoughtfully staffed by Balinese families, it feels less like a hotel and more like a private compound lent to you.

property_title: Kayumanis Ubud Private Villa & Spa: A Riverside Bali Retreat
property_intro: Tucked into a fold of the Oos River valley near Sayan, Kayumanis Ubud gathers just a handful of walled villas beneath a canopy of tropical trees. Each has its own pool, open-air pavilion and hand-carved timber details drawn from Balinese craft traditions. Days might unfold with a temple visit, a market walk with the chef, or treatments blending local botanicals. Villagers tend the surrounding rice terraces, and their rituals still shape the rhythm here.

property_title: Bungaraya Island Resort: Rainforest Seclusion on Gaya Island
property_intro: Tucked into the forested folds of Gaya Island, within Sabah's Tunku Abdul Rahman Marine Park, Bungaraya Island Resort lies a short boat ride from Kota Kinabalu yet feels worlds apart. Timber villas rise among ancient trees above a quiet bay, where hornbills call at dawn and coral gardens wait just offshore. Guests snorkel, kayak or simply drift, while the resort's marine conservation work and Borneo-rooted hospitality quietly shape every stay.

property_title: Casa del Mar Langkawi: Barefoot Elegance on Cenang Beach
property_intro: Set directly on the soft sands of Pantai Cenang, Casa del Mar is an intimate Mediterranean-inspired retreat of just 34 suites, where terracotta hues meet the Andaman Sea. Days drift between spa treatments in a garden pavilion, chef-led dinners at The Beach Grill and sunset paddles beneath Langkawi's ancient rainforest ridges. The family-run team supports local artisans and island clean-ups, lending a genuine sense of place to every unhurried, salt-air morning.

property_title: Villa Samadhi Kuala Lumpur: A Hidden Sanctuary in the City
property_intro: Tucked behind a curtain of greenery near Kuala Lumpur's embassy quarter, Villa Samadhi feels worlds away from the city humming just beyond its walls. Twenty-one rooms of recycled timber, blackened brick and lantern light gather around a swimming lagoon shaded by mature trees. Days drift between spa treatments, Malay-inspired dining at Mandi Mandi and evenings on your private balcony, with the Petronas Towers only minutes away when curiosity calls.

property_title: Anantara Peace Haven Tangalle: Sri Lanka's Coastal Sanctuary
property_intro: Set on a headland where a working coconut plantation meets the Indian Ocean, Anantara Peace Haven Tangalle occupies one of Sri Lanka's most secluded stretches of southern coast. Villas open to sea breezes and cliffside views, while days unfold with turtle conservation walks, spice-scented cookery classes and Ayurvedic rituals guided by resident practitioners. Nearby, whales pass offshore and blue-water lagoons draw birdlife. It is a place that rewards slowness, curiosity and genuine connection with the island's rhythms.

property_title: Wild Glamping Gal Oya: Sri Lanka's Untamed Lakeside Retreat
property_intro: On the fringes of Gal Oya National Park, where elephants swim between forested islands, Wild Glamping Gal Oya offers a rare kind of seclusion. Tented suites rest lightly among the trees, built with natural materials and shaped by the landscape rather than imposed upon it. Days unfold with boat safaris across Senanayake Reservoir, guided walks alongside members of the indigenous Vedda community, and evenings spent listening to the forest. Comfort here is quiet, considered and deeply rooted in place.

property_title: Aliya Resort & Spa: Sigiriya's Lion Rock Seen from Your Pool
property_intro: Set amid paddy fields and lakes in Sri Lanka's Cultural Triangle, Aliya Resort & Spa gazes directly at Sigiriya's Lion Rock and Pidurangala. Villas open onto private plunge pools, while earthy interiors nod to village craft traditions. Days unfold with sunrise climbs, Ayurvedic treatments, cookery lessons with local families and bicycle rides through Habarana's scrub jungle. The resort supports elephant-corridor conservation and nearby schools, so your stay quietly gives back to the landscape that shapes it.

property_title: Plataran Komodo Resort: Barefoot Luxury on Flores' Wild Shore
property_intro: Tucked into a private bay on Flores' north-west coast, Plataran Komodo Resort looks out across the islands of the Komodo archipelago. Timber villas, thatched roofs and Indonesian craftsmanship sit lightly among the hills, while the beach opens onto reefs alive with turtles and manta rays. Sail traditional phinisi vessels, trek to meet Komodo dragons, or join reef restoration and village initiatives that support the surrounding community. Evenings belong to the sunset, and to nothing much else.

property_title: Plataran Bromo: Volcanic Sunrises Amid Java's Pine Highlands
property_intro: Set high on the fringes of Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park, Plataran Bromo rests among casuarina pines and terraced farmland, where cool mountain air carries the scent of resin and woodsmoke. Javanese timber villas and glass-fronted suites frame views of steaming craters, while dawn jeep journeys, guided walks and firelit dinners fill the days. The resort works closely with Tenggerese neighbours, championing local produce, craft and culture with genuine, quietly attentive hospitality.

property_title: Plataran Menjangan: Wild Shores of West Bali's National Park
property_intro: Tucked within the savannah and mangroves of West Bali National Park, Plataran Menjangan feels worlds away from the island's busier south. Timber villas and treetop lodges rise among nesting Bali starlings, while the Java Sea glitters beyond a private jetty.
